text: I now know that I'm not a cruise person. Screw saving a couple hundy - I want to be freeeee! This Radiance of the Seas cruise was a Thurs. afternoon through Monday morning trip to Cozumel out of Tampa, FL. I was on a friend's bachelorette getaway with 9 other girls. The stop in Cozumel was 7 hours - and the rest was just cruisin...and cruisin...aaand cruisin some more. It was an older ship carrying just over 2000 people (small in comparison to the new 3500+ beasts that boast vegas-like pools, health food restaurants, and much bigger/better rooms). Myself, along with one other friend, were the only ones who had never cruised before - many of the girls had been on 5+. So this review is based both on a novice perspective and experienced feedback. The room: I stayed in a three person balcony, ocean-view room with the bride and maid of honor. It was supposed to be the nicest and most expensive of our bunch, and the level just below a suite. OMG. Think two dwarfed doubles and what looked like a large sized public bathroom baby changer coming out of the wall above the beds. Niiiice. Our understanding was that there would be a fold-out couch...but no such luck. The room actually seemed smaller than our friend's, who were in the ship's bowels. Our balcony was above a huge ledge, so there was really no ocean view. The bathroom: Sweet jesus no. This thing was minute. The sink constantly clogged. The shower was so small, I kept banging my elbows and ass against the wall when trying to soap/shampoo - and forget about bending down to shave. I have no clue how some of the large men (and there were plenty of them), functioned in there! Common area restrooms: I was totally grossed out. They all smelled putrid - and were out of order half the time. I left a comedy show one night to quickly use the restroom, and wound up three floors and 10 hallways away just looking for a working toilet! Food: One of the main reasons people go on cruises...which is painfully obvious in looking at most of the passengers. The food was totally subpar at best. Yes, you can order (in small portions), three appetizers, two entrees and two desserts at dinner, and eat all you want at the buffets - but I'd prefer quality over quantity any day. It was no good. We'd roam the buffets saying nothing looked appealing, and concur that dinner was gross. Surprisingly, and unlike most cruises as I understand, food around the ship wasn't easy to come by during non-meal hours. Service: Could have been better. Dinners were looong. We'd order wine and it would take 30 minutes to arrive. One night, they put the bottle on the table unopened and left it there for a good 25 minutes before coming back to cork it. Our room attendant hated life - and it was obvious. Room service took forever. Pool: MAJOR disappointment. It was smaller than what you'd see in a backyard. We must have asked three times "are you sure this is the main pool?" People: The majority of passengers were AARP members, women, and middle-aged couples on a low budge trip. There were a few young(er) people (who we knew by sight, if not name, b/c they were so few and far between). Entertainment: People on cruises loooove to participate in choreographed group dances. Everywhere you looked, there were electric slides and macarenas going down. *puts gun in mouth* Lots of contests - best belly flop, hot legs, name that lyric, etc. There was one club (which was definitely lacking, but we made due), a movie theatre, casino, rock climbing wall and gym. (Amusing gym side note: there was a class on increasing your metabolism taking place while I was in there. It was attended by four ladies drinking pina coladas and a 300lb dude eating fries...only on a cruise.) Bottom line: Cruises are not my bag. I had a good time - but that was because I was with great people and got to see Cozumel, not due to the cruise experience. They aren't much cheaper than a set destination, as you wind up spending massive amounts on bottled water, liquor and all the extras. ...I did it. I can say I've cruised. But I will absolutely be staying in a hotel and roaming free on my next trip!
label: NEG

text: Okay, let me preface this. 2 points: 1) I have not yet been to Barclay Prime 2) Butcher and Singer is NOT Peter Lugar's. That being said, for my 28th birthday, my wife and I, along with my brother and his wife, went there for dinner on Saturday. Upon first entering, i felt as though i stepped into an old film- kind of expecting to see Ava Gardner and Sinatra sipping on Martini's at the bar. Obviously, people, i am not retarded and i know that even in his greatness, Stephen Starr had no access to the flux capacitor(at least as far as I know) After being seated by our period dressed hostess(unless she was just a weird theater girl who always dresses like that), we were seated in quite possibly the most comfortable seats in any restaurant I've been in. TAKE THAT, SHITTY BAR STOOLS AT ALMA DE CUBA!!! We started with some cocktails and ordered some appetizers. We order a 1/2 doz oysters and the lump crab cocktail. Both were excellent, the crab was awesome (though I've always contested that if you fuck that up, then you sir, are worse than Hitler) and the oysters were equally as decadent. I was surprised at the knowledge that our server had about them- he described in depth where exactly they were harvested from. I don't really know a whole lot about them, but i ask questions sometimes to make myself look smarter. God, did that backfire. I felt like a hayseed jackass. For the main course, we ordered a porterhouse for three that was cooked rare and my brothers wife ordered the fillet that was cooked medium. As far as sides, we ordered the spinach, mushrooms and onions, and the stuffed hash brown. First of all the sides were excellent. The hash brown was in a word, sensual in its context. If i could eat that for breakfast at my local diner every morning i would die a cheesy, potatoey mess. The spinach was also excellent(again, if you screw that up, worse than Hitler. Listen close to that, "the palm"). The mushrooms were very good, an exotic mix, however the onions seemed a little bland. Small complaint, i know, but I've gotta say something bad. And now for the steaks. I didn't taste the fillet, so i can't comment on that. However, the dry aged porterhouse was borderline orgasmic. Perfect char on the outside-perfect, tender, rare center. Much to the chagrin of my wife, I found myself picking up the bone and ripping the meat off of it with my teeth. Note to self: Order rib eye next time; avoid spousal embarrassment There was a dessert, the fudge cake, which was good. But by that point I was already sold. I recommend this place to anyone who loves a good steak dinner and cool ambiance.

text: I was just here for a couple nights at the end of June and it is a beautiful property, but I don't think it is worth the room rate. Bacara's rate are similar to the 4 Seasons in Montecito and San Ysidro Ranch, but there were some obvious ways I felt they missed the mark during our stay. 1) we had treatments in the spa which were very good, but the lounge area had empty cups from guests who had left and the upholstery on the cushions in the rooms was a bit tattered. 2) We went to lounge by the main pool one day and a cocktail server came by for our beverage order and we asked for a couple ice waters. She returned to the chaise lounges right by us twice to deliver a couple drinks (her tray was not full!) without bringing our waters. After at least a 10 minute wait I went to the bar to get our waters (my friend thought it was more like 15 minutes). She came 10 minutes after I returned with our waters and there was no apology for us having to get our own drinks. I've worked in food service and this is just awful, no matter how casual the property/restaurant. 3) As the pool started winding down the staff began to put the deck chairs back in place and proceeded to drag them across the cement, making that lovely metal on concrete screeching sound - ugg! My friend had her chaise fully reclined and had been snoozing until this woke her up. 4) Bathrooms at the pool: were a mess, paper towels, toilet paper on the floor, water on the counters. And when I went in there the pool wasn't packed to capacity, this was end of day. The bathrooms shouldn't look so messy at a place where you are paying $700 a night. if the pool staff went thru here every 30 minutes to ck on it this could be kept from happening, but they don't act like they do team service or are thinking past where their next tip comes from. 5) Room service - the food was pretty good, the servers were very nice, but for 2 of our meals items were forgotten 1) we asked for ranch dressing w/ our fries and it didn't come. For breakfast one day there was no jam for our toast. Don't they have checklists they look over before they leave the kitchen? 6) I left an article of clothing at the pool and realized it when i got back to my room around 7pm. I pressed the "At your service" button on the phone and was told they'd ck w/ housekeeping and get back to me. I never got a call back so called the next am since we were cking out that day. they called me later in the morning and said I could pick up what I had left from the pool bar. No offer to bring it to my room, lame! Oh, forgot front desk staff - not impressive, a bit on the snooty side, could have been more gracious and welcoming. If you can't help a customer waiting in line cuz there is only one computer (I'm guessing) or you aren't trained to ck ppl in, but you are behind the counter, at least welcome them and let them know they'll be helped shortly. Bacara is right by the beach and has a groomed path, but once you get to the beach you have do the obstacle course over large rocks, why haven't they cleared a path so their guests don't have this obstacle to get to the beach? Again the property is gorgeous, the landscaping is amazing, the room service, bell staff and pool bartenders were gracious, friendly and fun. But for this kind of money I'd say go to the 4 seasons or San Ysidro. Or spend less and stay at Fess Parker right across from the beach!

text: If I could, I would give this place 2.5 stars. I ended up at Ice Kitchen thanks to a coupon. After reading the reviews here, however, I lowered my expectations. Overall I would rate Ice Kitchen average. Not blow your socks off amazing but it has some appeal, especially for drinkers. It's really on the edge between becoming a decent restaurant or falling into the abyss; hopefully they will go for the first. After being seated, the first thing we noticed was lipstick marks on both of our water glasses. The server apologized profusely and quickly replaced them (with clean ones!); something about it being too dark in the back to tell if glasses are clean---I really hope she was joking there. Overall service was good though occasionally slow; my drinks came out several minutes after my dining companion's did; it was wine, so nothing to be mixed or fussed with. Ice Kitchen's big claim to notoriety is their extensive vodka menu. As in, when I asked for the menu I was handed a huge, heavy, multipage menu for just the vodka. Vodkas from all over the world (countries you would never think making vodka). If vodka is your thing, I think you'll be happy here. I was not in a vodka mood, so I got the red wine flight, which was 9 dollars for 3 pretty generous pours (each was just slightly less than a full glass of wine). They weren't super outstanding wines, but pleasant enough. My dining companion got the martini flight, which had a pineapple/citrusy martini called the gold digger, a raspberry martini and a chocolate martini. The gold digger tasted a bit off; the pineapple citrus mix for some reason was not working. The other two were fine. These were also generously sized. Warning: flights are served in these cute 3 glass holder thingies; not all of them are very stable, so don't do what we did which was obliviously remove one without stabilizing the base. Splash. It would have been nice, since our server was right there when she reached for the drink to have mentioned that little piece of advice. Food was inoffensive. I started with a 3 spread plate of baba ghanoush, olive tapenade (which was just chopped up canned kalamatas as far as I could tell), and tzatziki served with toasted oiled pita points. The baba ghanoush was really good; wish I'd had a larger portion of that one. The tzatziki was not from the ilk of any tzatiki I had ever had before---no zip, no cucumber, no garlic. Didn't eat much of that one. Salad was fine, plated real fancy with fried sweet potato strings. I had the chicken lollipops which were ok, supposedly spicy asian style. Not at all hot however as billed on the menus. It was a small plate with 5 wings and a delicious spicy cabbage slaw in the center (only about 3 bites worth). Portions are smallish, but it's tapas so it's to be expected. As far as the restaurant itself, it seems to be having an identity crisis. The 4 sided bar in the center has flat screens on every side with sports going looking all the world like an upscale sports bar. Peripherally it is relatively dark with chi chi cool booths and glass tables, like how a 15 year old would design a super hot hipster locale. I will give them another shot; probably with a larger group next time. I probably wouldn't crave going there very often. Hopefully they will find there way to being a good restaurant or at least solve the identity crisis and just be an upscale sports bar. In any case, if you're in the area (or have a coupon) you can check it out, just keep your expectations low.

text: As a connoisseur of cupcakes, I can say with confidence that this place is better than *all* the cupcake stores in NYC (and I keep up-to-date with my surveys of same). For three weeks I collaborated with someone who had a studio nearby, and I came to know this place very well (the free samples are a real draw too). I recognize many of the cupcake batters and icings used in this store, and that is a very good thing, in the following sense. I recognize the recipes--many of them were passed down to my brothers and me by our forebears on both sides of the family (one set from the south, one from the northeast). The southern recipes in particular are genuinely represented here. Most of the cupcakes are absolutely delicious. After talking to some of the staff, I learned one reason for this: the cupcakes are made fresh each day. The business is so well-organized and so thoroughly patronized that they actually make only enough of any given kind of cupcake to sell on a given day; when that kind is gone, that's it until the next day or so. This means you *never* eat a stale cupcake from this place. The strawberry cupcakes are almost too good. The sour-cream-batter ones are also very fine. I'm not as fond of the chocolate icings or batters, but honestly even these are clearly authentically conceived and prepared, and are simply quite good. Only the red velvet (again very good) is less strong than those I make with my ancestors' recipes (but I have a gift too!). I haven't experienced the cake-ordering side of the business, because I haven't been in Philly enough to use it, but I'm betting it's professionally and artistically handled. In terms of service, once or twice there were specific counter staff who were snooty (one woman in particular) but this seemed to stop, and honestly none of these quibbles were enough to make a chip in my five stars.

text: Finally made it to Bibou (but unfortunately forgot my camera). There were six of us and many items on the menu looked good, so we ordered the entire menu, plus the 3-4 specials they had that night. The items that stuck out in my mind were: Oxtail terrine - delicate, yet packed with flavor. An umami bomb. Marrow Bones - this was a special for the night. Bones cut lengthwise, topped with a mixture of mushrooms, parsley and breadcrumbs if I recall correctly. Triple Casserole - Well cooked, making the tripe melt in your mouth. Foie Gras - perfectly seared with Griotte cherries. Pieds de Porc - pigs feet on french lentils. Crispy on the outside, gelatenous on the inside Hanger Steak - frankly we were going to skip this, but glad we ordered this as the steak had a nice char outside, but perfect tender and pink on the inside. Noix de Saint-Jacques - Perfectly cooked scallops on a puree of cauliflower and saffron cauliflower florets Loup de mer - the crispy skin and sea-sweet flesh of the bronzino went well with the marrow red wine sauce. Cheese Plate - showed more personality than the typical cheese plate in the city. My favorite was a cows milk cheese from Burgundy, who's name escapes me at the moment. While a majority of the dishes we enjoyed were very well cooked, we could not help but wish for some more seasonal ingredients featured on the menu, including some lighter dishes, especially in late spring/early summer. There was plenty of good wine that we enjoyed thanks to my dining companions, including a mature 1975 Château Léoville-Las Cases. Service was friendly and baring the occasional reminder to replenish the bread, quite efficient. The few seats get filled quick, so make sure you have a reservation. So, overall, while I would not compare my experience at Bibou to Per Se or other 3 star Michelin dining experiences, it certainly is worth experiencing the authentic family bistro ambiance and early days of what I am sure will be a noteworthy successor to Pif.

text: Let's face it folks, dining is about service, you go there to eat, but you also go there to have a good time. I planned to have my 18th birthday dinner at the California Pizza Kitchen. I had lots of friends say there were going to show up, and so I tried to reserve a big table, and for the most part the CPK was very responsive and nice about it. Until I actually showed up. Some people didn't come, or kept saying there were coming but didn't. And the management hassled me everyone couple of minutes asking if the whole party was going to arrive soon. I eventually figured out they wanted tables and told them to just take them, and some of the hassling stopped. I understand they need the tables for business, but if they really weren't supposed to sit people without their party, I would have been happy dividing my party to avoid the hassling. And on my birthday only annoys me more. But even the waiter was still ridiculously rude to my party. He claims they have a company policy that doesn't allow them to sing happy birthday or do anything for anyones birthday. Clearly this was a lie, because at the front, the hostess was telling me about a fudge cake I would get since it was my birthday, and then he had THE NERVE to come up to us and ask me if I wanted to BUY desert from them...for my birthday. Okay....NO. I don't know if he had ants in his pants or something, but he would stroll by every two to three minutes and ask how everything was doing, like he didn't have other customers to deal with, and even when he came he didn't pick up your drink for a refill, up to twenty minutes after it was empty. It was a horrible experience for me to spend, and even wasn't completely their fault, since I did have party cancellations, they didn't have to react the way they did, and I still ordered so much food that it's not like the waiter and restaurant didn't make a pile of money off my party and myself. If there's anything saving this place from one star it has to be that the food was still amazingly good, and that is about it. Restaurants can't just live off of good food though, they have to keep good clients and reputations to keep business going, and if I ever want to eat California Pizza Kitchen again in Brandon, I swear I will instead take it to go and just leave, screw the service there out of tips, and I will be sure to review them where ever I have an account to do so.

text: Tropicana Field is the worst stadium in professional sports. It's no more or less attractive than the old Metrodome, but it lacks all of that ballpark's atmosphere and charm. First, it's in a sea of asphalt parking lots and interstate onramps. Second, the stadium was barely two-thirds full for a Saturday afternoon game against the Yankees. Third, the fans who had showed up to support the Rays appeared confused by the rules and etiquette of baseball. Lots of cowbell slamming at inopportune times. This increased late in the game, despite the fact that the team was being no-hit into the 8th. As seemed to be a rule in the Tampa area generally, many fans were powerfully intoxicated, and the hour of day seemed to be no deterrent. Fans started leaving in the 7th inning. If I can sit in pouring rain in the Bronx to watch Daniel Cabrera almost no-hit my team, Tampans should be able to sit in this air conditioned pod for the same chance at history. Concessions were expensive, nearly matching YS prices, and disgusting. Are there seriously Outback Steakhouse concession stands all over this ballpark? Apparently, because people who couldn't bother to sit down or wait until inning breaks to inconvenience their neighbors kept milling through rows with bloomin' onions and some sort of nauseating chipped beef flatbread. Finally, one likes to walk around a new stadium to see it from different angles. Our walk around the field level concourse felt like a teaser for the special that premiered on the National Geographic Channel this past weekend: Solitary Confinement. No field views, and a long walk through concrete tunnels. And the line for the Rays touch tank was probably two innings long. Seriously? This team should move to Sioux City immediately. They'd get much better fan support. And a nicer ballpark.

text: A friend of mine is working for the PPA temporarily until he starts back up with school and has the worst things to say... One, he gets cursed out every day and if I ever see him, it's usually me cursing him out. Philadelphian's hate the PPA and with good reason, so curse them out when you see them. Two, he said they are held to such high quotas that they have to give out tickets even when people aren't in the wrong - otherwise he'll be fired and apparently they fire people all the time for being short 5 or 6 tickets per month. If you've ever seen the show, they sit there and watch the time go up and slap a ticket down before you can even pull a quarter from your pocket. Three, he said most of the people that he works with are drunk as hell on the job because there's nothing else to do all day aside from punching numbers into their ticket spurting death machines. It's a vicious system that really is out to profit from "the inconvenience we are causing the city of Philadelphia" by being a few minutes over the meter limit. And where the hell do they come up with the fines? If I'm 5-minutes over the meter... I owe them $26? They make more money on the ticket then they would all day on the meter so obviously they're going to try and get you. If you sell cotton candy for a living and people pay more for brand A than they do Brand B, won't you try and sell more of Brand B? Sure you would because that's where the money is at. Well I say F*CK YOU PPA. Now don't get me wrong, we need some type of Parking Authority in the city to keep people from abandoning cars on sidewalks and blocking sidewalk ramps... but come on. How are we to survive if this company continues to reach their big greedy hand in our pockets and take our hard earned money?! I say don't let them. Write a letter to Mayor Michael Nutter with photocopies of your tickets and the story on how you got them. I sent him 3 tickets two months ago and never got a response. text: I decided to visit the Philadelphia portion of Yelp just to give kudos to Blarney South. We came for a pre-season Eagles game and bummed around Philadelphia a bit. We came on a Thursday night and hesitated a bit in the doorway because the bar is actually situated near the front and we brought our 8 and 12 year olds along with us. They brought us right in and took us to the back, which was set up more like a restaurant. My husband had the most beautiful bacon bleu cheese burger I've ever seen. It was huge with no less than four thick slices of bacon and plenty of bleu cheese crumbles. I honestly don't know how he got his mouth around it, but he managed and it was gone (every last crumb) in no time flat. My older son had a chicken cheese steak, which he said was good, and I had a crab cake sandwich, which was good and filled with crab, but I was yearning for a bite of hubby's burger. My youngest, who just got braces put on a week before and had mouth sores, had potato soup. He told me that I HAD to learn to make it. The fries were great. They were all we had left at the end of our meal and we packed them all into a styrofoam container and took them back to the hotel with us. Service was great. The waitress seemed taken with my younger son (I'm sure it had nothing to do with him playing to her sympathies by refusing to talk and answering with a simple thumbs up or thumbs down) and gave him some extra bread and butter to take back along with some extra soup. We're craving that burger... I just wish it weren't so expensive! ($8 for the burger, $400 for the plane ticket!)

text: This is not the worst hotel that I've ever been in, but I definitely won't be back to this one.
label: NEG

text: Service was horrid. We were only 1 of 4 tables that were full and service was still atrocious, attitude and all. The only thing worse than the service was the food. I'm sort of glad I went though, now I know where not to go next time I want Indian food.
label: NEG

text: Capas is amazing. I took a pair of faux snake-skin boots there and had him put on 7" of platform for use with a halloween costume. They not only survived 2 halloween parties, BUT also survived a night of dancing in a club. WELL DONE... inexpensive for the quality of work! WOULD HIGHLY RECOMMEND
label: POS

text: This is perhaps my favorite restaurant near Penn. It is run in a quasi-self-serve fashion. You first order and pay at the counter, and then your food is delivered to your table. As a result, there is no need to tip, and everything on the menu is between $6.50 and $9. The owners of the restaurant, Charley and Mike, are very friendly towards their frequent customers. The food is very high quality. To keep prices low, the menu is a bit heavier on rice and noodle dishes, although some meat-heavy dishes are available in the $8+ range. This is the type of casual place that I go to twice a week with my buddies. If you want a "formal" Korean restaurant where you will have to pay more, but receive more formal service, go to Hanwool instead. Given the tasty food and low prices, I go to Koreana far more often.
label: POS

text: This simple little joint knows how to make a damn good gyro. The place is small... only about 5 tables, so planning on take-out might be a good idea. I tried both the Gyro Supreme and the Doner Supreme. Both were very good. There isn't anything on the menu more than $6. I'll definately be back. A few negatives... The place was warm and I was looking to get out of the afternoon heat. An investment in a better A/C system would be nice. There was a TV in the corner of the room that was blaring. It was pretty distracting. The hours don't fit my schedule as they close at 7pm.
label: POS

text: I work right next door and what can I say.....I love it here. Come on, I mean, they have Big Buck Hunter and amazing outdoor patio areas. The bartenders are usually on top of it...it's a college area and can get super busy. I like that it's kind of a divey feeling bar. They also have munchies available and everything is reasonably price.
label: POS

text: Best Chinese food in our opinion, we eat here at least once a month. Best kung pao chicken ever!
label: POS

text: Shu's is great! No where else do they tell you to go out and run around the block in their brand new shoes until you are sure you are happy with them. They have a great selection, new exciting stuff like Newtons as well as the tried and true New Balance and Asics. Last time I was in I spent over an hour running in different shoes. I tried on over six pairs and ran outside in all of them. The sales people are great and never try to rush me into a decision. The return policy is awesome! If you aren't happy with your shoes, it's definitely not their fault. The only thing that would make it better would be a treadmill and some video gait analysis by the staff. They have a machine to step on to get an idea, but a true video analysis can be really helpful.
label: POS

text: Don't believe the hype concerning this place! I have eaten Mediterranean styled foods all over the nation, and this is probably one of the last places I would visit if Mediterranean was on the menu again. Service was spotty, the meal took forever, WAY too much grease from the veggies, it was almost stew like. I ordered the chicken kebab and it took close to 45 minutes (It was a Sunday afternoon, no one was there). I got halfway through the meal before I started feeling a little pit in my stomach. After all that, guess how much it was for the chicken and 2 drinks? $40, not including tip! PASS on this joint if you want Mediterranean, and head to the USF area for the real thing..
label: NEG

text: Staff was stuffy. Alligator gumbo was delicious. Salad had no flavor and dressing was watery. Very disappointing.
label: NEG

text: I stopped into City Planter this morning, hoping to find something unique to plant my herbs in. When I walked in the door, the woman working was helping a customer. She didn't even glance up, let alone say hello. I walked around the small store, alone, perused the paltry selection of large and small pottery. I found a piece I liked toward the back of the shop, near the desk. I turned around to ask the woman working about it, but barely got an "Excuse me?" out of my mouth before she rushed out from behind the desk to help the other customer. I stood there for a few minutes (I really liked the pot) and when she came back to grab something off of the desk I tried to get her attention again, but she ignored me for the third time. At this point, I had been in the store for fifteen minutes and she hadn't bothered to make eye contact. I walked out of the store with nothing, and reminded myself that someone always says hello at Ikea.
label: NEG

text: I'll have to help out the neighborhood eatery here as some of the Friday night specials have been outstanding. Last November, I had the New England seafood bowl which was a dozen or so clams and mussels, four humongous shrimp, four equally humongous scallops, parsleyed potatoes, corn on the cob and huge wedges of crispy garlic bread served in a bowl full of rich seafood broth AND... topped off with a half of a lobster for $21. I don't know how they made any money that night but such deals do exist. As for everyday fare, OK I guess.
label: POS

text: I first tried Credo Coffee when I arrived a bit early for the Saturday City Market and sipped slowly on a very nice soy latte. It was a bit busy, but I grabbed a seat facing 104 street before they filled up, and even found an outlet for my laptop (p.s. they have wifi!) They use Silk soymilk (or at least did on that occasion), and it seems to have a (in my opinion) nicer consistency than the one Starbucks uses after being frothed. Another plus is they are NICE. My barista was friendly and chatted with me while he made my drink. Just a great atmosphere all around, the interior colour scheme is very appealing. Modern and comfortable.
label: POS

text: This place is really nice! And you will learn things. You have the option of doing solo classes, signing up with a friend or more, or doing my personal fave - the couples classes. There are two types of classes offered: A. you just watch them cook and then eat. B. You get assigned one part of the dinner menu to cook and then eat. Often they have drinks to go along with the meals, and I don't mean water! Hot Damn!! You get sent home with the recipes for everything that was prepared in class and a coupon for a certain percentage off stuff in the store. Signing up for a class is a breeze (cheap it ain't but food is good), watching everyone cook can be entertaining in and of itself, and at the end its like having a big dinner party you don't have to clean up behind! We've done several classes now and will be going to another soon.
label: POS

text: I never really felt the need to review a 7-eleven store before, and I haven't really gone to too many of them. However, this one sort of amazed me. I remember when I was in middle school, I used to frequent the 7-eleven across the street all the time to get all kinds of goodies such as donuts and pastries and chips and hot foods that they offer/advertise. This 7-eleven barely had a microwave! There was such a lack of selection at this particular location that I was very surprised. I mean, I assume that other Reno, NV locations of 7-eleven must be better stocked since this one is sort of in a far side of town type deal ... but goodness. Don't try to find all your last minute things here because chances are, there won't be any!
label: NEG

text: Right around the corner from Bourbon st is this place. Our room was alright. The beds were comfortable and the bathroom looked remodled. Wished they had a vent in the bathroom but whateverm we only stayed for a night. The stairway smelled like piss, but what stairway doesn't? If you're looking for a place to crash while you get your party on, this place will do the job. If you're travelling with kids, I'd pass.
label: NEG

text: One word, Bland. I used to be a fan until I tried the other mexican places in the area. Yes they have variety but everything tastes the same. When i eat mexican food i expect the whole dish to taste great, the rice and beans at this place need a lot of work. which is weird because i thought those were the easiest to make. maybe Im being to picky but if Im going to pay $10 for a burrito i would want the rice and beans to be at least halfway decent and not make me sick. If you have a weak stomach do not go here!
label: NEG

text: 2 weeks ago we decided to try something new, it was a Wednesday evening and when we called ahead to see if we needed a reservation we were told "no", we asked if we should make a reservation, again, "no". We also asked what the dress was, we were told "some people like to dress up but you don't need a jacket and can wear whatever you want". So off to Chez Leon we went. While we got sat immediatley it took 20 minutes to receive a menu, another 10 for the bartender to bring our drinks and take our order. 45 minutes later we receive our appetizers, now I LOVE salt, honestly, but the Lobster Bisque was so salty that I could only handle a few bites. It then took another hour to receive our entrees. I ordered the filet mid-well, it came out completly raw (still cold) in the middle and horribly charred on the outside. The potatoes Au Gratin were ok, not my personal favorite, but nothing really wrong with them per se. In addition to this I found a hair in the potatoes. My boyfriend ordered the veal and it was very over cooked , very similar to a country-fried steak, breading and all. Then the dessert. I was really looking forward to dessert, my boyfriend ordered the creme brule, it literally had a spoonful of unmelted granulated sugar on on top, I ordered the chocolate cake ( a usual favorite dish for me) and it was sub par. I did pay with a groupon ($50 off) and still paid $80 out of pocket I felt completly ripped off. I was so angry with the entire situation I didn't eat the dinner at all and just went home and made myself a decent meal. Next time I want to spend that much time and money on a meal I will go back to Tony's. I will never go back to Chez Leon.
label: NEG

text: I've never been in the Louvre, but I almost went in once. I walked around it and looked at it. It scared me: How could I possibly conduct a meaningful visit, when there is so much to see and appreciate and my tiny mind has only so much space? Wouldn't it be worse to have a bad Louvre visit than not to visit the Louvre at all? Apply that riddle to the Shop Rite of Ewing, a MASSIVE grocery store with WAY TOO MUCH to take in during a visit or ten. Many times, when I leave the SR of E, I think hmm...isn't there another way to get a hold of these few grocery items without being bombarded by sign after sign after bloody sign, and TV after TV after cheery pubic address, and without walking around display after display of shit I don't need now, or ever??? Yes, this store has a very impressive collection of items for sale--usual and unusual produce, extensive deli, tons of meat, big selection of iced seafood, tons of chips, tons of cereal, all kinds of so-called "international" foods, a bakery, a Dunkin', a pharmacy, tons of housewares, and an ever-rotating, expansive set of "seasonal" offerings...but HOLY LORD CAN I JUST GET MY THINGS AND GET OUT OF HERE?? OK!! You win, Shop Rite of Ewing! You have it all! You are all things to all shoppers!! Now shut the hell up, turn off those TV screens, and show me the door! I hope that's not how the Louvre is.
label: NEG

text: Great place to go for food, tv, outside seating, late night eating, drinking...service is standard and simple. Menu has some great choices for food and drinks. Burgers are great and Crab/Artichoke sandwich is recommended. Bar and family seating are separate and also a patio is an option. Great beer and prices are what you'd expect from a brewery. Also open late, so go check it out.
label: POS

text: Ouyang House generated buzz around Nashville because it was the only dim sum spot in Nashville for a while. Sadly they no longer offer dim sum, or the Shanghai menu but the buffet is alive and kicking. It's a medium or slightly larger size buffet compared to other Chinese buffets in the area, but most of the difference is made up with things to keep picky kids happy like pizza and macaroni and cheese. Some of the food is reasonably fresh, but sadly the more authentic Chinese items seem like they have been sitting for hours. I guess this is why Nashville can't support a dim sum place either. Or maybe the people who like authentic food were scared off by the oddly loud (like hard to think loud) soft rock of the 80s and 90s muzak blasting in every corner of the restaurant. If you like to eat a lot and get the most bang for the buck, the lunch buffet is a good bet. If you seek quality or authentic ethnic food, keep looking.
label: NEG

text: Our first visit was great. It was a busy Friday night and they did their best to seat us promptly. We were initially going to sit on the patio, but once outside we changed our minds and the very nice hostess gladly found a table for us inside. Our server took a little while to greet us but once she did we never had to wait long for anything we needed. I ordered a Bacon Martini with their special in-house infused vodka for their Bacon Bloody Marys and the bartender was even nice enough to come to the table to confirm how I wanted it made since it was the first time someone had ordered it. My wife ordered wine from their well sized and fairly priced "wines by the glass" list. The burgers were tender and moist and the truffle fries and zucchini stick sides were delicious. We had some guests join us late and our waitress was quick to bring new menus and drinks for them. Will definitely be back.
label: POS

text: After taking my vehicle to a different establishment, they confirmed the ground cable issue, stating that the cable was only connected with a hand-tight bolt. The amount of money, stress and time that this debacle caused me was unacceptable.
label: NEG

text: The Good: My girlfriend's hamburger was apparently fantastic. The ambiance inside seems fine enough. The hostess was friendly. The Bad: The bubble tea reminded me more of Kool-Aid with tapioca than of a decent bubble tea. Steamed dumplings should not be cold (not cool). The waiter wasn't quite sure whether or not the dumplings were supposed to be warm; it took him five minutes to find out. Once he found out that, indeed, they aren't supposed to feel like they've been sitting inside a freezer for twenty minutes, it takes another ten or fifteen minutes for him to final return with reasonably-temperatured food. By that time, I have no time to eat them. All in all, a terrible experience. The waiter was clueless and generally ambivalent, the food quality left a lot to be desired, and we almost ran late for our lunch because of both factors. Save yourself the trouble: don't go here.
label: NEG

text: Oh man! I can't believe I didn't review this place right after I went there for the first time. That's right, I forgot that I passed out due to the awesomeness of their food... Go. Just go. Stop reading this and go. Bring a friend. Ditch a friend, go alone. It doesn't matter. If it's not open, then sit outside and wait. Go. The food here is great! I've never really tried crepes until my wife said the word so much that it conditioned me to think that I really wanted a crepe. And of course, she was right. I've been here a few times, and have tried something different each time. It has an assortment of items that will cater to any taste your palate is in the mood for. Fruity, meaty, sweet, and salty--they got it. The restaurant itself can get pretty full, and the line can get lengthy, but somehow, by the time you make it to the register to order, a table has opened up. However, plan on getting into a "table-poaching" frame of mind, and it doesn't hurt to have someone with you. (Tip: in the winter, I suggest you sit on the side of the restaurant that the door DOESN'T open into. Avoid the cold draft) The coffee is good, and the food is outstanding. The tables are cozy, but we didn't have trouble fitting four of us on to one round. Try not to go in there with too many bags or else you'll be in everyone's way... You're still reading this? GO!
label: POS

text: The bar service is absolutely horrific (on the restaurant side). It only took fifteen minutes to flag down the bartender to order the one beer they were out of. Then when I throw down a ten and a twenty for a nineteen dollar tab, don't give me the ten and a single back. Break the ten for me. I don't want to wait another fifteen minutes trying to get change to give you a tip for the terrible service.
label: NEG

text: I've attended yoga classes in Chicago, New Orleans and at Invoke in Indy. I have to say that Invoke has been the best overall experience. When I made the decision to become a certified instructor, I chose Invoke due to my prior experiences as a student at Invoke. I'm set to graduate from the first Invoke Yoga Teacher Training class next week. Throughout the program, Amy, Eric, Ahna and the rest of the Invoke family were very welcoming and helpful. If you are thinking about certification, I highly recommend checking out the Invoke Yoga Teacher Training program. As a student, I always look forward to attending the diverse classes from heated yoga to challenging vinyasa. For you guys that are thinking about attending a class, yes, there are guys that attend classes at Invoke. If you are new to Indy, visiting town for a few days or moving to Indianapolis, I highly recommend taking a class at Invoke. Cheers.
label: POS

text: This place is convenient to the theaters, but besides that there was nothing particularly special about it, and there are certainly many better restaurants in the immediate vicinity if you need somewhere for pre-theater dining. I actually went around 8PM (so after the pre-theater crowd) and besides one other couple, we were all alone in the restaurant....that should have been our first sign. The hostess was very nice, but she seated us at a table which seemed to be directly under an air conditioner, and it was freezing! They moved us to a warmer table when we asked, and were nice about it, but instead of pouring us new glasses of water at that table, they took away the empty glasses at that table, and brought over the ones from our first table - I thought it was a bit tacky. The bread they brought was very dry and tough as well as being plain white rolls- basically like someone left out some dinner rolls too long. We got the gnocchi for an appetizer, and there was nothing special about it. The pasta was a bit heavy, the sauce was too creamy, and it was VERY salty...basically the opposite of the way gnocchi is supposed to be (light and fluffy, never too salty). I got the chicken as my entree, and it somehow managed to come out both slightly underdone but also tough - not sure how that happened! The red pepper sauce was flavorful, but also much too creamy - almost an alfredo sauce rather than a juice, which certainly did not go well with the chicken. My boyfriend got the duck breast, which was also nothing special, and the pesto risotto (which sounded amazing and I was excited for) was also disappointing - no good flavor, just salty. Overall, I was disappointed - the service was maybe 3.5/5 (they were nice but nothing great) and the food was a 2/5. The atmosphere was also a 2/5 - the servers kept talking with one another at the bar right behind us, and the fact that there was only one other couple there kind of creeped me out. It was not a horrible experience, but definitely not a good/memorable one either - I would not come back.
label: NEG

text: Oh Standard Tappa Tappa Tappa... Thank you for making my visit to Philly so pleasantly blissful. Never have I seen better use of 1 inch galvanized pipe as I have in this place. Thank you Katie for making me a better liver as opposed to having one. Haven't tried the Squid, Buffalo, Monkey or whatever... But damn you make good fries.
label: POS

text: Worst Indian food in North America!!! On top of that, they trick you by saying that the food is from the villages of India. The cusine is same as any other Indian restaurant, but they are cheating people by claiming that it is from villages of India. Honestly, REALLY bad food, bad service, and they will clean next table to you with chemicals (with mist coming to you and in your food). Do not kill your vacation or stomach eating the so horrible food. There are perhaps 2-3 more options in SB area for Indian food.
label: NEG

text: Not counting the years I didn't live in Nashville after college, I have been going to Maryland Farms since the days of the Maryland Farms Country Club. Now, it is a YMCA. The YMCA at Maryland Farms is extremely spacious and houses some very nice perks. The free weight area (which I use the most) has 4 bench presses, 4 squat machines, a decline bench, an incline bench, a leg press (with 100lbs. weights available, which is nice not to have to stack like six 45lbs. weights to do a decent press), and a row. There are, of course, every imaginable weight machine available as well from chest fly to thigh machines. The dumbbell area has dumbbells ranging from 2.5lbs. to 120lbs. and there are plenty of chairs and adjustable benches upon which to do anything from preacher curls to shoulder presses to dumbbell bench (flat, decline, or incline). Needless to say the weights section has something for the first-timer and something for the meatheads. The cardio machine area has ellipticals, treadmills, two machines that simulate rollerblading/skating, stairsteps and the like. The machines are newer machines with touchscreen technology that allows for docking an iPod to watching any of 65+ channels of TV while you run/walk/skate your cardio away. The spin classes run solely in the mornings, so if you're into spin then you'd better be into working out in the AM. Spin classes have start times from 5:15AM every hour until 9:15AM. Additionally, there is a movie theater room where you can do cardio (again on the same machines mentioned in the previous paragraph) but watch a digital projector 101+inch screen of a movie that is listed. They post the family-friendly movies for the next week each month. There is an Olympic sized indoor swimming pool and 3 or 4 indoor tennis courts. There are two large pools with slides and such outside accompanied by even more outdoor tennis courts. It's like belonging to a country club without the country club dues... of course, there also is not a golf course. It's a great YMCA.
label: POS

text: Dual rooms. The room to the right is for the bands. Deep enough for the bass waves to carry & narrow enough to keep the energy up... I wish they would turn the base up & treble down. The back area is for 21 up w/ plenty of tables (even one for pool), but I was allowed to drink everywhere (few people this night). The sound of the band was actually the best sitting on the booths in the back because the highs was absorbed & the bass carried and was not cancaled out. Now to the redrum, sorry red room, the smaller room to the left was quieter and more for hanging out. They tried to play different music, but the speakers in the other room were not directional enough and the sound carried through the door or they did not have equivalent sound... I miss the Other World & Sanctuary. Sorry, they need to invest in different speakers or noise canceling speakers for better separation so they can have two draws or atleast a true break. I honestly got annoyed here. The speakers aimed back @ the band had good sound & carried to the other room- I would put up a sound asorbing curtain on that side of the stage & on the wall. Put some woofers under the middle part of the stage for bass on the dance floor... Try switching the polarity on one the woofer speakers... Hire a true sound engineer! SORRY, I am not an expert but even I could walk around & hear the problems. Saint Louis needs small music venues like this & I really liked the layout, bands & attitude- but this is about music which is sound.
label: NEG

text: Particularly horrible. This WOW location is under new management. Given the Uptown location, they decided to take a more Hoosters-esque approach. Same food, but skimpier outfits for the waitstaff. The music inside was so loud that I was getting a headache. Conversation was impossible even amongst ourselves at our booth. We asked our waitress to see if she could turn the music down, but when she asked the manager, nothing happened! Multiple requests made no difference. I wasn't asking for some easy listening music at a barely audible volume. I even understand the aesthetic they are going for [bar atmosphere], but the music was just too damn loud! I hope they provide hearing protection for the waitstaff because hearing loss is a very real possibility. Oh. I almost forgot. The food was crap too.
label: NEG

text: This was one of my worst dining experiences in Philly! The place was nearly empty, except for a few basketball fans at the bar, yet service was painfully slow. It took 20 minutes to get our drinks. There was one other table already there when we sat down--they were already finished and nearly out the door, making our table (of 2 people) the only other table in the entire restaurant. This is why I don't understand the slow service. In fact, it took over an hour before the staff cleared that table (in fact, it was still not reset by the time we left)! The food was nothing to write home about. I had read that they are known for their tater tots, but honestly, my elementary school cafeteria made them better. These were deep fried so they lacked flavor and texture. Wings were the highlight of the meal, but it was only the appetizer. I generally expect the main course to be the highlight (or at least the dessert!). At the end of our meal, we both declined water and beer refills several times, and after another 20 minutes I just said "so how long do we have to wait for our check" and wow, got the check! Be careful...sound carries well in this place ;-)
label: NEG

text: I will start by saying that I strongly dislike Bobby Flay. He seems like a cocky jerk and ever since he disrespected the Iron Chef by jumping on his table I just can't get behind him on a personal level. That said, I am a fan of his burger palace. The concept is refreshingly simple but offers plenty of unique options. The sweet potato fries are great and the medley of sauces is lots of fun to sample with fries, burger and fingers alike. The milkshake options looked amazing (add a shot of Kaluah?), though I maintained my willpower and chose to stare at other people's fatty ice blends rather than eat one myself. As for the burgers, the L.A. burger (with a turkey patty) is delish and I will have to be go back to systematically try them all. Luckily for my waistline, the closest one is more than 1500 miles away :)
label: POS

text: Johnny Brenda's is such a cool spot to catch a show. I agree with others who described it as a both intimate and spacious. The balcony is great and gives you a terrific view of the performance. I also appreciated the upstairs bar, which has the same draft list. No jostling downstairs to get to the main bar. Bathrooms are clean and big. They even have an old-timey photo strip machine, which is pretty awesome. Good, reasonably priced, seasonal draft list.
label: POS

text: Awesome location, right across from Rittenhouse Square! There is also a library nearby but don't let that stop you from browsing here. B&N is huge, has about 3 levels, 2nd floor cafe. I love the B&N Classics collection... a bargain! I don't have any complaints about this store. It is like Borders on Broad, but with the nice plus of being near the park. I really miss this place. I did have one creepy moment when I was in the computers section and there was a guy hiding back there reading an erotic novel and masturbating. I guess this isn't unlike walking around a library and catching people doing naughty things behind bookshelves, but that was the only time I was freaked out. So if you see a shady guy doing something like this, do what I failed to do and let an employee know!
label: POS

text: OMG! Their Char-Grilled Oysters were orgasmic! Drago's boasts having the Original Char-Grilled Oysters. Kudos for such an inventive dish! So delicious and large and buttery and cheesy and smokey! The bread was fresh and perfectly crusty and they serve just enough to sop up the wonderful juices left behind. This is my "must-eat" pick for New Orleans! Kudos Drago's!
label: POS

text: The first time I took Megabus from Philadelphia to New York, it was fabulous, both directions. A five star experience. It's been downhill since then. The ride itself is always fine-- the bus is clean, air conditioned, there's free wifi, the bathroom is useable. All good. So what's the problem? The second time, the bus was an hour late. Actually, I bailed after an hour and took a very expensive AMTRAK train because I was meeting people and had to get to NY. The third time, the bus was also an hour late. They had re-scheduled and never told the passengers. On the return trip, I called to confirm and found out that the bus from NYC had a) been re-scheduled and b) they'd moved the stop from way downtown to Penn Station. Good thing I called. Next time, I try Bolt.
label: NEG

text: Oh El Vez, why do you sometimes do me wrong? I'm pretty picky when it comes to Mexican - and El Vez is NOT the best Mexican in the city, but we all know that. (I'm not comparing it to the South Philly gems or anything.) It's what it is - a fun place to eat with awesome atmosphere. We don't exactly go here for authenticity. (If you want that, head to 9th Street...) My 3 beefs: $18 for guacamole. Really dudes? How did you think that would go down? I can get double the guac in South Philly for a third of the price. It's so over-priced it's ridiculous. Food is up and down. I've been 4 or 5 times with friends and the quality of the food fluctuates. The Mahi-Mahi tacos are always amazing, but everything else... eh? Last time we went, we were celebrating a friend's birthday. We ordered two pitchers of margaritas at over $30 a pop. Now, we weren't going out with the intention of getting trashed. But after 4 margaritas each and relatively empty stomachs we were barely tipsy. No - we weren't even buzzed. Again, we weren't at El Vez to get trashed, but the lack of alcohol in the drinks must have been substantial. I'll get buzzed off of one beer on an empty stomach! My likes: The atmosphere. For what it is, it's fun. And the photo booth? Classic. If they could reign in the guac prices, up the alcohol in the drinks, and have consistency with the food - I'd be all about this place. It's a shame really.
label: NEG

text: The chicken panang curry I had delivered last week was completely flavorless. It didn't taste bad, it just didn't taste like ANYTHING. It looked like panang curry I've had at other Thai places, but had absolutely no flavor. Very disappointing.
label: NEG

text: It's times like these that I wonder how I managed to score my boyfriend. For my birthday gift, he planned out an entire weekend just for the two of us, and Saturday began with lunch at Alma de Cuba. His family are fans of the Starr restaurants, and after my birthday dinner last year at Morimoto, I too have become a convert and the two of us are determined to try each and every Starr restaurant. A birthday lunch at Alma was therefore the perfect way to begin our day. The interior is really nice, modern decor with clean lines. My boyfriend preferred the warm lounge on the first floor, but I enjoyed the second floor's more light and airy feel. Our waiter was clearly new, but he was very nice and extremely attentive. The menu is fusion Cuban cuisine, and damn is it good! We didn't have drinks, but their mojito seems to be popular. We shared their ceviche sampler (which everyone should definitely try), that was a tasting of each of their ceviches: Vuelve La Vida: shrimp, scallops and calamari tossed in a an aji amarillo sauce with cherry tomatoes; Hamachi Tiradito: yellowtail with red onion, cilantro, lime juice and a touch of aji; and Ecuadorian Shrimp: shrimp with roasted tomatoes, chives, avocado and corn nuts. The ceviches were incredible, each one spiced perfectly to accompany the seafood, although I wish that the hamachi had a lighter sauce because I really couldn't taste the fish (which I personally prefer), only the lime juice. We also shared two entrees, a special halibut one with both smoked and grilled halibut over a salad of mesclun, yellow beets and cherry tomatoes, and a cuban-sounding dish that was spinach and cheese layered with plantains and wrapped with zucchini with tomato sauce on top, served over a black bean and pesto spread with an onion-jicama slaw. Damn, damn good, but the plantain dish was waaaay too heavy for me. The halibut was perfect (except for the fact that I don't care for smoked fish EVER), a nice light dish for the hot summer. We both loved the food, but unfortunately didn't have enough (or any) room for dessert, which just means that we'll have to go back again in the near future!!

text: Without a doubt, this is the absolutely best full-service car wash I have ever ever ever ever been to. My sister is from Los Angeles, and she is actually the one who discovered this place during her visit about 8 years ago. Thank you Sis! I owe you girl. Rather than pay $60 on up to detail your car, go here and buy the inside and outside wash for about $17. It's been a year since I did this, and must do it again because I'm ashamed of how filthy my car has gotten. (Did I actually write that?) First they lather up the exterior of your car by hand, using long soft brushes, and they scrub a bit to loosen the dirt. Next they run you through the auto wash which is like any auto-wash. After that two guys clean -- by hand, using soft cloths - everything the auto-wash failed to get. Usually they spend about 10 minutes rewashing my dirty dirty car. The main reason is that I live in the old SW which is graced or cursed (depending upon your perspective) by tons of tall trees 60-feet and larger that spread their mess around to maximum effect. Not only does my car get bombarded with tree sap, there's plenty of small tree debris (seeds and pollen) and dust that sticks to the sap like glue! Next it's on to the interior cleaning station. This area is staffed by 3-5 hardworking South of the Border types who vacuum and wash your entire interior. They don't shampoo the upholstery and rugs, but they do vacuum those. They wash every hard surface including the inside of your windows, your mirrors, your dashboard, all around your gearshift, etc... I stay right there with them because I have dark gray interior and it's easy to miss spots. And man or man, have I got spots. Lots and lots and lots of accidents happen to the inside of my car, plus, small bits of trash that I simply overlook. This part of my car wash takes this crew of workers 15-20 minutes to complete. So the whole wash is a 30-minute affair. I always tip between $5 - $7.50 since the workers devote a lot of time to my pigpen and are consistently cheerful about doing so. To make it possible for them to do the best job I like to empty out my car before going here. That's probably why I haven't gone in a while. I'm carting around a bunch of junk and keep forgetting to take it out. I've just gotta get back here and soon before I drown in the debris of my trash-mobile.

text: As Christopher has already mentioned, the chef/owner Mike Stolzfus was the sous chef at John Besh's Restaurant August; his fiance, and several of the waitstaff, come from Commander's Palace -- this understandably results in rather high expectations. Coquette did not disappoint. But they didn't hit the bull's eye, either. The building was completely redone since its last incarnation, and while -- if dropped inside blindfolded -- I'd never mistake it for a Parisian bistro, it DOES have that casual, welcoming atmosphere. A small restaurant (narrow and long), with a long wood bar along one side and tables on the other, it's bright without being glaring, intimate without being claustrophobic. There are also a few tables outside on Washington . . . The bar turns out good cocktails, and the wine list is small but well-selected, with "not your run-of-the-mill" choices and reasonable markups. Someone knows what they're doing. Our waiter was warm and friendly, striking just the right balance of casual service and attentiveness without being your new best friend. The Soft-Shell Crab I had for an appetizer was perfectly done, meaty, and flavorful. Lynn had the "Pickled" Shrimp (the restaurant's quotation marks, not mine) -- delicious shrimp in almost a beurre blanc sauce done with a bit of sourness (hence the "pickle"), while our friend Amy had a Bibb lettuce salad that was fresh and tasty. For our entrees, Amy had the Flat Iron Steak and Frites -- very well done! (No, the steak was medium-rare; the dish was very well executed, and absolutely delicious.) Lynn had the Cochon de Lait -- pulled baby pork on a bed of grits and greens; very rich, very tasty, and very, very good. I opted for the Pheasant "Coq au Vin" (again, the restaurant's quotes) -- perfectly cooked breast of pheasant, along with a roasted leg and thigh, mustard greens . . . outstanding! The best pheasant I've had in a long, long time. Dessert was a stunner! Their beignets, filled with a vanilla pastry creme and served with chocolate dipping sauce were amazing! The perfectly ripened strawberries were served with an elderberry zabaione were awesome . . . and the press pot coffee was rich and flavorful. Everything was a five out of five! So -- where did Coquette miss? Timing. Everything came out of the kitchen sooooooooooo fast -- it almost felt like we were "speed eating," rather than enjoying a relaxing meal in "the Big Easy." Now I can understand a restaurant turning their tables -- especially when there are people waiting to be seated. But we had 8:30 reservations, the restaurant was no more than half-full the entire time we were there, and no one was waiting for our table. Further, when we left, there were still a half a dozen other tables in use, so it wasn't like we were keeping the staff from going home for the night. Maybe it's a "Commander's Palace" thing ("we gotta turn the tables, got more people coming") and old habits die hard, but I've never felt rushed at Commander's. Maybe the kitchen was just in a hurry, and were firing the entrees as soon as the apps left the line . . . . I don't know. But it DID feel very fast paced -- more like grabbing a quick (but very delicious) lunch and needing to go back to the office, rather than a relaxed dinner with friends. That said, Coquette is firmly in our "restaurant rotation," and we plan on coming back in the future.

We stopped there mid afternoon and there were a few people in front of us and a constant stream of additional clients entering behind us. I ordered a slice of yellow cake with white icing - you buy it by the pound and it isn't cheap - about $9.00 per pound. The cake was good - dense like you expect for scratch made but still moist and flavourful. The icing wasn't very thick, but it was soft and suggary - so you didn't need much. Everyone in our party had a bite and everyone liked it. The husband opted for the chocolate chip cookie dough ice cream and the kids wanted strawberry, our friend ordered vanilla. They said the ice cream was made by Bassett's, which is a very nice change from the ever present Hershey ice cream you seem to find everywhere (at least in the Central PA area). Bassett's is a Philly ice cream company that has been around for over 100 years. When you taste their ice cream it's obvious why they've lasted so long. It's creamy, not icy. It has good, natural flavor - it doesn't taste artificial. Best of all, it's dense so you actually are paying for ice cream and not for air like you do with some brands. Overall, it was a nice experience. Again, not cheap but good.

text: Review is for parents of toddlers: OK, I'll admit, the city museum looks cool as heck. It looks like it was created by Tim Burton. If you have an older kid (older than 7) you'll be able to tire them out with no problem at all. However, if you have tiny kids, avoid the city museum for a few years. Seriously, it's just not worth it for little kids. We decided on a whim to go to the city museum. I knew it would be crazy but I was picturing crazy along the lines of Magic House. This was crazy along the lines of a zombie attack. We paid $5 to park which isn't bad. But then we saw the line to get in. Honestly if I'd seen that I probably wouldn't have bothered but we thought "Hey, we already paid for parking, let's give it a shot" and we got in line. The lovely dad in front of us decided to smoke a swisher sweet the whole way in. Because that's just awesome. I love smelling like cheap cigars on a hot summer day. About 15 minutes later we got inside and waited another 10 minutes. We paid $26 for two adults. And it was a madhouse. Screaming everywhere, kids running everywhere, crying, yelling, fights between siblings . . . Way too many people to even move. We opted to get some food and you practically had to kill someone to get a table. And the table and highchairs? Filthy. Just vomit-inducingly gross. Covered in wet spots and food. The family that had the table before us just left a pile of sopping napkins and a half eaten jalopeno. I got out some wipes and did what I could. We choked down some of the food and went to go find the toddler room which was bleh. A pit of dirty looking balls and a slide. There were a few other things but older kids were on them and acting like crazed beasts. Couldn't see their parents anywhere. My toddler was so freaked out by the noise and the rambunctious older kids that he didn't want to do anything except tentatively play with some old dirty wooden blocks for a bit. Then we tried to walk around as much as we could but the crowds of people everywhere made it impossible. We ended up leaving after an hour. I thought it was a complete waste of money for a toddler. Maybe we'll go back when he's 10 and he can enjoy everything more. But seriously, if you have a little bitty kid, avoid it. Go to the Magic House. You can barely get a stroller around anywhere and there is nothing at all for your kid to do and the older kids get super crazed everywhere. It's a fun day for older kids but a miserable experience for little ones.
label: NEG

text: You broke my heart, Dmitri's. I was a loyal and frequent lover who made no demands. In return, you always gave me a satisfying experience: consistently delicious, fresh and simply-prepared dishes. Perhaps you fell victim to your own success and spread yourself too thin. Maybe you got a new sugar daddy. Or it could be that you just got bored looking at the same four walls day after day, year after year. I understand. But clearly your love for me has faded. Your octopus, once plump and perfectly grilled, with the texture of lean, tender beef, now is limp, chewy and cold. Your fish, when available, is prepared with none of the care or love of years past. And your once-famous generosity, too, is nowhere to be found, your classic plain white plates dwarfing your once-ample portions. Saddest of all is your coterie. Oh, how your ladies-in-keeping-us-waiting have changed. Once energetic and full of the charm of knowing they were slinging the best hash around, the new breed seem sullen and annoyed, more interested in the intrigue of their court than the satiety of their courtiers. Alas, nothing lasts forever, nothing gold can stay. 'Tis better to have loved and lost, than never to have loved at all.

text: I used this vet out of desperation when I discovered that my guinea pigs, which are considered "exotic pets," could not be seen by 95% of the vets in the greater Philly area. I was told that Dr. Balzer had experience treating guinea pigs, so I brought them in. The first visit was for mites, a fairly common issue with guinea pigs. It should be noted that like most serious GP owners I have an extensive knowledge of their health issues and how to handle them. (A cursory googling of the facts I assert here will confirm them to be accurate.) Dr. Balzer was friendly but I was thrown off by two suspicious things. The first thing was, when I told her it was mites, she began looking through my arm hair to see if I had any. The type of mites that GP's get do not transfer to humans - under any circumstances. It seemed like something she should know. The other thing was that she said she had a guinea pig, and that it lived outside in a wood hutch. Guinea pigs that are not living in the wild should never live outside. The temperatures in even just the fall will kill them. She also asked me other things like if I was giving them Vitamin C drops (a very last resort way of getting it to them - you should always try to get it to them via frequent veggies.) All in all I was left feeling like this woman had only the most cursory idea of how to treat my animals, even though she did dose them with the proper medication (Ivermectin). I really hadn't intended to go back, but I did because I got into a desperate situation where one of my GP's was rapidly losing weight. When I brought him in, I had mentioned that there were two new GP's in the house (living in another pen altogether, with no interaction with the sick one.) Her conclusion was that he was not eating due to stress of the smell and awareness of new animals in the house. Now look. It's true, guinea pigs do weird stuff that makes them sick when they are afraid or stressed - they're just that stupid. But the idea that my GP would be wasting away over such a situation was just out of control ridiculous. But she wouldn't accept that something else might be wrong! Another shocking thing was how different her scale (one meant to weigh newborn babies) was from mine. It was a dramatic difference, enough to make me think my scale was broken or off. Some testing around made me certain that it wasn't - hers was just dead wrong. When dealing with a sick guinea pig, even an ounce of weight loss can be a sign of a serious issue. So to have her scale off by 6-7 ounces was not acceptable. You'll be happy to know that the GP in question, Cookie, is alive and well more than a year later. It turned out he had become anorexic because he didn't like the food I'd switched him to, and that ended up giving him scurvy. He is now the fattest GP I've ever seen. I discovered all this by taking a 2 hour bus to a proper farm animal hospital in New Jersey. The crowded waiting room that's the size of a thimble I could deal with, as well as the long wait and the first come first serve nature of their service. (If you get there in the morning and aren't one of the first 10ish to sign in, you will be turned away.) But Ms. Balzer clearly only has the most cursory familiarity with treating exotic animals, and I would not trust her with mine ever again.
label: NEG

text: Morimoto is definitely the best sushi on the East Coast! The quality and variety of fish was impressive versus other restaurants in this market, as most places can't afford to have everything in stock on a nightly basis. For those of you who are serious sushi eaters, don't even waste your time in the dining area and just take a seat at the sushi bar. The head chef will take care of you and If he catches on that you actually know what you're eating or talking about, he'll throw in some rare goodies that aren't on the menu for you to try. As was mentioned in a previous review, the wait staff are eager to clear your area and really add no value when interpreting the menu. They have their talk track down and they spit it out like a seasoned telemarketer! The beer list was a bit disappointing, as I was hoping they'd carry a wider variety of Japanese brews, but was filled with the basics and some Morimoto microbrews. The sake list was more of the same and they didn't offer a traditional bottle service where they will hold the bottle for you until your next visit. Overall I was extremely satisfied and pleased with the experience. With all the modernistic cuisine for the clientele who enjoy the fluff, it's the traditional fare that really blows you away! **Omakase is a waste of time for those of you who know what you want and like. Just be prepared to throw down anywhere from $150-300+ for your meal.

text: Philadelphia has a lot of gyms. Now more than ever there are new ones popping up ALL the time...there used to be a World Gym up on Sansom Street where now exists a bathhouse, and once upon a time, I worked there. This of course, meant that I also had a free membership AND since I was the opener on the weekends, I had a key and free reign to workout before or after hours. Still, I had a membership to 12th Street. WHY? Because it is THAT good. These days, one of the places I am employed offers a free membership to PSC Rodin. While this is a nice option to some stale periods in my workout life, I always end up back at my beloved Gayborhood haunt. I have also, in my poorer days, taken advantage of every free and trial membership in every gym in Philadelphia. And still, I remain here year after year. The Sporting Club, PSC, The Westin, Sweat...I will take my Gay Gym over these anyday. Why? Well, let me add up the elements here. 1. Cost. Their regularly running "specials" are low enough in price, and they offer different payment options for easier to hack dues. But their student discounts and special deals with local businesses are amazing. Their price among all gyms, up until recently, was THE LOWEST in the area. (then that $20 a month place opened up - but - no comparison there. 2: Amenities. The offerings here are awesome - Not that I take advantage of all the extras - like Basketball court, pool, dry/steam sauna, sundeck, TONS of classes at all different times (This has actually been steadily improving, too - more classes, different times and days...), A shake bar with many different protein powder options, as well as a bring your own powder option, which is only $2 to make a shake. You can heat up food in the micro, throw something in the fridge for a few hours (not storage, mind you - don't be a tool) Sit on the couches and watch the flat screen - It all feels like home to me. Maybe because I spend too much time there. 3. Maintenence of Facilities. You can actually SEE your membership dollars at work here. New equipment every seaason, speedy repairs on minor glitches, new snack/drink machines, and the cleanliness is unmatched. The only thing missing is the overbearing smell of bleach - because they use some really great solution of Fantastik for cleaning that I actually LIKE smelling... is that weird? I hope it's not weird... 4. Other members. So, I DID mention it's the gay gym, right? That being said, not ALL members are gay dudes. But the ratio is overwhelming and this, my friends, makes working out as a woman VERY VERY comfortable. One of the big issues being a young blonde is having to ignore stares and peacock behavior, and yes, even sometimes COMMENTS, from testosterone overflow. And it makes me want to turn inside out and run. Read: NOT MOTIVATIONAL. But the straight guys here are secure enough in themselves and insecure enough in avoiding the gay mojo that they stay to themselves. Which, really, is where they need to stay. 5. I COULD knock a star off for hours, but I won't. They are as good as any other gym in the city in that arena. Would I like extended hours on the weekends? Sure. But an 8 am opening ON Sat/Sun, and an 8 pm/7 pm closing time, respectively, is acceptable. They are 5:30 am til 11 most every other day (save Friday when they close at 10...Gotta get your party on earlier, right?) 6. Locker cost: Pretty cheap for a year or 6 months - of course the longer you rent one the cheaper, and I get to cram - I mean, store - half my life in one 12x12 cube. 7. Seven points? yes, we are up to 7 points here: The Camac Center in the back of the gym houses pretty much all you will ever need for your life. EVER. Massage, Hair salon, Esthetitian and laser skincare (you know - botox, bitches!), homeopathic services, a kids gym, and oh, who the hell knows what else is back there. Maybe Santaland and a lollipop tree. Next thing you know they will have housing available. 8. Last one - promise. Trainers - tons of them. Swim lessons. Boxing lessons. Freebies on a regular basis (once in awhile an announcement of "we have a few pairs of free theater tickets for this evening - first to come up to member services, gets 2 free tickets!" or free dinners/training sessions/guest passes with your membership, and promotions from local businesses stationed in the lobby. It's pretty great and ties you into a feeling of "community", which is probably the biggest draw for me at 12th Street Gym. I have tried to find better, my friends. I have been high and low - seen good things and bad things, even worked in places where I could have had it all. But I have been a member here for over 8 years. And I have no plans on changing that. Because really, gay gym boys are really really awesome eye candy. Just sayin'.
label: POS

text: Some say that breakfast is the most important meal of the day. I tend to disagree. For me lunch is by far the most important.
