text: Phenomenal seafood. This restaurant was recommended by a waiter we met in New Orleans; it's won several awards of "best seafood restaurant" in New Orleans over the last five years. My partner and I went here, even though he normally hates seafood (growing up in Wisconsin, he didn't necessarily get the best exposures as a child). The food was so good that he not only finished off two courses of fish and shellfish, but asked that we go back for our last night in NOLA. As many reviewers note, the lobster dumplings are incredible. They reminded me of cockles that I had at Tragaluz in Barcelona: luscious, umami essence of shellfish, but encased in delicate wonton wrappers. The oyster appetizer is made by heating oyster shells in in a rock salt base on an iron plate to about 400°, then sliding half a dozen oysters into them and whisking them sizzling to the table. One side is barely cooked, the whole is warmed without compromising the oysterish flavor, and they're served with a deceptively simple shallot migonette dipping sauce and lemon wedges. I hope that the oil spill has not compromised their supply; we were there during the weeks that they were tracking the progress of the spill towards the oyster beds. My partner had the redfish on a plank one night and the blackened swordfish the other; both were great renditions of classics. I had the butterfish one night, and a special the other. Both also excellent. The bread pudding was good. The wine list is extensive (and a nice price for the Conundrum), and the sommelier quite helpful. Service was great. Dinner comes with delightful freshly baked biscuits. Dress code in the main dining room ranges from dress casual to coat and tie; reservations are recommended for the main room, but we were able to get places at the bar as walk-ins the first night, and a table in the main room at 6 pm the second night. G W Finn is a splurge, but absolutely worth it.

text: I could go on for days about how much I like McGillin's. I have been coming here since coming of (legal drinking) age, going on seven years, and it still love each visit as much as the last. I'll go through some of the things McGillin's has going for it. First, great pub fare. My personal staple is the R.B. McGillin - roast beef, au jus, kaiser roll, horseradish - must I say more? Plus, it's not a massive meal, so I save plenty of room for the great local microbrews they have on tap. This brings me to the second (should be first) reason why McGillin's is so great, they always have a large selection of microbrews on tap, and at great prices. You'll find at least one variety of all the locals, Yards, PBC, Dogfish, Troegs, Flying Fish, etc. No question you'll find something to your liking. Finally, you can't talk about McGillin's without talking atmosphere. This is a pub's pub. The history of the place is a draw in its own right, it's practically a museum. From the photos on the walls, to the exposed beams, fireplace, and dark stained wood, McGillian's is a place that will make you want to stay for a while, or maybe all day / night. Also in its repertoire, McGillin's has a popular karaoke night on (last I checked) Wednesday and Friday and other specials throughout the week. They also throw some popular holiday events. St. Patty's Day, of course, New Year's Day, and my favorite, Oktoberfest which coincides with the Mid-town Village Festival. I could go on and on. McGillin's is a great place for nearly any occasion. It's a great place to watch the Phillies, soccer (if you're into that), and other sports. It can get very crowded in the evenings on the weekend, and nearly any other time for that matter. You never know when a crowd could amass at this popular, historic bar. My favorite time to go is on a weekend afternoon, preferably Saturday for lunch and a few (or many) beers. It's a great way to start your day, and see where the wind takes you from there. I once found an extra life out the side-door alley. McGillin's has a special place in my heart, and if you are talking best pubs in Philly, McGillin's, in my opinion, sits atop that list.

text: At dinner the other night with some publishing folks who regularly exhibit at the comic & popular culture conventions (ie: Comic-Con), "con-curry" was described as the odor resulting when the elevator doors are opened upon a bevy of character-dressed attendees who've roamed the convention for three days without a change of costume. Not terribly pleasant. Nevertheless, I think I'd prefer to inhale con-curry over the scent of artificial coconut layered on top of the many years of stale cigarette smoke which assaulted me every time I passed through the Circus Circus doors. I dreaded to return here each evening. My room was spared but the scent did permeate every public space of this Hotel. The semi-connected El Dorado and Silver Legacy hotels fare a bit better in the olfactory department, according to the testimony of fellow trade show exhibitors. Outside of Houston, the largest concentration of obese Americans is here at this Hotel. But Reno may beat out Houston in the overall aggregation of unhealthy + ugly people. I guess this isn't entirely Hotel management's fault. But the decor surely is. My room was furnished with two clown paintings, the most offensive (nightmare-inducing dismembered clown head in lower right corner) of which I covered with a poster that I tactically picked up on my second exhibition day of the library trade show. I didn't care for the burgundy and forest green color scheme of my room -- which blossomed to full effect in my polyester bed spread, but at least the room seemed clean everywhere but in the corners. (Hard to tell with the floor, though, because of the busy carpet.) The soaps and lotions were too perfumed but the bath bars were slightly redeemed for being equipped with massage nodules which were a nice touch in the truest sense. My only real room gripes were with the high pitched whine that emanated from some kind of poorly plugged hole in the bathroom wall, and with the absence of bathroom ventilation. (Hey, maybe the plugged hole IS the ventilation system?) I couldn't hear the high pitched whine from the bedroom but, then, I did close the bathroom door at night. Closing the door did not, however, obscure the sound of the pair having sex in the room next to me. I'm for less shared sound in Hotels in general, but overheard sex doesn't always have to be a two-star-deduction kind of sound. Nevertheless, hearing the woman's haggard *speaking* voice made it so; I'm positive I beat the dude she was with to the shower. So props to their morning circus circus antics for succeeding where my wake-up call failed: rousing me after my own late night. Be aware of added fees and required deposits: My room had been booked by my Company, in advance, so in order to place (even local) outgoing calls from my room I was required to leave a $30. deposit. And I was charged a $15. handling fee for the package sent to my attention at the Hotel. *The handling fee for this 32 pound box did not include the handling of it across the street to the free shuttle bus that transported guests to the convention center. This Hotel really did feel like one of the great equalizers, though, on the level of our nation's National Parks. And there's something to say for that. I don't normally enjoy small talk but I kind of enjoyed it here, via passings in the lobby and shared elevators. No such thing as hip here. And if you think you are, don't expect anyone to care or notice.
label: NEG

text: This is one of the better Starbucks around. It's busy and the area is nice also. It's conveniently located across the road from Grant MacEwan University which might make it a lot noisier and tough to find a seat once school is in session. It's a pleasant, spacious location with a good array of indoor and outdoor seating. Unfortunately the lot here is managed by Diamond Parking as well. I have only begun to deal with that. Watch for my review of Diamond Parking and North Town Mall. It should be obvious that you should keep an eye on your car for the parking Nazis. If you're going to be longer than two hours, you might want to find a better parking spot. I think I saw some free street parking. Busyness - This is a pretty busy location. It's fairly close to downtown and just across from Grant MacEwan University. I would imagine that it gets even busier once school's back in. Noisiness - There's a nice high ceiling that seems to absorb the noise reasonably well. The music isn't too loud either. Ambience - I've been coming to this Starbucks for a couple of years and I've always liked it. Power - It is available, but the window seats and tables in the centre have an issue. I'd bring an extension cord if you want to use some of the tables in the centre. Free wifi - Available and works well. Being one of those people who keeps a number of tabs open, you might want to login with a browser which you don't use often, otherwise each page becomes a login page, oddly enough. (In Firefox Windows 7 at least.) Staff - Always friendly and helpful. I've rarely had a complaint about a Starbucks employee. Seating - There are 28 seats in this Starbucks, with four armchairs and two good sized tables for laying out a bit of work. I like the square tables they have here. They're at a nice height and are quite roomy, compared to the dinky round cafe tables I normally see at Starbucks. There are four or five tables outside on the spacious patio. It's also bordered by some hedges to give it a bit of privacy. I don't know if they ever use the patio heaters. Security - When I first started coming to this location, there was a homeless camp in the empty lot nearby. It's gone now, but the Starbucks is close to downtown. Not too bad of an area but 107 Ave is close by. Take the usual precautions.

text: Nestled in the heart of Hyde Park, this coffee house is an absolute gem! text: My husband and I came here twice in the same week. We initially went to celebrate our 1-month anniversary, but were drawn back 2 days later by the ribs and bread pudding. After it changed ownership I went less, and now that's it's closed down I've been craving a place w/ good jazz, good food, and friendly staff. Le Cochon Noir has all this and more. Everyone we've met who works there seems excited and dedicated to the place's success. The chef came to our table and talked to us for a good 10 minutes! One of the waiters we had said he loves jazz and that most of the people who work there are doing it for the love of the music. And the manager (i can't believe I've forgotten his name) was excited to show us where the bar will be (they're getting their liquor license very very soon!!!), and to talk to us about the artisits, musicians, etc. Speaking of which, they display different art there, on a rotating basis. Right now there's some interesting photography dealing with everything from civil rights marches to smoky jazz performances in by-gone eras. Apparently the artist/art changes monthly, and they have various events scheduled to meet the artists and talk to them abou their work. I'm a vegetarian, and I left STUFFED each time I went. Their mac-n-cheese is outstanding, the parmesan potatoes are just right, the coffee was great, and the cinnamon raisin bread pudding was out of this world. They have several sides, each of which is huge. As for the meat, my husband (who's as avid a carnivore as they come) was talking about the rib sauce all weekend! text: I love burgers, I really do. Burgers and enchiladas are pretty much my favorite foods of all times. So I came to BBP with pretty high expectations(Though I'm not a fan or hater of Bobby Flay). The wait just to order was kind of ridiculous. At 8 o'clock on a Tuesday night I had to wait about 20 minutes just to order my food. As some others have mentioned they had ONE cashier on hand when I first came in. This despite the fact that there were 3 cash registers present. Things started speeding up a little once another guy came out and started handling orders. I put in my order for a Bobby Bleu Burger, medium with onion rings and a beer. I grabbed my order number and headed off to the dining area. The layout is kinda odd in that they have these wavy bendy counter tops and some straight tables. The only free spot was at the counter, so I sat down. My beer appeared within a minute of me sitting down. Nice. My onion rings came out a little while later. They were ok,but I have had better better beer battered onion rings. I couldn't really taste much beer, and they were a little greasy. On the plus side they were big and the breading was consistent and crispy. The burger came out a short while later and it was pretty big. Accompanying it was a nice thick pickle slice. The first thing I noticed was that there was a LOT of blue cheese. It was literally spilling melted bleu cheese out of the burger. But I like cheese, so that's allright. However, when I grasped the burger in my hand I noticed two things immediately. One, the blue cheese squirted out and covered my fingers. Not so nice. The second thing I noticed was a bright red spurt of blood into the blue cheese that had dripped off my burger. Hoping for the best, but fearing the worst, I took a decent bite. I stared into a blood red burger bite. The burger was still mooing, it was that frickin undercooked. I asked a waiter, when I could get ones attention, to have it cooked ,medium. I then got into a discussion with a waiter, who said "Medium is pink inside". To which I replied bluntly "I know. Medium doesn't have blood in it, which is what squirted out when I grabbed the burger". Finally we were able to work it out so they cooked a burger Medium Well. In fact it was just past medium with a little pink in the center, but that's fine. That's pretty much what I wanted. The second burger had a proper amount of blue cheese and the bacon was just as crisp and tasty as what was on the first. The bun/roll was allright, but it wasn't anything noteworthy. The space was nicely decorated and very well lit. For me it was a time warp back to the seventies. Why they decided on it, I don't know, but it worked. It was kind of loud in there. Between the noise of the people eating, the music playikng overhead, and the people in line it was hard to hear myself think. The bathrooms were unisex and there were enough that no one had to wait real long in line. The setup reminded me of Distrito for some reason. I really wasn't too impressed with the burger, though that Santa Fe burger looks tempting. To risk EHEC again, or not to risk EHEC? That is the question.

text: This is my FAVORITE natural history museum. Granted, I have not been to the big ones in the East, but this is truly a great place to visit. The first time I came here was with a college field trip in the spring of 1973. I have gone to Tuscon 2 times since to bring my 2 younger kids, the first time, then my wife, 2 kids and a grand daughter. It has gotten better every time. They have made a lot of improvements and additions over the years. As others have said, it is part zoo, part botanical garden and part natural history museum. They have a little bit of everything. Their landscape captures the essence of the Arizona-Sonora desert. You can come face to face with a mountain lion, gila monster, black bears, and the more unusual critters like the ringtails, and coatimundis and many more critters. The javelinas, although really smelly were the biggest hit for us. Plan to spend most of the day here. They have 2 restaurants on the museum grounds so you don't have to leave for lunch. I have not tried the Ocotillo Caf, but it looks like it would be good upscale restaurant. Dine in the Irownwood Terrace Restaurant, did I mention that they have great burgers? The menus are online at their website. They also have a great gift shop, so you can take home one of the non-smelly versions of a javelina. This is a don't miss place if you are in Tuscon. And we have traveled from the Seattle, WA area twice with the specific purpose of coming here.
label: POS

text: Name a restaurant where you may not get your appetizers until 2 hours after your reservation time. Survey says... Pearl - is the number one answer! The night started out on the wrong foot when our party of 4 waited over an hour to be seated, even with a reservation. We had to ask the hostess what was going on, and kept being told we were "next on the list". And then we'd see other parties being seated ahead of us. After about an hour they did comp us a round of drinks when it was clear we were getting upset, but it was a round none of us really wanted - we only took it b/c it was free and we were still waiting. I know it's restaurant week, and I know that means extra busy... but don't overbook your restaurant, don't wait til people get pissy before apologizing about the wait, and DON'T tell them they're next and then seat same-sized parties ahead of them. Don't lie to me. Then when we were finally seated, we waited nearly 30 minutes for our appetizers! A table that was sat after us even got their apps before we did. After we said something to the waitress and it was clear we weren't happy, the manager finally made his way over to us and asked what he could do to make our dining experience better. Sorry buddy, we don't want anymore drinks, we're already getting apps, entrees and dessert with restaurant week, and we've wasted 2 hours of our life that you can't give back. Note he didn't offer to take anything off of our bill. None of this was our waitress's fault (she was quite nice), and after the apps the rest of the food certainly came out quickly since they knew we were upset. The food itself was quite good too - duck spring roll was meaty and flavorful, black truffle scallops were tender, and cocoa pot de creme was thick and not too sweet. But I won't be going back since the management is so poor. Bottom line: the whole night was poorly managed by the restaurant, and we were so annoyed by the time the food arrived that we decided we won't be returning, no matter how good the food was. You may have a better experience, but I will take my business elsewhere.

text: Modo Mio was old worldy, minimalstic and very authentic. This is not some Italian joint on the corner, this place is the real deal true Italian straight from Nonna's kitchen! Our waiter Steve was A-M-A-Z-I-N-G. He gave wonderful suggestions, helpful insight to the menu and was very knowledgeable. Between the 4 of us we pretty much sampled 60% of the menu. We each ordered the "Tourista" menu which allowed us to try 4 courses. I had a crab and marscapone fritter situation which was out of this world. I wouldn't share it with anyone! My pasta dish was a homemade paparadelle primavera (my FAVE noodle) . It had zucchini, asparagus, rock shrimp and magic. It was delicious! My my main entree I went WAY out on a limb as per the waiters suggestion and went with the Veal Cheek, yes, cheek, Hannibal Lecter style! It was similar to short ribs and/or pot roast. The Veal Cheek was topped with a cherry compote. So the overall taste was about a 7, I didn't love the cherry. The cheek was interesting to say the least. I would want to try something different next time. There WILL be a next time! Desert was unique, I ordered the Lavendar Custard (not the name on the menu, but I can't remember what it was called). It was subtly different, satisfying and a really nice surprise. PLUS it's a BYO! After all that delicious goodness we didn't break the bank!

text: Do you want you taste buds to hate you? Then, eat at Jim's If this is "the place" to get a a true cheese steak, then I think I may hate cheese steak, which is news to me. I got a basic cheese steak with provolone and onions. The bread was good, but the meat was dry and lacked seasoning, the cheese was tasteless, the onions were too sweet from being cooked too long, and my whole sandwich was dripping in grease. Not to mention that the line was out the door, the food was overpriced, and they don't take credit card. In this day and age, if you aren't going to take credit card, you better have a damn great product - and Jim's doesn't. Having had a cheese steak place around the corner from me growing up in California and loving their food, I longed to get to Philly for a "true" cheese steak. I was told Jim's was the place and I thought the line out the door was a good sign, but I think Jim's is just a tourist trap for people who don't know better. I can't believe how let down I was by my cheese steak experience! If you want a good Philly cheese steak (which, ironically, looks exactly the same as Jim's but has one million times the taste), go to Philly's Best in California (Fountain Valley or Irvine). It is owned by a native from Philly, who specially buys their bread from Philadelphia. Philly's Best has a delicious cheese steak - well, unless, traditional Philly cheese steaks are supposed to be like Jim's; and in that case, they are supposed to be a tasteless, greasy mess that leaves your stomach and taste buds wondering why you hate them.

A fish plate came out which was raw and my lasagna had a horrible odor to it. Off the charts- BAD! I insisted they take them back. The odor was so bad that it lingered at the table for some time. The second dish of fish was cooked better although in the thickest part of it -still raw, and served in a broth that spread throughout the plate, something that wasn't there on the first plate. As I lifted my beer there were white things floating in the beer! At this point I was telling the waiter that we were upset and wanted to speak the owner. The owner wasn't available. My friend had finished most of his beer when he also realized there were white floaties in his beer as well!!! The manager made absolutely no effort to resolve the issue. At this point I told the manager that we refused to pay for this meal, and told them I would leave my business card and if the owner wanted to call me, I would discuss the issues with him in an effort to resolve the problem. Well today is Tuesday November 30th and I received a call from Luciano himself. First, he left a nice voice message and when I returned his call he was very abrupt -confirmed with me that I had indeed eaten in his restaurant and then cut me off and said that I committed fraud "Just to let you know there has been a police report filled out." It's interesting to note that bad service and bad food start at the top! I am a business owner and I can tell you first hand that if any of my customers complain out my products or services I listen carefully- it's an opportunity to learn something about my business- and to improve! This guy had no interest in that what-so-ever. He has permanently sealed the deal- I will never set foot in his establishment again! There are far too many excellent Italian restaurants in this town to put up with this for sure. ...and I'll be sure to tell my friends, family and associates the treatment we received.

text: If your out of town, reading yelp to find a good place to eat classic New Orleans (cajun food), come here instead of Acme. So you cant sample here, so I just got their most popular item, the Ferdi Special, which came with their house baked ham, roast beef, debri, and gravy (and I asked for extra gravy on the side - nods off to Adam Richmond). I also got the crawfish ettuffle since that was the only thing I did not get at the Acme Oyster House. OMG ettuffle is delicious. Not too salty, (which was a problem at Acme), it has a broth which probably has a ton of butter and flour (or some sort of thickener), the crawfish cooked delicately with the flavor of the sea from the crawfish influsing into the broth very distinctly. The crawfish was sweet, tender, and fell apart with minimal effort in your mouth. No tough overcooked crawfish here. The ettouffle comes served over white rice, which when you are paying $8.25 for a small cup seems kinda a cheap move. Why cant they give me a whole cup of ettoufle with a side of rice. There's also another meat, most likely a fish in it. Altogether, this is probably the best thing that I had in New Orleans so far. More than anything, this reminds me of a good thick clam chowder, except with crawfish instead of clams. The Ferdi Special was alright. The broth was kinda flavorless, and to be honest, the best part of the sandwich for me was the pickles and mustard, which was a good combination with the lightly salty meat and gravy. Correction, the best part is the free pepper oil on the side. It was absolutely awesome. Sweet, sour and spicy at the same time, I ended up killing my sandwich with it. Well the chicken and sausage.The jambalaya is a bit less salty than the jambalaya at Acme, it also has a bit more of a spicy kick to it. An interesting note is that the sausage here is sliced and the chicken is pulled. I feel that this is a bit better than the other way at Acme. The chicken stays tender and chewable, and the sausage (which naturally has more fat gives the jambalaya an additional component almost becoming a compliment to the dish rather than depending on the rice as a medium He jumbo however is better at Acme. The chicken in my jumbo is dry, and the jumbo just isn't as flavorful as the darker jumbo at Acme. There is also less meat in this jumbo. The soup is just thinner. It's not as salty or as spicy. Again, the sausage is sliced thick, but in this case, I like it better chopped up like at Acme. Overall, I would say that this place makes the Louisiana classics a lot better than Acme. So if you want good jambalaya, entouffe, or gumbo, come here. But dont get the Fergi special. its pretty overrated. sorry travel channel (and subsequently Man Vs Food)

text: It's been years - YEARS - since I last went apple picking. Thankfully, my bf's cousin has a little 2 year old boy who is the perfect excuse for me, my bf and his parents to go apple and pumpkin picking together. For years they had gone to Linvilla Orchards so that was the obvious choice, and only 30 minutes away from CC Philadelphia! We opted to arrive in the morning, which turned out to be the best idea ever since the high temperature ended up being near 80 F on a bright, sunny day. We parked in the shade (SCORE!) and immediately walked over to the orchards. They designate which rows are what variety, and you wander up and down picking apples, dropping them into the cardboard box, and occasionally eating them, before paying by weight. We then walked over to where all the pumpkin varieties are - sadly not a literal pick your own pumpkin since the orchard staff already picked them and piled them into crates by variety. But you still get to choose which ones you want, and boy do they have ALOT of different pumpkins. Was very tempted by their peanut pumpkins but our tiny apartment can't contain that level of awesomeness...YET. They have a HUGE amount of family activities, such as the non-scary hayride and tour of the orchard, and other games and things like face painting that kids love. We quickly hit up their store, too, for things like honey, cider doughnuts, and pies (although there is far FAR more stuff there than that, like dairy products, produce, and pantry items), before opting to leave since naptime was fast approaching and we didn't care for the available food stands as a lunch choice. All in all, a very fun experience for the younger crowd, although a bit hectic and crazy for us adults. Definitely go in the morning, especially since by the time we pulled out there was a long line of traffic just to get into parking for the orchard.

text: The minimalistic decor might lead you to believe that this is a down-to-earth, friendly yet upscale sushi restaurant. After taking our order, the server went in the back and came out moments later to tell us that the sushi platter is "just for one person." I know what I ordered, thank you very much. Bad move on his part. The servers and the sushi chef unceremoniously spent the rest of our meal talking about us within earshot. I would have forgiven them if the sushi was any good. text: I saw Jersey Mike's in Nashville when I moved here last year, and had it on my list of places to check out. I'm originally from South Jersey and grew up eating proper hoagies with quality lunch meat, freshly sliced, on a soft fresh roll with lettuce, tomatoes, onion, peppers, and oil and vinegar with spices. I love me a proper hoagie. Since there's no Jersey Mike's near me, I've been going to Subway and trying to figure out how to get a sandwich that tastes that good, and I'm always disappointed. No, I don't want it heated. No, I don't want mayo or mustard, and yes, I asked you to put the oil and vinegar right on the bread. I'm always disappointed but at least it's cheap. So today I stopped in to Jersey Mike's and was surprised to see the meat being sliced fresh for sandwiches, and that "Jersey Mike style" means lettuce, tomatoes and oil and vinegar. The meat was quality, and the cheese was actual cheese (Subway, do you really think that we believe those little half-circles are actual provolone cheese? I think not.) I got the Italian. They told me the bread dough is actually made in NJ and baked on premises. It tasted great. That was one awesome sandwich. Now, if they only had Tastycakes, and I could top off my meal with a jelly krimpet, it would be perfect. I'm going to promise myself that when I crave a hoagie, I'll take the time to drive to Jersey Mike's and get a proper one.

They have hand rolls but no sushi or sashimi, when I inquired as to why this was "we do not want to compete with our other restaurant Teikoku" was the reply. Margaret Kuo has two restaurants in media (one on state st. and one in the Granite Run mall) less that three miles apart, yet Azie feels they will dilute the brand if the open a restaurant serving sushi and sashimi within 10 miles of their Newtown Square restaurant, give me a break! text: Carmax, you really need to do something about your supply chain. I don't know what the deal is but you need to get it fixed! Last Friday while I was waiting in the waiting room for my battery to be replaced, I overheard one of the service technicians apologize to a customer who was there to have her headlamp replaced. Apparently according to him, the wrong lamp was in the box. They were very sorry, but they'd have to reorder the part and call her when it was ready. I thought this was strange, but working in the service business I know there are disappointments. I myself was waiting on the arm assembly for my Windshield Wipers, but that part wasn't supposed to be in for a few business days. Flash Forward to this morning. I receive a call from TaTa saying that my Wiper Assembly has arrived and when would I like to schedule an appointment. As soon as possible was the best option, since driving a car in the rain without windshield wipers is very very difficult. So I arrive for my promised one hour wait. While I'm waiting, I overhear ANOTHER man talking to one of the service technicians about a part HE was waiting for being the incorrect part, and that they would have to re-order. I couldn't overhear the part this time, but he was visibly disappointed. What is going on I wonder to myself. But surely *I* will be okay. Right? Wrong. After almost an hour, I see the flash of my car out of the corner of my eye. Excited to finally be on my way, I head into the service area to pay. I notice that TaTa is saying something to me. Some word that I can't exactly make out. "Have to Reorder" and "Alternator" "Wait.. What?" "I'm sorry Mr. O, but we got the wrong part.. We received an Alternator instead of the wiper assembly.. We'll have to reorder and I'll call you when its in" ??? Now, if this had JUST happened to me, I'd be upset. But KNOWING that there are two OTHER victims of this same sort of problem in just a few days.. I really think Carmax Nashville has some kind of problem! Now, to be fair, and for the sake of full disclosure TaTa said they would cover half the cost of the labor, and half the cost of the part. I still find myself frustrated and amazed with all the hoops people are apparently having to jump through over there.

text: God, where do I begin to list the problems? I believe I'll go with a modified bullet-point system. - Complimentary salsa, but no chips?! What the hell is this?! text: Oh, man.. This place is awesome. I am a fan of Oriental food and this place shows off some amazingly good Thai cuisine. The outside of the business does not reflect how nice it is inside. It's one part of a strip of small businesses that all seem to be "hole in the wall" kind of places. Once you step in, though, you're immediately greeted by a very kind wait staff that ask you to sit anywhere you'd like. You'll notice how small the place is, but the style and decor makes this an authentic Thai experience; it's a very quaint and comfy place to be. *My review of the food is based solely on the lunch specials* Being a 19 year old student, working at a dead end job, taking my mother out to Thai Orchid for a nice lunch doesn't have me feeling like I just burned a hole through my wallet, once the bill comes. Seriously, the lunch specials are offered at a very reasonable low price! The kind waiter brings us water in nice stemmed glasses and comes back a bit later to take our order. My mother orders shrimp Pad Thai and I order the Pa-Nang curry and a Thai iced tea. The waiter leaves and comes back momentarily with a nice cup of chicken and rice soup and a rangoon of some sort, that is served with lunch orders, for each of us. It's a nice small serving of each that is not at all filling, but keeps you content as you wait for the main course. The Thai iced tea here is really awesome. Thai iced tea isn't anything like a regular iced tea so I'd definitely recommend giving it a try, unless you're not into sweeter things. It is some kind of tea that has a layer of sweetened condensed milk on top. After I stir that baby up, I'll empty the glass in record time. Once our food is served I stare at it, just a bit, to marvel at how much of a generous portion is given. The Pa-Nang curry doesn't disappoint. It has the right amount of spice and goes so well with the chicken, vegetables, and side of rice. My mom and I always swap plates halfway through to sample the other person's stuff. The Pad Thai rocks. Can't say much else; it just rocks. Period. By the end of our meal I'm feeling good and full. The waiter drops off our checks and thanks us for choosing their place to eat at. I take a look at the cost of this wondrous meal; $19.75. This brings a smile to my face and to my wallet. In all, this place is great to meet up with or take someone for a nice cheap lunch. What you get here is amazingly authentic Thai food with a nice comfy atmosphere and kind wait staff. Give this place a shot. *To get a look at the food we ate, take a look at the photos for this place. Looks good, eh?*

text: Went to dinner with my dad/sister, excited for some Italian food (we generally go out and eat Chinese...I know cliche!). Came here hearing how good it was. Got here, the ambiance is nice, everyone seems to be having a good time (but quiet). Get seated, and looked over the menu. There isn't a wide selection, but it's fine for a small type place. I ordered the mussels for an app, and the branzino for entree - I'm not usually a seafood eater, but my sister was saying how good branzino is, as she had it twice this week! I said, sure! She knows I don't like fish, but said I should give it a shot. The mussels were underwhelming. It unshelled and in a tomato soup like base. Again, I'm not a seafood guru, but I've eaten mussels before where I enjoyed them, this I just ate like it was cereal. Warm, tomato soup cereal where the corn flakes are mussels. The branzino came out - pretty good portion, I got 2 filets, 3 slices of potato, and some spinach. The spinach was awesome, if I had a plate of that I would've been happy. The potatoes were ok, tasted like a potato. The branzino tasted like nothing - maybe that's what it is supposed to taste like? Not sure, but it felt like I was eating fish without any flavor. Not being a fish fan, I guess that's ok...but what am I paying for? My dad/sister got the 3 course - (2 choices of app, 2 choices of entree, full dessert menu) for $30, which isn't bad - it's like restaurant week here (but only Tues-Thurs). I didn't have their salad/entree, but ate some of the tiramisu. Ok, I ate it all. But it was good. Looks diff than your average tiramisu, but still tasted good. A bit stronger on the kahlua flavor, but I was definitely ok with that. The service was professional. Not friendly, not mean, professional. Overall, it was an ok time. I wish I got the pasta, but no regrets. I can't say I'll give this place another shot unless someone else mentions to go there. It is a byob, so that's good. Maybe getting wasted will make it yummier. In summation, meh, I've experienced better. I also do not think this place is $$, it is $$$. Each app runs $8-9, entree runs $19-$27. For 3 people, 2 prix fixe, 1 app/entree costs $100+, fyi.

text: Oh, 50 Flowers. So I'd read a lot online about DIYing wedding flowers, and that 50Flowers' prices were really great. My now sister-in-law wasn't too jazzed about using flowers as centerpieces at her wedding, but my Mom was pretty intent on having at least SOMETHING on the tables. So we settled on getting a load of premium gerber daisies ordered from 50flowers.com and would just put 5 stems in each table's vase for some color. We ordered some white ones and some tinted green ones. I'm talking like, 4 months in advance. We followed all of their directions--Ordered for Thursday delivery for their Saturday wedding. So you can imagine our surprise when my Mom received the flowers that Thursday before the wedding. And there were white daisies and RED DAISIES. Not a green one in sight. Yeah. Not what we ordered. Especially when we're wearing KELLY GREEN BRIDESMAID DRESSES and all accents at the wedding were kelly green. Red. OMG. HELLO CHRISTMAS. Now most brides would have lost their mind, and 50Flowers was lucky that I was NOT the bride in this instance. I called them immediately and let them know what we received. They told me they'd been waiting for my call, as the bride who HAD received my green daisies had already called them. They didn't know WHO received her red ones. Turned out it was me. So yeah. TWO unhappy customers right there. Apparently they can't get the right flowers in the right boxes. I was then told that there wasn't any way we could get the correct green daisies by Saturday. Something about them needing time to tint. Great. She told me she could get me some more white ones, though. I opted not to. Frankly, I didn't want to end up in the same scenario on the day of the wedding. I asked for a full refund for all of the green daisies we never received. They obliged and said the refund would process to my credit card within 3-5 business days. That's when I got on the phone with some other awesome local flower shops, told them my scenario, and decided to order some daisies from them. Visser's Florist in Anaheim saved my day--getting me 75 AWESOME white gerber daisies the next morning for just 10 cents more per stem. But let's talk about the quality of the daisies we received from 50Flowers. This was the ONE thing I was worried about. Their pictures are awesome. And then the packaging was seemingly awesome, too. Each daisy came with a plastic stem holder, along with some netting around each flower, so the petals wouldn't break or fall off. We immediately put the daisies in water when we received them. Kept them inside, out of the sun, and changed their water the next morning to keep the bacteria out. The flower seemed small for a gerber--probably about 3.5 inches? When I think of "premium" (which is what they called these), this isn't what I picture. Saturday rolled around, and the white daisies looked AWFUL. Especially compared to the 75 white daisies I'd ordered from Visser's. They looked tiny (the ones from Visser's were at least 5 inches diameter--some bigger), and were completely wilting. Comparatively, they weren't even in the same league as the daisies I'd gotten from Visser's. We truly didn't know what to do with them. We used them in some of the smaller vases, but they ended up being a big waste, since we had to toss so many of them because they either lost tons of petals or were drooping to the point of no return. For some bizarre reason, the red daisies held up much better. Not that that helped us, since we had no use for them. They sat at my Mom's house in a vase. It's now been 10 days since I've asked for my refund (8 business days) and I still don't see it processed to my credit card statement. I e-mailed their customer service dept. about this on Friday, but still haven't heard back. I'll be checking everyday, and will be disputing it with my credit card company if they don't get it processed this week. I'll update about that when it happens. Definitely wouldn't recommend them. This isn't the sort of stress a bride wants to deal with two days before her wedding. Their nonchalant attitude was pretty offputting as well. I understand that quality sometimes differs from flower to flower, but sending you the wrong thing just isn't acceptable. ETA: Just wanted to update about my refund to my credit card. They sent me an e-mail regarding the refund on Monday, August 30, however, it didn't post to my account until Wednesday, September 1. I'm assuming that's how long it takes a refund to post, but I received the wrong flowers on August 19th. Seems like an awful long time to hold onto someone's money, especially when there was never even a dispute about what had happened.
label: NEG

text: I live right around the corner from this little spot. I would still come here for sushi. The sushi is consistently pretty darn good. And they have some inventive specialty rolls. However the real star is the price. You can fill up on delicious sushi for what 2 rolls cost at most places. It is not the kind of place I would go with a sushi snob, but for being right around the corner, I am all about it.If you find yourself in Pennsport looking for a sushi fix, look no further (not that there is anywhere else to go!). Last night I had the Philly roll, spicy tuna, Christine (Eel, Spicy Tuna, Avocado, rolled in tempura sprinkles and covered in roe), Dynamite roll (Crab, Salmon and asparagus, deep fried), and Cali roll I believe. The specialty rolls were really good, and all of them were above average. And the bill was $30. We brought our own Sake, and they heated it up for us. Very polite and great service. They also infuse their water with lemon, which is a very refreshing twist when eating their fresh sushi. I am not sure if they sell alcohol, it appears other people have gotten beer and sake there. But we brought a bottle of organic sake and they did not charge any corkage and graciously heated it for us. Our fellow diner was vegan and he loved the miso, asparagus roll, and tofu General Tso's. I tried the Tso's and it was really quite tasty. If you are into that sort of thing. We were all very content, and the wallet was left intact. I will certainly be back. One word of advice. I ordered delivery from there a while back. It was just your average run of the mill crappy Chinese. I was not impressed. As a side note, does anyone know anywhere that has some really good Chinese delivery in South Philly?
label: POS

text: I feel I should like this place more. I love Mediterranean food. The place is in the proper spot for great food. They have a lunch buffet. All the stars are aligned but the quality of the food didn't do it for me. The only thing that was good were the deserts and I can't justify going back to pay $10 for something sweet. I've only been once so it could've just been an off day but, with my list of favorite spots to go and other spots to try, a bad first impression can kill a place for me. Maybe if I try the place again I will go for dinner but I think it would take some convincing from someone.

text: Consistently delicious. Only about 5 vegetarian items on the menu but they are all well worth having. The meat dishes (especially the fajitas) look and smell amazing. Recommended: Vegetarian burrito, Vegetarian nachos, Vegetable Enchiladas, Potato stuffed taquitos (read menu carefully, you can get this stuffed with chicken OR potatoes), Several choices of quesadillas. The entrees come with lettuce and pico de gallo, refried beans and some with rice too. The quesadillas are good as an appetizer but not as an entree because they do not come with all of these side dishes. The free chips are fresh and delicious with two salsas that I like to pour all over my meal. Service is good.

Even though I'm not up on the most current Disney movies, they have stuff from my favorite childhood Disney movies like The Little Mermaid and The Lion King. And this is a great place to grab a gift foe the little ones in your life. I don't think there is a little girl alive that would not love to put on a Disney princess dress and dance around the house . Heck, I'm an adult and I would love to do that (they don't have my size though)! It's a good place for gifts for the kids and it's a fun experience for adults to relive a bit of their childhood too.

text: I think this is the third time i've been here with my coworkers and always love the service and food.. For appetizers, we ordered a couple items (seared tiger shrimp, crunchy golden lobster potstickers, wood grilled szechwan spiced baby back ribs, and I believe the sunrise at haleakala roll). The potsticker was very delicious, a little on the salty side. The pork on the ribs fell right off the meat and the wet rub that was glazed on the pork was out-of-this-world. The sunrise at haleakala roll is also something I would go for again, the fish was very fresh and cannot really be explained in words. You just have to try it out if you're a sushi fan. I think the only thing I would probably avoid is the Tiger Shrmip as it is your usual large-sized shrimp with cocktail sauce. For my entree, I ordered Roy's Original Hawaiian Blackened Island Ahi, and all I can say is that it was unbelievable! You have to order this rare as this is the only way to eat it. You will not regret. The Spicy Soy Mustard Butter Sauce compliments with the Ahi so well. Service is great here. The waiter and waitress always made sure our glasses of wine and water were filled and were very attentive. I think I wound up drinking 6-7 glasses of wine myself because my glass was always filled. Hawaiian Fusion usually isn't my thing but this is definitely a place I am looking forward to returning back to.

The service is always good. They serve you complimentary soup. They give you the most sushi for your dollar. My personal favorite rolls include the Asparagus Tempura (SO YUMMY), the Avocado Sushi pieces (topped with a creamy, slightly spicy sesame sauce), the Tamago Sushi, and my favorite starter, besides edamame, is the cold broccoli salad, which comes with what I think may be a wasabi ranch dipping sauce. I could eat there everyday if I could afford my sushi addiction. Now, whenever I got out to say, Sake, Hoshun, or Kyoto, I always find myself sad that I'm not at Sushi Brothers instead. Would I go there again? Hell, yes. I'll go right now, actually.

text: Let's be honest. Nico's is not fine dining. It's actually not dining at all. You go there to order, eat and go. That's it. End of story. So the story I want to tell is about a burrito. The burrito was filled with fresh potatoes, scrambled eggs and melted cheddar, all cooked up together on the grill and wrapped up like a yummy blanket'o'breakfast. Now, I was introduced to said burrito early one Saturday morning around 8am. It was love at first you-know-what. This baby was served piping hot with a side of Nico's standard little cup of hot sauce. (When was the last time you had to actually wait for a meal to cool down before you could enjoy it? It was that hot and has consistently been so every time I've been back.) All told? Nico's is fast, excellent, any-time-of-the-day-or-night fare. I would have given it the full five stars, but hey, you don't go there to dine. You go there to order, eat and go. That's it. End of story.

text: We have eaten here many times over the years. Mirama is not in the main Chinatown area - but in the East Jasper Ave Chinatown area. Dim Sum items can be hit or miss here but the price point is good. Many Chinese eat here because of the price point, style of dim sum and it is large and accommodating. There are many better Dim Sum places but all more money. We prefer Century Restaurant Dim Sum but today were are budget minded. Here is what we are eating this Saturday at 11:45 (in the pictures). Spring Rolls: but these contain no vegetables and really ground mushy pork only. The best thing about them as they are hot and deep fired. Shrimp Steamed Dumplings: These were very good, pieces of shrimp, chives, and assorted mystery items. Sticky Rice: Good but have had better at other places. Deep Fried Squid: very good, considering the size and thickness, they could have cut these into thinner prices. Crab Balls: deep fried with coconut, OK but nothing special. There was a small crab claw in each one, from a small snow crab and contained no meat. Total meal for 5 items with tip and tax $22.76. Normally we have eaten 2-3 more items, however we had early dinner plans so stopped at 5 items. We would rate this place: Quality of Dim Sum: 5/10, Variety of Dim Sum: 7/10, Atmosphere: 5/10, Cleanliness: 5/10 (chipped plates all over our table and serving dishes) Service: 7/10 (for its trolley servers etc.) Parking: 4/10. Hit and miss. If you are new to dim sum or looking for a good dim sum: try Century downtown Chinatown, Jumbo in the Westend or Golden Rice Bowl on the Southside - all better in every category.
label: NEG

text: I used to think Whole Foods was a great place, and now I see that it's crap. It's overpriced, and it's a racket. As many of you know (and probably choose to ignore the fact and keep shopping there anyway) it's run by a Republican/Libertarian who stated very clearly that the right to basic necessities "has never existed in America" according to the constitution. As a friend of mine put it, "that's what @#$%ing amendments are for." Whole Foods is a large corporation bent on growth and even people who complain about the prices and whatever else will still shop there because they think they have to go to a traditional, "normal" grocery store to buy their food. They have a lot of good stuff but who cares? Stop being so lazy and start shopping at multiple places: Reading Terminal (that's one-stop shopping actually), the Italian Market, smaller local grocers, Latin and Asian grocers, and of course farmers' markets. I get my organic dairy at Acme. Suck it, Whole Foods. Since moving to Philly I've been there once, because I really, really wanted heirloom tomatoes. I bought those, some not-so-fresh concord grapes for twice the price I got them at the little weekly farmers' market at 11th/Tasker, and a couple other things, and I don't remember the exact amount I spent but it was just way too much. If you want to complain about the staff (I've never had a problem myself), take note of the fact that Whole Foods pays low wages and probably has an extremely high turnover rate. Look at the posting for jobs on their website. They have a laundry list of what they want employees to do, including providing "delightful" customer service. At corporations where they want to create a whole brand or image employees are subjected to all kinds of crap, not the least of which is "forced kindness." Something that used to be human--giving a customer advice, selling them food--is encapsulated into a set of objectives that uses specific terminology and procedures. Asking everyone if they have a bag (even when they clearly don't) is an example of that. It reminds me of when I worked at Target back in the day and they had us all refer to customers as "guests," and as a cashier I was instructed by my supervisor to "schmooze the guest." I also had to ask people to sign up for the Target credit card. How can any self-respecting individual not be surly in that kind of work environment, where all their bosses are surely tools? I guess I can see wanting to shop here if you lived really, really close, but otherwise skip it.
label: NEG

text: This used to be my favorite Vietnamese restaurant in town, but has recently been replaced by Saigon 88 (in Sparks). But don't get me wrong, this place is still great! If I am near the University, I wouldn't hesistate to go to Golden Flower over Saigon 88 any day. The spring rolls... manna from heaven. Perfect combination of beef, shrimp, noodles, lettuce, and crack-cocaine (I kid, I kid... but it's that addictive) dipped in the peanut sauce sounds like home to me. Two ginormous spring rolls are too big for one person if you are going to get it as an appetizer (it could be a meal on its own). Be nice and split it with a friend - you'll have to save some room for the main course. Though I would prefer the pho (noodle soup) at Saigon (the soup base is better), no one quite makes the cold noodles (I usually go all out with the bbq pork, shrimp, & imperial rolls) like Golden Flower does. I usually ask for extra sauce. Mix it in. Devour. I haven't been too adventurous with other items on the menu, mostly because the cold noodle is gold noodle in my books, but I usually make envious glances at other people's food as the server brings them out. Which leads me to... Not the best service on earth. The lady that usually serves us has never smile (and I've been there countless times). But the food comes out at an uncanny speed, and they get what need to be done done. Parking is plentiful. The decor is unimpressive but not hideous. I wish they were open late night. The noodles would be great hangover food...

text: I'm sorry to say, something has changed here, and not for the better. The first sign was through the reservation process - don't bother with the website since they can't seem to handle that. But I didn't have many choices and I remembered this place being good. Waiter was nice, restaurant was more than half empty - all the way through the meal. Got a good wine (Blair Fox syrah). Appetizers, amuse bouche, and sorbet were all fine. Sorbet, even, was good. Entrees were all - ALL - uniformly overcooked. My scallops were tough, the Ahi was cooked all the way through (so far beyond 'seared' it was pathetic). The Sea Bass was tough. Only the chicken stood up to the cooking - not that it was very good. Needless to say, we didn't stay for dessert. Last time I had been here was about five years before, and it was stellar. Since then, the owner seems to be on a chocolate binge, and maybe he just isn't interested any more. This place is clearly off its game.

text: I signed up at the gym cause it happened to be convenient to my work. I only wanted a month membership, as I was thinking I might be moving. $149 later I was out the door...I thought, well I'll get in shape and blah blah blah. At the time I signed up, I asked if there was someone who could show me how to use the machines, etc., since I'm obviously NOT in the best shape. The guy who signed me up said it would be an extra $30 or so bucks for that. So I guess I was just supposed to either pay additional money or go and try and figure stuff out on my own and either look like an idiot (which is everyone's fear when they are out of shape and join a gym in the first place) or hurt myself. Long story short, I only went a few times and when I wasn't sitting on the upstairs couch the whole time, afraid, I just used the treadmill. They need to understand that not everyone is a gym rat and that some people do need a little help and motivation and encouragement. They just wanted to make a sale. I didn't want a personal trainer to be standing above me the whole time, which I could see paying additional for, I simply wanted someone to say how to adjust the weights or seat and figure out where to start. I wouldn't recommend Sweat unless you already know what you're doing and are prepared to not have any help.

text: Mother's Day dinner at Chez Bryce. Sunday night, relatively few people and we got a great table outside. Check. Menu comes... lots of options but probably 70% of everything has meat in it. For the most part, a very 90s menu. But, wait, apparently he cures his own pork and makes his own terrine for the charcuterie plate. Kudos for that and, well, 1.5 of the 2.0 stars are simply because, if indeed he does his own charcuterie, he clearly cares enough to be running a restaurant. But... Service was an absolute disaster. Our waiter was nice enough, but he just wasn't a competent server. It felt like he was more comfortable swapping out transmissions than waiting tables. There really were very few tables, but after 90 minutes, we had only received our appetizers (I did order the charcuterie and it was simple and good). C'mon, one and a half hours for a half-full restaurant to get appetizers to us. Our waiter didn't really acknowledge the slow service until I started getting pissy, but this really didn't hurry things along. Waiting for our mains, I ordered wines by the glass from a reasonably thoughtful list. Not super-impressive, but it did show that, again, someone did care about what they were doing. However, the pours were consistently miserly - removing any sense of generosity that makes you like a restaurant... as if you can hear the manager going over and over with the servers to pour exactly 5 ounces. Main courses arrive at nearly 1 hour 45 minutes into the ordeal. I ordered duck breast "rare" expecting that they would generally overcook it. Well, screw me, I got a duck breast that was thrown in a pan for 2 minutes with a very slightly browned skin that was soft, no rendering of fat and pretty much room temperature and uncooked (not rare, seriously uncooked) duck meat. I didn't send it back because I had no faith that the cook knew how to cook a duck breast and we just wanted to get out of there by then. Duck came with an onion tart that tasted good but the tart shell was ridiculously hard and challenging to eat (make them smaller or use puff pastry). I ate the ends of the duck but ultimately asked a random server to pack it up for the dog. Mom had a couple of appetizers, brother had a hanger steak - ordered med-rare, cooked very rare... but a mediocre piece of meat. I'd much rather see a couple dollars added and use meat that doesn't taste like you bought it from Meat For Less. Passed on desert. Was charged for the wrong appetizer. Notified server and 10 minutes later he came back and said he just took it off for having such a long wait. Frankly, that action was the only thing that got him a tip. I have only stiffed 2 waiters in my life, and this was about to be the 3rd. Monsieur Bryce, not that you asked for them, but here are my thoughts: * Hire/train competent servers. Teach people how to handle customers who have to wait a long time (apologies, jokes, and if necessary, a free glass of wine or something) * Pare down your menu. Your kitchen clearly can't cope with so many things and you just don't need that many dishes. Honestly, you could probably remove 40% of the menu and customers would be happier and you would execute much better * If necessary, bump up your prices a dollar or two. I think you have room for that. * Add an extra ounce to the wine by the glass. Your cost is probably $0.50 and it'll be appreciated. * Keep fighting the good fight. I certainly appreciate you trying to provide a fine dining experience and you clearly care about what you're doing... maybe just do a bit less with stronger staff and I wish you the best of luck.

text: This apartment has very nice big windows. That is why I decided to rent here. Unfortunately, that is the only nice thing about it. Here are some of the MANY problems I have encountered while living here: The windows don't open. The apartment functions like a greenhouse, trapping the tons of sunlight we get, making it unbearably hot, even sometimes in the winter. The AC sometimes works, sometimes doesn't. The blinds don't work properly. You have to open and close them inch by inch, which takes forever. We end up just leaving them closed because it is too annoying. So much for pretty windows! The security is seriously lacking. One security guard doesn't even look up when you walk in. Also, the management, without warning, took away Sunday night security, although that was advertised when we signed our rental contract. The lock to the front door to the apartment broke and it took the management over 3 WEEKS to fix it. During this time, anyone could have gotten in. The dishwasher does not work. You have to completely clean the dishes before loading it, so there is no point in even using it. The sink is tiny so water splashes everywhere when you're doing the dishes. The freezer periodically begins to leak into the fridge. The repair guy says he deals with this problem all the time. The hot water lasts about 15 minutes - beware the second showerer! You can always hear music coming from other units or from cars blasting hip hop outside when they're stopped at the red light. There is a sex shop directly across the street. There's an adult movie theater on the next block and within view from the window. We are hooked up to Hotwire, not Comcast (which is right around the corner!) Hotwire is more incompetent than Philadelphia Management (our management company). Besides Hotwire being a poorly run company, the internet is just slow. Read your rental contract carefully. We got a free month, and hidden in the contract was a clause that if we were more than 5 days late with a rent check, we would lose the free month! All in all, I would definitely NOT recommend this apartment building. If you do decide to rent here, make sure to have maintenance on speed dial.

text: I have been taking our cat Basha to the Cat & Bird Clinic for over 10 years now. About 6 years and some change ago, she had withered away to less than half her weight. Subsequently, Basha came down over the years with glaucoma, high blood pressure, arthritis and lost one of her eyes to a stroke. But she was a tough little beastie and forged on for another year and a half. She finally gave up the ghost last week. I want to thank the amazing staff in general there for always being compassionate both with Basha and with our bank accounts, as sometimes we didn't have the money to pay in full up front. They were clearly more interested in keeping Basha alive and healthy than the money, and I suspect they were equally enamored with our little Ichabod Crane-like feline. I just received a very kind condolence card in the mail this morning from Dr. Sellers and it very much touched my heart that she would take the time out of her day to compose it. text: This was the first Greek food I've had since eating in Greece last Summer. I was a little nervous I'd be disappointed, but I had a hankering for tzatziki (sp?), and my friend, an great cook herself, recommended it, so a group of us went together for a late dinner. The ambiance leaves something to be desired, which is the only reason I'm not breaking out star number five. Noisy space, fluorescent lighting (thank god I have attractive friends), and uncomfortable chairs were a bummer. But we're here because we like eating, right? So all that other stuff is okay. Eating with a group of six was nice, because we got to order a whole bunch of stuff as appetizers. Tzatziki was awesome and gone in a matter of minutes. The hummus was good, I thought (though it was def heavy on the tahini and lighter on the lemon than when I make it), pita was delish, and the calamari and greek salad were both excellent. The service was really good, and attentive, too. For dinner, most of us ordered fish. Actually I think we all did. Several of us ordered the special, which was Dorado grilled with lemon and garlic, with a side of spinach and rice pilaf. Our most gregarious guest ordered the whole fish, filleted it himself, then proclaimed loudly that he would eat Fishy's eyeball, then followed-through. No one seemed to notice this but me, oddly. Anyway, a couple others had the salmon (greek-style) with olives, feta, asparagus and tomato I think... Also quite good. Everything was just really fresh and cooked simply, which is easier said than done sometimes. Some ordered dessert, some ordered Greek coffees, and others of us simply had more wine to bring things full-circle. By the time we were finished - prob around 10:30 - the whole place was empty, and they had turned the Greek music up significantly... Which I think is sorta like the equivalent of the dance club putting on really whiny Country music (Read: LEAVE), so the Winos, Fish-Eye-Eater, et al. took the hint and called it a night.

text: "Casual elegance" is how Flyte refers to themselves on their website. I have to admit that I 100% agree. Friends and acquaintances have advised me to check this place out for quite some time. I had some friends in town and thought that this would be an opportune time to show off some creative food and vino! The setting was dark and moody but offered up a natural cozy factor that wasn't contrived. When I was seated (naturally, I was running a bit late), our server immediately addressed me by my name (my friends filled him in prior to my arrival) and offered up sincere advice on what wine I should enjoy. His selection was exactly what this broad needed! The perfect blend of earthy goodness with a hint of cherry and chocolate. Here we go! I was very impressed that our server addressed the complete menu with me and offered up suggestions on how to tweak items so that it would fit my dietary needs. Being a vegan at Flyte is a snap! The menu also points out that "fresh, organic and humanely raised ingredients" are only used. I decided on the "Salad Flyte" ($11) which include a trio sampling of their salad menu that currently includes a scrumptious Beet Salad. The servings were very filling. For my entree, I opted for the Vegetable Gnocchi ($20). Flavorful mushrooms, Parisian gnocchi, fall vegetables, fennel, and basil were executed perfectly. I am really trying to figure out how I can afford to eat here every night of the week. Would anyone like to sponsor me? I can't emphasis enough how INCREDIBLE the service is here. Everyone from the hostess and server to the bartender, valet, and accompanying staff were doting and sincere throughout the entire evening. If you have a special occasion or craving an impeccable foodie experience...Flyte should be on the top of your list.

text: I was truly bummed when I found out that the parent company of Davis-Kidd Booksellers filed a Chapter 11 Bankruptcy which has resulted in several locations closing..including the Nashville - Green Hills store. This location was part of one of the nation's most prosperous book-selling companies at one time and has been open for nearly 30 years. I am personally a sucker for any businesses that create an interactive element for their customers. Davis-Kidd has hosted discussions, book signings, and live music that draw both adults and kiddies. Bestsellers, newly released books, and bargains have always stocked their organized shelves and the staff kindly gives you a tour if needed. A well edited gift section and convenient Bronte Bistro round out this location and make it really tough to leave. I have spent hours here before without realizing that the time had flown by. It is sad to see this wonderful business close and if you haven't popped in before, be sure to come by to say goodbye. TIP: Store closing markdowns have already started and will continue until they vacate their space in December.

text: Back when I thought stir fry was the most exotic thing to eat I also thought that Mongolie Grill was a cool place to eat. It was never worth the hype it got, and now it's overshadowed by a million and one other Eastern-Asian type restaurants. It has always been overpriced. What you're paying for is the freedom to stack your bowl with whatever you want your stir-fry to include: veggies, meats, seafood and sauces. The catch: the heavier your bowl the more your meal costs. In the end, you've got an average stir-fry, much like Wok Box serves up, at double the cost. Also, since you control the qualities of sauce to solids ratio, it usually ends up not tasting that good anyway. I tried this place a couple of times and was always disappointed, by the food and the bill. Since we can all buy a sauce at Safeway and cook up a stir-fry at home (didn't we all learn it in Home Ec class?) I reserve dining out for things I wouldn't normally cook for myself at home.

text: I'll start with the negatives and end with the positives. El Rey was a frustrating experience. I've mentioned this before, and I'll mention again. I'm from Texas and highly critical of my Mexican food. El Rey does a disservice for Yankees. Here's why: 1. They are trying to look like a real Tex Mex place, but nothing is old, has a story behind it, or authentic. 2. You can't get pitchers of margaritas. 3. My Negra Modelo did not come with a lime. Blasphemy. 4. There is no salt on the table. (This is just like totally inappropriate for an authentic Mexican place) 5. Chips and salsa are not part of your meal. You have to order that. 6. The hostess is not assertive. She's passive. She's a hostess. Make it happen. 7. The "mexican" candles on the tables aren't Mexican at all. They opted for the pop art post mod expensive ones instead. 8. The napkins aren't cloth and the glasses aren't plastic. The positives: 1. Chicken Tinga is delicious and I'll probably go back for it. 2. The prices are fair. 3. The staff is friendly. 4. I like the lighting. 5. Good for sharing. 6. There are booths. I'll go back, and I should know better than to expect anything different. I was just hoping that instead of making a parody of an authentic Mexican restaurant, he might actually do something out of his comfort cookie cutter zone.

text: I know, I know, I know.... It's a chain, I get it. But I was actually hoping that this one was like the closer one to me (Avon location which is now closed) in which I got really good service and food. At the old Avon location they each turned their heads and yelled out, "Welcome to Moe's!" and this happened every time I walked in there. Where as corporate Q'doba? Well you might get an eye roll or a blank stare. Well on to this location. No greeting, but a not an awkward silence, just someone who was waiting to be prompted by requests without chit chat. (Okay, mousey with no personality.) Sub-par food here though. The cilantro rice like that at the defunct Avon location was replaced by some browner overcooked version which was flavorless and dried out (crunchy rice is NOT tasty.) The chicken was average, maybe. It just didn't have much flavor. And the one small scoop of Pico de Gallo didn't help me out any. However, the extra star came for their awesome salsa bar! They had several salsas to choose from and I settled on the corn salsa which had extra cilantro teaming in it! I wound up POURING a small sample cup on each bite of my Joey Bag o Donuts burrito. I used so much that the staff had to bring out some more! That savior of a salsa made the burrito go from the meh - unenjoyable range, to the gone in three minutes category! Restrooms were super clean, but again I had the issue of employees who were handling clean up of the soda area with chemicals were also going back to make orders without washing hands. What is it about Tex Mex places reinforcing stereotypes about hand washing in this city?!?!? Although the corn salsa was enjoyable, I would probably skip this place for better options in the area.
label: NEG

text: It's tough to try and diet when you live so close to such a great bakery. McMillans succeeds in many ways. They are one of the few purveyors of granulated sugar doughnuts still around. In fact, since Bredenbecks closed in Philly, this is the only place I know of that makes the granulated sugar cream doughnut. The jelly in the doughnuts tastes like real fruit versus generic sweet filling, and just the right amount of sweetness. The packzy's (imagine a jelly doughnut where the doughnut is made of raising bread) is fully responsible for at least two sugar fits in recent months. Bread and rolls are great as well, and the cakes, although pricey, are worth it. Danish is also a great option here, with the toasted coconut my current favorite. I did hear the other day they have a butterscotch danish, so I may have to try that one out soon. Steer clear of the butter cake. It's an interpretation versus the runny top sweetness you're probably used to. Petit fours are similarly disappointing, being solid cubes of ice pound cake. No jelly, no layers of colored goodness, very expensive. Cookies are hit or miss. I've had some that are great, others that are bland tasteless discs with colored sugar on top. Fruitcake was a bust too (and I love fruitcake). On the whole, if it looks good, it probably is. Service can be variable depending on who helps you. I've purchased a dozen pastries and sometimes I'm offered a bakers dozen, sometimes not. Go early, but no too early (seriously). I arrived right after opening one day to try and get the best selection and they were still bringing stuff out. It was like being there after the morning rush! For holidays and special occasions, do yourself a favor and order in advance for pickup. Parking can be exciting, do yourself a favor and park across the street at Walgreen's. You'll burn a few teeny extra calories walking over that will justify that 13th bizmark!
label: POS

text: I went to Woo for the first time today after purchasing a style blue print daily deal. The place is mainly a cosmetics/ skincare store that has one room with for facials. She came back in and immediately started the facial without really talking to me at all about my skin or any specific issues I was having. I told her it was my birthday and that I wanted to treat myself. She suggested that I get the microdermabrasion and said it was a little bit more than the regular facial and it also wouldn't last as long, but it would be better results. I took her recommendation. The overall facial was very quick and when I went to check out it was much more than I had anticipated. The microdermabrasion was actually double the price of a regular facial from $80 to $190!! I was only in there for about 30 minutes!! The whole thing felt kind of rushed and it definitely was not a pampering experience. I could not believe the price difference and that she didn't explain that better. I have had facials at several other locations in Nashville and all of them took quite a bit of time to talk to me before hand about my skin and my routines and definitely pulled out all the stops to make me feel relaxed and pampered and for probably 1/2 the price. Overall, my skin did look better after the service, but I could have gotten the same results somewhere else for much cheaper and felt pampered on my special occasion. Needless to say I won't be returning.

Its kind of small and the health department recently forced them to add a second bathroom taking away several tables. There are picnic tables outside with umbrellas for nice weather. I HIGHLY recommend stopping in for lunch if youre in Hendersonville during the week.

When the day finally arrived, as I entered the store a sales rep handed me a coupon giving me a certain percentage off and I prepped myself ready for a full on shopping spee packed with trendy European clothing. What I found (or rather didn't find) was nothing that met my expectations. My initial reaction was that the clothing styles are very similar to GAP and Jacob. Overall very generic/blah and nothing special. The prices were relatively pricey for the quality and lack of unique-ness for what you were buying. Basically you can buy the same style of clothing at any other store. Needless to say I didn't purchase anything that day. Since my big disappointment, I drop by every so often just to see whether or not they have gotten anything in thats new and exciting to the world of fashion. I have purchased a two-piece bathing suit for under $30 for the set and it was a good buy. But other than that, H&M has yet to still impress me with their supposedly ultra chic European styles and clothing. I have talked to friends who swears by the store and finds cute dresses and blouses every season but I either find the prints too distracting or too plain and not enough trendy for my taste. I will still go in if I pass by the store just to try my luck in finding that hidden gem, but like many reviewers before me, maybe H&M just isn't my style. Nothing to make a fashion statement with.

text: Moka's (the previous tenant to Savas) was shut down after they got caught selling booze to under-agers. (I'm not going to tell you about the time that I may or may not have been involved in a plot to break into Moka's after they closed in order to retrieve/borrow/claim some left behind hookahs inside. I'm also not going to tell you about how the tiniest of wimpy crowbars was used to pry open a door, nor will I tell you how the alarm went off with sirens blaring and guns blasting and it was intense. It didn't happen. It wasn't me.) Four years later, Savas has opened for the spring quarter. I wasn't expecting much to begin with and I was neither impressed nor surprised. Just another pizza/Italian place, but they sure did great with the interior and exterior. It looks like a lounge, but they've got a lot of work to do. I went on a relatively quiet Tuesday night and the bar stools were all occupied by students. Some people at tables but not many. 3 people greeted us at the front and told us to sit where ever we'd like. We chose a hightop and then continued to wait 10 minutes before we finally flagged down a server. Server was cute, extremely nice, and caring--just needs some more experience. Menu is really large and mixed. They have brick oven pizza, bar snacks, and various entrees. Food was ok. Price was ok. "Meh. I've experienced better". Suggestions 1) Need quicker, efficient, and attentive service 2) Music was great but could barely hear it, pump it up! 3) Dim the lights! It's a researched fact that people will typically eat more in lower, more comforting lighting. Better for my eyes, better for your wallet, Savas. 4) Less tables, they were lined up like a cafeteria. 5) Needs booths or couches to complete lounge feel. I am more than willing to give Savas many more chances (they've only been open for two weeks and booze wasn't too expensive) but sometimes I really want places to get it right on the first try.
