text: I do not feel bad at all for giving this the worst rating I will ever give here. Ok, I have a great deal of Philly Pride! I am also a techie. There is a huge part of me that wanted this to work. Think about it, an affordable WI-Fi service that is strong at home and can also be used no matter where you are in Center City! That's great for anyone on a budget with a laptop. I had this service for one whole year. I sold all of my friends on it. I watched them all cancel their services for one reason or another. One by one, not me. I was being Mr. Philadelphia and totally championing this services saying, "Give it a chance". After a year, I called them and asked to be cancelled finally. I felt bad because I really wanted it to work out! I don't blame the hardware, I blame the organization. May times, nonprofit leaders get comfortable with their salaries and meetings that they forget that the programs they are providing need to be consistently observed, revised and supported overall. This service was installed and virtually abandoned. When tech support is in Ohio or overseas, there is no way you can support a muncipal service from outside of the city. Tech Support told me, "Oh, I'm a customer too and I never have connection issues." I told them to say it for someone who doesn't support networks for a living. I hate when tech support asks you to do all of the things you did before calling them all over again! She said, "Is there anything else I can do for you?" I said, "I want to hang up the phone and no longer have service with Earthlink!" Earthlink was beat out in Philadelphia for dsl, what made the city think they would provide a reliable municipal wifi service? Sorry, this one is near to my heart as myveins are actually cat5 cables...hehe. Here's a tip, fire the guy who spearheaded this agreement and hire someone new to clean this place up!

text: Einstein Bros Bagels is a nice addition to the restaurant choices in Reno. The bagels I had were pretty nice. This restaurant is formally scheduled to open on Tuesday in the location of the former Krispy Kreme, so I guessed there would be a soft opening on the Monday before. I drove down there and saw people inside the store and people walking out with bags and I figured I had guessed correctly. I parked and walked up to the door when I saw a sign that said there was training going on and only people with invitations would be admitted. I had no invitation and turned to walk away. An employee opened the door and invited me in any way. Cool. I went to the end of the counter where yo place your order. They have a glass counter with baskets of bagels on the bottom rows -- I counted 23 different bagels -- and the top row has muffins and cookies. I ordered a bacon, egg and cheese breakfast bagel on a Florentine spinach bagel. I wanted to try a second bagel, so I ordered an Asiago cheese bagel toasted with butter. I also ordered a decaf coffee. There's a display with items like orange juice and cream cheese and then you reach the cash register. They rang me up. The bill came to $9.56. I pulled out a $20 bill to pay and the employee behind the register said breakfast was free this morning. So in the interest of full disclosure, I came on what was considered a training day and I got my meal for free. I feel kind of bad now though for ordering that second bagel. They make espresso and cappuccino but the drip coffee is self serve. They also have small cups next to the coffee pots so you can sample the different flavors. I only drink decaf so I had only one choice. The place was packed but I found one table open. I sat down and after a few minutes they brought my food to my table. The bacon, egg and cheese was an excellent match for the spinach bagel. It was like a bagel omelet. The spinach had nice flavor, the bagel crust was crispy and I also liked the cheddar cheese. The best part was the bacon. Not a lot of it but it's first-rate bacon. The weak part was the egg. It doesn't taste like they use fresh eggs. The Asiago bagel was toasted but came without butter. Since it was free I wasn't going to complain. Also a good bagel, but I wished I had ordered something like an everything bagel for more interesting flavors. The coffee was pretty standard drip coffee. They seem to trying to create a friendly atmosphere there. Employees wore shirts with sayings like "Protect your bagels. Put lox on them" or "Donuts schmonuts. Eat a bagel." People are inevitably going to compare any bagel with the best bagels in New York and that's not fair. I couldn't find a New York-quality bagel in Washington, D.C., Los Angeles or San Francisco. The Einstein Bros bagels I had today were pretty good, though, and I suspect they will succeed in Reno.

text: CAUTION. This agency screams scam. I can only tell you what I experienced. A friend recommended E&A as a way to get out and socialize in a new area, or with people who share common interests. I went to their site and found it locked down -with prompts to fill out a form. So I did, curious to see where it went. I got a call the very next day and was treated to the classic sales lure. I was asked a few questions about my age, job, etc. Although I answered them, I kept it generic enough to retain some privacy. However, I was beginning to *smell* the build up. And sure enough, I was flattered and promised impossible things. I was told I would meet QUALITY people, like myself. I was advised that they weren't like other social groups - which let ANYONE join. ?? really? What type of screening do they perform? I was advised that they liked to meet people and interview them to see if they are the type of people that should join their club. I asked what the qualifications are, but they dodged the answer, assuring me I was clearly their type of people and I wasn't going to have any problems joining their club. I kept getting that odd sense of elitist. I wasn't sure if the "special" nature of the members was racial, cultural, or financial. I asked what it would cost and got the next red flag: I wouldn't be told what the cost was to join. But I was assured it was affordable. I was told the fee was to help ensure that the members were QUALITY members. [Really? what exactly are "quality" members?] I was told that joining this group would open the calendar to me and expose me to lots of activities and fun! I asked if the events were free with the membership. NO. "most of the events do not cost more than $25". So if I understand this offer, I have to pay a membership fee in order to even SEE THE CALENDAR of events. And this fee is, according to the agent, a method of deterring some element of the populace. And so I must assume it is a financial deterrent, which means the ones who can pay are clearly QUALITY people. Then you get to pay for each event in addition. I started to hesitate about attending, and was treated again to a special courtesy... my agent moved other appointments around to accommodate my schedule. [Why?] I agreed to the appointment and ended the call. I received the email. This is the copied/pasted quote exactly out of the email: But people love Events and Adventures for the QUALITY of our members. Note the emphasis. It is bolded and underlined in my email. Something is wrong. I then googled this agency and checked with the BBB in other states (PA is fairly new). Everyone cautions that this agency requires a contract (never told to me over the phone), that it costs more than 1.5k to join (again, no details provided over the phone), and there is even a monthly fee on top of the event fees. I emailed my agent to cancel my appointment. I encourage everyone to research this agency/club/group before signing a single piece of paper. They used the classic 'flattery / special' statements to boost your ego and QUALITY, while insisting on a face to face interview. Which, if you know about sales pitches, is the best method of intimidating and pressuring you into signing paperwork and giving over money.

text: The Sheraton Sand Key is a "nice" hotel. But for the price and the amenities, I expect more than nice. The sand is really more of a ground sea shell/gravelly mix, not something you want to sink your toes into, much less walk on barefoot (surprisingly Clearwater Beach across the bridge is much nicer). And since the beach is on the gulf and there aren't any waves, most of the action on the water is confined to wind sports. The hotel itself is OK. Rooms are nothing to write home about and the restaurant and bar elicit half-hearted, "meh." Conference facilities are adequate. And because this is a "resort" and not much is really convenient without getting in your car, amenities that you would expect to receive gratis are rather pricey. Internet access will set you back $12/day, having anything delivered to the hotel will cost you a handling fee (usually $10-20), a bottle of water in your room will cost your $4. Hospitality staff can best be described as gruff. I've stayed in scores of hotels that are nicer, friendlier, and more relaxing than this, and many of them for less than the $275-300/night this one will set you back. The Sheraton Sand Key is like an expensive restaurant with bad food and a great view -- you quickly realize that you are paying simply to be on the beach.

text: The Note is like your favorite neighborhood bar went a little bit Goth and added a stage so it could provide some great live music. And The Note is designed so you can see the band perfectly no matter where you stand, even if the acoustics are a little off in some places. The stage is very high. The pit is sloped so you can see over the head of the person in front of you, unless he happens to be a foot taller than you. And the bar is at the same elevation as the stage, so you can see perfectly from the bar. The Husband and I have seen four shows at The Note: Rasputina in November 2008, The Flobots in December 2009, The Donnas in March and MC Lars (with MC Chris) last week. All of the shows were excellent. And we got to meet, shake hands with and talk with the members of The Flobots and MC Lars after their shows. Shows usually start at 8, and the doors are usually supposed to open at 7. But the doors have never once opened when they were supposed to and the shows have never started when they were supposed to (The Donnas didn't go on until midnight), which is a little annoying, and one of the reasons The Note didn't get five stars. The Husband and I like to eat at the bar before the shows start. The menu has standard neighborhood bar fare - burgers (your choice of beef, turkey, veggie or chicken breast), wings, chicken tenders, fries, fries with cheese, fries with cheese and bacon, tater tots, tater tots with cheese, tater tots with cheese and bacon, etc. The Husband loved the salads, but they're no longer on the menu (another reason the bar lost a star). So last week, at the MC Lars show, he tried The Californian - chicken breast with cheddar cheese, scallions and avocado (actually guacamole), wrapped in Romaine lettuce. He loved it, except for the avocado. I ALWAYS get the ridiculously delicious five-cheese grilled cheese (parmesan-crusted bread with brie, gruyere, cheddar and - I think - Swiss) and the tater tots. You can add tomato and/or bacon to the sandwich, but I don't. The sandwich (and accompanying tater tots or fries) costs about $6, and is worth every penny and then some. As great as the food is, it's a bit difficult to eat. The bar has a great big, several-inches wide bump at the edge, which prevents you from getting reasonably close to your food basket. And the only napkins The Note has are cocktail napkins, which aren't particularly helpful when eating a delicious, buttery and cheesy sandwich. (Yet another reason the bar loses a star.) text: So, I took my mom here so she could use a Groupon that I purchased a couple of months ago. The Groupon was for a 50 min. facial or massage. My mom opted for the facial, which was also supposed to include an eye treatment. Anyway, last week, I called and made an appointment for a 50 min. facial and the staff person on the phone told me to arrive 10 min. early so she can change. I've been to spas before and 10 min. seemed a bit short but I took her word for it and we got to the spa at the right time. My mom changed and we were taken back to the waiting area where she was told to wait for her esthetician and in the meantime, to fill out a form specifying any special needs (i.e. skin conditions, sore muscles, etc.). By the time the esthetician came to get her, it was already 20 min. into her appointment time. (At least 15 min. of us being ready and waiting for the esthetician to show up). About 25 min. later, my mom comes out and says she is finished. 25 minutes! Half of the time that was paid for. Now, I understand if a client is late for spa treatments, the person's time gets cut down accordingly in order to accommodate later appointments. In this case, we were not late but the esthetician was. I told the receptionist, hoping that she would either correct the situation or allow me to speak to management. I already paid for it through Groupon so I honestly wasn't sure what the protocol was for subpar service. She told me that she has no way of knowing what time my mother actually went back for her facial and that if we had a problem, we should talk to the woman who provided the treatment. So, we spoke to her and she immediately became defensive. First, she said that most ppl don't need a 50 min. facial because their skin just doesn't need that much work---so 25 min. was all that my mother needed. (Then why advertise a 50 min. session?) She condescendingly asked if either of us had even ever gotten facials before and said that she provided a really good service for the Groupon price and that we were actually getting a bargain anyway! Then she changed her story and said that she came out late to get us because usually, clients are late (doesn't mean we were though). Then, she started talking about how she was so tired and had clients back to back. She even went so far as to say that we got wrong information from the woman who booked the appointment---but that is still the fault of the business and not the customer. I think she expected us to fold and just leave. In the end, all I really wanted was some of the money I paid for the Groupon, to be refunded---I just wanted to pay for what we got and nothing extra...I really wasn't looking for anything else. But she did go ahead and give us a gift certificate for a massage at a later date. Overall, I found the experience a bit stressful. If she had offered a discount or something in the beginning, instead of becoming defensive, it would have been much better and easier for all of us. In her defense, I do have to say that these types of issues are something that salon management should take care of, not the beauticians. The beauty treatment staff should only need to concentrate on providing the service. Management needs to have some mechanism to deal with issues like this or better train their beauticians to do it.

text: Let's talk about how freakin' amazing Cha Cha Chow is, shall we? It's hard to decide what to order, so I'll tell you what I had: the strawberry agua fresca (wonderful, real fruit, blessedly without sugar), the Yucatan Pork tacos (tomatillo sauce and fresh white corn tortillas--divine), black beans (mmm) and curried sweet potatoes (OMG). Everything was fresh, seasoned really well (read: just spicy enough), and just totally satisfying. The only reason that this place gets 4 stars from me is because it took a full half hour to order our food and receive it. Come early--the lines get long quickly! It's not the most time-friendly lunch spot in the world, but who cares? It's so good. Worth the wait, definitely. Tracking the truck's whereabouts on Twitter is fun (@whereschacha)--sometimes, they'll give you a 'secret code' to mention and you can receive prizes! I scored a drink koozie today. Win. I'm just so impressed with this place. If this is what the food truck trend brings to St. Louis--great food with great prices, accessible to all--then bring it on. What a great time to be here!

text: Generally, bars in New Orleans that try at all to be upscale end up being merely pretentious. This is a city that whole heartedly embraces and celebrates the neighboorhood-dive bar concept and most bars that try to escape that tradition cater to tourists or just the douchebaggery. To the credit of Monkey Hill, it has managed to bridge the fragile fault line between neighboorhood bar and upscale scene for quite some time. Thanks to the great service, friendly atmosphere, and phenomenal selection this bar is a consistent hot spot in a category that is in constant flux. Yes, it can occasionally become overrun by yuppies but it also serves a diverse crowd and the couches are usually a great place to observe beautiful people, and maybe even make out with them. There's a reason this place is always one of the most happening spots uptown. Friday happy hour pops off. You won't ever get your drink on for too cheap but the cocktails are stiff and it's worth it for the quality company of the staff and patrons. The specialty drinks keeps many people coming back week after week. Top notch pool table and shuffleboard are available and they even have an obscenely nice 65 inch high def projection screen for big games. My only complaint is that the jukebox music relies heavily on Classic Rock standards and rarely plays anything to get people dancing. Other than that, is the closest thing New Orleans has to the Hybrid of bars- upscale, friendly, tasteful.

text: So lovely to look at, and a name that's so bold, but prices are shocking, and the food - well the food's just boring. Yes I know it doesn't rhyme, and that same sense of discord that you get from reading my bad poetry is a shade of what I experienced after eating here. Twice. I was so happy to see a higher end sushi bar going into Collingswood. Sagami has needed a little challenge on its home turf and the little chinese restaurant across from Wawa just wasn't doing it. Surprise! It turns out these are the same owners (as the little chinese place) taking on a new, upscale venture. It's a darn shame it's all pig and lipstick. Now I've read the reviews and I agree it's very pretty, and the staff is pleasant, but I ultimately don't care about any of that if the food is good. Let's face it - we've all eaten at a jersey dive at 2am and had the food practically thrown at us - but who cares - it was what it was and the attitude was the 'charm' of the experience. I was not charmed. Let's start with the appetizers. The sunomono was nice, but I would have prefferred more vegetables in mine. It was priced well for the portion of fish I received, but sunomono should be pickled fish AND vegetables, not fish with vinegar dressing and some seaweed for color. Sorry if you think that's a small deal, but I really like my sunomono and this was a poor effort. The Tako Su (Octopus Salad) suffered from the same affliction. On to the main course. Sushi for two. $40. Ok - I've paid that (and more) before, so let's look, we have two (each) shrimp, salmon, tuna, herring (bleah), squid, and eel. Tuna rolls (4 pcs), check. California roll (4pcs), check. That's it! This was like a $16 special at AOI in the city. Heck I could have got this at Wegmans for like $25. Was the fish fresh, yes, but there sure wasn't $40 of it. Plus look at it - Herring! Squid! Where am I - Wegman's kosher counter? Where's the Uni, or some White Tuna, or a nice Hamachi. This was boring - spell it with me - B.O.R.I.N.G. Add to that a king crab handroll, one, for $10 that was half the size of the one I usually get at Mikado or Fuji mountain, and both of then charge $6 and $7.50 respectively. Our bill came to $110 when we factored in tax and tip, and it was, frankly, shamefully overpriced. They should have called me the next day or sent me flowers to screw me over like that, and I received not bloom one nor has my phone jingled. Now I love sushi, and I've spent $300 a person at Morimoto's for a chef's tasting that left me so full I could still taste fish the next day, so to go here and pay for adequate (not interesting) fish in small portions at easily 40% more than Sagami or Mikado just makes no sense. Frankly, I wanted to give one star but I was concerned about the flaming, so I've cut my losses and given it two. After all, the fish, what little there was of it, was fresh. So I'll not be returning for a third try. I'm so disappointed at the lack of effort and overpriced food that I won't waste one more dime on them.

text: I am a huge fan of Spanish food so picked Bar Ferdinand for my birthday dinner. I had heard great things about it so was very excited to finally try it out. I had the red sangria which was just ok so I switched to a beer they had on tap after that, the Stoudt's Heffeweisen...much better!!! We waited a little bit for our drinks and then a little more for the first round of plates to come out. With tapas, the plates are usually just brought out as the kitchen finishes them...there is no real order to the madness and it's usually on the service is usually pretty quick. However with this meal things were a bit different. A few plates were brought out to start with. We then had to wait about 20 min or so for the next dishes to come out. Then it seemed even longer after that...about 30 minutes. Finally we were waiting for our last two courses and I kid you not this took about 1 1/2 hours to get the last course and dessert! Overall we were there from 8:15pm til 11:30pm! I don't know if they were having kitchen troubles or what but it was absolutely absurd how long it took. We even had to track down our waiter a few times to order more drinks because he was nowhere to be found. Some people at my table were almost ready to get up and leave near the end of the meal. The food was not fabulous but there were a few stand out items: the seasonal salad which had chickpeas, radicchio, cauliflower and potatoes in it (had a Mediterranean flare) and the empanadas with dates & bacon (very sweet, yet savory). Overall it isn't a bad deal for $30 a person for the amount of food you get. We ordered so much alochol to account for the time in between courses so that jacked up the bill, the food was so-so and the service was completely out of whack. If I venture back here I probably would order off the regular menu and see if its any better.

text: Truly a disgrace. I've been going to Tujaque's with my wife for over 15 years and have witnessed its steady, disappointing decline. It was one of the first venerable "Old New Orleans" restaurants I ever experienced. And I loved it. The set menu food was tasty, succulent and somehow original even though the menu had not changed in decades. I liked the attentive waitstaff and maitre'd who had apparently worked there since he was young. The place was always packed. I went there often enough that it felt like home. No longer. We returned to Tujagues about a month ago for the first time in over two years and, man, were we ever unhappy. The beef brisket, which was once the best possible way to start a meal, was rubbery, salty and bland. The waiter, a feckless girl, offered seconds. We declined. The shrimp remoulade arrived as a runny, sloppy mess. It was salty and the tiny shrimp were tough little bastards. I ate the lettuce because I was hungry. Same for the bread. I barely remember the soup except to say that my wife didn't touch her's. The real disaster started when the entrees came out. There were four choices: beef, shrimp, chicken and fish. We passed on the beef since the brisket was so bad. It didn't matter. Everything was alternately salty, overcooked, undercooked (that red stuff in the chicken was not gravy...gross), bland, slimy or, generally, unappetizing. We ended up trying everything because we had to send it all back. Some kind of dessert with "rum sauce". It was bland and salty. I don't think there was any rum in it. I don't know what happened to the Tujague's we loved. Maybe there's a new chef who never ate at the restaurant in it's heyday. Maybe he doesn't understand the history. Maybe the owners are now too old to appreciate good New Orleans food (too much salt, butter, love, etc.) Worse, maybe they are content to let the money roll in from all the tourists and assorted suckers who wind up wasting their time and money here. Whatever the reason, it doesn't matter. Tujague's is a disgrace and this was the worse meal I've suffered through in the past decade. It's all pretty depressing as the restaurant was once one of the jewels of our dining scene. I guess it's true what they say. You really can't go home again. R.I.P. Tujaque's. I don't know when you died, but it's a real bummer that you were replaced by Zombie Tujaque's.

text: Corporate acquisitions make for strange bedfellows that spawn odd, joined-at-the-hip (or at least under-one-roof) offspring - like this A&W Root Beer/Long John Silver's outlet - that vie for your fast food dollars. The cole slaw was decent, but hushpuppies and cheese sticks, while a weIcome departure from the standard fries, were oozing grease. text: Happy Hour everyday from 5 - 7pm. 20oz. drafts for $3! $5 Belgium drafts! I loved my Chimay. They even served it in a Chimay glass! The atmosphere is authentically Irish without the smoky atmosphere, but I think they've banned smoking in pubs in Ireland now. I like the various Scotch mugs lining the bar shelf. We arrived at 10:50 am, 10 minutes before it opened, and good thing we did because at 5 after 11 this place was slammed with a looooong line out the door. We ordered WAY to much food, as usual, and nothing really jumped out at us. The tortillas were hot out of the oven, and that was pretty much the highlight out of everything we ordered . The meat was all pretty flavorless, (We had the pollo, carne asada and carnitas), and you needed to load up on the salsa to get your taste buds to really react. I wish I would have tried the Chile Relleno which I hear everyone who tries it becomes instantly addicted. Oh well. Overall the food here is okay, and not spectacular. La Super Rica is overrated and not worth your time of standing in line or waiting for a spot to eat at the limited, and kind of depressing and gross, outdoor seating area. text: Russell Gardens Center is located in a residential area and they own a lot of land. This family owned Nursery and Garden Center grows most of what they sell. To the left and the right of the main garden center building, you can check out what they have planted in the ground and when it will be ready. Numerous greenhouses are beyond the outdoor gardens. Walking into the main building, which is huge, you are greeted by a large, glass enclosed porch, that is filled with a beautiful fountain and plant filled tables everywhere. I often fill my cart right here and now, have to take it inside to pay and then venture on. Once inside, from the porch area, you will find beautiful gift items, decorations for your home, pots, more plants and garden supplies. To the right of this main entrance way, their is an adjoining greenhouse, which is gigantic! They love geraniums and so do I. This greenhouse has a huge selection of geraniums in every size and color imaginable! Baskets of Ivy geraniums are hanging all over. On the other side of the main building is another glass enclosed room with exotic plants, such as orchids, bonsai, cactus and unusual house plants. Walking outside of this room, you are walking into a very large courtyard with more plants, vegetables, bushes, fountains and trees. They have a nice assortment of garden decorations and flags. Their pricing is comparable to the other local nurseries. So Mary, Mary, quite contrary, how does your garden grow? Mine grows with weeds, that make me sneeze and beautiful geraniums, in a row.

text: Wow, I'm not even sure where to begin. The Leasing staff treats you like royalty when they tour you around and try to get you to sign the lease. The buildings are poorly maintained, and as a result, there are frequent water/heat shutdowns and recently, they even had electricity shut off for more than one hour. Whenever there are maintenance requests, you can't ever be sure whether it will take them one or several days to take care of your request. When tenants inquire about the status of the heat/hot water/electricity, etc. we are told it's being worked on and given no further information. The staff is not pleasant when dealing with current tenants. Their bookkeeping is often screwed up, so they rarely have your records updated. Oh, let me not forget to mention my episode in the freight elevator, which got stuck between floors and when we tried to call the emergency line, the staff member on the other end kept hanging up on us because they didn't know that it was the emergency line calling. In addition, there is a camera in the elevator and although we waved our arms frantically in front of the camera, the staff still had no idea there were 2 people stuck. text: MMM - warm soft pretzels right out of the oven - is there really anything better? No web site for this place that I can find, which is a shame as they're products are great. I think it's a franchise, but again, no web info so not sure. Who cares anyway - their pretzels are great. These people get up really early to start making pretzels, and it seems like the crew has been the same since they opened. The pretzels are what you expect, tasty, salty, yummy, and fresh. I love the pretzel braids with sesame seeds, though the everything ones are very good too. Shamrock shaped pretzels near St. Patrick's day were a fun touch. Party platters are a great buy. For something like twenty dollars you get a hundred, yes 100 pretzel rods (about 4" long) plus mustards and cheese dips. These go over great at parties or as an alternative to donuts at work. I'm not a big fan of the rivets, pretzel bites similar to what you get at the movie theaters but fresher, but my son loves them. The small pretzels, half the size of normal pretzels are also a nice treat if you're not hungry for the big ones. I've never had anything from them that I didn't really enjoy, and my only complaint is with myself for not stopping by more often. So why not five stars? One - no fountain soda, and two, no new products are being introduced. What about a sugar cinnamon pretzel, or a pesto one with asiago cheese melted on top? For five stars I want to be really impressed, and while I admit the products here are excellent, there's nothing that's truly 'over the top'.

text: I have only been to Crêperie Beau Monde for brunch so let me humbly admit that I fail at life for thus far never partaking in their breakfast, lunch or dinner offerings. Beau Monde! It is a treat for the senses. I'm a sucka for elegant design, and the interior reminds me of a gilded apiary. There is always nice natural lighting inside which compliments the decor. Although there has always been a lot of customers at the times I have been there (are they - in fact - my secret fanclub or something?) it has not felt crowded, noisy or uncomfortable. Other times I had a server who seemed bored, curt and even sarcastic. As we all know, a dining experience is comprised of much more than just the food and drink. text: So. I'm not quite sure what a "utilitarian bar" exactly means but I can tell you that I like it. A lot. A couple of months ago, some friends of mine mentioned that a snazzy new establishment was prepping to open next to Dino's Bar + Grill. I was a little shocked by the locale but curious and thrilled that the East Side would home another independent biz. Fast forward to Tuesday evening, my friend let me know that she was at a "soft opening" and suggested that we have our planned "girls night" at No. 308 in lieu of our original plan to head to Holland House. Sure, why not? I knew that I was in for a treat as soon as I walked into the dark yet spunky retreat. The retro furniture and booths were perfectly appointed but not overly staged. Even the striped walls stood out yet didn't take away from the overall tone of the space. I absolutely loved the bar. The contrast of wood and metal pipes masterfully showcased character. Bottoms up! Our group nestled into a massive tufted booth and started ordering the "goods". The drink menu boasted imaginative cocktails with interesting names such as the "Writer's Block Shots" section ($5) that included the William Burroughs and Charles Bukowski! Smitten. I opted for a gin laced cocktail named the Suffering Bastard ($8) which nearly knocked me on my arse. Delish but potent! Our whole table enjoyed the libations and a few even ordered some food. The Sweet Potato Soup was on point and comforting! My friend knew the owners well and made the intro. I really enjoyed meeting Alexis and her staff. She proposed to the other owner in a Manhattan hotel room...guess what room number they were in? No. 308 Witty right? The owners and staff were casually dressed in tee shirts and jeans and was actually a refreshing contrast to what some may expect. It further drives the message home that this is going to be a fantastic destination place for some but still manage to be a cozy neighborhood bar for me. No. 308 is a real bargain due to crafty cocktails and interesting space. I am sure that I will be "checking in" a ton moving forward! TIP: The playlist was a fun mix of Johnny Cash, Top 40 R&B, and Indie Rock...gotta love it.

text: I really wanted to like this place, having become an immediate fan of their sister restaurant/bar a block away, Bridge. Walking in for a very late breakfast/early lunch, all seemed to be going well. Nice decor, tables, windows. But the hint of greasy smoke wafting through the air should have been a warning sign. During the 30 or so minutes I spent at my table, the level of smoke in the place grew, and my hair and clothes became totally inundated with that "greasy spoon" smell. I had to completely change clothes after returning to my hotel room. The menu was nicely organized and included some creative breakfast and lunch options, particularly crepe-based ones. Not being in the mood for eggs, I ordered a chicken caesar wrap (served in a chilled crepe), with a side of their breakfast potatoes. I ordered the wrap with no tomatoes, but it arrived at my table with tomatoes throughout. No big deal, I ate it as-is. It was fine, but crepes do not make for a very sturdy container for wraps, I've discovered. The breakfast potatoes were thinly-sliced discs that were seasoned with a very odd combination of spices and heavily fried. They were extremely greasy and were pretty much cold when they arrived at my table. Service was just fine. Granted, there were only a few other patrons in the whole place. Basically, the smoky, greasy air ruined the otherwise-pleasant atmosphere for me. They need to address the air ventilation of this place. And perhaps it was simply what I ordered, but the food left me unimpressed. Nice try, but I probably won't return.

text: After this meal I can honestly say that I understand Plato. Here is the punchline for those of you into the whole brevity thing--noble is good. It's Meme good. It's Amada good. The drinks and the food kick serious ass. Ok onto the story. There are so many ways I can go with this review. I can talk about how they have a rooftop garden for herbs and veggies and the stuff is so fresh it's like a punch in the face from nature. I can talk about how they really know how to make a drink. Their bartenders make mixing a drink look like a lost art. I can talk about really great decor and chairs that effortlessly glide on the concrete floor. No, I want to talk about philosophy. I remember sitting in high school and learning about the differing viewpoints of Aristotle and Plato. The Plato one was cool because it talked about a chair. He said that while there are many chairs in existence, all these chairs are a mere impression of the one "ultimate chair." This we can think of as the abstract chair. This abstract chair is the perfect embodiment of what a chair should be. All real chairs (instances) are an interpretation of the one abstract chair. How does this have anything to do with Noble? The Pan Roasted Chicken. I never eat chicken when I'm out. I'm always drawn toward more exciting things. Previously, chicken was the tofu of meat to me. I took a chance however on Noble's Pan Roasted Chicken and it brought me full circle. If there is a perfect chicken dish in the universe, they have duplicated it. It's almost like the universe was going to explode, but it didn't. This was a breast of chicken, with crispy skin and a moist inside. It tasted like chicken should taste (in the ideal sense) and if that wasn't enough, there was a little piece of chicken sausage on the plate too. If that wasn't enough, the pieces of the breast were cylinders themselves (as a nod to the chicken sausage) If that wasn't enough, it was over escargot, bacon and broccoli rabe. Hallelujiah!! Holy s&*%!! Where's the tylenol? My first course was the white chilled asparagus soup. It had a very dramatic presentation and it tasted incredible. There was some kind of garnish in the bowl already when the waiter poured it in. I made sure to mix it up before I nomed it. For dessert, we shared the Milk Chocolate Parfait. Two things of note here. 1. Rosemay caramel - if this meal wasn't amazing enough, they put rosemary in caramel. I mean cmon. Awesome. 2. It was just enough dessert to maximize my enjoyment of the meal and not send me teetering over the edge into the full zone. I think this place is just so amazing. It's not an everyday kind of place but it's not snooty enough to be one of those special occasion places. It's really in its own category, which is just fine by me.

text: This is a great local pizza and sandwich shop. It's just the kind of place you want to have in your neighborhood. It's fresh, it's fast and it can actually be healthy - not something most pizza places would (or maybe should) claim. And they have way more than just pizza at reasonable prices. Their pizzas are more of the gourmet variety. If you want a basic, giant slice of grease and crappy cheese - this is not for you. Their plain pizza is very good, but their gourmet pizzas are terrific. Their Southwestern pizza is a great blend of BBQ sauce, red onion, bell peppers and chicken. The Hawaiian is great. But the best pizza by far is the "That's Amore." It's grilled eggplant, mushrooms, mozzarella and Romano cheeses. It is amazing. It does require a fork and knife as the toppings make it a little soggy - but it's worth it. Loved the tuna hoagie - roll was chewy, not soggy and the tuna itself didn't taste like an afterthought. The grilled vegetable wrap was very good and so was the grilled chicken one. They have many low fat and heart healthy options, but if you want to indulge, their wings were fabulous. Very crispy and not greasy. Even their french fries stood up to take-out without getting gross. They also have a huge selection of salads. My fave is the Mediterranean with spinach, fresh veggies, Greek olives, feta, roasted peppers, and sun-dried tomatoes. It was so good that it didn't even need dressing. Other than the incredibly huge menu, the other great thing about Sun Valley is that they have a VERY reasonably prices kids menu ranging from $2-$5. Sometimes it's nice to get take-out and not cook and Sun Valley doesn't want to charge me $8 for a bowl of noodles. It's only $2.95! I have to add that it's also a great place to eat with kids. They have a big fish tank that is up against one of the tables. This provides the perfect amount of entertainment mixed with the "Is our pizza ready yet?"

text: Great food, cool staff, decent prices in a WYSIWYG atmosphere! If you're looking for Indy's centerpiece of style, swanky, and sophistication...keep looking. Please. Weather permitting: their patio is pretty cool...and the 4-way intersection offers some great views of some of Indy's dumbest drivers! The dining room is a simple, but cool and comfortable flatiron style room with full service. The bar is one of Indy's coolest little hideaways: seating for plenty, either at the bar or one of many tables, but not big enough that you have to start searching for your server or bartender. Don't worry, there are enough TVs that you won't miss your game or event. They have an upstairs area too: pool and a few games, a smaller bar (but still room for plenty), and a few tables in a small, front room with bay windows overlooking Pennsylvania St. Be warned: it gets smokey; really smokey. But for someone who *hates* cigarette smoke, I like Elbow Room enough to be a regular. The dining room never seems that bad -- so that's a good place to start. Want a few food tips: the breaded tenderloin is nearly as big as the plate, and worth every bite. The Club Pita is also extremely delicious. For you herbivores, I've heard the veggie burger is awesome too!

text: warning: epic review (and epic pictures) for epic establishment. the service:: unbeatable. i called the day before for a large party, but they were fully booked. i told the nice woman on the phone our plans were to get there right when they opened at 5ish, and she said we'd probably be okay. when i rolled in the next day with my party of 12, the host repeated that they were fully booked but went out of his way to give us the two tables outside. awesome. dustin and courtney, our two servers, were so nice and answered the many questions we had about the menu. the food:: oh lord, where do i even begin? the meal started out with delicious cheesy-garlicky corn muffins with green onions on top. then we were all given a small spinach salad with a plum sesame vinaigrette and a fried oyster on top. after this, our appetizers came out. i'll make this quick: the shrimp and alligator cheesecake is a must. you know how the best part of food is usually the first bite? well in the case of the cheesecake, the LAST bite is the best--the "crust", if you will. it is THE perfect bite. the calamari was also good, not too heavy or drenched with oil. instead, it was drenched with garlicky flavor. after the appetizers, the sides started coming out. all entrées come with two sides. i got the red beans and rice and corn maquechoux. though just okay on their own, it was spectacular after i mixed everything together. actually, all their sides are delicious. the fries are tiny and stringy and are perfectly salted, the collard greens are just a little bitter and absorb enough of the juices, and the mashed potatoes are fluffy and flavorful. i consider myself very lucky to have been with 11 other generous people, because i got to try a bit of everything. my favorite dish wasn't even my own. i went with the traditional blackened redfish (which was yummy), but what really took the cake was the stuffed pork chop with ground beef and shrimp. holy moly. it was an explosion of flavor in my mouth. and the portion was GIGANTIC! dustin wasn't lying when he said two people could share it. the chicken pontalba was also delicious (and that was a huge breast), mostly because of the amazing béarnaise sauce. so. creamy. the stuffed catfish with crabmeat dressing was great, as was the shrimp étouffée, the new orleans style bbq shrimp, and the fried chicken topped with pickles. boy was that fried chicken good. the three things i tried that just didn't *wow* me like the others did were the grilled grouper (even with a tasty cream sauce, it was just..plain), the paneed duck (i like duck but the sweet potato shrimp sauce just wasn't cuttin' it for me), the stuffed shrimp with magnolia sauce (it was *too* stuffed if that's even possible..i didn't like how heavy the appetizer was) and the vegetarian delight (the thai coconut cream sauce just didn't blend well with all the cajuny flavors i had tasted prior to this). however, all the people who had these dishes loved them. with no room left for dessert, we thanked our trusty staff and said goodbye to the rather large crowd of different groups that formed outside, waiting to be seated, since our arrival. the friendliest staff ever, generous portions, and that authentic nawlins cuisine are the reasons why that line is so long. i will be dreaming about this place for a very long time.
label: POS

text: Okay, I'm likely showing my age here, but I saw one concert at the Shaw well over a decade ago...it was Moist. I remember going with my sister and being afraid she'd get crushed in the mosh pit. She's a small girl and was then, too. Still, we were both huge David Usher fans. Aside from that, the experience was okay aside from levitating once in awhile (my feet left the ground and I wasn't crowd surfing) and getting kicked in the head a lot. To be honest the levitating was kinda fun and I decided a kidney pinch was a good way to get back at a boot to the head. (Who me? ~ eyelashes fluttering innocently ~) At one point I got shoved to the front but way off to the side. That wasn't bad, I flirted with the keyboard player a bit. Maybe I've become a bit of a concert snob over the years, and having worked at the Winspear for several years likely influenced it, but the sound in the Shaw for concerts is pretty crappy. Seriously, it's your favourite band live from a tin can. It's kind of fun as a teenager because you generally can't get into the bars and just want to let loose and be stupid anyway. Of course, back in the day you had to go out into the lobby to purchase any kind of beverage and they weren't allowed in the conference room where the band was playing. No tables, either. It was band, mosh pit, wanderers, wide open space, bleachers. I think everyone in the city has attended a graduation ceremony at the Shaw. If not, maybe a wedding reception. You still get the tinny acoustics but who the hell cares, you're just there to celebrate and get drunk. I think it's best defined by its title - Conference Centre. Aside from some really awesome photo ops inside, this is a really cool venue for a trade show - like the annual wine festival they host, arts and crafts fairs, tattoo conventions, that sort of thing. It's the perfect size and the atmosphere is awesome for that kind of event. Lately what I've been going there for is the grounds. The building is built on a hill (cool slanted glass elevator inside!) so outside they have sort of (flower/tree) garden blocks on various levels with benches. You can take the stairs from Jasper Avenue at the Shaw all the way down to the river if you continue on to the park below. Now THAT is an awesome workout! (Again, mind the pot-smoking teens at night. They're a little slow moving but chances are good seeing you will freak them out enough for them to scatter.)
label: POS

text: Tequila's is a beautiful place, but the food leaves a lot to be desired. Our server, on the other hand, was great. I loved that he kept calling me and my friends "Senoritas" (until he broke, once, at the end, and called us "Ladies," ah well) though at first I thought it was a little too cheesy. text: I went to Alma de Cuba for my birthday for grown-up dinner with my husband WITHOUT the kids for a change. We were in the Rittenhouse Square area and wandered the neighborhood eyeballing restaurants and their menus until we found something that appealed to both of us. We didn't have reservations and were initially told they couldn't accomodate us. But we left our names and got a table about 30 minutes later. I'm glad we were able to get in because Alma de Cuba provided one of the best meals I've ever had. With the exception of one thing, the food was orgasmic! The ambiance is intimate, dimly lit, urban-chic for professionals and young couples- definitely not a good place for children. The pricey menu is an eclectic mix conceptually based on the flavors of Cuban cuisine. I opted for the tapas approach to a meal and ordered a bunch of small items in lieu of an entree. I thoroughly enjoyed 4 of the 5 items I chose. I began my meal with what turned out to be my least favorite choice, the Sanchocho de Pollo. This soup consisted of a delicious lime, chicken and coconut broth with dry, overcooked chicken and mushy vegetables. The soup had nice flavors; I think perhaps I just caught it on an off day. Then I had the Royal Palm dates. Although I had reservations about it when I ordered it, they turned out to be one of the most delicious things I have ever eaten in my entire life. This appetizer is a perfect combination of flavors- almond stuffed dates with bacon and Cabrales blue cheese served on lettuce boats. I could have eaten a whole entire plate of them. They were heavenly! Next came the Empanada de Verde. These empanada (turnovers) were a tasty combination of Manchego cheese and spinach served on a artichoke escabeche. Parts of the escabeche were delicious, in particular the olives in the escabeche paired very well with the empanada. However, other parts of the vinegary escabeche just didn't mesh with the empanada and left a rancid overtone on my palate. I think it was a questionable pairing, but separately the empanada and escabeche would have been fine. Then I had a delicious salad, that happily, I have been able to replicate at home: Ensalada Blanca. The salad of frise' lettuce, feta cheese, grapes, almonds and Amaretto gelatin may sound a little odd, but was truly delicious and inspired. I completed my meal with a perfect cup of coffee and a dessert of the day. The artfully presented crepe was stuffed with fresh black cherries, homemade lemon-cardamom sorbet, and flavored whipped cream. Delectable! The tab set us back quite a bit, but we had the table for as long as we wanted it, and our server was a true professional who made it her business to cater to her customers. I highly recommend Alma de Cuba for a intimate dinner for foodies who love to have their palates challenged.

text: Sorry Mama Lovers, but we were very disappointed with our lunch here. On our trip to New Orleans for New Years, we craved a burger on New Years Day. It was packed, but no one was standing waiting, and two seats open at the bar. We asked if we can just sit and the bartender smiled and said sure, but just be warned it is only me working right now, they'll be a wait. Waiting is understandable at any highly reviewed joint, so we parked ourselves at the bar. Looking around the place, then realized everyone must have just sat down, no one had food in front of them... like 20 some people... but I was tired and slightly hungover, and just wanted a coke and a good burger. After a few minutes we got our cokes and ordered the chili cheeseburger with mac n cheese. We heard a table behind us complain that they wanted a burger done rare, and she said "sorry, my cook is slammed and all burgers are done med-well right now." Which we then realized she didn't ask us, and ours would be well too... hmmmm we don't want med-well, but too late. 2 slow refills and 45 minutes later our burger came out. We were starving and dug in... but all it did was ease the hunger pains. The burger was charred on the outside, and had no distinct flavor whatsoever. The chili was blah (out of can) and just didn't taste that great overall. Mac n cheese was pretty good though, actually better than the burger. Stopped about 3/4 way through burger because I ran out of coke, and realized that I had not put any ketchup or mustard on my burger. Sat for about 5-10 minutes waiting to get her attention for a refill and condiments. Overall, not a good experience. It is sad when you can say you've had better burgers at places that aren't even known for burgers... And living in Chicago, we go out for burgers all the time, at various places, and are rarely disappointed. The only reason I give 2 stars than 1, is because of the bartender/waitress/bus person all in one behind the bar - she warned us with a smile and continued working a crowded hungry complaining room of people with a smile, by herself. I give her the extra star that she can wear like a badge. Note to Yo Mamas: You are located in the French Quarter, it is New Years Day, with the Sugar Bowl happening later that day... did you not realize that you would be busy? Why only one staff? And with such a limited menu, I think charred burgers isn't going to help you keep your reputation of the best burger in New Orleans. I would like to give you the benefit of the doubt, and hope that all your staff called in sick and you just tried to make due... but you did not satisfy our burger needs :(

text: I took some time to read the other reviews before I wrote mine, so do not think the two stars is a snap judgment. Like many others, I've been coming to Zern's my entire life. I have been bringing my son there since he was born, and my 90+ year old Aunt tells stories of when it was new and in the middle of nowhere. But Zern's has changed, and not in a good way. I've watched the cafeteria close and never be replaced by a business that has stuck for more than a season. I've seen the flea market reduced from a huge venture to a few very old retailers hawking the same products they've been selling for the last ten years. Watched as craftsmen and real vendors have been replaced by dollar store vendors, siding salesmen, roof repair hawks, and empty stalls. Even the huge army navy store closed a couple years ago. replaced by a bunch of smaller craptastic hawkers. Spring Glenn farms, the last true purveyor of true PA Dutch food closed a few years back (Allentown Market Fair has a stall). There is only one Bakery left, and they are hit or miss with what they have, and Burts Farms, the best purveyor of meat in the market, closed this week. Years ago you'd see local farmers selling fresh produce along side their wives, who sold their jams, jellies, and fresh baked goods baked fresh early that morning. Do you remember? Zern's apparently does not. Yes - there are still some glimmers of hope. Little Richards, eternally staffed by teens still serves a decent lunch. The spice shop is well stocked and fair priced, and (some) of the fruit and veggie vendors still sell decent local produce. But the decent vendors are fast fleeing, and management seems content to let the market die. Maybe they'll put in a nice Wal*Mart - wouldn't that be grand?

text: I loved Jones! I went this past Saturday when I was back in town to celebrate my birthday with my family. I chose to come to Jones for dinner, having heard about it before, and knowing my brother comes here often with his friends. The way I see Jones, and similar restaurants (i.e. other Starr restaurants) is that you're coming here not only to get a meal, but to also have an experience. You are going to this particular restaurant because of the unique atsmosphere. That said, I also expect the food to be good with decent sized portions. Upon entering Jones we were seated right away. This was about 5:30/6 on a Saturday night. The place was pretty full, but obviously not packed since we got a booth for 5 with no wait. We sat 2 on one side, 3 on the other in our booth. It was comfortable for my parents on their side, however elbow room was a bit tight for the 3 of us sitting on the other side. It wasn't as tight as some people have described it, though. I wasn't at all uncomfortable; it just made it difficult when we all needed to cut our food at the same time. This was not a huge deal. Theme: The décor of Jones is exactly how others have described it: retro 70's, complete with avocado green booths, wood paneling, orange chairs and funky lighting fixtures. I absolutely loved it. Menu: While the menu is not huge, there are certainly a number of meals to choose from, as well as a wide variety of food from seafood, steak, pasta, and typical favorites like chicken pot pie and meatloaf. There are also a bunch of sandwiches as well. Menu is available on their website. Service: Despite what some may have said about their service, we had no problems. Our waitress even brought my dad's half eaten meal back under the heat lamp to keep warm while he got up to take an important call. Either way, I try not to judge a place based on their service unless I've gone a few times and still have a problem. You can get a bad/snobbish/inattentive server anywhere, from a 5 star restaurant to a local dive, and unfortunately unless you address that with the server or manager, it may not change. But again, we had no issues, just good service. Food: All of us were happy with the food. First of all, the portions were large so I felt the prices were justified. Secondly, despite what I've read on here, I would not put the quality of this food in the same range as a diner - it's most definitely above. While the menu items may have included diner-type meals, you can't forget that it's a part of the theme of this place. What would a retro-themed restaurant be without serving those at-home favorites? The quality of food was what I would expect for the price and type of restaurant. The 5 of us shared two orders of the pierogies as an appetizer. We all raved about how good they were, I definitely recommend them. However, while I found all the portions to be large on other foods, there were only 3 pierogies to an order. Slightly pricey for only 3, but I would order them again because they were that good. For dinner, my mom ordered the chicken pot pie which she was unable to finish due to the size. My dad ordered the pistachio crusted tilapia, and my boyfriend had the spicy jambalaya (and loved it). I went with the make your own salad - there were so many things on the menu that I wanted, but I've been on a major salad kick lately, and when I saw how huge the salads were, I was sold. I have to say, the mini clipboard/checklist sitting on the table for ordering the personal salad was a cute touch as well. Lastly, my brother, who has been here many times, never ordering the same thing twice, tried a hamburger this time. He admits that it was not the most flavorful hamburger and won't order it again, but still loves everything else he's eaten here (including the crabcake which I was considering ordering). Dessert: My dad and I each ordered the strawberry shortcake -delicious, and the boys each ordered the chocolate cake, which was actually served with a cold glass of milk. A cute idea and perfect touch! It's safe to say that I'd like to go to Jones again when I'm back in my home area sometime. I enjoyed the food, the atmosphere was fun and unique, and the prices were pretty much what they should be for this type of place. The dress code can range from casual to dressy, meaning whatever you wear in that range you'd fit in. I recommend Jones if you're looking for a fun place to get a good meal in the city.

text: Volpe real estate rents and sells almost exclusively in the graduate hospital neighborhood of philadelphia. from my experience, they charge low rents and expect their tenants to deal with poorly maintained apartments. their service lowers the bar for philadelphia landlords that already have a terrible reputation. let me give you a few examples to serve as warning. 1) when i looked at my apartment, the tenant had painted the walls dark green, bright yellow, and brown. not my taste. Volpe assured me that they would paint it white and that since there would be a two week overlap between her moving out and my moving in, he assured me that the apartment would be all ready for me to move in when my lease started. however, on the day after my lease started, i went to my new apartment to do some cleaning before moving in. when i arrived, i saw a small man climbing out of the basement window of my apartment into the street. after a very confusing conversation, i came to understand that this was not a burglar, but a workman who was doing a lot of work on my apartment and the one above mine. he was a painter, he said proudly, although the painting was atrocious. he was also fixing the roof, some pipes, and the washing machine (unsuccessfully). without giving me any notice, or alerting me when I picked up the keys, Volpe and the owner had arranged to have 3 workmen work on my apartment almost every day for the first 3 weeks I lived there. They came without notice, at every hour of the day, worked terribly slowly, and left the old pipes that they had removed all over. when i reminded the real estate company that they had assured me that all of this work was going to be done before moving in, they shrugged. Not their problem. 2- the first time that i used the dishwasher was about 2 months into my lease. when I ran it, I found that no one had ever hooked up a water pipe to the washer! Volpe sent the painter twice to fix it, unsuccessfully. Each time I was told it was fixed, but still- no water. It wasn't until a few phone calls of hounding that they actually send someone who installs and fixes dishwashers. 3- the tiles in the bathtub all came loose some months into my lease. I alerted them and they sent someone to fix it while I was on vacation. When I returned, they had finished the job, but had left their tools all over the bathroom and a white film of dust all over the bathroom and the entire hallway. have they never heard of clean up? Renter Beware. If you already rent from them, make sure to keep a record of everything that goes wrong, about every conversation with them, and maybe even put everything in writing. Assume nothing.
label: NEG

text: Reading the other reviews for this place I think we agree on about everything that is wrong with the place. Except that I found the food to be foul. I had the Bumblebee stew, which was ok I guess. There was a good sweetness too it, and it was a plethora of some of my favorite things, including black beans, corn, rice and chicken. The problem came in that there was an overbearingly bold undertone of spiciness that destroyed the flavor of this dish. The misses had the Crawfish Etouffee, which smelled and tasted offensive. The taste was bitter and the craw fish tasted like it was frozen then left to thaw then used 5 days later. Simply aweful. We both ended up downing the bread for some substance before leaving over half of the dishes unkempt. Looks like its same ol' same ol' for this place and the bad food. Our server, once he showed up, was a really nice guy. We did have to wait exceedingly long, which is a cardinal sin in my book of restaurant faux pas. The iced tea was that brisk garbage off the fountain and they don't have splenda. The atmosphere is exactly the same as it was when it was Badda Boomz. Truly, the guy that owns this building needs to just make it a beer house and leave it at that, maybe have some simple fast bar food, but please do us and yourself a favor and stop trying to run a restaurant with a full (ish) menu. On a lighter note, they still have the most unbelievable beer list I have ever seen anywhere, ever.
label: NEG

text: One of the best sandwich shops in the city has somehow found a home in West Collingswood Heights. Roast pork with long hots is a messy but wonderful lunch. You will use any and all napkins while eating...and that is a good thing.

text: Visited New Orleans for the New Year.... In a Nutshell: Good Location Bad Room Service Terrible Housekeeping Lousy Front Desk Service I was incredibly disappointed in this hotel for many reasons. On first arrival I was pleased and had high expectations. The hotel lobby was swanky and clean looking, neat furniture and great lighting. I was surprised that our room was so small and barely furnished considering we had upgraded to the suite. We had a decent view though and the room was nice enough, regardless of size it was still fair value. We arrived late and hit the streets. The walk to Bourbon is about 5 minutes. As far as location goes it's a great place to be because you are close enough to reap the benefits of Bourbon but far enough away to get away from all the craziness and noise. This was about the only good thing about the hotel. New Year's eve we slept in and missed the available cleaning times. No big deal, we had gotten in late. New Years day the cleaners came and made the bed, that was it. We were shocked, they left our dirty glasses, didn't take the dirty towels despite leaving them on the ground as instructed when we wanted them changed. Much to my horror the cleaners rehung a washcloth that was clearly soiled. They emptied the garbage, but left our champagne buckets and empty bottle. They did NOTHING else. We are not messy people and do not require much in the way of cleaning, but we do have expectations when it comes to hotels. As it turned out this was the only time our room was serviced during our 5 day stay. In particular I spoke with the man at the front desk and let him know that we would be stepping out for half the day and would like our room serviced...by then it was day 3. He said of course, when we returned five hours later, the room had not been cleaned. I was furious at this point. Again the next day the room was not serviced because we were in the room at the time that was convenient for the hotel staff. Unbelievable. When I tried to talk with the front desk staff about it, all I got was excuses. Not apologies, not "how can we make this better?", nothing. In fact they made it seem as though it was our fault for being in our room in the middle of the afternoon or early morning. When we checked out I was so disgusted with our room I was beside myself. The front desk again failed to acknowledge fault on their part and offered us no compensation. Additionally I think I may have gotten food poisoning from room service, which came without trays and in plastic containers and cost over $150, which I didn't realize until the next day! We had a terrible cheese plate, a soup, salad, and some fish. $150? Really? So so so disappointed. I will never go back. Don't order the food and don't stay if you like a clean room.
label: NEG

text: First off, I would like to say that tipping is not required. I've never been one to not tip, but in this case, i really shouldn't have. I've normally had a decent experience at this place. I typically enjoy their food, especially the soft shell crab. My friends and I went their for dinner one Friday night. It wasn't busy so we got promptly seated and served. One of my friends orders a dish to go for later. As the bill came up, I calculated our total and included an appropriate tip for the dishes we were served. I did not include a tip for the dish that was ordered to go. My general thinking is to not tip on orders that were not served to me. We pay our tab and got ready to leave. The person at the door stops us and questions our tip. I told him we left an appropriate tip for the stuff that was ordered there and not for the to go item. He was adamant about us leaving a larger tip. The Oakland in me should have just shrugged it off and kept on walking. In the end, we gave him an extra $2. $2 doesn't really amount to me and I really could care less, but it's the principle behind it! Why are you going to expect me to pay tip on a dish I ordered to go? If I had not sat down for dinner and ordered a to go item, would the restaurant have expected me to tip for that as well? Like I said, I generally have decent experiences here.. but because of this incident, I will no longer be returning.
label: NEG

It was satisfying but not overly filling- and that whole wheat pita was more flavorful than the average whole wheat pita for sure! I also tried the cucumber salad, which was okay, but definitely not worth $2.95. The counter staff was really friendly and offered suggestions of toppings for my pita. The place was immaculately clean. I'll definitely be back to try another of their delicious pitas!

text: We stayed here for two days for a Christmas business party, it was nice. We had a double queen room all done up in pink(yuck), the room was nice had a few chairs, a small table, a desk, and a makeup mirror. The bathroom was nice as well, pretty typical of a hotel with the shower bath combo but a big enough bath that you could lay down and soak, but not big enough to share. The beds were uncomfortable, but I think most casino beds are so you can't sleep and get up to gamble more. I was also a little cold at night and had to take the blanket off the other bed to stay warm. The hotel itself was nice, with 4-5 different restaurants, ranging from nice steak house, oyster bar, cafe, to your typically buffet.(see separate reviews of restaurants) There were of course many bars, we tended to say at the one in front by the front desk because you could pretty much see everyone who walked by and we were a large party so we pulled a ton of tables together and drank plenty. I noticed on the weekend mornings that they had a make it yourself bloody Mary bar for $5 with an assortment of vodkas and spicy and plain tomato juice with all kinds of condiments to add to your drink, I am not a bloody Mary person so I didn't partake but it looked nice. Major bonus was the Starbucks right by the bar we took over. I need caffeine in the morning and am pretty partial to a venti white chocolate mocha and I honed in on the Starbucks within seconds of checking in to our room. The amenities were pretty usual with a free fitness room for guest, a salon/spa(see separate review), and nice looking indoor pool. As far as gambling went I personally didn't do so well but hey I did break even so I guess I didn't do so bad either, but a few people that were with our group won a few hundred. I played a few slots, they had a good selection of nickle, quarter, dollar, and even penny. Then I hit the $5 black jack table, I went with a single deck and started off doing very good I really like the dealer she was awesome, but then the enviable happened they switched dealers, now I should have walked away when that happened but no I decided I was doing good so I would stay that was my mistake the next dealer was hot, and I lost, but hey you win some and you lose some. We did have a party in the pool terrace room, it was next to the pool on the 5th floor, they decorated it nice and pretty, had a no host bar, a DJ, a tiny dance floor, and a buffet...we had a good time I can't wait for next year.
label: POS

text: Pinsetter is great! Let me preface my review by saying that I was slowly but surely starting to be come one of "those" Jersey people who go to Philly for just about everything. For so long, the options on this side of the river had been so limited, but Pinsetter and a few other places are slowly making me change my ways. I had my birthday party at Pinsetter on Saturday, 10/9. My brother had thrown his girlfriend's birthday party there a few months before, and I know my brother, so I knew Pinsetter wasn't the stereotypical grungy, smoky bowling alley. I worked with Danielle to plan my party, and she was very helpful and assisted my in finding the combination of details to personalize my party. The night of the party, I really didn't have to do anything but show up with balloons and my cake. Everyone was very helpful, and our server, Kelly, was very friendly and attentive. The live music was a plus, too! There was a slight misunderstanding as to the price of the bowling - my friends and I were under the impression that the cost was per game, but it was really per person, per game. No biggie - I'll just know that next time. All in all, I had a great time, and despite my terrible bowling skills, I will definitely go back to Pinsetter!

text: Our dog loves it here! We often take him to this dog park or the one off of Longford Road. Reservoir Dog Park is a nice shaded place for your pup to run around and socialize with other dogs. There are tons of trees and forest like elements so this dog park isn't just the typical open field fenced in. There are also benches, which are decently clean for a dog park. If you go to the back there are also a few short trails to walk around. There are 2 sections: one for the small dogs and one for larger dogs. Appears that dog owners are good about picking up after their pets and the people who take their dogs here are friendly. The negatives include the amount of bugs (tons of those little gnats, so go when there's a slight wind and you'll be fine) and the owners who let their dogs attack other dogs and think their dogs are "playing" (but I guess you find that anywhere). Come bring your pup to play here!

text: We ate here for a wedding reception. The staff were very attentive and really gracious. There were about 80 or so people at the reception and the courses came out a little slow but that can be expected when serving so many people. We started with fresh mixed greens salads with a light balsamic vinaigrette. The issue was that there was little to no dressing on our salads. So, it was a very, very dry salad. We kept reaching for our drinks and hoped no one would start choking. The entree was fabulous. It was shrimp and a filet mignon. The shrimp had been cooked in garlic - and I mean lots of garlic in that you can smell it when they put it in front of you. A little too much garlic, but luckily everyone was eating the shrimp. They were cooked perfectly and were very warm when we received them. Now, the reason for the 4 stars is the Filet Mignon. It was cooked perfectly! And so, so tender and juicy. This is a steakhouse, and they definitely know how to cook a steak! One of the best steaks I have had!! And they were serving 80 people at once. We can not wait to go back and have a meal in their dining room. If you live in Philly and like steak, consider yourselves lucky!! What a find, we will be back!

text: Overall it's not a bad hotel, but I don't think I'll ever stay there again. It has a friendly staff and a convenient 'market,' but the lack of soundproofing turned out to be unbearable for me. I stayed there on the 1st floor for 3 nights this past week. On the first night, I had to listen along while my 2nd-floor neighbor watched TV all night. Then the next morning, that person's clock radio woke me up and ran for at least 15 minutes. I could easily tell when that person walked around his room. The second night was better, but the morning after that was awful--my next-door neighbor got up at about 5:00 am and had two conference calls. I heard both conversations so clearly as if they had been in my room. My co-worker who stayed on the same floor was also bothered by her neighbors' noise. Honestly most business travelers are not noise-makers, but the lack of sound proofing at this hotel may make your stay a nightmare.

text: The studio is beautiful. The massage area is cozy, dark and soothing. And then there's the ever-talented Zoe. Aside from getting semi-regular massage tune-ups over the years , I've gone to Zoe for trouble-fixes more than once. I have recurring problems with my back and several bulging disks that act up during times of stress, etc. At one point in 2001 when I had a flare-up, I wasn't able to touch my toes for 3 months. I had some deep-tissue massage from Zoe, who assessed and worked with me to see how much pressure I could stand. It was truly a miracle. I went from being someone who, even with narcotic pain killers, couldn't stand up straight, sit comfortably, lie down flat, or walk without pressing my hand to my spine like a rudder, and who took 5 minutes to get in & out of a car (even though I was only 25 at that point), to someone who had 50% more mobility in 2-3 days and 85% mobility in a week. I'd gone to 5 or 6 different specialists at Ochsner, tried a chiropractor, had MRIs, bone scans, etc., and no one could figure it out, but Zoe was able to help. I'm not saying she fixed it--the disks are still bulging--but she was able to realign everything that was so far out of whack and therefore help me hugely. Zoe performed miracles on my neck when it was out because of a strange desk setup at work and my computer responsibilities suddenly increased. Zoe was kind enough to squeeze me in last-minute, even thought it was during JazzFest, and in an hour she took away a week's worth of shooting neck pain, not to mention helping to balance out the rest of my body that was trying to compensate for the neck. Basically, she's fantastic and although there are other places that'll throw rose petals at you or greet you with a cocktail, I'll buy my own champagne, thanks very much, and go with an exponentially better masseuse. (And I live one block from one of the biggest and most posh day-spas in town.)
label: POS

Definitely will be going back.

text: I remember reading an old review about this restaurant where the patron complained about the horrible service he received. I thought it couldn't possibly be that bad. That review has for some reason been deleted and all that is left are the other glowing reviews. Well, I tried this place recently because the location fit the bill. My experience more closely mirrors the upset reviewer. I will give them kudos for having the best clam chowder I've ever eaten. Seriously, it is really good. That said, the service was horrible and my opinion is that the food is overpriced. The waitress promptly delivered our menus but then disappeared without taking an initial drink order. Now, there was only 1 other table occupied at this time so it wasn't other customers keeping her busy. Instead she was involved in what must have been a very important conversation with the other waitress. This went on for 10 minutes (and with just 5 items on the menu, you really don't need that much time to decide). So after coming just short of waving our hands in the air, the waitress finally came to the table and asked if we had decided (still no drink order). I went with the entrée special salad. Peaches and blueberries on spinach with blue cheese. In my opinion, $11 is a lot of money for a salad that doesn't have meat on it. I was unimpressed. The hamburger my mom ordered was thin as a piece of paper (as other reviewers noted) and about twice as big as the tiny bun (think: generic brand Kroger bun) that was attempting but miserably falling short of containing it. Some might argue that this place has charm ... my thought is just that there are many other charming non-chain places in this city - with better service and prices. Oh and they still aren't accepting credit cards. Cash or check only.

text: Kids grow....quickly! So I choose to not spend too much on kids clothes. I've got 2 girls and I can't help but want to buy the newest looks and dress them to look their cutest. Once Upon A Child is a retail store that offers new and gently used stuff for kids and maternity clothing. You can bring in your items and they will pay you on the spot for items they think they'll be able to sell again. The first time you try to sell them items they may seem picky to you, they even use a black light to find stains not visible to the eye. Lately I've been buying clothing there for my girls. The majority of the clothes are in great shape, or still have the tags on. You can shop with your kids because they have a little sectioned off area where they play a kids movie and have toys. Most of the time I find it easier to go by myself because their inventory is so packed together that you will need time to go through to find what you are looking for. The other day I bought two pairs of name brand jeans for my daughter, a brand new Razor helmet, a dress, and 3 shirts for $35.00. And when they've outgrown them if they're still in decent shape and not out of fashion, I can sell them back!
