text: I went here on a date once. I loved this place, so I'm not sure why I haven't gone back. I think I forgot about it when I tried to repress all memories of the guy the date was with... Hm, the food sure was good, though. That's it, I'm going back there. Soon. The decor is really cool, very modern. The seats were comfy. The food was fantastic - fresh, tasty, perfectly presented, and nicely portioned. Plus, the coolest part? The servers are really, really nice and professional. The waitress even showed us how to fold our cloth napkins to look like a lotus flower because we commented on how cool their napkins were on the place settings when we were seated. How nice was that? UPDATE: My ROTD of this place reminded me to update my review, now that I've been there a few more times with friends. I like this place even more than I did the first time. The food has definitely got some heat, even if you ask for it with the least amount of spice they can cook with (they have a spice rating of 1 to 5, with one being the least, when you order). Last time I went, I got the pad thai and calamari for an appetizer, both of which were good. The time before that, I was more daring and got something (don't remember the name) that involved shrimp in a coconut milk-based spicy sauce with pineapple chunks over rice. It was so spicy (on #1 spice, I'm a wimp) that it made me sweat, but it was so, so tasty. The most daring person I have eaten there with is my boyfriend, and he has gotten a dish with a #3 spicy rating. He turned bright red and started to sweat, but he said he liked it. I tried a soup he got before, and it was really good, even if it was too hot for me to eat a whole bowl myself. The only thing is that this place gets crowded, now that people know it's there, so get there early on Friday or Saturday night for dinner to get a table without a wait. And sometimes, the food takes a while to come out, but it's well worth being patient.

text: I still don't get the love for this place and trust me it is not for a lack of trying. I went there today for lunch and was once again completely underwhelmed. It is hard to get edible food at at restaurant early in the morning in Northern Liberties. Dew Inn is about the only other option and their food is not so edible. I have tried the french toast and an omelet and found nothing special about either. I tried an item off the lunch menu today, a turkey burger with pepper jack cheese and a side of potato salad. The burger was waaayyy greasy which is kind of disappointing since I typically order a turkey burger since they aren't as greasy as typical burgers. The meat itself was kind of falling apart and looked haphazardly slapped together. The only things I really enjoyed were my tiny side of potato salad and the side of pickled veggies. They do have really good coffee as well. I finished eating but hung out and drank coffee for a while reading the hilarious satire of Craig LaBan in the PW when the servers were goofing off throwing things at each other and a crumbled up piece of paper hit me in the face. I was not super upset and did not make a big deal of it but I think it sums up my feeling of the place. At the least I would have enjoyed an offer of some sort of compensation but I got a sincere apology from all parties involved, basically all of the servers working. I think I have officially written Honeys off and feel pretty good about it.

text: I was brought here for lunch during my interview at LSU. This is a quaint little restaurant that has an old fashioned feel to it. All the tables have fresh white table cloths, very welcoming decor. The waiter was very friendly and helpful. If you're vegetarian, as one in our group was, the selections are very limited. She ended up getting the oyster salad w/ no oysters and no bacon. Pretty much an overpriced Ceaser salad. The rolls that they serve before the meal are amazing. Warm enough to melt a pat of butter and it breaks down into flaky goodness. Loved them! OMG, soooo good! For my appetizer I got the gumbo. I'm not an expert at gumbo by any means, but it was really good. It wasn't too much rice and it had a good heat to it, mild for my taste, but any heat is better than none. I would recommend it highly. For my main course I had the ham sandwich with egg, that was then dredged in custard an fried I think. It was soooo rich. Too rich actually. They must have put a ton of cheese in the custard coating, because I was tasting cheese everywhere. It really masked the sandwich to the point where I felt like I was eating blocks of cheese. The ham sandwich itself is quite plain, but the waiter recommended this if you wanted to try something new. It was indeed new to me. I hate wasting food and I'm ashamed to say that I barely got through half of it. It wasn't bad, it was just too much. I wouldn't be surprised if it was more than 1500 calories. It's a novel concept and they do it well, but it didn't impress me enough that I would order it again. This place is a little pricey, but I think the food was all high quality and I enjoyed my experience here. If you go, take advantage of the bread and consider the gumbo.

text: Just had lunch at Lola and I have to say I'm pretty disappointed - after all these great Yelp reviews I was expecting more. It's Thursday and the place was deserted when my friend and I got there just before noon. Only two other people came in while we were dining. The waitress was pleasant and gave us plenty of time to decide, and there looks like a ton of great things on their menu. It's pretty hot & humid so I decided against the lobster corn dog w/mac & cheese, which was what really intrigued me. Instead, I got a sandwich - the Medusa: spinach & feta spread, muenster, mozzarella, white cheddar and roasted tomato on sourdough. Plus a side of frittes. My friend ordered Antoinette: strip steak, gruyere, onions & mushrooms. "Roasted tomatoes" says something to me other than "sliced romas," which is what was on the sandwich. It pretty much tasted like a grilled cheese & tomato. Which isn't bad, but I was thinking there'd be more green on it from the spinach spread. It was way too cheesy for my taste, though it was definitely a tasty grilled cheese sandwich. The fries were warm when they came out but cooled quickly; my beef with any restaurant that serves fries is that they should be served in a cone like Belgians do, so they stay hot. Not Lola's fault that we're not in Europe, I suppose, though a good idea should be cross-cultural. They were definitely homemade and had the slightly greasy consistency of really good homemade fries. Quite tasty. The bread was fresh and grilled just right - very tasty bread. Jay's sandwich was a big disappointment: The meat was tough and one piece of it was half gristle! No one wants to dismantle a sandwich to cut off the gristle & then reassemble. Blech. Why serve that? It wasn't that it was bad, but for the price & all the good reviews the place has gotten I just expected more. If someone suggests Lola in the future, I'll go and try something different - maybe a crepe, since that's why Jay loves the place and that's what he usually gets. But I won't be craving it between now & then.
label: NEG

text: Ate at Ricardo's Saturday night with another couple. Looking at the menu beforehand, I was prepared for a mediocre experience. I was pleasantly surprised. The atmosphere was great for a date. I would say this is an excellent place for a business lunch or dinner, too. We had an opportunity to sit and chat with the owner while waiting for the other couple, then for four of us had a drink at the bar and continued the conversation. She was very friendly and helpful - obviously willing to do whatever it took to make our visit enjoyable. The menu is pretty standard Italian. We had Lasagna, Cannelloni, Chicken Parmesan and Eggplant Parmesan. All of the appetizers looked fantastic and the two I tried were great. A big plus here is they have two sizes for their pasta dishes. The smaller size is just right for most people and most are priced UNDER $7, so it's an amazing value. Red wine by the pour was from $6 to $8 - very reasonable for a nicer restaurant, and the pours were very generous while not so full that you couldn't swirl the wine. One complaint that keeps this from being a five: the house salad was only okay - light and vinegary with not as much cheese as we would like. A big bonus of eating here is that Bailey's Chocolate Bar and 33 Wine Bar are on the same block, so you can visit either for an after dinner drink or dessert. Lafayette Square is my favorite date place in St. Louis, hands down and I'll be recommending RIcardo's a lot from here on out.

text: This place has consistently disappointed. On two occassions I have made reservations for large parties and waited over 45 minutes to be seated. On both occasions we arrived on time and with everyone in our party. On both occasions the restaurant was over-crowded and the hostess was completely overwhelmed. The first time I went there, my party of 10 waited for about an hour after our reservation time and finally sat down to eat a mediocre meal. The food is inexpensive and average. The dishes are the same italian dishes that you get anywhere else. Except elsewhere you get to sit down and eat your average italian food soon after you walk in. Most recently, my party of 11 was told upon arrival that our table would be ready within a few minutes. That was at 7:30. At 7:45, the hostess told us that it would be another 10 minutes. At 8:00, no table. All the while we told the hostess (who was impatient, if not arrogant) that we were pressed for time and could not wait much longer. Yet, we were once again told that it would just be a few minutes more and that we'd be seated ASAP. Finally, at 8:15, we walked out disgusted and hungry. When we indicated that we were leaving in a last ditch attempt to expediate our table, the hostess simply said she was sorry and that we could do whatever we wanted to do. She gave us no reason to return in the future. Needless to say, we will not be going back. To say that this place was overbooked is an understatement. During our 45 minutes of standing in the doorway and the sidewalk outside in the cold (there is no place to sit and wait inside), we watched two other parties of 12 and 15 people squeeze in only to be given the same song and dance that we got. As we were leaving, we spoke to another group of people who had been waiting for just as long as we had been waiting. This is the only place that I have been to in Philadelphia where your reservation does not entitle you to actually eat your meal in a timely manner but instead entitles you and your party to stand around in a hallway that is as crowded as (and strangely reminiscent of) a casino bus terminal.

text: I'm probably the last person who'd spend $60 on a haircut. Before I saw Danielle, I went to the same stylist for years and, starting in college, decided to be super punk rock and DIY my hair. (It, uh, didn't go too well, though I could eventually manage a barely-passable bang trim.) But I had a little extra money burning a hole in my pocket after starting a new job, I was in the area, and they had a free appointment for that day, so why not? More money for a cut means it's better, right? I'll preface my reaction by saying that my hair sucks. It's thin, it's wavy, occasionally it manages to be both flat and frizzy. I usually wear it tied back, but my big resolution for this year was to ditch the ponytail and get a nice cut. Danielle actually took the time to hear me bitch and moan about my hair, then steer me towards a more flattering and practical cut for my hair type and face shape. Instead of giving me a style that wouldn't work or look bad (like the terrible Amelie-inspired 'do I rocked through most of high school), Danielle opted for a more subtle, layered approach. I came out of the salon feeling like my hair was looking and behaving the way it was meant to. It wasn't drastically different but it felt right. I think my hair actually bounced as I walked through Rittenhouse. Best of all, it still looks awesome after a couple of weeks.

text: This is quite possibly the worst cajun creole food on the planet. I can only say possibly because it's the worst I've ever had and I haven't been to every cajun restaurant in the world. But I'm pretty sure I could get away with making the claim of it being the worst period without catching too much flack. Where to start? I had some questions before ordering and the young lady (YL) behind the counter wouldn't let me finish a question before blurting out an answer to what she thought my question might be. YL: Are you ready to order? Me:I have some questions. Can you... YL: I can give you samples of stuff. Me: Thanks, but what I really would like to know is... YL: It's all on the board if you want to try it. Me: What is the... YL: blah blah blah blah blah I finally gave up. The chicken and mushroom etoufee tasted like someone had rushed to make milk gravy and accidentally spilled some rice in it. Imagine gravy made with too much flour and then undercooked. This is so far from a roux, that I thought we were at Bob Evans. The seafood gumbo looked and tasted like beef barley soup, complete with shredded beef and rice instead of barley. Still can't quite figure that one out. We sifted through it, looking for something that resembled seafood in the peppery beef broth and finally gave up. The jambalaya was watery, bland and had no cajun flavor characteristics. It was literally like someone made uncle Ben's rice and at the last minute said, "darn, we forgot the sausage and all that other jambalaya type stuff. Quick, throw some in it before you serve it." The crawfish casserole was...um...well, just read about the jambalaya above and replace "jambalaya" with "crawfish casserole". Shrimp Po'boy. It's supposed to be on a hard bun, not a soft one. The shrimp and the side of hush puppies had the same flavor. I'm assuming there is deepfry'omatic 3000 in the kitchen where everything goes in one end and comes out the other. It was about the only edible thing in our meal. Certainly the only thing we finished. Tea is out of the fountain, not brewed and tasted like a mud puddle. Long story short, it get's one star only because you can't give a place negative stars. For $7 less, we could have gone to Yats and had larger portions of the best cajun creole food outside of New Orleans. No offense to Mia, but this is not what cajun creole food is supposed to taste like. We really hoped this would be good, because it's so close to our home compared to Yats. We'll happily make the extra drive. I need to add this after the fact. i went to their website and looked at the menu. The pictures of the dishes are nothing like what was served to us. Extremely misleading to say the least. Edited on 6/27/08 to add the following: I'm not affiliated with any restaurant, let alone a competitor of mudbugs. My taste buds are just fine and able to differentiate between all kinds of flavors, textures and consistencies.. When I was there almost a year ago, both the food and service were horrible. Perhaps in the last 11 months they've gotten their act together. If so, kudos to them. They had a long way to go and it wouldn't have been easy. Judging by the other reviews, you'll either love the place or never go back a second time.

text: I've been to the Swift Half about four times since it opened, so this is a pretty well thought out review. Although I don't have any pictures from my trips, I do have a good amount of insight. Here it comes: I expected this new Good Dog outpost to have excellent food. I went recently with Allie, John, and Rachel and they were all ready for dinner. They ordered mussels, fish and chips, and cucumber sandwiches, respectively. I had a few mussels, and they were decent, but this is clearly not the spot you want to hit for mussels. The fish and chips looked delicious when they were served, but further investigation revealed that they were overly breaded and couldn't keep up with Memphis Taproom. Rachel commented that her small appetizer was good, but also that she could have made something better at home. Needless to say, the food is not a selling point. To be honest, I'm also disappointed with the beer list. In fairness, Swift Half has some good beers on tap. But when a week passes in between visits and not a single tap changes, I'm not inclined to return anytime soon. The beer list is not totally uninspired, with Southampton, Flying Fish, Stoudt's, Brooklyn, even Chimay represented on tap. The bottle list is extensive and well priced. One nice part of the menu is the inclusion of small plates of meat and cheese that could be matched to beer, if you're so inclined. Currently, they have the Six Points Sweet Action on tap, which I raved about ever since the first time I had it at Sidecar. It's not as amazing as my memory made it, but I was glad to see this hard to find beer on tap. It's still excellent, and a nice find for a rare style: American Blonde Ale. Service here is meh. It's not bad, I think it's pretty hit or miss depending on who's working. My favorite thing about this spot, and the reason that I keep coming back, is the outdoor seating. The piazza is a really cool area, and it's great when the Phillies are on the big screen. Inside Swift Half is a normal bar, and I wouldn't eat or drink inside. Outdoor seating is closed at 11:30 on weeknight, which can be annoying if you want to just hang out, or are shoo-ed inside as you're finishing your last pint. Bottom Line: This is just another spot on my list of places that are most remarkable for outdoor seating. As the list grows, Swift Half loses favor in my book. The food is okay, but I wouldn't want to come here for a meal. Really, this spot is only a go to for me if they continue to have beers that aren't available elsewhere in the city. I was trying to decide between 2 and 3 stars, but this place just doesn't make the cut in the end.

text: I want to understand. I really do. Will someone please explain what happened in the years since I stopped clubbing? I was so dumbfounded and confused, but aware of the line behind me to get in - that I signed and rushed up the stairs. The decor is hard to figure out. Clearly this was once a nice victorian brownstone - but it's been adulterated to a sickening degree. There is no more opulence, in my opinion. The walls are decorated with ugly murals. The floors are trashed (as you would expect in a bar.) The carpet is nasty. We get to the 2nd floor bar - and I order a drink. Vodka and soda. Hubby orders a beer - and the bartender says "but that's not free." I guess we'd stumbled into a happy hour - no cover, free well drinks and miller lite. (I can see you college kids tripping over each other to get there PRONTO!) I was handed my drink in a plastic cup (just like when I was in college) and hubby stuck with his pricey (not free) Yeungling. The DJ. Seriously, he was SO BAD. He really wanted to be clever and original with his spinning - but what we got instead was awkward transitions, overlapping songs with different beats that DJ AM wouldn't attempt to force together. I wanted to dance! But instead I'd stop mid-beat to try to figure out exactly what dude was up to and how I should be groovin' next. Maybe I just got an off night. I'm certainly not complaining about no cover and free drinks. But I was thoroughly confused by the "club" thing that apparently EVERYONE can join without a fee. I guess that paper I signed was freeing O.N.E. Rittenhouse from any liability should I have too many free drinks and get behind the wheel of my car.

text: It's hard for me to understand the rave reviews about this place. I think the food quality is decent, but it sure isn't GREAT. You order and pay at the register, then shuffle over to the employees who are actually cooking the meat and assembling the pitas. Where they then ask you what you just ordered. You're asking me? I ordered it over there--ask the guy who took my money 20 seconds ago. It just screams 'amateur' is all. Hell, even Subway can figure this one out. Why can't you? Food quality, not bad. They have a decent selection of fillings that apparently can just be mixed and matched. And by that, I mean there is NO STANDARD to what goes in what. If I order a gyros pita, should I have to ask for tzatziki and feta cheese? Answer: no. That's what comes standard with gyros. Here, you DO have to ask. Same thing with the spicy chicken pita (I forget the name) but wouldn't you assume that I want.... spicy sauce? Is this concept THAT HARD for this place? I only come here when I have a BOGO coupon (that's Buy one get one free, but the word FREE is implied so the trailing F is unnecessary--it's BOGO and not BOGOF). 7 bucks and change for two pitas seems like the right price point. 7 and change for ONE? Not so much. So after you finish shopping at Whole Foods, drive your Prius on down to Pita Pit and order an alfalfa sprout pita. And don't forget to ask for alfalfa sprouts in that, otherwise, amazingly enough, they won't be included. Oh, and if you ARE driving a Prius, could you please make sure you know how to turn your car off when your accelerator sticks and your brakes fail? Otherwise Darwin's gonna getcha. "The driver couldn't figure out how to turn off the car as it was accelerating, then the car hit a wall and burst into flames". Our group of 4 ordered right away and sat down at the counter, with only 3 other customers in the whole place, and it was, no joke, over 45 minutes before we got our food. The guy at the grill cooked every single item one at a time -- I mean, for an order of 2 pancakes and 1 egg, he didn't even cook the egg while the pancakes were cooking. It was unbelievable. The waitress was bitchy (although trying to be friendly, odd combination) and gave orders away to the wrong people. While we were waiting, we had plenty of time to read all the good reviews on the wall -- like the 2004 newspaper article where they proudly said the Awful Awful would never change from $3.50, no matter how much money they lost on each one, right below the "Awful Awful, $5.50" sign. This is a bit unfair, $5.50 would still be a great deal assuming the quality is anything like what it was (unless it takes an hour to get it -- what do they do when the place isn't completely empty?), but it's amusing nonetheless. We have to give them a second star because the quality of the food was actually pretty good, although most of the menu items don't seem like much of a price value -- the biscuits & gravy were good and cheap, and a few of the specially-prices items are good value, but normal menu items aren't. The coffee was just plain awful, and we don't mean "big" or "good."

text: There's a reason La Dolce Via is a must-stop when I entertain out-of-town guests. It hits all the right notes with food, service and atmosphere. Food -- I've never hit LDV up for its relatively new dinner hours, but Sunday breakfast/brunch? Hells yeah! I typically get the blueberry pancakes and a side (or three) of potatoes, called hash. The pancaskes are bursting with blueberry goodness, and they're so fluffy. Four on a plate -- be a pig! Dump a ton of their yummy syrup on them, and you're good to go. The hash is delicious, too. The potatoes are diced and combined with tiny bits of onions, parsley, spices and other scrumptious things. One day, I'll order nothing but five plates of this stuff! I've also tried LDV's multiple berry pancakes and their new berry waffles -- all good stuff! In addition to breakfast foods, they have sandwiches, eggs, omelets and more. Don't forget about scones, cookies, cakes and more! And EVERYTHING is homemade! Service -- The good folks at LDV are out of this world. The same family members are there each time you visit, and they have honest-to-goodness conversations with you. No, seriously, it's not annoying! They'll talk to you about their food, zombies, the latest political scandal, whatever! They're some of the nicest food folks I've come across in St. Louis, and I'm totally happy to eat the yummy things they serve up. Oh, they bring your food pretty quickly, too. It should be assumed, considering the praise I just gave them above, but thought I'd throw it out there. Atmosphere -- LDV is charming, situated on a tree-lined corner on Taylor. It's one of those adorable, pointy buildings you find throughout the neighborhood, and you can't help but feel at home here. You can eat outside and watch the world go by, or venture indoors and take in the fab indie music, delicious smells, and variety of reading materials. Also awesome -- no smoking! FYI - You can drive to LDV, but why not take the Metrolink to the CWE station and walk south a few blocks? It's a lovely walk on a nice day. La Dolce Via seriously is one of my favorite places in St. Louis. I'm so proud that we have such fabulous restaurants that are run by people who love food and community!

text: I am a small business owner, so I always make it a priority to spend my money at local businesses. As other reviewers have indicated, things started well with the Tile Source. Having had a good experience, I returned to buy my second round of $415 of tile. The first red flag was that the $65 floor sealer was in a tiny bottle - a bottle so small that anyone might start to wonder, "Is this tiny bottle really worth $65?". As I soon found out, the answer is NO. Home Depot carries the same exact product for ~$30. I understand that small businesses have a hard time matching the price of an international corporation, but a $35 difference on a $65 product is unreasonable. When I went to return the sealer I was told that it is one of many many many items that they do not let you return. You might be hard pressed to find any items that they would actually allow you to return. They do publish their return policy; however, it is on the back of the receipt, so the first time you will see it is after it is too late and you have made your purchase. It is hard for me to imagine that this doesn't break standard business practices. The very clear outcome of their inflexible return policy is that the remaining tile I have yet to purchase (~$1200 worth) will be purchased elsewhere. Please read the other reviews. text: I don't know how Acme overcomes its temptation to just throw in the towel...its reputation for seafood, particularly oysters, has already been solidified; its location right off Bourbon Street guarantees that tourists, drunk and sober, will come in for some kind of fried seafood; and it's opened up several other locations in the gulf coast area. Yet somehow when three friends and I showed up at the restaurant purgatory time of 530pm for a quick bite, Acme lived up to the hype. After waiting on line for about 20 minutes, the friendly lady with the clipboard yelled out our name and we entered this legendary restaurant. You really do feel a sense of tradition at Acme--it's divey, wooden, but comfortable, and the focus is still on the food. Since we had dinner reservations in a couple hours, our waiter gave us a confused look after we ordered only a dozen chargrilled oysters and a peacemaker po'boy...we tried to explain our situation but i don't think he understood how the four of us could eat so little. Regardless, our waiter still gave us the time of day and made us feel a little less guilty. But wow, the food made me feel like I was now in New Orleans. The oysters came out on a huge tray, right off the grill, and were piping. The butter and grated romano cheese on top of the oysters created a bubbling, gooey crust that was ridiculously good. While a little gritty, the cheesy oyster paired with some french bread made us grown guys giggle...yes, giggle. Meanwhile, the fried peacemaker po'boy (fried oysters and shrimp in a po'boy) was already cut into 4, and the sandwich was fantastic. The simple combo of fried seafood, lettuce, tomato, pickle, and mayo within the po'boy bread made me wonder why this sandwich couldn't somehow be replicated in New York. Upon leaving, I understood why our waiter gave us a look of disbelief when we ordered. Acme is not a stopping place before the main meal...it is the main meal.
label: POS

text: I have now been to Green Eggs twice, two weekends in a row, and while there are some things I LOVE about this place, I can't quite give it 5 stars due to some deficiencies. As others have stated, it does get crowded, but neither time did we have to wait too long-- maybe around 15 minutes. And yes, it is cheaper than Sabrina's with similar quality (and much closer to my house, which is a bonus). The first time I went, I was with two friends who were visiting from out of town. They were wowed by the low prices, as was I. One of them got the Belgian waffle with fruit, which she liked, and the other got the creme brulee French toast, which she raved about, before-- I am sure-- slipping into an insulin coma on the drive back to DC. We all loved the brown sugar cubes they gave us with our coffee. I don't usually sweeten my coffee, but that is a nice touch. The coffee was excellent as well. The spinach and chorizo omelet was slightly disappointing, since it didn't have a lot of either thing in it, but overall, the plate was good, much aided by the rosemary potatoes (slammin'!) and the LeBus multi-grain toast (one of my favorite breads ever!). One of my friends got an order of bacon, which was thick cut and delightful. On the second trip, I ordered the three eggs with chorizo, which turned out to be a much better choice, since it had two decent-sized patties on it. I don't know where they get it, but it's not that overly spicy/greasy red kind. It's really delicately spiced and awesome! As for the service, we didn't have anything extremely bad happen either time, but my boyfriend had a weird encounter with the server when he asked if he could get The Kitchen Sink with rosemary instead of signature potatoes, which contain onions. She said, "I don't know" instead of "let me find out, " and my boyfriend and I got the impression that she was expecting to just put the order in and then we would have to wait until the plate came out to find out if there were any potatoes in the dish at all. He ended up switching his order to get the three eggs with chorizo as well. Another minor annoyance was she only gave us three pieces of toast between the two of us with our breakfast. Why would you do that? Doesn't she know it's LeBus multi-grain bread, and I am crazy about it? I am now regretting not getting the quinoa porridge, since I considered it both times and didn't get it, and everyone else is raving about it! The next trip, I suppose....

text: Disappointing but super convenient. I appreciate the largish options and the fresh produce available so close, but have to admit that I try to avoid this store for any real grocery shopping. So while it is useful for a few missing items, you may have problems building an entire meal - particularly if you plan on having any protein. Someone once told me that they spray their proteins with something to keep them pink or fresh looking in the store. I have no idea if that is true so please do not put any stock in it aside from the implication that I am not the only one who is seriously creeped out by their meats. I have always avoided the chicken options as they are obviously scary when you immediately see them. The beef options though are delayed scary. text: So it's only been open a week, so I'm really hoping to be able to give the White Dog Cafe Wayne an updated, improved review in the future. As an active Penn alum, the University City location is a regular favorite, and my wife and I were so excited about the opening in our neighborhood. Unfortunately, our first visit (Friday 11/19) was, in summary, mostly disappointing. The "dog-and-country" decor is fun and novel, and one of our two dishes (the Spicy Lamb Bolognese) was very good - spot on! However, those two positives were strongly outweighed by a very chilly table, inattentive/slow and awkward service from several staffers (each of hostess, bar, and server), and a second entree (Prosciutto Wrapped Brook Trout) that was mediocre. The prosciutto was overcooked to a barely recognizable and somewhat tasteless point, around very flavorful and well-cooked fish, but then sitting atop rock-hard charred toast (near impossible to cut). Our appetizer - the Beef Tartare - was also less than satisfying: dense, dark beef, and the quail egg would not easily mix (it was like a rubber ball). Drinks took long to order, longer to arrive (10-15 mins), beer came with literally 2"+ of head, and all drinks (including water) ran empty at one point during the meal. The crowd is lively (even boisterous) in the bar, but the various dining rooms seem to have vastly different crowd/feel/vibe, which means that the "atmosphere" for your experience is very unpredictable. We commented that it would be easy to love one room, but really dislike another. Will they offer you a choice in reservations/seating?? Tough issue. We'll probably give it another try in a month or two... hope to have a better experience once they "work out the kinks"!

text: The Chi is the Peppermill's new chinese restaurant located inside their casino, in what used to be their steakhouse. I was very excited to hear about it, because I loooooove chinese food! When I stepped inside, bells went off in my head when I saw an entirely asian staff (whereas the rest of the Peppermill is a cosmopolitan mix of races and creeds that I've come to expect - as a result, the "bells" went off in what appeared to me to be a poor attempt to project a sense of "authenticity" or credibilty to be manufactured with their staff choice (or perhaps Chi is privately owned and just located in the Peppermill, and the staffing is coincidence and I'm wrong - either way, it didn't look good to me when I first stepped in - if it was an ordinary restaurant back home in the bay area, I wouldn't have given it a second thought, but since it was in the Peppermill, I called schenanogans). The restraunt decor was absolutely gorgeous! They even kept the "peppermill" feel with red neon lights underneath the seating providing a glow that worked well with the black and gold through the rest of the facility. My friends and I ordered what are usually my three favorites, Lemon Chicken, Sweet and Sour Pork, and Mongolian beef. All were "meh". I was very disappointed in the taste of food that I was serverd here. I'm from the San Francisco bay area, and in comparison to what I would call average in the bay, Chi rates "below average" to "way below average". The fried rice that was served with the meal was also pretty bland. I looked at what was served at the table (we ordered the family meal that is $24 a head) and said to myself "This meal was not anywhere near worth $75 (there were three of us). The only redeeming factor (besides the beautiful decor) was the gelato that was served to me at dessert. I had their lychee gelato, and holy cow was that spectacular! I don't plan on returning to Chi, unless I feel like getting their lychee gelato. I certainly hope their food improves, and that I hear about it, because I would love the opportunity to come back with a redeeming review for Chi(meaning I had an awesome meal). I hate the fact that I'm the first poster, and I'm giving this place a crummy review. =o( I'm rooting for you Chi! I'd love to be able to expect to have a great chinese meal at the Peppermill! (I visit the peppermill 3 - 4 times a year)

Turns out it was a floor model and someone at Gerhard's thought it was acceptable to send me a dented floor model fridge when I paid in full for a brand new one. Then they tried to convince me to take the floor model as a loaner. They plugged it in and it did not even work. Then they could not remove it from my house because they had no more room on their truck. When I tried to call the store several times, I was spoken to with attitude and extremely rudely by several staff members, no one seemed the least bit sorry about the situation (except one of the delivery guys) and no one offered anything to rectify the situation. It took several more days before they came to get their piece of crap fridge from my house but ultimately they did and I received a refund. The server said he couldn't honor the second coupon, so my boyfriend asked to see the owner, Chef "Benner" himself. A few minutes later, he comes huffing and puffing out. Before even giving us a chance, he says "read the fine print... one per table and no split checks." My boyfriend again argued the point that this was not technically a split check, it was 2 separate couples. He then pointed out that we invited the other couple, so that was two extra meals that he got that night. Chef "Benner" said that if all we came for was $10 off, then we were the kind of customers that he did not want. He then threw the coupon on the table, and proceeded to huff away. The food was overrated, and just because this Chef has had a couple good write-ups, his head is as large as a globe. Hey man, you own a mediocre restaurant in LAND O LAKES, FL... Here's a hint, if you don't like people that use coupons at your restaurant, DON'T SEND THEM OUT. I will never eat there again

text: We've stayed at the Hotel Arizona every year for the Tour de Tucson due to its close proximity to the expo. Wow, what was marginal at best before is really just comically awful now. Highlights of the week included: -being told by the gift shop-coffee Batista-restaurant-hostess-and-waitress that she wasn't going to come and get me coffee -being locked out of our room multiple times -being ignored at the front desk for minutes seemingly every time we had to show up there -sloping bed due to broken box spring -oooooh the pillows. oooooooh lumpy awfulness. -every time you take a shower, the water pressure is SO great that it floods your floor. awesome. text: Visited 12/12/2008 and had the worst experience ever. Let me begin by saying I am certain the place is just minutes away from closing. The service, food and scams have run their course and now its time to pay the piper. Last evening we dined with only a single other table occupied in the entire place. The owner and his daughter were the only ones working and the whole experience stunk. We ordered garlic naan (dry - flavored with garlic powder), and two vegetarian combination dishes. That, along with 2 beers was over $70!! The food was below average, and I'm being kind. What was especially troubling is that the restaurant contracted with Restaurant.com and sold vouchers for $25 off the meal of at least $35. Well we PURCHASED a voucher and upon presentation, were informed they no longer accepted them. WHAT??? Its equal to purchasing a gift card and being told, we don't honor our own gift cards any longer. Anyway, the place stinks, the food is awful and the service is the worst. Avoid it at all costs and if you are in the mood for good Indian food in Reno, head over to India Kabob and Curry near Vassar Street and South Virginia. Its hands down better food and atmosphere.

That being said, Wasabi is at the top if not the top of STL sushi restaurants. Price is really pretty reasonable for sushi, I never get worried that I will be broke when I eat here.

text: There isn't much to Riverfront Park that goes beyond its name: it's a park, and it's on the river. However, if you are ever wondering where a Nashville city event is occurring chances are that it's at Riverfront Park. Host of concerts galore, my most recently attended event was the ever so hilarious Red Bull Flutag. text: After eating at Dock Street, the slowly growing crew decided karaoke was the way to go. I'm not into karaoke, and can normally watch people do it for a little while but generally prefer just to listen to the actual song and skip the whole mess altogether. But whatever, I can play along. I dunno if its a regular Thursday thing, but the bar quickly filled up for the event (and I'm assuming that is why everyone was there, as that side of the bar was packed, while the actual "bar" area was much more open). Nice mix of tunes (old-school RnB right into Queen), lots of sing-a-longs, and some good performances. One apparent regular totally nailed James Brown. I honestly thought they were playing the actual record for a second. Dude was legit. And I can't remember the last time I ordered two drinks (Jameson on the rocks and a Tanqueray and tonic), was able to pay with a $10 bill, and then receive change. Not only that, but the bartenders were friendly, quick, and didn't have a problem giving you a good amount of the booze. Thats pretty awesome in and of itself. I found it amusing that with all the singin' and hollerin' just a few feet away, a few regulars were more interested in watching a James Bond movie on the TV at the bar. They kept turning up the volume, even. Hey, whatever you wanna do. Anyway, the crowd was lively, diverse, friendly...just a good time all around. Never been here before, but would like to go back again. On the way out I saw some people with a large plate of Ethiopian fare...will probably save room in the tummy the next time I'm in the area.
label: POS

text: This is a positive review, trust me, I am a fan of this place and go here even though there are 3 Y's closer or as close, but I'm going to review some of the problems with the place. I think you should go here, forsaking all other gyms (they have their problems too.) Good review after I list the problems. Why am I doing it this way? Because honestly I don't want a bunch of new people clogging up my gym ;) The weight machines at this Y give you a false sense of what you're accomplishing. I'm not sure if it's that brand there or what, but if you get on any other gym's machines and do the same weights you'll see the difference. Even there, the same machine on different floors is different. I'm not sure if this is just they bought machines that make you feel like you're doing great or what. Machines at other Y locations seem to mimic reality. On floor 2 I can do 400 pounds on one machine and on floor 1 on the same I can do over 500 - I would love to think either of these is true, but it looks like my leg abilities are a little lower than that. There exist a series of people who evidently think their stink doesn't need to be washed off of the machines. I'm sure this is prevalent in other gyms, but I see the same puddles of ass-sweat from the same people quite often. Someone needs to either put up a sign or start shaming people. The cell-phone policy - there's a no cell phone policy in the gym and locker rooms. I can't recall any time when it's been enforced by anyone who works there. I've only seen other members attempt to enforce it. Cell phones and complete nudity seem to be the standard in the men's locker rooms... I have no idea why so many guys find it that difficult to wear a damned towel from the shower to the locker, but I guess they want to wave their junk about. Maintenance of the machines peripheries is not a priority. They have a bunch of treadmills that support iPods, of those perhaps 25% do not work with ipods due to broken connectors, busted cables. Most machines now have TVs, but the cable will be broken or something will be up on those quite often. Leather maintenance is not up to snuff. I went last night and the elbow rests in one of the machines had worn completely out and the insides were sticking out. Padding on other machines was squished to the uncomfortable levels. The air flow needs to be worked out a bit when the place is packed - it seems designed at the moment to cool the people who are in the front of the exercise machines and baste the ones in the back with the hot and humid sweat cloud from the people in the front. Could be solved by just turning a couple of fans. Now the good on this place The staff are great. I suffer from a back problem and Steve, who works there, has helped me quite often figure out how to strengthen what needs strengthened for me to continue walking without surgery. They always seem to make time for someone even if they're busy. The turnaround on downed machines is pretty quick. With only one exception, it seems that if something is broken there's a fairly fast response to get it back up and running. The classes I've been to have been very well presented and executed. They have a system there that allows you to track your progress - weight, fat, endurance, strength, etc - it's called Microfit and you just go in, get pinched a few times, jump on a bike for a few minutes, and bam - you get a details of where you are, what the average person is, and how much better or worse you're doing since last time. Parking is generally awesome unless you come right during rush half-hour. They will not try and rush you into purchasing a membership... they don't care... I mean, they do care, but selling you product$ is not their goal. The citywide membership means you can go pretty much anywhere... and other Y's in other states often honor your card without any fees so if you want to go to a gym while on a business trip or vacay, you've got a good chance at not having to pay anything. I love this Y, it needs some work, I know they're still recovering from the expansion followed by the flood, I think they're going to get everything awesome again soon.
label: POS

text: I literally live two blocks from this place, so resisting their 30 cent wings on Tuesday is a losing battle for me. I am dying to know what kind of blue cheese they use. Beer selection is great & reasonably priced. They usually have anywhere from 3-4 ciders available- which is nice for me since I don't drink beer. Wish their Lambic was a little cheaper, but I can't manage $13 for a pint. Their burgers are by far the best on Main Street with thick homemade patties & hand cut fries. The lamb sliders are pretty choice, too. The ambiance is somewhere between your classic pub & a dive bar. My only real quibble with this place is if you go anytime after 7 you'll end up waiting for a table for up to 20 minutes. Oh, and don't expect the bartender/owner to be very attentive, gotta wave that dude down if you want some service!

text: This is a great mall and it's the mall closest to the city. It's a very clean mall with tenants ranging from good ole' Macy's to Louis Vuitton. Other highlights of the mall include the Mac (Apple) store, and MAC Cosmetics (isn't that cute, they have the same name!). This mall isn't too much different than any other mall in America, other than they have very upscale tenants. But they also have the store for all America, The Gap. So, you can still find reasonably priced items here, and rub elbows with whoever is shopping at Tiffany's that day. Me, I always head here to fish through the Macy's at clearance time. I can always find something for 90% off, and basically they are begging you to take it from the store. So bargain shopping can even happen at Green Hills Mall.

text: We checked out Mad Donna's for brunch today. First things first, the 2 for 1 mimosas were fabulous! Despite coming at prime time, we didn't have a wait, and the staff was very friendly and attentive. I had an omelette, which was fine. My husband raved about the Crab Cake Benedict. My only complaint is that it took a little to long for us to get our food. However, we were able to enjoy some great people watching during our wait. I definitely recommend Mad Donna's for brunch!

text: Kai Sushi Shabu-Shabu is just okay. I felt like a lot of the (simpler) dishes were wayyy overpriced. The tonkatsu I had (an appetizer plate, so just the pork and a little salad) was tiny for its cost! The mango salmon sushi I had here was decent, but pretty small. My friend's katsu-don looked comparable to Takenoya's in Goleta, except it cost more at Kai Sushi. Perhaps you're paying for the location of this restaurant? Another things which really peeved my friends was how one of them ordered the appetizer tempura (which was around 10 or 12 bucks), but the waiter instead brought her the tempura meal (which cost $23). When she pointed out she asked for the appetizer instead, the waiter was really reluctant to fix the order and so my friend stuck with the whole meal (in addition to ordering sushi). Overall service wasn't good. I would not come back here. It was overpriced for the quality of the food!

Chips: thick and greasy Salsa: seemed like canned tomatoes with no spices Guacamole: large veggie chucks but blah favor Drinks: weak and below average Entrees: we were both underwhelmed. My wife's was meal was way overcooked. The service was good, but that was about the only positive.

text: I'm currently staying at the Millennium in the South Tower. While I have not seen the North Tower, I can't imagine it'd be much more run down that the South seems to be. I am not at all impressed with the room. It's quite small and while I realize this is the "budget" side, I still expect it to be a little nicer, i.e. no stains on the carpet, no traces of peeling wallpaper, etc. The indoor pool is sort of a joke. It's a small wedge shaped pool that is 3' and 4' deep. The outdoor pool by the North Tower is considerably nicer though it was quite crowded with pool drinkers (AKA intoxicated people enjoying their beverages in the pool itself). The lobby is actually quite pretty with gorgeous views of the park and the Arch but that's about the only impressive thing I can say about it at this point. The staff was quite friendly and efficient. If you're going to a Cardinals game, Busch Stadium is only two blocks away so it's quite convenient for that purpose. It just doesn't seem worth the money though.

I swear they put crack in the cheese. How else to explain its addictive powers. If that makes me a crackhead, SO BE IT.

text: When husband and I head from Chicago to Florida for Christmas, my in-laws take care to ensure that we don't miss a week of deep-dish. It's kind. They feed us much better than we feed ourselves most days. Still, going to a Giordano's in Florida is weird. It's weird to see that they won this Taste of Brandon award when they're the taste of Chicago. But a chain's a chain, I suppose, and it was cool to see how they did it. Food was fine in the end. Slightly different from Chicago Giordano's; the spinach seemed a bit less cooked and the sauce was a touch thinner. But not bad. Certainly Giordano's. The dining room is cute; I like the Chicago-to-the-max decor, especially the mural by the front door. But the best part is coming up here below: Half. Price. Pizzas. on. Wednesdays. Seriously. 50% off the food bill has this Chicagoan grinning. Because I love my deep dish here at home, but I don't have the cash to sustain the habit. So keep up these promotions, and Brandon's Giordano's will do just fine during our snowbird winters...
label: POS

text: Swift Half is more like Good Dog's red-headed stepchild. After mad attempts to make myself love this place, even without the comparisons to Good Dog (a few of its staff pull double duty both here and there, so it's hard to remove yourself from doing so) - I still find the place to be sterile and devoid of a personality. You'd think with the huge space, and a bigger bar that management would try to accommodate more clientele (*perhaps more tables?) and be a little eager to please - on more than one occasion the manager (host?) has seemed impatient, aloof and utterly insouciant. Service, on the other hand (and most often), was attentive and helpful. Menu is a little more ambitious now - with a lot more items, but its portions still deceptively small and the food, again, for the most part, was nothing to write home about. I was waiting (and hoping, really!) for this place to hit its stride, but at this point, I don't think that time will ever come. There are way too many great bars in my 'hood to waste my time or my dollars on a place like Swift Half.

text: I had a late brunch here with my dad on Sunday before heading to the Cash Poor Art Show. (God, how white and middle class are we? Very, apparently.) The service was outstanding, though that may have been due to the fact that we were only one of two parties there. Nevertheless, the servers were enthusiastic and really nice, and the executive chef came out to ask us how our meal went. The staff were all so nice and eager that we didn't really have the heart to tell them we'd best describe the food as "meh." There weren't a ton of vegetarian options on the brunch menu, except for the breakfast options. 2 of the 3 salads, 2 of the 3 sandwiches, and all of the entrees had meat or fish in them. I ended up getting the omelet du jour, which had red and green peppers and cheddar cheese, while my dad opted for the seared tuna nicoise salad. My omelet was smaller than expected, but luckily I wasn't super hungry. The big downer was the bread that came with my eggs - I ordered wheat toast, expecting some crusty artisan whole grain or something similar. What I got was, I'm pretty sure, two slices of barely-toasted Stroehmann's wheat. My dad's salad looked really good, but he didn't like it too much. He said the tuna, though seared, was cold, and that the salad wasn't as fresh as he expected. We didn't get dessert, but the table next to ours did and it looked fabulous. I may come back again for dinner to see if this was a fluke, but I wasn't super thrilled with the food. The staff were a delight and I liked the clean space and the classic rock playing at a nice low volume, but the food just didn't live up to my expectations.
label: NEG

I did get a ride back to the city, and this is where the one star goes away, parking is a logistics nightmare. It took forever to get out of the lot. I don't get why people drive anywhere! text: I have been just waiting to get to a Big Easy Rollergirls match and last night I got to see the Crescent Wenches battle against the Red Stick All Stars from Baton Rouge. It was great! Tickets are $15 at the door or $12 online beforehand. I don't know if i'd be shelling that out every weekend, but it was worth it for my first time! There are two half-hour halfs and we got to see the band J.D. Hill and the Jammers during half-time. Besides the rollergirls, there are many other sites to see: - the cheerleaders known as PussyFooters, - the rolling Elvi who throw candy to the crowd, - the announcers Skip 4-Play and Reverend Psych Ward ...it is one big fun adventure. The girls are tough- pushing, shoving, and falling down a lot (they get back up quickly!). My favorite names of the girls I saw last night include Vieux Careen, Turbo Tyke, Moxie Balboa, Anti Em, Tank Goodness...they're all great. Finally, food and alcohol is served. But not just any alcohol- NOLA Brewing Co is offered here as they support any event that includes 'broads, bruises, and brew.'

text: very American-ized sushi; rolls are massive and include ingredients like mayo, okra, corn, etc. Sushi snobs stay away, although the quality of fish is high and I have to admit it is tasty in a cheap American way. Fun atmosphere, techno music, trendy.

text: This place is so new I couldn't even find a web listing with a phone number---I got the address by actually driving past it again. Oh, YUM. This is the sort of fast food/Mediterranean place I thought I'd left behind in Chicagoland--I'm so glad they're here! I had the house combo, which is gyro meat, a chicken breast, falafel, hummus, a little salad & rice. Gyro meat was good, as was falafel. I thought the hummus was a bit heavy on the tahini, but still, it was good, & I liked the heavy dusting of paprika on top. The salad was very good--I usually just ignore salad when it comes with a combo like this, because it's mostly just iceberg & boring. But while this did include iceberg, it was a mix. There was also cucumber & tomato, and a basic oil-and-vinegar dressing that had a nice bite to it. But---the chicken. Oh, the chicken. It wasn't my focus when ordering; I wanted the gyro meat, hummus, & falafel. But this chicken breast was beautifully grilled and delicious! Husband had the gyro sandwich with spicy fries. Sandwich was generous, the kind I would eat with a fork rather than try to pick up. I stole a fry: freshly fried, hot, crispy, nicely seasoned. I got a piece of baklava to go for dessert . While I was picking it out (they have different kinds, which is nice I guess but I like plain), I saw a cake-ish thing in the plate next to it and asked what it was. The counter guy responded "it's a Middle Eastern cake" and told the guy boxing my baklava to put a piece in. So even if the food HADN'T been great, they'd get repeat business from me for that gesture. Minuses: I think the pita bread could've been a little more fried, not a fan of very soft pita if it's meant to be used as a scoop for hummus, etc. And I wish they had an appetizer combo plate so I could've tried the tabouleh & dolmas along with the falafel & hummus. Probably should suggest it to them, they may just not have thought of it yet.
label: POS

text: Good place for pad thai. My fiancé and I go here often when in New Hope and for a small, quaint little restaurant, it's not bad. The scenary is good as the seating is on what looks like an old house's back patio... right on the stream flowing into the river. Not sure if they're open or not in the winter but catch this place when the weathers good.

text: McGurk's is one of the best places to drink in St. Louis. This is an amazing mix of an authentic Irish Pub and a young, hip hangout for college students / graduates. The main room, which generally houses an older crowd, encompasses live irish music pretty much 7 days a week. The back rooms are just there so that you and your party can sit and enjoy a beer. The back patio / garden is a great place to mingle and meet new friends and is occupied by the younger crowd. One glance at the menu and you will see a drink and food selection that truly represents everything an Irish pub should be.

text: My roommate and I always come here as our default restaurant because, well, they have unlimited fries. I do like this place but there are a couple of complaints that I feel the need to share. Firstly, my friends and I (a group of 8 give or take 2) came here for breakfast and every single persons' eggs were disgustingly overcooked. This maybe might not be such a huge deal if everyone ordered scrambled (oh wait, it still would be), but most of us got eggs benedict, which were HORRIFYING. Truly, horrifying. The second is that they have this little bumper car like thing rotating in the center of the restaurant that you aren't allowed to touch or ride. Yea it is cute to look @ buuUuUut I WANT TO RIDE IT SO BAD (that's what she said) and I can't even IMAGINE what kids must think when they see that. When I was a kid and I wanted to do something, I would want it with my entire body. Oh it must be so torturous for them. Third, the meatloaf and loaded mashed potatoes were aigghhhtt... but not great, which is strange because I was having XXX fantasies about the taters... kinda disappointing. NOW the good. Their chicken finger things are DELICIOUS--crispy, salty breading surrounding the TENDER, SUCCULENT and JUICY chicken that can be dipped into ranch, beebeecue or honey mustard sauces (i'm sure there are more but my roomie and i stick to those three). The Kobe beef sliders. OMG. OMG. They use Hawaiian rolls and the grilled onions are all caramalizey and ... DROOOOOOOOLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLLL!!!!!! The BLT's bread was good but the bread (Parmesan-crusted, grilled with butter or oil) was so crunchy that it was literally shredding the skin inside my mouth. OW but a delicious OW. This turkey sandwich I got with avocado and bacon was also REALLY good and HUGE. I could only eat half the 'wich and my fries... I couldn't even get a second order of fries!! Also, they always have $5 coupons floating around (the UCSB money book thing or in the clipper), which are SWEEEET and the ones that I used had no minimum purchase requirement Note: the "flavored" fries they have aren't really worth it or much better than their regular fries. I clearly eat here way too much. But I would like to add that though it is pretty scrumptious, it's part of a chain. So if you're visiting SB, you may wanna try something that you can only find in SB. I have no suggestions but hey, you're on yelp. -------------------------------- I wanted to add that I got the root beer float here and it was horrible. The root beer to ice cream ratio was all off. It was like ice cream with a splash of root beer which made the root beer foam out of control like the mouth of a rabies infested animal. They did add more root beer when I asked but all was lost by then... Derf's... now THAT place has some good root beer floats! --------------------------------- there are two gumball machines. a 25 cent jumbo gumball machine and a one cent teeny gumball machine. i forced my friend to get 10 of the one cent ones, which are obviously a better deal... for 25 cents you can get a LOT of small gumballs... plus what're you gonna do with all those pennies anyway? also, the machine is beaver brand... obviously my favorite brand in the entire world

text: Lucky 13, formerly known as Barwild, is a pretty nice place. They have a cool bar area that Las Vegas feel to it but that is where it ends. The place is pretty big and usually crowded but when I was there it was a bunch of young kids partying. I wondered if this place even checked ID because a lot of the people were under 18 for sure. I know this because I checked their ID's myself to make sure.. but really I knew some of the kids there and I was just as shocked to see them there as they were to be caught there. The music is more dance than anything which is OK but they should switch it up more often. Not really my kind of place.

text: So, yes before i get hate mail about reviewing fast foods i want to prefice this by saying i am only doing this to tell you of my craptastic day. So, imagine that i was hungry for lunch having been running around getting things for easter and wanted something quick. So i went there and took the food home. text: Got around to checking this place out last weekend... I agree with one person's comment about its nothing like satco - THANK GOD! The staff seemed very friendly and eager to serve, which was a good thing. The menu was small and simple... which is also nice sometimes. Too many options can make choosing difficult! They have about 8 different soft tacos and I think also about 6 different enchiladas.. all the tacos are $2.50. They also serve up some sides like salsas, queso, and guac - all for a good price of less than $4. I think they also had some other items but since I was there for tacos, I didn't really read them. The southern fried taco wasn't too exciting - just some fried chicken and a sweet sauce in a taco - so i'd pass on that one. The korean bbq one I thought was really tasty - great flavor to it! My boyfriend had the fish taco - he said it was good, but not great - and he also had the spicy shrimp taco which he said was excellent... and now wants to keep going back just for that taco - apparently its super super spicy so beware! I liked the queso, I didn't think it resembled gross melted down cheese like someone else mentioned. it was creamy and tasty. served its purpose! They also had an interesting drink menu - I'm gonna try the "lojito" next time I go - which was basically a mojito that uses a local rum in it. So all in all - I thought it was a great place - its super affordable, it can be quick if your timing is right, and they had some really interesting fun flavors instead of your standard boring tacos. I mean "Kelly P" if you want boring standard tacos - then go to SATCO, or las palmas or whatever mexican restaurant you're used to going to - this place is for interesting flavors, proper portion sizes, good prices and quality food. Oh and they valet park - which I hate using, but its convenient when theres no parking spaces! ***** UPDATE ****** So I went back to Local Taco last weekend and decided to remove a star from my review. First of all - the music they were playing was VERY LOUD. Now - Loud music doesn't necessarily upset me, but I had to yell across the table to speak to my boyfriend during the meal! YELL. Not only that - but the music they wanted to blast... was Maroon 5!!!!! WHAT?? And not just a song - BUT THE WHOLE ALBUM. I HATE that band - so it totally ruined my whole experience in there. Why on earth would you play an entire album at a restaurant? There is a reason for the radio or mixes... so your music can appeal to the masses... not single them out. jesus. it was terrible! Ok so on top of the awful loud music - there were flies buzzing around us the whole time (and we were eating inside due to the intense heat outside).. they were swarming our table. Very unpleasant experience. To top it off - about 2 hours later, both of us were experiencing sour stomachs.. This really upsets me because I really really wanted to like this place, but after this last visit I don't think I want to return.

text: Who thinks there is nothing good by the airport! King Market will shoot all of you down. King Market, consists of a super market, jewelry store, and a small sit down restaurant. The owners are from Laos and the food represents traditions Laos cuisine, and is AMAZING! Today I tried the Seafood Salad to start, which was pretty spicy and contained shrimp, squid and mussels along with red onions, red peppers, and jalapenos. For the main course I had the Sukiyaki, which is a Laos soup containing beef, shrimp, egg, cabbage, celery, and special Laos sauce that is to die for, if you like Pho give this a shot. My wife had the Seafood Pho, which happened to be incredible. It contained shrimp, squid, noodles, and great fresh basil and bean sprouts. On top of great food, everyone who works there is extremely nice and helpful. Its truly a hidden gem, and if you have an adventurous palate I suggest you hit them up!

text: Best breakfast spot in the city. There, I said it. At first, I was hesitant to go...all the way to South Philly? For breakfast? But what the heck...lets do it. And it was SO worth it. For starters, as noted, the place is very, very small...three tables (I think) and a few spots at the counter. Thats it. One cook, one server. Somehow we lucked out and got there when the counter was empty (on a Sunday, no less) so we didn't have to wait. But, apparently, that can happen often. The server, Alexei (sp?), was incredibly warm and inviting, and we were seated with large mugs full of coffee/tea right away. No menu, save for what is on the board...4 choices, I believe. Somehow choosing from 4 dishes is harder than choosing from 40...not sure how that works. Anyway, I went with the omelette. Stuffed with steamed broccoli, onions, goat cheese, and some other tasty tidbits I can't recall (oh yea, it was BIG), it was served alongside potatoes, toast, and lamb sausage. Fresh preserves, too. Simply divine all around. I ate every last bite, and didn't need to eat again for almost 12 hours. This is not a cheap breakfast place (the bill for 2 was slightly north of $30), but worth every penny. Also, as previously noted, the decor is totally unique (and totally South Philly). Hard to describe, other than to say you need to see it for yourself. Won't find this in Center City (or any other city), that is for sure. I hope to return, soon, and dine in the pickup truck parked outside (yep...pickup truck). Lots of friendly conversation will be had (as everyone in the place is within normal talking distance), as well. If you are a picky eater, and/or the sort who always has to tweak something, you might want to think twice about coming here...Carman don't take no guff. But I hope picky eaters don't read Yelp, so this warning will likely be unwarranted. Finally, people, its CarmAn. Not CarmEn. And bring cash.

I asked my Chinese buddy at work if he knew of any proper spots in or around Philly. He got excited and pointed me to Han Dynasty. I trekked out and understood why - the place is great. I've made my way through most of the super spicy seafood or veg dishes, always chatting with Han himself for tips, off-menu stuff and to make sure no other meat ends up in the order. Like everybody else has mentioned, Han is the man. He always chats, makes goofy jokes and gushes enthusiasm about his menu. He's gotten to know what I like and sets me up good and hot. It's in a stripmall/suburban type of hell, but worth the drive. Pair it up with a couple of beers around the corner at Sly Fox, especially for the stuff on tap you can't really find in town, and tote along a growler for the meal. Not so bad, afterall. Han cracks me up.
label: POS

text: I had lunch here today, and I suddenly realized what gross neglect it has been to not write a review. The burgers - awesome. My readers know how I love an undercooked slab of beef, and everything here is well done, but somehow it stays tender and juicy. Get any toppings you want - the Bob special is pickles and jalapenos with ketchup. For a regular burger, they put two slabs on your bun, and its quite a mouthful. The fries - cooked in peanut oil, and as good as any Thrashers at the beach. And they give you LOTS. While you wait for your order, you get to fill your drink and wash it down with peanuts that you shell yourself. What could be better than that? The prices have risen over the years, and that's about the only reason I can't do five stars. This is a treat place for me, about every 2-3 weeks. Don't worry, you can work it off in that time.
label: POS

text: Like Matthew M, I also just moved back to NOLA after a seven year hiatus, and I loved the bar. It feels relaxed and sophisticated, yet still has a certain funkiness that makes it comfortable and endearing. The selection is fantastic and the prices are very affordable. On the particular night I visited, I guess there were some issues with the service crew. The owner was behind the bar and super stressed and made us wait for nearly 10 minutes for the second half of a glass of champagne (he emptied a bottle with the 1st half). Then, he was talking to someone else while he finished the pour, but didn't tell us how much we owed him. My friend became quite pissed, as she was in town visiting friends and didn't want to be staring at this stressed out bartender--she wanted to be with her peeps. Understandable. I thought this would be a good opportunity to try out a theory. I wanted to sort of shame this guy into good service since we'd be there for a few more rounds, so we left him an $8 tip for his crappy service for our 2 glasses of wine. It totally worked. However, this is not a tip to service industry-types who may read this. He didn't get a tip at all the next round, so it came out even anyway. Also, he knew the people at my table, as it turns out, but once he got things under control, he came around to wait on our table regularly. So, I'm not sure if it was my smartass/jackass theory or him knowing people, but at least we had perfect service after that. This would be a fantastic date spot, by the way.
label: POS

text: What can I say that is good about this place. The service was good. And the people where nice. Ok now the bad side. Its small dark, cramp, not very welcoming. My friends and I decided on this place after a movie. So fulled with curiosity and a empty stomach I look forward to trying it out. So sit and look at the menu and I have a double take on how much everything. Even the appetizers were over priced. 4.50 for miso soup that you can get anywhere else for 2 dollars. I swear that I didn't see a entree under 12.50. We just got a couple of appetizers and left. Disappointed and not even full. I don't think I will try them again.

text: I almost NEVER put 1 star rating, but this is the 2nd one and guess what?! Another DRUNKEN FISH!!! First I stepped in, I was like "Oh, this place is packed and there is a live DJ who is not playing music too loud like the other Drunken Fish, cool". Anyhow, it was our new friends get together, and the hostess sat us in a booth with walls surrounded us, so I really liked that we have a privacy space. So far so good, huh? Here comes the reason for 1 star. Say, if we are a group of 8, you can not bring 6 ppl's food first and bring other 2 ppls' food 20 mins later. Obviously, it's a party and we want to eat, drink, share, and chat at the same time! 6 ppl felt bad for other 2 ppl not having any food infront of them and it created an awkward atmosphere. When 6 ppl finished eating, 2 ppl just started eating. GREAT,,,,,..... Thanks. I think they charge enough price to hire enough ppl in the kitchen and more waiters. "Saturday night" is not an excuse. We paid SO MUCH for an appetizer amount of Sushi. Can we at least get some service here? Especially when you are with your new friends,,,, we just want to have a good time with good food. By the way, Their Sushi isn't good at all. SO NOT WORTH IT. Go somewhere else for food and service. After paying SO MUCH, I was still hungry like I never ate.

text: I've been around the cheesesteak game in Philadelphia for quite some time and after trying all of the places that great great reviews I have found Delesandros to be my favorite. There are definitely two different type of cheesesteaks in Philly so if you are looking for the large pieces of steak with wiz like you'd get at a Tony Lukes or Genos then this place isn't for you. The rolls here are always fresh, the meat is finally chopped up and I always get mine with extra cheese. They do a great job of melting the cheese throughout the steak. Ad some hot peppers and it is good to do and I consider it the best cheesesteak in Philly. Only problem with the place is that they don't sell french fries and its all the way out in Roxborough.

text: Not as urban/hip as an Ooka, but I've eaten here about ten times and it's always been reliable. Decent decor, definitely does not feel like a strip mall "joint".

text: This thrift store is a great find! You walk in, and have to first get over the sight of tons of stuffed animal heads on the walls of the place, but after that you find a plethora of great items for your home. The store is huge, they have room after room of all kinds of antique and new furniture and housewares. Apparently, they buy out all of the items from houses and then sell them for cheap. My roommate and I got 2 mattresses (no box spring), an old desk, and a leather chair for 230 bucks! It was quite the deal. The employees there are extremely friendly and willing to make a deal on the furniture you want. If you are in need of some furniture and want to buy it cheap, check out this place first!

text: Just had a great time here over the weekend. text: I have never been to Angelino's, I have only had them deliver. Their pizza is pretty good. They brush garlic oil on the crust, which is divine. text: This is by far the best place for pad thai! Amazing....! It's so peanut buttery, the noodles were cooked al dente, the shrimp wasn't over-cooked and they served a huge portion of it. I also ordered some peanut butter ice cream dessert. Loved it! It was a huge ball of ice creamed cut in half, covered with a thin layer of milk chocolate and filled with peanut butter, caramel and vanilla ice cream. Amazing ........! I gave it 4 stars instead of 5 bc 1) their chicken spring roll was pretty disappointing --- it was bland and the skin roll wasn't crunchy enough for me --- and 2) their Thai ice tea wasn't authentic --- as soon as the waiter served it to me, I knew that it wasn't going to be good. It looked cloudy, diluted and they def used powder tea instead of brewing the tea leaves which made it awful... I didn't even finished it.

text: Mentally, my image of dim sum is a big dining hall with servers pushing around carts of small dishes from which you can choose whichever plates of food look appetizing. So entering Dim Sum Garden, I was almost unsure whether I had walked into the right restaurant. I took a seat with my friends, and we ordered an array of dishes, they being more knowledgeable about the nuances of dim sum, I simply sat back and waited for the dim sum nom noms to arrive :) The food took a few minutes to come out, so I could tell that it was freshly prepared. And I would be reminded that it came straight out of the steamer: I put an entire soup dumpling in my mouth and with the first bite immediately scalded my entire mouth! There was no cold water to temper the boiling liquid in my mouth, only hot tea. So after that experience, my taste buds were toast and I couldn't taste anything else in the meal. We asked for cold water, but the server didn't give us any. I did feel woozy afterwards, so I'm pretty sure I did ingest some MSG. The shu mai is a different style than what you may be used to - it's Shanghai shu mai, so it's filled with rice and larger than the small but juicy pork dumplings you may be used to.
label: NEG

text: Let me start by saying I got my eye exam at another location (Pennsylvania Optemetrics). The eye exam was great. I'll leave a positive review for that bit, but the salesman drove me away from the shop that day. There was also an issue with my insurance, where they would not accept it for direct billing and would require reimbursement. So I called around, and found For Eyes. The call lasted less than a minute. She knew exactly how my plan worked (actually, how both options worked - I wasn't sure, so she quickly explained both). I shot down to check out the selection. She took care of the insurance bit, then came to help me pick out some frames (finding something that fit me, not her commission). We found some good frames, she rang me up, $12 out of pocket for $188 price tag. She found me $57 worth of discounts and billed the rest to my insurance. Penn Optemetrics had me at $175 before I picked my frames, which were looking to be about $125+.... The combination of the two was perfect for me, although I have no idea how the exams were at For Eyes. If you're looking for decent frames at a good price, with friendly and knowledgeable staff, this is the place.
label: POS

text: Not sure why this place put "Sushi" in its name...I have nothing to write about "sushi" at this place other than mixed style "rolls" - not quite sure the point of mixing things together though. Yes, price is reasonable for rolls; but taste and presentation were not good at all. Many rolls are fusion mixed kind...which I am not much fun of. ...will not go back.
