text: I love visiting Philly and discovering the restaurant renaissance here. While I do love cheesesteaks and hoagies, it is nice to get fresh wholesome cuisine without all the grease. Supper's atmosphere is casual and simple yet classy. The focus here is on the food. Meals here are meant to be savored. For starters, the pretzels with a beer cheese fondue were yummy. I dipped my leftover bread to lap up the last bits. The deviled eggs were original and the carrot and tangerine soup with a smear of coconut marshmallows offered a nice mix of flavors. The scallops were nicely cooked as well. Portions here are small, but meant to be layered. Personally, this was perfect for me. I also liked the warm banana bread pudding with carmalized banana. It was pure sophisticated comfort food without the heaviness. I would recommend Supper again. This is also a crowd-pleaser with something for everyone-from foodies to those who aren't as adventurous.
label: POS

text: A friendly word of advice to single (or married, divorced, or cougar) women: Do NOT take a man who likes to EAT here on a date. You will piss him off. I seriously thought it was a joke, but no, for eighty bucks, you too can cook your own food and then dip it in a sauce. I will now switch to sarcastic review mode: {SARCASM} OMG! Like seriously! You mean all these years of me learning to barbecue and buying groceries at the store have been totally wasted? I mean the experience of doing it at home has now been surpassed by me doing it at a restaurant. What an absolute idiot I have been! To think that I've been out there slaving away over a BBQ pit while sloshing sauce on delicious oversized pieces of steak, chicken, ribs that I bought fresh at the butcher store, I could have been doing that on a much more miniature scale here at the Melting Pot. I mean, now all restaurants have some serious competition here. I mean, they don't even have to pay a chef here, think of the savings! They are really tightening their belt with the recession here, give 'em credit. I recognize smart business people when I see them. Now every restaurant will definitely catch on to this craze, for sure! Why pay a chef when your guests will pay you to cook it? It's downright brilliant!!! And to think I've been clipping coupons and hitting up sales at the grocery store. What have I been thinking! I mean, I could just give $80 to the Melting Pot and cook much smaller pieces of meat myself. Why bother the wait staff or chef? I can do it myself! Oh and don't forget to tip the person who brought you that watered down lemonade? Gosh, why didn't I think of adding more water to my lemonade? {/SARCASM} I will now end sarcastic review mode: I'm glad we got up and left before they made us pay and went to Sullivan's Steakhouse where we have professionals that make your food exactly how you want to eat it, not cook it.
label: NEG

text: I went in for an eyebrow wax and pedicure. First the waxing. It was not a good experience. The waxing itself as fine, but the woman doing it for me really concentrated on plucking to shape. I have been waxing and plucking for years, and it has never hurt like this - the tweezers kept grabbing and pinching my skin. I was getting nauseous. I have to say, they looked very nice when she was done, but it was strange to have her put neosporin on my eyebrows! Now, 18 hours later, my eyebrows are still sore. The pedicure was good. Their chairs are not comfortable, though, and there were no magazines available to read. I am not convinced that their sanitation is the best. At least is was cheap. Both services were $33. But I won't be back - I'd rather pay more somewhere else. I'll be on the lookout for a nail salon I actually feel comfortable in.
label: NEG

text: We decided to check this place out after going to Arigato WAY too many times (not that it's bad or anything; we just wanted to try something new). We almost missed this place since it was on the very end of a strip of stores, and just by looking at it from the outside I got really skeptical. It looked extremely small and slummy, but once we got inside it was actually quite nice! The first thought I had was that it reminded me a lot of Arigato, and I remembered reading a review that Ahi is the "rival" of Arigato. They seriously have the same menu setup, some same sushi rolls, and the whole look of the place was similar (ie: the candles in the red glass tubes on the tables...VERY familiar). We got seated at the sushi bar, and we ordered about 5 rolls. We tried the Fisherman's, Crunchy Spicy Ahi, Alaskan, Spider, and Dragon roll. They were all very good and the presentation was pretty. (They also came with "special sauces" on the plates). One thing was that they didn't give us very many rolls. For the Dragon they only gave us about 4 which was disappointing since that was my favorite. And they didn't have as many roll choices as I would have liked. But overall it was nice trying something different. I left satisfied and full. Yet I think since it was practically the same price, I'd choose Arigato over Ahi any day.

Pho Thai Nam is very nicely decorated and the staff is accommodating & friendly but that really doesn't make up for the lack of taste & size of their dishes. All in all, I've had better. Way better. I think you're better off taking the drive down to Center City, Adams Ave or Washington Ave.

text: I know there's that other Greek Festival every May out in Des Peres, but this remains my favorite Greek Festival in the city. Every Labor Day weekend, St. Nicholas opens up its doors, and Barnes opens up one of their garages, and the entire area around Kingshighway and Forest Park is inundated with all things Greek. The food is AMAZING and you can fill up for under $10 easily. Buy a bottle of wine or a few Greek beers, sit back and enjoy the music. The pastries are the best. I could eat my weight in this baklava. Quite frankly, as much as I love Olympia, I can't help but admit, this Greek food is better and the atmosphere certainly cannot be beat. This festival runs for the entire Labor Day weekend, and is filled with dancing, music, (as I said and couldn't shut up about before) amazing food, and plenty of OOOOPAAAAAAAs. You can also buy plenty of items at the Flea Market of Athens such as T-shirts, olive oil, and other Greek goodies. Certainly something to put on your calendar next Labor Day weekend.
label: POS

text: i go to ccp so i've been to the callowhill location a few times. i like the veggie cheesesteak and fries when i'm in the mood for fatty points. the service has always been okay but the staff is a little awkward. i stopped by the italian market location on my way to work the other day. what a disappointment! the server was such a jerk. first off, she literally asked me four times if it was just me before giving me a table. i understand some people find it weird to eat out alone but i enjoy treating myself without having to work around someone else's schedule. i ordered the sandwich with parmesan fries. it came out really quickly and i was excited about that but it tasted horrible. dry and little to no flavor. my fries were soggy? the waitress came up to the table too many times to see how i was doing. it was as if she was rushing me. it wasn't busy. no need to push the customers out the door, hun. she basically forced me to box my food before i was done eating and didn't offer dessert or coffee. my little date for myself ended way too soon. bad music, bad service, annoying fellow patrons...i'm going back to callowhill.
label: NEG

text: The one extra star is for the inexpensive buffet that had pretty good food and an attentive server that made sure we were taken care of. I was leaving the Eldorado on my way back home and remembered that I'd seen a merry-go-round in the window. I'm a little kid at heart so I jumped at the chance to go. We first stopped to get food at the buffet and then made our way to the "Fun Center" that was more sad than fun. It cost me $1.50 for a short ride on the merry-go-round and rather than feeling like that little kid again, I felt more so how the ride-operator looked: weary, dejected, bored, bitter and disappointed. ...sigh...I know there's a merry-go-round out there someplace that will make my heart jump...this just wasn't the one.....................
label: NEG

text: This is the flagship bar of the people who own Mikimotos and Presto, and this is definitely the one they got right (at least in terms of libations). So as I'm sure you've all discovered about me, I lovelovelove good beer and I think Delaware has some of the shittiest beer selections in town. Imagine my surprise when my parents and I stop inside of here to say hi to a friend and I see like 6 amazing beers on tap out of a list of 22 meh-to-decent beers! Dogfish Head 75 minute in cask, Dogfish Head's World Wide Stout, 90 Minute, and Burton Baton on tap right next to Scaldis Noel (only my most favorite Christmas beer OF ALL TIME) and Saison Dupont...I swear to god it was a freakin' Christmas miracle. For the next hour or so I got to talk my parents' ears off about beer while very quickly getting drunk on a Scaldis and WWS. I'm still in shock...I mean, good beer in Delaware? Pinch me please, I'm clearly dreaming. I can't attest to the food because we never ate, but I remember seeing a beer and cheese soup on the menu and that soup was created in heaven so I'm sure their version of it is just as tasty. If you drink good beer, go here. Even if you don't, go here anyway so you'll start drinking good beer. Start the beervolution in Delaware!
label: POS

text: I feel like I should like this place more than I do. Yeah, it's a wine bar, yeah, they serve tapas, and yeah, it's datey as hell, but I have a problem with places where I have to walk a bartender through the steps of certain classic cocktails (read: if you cannot make an old fashioned, you should not tend bar). Anyway, this place will persist in popularity, I'll get brought there with big groups/dates, and I'll just pay the $5 for a beer next time, saving all of us the embarrassment.

text: I won tickets to a Frankie J concert a couple of years back so Lisa M. and I decided to go check it out. The night started with a very boring wait outside the place while they opened and began to search everyone. Ok, no big deal. We then went inside to realize there were no seats. We hurried to the front so we could take a spot close to the stage. The ladies were swarming and pushing even before the concert started. The atmosphere had a dingy feeling to it. It was just dark and dingy in there. That's the best way I can explain it. There was a little area upstairs to sit and watch but by the time I noticed it, a million people were already on their way up. Most of them ended up coming back down. That was my first and last time at the Electric Factory. I did enjoy the concert. Especially when Frankie J sang to me :) but I'm glad I didn't spend my money on those tickets.
label: NEG

text: Who knew St. Louis could be so hip? The Grove area has it going on these days - first a giant sign that now lets you know exactly the name of their 'hood, now a bicycle-friendly bar! Seems like our fair city is starting to keep up with the rest of the world... Stopped in Handle Bar for a quick drink with a gal pal the other night. It was empty inside, but I got here right at 5 pm. In addition to cheap drafts during happy hour, they also have a "Bartender's Special" - that night it was Guinness. I wasn't having it, but I know we have some yelpers out there who are fans. I tried the Six Row Whale - MAN! That's some good beer! Had I not had other plans that night, I would have been content sitting at that bar and drinking myself silly with Whale beer. My companion and I tried to order an appetizer, but the kitchen wasn't opening until 6. And about the time we were packing up, our cute little bartender brought us a plate of hummus. I felt terrible 'case we didn't have time to eat it, but I'm thinking she was able to put it to good use (i.e., her tummy). Come check out this cool bar! It's in a great STL area, the drinks are cheap, the staff is nice and they care about the planet. What more do you want, people?
label: POS

text: This is a review for take-out only. I came in here a few mornings ago when I knew I needed coffee/water to make it the three more blocks to the subway. The space is small but cozy and the staff I encountered was super friendly and the service was fast and efficient. My coffee was reasonably priced and strong. There was an upcharge for soymilk which was unexpected because I have been going to grindcore alot lately. I ordered an egg and cheese on an english muffin which was cooked quickly and tasted a whole lot better than the rank dunkin donuts near my work. I will be stopping by again on my morning commute. They have a free water pitcher which was a nice touch, I like to hydrate before downing caffeine.

text: This place was recommended by our hotel so we tried it and we're very glad we did. The staff was friendly, the food was good and the martinis were amazing. We sat at the bar and were promptly greeted by our bartender Casey. She was friendly but not intrusive and made thoughtful recommendations when asked. We shared the sweet italian sausage flatbread, penne bolognase and had peach martinis. Everything was delicious. Casey was on top of it and we enjoyed our experience thoroughly. We'll definitely go back.

text: this is exactly what the doylestown area needed - a bar and grill that isn't tiny and overpriced and isn't a crappy chain restaurant. they have TONS of beers, and you can get any of the ones on tap in a pitcher. there are large TVs around the dining area so it would be a great place to watch a game. the food is tasty and very reasonably priced. i ordered a pork panini and i loved it. (pork loin, bacon, provolone, and mixed greens with a balsamic sauce. muy tasty.) i'm looking forward to going here not only to hang out at the bar, but at the outdoor patio as well.

text: A rare vegetarin-only restaurant in St. Louis County, whoo hoo! Thankfully Gokul has recently redecorated and lost the horribly vertigo-inducing movie-projection on the back wall. Much much nicer now. The food is quite good. Mid-week lunch buffet tastes a bit "leftover", but the navratan korma is delicious. Naan could be a bit fresher, rice, while a jasmine, is good but too sticky for proper indian. If you are lucky to arrive on a masala dosa buffet day, count yourself lucky, it's my favorite!

text: Ra is a place I return to often even though I know I will leave feeling it could have been better. Time has not been good to Ra since it opened. The first year it was actually a really nice place to go with good service and okay sushi. But today its a different place, they take for granted their customers will come. if I were to single out one aspect of why I don't like Ra anymore it is the hostess. On a recent Sunday when the restaurant area was 100% empty but the bar/patio were hopping, I was made to wait until all of my party of 9 arrived to be seated. I completely understand such a policy when the restaurant is busy, but 5pm on a Sunday and you don't have even ONE table seated I think it was ridiculous. I can't say this is a one time experience with the hostess staff, they are always rude. The servers are mostly college students and sometimes you have to wonder what is going on in their heads. They can be absent minded to the point you are repeating yourself constantly and reminding them about your drink order from 10 minutes ago. The sushi though is good. Not stellar, but good. Yes it is more expensive than most places, but at least the quality is consistent. The happy hour specials are worth coming early if you can.
label: NEG

text: Stopped here several times for lunch, including a late lunch today. Very dark inside, dark wood, dark floors, dark ceilings, and all the windowblinds closed. But hey, it's supposed to be a cozy pub, right? Typical pub/bar fare, not that great. Had the traditional pub tenderloin, this one looked like it was fresh out of the deep freeze from the wholesaler. No hand breaded tenderloin here, just some institutional stuff like you'd get at the high school cafeteria. The bun looked like something I'd have leftover in a bag of buns smashed down in my bread drawer for a week. Cole slaw was most likely from a tub as well. But it was edible, not horrid, and the place was clean. Must be the hangout for chain smokers, because the place smelled horribly of stale smoke, despite the exhaust fans running like crazy. Came out with my clothing saturated with smoke smell, even though I only saw one person smoking on the far side of the room.
label: NEG

text: Delicious ice cream! Came here on an autumn night which meant....PUMPKIN ICE CREAM. Yum! So creamy and delicious along with the mint chocolate chip I tasted from my friend. It's making my mouth water while typing right now. By the cup, cone, sundaes, splits, and floats, Franklin Fountain should be able to satiate your sweet tooth craving. Loved the old times atmosphere when I walked in. Next trip, I may buy the random doo-dads they have for sale. And if I want instant diabetes (jokingly), perhaps the ice cream waffle sandwiches or Mt. Vesuvius or the other awesome sundaes they offer.
label: POS

text: This service and the people that work for it are completely unprofessional. Had they been a part of the Better Business Bureau, I would have filed a complaint. After waiting for their shuttle for over 30 minutes at the airport (arguably the place that should have the lowest possible wait time), the shuttle arrived. I had talked to the dispatcher on the phone and he quoted me $10/person. The airport help desk confirmed. I asked the driver as well, who also assured me it was $10/person (outside the shuttle). However, after loading our things onto the shuttle, he demanded $60 for 4 people (instead of $40). I argued, and he called his dispatcher (Salomon). With the radio on 'loud', we could hear the dispatcher yell "if they don't pay $60, you can throw them out" and "have them take a taxi, I don't care about them". They then attempted to make the argument that because of our luggage, no more passengers would fit in the shuttle. That might have worked, except they didn't have any other passengers to pick up. This service is worse than something I would expect from a third world country, not in the US.
label: NEG

text: So, I had seen this place ever since I moved 5th and rosemont, wanted to try it for a while but did not have the time. I finally got the chance to visit this restaurant,. I love to try different foods, and my sense of adventure was at it's highest. Early afternoon, i walked in the place was empty, with the exception of what I just came to the conclusion it was a lawyer. The waitress was not very helpful, neither the cook, so; needless to say, I felt that it was not a good time to eat there. I stuck around anyways and order goat curry, (I love goat, when prepared correctly, I have not had birria [a delicious Mexican dish] in a very, very long time) I was excited about eating goat meat once again. the meat was warm, had lots of bones and fat. I tried to enjoy the food as best I could, but the meat had just no taste, I felt like walking out but my adventurous spirit prevented from doing so. Perhaps I just picked the wrong day to visit this place, I have being reading other costumers' review and I just cannot comprehend why I had such bad experience I cannot even bring myself to give ceedee's a one star (but have no choice,personally I'd give it a -2 star). The prices are not bad, is the food that I just cannot bring myself to try again. I won't be going back to Ceedee, not only the food was bad, the treatment I got was below my standards, I have had a better experience at the little hot dog stands...... Trouva

text: Eh. I waited for what felt like days at the front to be seated, but it only turned out to be just shy of 10 minutes. I was seen by every single person that works there, which is what reaaaly bugged me. It was 11:30 am, and there were less than 6 tables sat. I was finally approached by a woman who insisted on calling me "ma'am" (This bothers my well under 30 ass tremendously). She unapologetically sat me and let me wait almost 5 minutes while she retrieved a kids menu. I had an ok BLT on a croissant. I had a coke. My son had a grilled cheese and a chocolate milk. I also had a gift certificate. The cert was purchased at Livingsocial.com and was supposed to be good for $20 at Sweet & Savory. I was told that it was not in fact good for that amount, but for half. She told me it was a half off coupon. My total was less than $15.00, so I was then informed that I'd need to buy other junk (cookies, popcorn, whatever) that would bring my total closer to $20 so that I could then pay $10.00. In essence, I paid $22.95 for that silly little lunch. ($10 for the coupon, and $12.95 for all the crap they made me buy along with lunch). I couldn't get a manager, or anyone else that could read and decipher a printout with about 35 words on it. I dunno. The food was good, but I feel a little bitter about the whole experience. I don't like arguing with servers. I tend to feel exceptionally turned off of places who's waitstaff, or staff in general for that matter, come off as inept. That's how I feel about this Sweet & Savory.

text: The Head Nut is unlike any other place. You have to plan your attack here, as the store is set up in a chain of rooms that are stuffed from top to bottom with every type of nut, candy, or canned thing possible. Their dark chocolate almond bark is to die for, and they have some interesting trail mixes as well. I'll be the first to admit, The Head Nut be a little overwhelming because there is just SO much to look at. You can definitely run in and out, but this isn't Di Bruno Bros, so don't expect the employees to help you too much or offer free samples. All the cashiers that I have seen have been teenagers who are there to get the job done and get out, but are perfectly friendly while doing so. The hours can be a little funny, so make sure you call ahead before making the trip. Happy searching!

The shelves are filled with treasures for those with time to explore. I always enjoy scouring the used CDs. She's got a decent vinyl collection, too.

text: Hooooooo, mmmmmmm, I thought I'd write this before I am filled with regret over everything I just ate! As an out-of-towner unexpectedly stuck in town for a night, I consulted Yelp for some recommendations. I was stoked when I realized this was 2 blocks from my hotel - since I don't have a car, it was a winner! Okay, so I didn't try a burger, but I definitely got the onion rings. Mmmm, they were salty and delicious, perfectly cooked, and came with the good kind of ranch... kinda runny and really tasty. Some bites were really salty, but I do love me some salty salt salt. I went with the cobb salad, and it was actually good - the chicken was tasty! For fast-food-type fare, it was WAY better than anything I've had elsewhere. Plus - bonus! - onion rings + salad + large drink = $12. Are you joking? My company's expense account thanks you, too.

text: This isn't a restaurant. It's a kitchen in someone's home. That's the feel you get when you walk in. The ladies behind the counter gave me healthy amounts of samples when I asked about what things were so I can really taste and choose what I wanted. When I decided on the Catfish Po' Boy, rather than giving me the stuff that was on the heating tray, she waited until a new piping hot batch came out to stuff my po' boy. It was steamy with a very light crisp coating of batter. (see picture I posted). Well worth the wait. Unfortunately, I used my college level reading skills too late to realize that it was CASH ONLY. When I didn't have enough cash on hand to pay for my drink, the lady gave me a Coke, on the house. How nice are they. The place has very limited seating and I saw numerous accounts of people giving up their tables so that others can sit together as a group. I wish the world was more like this restaurant. It's 2 blocks away from the French Quarter on Camp, across the street from the La Quinta. It's not a tourist trap. This is the real thing when you're looking for a taste of New Orleans and true southern hospitality. They close at 2:30pm. Bring cash and a big appetite because their portions are more than generous. I only regret that I didn't have enough cash on hand to get the heaping plate of Red Rice & Beans and the Yam Fries.
label: POS

text: Diner beware! Kid friendly couldn't be farther from the truth. We intended to dine for lunch one day as my family and I walked up to the front entrance, continuing to stand there without an employee in sight. Finally, a gentleman came and greeted us, if that is what you called it, we pleasantly asked to be seated partially outside as we had a party of nine. He abrubtly said no, and I said we would be happy to sit at seperate tables. Side note: there wasn't a single table in the restaurant. Anyway, he said let me check and ran to the back of the restaurant. In the interim my mother-in-law proceeded to go to the restrooms. Not knowing that she was a part of our party she overheard the employees in the back of the service station talking amongst themselves that there was a party of nine with a bunch of kids and one staff member stated "do you want me to tell them we can't seat them". Are you kidding me??? Even though you are thinking it you never say it! And business is business especially in this economy. Are they so well off that Palazzio can pick and chose their guests? My husband and I are both restauranteurs for a prominent restaurant in La Jolla, California and we were completely offended by the way we were treated. Either the staff isn't being trained properly or the management doesn't care. Unfortunately, for them we didn't get to taste the food because this could have had a chance on a semi-positive review, they also missed out on the sales.

text: This one time, I had a hangover, and only a falafel would cure it. Yes, I know. You are supposed to eat cheeseburgers and Doritos's and mountain dew. But, on this well hungover day, all I could think about was loads of tzaziki sauce drenching crispy balls of fried green falafel balls and pita bread. I live about 3 blocks from TGC, and reading all of the rave reviews on Yelp about it, I thought I'd try it out and see if I could fix my aching brain. I think it was lunchtime on a Thursday and the place wasn't that busy. Of course, being the child of the debit card age, I did not have cash, and thus had to leave the store and get some. Dutifully I came back to get the Falafel I had ordered. But, this is not why I give two stars. My two stars are for the dark brown lumps of mash that turned up in my pita. The lettuce, tomato, and tzaziki sauce were spot on, but I just did not like the taste of the falafel at all. Maybe I'm spoiled with Pita + falefel, but TGC's falafel had a dark meaty taste that was nothing like the light, flavorful crispy balls you get from Pita +. Given all of the positive reivews of TGC and its proximity to my house, I will probably try it again, but order something other than my beloved falafel.
label: NEG

text: I think that Jim's on 4th and South is slightly better, but I actually think that Lickety Split may be better than both! I went here yesterday on my way out of Philadelphia. Earlier in the day, I went to Jim's. Jim's is slightly better (I rated it 3-stars) and their meat is more seasoned and minced/chopped. SUMMARY: Philly Cheesesteaks need an update. Anything that has CheezeWhizz as an option is bad news. It's better to eat NYC pizza instead.

text: My experience there left such a bad taste in my mouth, my next 3 visits to firearm shops were tainted by the memory. The two men behind the counter were snide, inconsiderate and treated me like a criminal. I had recently purchased a gun and needed an extra magazine so while I was at work, my new roommate did me a favor and called around to find a good price. That night I went in to buy my magazine with my roommate in tow - looking forward to our first Reno gun shop visit. I've been a Nevada resident for almost 6 years and even have a Nevada CCW but because my newly moved roommate was with me I was refused service. I was not only turned away, but given the 3rd degree and made to feel unlawful the entire time. We went to Scheels later that night and were greeted warmly, helped almost instantly and never interrogated. I walked out not only with my new magazine, but also 1000 rounds of ammo and other accessories. Since then I've bought firearms at Silver State Arms (near Moana on Kietzke) and US Firearms Academy on Moana near Virginia - both locations had great prices and helpful/courteous staff that made us feel welcomed and appreciated the entire time. Whether you're a new buyer or experienced shopper Gun Trader would be the last place I'd recommend.

text: I wanted to check this place out, as Modo Mio is currently my new favorite resturant in town. Had to head down to a customer a few miles away, so I finally got over here for lunch. It was late on a Friday, so I decided to grab the Arista for myself. The crispy meatloaf parm for the wife, and a Daddy Wad for us to spilt for dinner or later in the night. The wife's meatloaft parm was tremendous, but I must say, the Arista is the best sandwich I have ever eaten. With every bite, I was like "Oh my god, this is incredible." I felt kind of bad the next day when I was still talking about it, and my wife pointed out that I never offered her a bite. Whoops. I think that maybe it was so good, that subconsiciously, I didn't want to give any away. And I feel like I'm a pretty good sharer. But that's the bottom line of my review. The Arista is so good that you won't even want to share it with your wife.

text: I have been here numerous times and have been quite pleased with both the food and service. They serve Korean, Japanese, and Chinese dishes, but I usually tend to order the Chinese entrees and save my sushi outings for Bluefin. The honey walnut shrimp is very light and crispy with a delectable creamy sauce that doesn't taste like mayo straight from the jar. My favorites are the scallop and conch with shrimp-stuffed fried tofu and braised pigeon. This is the only place that I have been able to get pigeon...outside of say Shanghai. The lunch bento boxes are decnetly priced and also worth a try. Service is always impeccable. Definitely recommend if you're in the area and have a craving for Asian food.

text: I had called them on a Tuesday asking if it would be possible to set up some appointments to look at apartments the following Saturday. 'No problem', I was told. I gave them some info about what I was looking for, price range, etc. TPAC employee Jeff then sent me some listings via e-mail. I wrote him back with the ones I liked. A day later: no response. I then write a follow-up message to make sure he got our list. Finally on Friday I get an e-mail with the subject line: "Sorry" and this as the message: "I am trying to set up appointment for saturday. The one you were wondering was a 1 bed or studio is a 1 bedroom. I will try and setting appointments up for saturday for the list you sent me. Sorry for the delay getting back to you. Talk to you soon." Ok, no problem. So then my wife and I take a bus down to Philly for the day. While on the bus, I give him a call to see where we should meet, etc. He says "did you get a confirmation from me?" Uhh... what? Apparently he hadn't actually made any appointments at all. He FORGOT. That bus trip cost us $50 and completely wasted our day. How was I supposed to know I had to wait for a confirmation e-mail? We didn't get to see any apartments at all. That's not what I call professional.

text: We love Cafe Alma. Go there pretty often. Atmosphere is great: it is lower than street level in down town St. Pete, so it has a cool Northern up scale barish feel. Lighting is well done, so the tables are lit (most of them, I suggest making sure you either sit at the bar, or get a table than has one of the small spots aimed at the middle of it) and the exposed brick walls are lit nicely as well. The have a small bar that seats about 12. Quality cocktails and good bar tenders. They also have a surprisingly impressive beer selection for a restaurant with good as good as theirs... They have about 4 or so good beers on draft and another 20 or so on the menu described very well... Beers like Left Hand Milk Stout, Three Philosophers, and Magic Hat #9 on draught. The whole menue is online: http://www.cafealma.com/menu.html Food: Excellent. quality meats, well balanced flavors but not too much fuss. Just perfect. We love the Wild Mushroom and Grilled Vegi Risotto.. so creamy and delicious. Great to balance a nice red wine... Oh yeah... their wine list is fabulous and their servers are very well trained on what they sell, and how good it really is. Service...excellent. They keep servers for a long time and it pays off. Their servers are fun, efficient, and know their food and wine very extensively.
label: POS

text: 2 stars and pricey as well. We arrived here for a late dinner at 8:50pm on a Tuesday. We darted in from a rare pouring rain in Tucson to see an empty restaurant, chairs on the tables and 4 startled employees that blurted out something along the lines of "We're not closed!" Since we were cold and wet we decided to get the food to go. We planned on sharing chicken satay and pad thai. The satay seemed expensive at around 7 bucks for 6 skewers. The pad thai was similarly above market price. While we were waiting we asked for some tea to warm up. Cha-ching again x 2. Another 4 bucks for "2 teas". You know, I started my review at 2 stars but 1.5 is more accurate. The pad thai was very bland (how can you make Thai food bland?!). The satay was mediocre. I will say to their credit that I interrupted the cleaning of the bathroom so that I could avail myself of the facilities and they were spotless. So how much for 1 pad thai, 1 satay and tea? 'Bout $22 bucks.

text: Very interesting...they make you pay by the hour! Great if you're only interested in BLASTING a lot of balls downrange. But if you're like me and trying to improve your swing...stay away from this place. It's distracting as hell "being on the clock". I mentioned it to the people working there and they said the owner doesn't like people to use the practice areas free of charge. Um....it's a place to PRACTICE buddy! You shouldn't have to worry about taking your time and getting charged for it. You take a practice swing....charged for it. You clean your clubs....charged for it. You take a break....charged for it. They do offer unlimited practice for $175. Not a bad option if you go more than 15 times a month since they charge $12 per hour. The bottom line - if you are working on your swing....go somewhere else. Oh yeah...it's a pretty good grass range.

text: Ok. Honestly I have been going to this IHOP for a year now and haven't really had any problems. I haven't been totally impressed either....until today. From the time we got there to the time we left the service was GREAT!! Zaira was patient and helpful and clear in what we could get and couldn't get and how much it would cost. We have always liked the hash browns from IHOP. Oh so bad for you but oh sooo soooo very good. Our eggs were cooked correctly. The pancakes were fluffly and warm. And lastly all of the meat was cooked right! One thing that was amazing was the bacon. It was just perfect. Not too crispy or soggy or greasy. If I could cook bacon like this everyday I would probably weigh 400 lbs. Of course this was a Monday morning just after the morning rush. This was my best experience here and will continue to return. PS don't forget that they have bottomless OJ too. 100% not from concentrate OJ. And kids eat free every day after 4:00.

text: This place is hit or miss. Restaurant: Service can be decent, or it can be marred by the magical, disappearing waitress. The food is decent, but it's far overpriced. The redeeming quality here is the $1 burger night. They getcha with all the toppings, but it's still likely worth the price. Bar: Until I went to Pepper Lounge, this place had what I considered to be the worst service in the city. Neither time of day nor day of week seemed to matter; the bar service was consistently awful. Someone who's not friends with the bartender could wait upwards of 15 minutes just to be noticed. Even cash tips don't appear to grease the wheels. The redeeming quality is $2 drafts on Thursday nights. Every draft from their extensive selection is $2. However, the place is so expensive otherwise that Thurs is really the worthwhile night to go.
label: NEG

text: Hawrelak Park is one of my favorite places in Edmonton. I have very fond childhood memories of family outings at the Park, and to this day, I continue to make new memories there. My favorite thing to d at Hawrelak is just to walk. I know that sounds boring but it's not. I love admiring the scenery, feeding the ducks, and soaking up the sun (usually in the summer). I also love people watching there. It's funny because Hawrelak Park brings so many diverse crowds together onto one piece of land. You have your families who take out the paddle boats and eat popsicles down by the water, you have have couples going for a rollerblade or bike ride, sometimes they just lay in the sun and cuddle too. You also have your young crews of 16-25 year olds barbecuing or playing volleyball or frisbee. It's really amazing to see all the different groups that come out to enjoy Hawrelak Park. I love it.
label: POS

text: Enough waxing poetic around the thrill of an old and antiquated transportation system. First off I have been taking Northern Corridor trains for years. And what I have learned is that train travel is one step below bus travel. There record here in the north east is abysmal and they, well don't care! The last four trains were either delayed hours, broke down or never came and this is out of Philly. I feel like I am somewhat knowledgeable since I have spent months in Europe and they have one of the world most efficient mass transportation systems. We cannot even begin to compare the differences in service, price and coverage. As the world runs out of fossil fuels and those huge SUV's become paperweights with payments in our driveways we will be stuck in our own mess with no real transportation infrastructure.

text: Two things: first, it's funny that one of the reviews from 2007 mentioning the surly service could have been written today, three years later; and secondly, why is this place so expensive? text: Early on weekday mornings, you'll find the guys at Jack's counseling distraught and sometimes grieving car owners. Often there is a queue three or four deep, and I've listened as each takes a turn on the bar stool at the counter, and shares his or her sad story of auto misfortune. No matter how hot the weather or busy the schedule, and no matter how impatient the customer with the process of garage triage, he or she gets a listening ear, and a careful explanation of potential problems and options for treatment. During the past week, I've visited three times. Lou got my son's Grand Prix running after a tow for an electrical failure. Todd fixed up my Trailblazer with a new idler pulley assembly and serpentine belt. I also stopped by to see Steve and Lou for advice on an emissions repair and inspection. I've been happy not only with the quality of work, but also the price: upcharge on parts seems modest, and labor charges never seem overbooked. If a part is going to be expensive, they will let you know; if a job will be particularly time-intensive, they will explain why. My first trip to Jack's was for an electrical problem. A previous trip to the dealer had resulted in a $150 partial fix, and recommendation of an expensive new gauge cluster. One hour at Jack's, and the short was tracked down and repaired for one hour labor. It was just a wire pulled free of its contact point in a long harness. That was eight years ago, and I've been going back ever since. Jack was the original owner, and moved the business a short distance to N. Main from its former location actually on the old Route 66 in Edwardsville. Steve bought the place a few years ago, and Lou is his master mechanic right hand man. These guys are smart: they make cars GO!

text: I have taken several weeks to not write this review because of my obvious bias: 1) I'm sending my kid here, and 2) I'm also [censored by my baby mama.] That being said, however, after several weeks of critical thought and analysis, I am now ready to give my full report on why The Orchard School is the finest school in Indianapolis. The primary reason is their core values dictate what they do. Their values reflect a forward thinking learning environment that fosters and celebrates individual achievement and experimental learning in a unique and culturally diverse environment. Uniformity and conformity are not found here. A strict disciplinary approach with rigid structure is not here either. Every student is taught with individual needs addressed, not a curriculum of pass/fail or right/wrong. Instead of telling a student the answer, the teachers teach them HOW to solve the problem, HOW to think through to the answer. Usually, these types of pedagogical approaches are not found until well after post secondary education, yet Orchard is applying these principals early education. The results are impressive. The students show maturity well beyond their years. Their ambitions (along with their achievements) would be impressive for most high school students, much less elementary. For example, I had a third grader telling me about how he just updated his resume, and explained his plans for after he completes his college degree, in addition to what he wants to accomplish along the way. The kid had more in the works in his advanced mind than most adults! But consider this: He is not the only one and far from it. All of these kids LOVE their school, love learning, and are disappointed when school breaks come around. Another reason why I love Orchard is it's approach to the community as a whole. One of Orchard's core values is diversity. Purposely, the school wants, and works, towards an multi-ethnic, multi-income, multi-viewed world in their classroom. Inclusivity and celebration of diversity is real at Orchard, not faked or seen as some chore. It is palpable and a true vision of how a multicultural America could be. How does a private, non faith based school make their tuition affordable? Their large network of donors, of course! Even the teacher's give to the Annual Giving Fund. Corporation donations, grants and a large endowment fueled by gifts from interested parties, parents and alumni defray the actual cost of tuition to affordable rates. Yes, Orchard actually charges less in tuition than it actually costs, and offers need based financial assistance, in order to insure that they capture a diverse range of ethnicities, incomes, and backgrounds. And yet, the students there seem very similar: Eager to learn, a deep drive to succeed, and very well mannered in social and professional graces. The last, but certainly not least, reason I love Orchard School are the dedicated to the point of fanatical parents, teachers and alumni. The teachers are incredible in that they are fantastic and patient with each one of their students, but that once they get to Orchard, they do not want to leave. I cannot recall the exact number but the average teacher has been there ten to fifteen years!?!? That is unheard of in private education, much less public school. My child's teacher has been there for over twenty years and that was her first full-time teaching position. Everyone loves her and she could go anywhere she wanted to (especially with her accomplishments) but she loves the school. The school is in her and much as she is in the school, and she is far from the exception! Also, the parents are the main recruitment tool for Orchard. Almost every single Orchard parent was referred by and Orchard parent. Those that were not recruited directly, were recruited indirectly by parents eagerness to put "Open House" signs in their yard. It's hard to find this much fond dedication from alumni of colleges, but parents seem to be even more motivated to spread the fame. Also, alumni also are involved and give back to their school out of their time, talents and treasure. Several parents offer products of theirs as raffle donations, and we are not talking about small freebies, but big ticket items like AUTOMOBILES! That's dedication! In summary, Orchard is the best school I have ever encountered, and I am somewhat jealous that I can afford to send my kid here. I just wish I could be a kid again in her shoes for a little while!
label: POS

text: I stayed here in 2007 and I remember it as a very nice hotel. I expected it had been kept up but it is not what you would expect a Westin to be. Like other guests, I was disappointed. There is an additional $15/day self-parking fee as well as a $12.95/day internet access fee so be sure to add that to your room cost. Breakfast is also not included. If you can get a better rate at the Embassy Suites nearby, stay there. It is a newer hotel, very well maintained, and includes a buffet breakfast and free internet. The Marriott which is also a block away is another option (until this hotel is renovated). From the moment I walked into the hotel from the parking garage there was an unpleasant odor of moisture and musk. The elevators are worn, the floor tile cracked, the tiles elevator floors were filthy, and the wooded panel extremely scratched - a horrible first impression. Even the up/down elevator buttons in the lobby are heavily scratched. The up button does not light up. The front desk attendant who greeted me was wonderfully kind and professional. This helped soften my disappointment. Check-in was quick. I was even allowed to occupy the room before check-in time which is welcomed perk and much appreciated. The hallways carpets are worn, stained, and visibly torn. I have never stayed at a Westin with the common areas in such poor condition. The carpet in the lobby area was similarly worn and parts were torn. The furniture is dated. The actual room (820) was a good size and had a view of the canal and part of Tampa Bay, in addition to overlooking the parking lot and garage. You could see the pool below which was extremely small and not what you would expect of a resort. The kind-sized bed was comfortable. The linens were clean but also visibly well used. The bathroom had a granite counter and a basic shower/bathtub. The entryway and bathroom had a clean and light colored ceramic tile which was very pleasant. The toiletries were nice (not brand-name high end though) but I had to ask for shampoo and soap (which were missing). The bathroom had plastic wrapped cups but if you want glass there were two glasses with the ice bucket. However, the ice bucket did not have the usual sanitary plastic bag. When I asked for one I was told it was no longer provided which I found highly unsanitary. No bathrobes. The towels were fluffy, appeared to be relatively new, and clean-smelling. The water pressure in the bathroom basin was excellent but the water pressure in the shower was so poor that I had to ask for an engineer to check the shower head. When I returned after dinner, the shower head had been changed and the water pressure was acceptable although not excellent. Again, the maid should have checked to ensure the showerhead was clean and the water pressure adequate. The problem may have been with caulk build-up and poor maintenance/cleaning. Again, not what one would expect from what Hotwire and others label as the only four-star hotel in downtown Tampa. I deserves two starts at most (until it is refurbished). The bedroom was spacious. The drapes were in excellent shape although visibly worn. The furniture was also well-used but acceptable (had this been anything but a Westin). The internet connection worked well. There were two plugs on the large working desk which were perfect to connect the laptop and the phone charger. The flat screen LCD TV worked perfectly and had an ample choice of channels. There were an ample number of drawers and the closet space was normal but well lit. I liked the Starbucks coffee packets and machine provided in the room. Adding the extra costs to the Hotwire room cost, I should have stayed elsewhere, either at the Embassy Suites, Marriott, or the Residence Inn which are all nearby. The injera (bread) was essential to the meal (the earthy flavor helped cut the heat of the spices in the beef) and served the dual purpose of your utensil. Since they didn't provide utensils, you used the bread to scoop up the food. I really enjoyed this aspect of the dining experience. Overall the food was great and reasonably priced ($10/entree...another huge plus). We ordered some beers along with our dinner, but wine and liquor were also available. If you have never had Ethiopian food, I would highly recommend it, especially if you are a fan of Indian food as the spices were reminiscent of Indian cuisine.

text: Sixteen years ago I adopted the best dog in the whole world. Found in cage number 11, he barked and smiled and barked some more and it was love at first sight. But, the SPCA did not want to let me adopt him. I was young, I rented an apartment, I did not have a property deed. It is understandable to want to ensure that a pet will have a good home. And perhaps promises of undying love and devotion are not enough to warrant the transfer of a dog from a shelter to a stranger. But they made me jump through many hoops: copies of my lease; wanting to talk to my landlord (before cell phones made this possible at the times they were open.) And, they were not very nice. Rude, dismissive, too busy to be bothered, annoyed. Three times I visited hoping to adopt him. And next to me were homeowners (this seemed to be the key) looking at a dog. They clearly stated, "If he doesn't work out we can just bring him back." It was unbelievable that these people, elderly but possessing a property deed, were able to be so brazen about their lack of commitment and still allowed to adopt the dog. Well, the short side of the story is that I did what all young girls are tempted to do when they feel mistreated. I called my father. I am not sure what he did, or who he talked to, but on the fourth day and fourth attempt to adopt Kota, I was granted the privilege of taking him home. We have been together ever since. And I am very thankful to my father for his mysterious assistance. Just recently, 16 years later, I found a dog running lose, trailing his leash behind him in Media. Of course, I grabbed him before he ran into traffic on State Street and proceeded to ask everyone I saw if they knew the dog. Then Sam and I spent several hours going from place to place, pet store, emergency vet, etc. to see if anyone knew where he lived, if he had a micro chip, etc. The Del. Co. SPCA was our last choice. Funny, that ideally it should have been our first choice. But the sentiment was consistent at each place we visited. Perhaps better to keep the dog for a few days and post signs than to drop him off there... In the end we had no choice. We walked into the SPCA and were completely ignored as the staff talked amongst themselves commenting on a recent client...negatively in front of other clients. They seemed disorganized and annoyed (still!) And there Sam and I stood wtih a little dog in our arms...waiting...waiting. Finally we had to be rude to get someone's attention. (What did they think we wanted standing there with this dog anyway?) There is a happy ending. Someone realized she had taken a "Lost Dog" call for the dog we had found. The owners were called and we volunteered to drive the dog home. He never had to be checked into or checked out of the SPCA. It would have been hard to leave him there. If people love animals and want to work with them, I would hope that they would like people who also loved animals and are trying to help them. But it seemed there is no protocol to dealing with people, or communicating, or being helpful. A place to adopt animals should be much friendlier, perhaps cleaner, perhaps more organized.

text: Panda King is actually two restaurants in one: a buffet place open every day and a push cart dim sum place in the adjacent building that's only open Saturday and Sunday between 10:30am-3pm. Dim sum is basically like Spanish tapas, except dim sum came first and it's better and cheaper. This review is for the dim sum experience ONLY. If you're curious about the buffet, I can sum (haha, I made a funny) it up in a couple sentences: there's boring, and then there's the Panda King buffet. It's bland even by Chinese buffet standards, and the selection is pretty weak. THE GOOD Push Cart Service: What do I mean by push cart? Traditional Chinese dim sum is served on carts that are wheeled around the restaurant, allowing patrons to select what they want as the carts pass by. I really like this style as opposed to the a la cart style that you may have tried at Royal China in Metairie. It just adds so much to the dining experience. The Food: There are so many choices that it can be intimidating for newcomers to the experience. Trust me, it's all pretty good at Panda King. Here is a partial list of what we have eaten: *Ha Gow - steamed shrimp dumpling. Standard fare, but always good when done right. They do it right. *Shu Mai - steamed pork dumpling. Also pretty standard, but larger than expected which is good. *Cheng Fun - rice paper rolls with meat inside. This is probably my favorite dish. It's basically the same noodle as in beef chow-fun, wrapped around either sweet BBQ pork, shrimp, or beef. The kicker is the sweet soy sauce that they pour on top. Absolutely divine. However, you need to practice your chopstick skills before ordering, because the combo of noodle and sauce make this dish kind of hard to pick up. *Pork Spare Ribs - usually comes with black bean sauce. Their version also has red bell pepper with it, which I found kind of odd. *Chicken Feet - yes! If you don't mind spitting out tiny bones onto your plate, this is the dish for you. Theirs is spicy, which can be good or bad depending on your preference. *Fried Taro - fried shell (Panda King gets a gold star for making it perfectly light and crisp) with steamed taro inside. You're not gonna find texture like this in any other cuisine, so it should definitely be on your try-it-just-once list. *Carrot Cake - not at all like the dessert, it's a mixture of carrot, taro, and meat (maybe some flour too) pan-fried and cut into squares. Same advice as with the fried taro. Success again as they didn't over-dry it, which can happen more often than it should at other places. *Steamed BBQ Pork Buns - sweet BBQ pork wrapped in a fluffy white bun. A favorite for everyone. They are generous with the pork which is always a plus. *Congee with "thousand-year" egg - Rice porridge with preserved egg. The egg looks old and gross but don't let appearances fool you, it tastes delicious. *Gai Lan - The famous Chinese veggie. Dark green leaves still attached to crunchy stem. It is topped with oyster sauce, which helps counterbalance the slight inherent bitterness of the vegetable. *Egg Tart - OK so maybe THIS is my favorite dish. Flaky pastry shell filled with a flan-like center. I once ate twenty of these by myself. If you like flan at all, then you'll love this. Perhaps my favorite dessert, ever. Price Point: This place is super-affordable as long as you stay away from the big dishes like Peking Duck or the large plates of Fried Rice/Chow Fun. Those are the trap dishes. At prices ranging from $1.99-$4.99 for every item, just stick to the dim sum and you can be completely satisfied at $10-20 a person depending on how big your appetite is. As for the Peking Duck, just walk to the other side of the shopping complex to Hong Kong Food Market and get a whole one. More cost-efficient, plus you get to watch the butcher chop it up for you. THE BAD None. PURGATORY Speed and Quantity: This is the one dining experience that I want things to go quickly. PUSH THAT CART OUT ASAP! Unfortunately at busy times if you happen to be sitting at the tail end of the restaurant you may have to wait for the cart with your favorite items to be reloaded once or maybe even twice before it gets to you. I think I counted about six carts in total, but they need more. Man, dim sum diners can be straight vultures... OVERALL Is this the best dim sum place I've ever had? Nope. Have I been spoiled by the awesomeness of places in Vancouver, Canada? Most certainly. That's why this place gets 5 stars: In no way would I have expected to get push cart dim sum in this city, and not only does Panda King deliver and then sum (I did it again!), but the quality at the price they charge is more than suitable to satiate my dim sum cravings. Good job Panda King. Now get more carts. Go if you: like dim sum, are adventurous with food, want to try new things, like eating for value. Don't go if you: like sticking to the basics, don't like going to the West Bank

text: How does that saying go..."If you build it, they will come." Why doesn't that apply to Chinese food? Why does chinese food in Nashville have to be Amereicanized? We then had the mu shu pork, some veggie lo mein and a chicken and broccoli. Mediocre at best. But the veggie lo mein - again. Where are the vegetables? This lo mein came with a couple pieces of broccoli (uncommon for lo mein which usually is served with a plethora of onions, cabbage, carrots, snow peas), two pieces of baby corn (always from a can) and a couple slivers of napa cabbage. I mean, come ON folks. I know you are serving a mostly American clientele (and judging from the reviews below, with not very discerning palettes), but still. Quality really counts and if Chinatown were to up their vegetables and their presentation, more people would come! It really would not take that much effort. So sad....

text: I went to Tria this past weekend to meet up with some friends, a little early start to the night's Memorial Day weekend festivities. First, I mistakenly went to the 18th st. location, only to realize my friends were at the one on 12th & spruce...no matter, a quick cab ride got me there in no time. FIRST IMPRESSIONS: This place is clearly for the sophisticated crowd, as if there is a such thing as the unsophisticated wine and cheese bar (I won't ask). It's a place to go to enjoy a fine glass of wine and a small thing or two off the menu. It didn't strike me as a place to go for dinner, although this might not be the case...I had a couple glasses of the Four Graces Pinot Blanc, and the Italian Meats tray. THE LAYOUT: Sophisticated and refined are the key words here. It's not some lifestyles of the rich and famous kind of pomp-shack...but if you are put off by yuppies in sport coats laughing pretentiously at the toiling of the average lowly peon, this might not be the joint for you (okay, I didn't hear any laughing about said subject going on, but you get the point hopefully). Dark wooden furniture, lit naturally by the afternoon sun peering through the large open windows. There is a patio section and an indoor section, separated by these large windows, which are open in warmer months. THE WINE & FOOD: The reason I tried the Four Graces is because Tria does a special, pairing a selection of wine, cheeses, and beer, first round is half off. It was exquisite in my (unseasoned) opinion-- I was looking for a wine that wasn't too dry, a little fruity, and that held it's flavor and consistency throughout. Hit the nail on the head. The Italian Meat platter was also very good-- various Italian meats that I won't dare to try and remember the name/spelling, some of the sweetest red peppers I've ever seen, and a delicious mixture of garlic-infused olive oil with a tangy red pepper/garlic paste for the bread...oh yeah, and Caper Berries...I don't like them, so I won't allow it to affect my review, if you like em, you will probably enjoy them here. It was all very tasty, if not a little expensive (although not necessarily overpriced)...I wasn't expecting more for my money, per se, I was just surprised at the bill. It's not a killer, but it was a little high. THE SERVICE: We were fortunate enough to have Shuli (sp?) as our server, she was very friendly, attentive and knowledgeable. Sometimes when you visit a place like this, you get some hipster wine snob who expects you to know Napa like the back of your hand. Well in Shuli's case, despite my constant ignorant inadvertent insults to the finer things in life, she was able to boost my experience by being so nice. I don't know if it's a good thing or a bad thing that there isn't a set dress code for the staff there, but someone behind the bar was wearing a plaid shirt...not what I'd expect to see, but I don't get bothered by things like that. THE ATMOSPHERE: We spent the afternoon in a wine-induced haze (not drunk, mind you) feeling the buzz and the warm breeze. We talked about all kinds of things, including the VERY eclectic soundtrack, which went from kama sutra-esque ambient, to underground chill hip hop, to country, to pub rock. I don't know who the hell put together that playlist, but it drew more laughter than anything else-- the transitions were too abrupt. It didn't take away from the experience, but it was notable. THE VERDICT: If you are looking for a great, relaxing, refined experience, or if you want to throw (or enjoy) a wine and cheese party outside of your designer loft, Tria, is the place to go. I gave it 4 out of 5 for the minor annoyances I had (I'm like Larry David when it comes to wierd random quirks like that), but it really was an excellent way to start the evening, and I would love to go back again!

text: New Orleans Birthday Trip = Shopping in the French Quarter Ever since accidentally wandering into this store, our ongoing joke has been "when I collect enough stuff I want to open a store and then just sell it off," because it's true. This store really feels like its owner just found all his stuff in his closet and said he needed to sell it to make some room, but what great stuff you'll find in here. Selection: Think of that old record store that used to be down on the corner of Main Street. Now think of that weird old guy that used to run it--that's who was in the shop when we showed up. Between the wall full of vinyl with everything under the sun, the pile of old school comic books including Vampirella, and just about every edition of The Joy of Cooking ever, the older shopkeeper only made your choices even more vast. You know they were all things that he'd picked up over the years, and that just makes them all the more real. The array of used copies of just about everything will knock you off your feet, and if that doesn't do it the low low prices well. There was an extensive section on Cajun, Creole and Southern cooking, as well as baking, healthy and world cuisines. There's a nice stack of old Maxim and Penthouse and Playboy magazines too, back when showing a little nip was risque. Looking around you'll find knickknacks and trinkets that charm and entice, but if you're like me you'll revel in the used cookbooks everywhere. Used cookbooks mean amended recipes and better suggestions for pairings, dogeared pages and circled favorites. I found myself an old copy of River Road Recipes to perfect my jambalya and gumbo. What will you find? Venue: Kitchen Witch is one of those places you'd never find if you were in need of it. Like a gas station when you're running empty or a liquor store when you've lost your buzz, when you're really in need of a cookbook, you'll forget all about it and forget where it is. But on a hot say when you're waltzing back to your hotel and looking forward to a drink and a nap, it's the perfect reprieve. Like most else in NOLA, it's somebody's old house converted. A one story store, the interior walls have been removed but the remnants of two, maybe three rooms remains. Large wooden shelves and bookcases line the walls and bins litter the floor. The big table doubles as a counter and two dogs lounge on the floor eyeing your wearily. There's dim light and a chair to sit in, but really, it's the perfect shop for the cook/man/music lover/geek/old guy in all of us.

text: The woman at the Hertz counter was an angel! She worked very hard to get us into the right van. I had made a reservation for a minivan for the 6 of us and had a coupon to use. I would have been ok with a car if we could all fit but there was a conference in town and they didn't have much of anything to offer. After waiting patiently and explaining we couldn't fit into a car this angel sprinkled her dust and worked her magical fingers to get the computer to take our coupon. She gave us the discount we would have gotten for renting a car and we paid the difference for getting the van instead. Yeah, the Brady Bunch now has wheels. We opted for the fuel refill by Hertz since their prices were lower than the going rate and then our angel gave us two sets of keys and off we went. 4 kids, 3 pieces of luggage and 4 back packs of toys and barbies, 1 bear, 2 American Girl dolls and me and Mr. G boarded the Chrysler 2010 New Town and Country. The ride was smooth and the cabin had a great openness to it allowing lots of light in. We have a minivan at home but this one was a winner by all of us, maybe because it was newer too. Trying out rental cars is a good way to shop for a new set of wheels. Either new or old they are well tested since they are driven by so many, go so many miles, and tend to get beat on. What better way to see how a car does than by going to a rental place. I love Toyota and Honda so making a shift to Chrysler would be a big leap. The return back to the airport was easy. We drove up and two reps approached. One jumped in to take all the stats and the other did an inspection while a porter had our bags and stuff all loaded up. Within minutes we had our receipt and away we went. The dining room is tiny. They don't take cards, only cash. All in all, this is one of those little known, "locals only" kinds of restaurants. text: Yes, there really is a bus, and yes, they do serve tacos. The bus (long-since disabled and permanently parked) houses a tiny kitchen and one or two people taking orders. Giant laminated menus frame the order window and list options ranging from Lengua Burritos to Vegan Butternut Squash Tostadas. This establishment (better known as "The Taco Bus") is not really a restaurant, but more of a "lunch counter" kind of place. There is outdoor seating (covered) and a little bit of seating inside a small building, but there's no AC.There are bathrooms inside the building and they are always clean. DO NOT be one of those annoying people that comes to this place and expects to be waited on hand and foot. Go to the counter, order your food and sit and wait for it to be brought, steaming hot to your table. Don't expect a "server" because that's not what this place is about. Parking is also limited; I advise entering the back lot off of Nebraska since turning off of Hillsborough is a pain. Turn on Nebraska, make your first left and there's a big arrow on your left that says "TACO BUS". The menu is broken down (and Gringo-friendly for all of us who love Hispanic/Latino culture and food but lack the language skills to know how to read a menu in Spanish) into "fillings," a list of different preparations of meat and non-meat items, and "wrap it your way," which lists your different options for tasty filling-holding. Meats include pork, beef, chicken, fish and tofu and wrappings include plato (served on a plate over rice and beans); taco, burrito, quesadilla and torta. This place is definitely vegetarian and vegan-friendly, but if you're a hardcore vegan, you have to order "without cheese" since it comes standard on everything. The veggies that will top your little taco from heaven include red onions, cabbage and cilantro; a refreshing departure from wilted lettuce and shady cheese shreds. Cotija cheese sprinklings crown just about everything and the Butternut Squash Tostada is no exception. What to order: SWEET TEA Tofu Taco Burrito Prenado (with just veggies or with meat) Ceviche Tres Leches Cake Oh, and did I mention it's 24/7?

text: What can I say that hasn't already been written in one of the previous 145 reviews? My fiance (first time referring to her as my fiance!) had an omelet with smoked salmon that was light and fluffy. Overall, it was a wonderful experience and a special way to celebrate. Although a little pricey for brunch, it's not that bad if compared to a nice meal at night. (He makes me order it so he doesn't look girly.) My go-to appetizers are the wings, coconut shrimp or shrimp with cubano bread (to dunk and soak up all that buttery goodness), and soups. Please please please avoid the entrees and split some appetizers because they're large servings, cheaper, and have all that island mojo you crave! And most of their cocktails are $6 or less. You can't even get drinks that cheap at happy hours in Manhattan. I hate to love Bahama Breeze.

text: My family and I haven't been to New Dragon Palace in a long time, so we decided to see what we have missed these past few years. We decided to order Peking Duck, an extravagant meal that is a real test of authenticity for every Chinese restaurant. First came the duck soup. The broth itself was alright, although a bit on the salty side. I noticed that some of the pieces of duck in the soup were a bit tough, despite being soaked in the soup. I was not very impressed when the actual duck dish came out. The pieces were too well cooked, and you could tell from its dark appearance. The duck meat was also very dry and tough. The wrap that you get for assembling your 'Chinese taco' was also very moist, and kept on ripping or simply falling apart on me. The service was good in the restaurant though, and the food came out quickly, which might have been its only saving grace. This may have been a bad day for the chef, but we probably won't go back anytime soon.

text: Mexico on the Square is good. Delivery was super fast and the ingredients seemed to be of high quality. My sticking point is the burrito. It might beat Qdoba or Chipotle, but that is not saying much. Soggy, odd texture, minimal meat, sub-par rice, and a lack of spice. I ordered it without sour cream, so the sogginess was inexcusable. It clearly wasn't put on heat once it had been wrapped. The rice was very soggy and lacked beans. The worst part was the raw green peppers - the crunch gave the burrito a very odd texture. And NO spice. If you need a burrito in this city, go to Don Memo in West Philly. You will wait almost an hour, but you will be rewarded with the greatest burrito you have ever encountered.

text: I studied at Norquest for two years before I got accepted to the university, and I have only good things to say about this college. Firstly, the instructors are fantastic. They know the subjects they teach in and out, take the time they spend in a classroom very seriously, and make sure that all students gain as much knowledge as possible. Good attendance is of utter importance at Norquest because instructors don't waste a single minute of their classes on chats and jokes, so skipping classes will have negative consequences and will result in lagging behind. In fact, I believe that Norquest has a policy regarding how many classes a student is allowed to miss during any given semester. The second unique thing about Norquest is that this college is being attended by students from all over the world. I know for sure that Norquest college is the number one choice of new immigrants who just begin to study English, or need to take Academic Upgrading in order to proceed with their studies at UofA or Grant MacEwan. Norquest is such a fun place to meet new people! Finally, what makes Norquest great is the fact that all classrooms are small. This way an instructor can devote a lot of attention to each student, and follow everyone's progress up close. In addition to Academic Upgrading, Norquest offers lots of certificate and diploma programs in the fields of business, human services and health care.

Oh, and they participate in the Live in HD opera program! The lobby is covered in signs about children, teenagers, and the parental supervision requirements which is nice. Our steaks were perfect (rare is rare) and could be cut with a fork, literally. Gorgonzola cheese with mine and a very nice Bernaise on the wife's filet. As we thought, it was very tasty and we enjoyed two bottles! Dessert was just over the top chocolate cake that we enjoyed with a few tawny ports and nice, hot coffee. All-in-all, our time at Lucky's was enjoyable and memorable. If I live in Santa Barbara area, I'd treat myself to Lucky's once a month. text: I will respond to two interesting reviews of this city with my own celebration of its mediocrity and hope to inspire others to help me make it better here. The most common praise I hear from people new to Tucson is that the weather is great and they like the sight of the mountains. Even though this is probably just a say-something-nice-or-dont-say-anything-at-all, the weather is actually convenient, you can do things outside on any day of the year, and there are mountains and therefore parks, trails, etc in every direction. It's a myth that it's too hot to do things outside in the summer in AZ. Other places are hotter. There's the U of A here, which makes things better, and a nearly unlimited diversity in types of places to eat, buy crap, hang out, get drunk, be offended, etc. As a vacation spot Tucson is one of the best places to chill without a beach, especially if you are really old and like to golf, and has some very nice resorts. The only really important tourist stop is the desert museum, which is not like the museums you're thinking of. The one complaint I get most often from people visiting or who have recently moved is that the people at bars are not friendly and even sometimes rude. Honestly, I've tried to make this exact sandwich at home and it never tastes the same - it's gotta' be that poppyseed dressing....haven't been able to find the kind they use at Mama Bear's. On our visit, hubby had the BLT, which he raved over because it had a light smear of cream cheese along with the usual suspects. He said this made the sandwich really pop. Sadly, we did not have room - or the calorie budget - for any of Mama Bear's pies or other goodies. However, I have had them in the past and they are wonderful. text: I'll preface this whole review by saying that I have a weakness for cheap, hole-in-the-wall diners filled with bunches of interesting "regulars". I love picking up the check for a table of five and finding that the bill is $21 even. I love walking in and feeling like the only people who know of its existence are sitting in its booths. I love seeing the same faces, eating the same breakfast platters, in the same reserved seats, while reading the same sections of the same newspapers each Sunday morning. I love trying to imagine what these people do when they are NOT eating eggs and drinking coffee. It's as though I (along with a coven of fastidious senior citizens) have discovered The Fountain of Deflation and it serves pancakes. Pancakes! The Ranch House is the Crme-de-la-crme of such diners in the Town 'n Country area. It's located at the east end of an old strip mall and easy to miss. It's a small place with a coffee bar, eight or nine tables and four and a half booths. Yes, there is one half of a booth. Stop by. Seat yourself. Order some greasy bacon. Enjoy the scenery. At the End of the Day - Once in the Ranch Houses' parking lot, look for the flashy pick-up parked in the handicapped slot with the personalized "PIMP" license plate and try to match it with its owner sitting inside. text: I really can't say I'm a fan. Sure, all the ingredients are local and everything's presented nicely, but the stuff has got to taste good too. The four of us ordered off the 3 course tasting menu. The bisque served was very good, but it was pretty much downhill from there. There are plenty of other places that serve just as good a bisque anyway. The "mojito ceviche" was pretty tasteless beyond some mint. The main courses didn't offer anything memorably welcome either. A pork tenderloin served with a seared pork belly yielded hunks of fat with a ridiculously unchewable seared side with unimpressive sliced tenderloin. The fiance ordered the roast chicken expecting some dark meat only to find that it was all white. I'm a fan of white meat but it was pretty dry. I ordered the shrimp with grits that came with a stuffed trotter (I could have sworn it was snout, but anyways...) and the shrimp and grits didn't offer much of anything. The trotter, which was nicely crispy on the outside with some fat, but the inside stuffing was some five-spice flavored lean ground pork. I wonder if the chef had the intention of the fat in the trotter to moisten up the pork (Have had such a trotter stuffed with sticky rice and pork before... that rocked.) but it definitely didn't work out. I'm getting the impression that this place is trying to bring the "farmer food" with some "elegant flare" but this place just made me leaving pretty pissed off. Beyond the great atmosphere, An American Place served up little else.

text: I went here for the 5 course tasting menu on Sunday, 28-Dec-08. From start to finish, Pumpkin delivered a fantastic meal. I would definitely return without an iota of hesitation. Service is one of the most controllable and influential aspects of dining out so its nice to go to a place that really cares about satisfaction. The meal was good sized portions for a tasting menu which is nice considering the potency, complexity and balance in each bite was worth revisiting. I really enjoyed the walu appetizer and flank steak entree. The only part of the meal that was just OK was the salad. This meal was really good because for the week before hand, all I ate was Polish holiday food in my hometown so the freshness and flavors were a great break to that monotony. The only potential downside of this place is that it can be loud. When I was at Pumpkin, there was a table of six people who apparently could only communicate by shouting to each other despite being 3 feet away. Also, I cannot understand how a restaurant like this doesn't take credit cards. I can see the point of not taking cards from a logistic and managerial standpoint but I hope they start taking cards in the future. They also should have a real website. If your a fan of an ever evolving menu and fresh, wholesome ingredients, then you should definitely visit Pumpkin. Great place that I hope is around for a long time.
