text: I used to go to Bubbles on Rittenhouse on a regular bases. My stylist Cyndi was godsend, because she knew what was what. She knew she was a good, solid stylist working at a chain location that desperately wanted to pretend to be more high profile and classy than it actually is. See, I'm a guy. And on top of that, I'm a fat guy. A fat, gay professional rock and roll musician. I like wacky haircuts. And I have a beard that constantly needs to be styled. And Cyndi understood that. She understood that I was not the typical Bubbles customer, but she never once made me feel unappreciated and out of place. Six months ago, after going to Bubbles for a year and a half, Cyndi left. How do I explain the change? It's like replacing the diamond in your wedding ring with poop, because glass is just too classy. Out of my last 6 visits, only one was acceptable, and I don't know why I kept going back. I think I had just held onto hope that things would go back to the way they were when Cyndi still worked there. The final straw was a few days ago. I went in for a cut&style plus a beard trim, and I brought in my best friend Toshio. Toshio is also a rock and roller, even moreso than I. He is - surprise - Asian, and he has thick black hair. On this occasion he wanted it shaved into a traditional mohawk. Before our appointments we were quoted a price of $25, each. My haircut was decent, but then again all he did was shave my head and style my beard - and I brought in pictures for the beard, so it would have been hard to screw up. Toshio's stylist was a snotty little man bitch. I was not privy to the experience, but I heard back from Toshio that the stylist was constantly arguing over the actual style Toshio came in for. He wanted to give him some kind of fashiony feauxhawk with a tail or some nonsense. Hey, know what? I think it's great you have ideas and input as a stylist. You should definitely share that. But when you are so insistent that you make your client uncomfortable, there's a problem. Toshio finished before I did, and they charged him $35 for his cut and style. If you were paying attention, you'll note that's $10 more than quoted. They charged ME $30, and mine included a beard styling. Then, when we got outside into the light, I noticed they had BUTCHERED his hair. The mohawk part was decent, but the side areas that were supposed to be totally shaven had splotchy areas where the hair was visibly longer than the rest. And not in some kind of intentional pattern, mind you, but just clearly a hack job of a shaving. What followed was 4 days of arguing over the phone with "Dallas," the district manager with an attitude, and now I am scheduled to meet the store manager John today at 9AM to get a refund. I guess I can report back on how that goes. Suffice to say, my Bubbles have burst.

text: I'm going to completely honest here. This place is not for everyone. And yet there's magic afoot if you're part of one of the following rather niche demographics: ---- 1. prefer to be left alone by your fellow diners and bar patrons 2. cannot tolerate excessive noise, light or slow service while dining 3. have young children / are tired of going to restaurants where there is no buffer between breeders and non-breeders / are prepared to punch the next person who rolls their eyes at you in the mouth 4. are strict vegetarian yet smoke and enjoy more than 1 non-mixed drink a day (like me... but still... please keep you smoke away from the patio) 5. aren't a food snob, trust fund baby or ethnovangelist 6. are not JLO (see above) 7. are too hungry for dainty portions and / or have a hankering for Grimexican (read: middle of the road) food 8. understand that kitsch is a state of mind and not a fashion statement 9. are in search of a good meal that you won't regret later (financially or gastronomically) 10. actually give a shit how the person who serves you is being treated by their employer, whether or not they were born North of Texas 11. are trying to arrange a marraige well in advance for your 2-year-old son; who freaks out every time he sees a certain beautiful waitress that loves to "flirt" with him / dotes on him (in spite of the fact that her English and his Spanish are both rather thin) 12. hate empty restaurants as much as crowded ones 13. want to get seated right away and appreciate decent service 14. can buck up and realize that while nothing is perfect to everyone, some things are perfect as you find them 15. know a humorously disgusting mixed drinks list when you see one ---- Suffice to say, this isn't my "dining out" spot -- it's a reliable "eating out" spot, and has been for many years. I've always been able to customize anything on the menu with no trouble at all; not sure about the "frozen" thing. Nothing here tastes that way, either. The 2nd time I went for a burger, a specialty (cheese steak burger on a pretzel roll) my friend and I split a side of onion rings. So good. I hate it when you're eating an onion ring and the onion slides out of the breading. These onion rings don't do that. They are on point. Some day I would like to try the peanut butter and banana and jelly sandwich. Someone wrote that their burgers aren't very big - I felt like they are a decent size - not humongous but big enough - and loaded with delicious and rich toppings. That special sauce is good. It's a different style burger than some of the other ones you get around town. Also, how big do you need your burger to be if you're ordering onion rings and/or a shake to go with it? My only complaint about PYT is that their food is soooo rich that it is very filling - I can't possibly finish a whole order of anything by myself. I tried once because it tasted so good, and was so stuffed I felt like I was going to pop afterwards. I had to take a nap and couldn't enjoy the rest of the evening. No apology, just a "we can move you to a different room". Of course, it was another smoking room. At least this room was sightly less stinky. I just can't get over the customer service here. text: I hope I came on a bad night. I love African food. I love the freshness and the simplicity. What I got at Bennachin was overcooked mush over soggy rice with a big helping of salt. Now I know they weren't always so bad. I used to stop by there on my way home from work when they first opened up. I knew the service was dirt slow but I liked the fish pies. But this experience was awful. The only place in town I would give a lower score to would be Nawlins Flava (totally off with that name). Not only was the food (should I call it that?) horrible, but our very nice, pixie-like waitress(She really was nice and polite) smelled so bad that whenever she came to the table or even half way across the floor, a wave of odor would make our eyes water and our noses burn. The people at the table by the door also coughed and gagged a bit when she came by. We exchanged looks when they were leaving (With most of their meal uneaten). Don't get me wrong, I'm all for gutter kids getting jobs, but you sort of need to bathe before work, especially in a restaurant. We also left after just a few fork fulls between us. Having said all that, I have been reading the other reviews and not seeing much similar to our experience so as I said...I'm hoping to all that is holy that I just came on a bad night. I'm just too afraid to try it again. Wish we had another African restaurant around here.

text: Effie's is kind of iffy. It's not great. And we had to wait. Friday night seated at 7:15 pm. Dinner arrived at 8:20. I mean seriously. BYO wine, made it passable, but come on. Inside by the hostess i could see the large metal tray containing uncut moussaka, and food being re-warmed in a microwave. Teas can be ordered hot and French Press as well. The space is very bright and friendly, and there is free wifi. If you're hungry, there is a small selection of pressed sandwiches, as well as waffles. My iced coffee was shaken right in front of me, made to order with the amount of cream I requested. It was served in open of those tall plastic cups used for bubble tea - complete with the seal on top. Gigantic! And at under $4, very reasonable. text: This is what I have been waiting for. A place where a man can get a man's sandwich. And a place where the sandwiches are affordable. And a place where the sandwiches are delicious. Fozzie's is a sandwich lover's dream. A menu chalked full of classics and Fozzie originals. This isn't your Fozzie-the -bear-muppet kind of sandwich place. I was dying to try Fozzie's ever since they opened, and upon viewing the menu, I know I will become a regular within no time. My first visit I opted to go with The Big Bend Mafia. A delectable mix of spicy italian beef and salsiccia suasage covered with peppers, onions and cheese and smashed between two hoagie buns. We got our meal to go, and by the time I got home the juices from my sandwich were seeping through the paper my sandwich was wrapped in - a true sign of a great sandwich. The Mafia was bursting with spices and flavor - and the meat had some kick to it. My wife had the falafel sandwich, which was pretty good but didn't compare to mine. The falafel came on a bun in 3 round "pucks" along with a bunch of other more healthy toppings than my Big Bend Mafia. It still tasted good. We both had the home-made chips which were surprisingly crunchy and delicious, cut very thin and cooked to a good crisp. Most home made chips are too thick and soggy and covered in grease, these had a good crunch - quite the opposite. She also ordered the Carmel milkshake - another big hit. Sweet and creamy delight! I liked this place so much I brought my brother back the next day and he had rave reviews for it as well (he had the classic italian sandwich). I would recommend ordering ahead by calling - we did have to wait awhile for our food when we just walked in to order. But, everything is made fresh, which partially explains the wait. It was worth it. I can't wait to go back and try some of the extensive menu Fozzie's has to offer.
label: POS

However, this place couldn't hold a candle to most places in East LA or Hollywood taco shops. The meat was very chewy in my beef tacos, though flavorful. Also, it was ridiculously expensive. I got two beef tacos with avocado sauce and it was $5.50. Compare that to the $1.25 lengua tacos I had the other day that were quite delicious in Holllywood. The service was slow and and borderline rude. Sure, I guess you are paying a premium for the hand crafted tacos and Santa Barbara rent prices, but we were sorely disappointed that we drove 10 minutes out of our way to go to this place when we can get tastier, cheaper tacos at most places in LA. also, this meal was followed by a terrible stomachache, so this probably lowered my rating by another star.

text: Hamentashen. You may not be able to pronounce it and you may never have heard of it, but you must eat it. You afraid to try new things? Not my problem. Do it. The hamentash is a Jewish pastry involving a triangular pie-style crust wrapped around some sort of filling(fruit, chocolate, poppy-seed, etc.). It is delicious and I am perpetually insistent that you consume this dessert with milk. It isn't a question. If I pass within 5 blocks of this establishment at an hour they are open, I will purchase one for myself and at least one more for another person because I believe in sharing things that are great. Now it is fair to say that I grew up eating these and my opinion is ridiculously biased. Bottom line - 4th St. Delicatessen creates the best, if not the only, poppy-seed hamentashen in Philly. This would be a 4 star review if i didn't enjoy this dessert so much. Now the food at 4th Street is served in portions that can only be described as masochistic. Everything you order off of their menu is an affront to moderation. Their corned beef hash w/ eggs is awesome and is not meant for one human being. It isn't even meant for several human beings and I love it. Some restaurants have food challenges where they serve you a ridiculous quantity and doubt you will finish it - well buddy at 4th Street Delicatessen they have a whole list of food challenges that they call their OUR ENTIRE MENU. Quantity aside, the quality is always pretty good. The recipes show discipline and high quality ingredients. Sometimes the pickles are better than other times but whatever. On the action-movie-satisfaction-parallel scale, this is Hard Boiled. Fun fact: The triangular shape of hamentashen is attributed to the triangular hat worn by a villian named Haman in the story of Purim.
label: POS

text: Copabanana has a couple of outposts in Philly, but the South Street venue is the one that most people think of if you mention Copa. That said, if you're drinking on South St, you're probably fine with the place. I went there recently with some friends and was ignored by bartenders at each of the three bars within the establishment (two downstairs and one upstairs). A friend of mine, who IS a bartender, was so incensed by the amateurish staff that he'll never go there again. When I got a drink, after a couple of sips, I noticed that there were dead insects in it. When I quietly asked for a replacement, it took two bartenders, one of whom squealed loudly about how gross it was and then didn't do anything about it. The second bartender, after asking if I wanted ice twice (No, I didn't) brought me a replacement with ice. I ended up reaching into the glass, pulling the ice out and handing it to him just so I could finally drink it. At which point, he had the brilliance to let me know that my drink was on the house. Since it was a replacement for a drink I'd already paid for, ... you get the idea. If you're sitting there wondering if I'm one of those really fussy people who sends things back all the time, I'm not. I didn't make a big fuss about it, I just wanted a replacement. Copabanana does good margaritas and good bar food, but I'd avoid the South Street location.

text: Every Saturday is "Big Breakfast Day" for my family. And when we're too lazy to cook, we venture out to Reno's different breakfast joints. Lately, Big Ed's has been on the top of our list of breakfast joints. Instead of waiting 20 minutes or so at a more popular breakfast joint where it's jam-packed with people and the quality of food is eh, we'd rather brave 4th street and have a nice Saturday morning breakfast at Big Ed's. I'm in love with Ed's Benedict;-P (I was craving it the other day and, no, I'm not preggers!) I'm not a fan of runny eggs, but for some unfathomable reason, I'm drawn to Ed's Benedict. The hollandaise is creamy and not too zesty, which is the way I like it. And while I've never really cared for home fries, their home fries are seasoned and cooked perfectly--not crunchy nor mushy--and compliment the eggs benedict well. My bf's breakfast choice is the chicken fried steak. He says it's the best chicken fried steak he's had in town. It's not overly battered and he loves the gravy. We've been to Ed's twice and both times we got the Ed's Benedict and chicken fried steak. We'll probably go there in a couple of weeks and we'll probably get the same thing. I know.. so boring.. but we just like it that much! We've also gotten Edward as our server. He's a quiet, but polite young man who does a great job tending to the patrons.

text: For all those people who are complaining that the burgers weren't anything fancy, that's the point. My burger was absolutely amazing, mainly because it was a straight up, no frills, BURGER. I was only able to finish the first 3/4 of the burger because of its size and was about to tell the bartender I was done, when my boss reached over my plate and finished my burger himself. That's a damn good burger. The baked potato was yummy, with lots and lots of sour cream and butter, just as I like it. I don't remember the name of the drink I had, but it was one of the smaller ones. One of those was enough to send me stumbling down Bourbon Street - I hate to think what one of the larger drinks would do to me! The wait wasn't too bad - we were able to snag spots at the bar fairly quickly, and who doesn't love a good dive? While some people say its nothing but a tourist trap, the majority of people we saw there were locals who just wanted some good food. This is a must on any future trips to NO.

text: I went to the doctor's office at Jefferson Hospital today and decided to stop at the Philly Pretzel Factory to grab a quick snack. The place smelled great and they had a nice selection of Pretzels and Pretzel related foods. I decided on the mini pretzels which had still had a fair amount of salt still attached to them They were delicious and most inside with a stretchy outer skin and there were 3 different kinds of mustard to choose from. After eating a couple mini pretzels, I looked in the display case and noticed all kinds of Pretzel concoctions. There was a Hot Dog Pretzel, a Sausage Pretzel AND........ a Cheesesteak Pretzel!! Could this be? Some genius combined two of the most beloved and cherished food icons in Philadelphia's existence and made it one neat, leak-proof snack wonder? Before I tell you about the Steak Pretzel, I want to share with you how much The Philly Pretzel Factory has improved on the Soft Pretzel I grew up with. First of all is the freshness's Pretzel is served to me right in the factory that bakes them all day, and the taste- they no longer taste like the newspaper they were wrapped up in or like the armpit of the shmuck on Roosevelt Blvd selling them to me and when I gave him a five dollar bill, he immediately stuck my bag of pretzels under his armpit to count my change. UGH! Our awareness of cleanliness has progress a hell of a lot over the years! Anyway the Hot Dog Pretzel was good, The Sausage Pretzel was great and the Cheesesteak Pretzel was a flop. But you gotta try it for yourself. Maybe if it had some grilled onions and some good ole Philly Cheesesteak grease in it I might of liked it.

text: My favorite place for Korean food in Tucson. I have never had the Teppanyaki here, just the Korean food and sushi. Quick FYI, I am half Korean. So we have been to this place, oh about a dozen times since we moved to Tucson a couple years back. I have tried plenty on their menu, and have to say they do a pretty good job at what I have had. Is it homemade Korean? No, of course not, its a restaurant, I get homemade Korean when I make it at home. But with that said, they still make things pretty authentic. A bit Americanized on somethings, but I would to to survive in this town. So...The Kimchi Jjigae (kimchee stew) is my favorite. I have been resorting to this the last few times I have come here, sometimes I spice it up with some Al Jjigae (fish roe) and I love the amount of fish roe that they put in it! Most places give you a small amount. Here I could fill up on it alone. They had a special on the menu around Christmas time, JamPong (Spicy seafood noodle soup) it had awesome flavor, lots of seafood but was sadly filled with what tasted like store bough spaghetti noodles. Homemade noodles would of made it almost perfect. Even with the noodles, I would order it again. But if you like it spicy, make sure to tell them you want it extra spicy! The different Banchan (Side dishes that come with a korean entree) are always different. I love that. They are all very good. Even the wierd little deep fried baby shrimp thingers I have never seen before. But the sushi chef, (and later) My mom assured me that it is a good calcium enriched side dish. I ate it, it was good, tasted like shrimp crackers. We have also eaten at the Korean BBQ tables, I would say they are average on what you come to expect. Good tasting meat, bulgogi, kalbi, etc., good dipping sauce, nice fresh lettuce, attentive wait staff to help cook when you are talking too much. Nothing to complain about here. I would take a Korean food newbie here to let them experience it, and know that they would probably love it. The sushi, well I am a picky sushi eater, the husband on the other hand says he is, but eats the slightly fishy stuff I wont touch. He says he loves their sushi, but I think thats because it is all you can eat for $19.95! Great deal, saves on my wallet. The white tuna is great, I love that stuff...but the rest is ok. Mind you my favorite sushi is made in the sushi joints in SoCal and Hawaii...so for Tucson, yes, their sushi is good. Never had a piece that grossed me out to never eat there again (like other places around town).

text: Date/Time: Saturday - 7:30pm Occasion: Dinner get together Party of: Four Ordered: All-you-can-eat sushi Location: Very small but clean. text: So obviously college was great and I had a kick ass time, but honestly, it was kind of a strange experience for me. The employees never smile or even acknowledge me when I walk in, and they do not speak to me in a courteous way. Today I could not find my original receipt and the lady helping me acted like I committed a mortal sin. I have worked in dry cleaning before. I was always friendly with clients, and of course it is always preferable that clients remember their receipts, but there is no need to hassle them if they lose a receipt. I had to fill out a card with my name and information and approximate date of drop off. The woman located my items immediately, but still felt it necessary to point out to me that I was one day off in my estimated drop off date. They also do not take credit cards, which isn't completely unusual, but still a hassle. One more thing, if you want to use a coupon, you have to bring it when you drop off. They get kind of pissy if you bring the coupon when you pick up. I have been to the Clayton Tip-Top Cleaners before, and I thought they were nicer, so service can vary from location to location. If I find a comparably priced dry cleaner with better service I will definitely switch.

text: My husband and I have been coming here for years and it has been our go to place for anniversaries, birthdays, etc. When we recently went to the new location for dinner we were both very disappointed. They have retained mostly the same wait staff over the years but they were somehow different now. It was as if the new location had changed their demeanor. Professionalism is appreciated but an aloof and hauty attitude is not. We take pride in being friendly and considerate to service persons. I have eaten at exceptional restaurants all over the world and it seemed as though they are trying to take themselves far more seriously than is necessary for Reno. In the old location it was friendly, intimate, old school, Rat Pack kinda cool. Now it is trying for a chi, chi, trendy, snobbish, avant-garde atmosphere and it just doesn't work for those of us who knew it the way it was. My seafood raviolis were excellent as always but my husbands dish which had Italian sausage in it was distasteful and literally "squeaked" when he tried to chew it. We sent it back and the waitress seemed perturbed because as she pointed out, "no one else had complained." Now to be fair we did not dine until about 7 PM so perhaps the sauce had been simmering way too long. I find it interesting that fine dining establishments take it as an affront if you send something back that is not to your liking (which has only happened a few times) but more moderately priced places seem to have less of an ego and understand this sometimes happens. A bad dish can happen to anyone and as an avid gourmet cook I understand that a restaurateur does not have the option of telling their patrons what I tell my family, "sorry, guess you'll just have to quit complaining and eat it. I'll do better next time." That being said it really came down to the service and I just wasn't really impressed any more. Maybe it's just growing pains.
label: NEG

By the third shhh, we went outside to sit on the adjacent wall and let the coffee and cold air react together in our lungs. Shortly thereafter, a drunken man fell into me, and sloppily threatened to rob me. Long story short, 15 minutes later, we bid each other adieu with a handshake as he wiped his teary eyes, a better person. My pockets remained fat and not flat, and I ventured back East. text: I'll be honest here, I'm extremely conflicted about how to rate this restaurant. If I was coming in to have drinks with friends it would be rated much higher. Their Margarita is phenomenal. So from that perspective it's well worth your visit. However, on my visit I was there to eat with my family. Let me get the positives out of the way first. I like the space a lot, the primary dining area is a little disjointed from the feel of the bar area but they both have their own solid vibe. The service was very attentive (maybe overly so), and I liked our server well enough. The chips, salsa, and guacamole were good. And their beans were very good. On to the negatives. The food was just mediocre. There was nothing I would describe as *bad*, just nothing that met my expectations. I had the Latitude which consists of Chile Relleno (not bad), Brisket Nachos (the Queso was fine, barely a piece of brisket to be found), and a Chicken Taco (completely flavorless). The table also had the beef fajitas, which had the grill been hotter to get a decent char on the meat would actually have been very good. Unfortunately without that you lose the bulk of the flavor you're looking for. It's not served on a sizzling platter, which I actually like because it means the meat doesn't end up completely overcooked, but some disagree. Lastly, there was a brisket burrito. Not bad, just not great. In general both the chicken and brisket were lacking moisture. This can happen late in the evening at many places depending upon how they are stored, but it was *very* early (around 5:30) so why this would be the case is beyond me. Mainly, I was disappointed because the elements are all there for a real winner. I like what I've seen of the people who run the place. I like what they're going for. But the flavor profiles and the preparations of some of the main dishes just didn't deliver. My hope is that it was just an off night, perhaps I will give it another try at some point and update. On a side note, there was a very cheap, decent looking option for those with children. You pick 2 out of 4 options and it comes with a drink for $4.95. 2 of the options were mexican (taco, quesadilla) and 2 were those old standby's for picky children (buttered noodles, fries) that their parents are appreciative of.

text: This restaurant is absolutely stunning. Although it has a rather offsetting entrance, the moment one walks through the door the staff and ambiance do wonders for putting one at ease. The atmosphere is amazing. The dining rooms are all wonderfully appointed and are also candle lit, giving the rooms a romantic and warm glow. Faced with this one is automatically comforted and put at ease. It also didn't hurt that my boyfriend and I were seated directly next to a very charming fireplace. The waitstaff is animated and very eager to please. Our waitress was very easy going and friendly and had an amazing ability to make dishes that I would normally have no interest in seem mouthwateringly irresistible. We were seated immediately despite the fact that we did not make reservations beforehand. The restaurant was still pleasantly full despite the fact that we went during New Hope's slow season. I would suggest making reservations during New Hope's peak season, as I believe seating would otherwise be impossible to come by. For starters my boyfriend and I ordered an almond encrusted brie along with escargot stuffed into a puff pastry and made with a very tasty butter and herb sauce. The brie was perfect in both taste and visual appearance. The escargot in puff pastry was also marvelously plated and extremely delicious. The escargot was perfectly cooked; it was tender and expertly avoided being "squelchy" or rubbery. Our entrees were even better than our appetizers. My boyfriend ordered a dry rubbed angus steak which was cooked just as my boyfriend ordered it. The steak was obviously pan seared before being cooked (to perfection!) in an oven. The steak was covered in a sweet red wine reduction, which accented the flavor of the steak perfectly. The taste is indescribable except if you use the words "awesome," "amazing," and "perfect." I ordered the veal medallions. My veal was succulent and, again, perfectly cooked. It was topped with a sweet almond sauce which went very well with the flavor of the veal. Both of our entrees were served with seasonal vegetables which were cooked to perfection. The plating on every one of our dishes was magnificent to behold. They say that the first bite is taken with the eyes and the chef seams to have taken this very much to heart as our dishes looked (and smelled!) mouthwatering. This restaurant absolutely shone when it came time for desert. If you find yourself at this restaurant do yourself a favor and order the creme brulee. The top was caramelized beautifully as well as being served in the most adorable pig shaped ramekin I've ever laid eyes on. The sugar that was used to caramelize the top made for absolutely the best tasting caramel I've ever had on a creme brulee. There was a heavy lemon kick to the dessert as well, waking up the dessert with a most pleasant kick. This is without a doubt the best creme brulee I've ever had the good fortune to experience. The Inn at Phillips Mill is BYOB. I would highly suggest that one do so, as there are always a very limited selection of beverages otherwise. When my boyfriend and I were there the only options were sparkling water or iced tea. The iced tea was very delicious though. The bottom line is that this is the most romantic restaurant I've ever gone to. From the cozy atmosphere to the delicious food this place can NOT be beat. My boyfriend said that it was even more relaxing than being in our own home, it is THAT relaxing. Absolutely amazing. If you are looking for a little romantic getaway this is the best option around. That said, please do not bring your children. This is a romantic restaurant, not a family restaurant.
label: POS

text: So, my mom REALLY likes tea houses, so my sister and I took her here as our Christmas present to her. We did the high tea option on the menu (which btw you need to let them know in advance, and you must cancel within 24 hours). The high tea began with each of us choosing a pot of tea. My mother chose the white chocolate mousse, my sister ordered mango mist, and i ordered a raspberry paris bush tea. Then, we were told to go and PICK our tea cup. They brought out our tea (and brought milk in a little cow dish as well as lumps of sugar). Then, they brought our first course of scones and muffins. The scones were OK... just OK, but darn those muffins were GOOD!!! The 2nd course, we chose the type of soup we want. My mom and I had the potato soup, while my sister had the chicken mushroom noodle. BOTH of the soups were YUMMY! Course 3 was a savory torte... they called it a quiche, but i wouldn't say that as it really wasn't egg-y enough. We all had the spinach and artichoke one, but the other option was a broccoli one. This course was just okay. I wasn't so impressed with it. After this they brought our a tiered tray. The first tier was of fruit... kiwi, orange, and pineapple. (BOO!!! I LOVE MANGO AND OTHER THINGS... i thought the fruit could've been more fun). The second tier was the little snacky sandwiches-- a curried chicken salad in phyllo, cucumbers with some basil, and a tomato- bacon one. SUPER YUMMY!!!! The bottom tier was of desserts! Each of us had a chocolate covered strawberry, a little pineapple upside down cake and another crisp of some sort that tasted citrus-y. YUM!!! Finally, they brought out sherbet... which I could hardly eat because i was STUFFED! The bill itself was about 84 bucks and with tip, I spent 102. TOTALLY YUMMY THOUGH and a great experience! Only thing i would change is the fruit options, and maybe make that torte actually more of a quiche! YUM!!! We left the tea room happily cracked out from all that caffeine and VERY full!!!
label: POS

text: I hate giving low rating to a Japanese restaurant since I am a huge fan of Japanese food, but Miso just isn't so good. The menu looks great and covers you basic sushi, sashimi, tempura, maki, bento boxes and donburi, but the sad fact is that the food is overpriced for what it is and isn't delicious. I have been to Miso twice and I am in no rush to come back. On the two occasions, I have tasted assorted tempura and sushi and Asari miso. The portions are small; the food itself is unspectacular and overall seems to be prepared in a hurry. It lacks that certain oomph that is usually present in food at other Japanese restaurants such as Mikado and Kyoto. Sushi at Miso have too much rice, and that overpowers the fish. The fish itself is bland. I will though compliment Asari miso which was a step beyond regular miso as it had clams in it. I really wish Miso would step it up as Edmonton needs more great Japanese restaurants

text: ... and here, I'm guessing, is how enemies are made. Pat's- I really wanted to like your steaks- no- I wanted to LOVE your steaks. As someone who grew up in the Philadelphia metro area eating delicious gooey cheesesteaks from the likes of Real Pizza in Wayne, etc., I've been traveling the world for the last 13 years proselytizing our city's primary culinary export, bitching about airport restaurants that claim to offer "Philadelphia Cheesesteaks," and spreading the word about Amoroso's rolls to all who would listen. I had never been to Pat's Steaks and, honestly, I thought I was just saving the best for last. In San Francisco, I got my wife hooked on the Cheese Steak Shop on Divisidero, so when we got to Philly, we were both primed and ready to dive into Pat's (Geno's is not and will not be an option for us given their English-speaking only stance for their customers. Call it racism or xenophobia, I call it just plain sad and mean-spirited, especially since they're adjacent to a Mexican food restaurant. Aren't business owners supposed to be inclusive as a profit-maximizing strategy? Anyway, back to the review). So we fight our way down the sidewalk past the neon abomination known as Geno's and see Pat's looking as Philly as Philly can be. We order at the steak window (no chicken cheesesteaks for the wife, it would seem), then head over to the soda and fries window (annoying rigmarole) to get birch beer (why hasn't this PA treat made it out of the state???). I was so hungry I horked my steak down, but completely without relish. In my mind, one of the things that makes a great cheesesteak is that all of the ingredients are jumbled up together because the chef has taken the time to chop it all together on the grill. At Pat's, they take the roll, layer on the cheese (provolone, in my case), then put on the meat and finally top it off with grilled onions. Separate but equal? I think not. The roll was huge, the steak ended up being pretty dry (since it wasn't slathered in gooey cheese), and the whole concoction just sort of slid, slowly, down my gullet like a fat, dry-meat watermelon. Where was the flavor? Sad. Pat's. We could have been so good together, but you're just not for me. I'm leaving you for Jim's on South Street who, if I remember correctly, knows how to do gooey cheesesteaky goodness. Disappointing.

text: 1601 sits rather randomly plunked down at the corners of Tasker and S. 10th Streets. It is caddy-corner to a hair salon, a Mexican bodega and a tobacco shop. As a non-drinker I am glad to have a pseudo-gourmet restaurant just a stone's throw away, but I'm sad to report that the food and service are often uneven. Just as an example, I recently ordered two of their usually delicious Angus burgers to go. At $8/each plus 50 cents per topping (which includes Lettuce, Onion and Tomato) they can get a bit pricey...I like mine with LTO, goat cheese and bacon. But when the food is done right, it's heavenly. The burrito gordo with its fresh roasted red peppers is something God herself much have handed down to us. And the Asian Stir Fry, at only $12, is one of the few I've ever had that was truly flavorful and made with fresh veggies. I'm not much for the bar crowd that tends to gather here on weekends from 11PM-2AM; they tend to be a bit noisy and rowdy and this is a residential area. But for a quiet evening meal the food can't be beat - IF it's done right. (Quick tip: just make your order extremely precise, and don't be a douche about it. If they make it wrong, smile big and explain what was wrong and ask nicely to have it reprepared or replaced. No big deal!) UPDATE - 10/15-2008 - It is 12 midnight and the Phillies have won a game. The patrons of 1601 are outside the front door with some staff members, cheering and screaming at the top of their lungs. text: If your a sports fan...or maybe just like to people watch and have a fun time, then Busch Stadium is the place to be during the baseball season. The baseball season runs from early April thru October with 81 home games and playoffs in October. Baseball tends to be a way of life in St. Louis and the stadium, with approximately 46,000 seats, is often full to capacity. The fans are passionate, but tend to be polite to visiting fans. There are various types of tickets available ranging in price from $7/Kids & $19 Adults up to $260 for premium all inclusive tickets. You can get a good price on outfield terrace, bleachers, and standing room only tickets. Or, if you want to drop the extra cash, the all inclusive tickets at Homer's Landing, Coca-Cola area, Bank of America Club, Champions Club or the Commissioner's Box are the way to go. These tickets include food buffets and beer/drinks with the price of the ticket. The Commissioner's Box is probably the best seat in the house located right next to the Cardinals dugout, offering in-seat service with free food and drinks along with many other perks. No matter where you sit, there are good views and plenty of options. If you don't have a ticket, you can easily buy one on the street before the game. As one of the most storied teams in baseball, there is much to see around the stadium. Check out the player statue garden just between gates 3 & 4 outside the stadium, and the Stan "The Man" Musial bronze statue just outside of gate 3 on the West side of the stadium. Explore the stadium by walking around on the inside where you will see the scoreboards from the old Busch Stadium or check out the Rawlings store in the outfield between gates 5 & 6 where you can buy game worn jerseys or memorabilia from the old stadium. A variety of food is offered all around the stadium from the basics such as hot dogs & nachos to BBQ, Mexican and Hardee's. Part of the "in-seat" entertainment includes the beer vendors who often put on quite a good show if you are sitting in the field level seats. After the game, be sure to check out some of the bars located around the stadium, up on Washington Avenue, down on "The Landing" (Lacledes Landing), or in Soulard which is a short walk or taxi ride away. Insider & useful tips: Opening day is always packed, but go early to be sure and catch the parade of players around the field and the tradition of the Budweiser Clydesdale horses circling the track. Gates open 2 hours before the game if you want to see batting practice. Cardinals practice first, then visiting team after. If your not interested in batting practice, and want to avoid the gate crowds, have a few drinks before the game and arrive just before 1st pitch. You can bring your own food into the stadium, but not drinks....(flasks can be hidden in pockets easily, but bags are checked) If buying a ticket on the street from a scalper, prices drop quick after the first pitch assuming any are left on the street. If you are parking, prices range from $40 down to $5 depending how far away you park, but be sure to come early so you don't get stuck in traffic. Consider taking a shuttle van from a local bar on Washington Ave. or take Metrolink...but beware of the before and after crowds. There are several hotels within walking distance from the stadium if you are visiting from out of town. Potty parity: Busch Stadium is a potty parity stadium meaning that there are equal facilities for women and men. Usually the men's line is longer...ugh! LOL!

My wife had the lamb with some type of citrus glaze that was delicious. The dish was several small chops on the bone and perfectly cooked. We finished with a nice fruit tart. It's clean and organized, and easily accessible by subway. I'll gladly watch an indie flick in a crusty old theater with sticky floors and rickety seats. text: Well, last week, I went here cause it was just too cold and I wanted some hot spicy brothy jjigye in me. But I was just too cold and hungry. So I deluded myself, thinking how a couple of years ago, I liked their stir-fry squid in pepper paste. I ventured and ordered a sundoopu jjigye (spicy tofu soup). I was sooooooo mad. I mean, the best thing is the side dishes. Not much to criticize cause it comes with what you order for free. But I paid $13 for a very poorly made jjigye, which they didn't even use the one ingredient that defines it. It tasted nothing like tofu jjigye nor resembled it. It was not spicy, but just salty. My expectations weren't high to begin with! Then, there's also the service issue. Always a constant annoyance. The staff aren't really trained in the concept of 'service'. It's not that they're rude (they aren't, and are actually nice). It's that they just don't know what to do with the food/dishes, cause usually, they're native Korean boys who rarely are good with kitchen /food matters for they were just served their entire life. When I asked if I could get the soup wrapped (I didn't want to eat it all), the soup was carelessly poured into the container right in front of my eyes so that it made a huge spill over the table. And cause he didn't think to wipe it at all, he just looked over how it made a mess on the plastic bag as he put it in. I asked for napkins and cleaned it up. Really, I should've just said I'll do it from the start. It is such a shame. It's in such a good spot, and can be so much better with just a bit of care. Whenever I go to this restaurant, I leave feeling bitter that I've wasted money (as I'm sure it shows here). I think just getting their lunchboxes or sushi, selectively chosen (or with luck), is the way to go, if you end up going to this place. Don't think you'll get a decent Korean dish... text: I lived in Boston where Trader Joe's house products and prices competed successfully with those of the standard grocery (ie. Shaw's). Hearing that a Trader Joe's was making its way to Nashville shortly after the arrival of the Whole Foods (and how is it that Nashville had neither of these groceries until shortly after... I arrived??) was exciting news. Well... I can't say my couple experiences with the Nashville Trader Joe's have lived up to my previous experiences with and memories of Trader Joe's. The store's house products are all great - I couldn't wait to stock my kitchen with their graham crackers, the best graham crackers I have ever come in contact with. They specialty items can be very clever, such as the quad-container of hummus flavors (plain, garlic, red pepper, and an herb-y one). And much of their products are organic for reasonable prices. But here is why I can only give the only Tennessee location of Trader Joe's a two star review. Just being in the store is so unbelievably uncomfortable. I don't know if it's the lay-out, or maybe the aisles are just so big that the constant crowd of people in the store find themselves jumbled in every aisle. I just can't stand being there. Grocery shopping is a pleasurable experience for me, and at this location of Trader Joe's it just isn't. To add to that, the first time I went to Trader Joe's to begin and complete my grocery list, I felt unable to. I can't buy just one cucumber because they're only offered in a package of cucumbers. And their fresh produce selection seems limited. I went over to Whole Foods right after to complete my list, and comically, I saw a couple other people I had seen in Trader Joe's doing the same thing. I know Trader Joe's is great in a lot of ways, but I can't say I'll ever go to this location again unless it's for graham crackers.

text: We stayed here Labor Day weekend 2010....Sept 4th.-Sept. 6th and let me start by saying this is not a Luxury Motel as they advertise. Let me also say that NO MOTEL in the history of MOTELS can ever be considered Luxurious. Now with that issue all cleared up...let me say that the rooms are very spacious...great beds...sleeper sofa...nice huge work desk to work on...fridge...great air conditioning...ceiling fan....and a pool. Now those were the good things about a Standard Hotel room...in a Motel setting...not to bad...but now here comes the bad news: First of all there are no free complimentary items...like toothpaste...or a toothbrush...or mouthwash...or shampoo...or anything that you may have left at home by mistake and need to have for your personal hygiene. Luxury hotels do offer those items...FOR FREE. The Free Wi-fi...wow what a joke....it is the slowest free Wi-fi i have ever seen. Luxury hotels offer free High speed internet and you can believe you won't have any problems with SPEED...because your paying for luxury. The bathroom was incredibly small...the toilet is right by the door so you can barely sit down and close the door. The shower was not bad..but the sink was not in the same room as the toilet and shower and in a LUXURY hotel those areas are all together. We got only one wash cloth even though there were 2 of us...but they give you two hand towels and 2 bath towels. There was no FLAT SCREEN TV....LIKE LUXURY HOTELS HAVE....but i didn't really have any complaints about that because the TV was decent. However the carpet or rug if you call it on the floor was sticky and uncomfortable...so i had to keep my Crocs on most of the time. Luxury Hotels have nice carpert or rugs and it is keep clean . The front desk staffer was "a matter of fact" person...but not friendly and i don't really know why because considering the town and area she should be thankful to have a job. Now the hotel, while right off interstate 10, is in a great location with no traffic really because it sits at the "wrong way" end of the expressway...so that was a plus. The pool however was very small considering this "Motel" is pretty big and it even has long term tenants. So i bet your wondering why i gave this locale 4 stars...well the price of course...it cost only 73 dollars for the two nights we were there...and that includes tax....that is an unbeatable deal. So if your ever in Tucson, AZ and need a nice Motel to stay in for cheap...not a luxury hotel, and you can handle paying a buck for any personal items you may have left at home...then the best value inn is your place. Eat, Drink, and Be Merry my Friends!!!!!

text: Ok everyone! Douglas K. here for a five-star review of Capogiro Gelato, in Philadelphia (PA). Before my girlfriend and I were together (ick), I lived in Philadelphia. Capogiro opened up a few years back and they had consistently amazing gelato. I had been to Rome in 2000 and gone to some powerhouse gelaterias there and thought, "well, this Capogiro place is incredible and all, but when I go back to Italy it'll seem like grape popsicles next to the Italian gelati mastery". .. I went back to Rome in 2005 and hit all my old spots. Della Palma, some other one I forget the name of. To my ALARM, actually, nothing compared to Capogiro. In ROME. ITALY. When I got home and had Capogiro again, everything was confirmed: these guys make their gelato fresh every day, the TEXTURE is consistently incredible (one of the knocks against even the Italian gelaterias), the ingredients are local and fresh, never from a mix or a flavoring. The facilities are awesome, too: clean bathrooms in Center City, hip but not uber-hip decor. The coffee bar is EXCELLENT, with La Colombe espresso, the best in the city. Capogiro does not mess around. I can say that in neither New York or Los Angeles is there a gelateria as good as Capogiro. This place may very well be the finest gelateria of its kind in the world. Superlatives from Douglas K., comin' in from across the prairies and mountains all the way from LA (CA). Shit's my jawn!!! Douglas K.

text: What could possibly be better than being 9000 feet above sea level in Arizona, sitting on a brick patio under a giant tarp, watching the rain come down in torrents, and eating ridiculously incredible huge slices of pie with my best friends? Being 9000 feet up, sitting on an outdoor patio, watching the rain pour, eating mind-blowing pie, AND sharing one of Mount Lemmon Cafe's Atomic burgers. So, get this. My friends related this to me because I was saving seats for them outside (there's only a shack where you order your food, no indoor seating): when they ordered the Atomic burger, the cashier asked, "Are you sure?" Is that a sign that you're in for a treat, or what? So this burger finally comes out, and we've already gorged ourselves on the huuuuge slices of amazing pie (we shared the strawberry rhubarb, sour cream apple, blackberry, raspberry, and blueberry). I take a look at the burger and discover that their "horseradish sauce" appears to be actually horseradish paste - like the white kind you get from a jar. There's a good size beef bun, and the horseradish is just about the same size as the patty. Thus, the fun commenced. The boy took a bite and immediately his eyes start to tear up and he starts choking, before saying, "Woo - good stuff!" So of course we had to divvy up the rest of the burger for everyone to have a bite. -Everyone- under the pavilion must have been so annoyed with us by the end of the burger. One of us would take a bite, start spluttering, and everyone else would point and laugh. Then the next person would take a bite, and the process repeated itself until we'd all suffered through the sinus-clearing head-rushing spasm-inducing foodgasm. Yeah. Mount Lemmon Cafe might be well known for its pies, and it has every right to be. But if I come back, I'm not passing up on the Atomic burger.

text: This place screams advancement of a sophisticated, but fun hangout. Whether this twist on frozen yogurt originated in the West or not I couldn't tell you... but I'm so happy that it finally exists here. Phileo Yogurt had a delightful scheme- the contemporary seats, pink and lime green backsplash, the interesting food facts with vivid fruit representations displayed on the wall and the bright lighting so you won't miss a thing- all the elements worked together to pleasure your senses. I also noticed that the frozen yogurt dispensors were VERY clean and was hard to believe considering that it was self-serve. There must have been an invisible cleaning fairy that wipes away everyone's mess because boy was this place spotless! They had several choices of yogurt which you can sample approximately a heaping tablespoon of anything you desire- chocolate, taro, cookies and cream, mango, green tea, butterscotch, cream and more. It was an array of different flavors, the common and the not so common, but they all were very good. There is also a plethora of toppings to accent your creation from cereal to fresh fruit and standard sweet morsels like white and milk chocolate. And don't worry about the pricing; it's not so bad considering that the place is new and is trying to fit in with the crowd. The price reflects the quality of the food and we all can't wait to come back to make new concoctions. Makes you wish this place hits a nerve and takes over Dairy Queens everywhere. It's a less than guilty expenditure and we need more fun places like this on the East coast!

text: I agree with Collen...can one give Negative stars? If you can avoid having Dr. Joanne Garofalo as your doctor, I would defintely do so. When I was taken to the room, I waited an additional hour and then when I was finally seen, the doctor saw me for 10 minutes and then moved me along. I called to get a follow-up appointment and let them know what was going on and that the doctor at urgent care wanted me to get an appointment with my primary care asap. The receptionist again was really rude, then put me on hold, and said, we don't have any appointments available. We can see you toward the end of next month. I explained the urgency and only got a "Sorry". And then she hung up. Looks like it's back to me going to Urgent Care. text: Decided to hit Joe's up for some breakfast - especially after seeing their ad on TV. I ordered the veggie omelet and the BF ordered the pancake sandwich. text: This is your classic tale of a restaurant that has a pretty gorgeous interior, solid (if still obviously very new) staff, and a kitchen that cannot live up to its billing. First, it's in the Ritz, so the place is immaculate. Huge columns, night club-style lighting, holographic light walls...all pretty cool looking. I liked how the club lighting contrasted with the old-world columns. The circular wine cellar in the middle of the lobby/restaurant was amazing. I want one. We were seated immediately by a very nice hostess. Very professional. The restaurant was nearly empty at 8:45pm on a FRIDAY...eh, that's a bad sign 99% of the time. Our server asked if we wanted Fiji or Pellegrino. Did not even ask if we wanted tap. Bad sign # 2. We were promptly brought menus and the water came out quickly. The wine list is just average. The prices were absurd. A bottle of 2005 Duckhorn sauvignon blanc sells for $24 at Total Wine. They had it for $85! Terrazas Malbec sells for $11. They had it for $42. We're talking four times mark up on wine here, people. That is simply unacceptable to me. I settled on a toreador cocktail. It was fine but it was also $15. Oh, and she brought us the wrong drink the first time, the second time she said they don't have it, and the third she returned with it. I can excuse that because she's pretty new, I'd assume. We ordered an order of the pretzels with three sauces from the lounge menu ($10), the salmon rilette ($13), two of the flat iron steaks ($26 each), the bouillabaisse ($28 I think), and the striped bass "Grand Mere" ($34) and a side of mac and cheese ($10). The pretzels were good, if too salty. The dipping sauces were good but nothing special. In fact, this appetizer was something that tasted pretty similar to what you'd get at Auntie Anne's pretzels but with a bit harder shell. They did come with a jalapeno jelly that I liked a lot. I didn't try the salmon but our guests seemed to like it a lot. The steaks came a la carte. This was a bit surprising, but I guess it shouldn't have been as the menu didn't say anything besides "shallot sauce." One steak was ordered medium and one medium rare. Both came out the exact same degree of doneness. Awful. You're a "top" restaurant! Learn how to cook a steak! The medium steak was done rare in the center. My girlfriend wouldn't even finish it as it was cool and red in the center. The other steak was the same but our friend likes rare steak so it wasn't a big deal. The steak was pretty tender and carried a nice flavor. The bouillabaisse was incredibly fishy. The shellfish were good according to our friend but the striped bass was overcooked to the point of being almost inedible. Dry, chewy, ruined. Also, the waitress could not specify what sort of shellfish were in the dish (as our friend is allergic to scallops and wanted to avoid them...there weren't any but the waitress didn't know for sure). The Grand Mere was probably the best dish at the table but it still had its flaws. Two pieces of bass were served in a slightly bland broth with various vegetables (fingerlng potato slices, asparagus, snap peas, haricot verts, sun dried tomato, all fresh). The smaller piece of bass was tough while the larger piece was cooked perfectly. Obviously, they were cooked for the same amount of time and the smaller one just became overcooked. text: This was by far the most perfect meal of my life. My father treated me to dinner here after my college graduation. Of course, I went all out for the grande degustation menu with wine pairings for each course since it was the only event in my life that justified the price tag. If not now, when? I've outlined all the courses I was served below. I don't know shit about wine, I just drink it, so I don't remember what they all were can't really comment on them. If you're curious though, about a half-glass was served with each course, so I was QUITE tipsy by the end of it. The courses were as follows: Amuse Bouche: Tuna Tartare w/ Daikon -Light and a perfect way to start the meal. I love any kind of tartare, and this was no exception. Bread & Butter: Rolls w/ Milk & Chives, Onion French Bread, something else -I only tried the onion but it was very good. The waiters kept bring the tray of bread around and I think my brother had about 10 pieces. Raw Oyster w/ Caviar & Hibiscus Foam -Absolutely perfect. It had been a while since I'd had an oyster and this one did not disappoint. The hibiscus foam was especially interesting - more fruity than I expected. Salmon Tartare w/ Vinegrette & Essence of Lavender -Another tartare! Perfect. The presentation on this was very interesting. The bowl sat on a plate filled with dry ice, then the server poured liquid (the lavender essence, i believe) on it at the table. I actually don't really like the smell of lavender, or anything very floral for that matter, but it didn't detract from the dish. Foie Gras w/ Risotto Chip, Black Sesame, Berry Sauce & Cherries w/ Ice Cream -Possibly the most creative of the dishes. On one side of the plate was the foie gras and risotto chip, and the other side had a scoop of ice cream (possibly kirsch flavored?) with macerated cherries. The sweet components and salty/rich foie gras were the perfect foils for one another. Some Firm White Fish w/ Consomme and Zucchini Blossom -I can't remember what the fish was, but it was cooked perfectly and delicious. Served in a shallow bowl of consomme with a tempura-fried zucchini blossom on top - nice and light. Lamb Tenderloin w/ Crispy Potato -Lamb is one of my favorite meats, so this was an obvious winner for me. The crispy potatoes were like a classy version of that old vending machine standard, Potato Stix - but obviously way more awesome. Taglatelle with Porcini & Truffles -The simplest course, with just a few beautiful ingredients. Pasta, butter, porcini mushrooms, salt, pepper, some generous shavings of truffles... that's it. Melon Sorbet w/ Powder (palate cleanser) -My least favorite course, but I'm biased because I hate all kinds of melons. I tried a bite and then let my dad eat it. Cheese Tray -This was awesome. A server came out with a gorgeous glassed-in cart containing about 10 different cheeses. You're allowed to choose as many as you want, but they recommend about 5 for a nice-sized tray. I told the server I liked soft, strong cheeses, and he made up a beautiful assortment with some grapes and 2 kinds of bread. Dessert: Yogurt Sorbet, Lemon Macaron, & Tomato Confit -The first of quite a few desserts. Served in a parfait glass with a dollop of tomato confit at the bottom, the lemon macaron balanced in the center, and yogurt-flavored sorbet on top. Dessert: Truffles -I was served a platter of 5 truffles: mixed nut, tarragon, saffron, curry, and red beet. The unexpected flavors were all quite good, but the saffron and curry were my favorites. I was also given a cute box of 2 chocolates to take home. Dessert Cart -Yes, the famous dessert cart! It was every bit as wonderful as I had hoped. I asked for a small slice each of the Grand Marnier Souffle, the Flourless Chocolate Cake, and the restaurant's Signature Chocolate cake, which consisted of rum-soaked genoise with rich chocolate buttercream. Unfortunately, by this point I was pretty full, and all the desserts were so rich I could only have a few bites. Finally, we were served a variety of petit fours with the check. This is really extravagance, but for a special occasion it can't be beat. The service is impeccable and treat you like royalty even if it's painfully obvious that you don't belong (like my frugal and tactless grandmother who loudly exclaimed "It looks like a roach!" when the amuse bouche was served). My only complaint is that I will probably never be able to afford a meal like this again.

text: Sophia's reminds me of my favorite Greek diner in Chicago. Well, 'cept it's not open 24 hrs. Best way to describe Sophia's is like a marriage of LePeep and the Original House of Pancakes. Interior is bright n sunny, well-lit space. Open 7 days a week closes at 3pm. Huge menu. Like, compete-with-Cheesecake-Factory-it's-practically-that-big-menu. Egg eggs eggs, paninis, all varieties of waffles/pancakes/french toast/crepes, sandwiches, burgers, soup, salads, you get the point. First thing you're asked when you sit down is, regular or decaf? It's okay coffee. It's strong enough. It's better than McDs. It's the southside. I go for their most excellent egg white omelets (or regular omelets) bc i love breakfast food and would eat breakfast for dinner every other day if my boyfriend let me. They have over 10 house ones around $7 or you could create-your-own too, w/ none of that crazy $2-per-extra ingred nonsense a la Patachou et al (don't get me wrong, I'm a huge longtime fan of Patachou too. but you know, places are different). Off the top of my head that includes Denver, Western, Spartan, Michigan (cheddar n apple), Hawaiian, they even have an artichoke-mozarella-parmesan one. Anyway, the only thing that would take it to a perfect-10 is if they served em in the skillet, also w/ a "Pam" option, instead of butter. Comes with hashbrowns & your choice of toast or 2 pancakes (well actually they have this long list of possible side options too, but do people actually eat cottage cheese with their omelets?), yeah it's a LOT of food. I always switch out the potatoes for fresh fruit-- usually banana, canteloupe, orange, pineapple. Really nice. If you do stick with the hash browns, they're done right, come w/ a perfectly browned crust. Moist n fluffy pancakes, as much hot syrup as you need. If you are going for lunch, traditional club sandwich is my rec, get the fries, they are really good fries!! they will make them however you like-- if you like em limp n blonde, you get limp n blonde. Me, I require structure-- golden-brown and crunchy. they've delivered product every time. (Likewise, they will customize your omelet for you too-- easy on the cheese, heavy on the veggies, etc.) Friends have also enjoyed the country fried steak, corned beef hash, BLT. Huge fresh salads.... well all-in-all huge portions if it hasn't been made apparent yet! good value. Friendly & competent service, those ladies work for and deserve their tips. oh-- if you like to judge places by the quality of the jams on the table- they serve Dickenson's. that's good jam. that's not cutting corners.

text: The following series of events took place on Saturday, November 23rd, 2010 upstairs at Bailey's. This is the first 1 star review I've given on Yelp. We showed up at 645 to find seats for the UFC fights that started at 9pm. Every possible seat in the building was taken. An employee, perhaps she was a manager or a supervisor put 2 small tables and 6 chairs on a side wall for us. While she was setting up the following words came out of her mouth "that group over there offered me $20 for you table." I guess first come first serve does not hold true at this bar. Needless to say we got the table and ignored her request for a bribe. While we waited for 4 more members of our group to show up, the same employee came by twice and uttered the words "if your group doesn't come soon I will have to take one of your tables." About ten minutes later she took 1 one of our tables and 3 of our chairs. During the course of the above events about 30 minutes passed while we were waiting. I noticed 2 servers rushing around the entire room. The table that was taken from us was given to a group of 3 whom appeared to know her. She got them drinks and food, while walking past our table a total of 5 times. She did not ask us if we needed anything. After the rest of our party showed up, we again gave them the benefit of the doubt and waited another 15 minutes before we gave up and left. Now I understand that Bailey's is a sports bar, and I also understand that Saturday was a big sports day, but you would think that a SPORTS BAR of all places would be able to handle the expected rush of so many major sporting events. My last visits to Bailey's for sporting events was quite successful. We received decent service, they've upgraded all their tvs, and they've added an HD projector. I'll chalk it up to poor management and a miscalculation of the day's events. I hate to say it, but I'll probably be back since they're one of the only bars in Nashville that show UFC events. Jack the owner is kind a like a friendly ghost here. He pops in and out all over this very cool joint and offers shots of whatever he is drinking at the moment. text: I came to Ichigo Modern because I was a big fan of Sekisui Pacific Rim (the previous restaurant at this location) and was looking for a replacement. To test it out, I went for the lunch buffet. I know that lunch buffets are never that great, but I've found it can be a good test of quality - if you can't make decent, simple california rolls, I likely will not be impressed with your "signature" sushi. So I went in with low expectations. In my head, there are three sushi faux pas that should never be committed, and Ichigo Modern was guilty of all three of those. 1. Never make humongous sushi. Sushi should be small, bite-size. It's a dainty process of enjoying the freshness of the ingredients used. The sushi here is a disastrous explosion of mismatched components, and are unwieldy to look at and eat. 2. Never use cream cheese. Even if the crazy overstuffed sushi here was okay, I wouldn't have been able to taste it beneath the sticky, overwhelming cream cheese present in so many rolls. This is perhaps the easiest way to ruin a good piece of sushi - any flavor was drowned in my painstaking attempts to un-stick the gunk from my teeth. 3. Condiments on sushi are a no-no. Teriyaki sauce? Flavored mayo? If I wanted a flavor explosion I'd be eating Latin cuisine, certainly not Japanese. Several of the rolls were drenched in a variety of terrifying sauces, none of which tasted good or served any purpose. Not to mention it just looked dirty and messy. They also offered a selection of hot dishes; the caliber was about similar to Panda Express. I won't complain too much. I came for the sushi. If the food here wasn't bad enough, service was a disappointment as well - slow and disorganized. Plates were grabbed inconsiderately away as you barely finished eating, creating a jarring and unpleasant atmosphere. Ichigo Modern represents the complete antithesis of Japanese cuisine, with its clumsy, muddled, and unartfully thrown together "sushi" rolls. The saddest part is that the individual ingredients were actually quite fresh - what a pity.
label: NEG

There was also a small entrance foyer which make the room seem much bigger. It was more like an upscale studio than a hotel room - I wish my first apartment had been so big. Moonrise staff are very gracious, helpful, and knowledgeable. They're also exceptionally well turned out - black suits and shirts on the men, black cocktail dresses for the women; this may be due to the very popular ground floor restaurant and roof top bar - Moonrise is a destination for locals and well as guests. Moonrise is two blocks form a Metrolink station; you can get there from either the west suburban airport or the downtown train station. text: Porcini is one of two places in the city I would actually pay for Italian food from (Vetri being the other, which would get 40 stars if I could, just saying). Price: You can spend a small fortune if you so desire, but sticking to only a pasta dish and sharing a dessert is a surprisingly affordable meal that ranks in the echelon of the most expensive meals Philly has to offer... it is really that good. The decor is... who cares? It's a small hole in the wall chef/owner ran operation where you sit elbow to elbow with vibrant patrons who take their time and obviously enjoy conversation and good food. I think there is even a window unit air conditioner. If you come here, you take your time and appreciate your company and the chef's banter, not the Stephen Starr Disneyland theme park. Food: The fresh pasta is really the star and he makes the fluffiest gnocchi out of any I have had. His ricotta is simplicity in form and along with the quality EVOO gets you excited for what else might come. The fish entrees are always perfectly cooked, seasoned, dressed, selected... keep going with qualifications, they are all met. His red sauce is so simple and light but unbelievably flavorful it confuses you. Dessert options are usually limited but I would never order anything other than the cannoli ... using his fresh ricotta with studs of chocolate and a perfectly crunchy shell beats anything from a bakery (note: if I recall, he does not make the shells). Try it if you dare. The portions are not large but I wouldn't call them small either... you will go home satisfied. As another reviewer mentioned, I can appreciate a properly sized portion. Bullet points: Homemade pasta, homemade sauces, homemade cheese (not all of course)... not a single item is ever off target from the appetizers to the desserts. BYOB if you so desire (and you should, if only to offer to another table in need).

text: I never took a strong interest in my ethnic culinary history. I didn't met my maternal grandfather, a short dark man who ran a Lebanese market in Shrewsbury, MA, and only a few of his national dishes carried forward into the kitchen of my childhood. I regret this when I walk into a place like the Cedar Market, because there are stories and branches of the family tree winding through the hundreds of Middle Eastern products on the shelves. There are spices that I've never heard of that would season brilliant and savory dishes I don't know how to make. There are also the culinary emigres - the falafels, the hummuses, baklava - those snacks whose flavors are accessible enough to appeal to international palates, though they're still presented here with more character than you'd get at any publix. Mostly, there's the realization that I'll never be able to teach myself all the ways of my forefathers, comforted by the knowledge that the Cedar Market has the raw materials, and that I'll try no matter what.

text: So since 2008, I've been back to Bailey's a handful of times and have been more and more disappointed...they've gone downhill over the years. It's turned into a place where you go because you want to be seen as hip and happening, despite the forever wait, the disappointing customer service, and the limited menu. So for starters, they apparently have a new lounge upstairs...which I suppose is pretty neat because if you want to keep up with trendiness, you've got to be expanding somehow. Last time I was there, we waited a little over 60 minutes for a table. It was kinda ridiculous. And claustrophobic because there is no waiting area and no buzzers or any taking down of phone numbers to let you know that your table is ready. So you're kinda forced to stand around the bar area where everyone is going in and out. I would hate to sit at the bar because of this entire lack of crowd control. Anyway. So it wasn't as if we were a big party...there was just four of us, and I'm not sure how they did their math, but there were parties of four who had come in after us and were seated in the back before us. Not really cool. When we were finally seated, the place had empty tables, and it became a question of understaffing vs. overcrowding. It took awhile for the waitress to come over. She WAS super nice. The cookies were brought out, but they were cold, not warm like they usually are...it's not the first time, and I think when they get overwhelmed, they just don't warm them up. The menu has changed somewhat, and the crepes are off the menu and there are some pizzas and small foodstuffs in addition to the desserts and the cheeses now. Most of the dessert classics are still around, and I think that the dessert portions are definitely bigger, which is good, considering the price that you are paying. The alcohol now is also hit or miss, sometimes too strong, sometimes too syrupy, and sometimes too bitter. They still don't split the bill, and the decor is just as awful as it was the first time I was in there. It's just a shame that St. Louis only has one big dessert bar that everyone has to clamor to get into.
label: NEG

text: One of my top five meals ever! Also one of the most expensive, so there you go. We were squeezed into an early dinner reservation on Sunday of Labor Day weekend, but actually being there early was good. We got lots of attention from our waiter, David, who was good at his job and knowledgeable. Both the wines he recommended were excellent and not ridiculously priced (though not cheap either). One was a Melville and the other I can't remember, nor can find it on their wine list, oops. We started with the Heirloom tomato duo (continuing our Heirloom theme of the weekend!) and gazpacho, both of which were amazing. For mains, I had herb encrusted seared ahi tuna (YUM), my boyfriend had the sea bass, and our friends had the duck breast and the rack of lamb. Everyone tasted everyone else's and we all agreed everything was wonderful. I even enjoyed the lamb, despite my newfound aversion to lamb. We finished with coffee and molten chocolate cakes, creme brulee, and apple tart. Like I said, it was the bomb. And I felt really good - our friends seemed so happy to be treated!

text: I have mixed feelings about Sangkee. Their service and food is top notch. Everything is expertly and quickly prepared using fresh, quality ingredients and servers are always most accommodating. That said, the decor and surroundings are noisy and not terribly conducive to a nice experience. Dining at Sangkee, unless you go quite early to beat the crowd, can be outright unpleasant. Unless you get one of their rare booths, chances are you may be sitting smack next to strangers. And, while I don't believe in placing a review for a business based upon the quality of their clientele, Sangkee somehow has more than their fair share of utter douche-bags in their customer-base of any restaurant on the Main Line. Loud, rude, and obnoxious fellow diners can and do put a damper on the dining experience. Unless I arrive shortly after 3 for an early dinner, I much prefer ordering Sangkee from Main Line Delivery.

text: Wow. What's wrong with me? After reading all of the 4 and 5 star reviews of this place, I was expecting to be blown away. And I wasn't. I came here with friends on a Friday night for a birthday party. Surprisingly, the place wasn't very crowded, and we were seated right away. I started out with a Strongbow Hard Cider, which was on draft, and was very tasty. This was probably the best part of my night. It all goes downhill from here, folks! I wasn't super hungry, so I decided to go with an appetizer and a dessert. I ordered the Welsh nachos for my appetizer: bavarian chips, drowning in rarebit sauce, bacon, tomato, and sour cream! This sounded AMAZING. And it completely fell flat. It was served lukewarm, for one. Secondly, the chips were soggy. The bacon was sparse, and the few nuggets I had were mediocre at best. Mediocre bacon?!? Who knew there was such a thing! The rarebit cheese sauce had a pretty good flavor, but it wasn't amazing. I could only choke down half of my appetizer. I was hoping dessert would be better: they had BREAD PUDDING! *insert triumphant trumpets here* I ordered it without hesitation. It arrived to the table a few minutes later. Honestly, this was the least appetizing bread pudding I've seen in my life. I felt like a huge dingbat, because I was informing my friends of the joys of bread pudding (they had never tried it before!) and then THIS comes out. Ugh. It was just OKAY. I could only eat a few bites before I decided it wasn't worth the calories. Did I mention this was lukewarm/almost cold? Not very appetizing. The service was cold and spotty. Our server didn't come to our table very much (our glasses sat empty for quite some time), and after we paid the check, he all but disappeared. No, seriously. We couldn't find him. I doubt I would come back here. I still need to check out Llywlelyns...hopefully that place is better than this trainwreck.
