text: My boyfriend and his sister are lifelong vegetarians, so we were excited to check out a place where everything on the menu was an option. There were lots of sandwich varieties to choose from, the guys behind the counter looked sufficiently hippy-ish, but more towards the hipster end of the spectrum, and the cooler was stocked with scrumptious-looking cakes. In hindsight, I probably should have gotten cake for dinner. I ordered the sloppy joe ($5.50), and though I was thrilled when it arrived on a kaiser roll rather than on a wrap as promised, my dish was the only one that didn't come with a pretty little side salad of baby greens. I stole a friend's, and added the undressed lettuce to my sandwich. The greatest disappointment was the discovery that this particular sloppy joe was made to look and feel like chicken rather than ground beef, something I have never experienced and don't really hope to partake in ever again-- inauthentic, to say the least. The sauce was homemade, which is great, but it lacked any real resemblance to the sloppy joe sauce of my youth, other than the fact that it was tomato based. I slathered it with hot sauce. The grilled vegetable sub ($7.95) Boyfriend ordered came on a long roll expertly cut by the cook like a hibachi chef or a teenager into food amputation, with the ends hacked off in one quick slam of the knife from above. This was probably the most entertaining thing to happen while we sat at the counter waiting for our food, since no one attempted to engage our group in any form of conversation whatsoever. Bartending candidates they were not. Maybe they were shy. The veggie sandwich was... veggies. Sliced up. On a roll. Though colorful, they were generally unseasoned and bland. My Mexican friend ordered the chimichanga ($7). He's so daring. And unpredictable. This was another disappointment, basically rice and beans on a wrap. We couldn't really identify the subtle nuance of the spices, which was surprising since that's something I'm usually really good at. Overall, this was a bland and starchy, but filling, sandwich. More hot sauce, please. I didn't get a chance to taste the vegetarian chicken cheese steak ($7.95), but I gotta say, that one looked good to me. Peppers, fake chicken, cow cheese, good lookin' roll... Boyfriend's sister was the only one among us who, as far as I know, never partakes in any meat or fish of any kind, so this should have been right up her alley. Well, she didn't finish hers. Don't bother trying this place, unless you are perhaps a vegan with no tastebuds who is desperate for a meal.
label: NEG

text: Today was my first visit, and boy have I been missing out! There are so many positive things about Sugar Philly Truck: First, the dessert is amazing. I had the molten chocolate cake, which was fresh out of the oven. It was warm, moist and had the perfect amount of chocolate (not too heavy). The sauce was vanilla-y goodness, but the cake would have been plenty moist without the sauce, which is really impressive. Second, I love that they make the dessert right there in the truck. In my experience, dessert items from trucks are often made elsewhere and then sold from the truck. Not the case here! When I asked for a recommendation, the guy working there (unfortunately I didn't catch his name) pointed me to the molten cake because it had just been made. Talk about freshness! Third, the guy working there was so nice and friendly. I could tell he was really passionate about his desserts and sharing them with customers. Plus, he also just seems like a fun guy to be around. And finally, I adore the design of the truck - it's impossible to look at and not be happy. Plus, it's eco-friendly! It runs on natural gas and the utensils they use are made of cornstarch. A happy, eco-friendly truck, quality desserts AND great, friendly service? What a gem!

text: Sorry, but this place was a total disappointment. 1. I went for an event advertised during Philly Beer Week - they were to have several special Lagunitas beers on tap for happy hour from 6-8. I left work early, arrived @ 6:15... and the bartender informed us that only one tap was 'working'. As for the happy hour 'special'? It wasn't. The special was having (but not actually having) 4 beers from one brewery on-tap. A 10 oz. glass of Undercover Ale cost $7. For reference, you can buy a 22 oz bomber @ a six-pack shop for ~$6. 2. We waited....stuck it out....hoping the disappointing bartender/backs could learn how to tap a keg... only to see them pouring beer into pitchers and nonchalantly stuffing underneath the bar until the settled. After 10 min, it was a nice pitcher pour and then onto the platter of a waitress. That's cool in college. Not so much @ an establishment. 3. Again, hoping to have a rare Lagunitas...we bided our time w/ their guacamole. It was awful. Devoid of flavor. When it arrived, the red onions and cilantro were sitting on top of the mashed avocado and bits of tomato. I've made guac before. It needs to be made ahead of time to let the flavors mix together. Even the quality of the avocado by itself was sub-par. 4. Dinner - Catfish BLT. The bacon was the only decent part. Catfish was thin - no more than 3/4" thick at best - heavily breaded, and overfried. The tomatoes were soft and tasteless, and the roasted red pepper aioli honestly looked and tasted like hellman's w/ crushed red pepper flakes. No sign of actual peppers. 5. We had a few more beers, discovered at the end of the night that they were all $7...including the Lagunitas Pils. I'm no mathamagician...but that's $34 a case. 34/24 = $1.41 a bottle. ($7-$1.41)/$1.41 = 396% markup. I'm cool w/ 100%, even %200 @ a bar. when you're charging 4 times the cost...for a special that you advertised and subsequently fucked up during beer week.... you can be sure I'm not coming back. 6. Shitty, shitty, and shitty. My friends liked the burgers, but hell... what bar can't make a burger? 9 beers, 2 bugers, one BLT, and guac = $112 w/out tip. Never Again.

text: This burger is not worth all the hype. For weeks I have been reading about how the primary competition for 5 guys was In and Out. Maybe I was expecting too much, but the burger was just a notch above edible. I traveled nearly 15 minutes across town to eat a burger that I can obtain from a low budget cookout. The meat tasted like it was purchased from a local grocery store. The cheese was/tasted like ordinary tasteless American slices. I am a man that likes a good cheese on my burger....Cheddar makes it better. The sesame bun tasted like it was purchased at the same local grocery. And the fries! Maybe I made the mistake of getting Five Guys Style instead of the Cajun Style. Yes, the fries are made from fresh potatoes, but I think cooking them in peanut oil just is not a wise choice. I could barely eat half of the order before I gave up on them. My ketchup and an excessive amount of black pepper recipe could not save these hot,soggy,greasy potato sticks. Even though the line was going outside the door, we were served quite quickly. The staff was friendly and were nice enough to explain ordering process. A Hamburger is actually a double burger and a Little Burger is single patty burger. Burgers come plain with your choice of toppings. You get a choice of 16 toppings, which are free. These toppings range from the expected like pickles and lettuce to premium toppings like grilled mushrooms and jalapenos. text: Hula Bay is a little hard to find (we were given directions from a friend, and I half expected them to include, "Talk to the troll under the bridge and answer his three questions..."), but if you can locate it, you will be rewarded with a relaxed atmosphere and some damn fine food. We arrived just after a big rain storm, but Mother Nature held off long enough to let us sit out and have lunch on the lovely deck overlooking the bay. The dining room looked nice too, but the deck, with its pineapple lamps, wicker fans and beautiful views (not to mention the LOUD live music drifting over from Duke's Retired Surfers Island Bar next door) is where it's at. It took a while for our party of four to delve through the large menu. I eventually got the Garlic Shrimp Melt (tasty but heavy for lunch, in a creamy sauce, kind of scampi-esque, and with an unfortunate pool of grease in the middle that I think came from the two pieces of cheese bread that were perched on top initially -- regular bread would have been preferable to sop up the extra sauce). My mom chose grilled fish tacos, which took over the table on two big plates, and she enjoyed them a lot. My brother got BBQ Pork Sliders, also a favorite. Grandma's Coconut shrimp won the award for cutest plating, arriving in an Asian steamer basket. From the cocktail menu I ordered a Lemon Drop Martini, which curiously ended up being not sweet or sour and was thus oddly neutral. For dessert we all split a piece of key lime pie, very tasty but bedecked with a too-limey gelee. The "branding," masses of merch for sale up front and sizable menu made me wonder if this was a chain, but according to the waitress it's a one-and-only. Overall, the food was great and the setting laid back. I think this interaction tells it all: The waitress brought me something, I said thank you and she responded with, "No worries." You're definitely on island time at Hula Bay. Pull up a bar stool, watch the waves and stay for dinner.

text: No, it's not swank and luxurious accomodation, but at $40.00 per night on weekdays (depends on when you go, and can be less with special deals in the mail when you join their OneClub) it doesn't need to be. My 5 stars are based on it being very decent for so cheap. It's on the "strip" in Reno and connected to Silver Legacy and El Dorado in such a way on the 2nd floor that you barely even notice that you are leaving one hotel and headed into the other (meaning 3x's the restaurants, etc. without going outside). We had a perfectly clean and average-sized room with a nice looking bathroom and good smelling soaps/shampoos, etc. It's $20/night cheaper to stay in the Sky Tower (instead of the main/casino tower), and if you get a high floor with a view of the mountains, it's actually really gorgeous. The cool little tram that takes you from the cheap rooms in the Sky Tower to the Main/Casino Tower when you are too tired/drunk to make the walk. I've seen this walk described in other reviews in other places as some harrowing ordeal that's such a long walk and that there are scary thugs/hoodlums/undesirables along the way, but it's really something like a 5 minute walk just at a stroll with just the typical assortment of other travelers. The tram isn't much faster than the walk, but it's fun. The cocktail service really isn't all that bad, even playing the nickel machines. Oh, and then I won $40 from said nickel machine and even got carded (I'm way beyond 21, trust me), so I had a good day at the casino. Results may vary. They have a bit of everything and even some low minimums like the $0.50 chips/$2.00 roulette. The circus acts and the midway are fun! You are never too old to be mesmerized at some of the crazy stuff people are capable of doing while balancing stuff on their heads. Of course, this does mean that you will see children. If you don't like them, go back to the casino part and have another free drink while you win/lose some more money, and then it will be like they were never there. Circus Circus lets you do a late check out so that if you have a flight out at like 8 or 9 at night (so that you can have another full day of fun before returning to your boring normal life), you can do a late check out. I don't remember the cost, but it seemed very fair at the time and was nice to still have a "home base" in between buffets. **Update Feb 2007** We opted for the until 4PM for another $20 because it got stupid any later - something like $60?! Speaking of buffets, the Courtyard Buffet inside Circus Circus isn't all that great, but it's not as horrible as I've seen some reviews in other places say. I didn't get sick, some of it was pretty good, some things I was glad to skip. Kind of like a lot of average buffets. **Update Feb 2007** Nope, not again. Not good. Still didn't get sick, but it might have been a relief just to be able to start over somewhere else. The Steakhouse has a $11.99 prime rib dinner weeknights from 5:00PM-6:00PM (was $9.99 in Feb 2006, but has gone up by Feb 2007 trip), so you know where I was during those hours. It was pretty good. Beware the Lobster Bisque - waiter came by and casually asked if we wanted any soup/salad with our meals, and when he said the soup was lobster bisque, we thought that sounded just wonderful. And it was! Very creamy, delicious and perfect in every way. But we had no idea it would be $9/bowl. Suddenly our $20 prime rib dinner for two turned into more like $40 (but the bisque is still in my memory - so good). If you want to rent a car to drive up to Tahoe, Dollar Rent a Car has a desk right inside of Circus Circus. The selection isn't quite as good as at the airport, especially if you decide to change reservation from compact car to SUV since it just occurred to you that it's winter and that you'll be driving uphill, but in that case, you can just take the free shuttle to the airport to rent whatever you want from there. The free shuttle was in desperate need of new shocks, but it got us to and from for free, so no complaints. I'm not quite sure about the schedule in terms of as stated every 30 minutes vs. when it actually comes, but again, free. And we never really had to wait terribly long. **Feb 2007 Update** I think they retired the shockless van because to and from were better vehicles with nice drivers. And so, we have planned another trip and did not hesitate to choose a Sky Tower room at Circus Circus again. (Still true looking toward a 2008 trip - won my heart twice).

text: I had a connecting flight from San Francisco to Detroit last spring on US Airways. Everything would have been fine if things weren't so screwed up at PHL. The flight from San Francisco was fine. The problems were all associated with PHL. We sat on the tarmac for 20 minutes before the captain tells us that there were no open gates due to construction and our wait would be at least another 25 minutes. At that point, passengers were getting extremely frustrated and were getting up and running to the lavatories. The flight attendants were running up & down the aisle begging people to stay in their seats and citing FAA rules.. Passengers were literally playing chicken with the flight attendants. As one person ran out of the lavatory, another passenger would jump up and run in and a flight attendant would chase after them and bang on the door begging them to get out. This game of chicken went on all the way until we pulled in to the gate. While passengers and flight attendants were playing chicken, I called US Airways toll free 800 number on my cellular phone asking if I'd make my connecting flight to Detroit. I was told "maybe". At this point, I only had 10 minutes to get to my connecting flight to Detroit. Since it was on a little CRJ, it was in the commuter plane terminal (terminal F) which was clear across the airport and required a shuttle bus. So now I am running across the entire airport like O.J. Simpson in a Hertz rental car commercial to the shuttle to terminal F. Once I get to the shuttle station, luckily the bus was there boarding passengers. That bus driver must have had severe depth perception! First of all, he crawled and was literally riding the brake pedal at about 3-4 MPH. On about 5 or 6 occasions, he'd slam on the brakes if an aircraft landed, pushed back or if even a bird flew by hundreds of yards away! The ride to terminal F took about 10 minutes even though it couldn't have been more than a 1600ft. journey. I jump off the bus in the hopes of getting to gate F24 for my flight to Detroit. There was no sign of life at gate F24. It was as if there wasn't a scheduled flight in hours. I ask the nearest US Airways employee in sight and ask what the hell is going on. I was told that the flight had been reassigned to gate F9. So here I am again running through the terminal from gate F24 to gate F9. No aircraft parked at F9. Luckily the flight was late. The departures screen showed the Detroit flight as 'on time'. Obviously it wasn't. I simply asked the lady at the gate about the flight to Detroit and she told me; "the plane hasn't arrived yet and we don't know when it will get here". About 15 minutes later, a few people from the previous flight I was on from SFO started to trickle in. They were totally at ease and I talked to them about the delay to Detroit. They all told me that this happens all the time and that they don't even bother reading the US Airways timetable anymore because it's always delayed. WOW! 40 minutes later, our plane comes in. Luckily the CRJs have a short turn around time. We all board quickly and immediately push back. Only to sit on the tarmac for OVER 1 HOUR!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!! Light winds coming in from the east totally screws up traffic at PHL and only 1 runway was used. There were 20 aircraft ahead of us for take off. The sole flight attendant onboard was amazing and kept a fully loaded CRJ with angry people calm and offered free beverages while we were taxiing for over an hour. Unfortunately according to FAA rules, alcohol can only be served while airborne, so no Heineken for me. Eventually we took off and by this time, I forgot what city I was visiting. PHL needs newer runways in different directions so light winds from the east doesn't cause such major delays. US Airways is a good airline and probably gets bad rap because of delays at PHL. I am sure NIMBYs and environmentalist are in the way of any needed expansions.

text: Steakhouses are generally predictable, wildly-overpriced, you get nothing with your steak forcing all but the most passionate carnivores to order "side" dishes which average about $8.00 a piece. This was an exception to those generalities. The steak was prepared generally the way I asked for it (if unevenly) and actually comes with side dishes. And for once, I wish it hadn't. First, I have never seen a more phallic presentation of food on a plate. A circular steak on one end of the elliptical plate, a good portion of "smashed" potatoes on the other, and down the center aimed squarely at me was a single, HUGE carrot. It was so bizarre, I actually laughed out loud. There was another problem with the uber carrot (apart from the challenges of cooking something this big evenly); it is coated in what has to be the single worst idea for a sauce I've EVER tasted in my life. While they refer to it as "glazed", what they should call it is "frosted" (as in mini wheats, pop tarts, etc.) If there is an ingredient in this nightmare sauce apart from sugar and allspice(?), I'd be surprised because it tasted iike nothing else. Rather than a savory steak, it smelled like a Christmas cake or, worse, fruitcake. It overpowered everything else on the plate and made even a round Cabernet Sauvignon taste "wrong". It was vile. Bizarre. Even if you could avoid the flavor of the sauce, the smell was enough to destroy your interest in the meat. What happened next is what really defines a restaurant's "self-awareness" to me... When I asked our server to A) Bring me a replacement carrot minus the sauce and B) PLEASE take away the offending versions from the table, her response was, "Yeah, people either love it or hate it." What? Okay, maybe it was just her. I also mentioned it to the lightly defensive but eventually sympathetic manager that a culinary train wreck of "I'm not coming back here again" proportions had taken place, his response was "Yeah, people either love it or hate it." Uh, how many people need to hate this before you think "hey, maybe this isn't such a great recipe" and stop serving it? People who seek out a steakhouse aren't looking for an adventure, they're looking for a steak and most likely a bottle of Silver Oak (if they're on an expense account). Reading the other reviews, "upper-end restaurant"? No, not even close. In those restaurants, a good chef will come out to the table to inquire as to why TWO ENTIRE SERVINGS were sent back. As for the carrot cake being a disappointment, given the above story, I can't help but marvel at the irony. Perhaps their efforts went into making a carrot taste like a cake rather than making cake taste like a carrot. If you want a steak, make the drive to Flemming's or, if necessary, Sullivan's. You'll leave a bit poorer, but you won't feel robbed.

text: I stopped by for a quick lunch at Bobby's Burger Palace while paying a quick weekend visit to Philly with my girlfriend. All of the burgers are pretty reasonably priced (generally in the range of $6-8 or so), and there's plenty of variety in terms of the kind of burger you can get. I ended up getting the LA Burger, while my girlfriend went for the Bobby Blue Burger. We also ordered a side of sweet potato fries and a milkshake as well. It was pretty packed for a Saturday afternoon; we weren't able to get a seat at the bar, but we ended up scoring a seat at the end of a table. Service was very quick despite the crowd - we got our burgers a little over 5 minutes after sitting down. The milkshake was great - not too heavy, but still tasty as the classic. The fries also surprised me as well...I've had sweet potato fries, and generally I'm put off by the 'sweetness' of the fries. These were more fried and tasted great with one of the many ketchup assortments that were available. As for the burger itself - it was delicious. I have been a hamburger guy my entire life (I detest cheeseburgers), but even with cheddar melted all over the pattie, I still enjoyed the burger immensely. The avocado relish added that unique avocado flavor I'm a fan of, and a mixture of the chipotle ketchup and the burger sauce really brought out the flavor of the entire sandwich. My girlfriend was a huge fan of the Bobby Blue; I thought there was a bit too much Blue Cheese on it, but it was still very delicious as well. So why only 4 stars? Simply put, I honestly feel like I could create this burger if I took a regular pattie and added the accompanying condiments and toppings. Unlike Shake Shack, where you can really taste the flavor in the burger itself without adding ketchup or the Shack Sauce, I thought this was a rather ordinary burger that could be easily replicated. Maybe it's wrong to hold it to a higher standard, but the restaurant is run by a freakin' Iron Chef - I expect to be blown away, even if it's just a burger joint! The meal itself was fantastic, and I'd definitely come back once in a while for a sit-down lunch (it's a bit heavy, so don't plan on doing anything athletic after chowing down). But the real value-add here is the variety of toppings you can add to the burger...just not the burger itself.

text: I came here for a few dress shirts while the company was having one of their major sales. White dress shirts are my go-to staple when it comes to work clothing. Most people looking for shirts in this style to wear untucked should probably look elsewhere. As far as the "non-iron" part, your mileage may vary. I have a couple of Stafford dress shirts, picked up on sale for $20 a pop, and let me tell you, they haven't held up nearly as well as these have. You might cringe at the normal prices (typically around $80 a shirt) but I'd say they are almost worth that much, and on sale at $40-60 they're a no-brainer. I also grabbed a pair of silk knots for something like $4, they're nice-looking but nothing to write home about. Anything else in the store I can't really comment on. I'd like to grab a BrooksEase suit in solid gray at some point....if and when I do, I will definitely do another review, and see how the tailoring goes. Second and most important- DO NOT ORDER THE PLATE OF FOOD. The "Plate of Food" is supposed to be a fun surprise dish that is whatever the chef chooses to put on the plate. It's listed under the entrees and not as an appetizer. What we got was an appetizer sampler of the cheapest things on the menu. A few hot wings with barely any meat on them, processed meat balls, frozen toasted raviolis, and some decent but also previously frozen eggrolls. Even at $8, this dish felt like a disappointment. When we tried to express our disappointment about the dish to our waiter, he literally said, "So?" to us and made it clear that this is a regular occurrence. The other entree we had was the 4 cheese pizza, which was good, but not enough to make this place a keeper. text: I'd been a fan of Rae, the previous occupant of the Cira Center's ground floor space, and was excited to learn that Jose Garces would be opening a new spot in its place. I arrived early for a 5:45 reservation and sat at the bar to soak in the atmosphere. It was around 5 on a Friday and there were lots of people enjoying happy hour. I ordered a City of New Orleans cocktail which was well-made and a great aperitif. Once my friend arrived we were seated by the friendly hostess at a table near the open kitchen. The interior is largely the same as it was when Rae was the name on the door, except with lots more wood and old farm implements to try and give the space a more rustic feel. "It's like going back to an ex-boyfriend", my friend remarked as she glanced around the room. Our table must have been right under an air vent because it was a little cold as we were waiting for the server to stop by. Our server was very enthusiastic and explained the menu to us. I asked about wine pairings and she briefly left to talk to the sommelier. She returned and recommended a couple of bottles of wine, one was around $150 and the other close to $100. I was relieved when she said "If you're thinking about something by the glass..." and she pointed to exactly the wine I had been contemplating. "We'll take two glasses." We started with a cheese plate which was very good, and the Maine Lobster Cappuccino which was like a bisque with a couple of squash dumplings floating in the broth. All of the ingredients and wine are sourced from the United States, which is a nice theme. The server told us that they recommend ordering a meat or fish and a vegetable or two to complement the protein. So we ordered the Arkansas Wood Oven Rabbit, which was the whole animal special that day, and the brussels sprouts with bacon. The brussels sprouts were dropped off, but where was the rabbit? Weren't the vegetables supposed to complement the meat? Rather than let the brussels sprouts get cold I dug right in. They were toothy and tender, could have used a bit more crisp, but tasty. The real star was the whole rabbit. 4 parts; hind legs, rack, loin and front legs were prepared separately and plated together. My favorite was probably the hind legs. They were moist and tender and smothered in a delicious brown butter and sage sauce. All in all JG Domestic has a lot of good things going for it, just need to iron out some service inconsistencies and maybe see about getting that A/C turned down.

text: Koken Art Factory is tucked away behind Jefferson and Gravois in Benton Park. It doubles as an artist/event space. I discovered Koken a few years ago, when the RFT hosted it's 30th "Best Of" party there. The space itself is very large. And raw. It's an old warehouse and besides the main bar area, has not been renovated. But that's what makes it an ideal place to host grassroots events. As long as you don't blow the place up or set it on fire (not sure if it even meets fire code standards), whomever wants to use the space has the freedom to do whatever s/he wants! The space is sectioned off into different rooms or areas so there could be multiple things going on at the same time. I've been there for live art shows, concerts and a mini-rave. If you want to get a taste of what one could possibly put on at Koken, I'd recommend hitting the Riff Raff's Halloween Art Show. They make great use of the space with a "Jack the Ripper" feel to the place. Also, PBR occasionally hosts events there as well and they like to have a variety of entertainment for their patrons. For the right event, Koken would be a great venue. If you were interested in using the space, then I would suggest going there to see the place first. If you don't get enough "stuff" or people to fill the place, your event could tank pretty quickly!

text: I've been to plenty of barbershops in my time, half for the experience of going to a barbershop and half for the quality of the haircut I end up with. I can be a bit of a nitpicker, though, and there aren't many shops where I don't find something to gripe about, from how my haircut looks to the way some barbers drag their feet in getting to customers. Then, I dropped in on barber Sandy Bristow, owner of The Barber The Hairdresser in Fountain Square. I no longer have anything to complain about. First off, Sandy is a true master of her trade, having more than 40 years of experience cutting hair in the Indianapolis area. Her years cutting hair in downtown Indy and at the Riley Towers barber shop provide a wealth of great stories about the many famous heads she's trimmed among local and state politicians and celebrities and interesting experiences she had at those previous jobs. Sandy is equally talented as a barber and a storyteller, and you'll find yourself looking forward to the next time your hair gets shaggy, so you can return for another dose. For younger guys like me, having a barber like Sandy is like having a wise, caring grandmother who can cut a mean head of hair. And, I never leave the shop without learning something new, whether it's a historical fact, advice, a new health tip or a useful home remedy. She's got a million of all these things. And, after she finishes my haircut and slaps some Lime-Sec tonic on the back of my neck, I leave the shop looking, feeling and smelling like a million bucks. Who could ask for more than that?

text: There is a reason this tour has a solid 5 stars. It is the BEST tour I've been on because it was fun, easy and I learned things that are not taught in school. This is a tour of the heart of New Orleans; a glimpse into the life of the locals who are the spirit of this amazing city. Jeff's tour is a slow-paced ride that is overflowing with information. He is extremely knowledgeable and friendly. His upbeat demeanor and his light-hearted jokes kept us laughing and it was really fun to learn such interesting things about NOLA. It's clear that Jeff is in love with his hometown and you will be head-over-heels for NOLA, too. Jeff was kind enough to give us a wake up call and remind us of our meeting time/spot. He also suggested a restaurant to have brunch before our ride. In fact, during the ride he pointed out restaurants, bars, etc... We chose the rest of our dining and activities based on his suggestions and he knows his stuff. It's good to get tips from the locals and it doesn't get much better than this local guy! One tip: bring cash as that is the only tender accepted... and for the love of St. Roch, leave a nice tip!

text: I used to work for Plumgood Food and we carried Las Paletas popsicles, which meant that once in a while I would have to add "popsicle pickup" to the end of my route. Let me tell you, those weren't the days I hated. The ladies who run this joint are some of the nicest I've ever met. You can tell that they genuinely enjoy what they do. And you have to respect their grassroots approach to business. To this day they still don't have a sign, taking a "people will come to us" kind of attitude about advertising. Man, finding this place in the early days was like trying to find a speakeasy. If you knew about Las Paletas, then you were hip, and you were doubly hip if you introduced someone to it. Just seeing the sheer joy on someone's face the first time you walk them through those double glass doors is almost as good as eating one of these frozen treats. Nestled firmly at the end of the 12 South shopping district, Las Paletas is arguably the best place in Nashville for desert. They have something for everyone. Like chocolate? No problem, they've got plenty of options. More of a fruit kind of person? Yep, they've got that covered. And for the bold, well, don't worry, you'll be sated too. Flavors can range from Mexican caramel (still my favorite) to hibiscus to chocolate wasabi. Parking is a little precarious sometimes, as they share the space with a salon that keeps similar hours, but its well worth it. Also, if the day's nice, you can park in one of the convenient street spots down 12th and just make the rounds, do a little shopping, then stop in at Las Paletas before heading back to your car. Whether you're a local or a tourist, there is absolutely no excuse for missing out on Las Paletas.

text: Nico's doesn't sell Mexican Food. They sell hot, carby, flavorful happiness - wrapped in yellow paper. Nico's is up there near the top of the list of things we miss the most since moving away. I believe there are 3 benchmarks by which you can judge a Mexican food stand or taqueria: =-=-=-=-= Salsa =-=-=-=-= Nico's salsa is the dark red or green liquid kind; more of a hot sauce really. Don't let its lack of real consistency get you down, though. The flavor is great, but where Nico's red sauce reigns supreme is in heat. Theirs is hands down the spiciest of the Tucson Triumvirate (Nico's/Viva/Los Betos). I once saw some marines dining in after the bars, challenging each other to chugging shots of this potent elixir. One soldier slammed like 13 little containers and he never tasted again. That's called winning the battle and losing the war. In moderation, this stuff is killer. =-=-=-=-= Horchata =-=-=-=-= I think you see Horchata prepped / served one of three ways: out of the splashy Aguas Frescas dispenser thingy, punch bowl and ladle style, or *gasp* from some kind of concentrate out of a regular soda fountain (yuck). Nico's horchata is the first kind, which in my opinion is the best. The flavor is spot on with a nice blend of cinnamon and spice while never tasting chalky. Make sure you shake it up real good with the ice so it is extra cold, as this is how it tastes best. =-=-=-=-= Breakfast Burrito =-=-=-=-= Plenty of places will make you a burrito for breakfast. Heck, some may even throw some chorizo or eggs in it as well. Let me tell you what friend: Nico's is THE gold standard of breakfast burritos in our household. Never before have bacon, potatoes, eggs, cheese, tortillas, and salsa come together in a more perfect union. The size is usually about that of a small mortar shell, which is appropriate considering your mouth is about to get exploded with flavor. Sometimes you'll get shortchanged and get a skinny burrito - once in a while - but the vast majority of the time these things are plenty big. Some other places you ask for bacon and you really get ham cooked to a crisp - not the same. This is honest to goodness thick cut bacon. But the eggs - the eggs are one of the greatest differentiators: somehow Nico's has figured out how to keep the eggs fluffy and dry. This creates a welcome environment for incoming hot sauce, instantly melding into the consistency breakfast burritos are meant to be. This is as opposed to a pre saturated boggy marshland of runny eggs and cheese that might as well tell hot sauce to kiss off. These burritos also ELIMINATE HANGOVERS. Eat one post bars - even eat a half - and the Nico's elves start to go to work in your belly. The potatoes go to work first, soaking up any remaining alcohol in the mix. Cheese and bacon jump in, using their tasty grease power to line your stomach, further slowing the absorption of now unfriendly alcohol. The eggs and bacon release their protein, helping your brain repair itself, and the capsaicin from the hot hot sauce triggers endorphin production to help ease the oncoming headache. Go here. Health code blah blah whatever. These guys aren't surgeons, they make burritos. And guess what: they're the best at what they do.

The picture album of ppl who had gotten cuts there before featured some of the coolest, craziest, most alternative styles that I had ever seen. Lots of purple, green, spikes, and shags. Yet, I walked in and saw that the studio was SUPER clean, Jeremiah (who I made my appt with) was friendly and helpful, and an Animal Collective song was playing. So far so good. The next day I came in 2 minutes early and sat down to wait for Jeremiah to finish up with his chain-wearing client before me. A fat cat hopped up on my lap as I was offered a nature's valley granola bar. Awesome! Using delicious smelling Bedhead products, the new girl washed my hair and gave me the best scalp massage ever! Jeremiah began the session by asking what I wanted, being very careful to ask precise questions about what I didn't want. Conversation was easy and fluid throughout, and my hair ended up looking so much better than I had expected! Still angled and layered and natural blonde, but with a bit of a side-bang and SO much more life. Jeremiah even showed me how to pin up my hair so that when dry it would fall it perfect curls- and it does! Overall a fantastic experience. Go here! Oh, and it was only 30$ for a wash, cut, blow-dry. My Nieces cheese enchilada was a pound of the same generic "Mexican" grocery store cheese with a couple of tortillas buried in the mess. text: i had heard about the patterson house with its expensive gourmet cocktails and low profile, and so when a friend suggested that's where we meet before a movie last week, i was looking forward to powerful oz. it was very early, just 5:15, and we told her we were meeting someone there, and she knew his name, and ushered us through the curtain and to the small booth where he was waiting. i loved not the japanese mold), but we figured it wouldn't make it through the movie. we needed to eat, too, and ordered deviled eggs with bacon (4 of them for $5 is a good deal, and they were good, but again, they had great bacon on them, so that's a given). the bruschetta was good, and the shrimp corn dogs bordered on brilliant. if you're a little hungrier, they have small paninis for $7. we tried five or six of the plates, and all were great. i'm definitely going to be back to the patterson house, but reading all the other reviews, i will avoid weekend nights and make sure to get there early text: I chipped a tooth and needed a crown put in. The dentist I'd been seeing for about 10 years was no longer in my network and would have charged over $1000 out of pocket. We called three dentists in network for quotes and went to this one because it quoted $400 out of pocket (after insurance), the lesser of the three. When I went for x-rays 2 weeks before the tooth-removal procedure, I was prescribed sedatives because I have gag reflex; I was told to take 4 pills the night before and the rest (about 8) when I got to the dentist for the procedure. I also paid the amount I was quoted right before the procedure and assumed I would owe no more. The next thing I remember after getting in the chair was staggering into my bed several hours later. I thought when my mind was clear that the drugs that knocked me out were excessive and I found out later from my mom, who drove me to and from the dentist, that indeed it was excessive. More on this shortly. When I went back two weeks later to have the crown put in, I was told to pay $64 for sedation that apparently was not covered by insurance. I questioned this because I assumed this was part of my quote, but the staff still insisted I pay. I thought now, whatever. The staff tried to small talk me during ths procedure, but I was not interested in conversation; just put the crown in and send me on my way. Three weeks later, I get another unpleasant surprise; a bill that stated I owe $250 more. There was was no explanation. I had to call back the next day and a lady said it was for additional sedation to put me to sleep. I assumed this was covered either by insurance or the quote. I was not told of this beforehand and I was very upset about that, with good reason. The lady said the quote was no guarantee of actual charges insurance would pay. I was lied to and told the woman that on the phone. The woman told me not to yell and scream Lady, I will calm down when you tell me the truth. I later found out from my mom they gave me additional drugs without consent from me (because I obviously was in no condition to consent and if I was I would not have consented) or from my mom (she said the staff did not ask her).. I find this cowardly and unprofessional. Also if there were complications - it's very possible - that is grounds for malpractice. I had to pry from the lady on the telephone I was being charged for this excessive sedation as well as labor for doctor; isn't this what the dentist is being paid for? I will pay this only because I do not want to deal with a collection agency and, though I have a good case, don't want to pay attorney fees that would be more than my bill. So far, the amount I've had to pay out of pocket is what I would have with my previous dentist, who was up front and did not sneak any bills by after the fact. Enjoy your money pal because you just lost a patient, permanently, with your deceptive and dishonest practices

text: Gotta love a Portuguese byob in the no libs. I have been eating Portuguese food for years. One of my best friends is Portuguese so I cut my teeth at a few places in Newark. With that being said, I enjoyed my dinner at Koo Zee Doo. Four of us walked into the small, quaint space on N. 2nd. First things I noticed were the open kitchen (plus) and the exposed brick (double plus). We were seated immediately and began to look over the menu. We decided on the shrimp in piri piri, chicken gizzards and the Salada de Cores. I was very happy with all of the appetizers. The shrimp in hot sauce was very flavorful and they prepared the dish with large shrimp, head on (that's where all the flavor is). The sauce was so tasty that I cleaned it up with some bread. The chicken gizzards were served in a small casserole in a delicate sauce. They were soft and very flavorful. The salad was also surprisingly good. It was bursting with flavor from the dressing and the veggies were cut nicely so it wasn't awkward to eat. Nice presentation. For the entrees we chose the rabbit special and the Feijoada de Marisco. The rabbit was awesome. Very rich tasting but not heavy. I definitely ate more of it than I should have. Rabbit tends to be bony by nature so this was just par for the course as far as I was concerned. Once again, some bread was used for sopping up sauce. The seafood and bean stew was prepared well but lacked the "pop" of the other dishes. Don't get me wrong, it was very tasty. It just sort of paled in comparison to the rabbit. Our meal concluded with four of us splitting one dessert. Tarte de Amendôa which was light a flavorful. Just the right amount of sweet after our very savory meal. I will go back to this place. I once watched "The Good Life" perform their album, "Album of the Year" at Solar Culture. Tim Kasher stood on that little wooden stage performing with a bottle of Jack Daniels next to his feet. He was obviously distraught. He would take a swig of whiskey after each song, almost as if he was numbing himself from the painfully beautiful memories he was sharing with us through his music. It was extremely powerful and moving to see this man falling apart physically and emotionally onstage. By the way, I take no pleasure in seeing men fall apart, I'm just a sucker for raw emotion. Anyways... This kind of experience is something you will seldom (if ever) experience in a big money making venue. You also won't get the kind of deal on tickets you get at Solar Culture and lastly, you would never be able to bring your own alcohol. These are just a few things that make Solar Culture so special.

text: I have always been the type of gal who said that I wouldn't "pop" my yelp cherry with a negative review, because well, I didn't want my first memory to be of me tearing a new hole into a business. HOWEVER, I had to do it. I can't help it. I promise I'll write something nicer in the near future! Let's start first, when I came in, I gots NO greeting for at least 4 minutes. Luckily, I was completely entranced by their amazing selection of OPI and Essie nail polishes to barely notice. I have acrylic nails, and I've been on a search to find a good place for about 4 years. I wanted a refill and a pedi....and this was a WHOPPING $55 bones....say what?? I was totes okay with paying that amount, because I wanted to see if the price was worth it, if it was, I would definitely go back....it wasn't. First of all....OUCH! The next day my cuticles (both feet and hands) were puffy and red cause they had been cut way too far. Their dryers suck, so they had to repair one toe TWO times before I left out. And even after that, it smudged. The paint on the nails started chipping a week after I got them done....and now the actual NAILS are chipping. I'm going to have to get a fill-in to save my nails after a week and a half! Okay...on to the nice stuff (momma said you should always lead with the nice stuff, but screw it). The staff were really nice for the most part, the young lady that did my pedi was nice, the girl doing my refill was cool too. "Free" massages while getting your nails dried, which is nice, but if that means I gotta pay an extra $10 for a fill in....I'm straight. They took their time, which is definitely a first for me in Philly. It looks great in there, as it should cause it's pretty new. And, like I said earlier, their nail polish selection is TO DIE FOR! And they had cute designs if you're into that. I don't know, from the reviews I saw on this great site, I thought that I had finally found the grail of nail salons. And maybe they're great for just manis and not so good with artificial nails. But I'm definitely, still searching.
label: NEG

The theatre is big and nice, but it is old. The seats are comfortable, and there's enough room, so you can stretch your legs out. The intermission is a treat to look forward to, since they sell frozen desserts like ice cream on a stick... mmm. And although you can bring your ice cream in the theatre to eat, you cannot bring your garbage in there. I guess they don't want crinkly noises going on during the play. I waited about 10 minutes to get my card/ID back, and went to sign the slip- THIRTY FIVE DOLLARS. That's a lot, even for a place off bourbon street. She couldn't give me an itemized receipt for some reason, and they AUTO GRATTED me (as in, they decided how much the tip would be without a sign or warning stating that this is their policy) I used to love this place, but the automatic gratuity should have been explained before I handed over my card- I would have gone somewhere else or to the ATM. text: Downgrade! I'd be misleading people if I kept my four star review at four stars; my recent experiences with Chow's have been anything but. For starters, they won't take credit cards for orders under $20. Does take-out Chinese EVER cost more than ten dollars? I think not. Next, the food. Last Friday I defied Lenten mores and ordered the chicken with broccoli. At $4.50, there is no denying that this is a total deal-- until you taste the chicken. The uniformly flat pieces seemed suspect, and the taste was not good, no matter how much sauce was soaked through. The chicken itself was also minimal; the dish would have been more appropriately named, broccoli with chicken. Even though I ask every time I call, there is still no option of brown rice; just boring old white or fried. Surely I can't be the only person who wants brown? The "amazing chicken" was still tasty the last time I ordered it, and I've always been pretty happy with their wonton soup. When I'm craving one of these items on my lunch break, Chow's will suffice, but I'll be trekking to Han Dynasty for now on when I really want to get down with some good Chinese.

text: IMHO, one of the best places to come in this city for a house baked good. Everything is just fantastic and, if you're a vegan, this is your baked goods heaven. As a coffee shop though? Maybe not. When I first moved out here this was one of the first coffee shops I found so I came here quite a bit. It's an old building, so plugs are hot commodities and, even in the summer, the place is pretty busy all the time. Lots of people there just to be seen, but a lot of people also working. Quite a bit of loud conversation too (the high ceilings don't help) so, if you're going to work, bring headphones. Bathroom's an issue. There's only one and it requires a key from the front. Wifi never really worked very well. Probably because of the sheer number of people using it. Seating's an issue. Even if you don't need/want a plug, it's tough to get a seat in there many times, especially during the school year. So, now, honestly, it's one of my last choices for a coffee shop in town. However, if I'm on 4th and want something sweet, or with some friends and we're looking for a place to sit for a while and eat or drink something good and non-alcoholic, Epic is first on my list. I just LOVE their food and it's a great place to come for breakfast. I also noticed this time that they've put up a bunch of ultra-passive aggressive signs regarding, for instance, use of the wifi, leaning on glass cases while in line (the line gets really long, another minus for this place), the use of nuts in their cooking, etc. But how about the coffee? It's not bad but it's not great. They seem to like to burn the beans sometimes. Typical price, $0.50 refills. Large sizes are served in regular glasses, which is a little annoying. Mediums are in a mug though. The weird crowd can partially be explained by the neighborhood but also by the fact that there are an abnormally large number of halfway houses and rehab centers within a few blocks, in addition to a methadone clinic. I mean, I've never had problems, but it seems to freak some people out. Parking is free and there's a big bike rack right outside. Definitely a plus. $7 minimum on credit cards.

text: I was about to give this place 4 stars but after seeing the positive feedback on here, I had to go with the majority with this one and go for the full 5. I've only been here twice, the first time was for their hyped Pierogie Week. In fact, I think prior to hearing about it... I probably wouldn't have come here. I went with 3 other folks and back then, the service was awful. I don't think they were ready for the amount of business that would be produced by some coverage in (I think) Philly.com and getting the local blogosphere all ablaze. All in all though, the food made up for the kinda flakey service, the pierogies were amazing - especially the buffalo chicken (though, I'm buffalo-anything biased). Now, I came in here a few days ago to check out their highly anticipated Pierogi Hoagie that I'd heard about. And although it sounds like it'd be a carb-fest explosion, I honestly think it's more reminiscent of a Cuban Sandwich if anything. It was good and though doesn't have that large of a footprint, it was deceptively filling. Here's where all the bonus points come in - the owner, Jamie is the man. I had a good 20 minute conversation with him about Star Trek. In fact, you'll be able to glance at an authentic Vehicle Team Voltron, unboxed sitting above the bar. That's not mentioning all the miscellaneous Star Wars figurines complete with AT-AT. There's also a 4' LEGO Pirate standing in the corner. Now, if all this geeky stuff sounds up your alley, you'll feel at home. Aside from the geek talk, I was pretty impressed by the new addition of brunch which I have to check out. Jamie plans on having at least 6-7 varieties of waffles on the menu. These vary from chicken & waffles to "shit on a shingle" (one with portabello "shit" to create a veggie alternative), to an impressive cornmeal waffle topped with veggie chipotle chili and stuffed with cheddar cheese? (Did I take these notes down correctly? Either way, sounds awesome.) All in all, we had a great chat about all the awesome food concepts he has. Even as recent as maybe 5 years ago, I never would have expected a little neighborhood bar to be coming up with such ambitious and creative food. I'm impressed and look forward to many return visits.

text: I have been raised around Italian cuisine my whole life. So I was excited to go with my family for a nice lunch on a beautiful afternoon and eat on the Hill - famous for it's Italian cuisine. 1st off - we were seated after standing @ the door for 5 minutes completely unrecognized. Our waitress mozied over and sat us. And that was that. It literally took her almost 15 minutes to actually great us and get a drink order. We put our food order in at this time as well, assuming it would be another 15 minutes til we saw her face again. It was a good decision on our part. As we were sitting there wondering if we'd ever get recognized, I had noticed there were 5 tables in the place total, including us - and 2 servers. It honestly doesn't take 15 minutes to just get someone a drink order, or at least let us know you'd be with us as soon as possible. She did apologize for our wait, I have to give her that. We decided to order bruschetta as our appetizer. SOOOOOOOOOOOOOO bland. Every single one of us was salting it. It was diced tomatoes on toast to put it nicely. My dad, sister, and I ordered caprese salads. I didn't know someone could screw such a simple, fabulous dish up! It wasn't traditional and they were very skimpy on mozzarella and basil. Edible at best. For my entree, I went ahead with the chicken marsala. It was one small chicken breast in a sauce I was assuming was a marsala, yet did not resemble the rich brown color it is normally. It was orange. This dish too I had to salt. My mother ordered the manicotti. It was so small and cost a whopping 10 bucks and came with nothing on the side! All and all, the meal was mediocre at best. The most enjoyable thing was the bread and parmesan cheese with garlic olive oil. I can make better italian food than this - and i'm a polish girl!

My friends had all ordered the Latin combo specials with different meats - Pulled pork, Carne Asada, chicken, etc. Overall, no one was pleased with their choice. There is so much they could've done with this sald to make it better while keeping it simple. Use darker greens. Add some herbs. Some chopped peanuts. Mango. Whatever. The tofu teriyaki. This was 6 pieces of heavily battered tofu with caramelized onions and steamed broccoli, bathed in teriyaki sauce. Now, I've had tofu and other teriyaki dishes at lots of Japanese restaurants. This tofu was weird. The batter was too thick, and since it was dressed in the teriyaki sauce, was soggy. There were too few vegetables. They could've added carrots, asparagus, so many other things that they could've used that woul'dve made this good. This came with a side of rice. It was fine. They were stingy. I haven't had the soup but it smelled good. All that said, I wouldn't not get this again. I tried the teriyaki sauce on its own. That was some really good teriyaki sauce. It wasn't cloyingly sweet like some can be and it wasn't thick and goopy. You couldn't appreciate the teriyaki sauce they way the tofu was prepared. Fix the tofu (steam it, or figure out how to improve the crust, whatever), add some vegetables, and they could have a real winner. Now on to the vegetable tempura. Simply put: this was the worst tempura I have ever had. The batter was way too heavy and puffy. The vegetables included sweet potato, broccoli, onion and mushroom. The broccoli was tasteless, it had a sort of par-steamed texture, and then since it was wrapped in this terrible batter, was all around bad. The sweet potato was ok. The onion was weird. It was a thick ring of batter with some slime in the middle. The mushroom was the worst. It was this weird, slimy, thing and I couldn't eat it. If I were them, I wouldn't serve the tempura to dogs, much less human beings. There's some promise here, and I'd go back to try other things, but they need some real work.

They bring you chips and salsa as soon as you sit down, and while the chips are hot and fresh, the salsa is that liquid slurry kind with no chunks. Everything looks the same, no matter what you order - a flat, greasy landscape of beans and cheese and tortilla. I had a tostada salad here once that was most unimpressive. The chicken tacos are okay, if not great, but 3/4 of your plate will be filled with a sea of beans and Rice Island, always threatening to encroach on your real food with its beaniness (because who eats that stuff? Nobody I've seen - it's like liquid garnish). No matter what I order here, I always seem to end up filling up on chips and salsa, pushing my bean-heaped plate away. Which is why I try not to go if I can help it. I'm sure some will disagree with me, since it's (bizarrely) a local favorite, but I'd go to Chevy's before I'd go to Bertha Miranda's. text: I'm really surprised that I'm just the second person to review this place. This is your typical, no frills, inexpensive family owned restaurant serving up delicious cuban food. This is a great spot if you're looking for real deal cuban food at bargain prices.

text: This place is awesome! I can't believe I haven't been till now. I bought the groupon back in February and finally got a chance to use it last night with my foodie group. Informed us there was no sampler when we talked about ordering it and told us when our food was coming. 3. The food is delicious and amazing. Started with the mango salsa, definitely the BEST I've ever had. very fresh and mango was not stringy. We started with the jerk wings, a bit dry, but good sauce and crab rangoon. For entree, we ordered oxtail stew, creamy pesto with chicken, brown stew chicken and another pasta dish. Food was really good and the meat was so tender. I liked mixing the stew with the rice. text: Went here based on a recommendation, and I'd like to think they were just having an off-day because it was pretty bad (although I went on a weekend, and don't restaurants usually staff their best chefs on the weekends, since there are bigger crowds?). The shrimp remoulade was okay, but it was just a pile of cold (what I assume to be thawed) shrimp and some sauce over it - nothing spectacular. The gumbo was really terrible, which is strange, because I'd heard it was good. text: I was visiting from the NY area and read the positive reviews of this place. It sounded like a perfect place for a traveling vegan looking for some great food. The reviews were all spot-on. (Any tips?) Also, the man who works there is vegan, which felt very reassuring. We also enjoyed the dessert, which was some sort of mung bean tapioca pudding. It was very subtle but nice. Regardless, anyone looking for a great meal in St. Louis should check this place out. I can't wait to go back.

text: We selected this boarding facility and vet based on my cat vet's recommendation. Sadly, I should have asked around more. After our initial vet visit, we decided to use their boarding service. They reran tests that they had run previously and charged us for everything. A few days later, a large red cyst appeared on our dog's foot. text: Have been to Farmacia for brunch and dinner and both times the restaurant did not disappoint overall. Great shabby-chic feel to the place. Brunch was great. text: This place is excellent. My father in law had the Alligator Basket with Hush Puppies and Fries, my husband had the Chicken Dinner with Macaroni and Cheese and the Sweet Potatoes, and finally, I had the Rib Basket with the Greens. We also got a basket of Okra and a Sweet Potato Pie. All of it was excellent! I've never had Okra before, and was very skeptical. I have nothing to compare it to, but it was phenomenal. The ribs were fall of the bone good, the Alligator was moist and flavorful without being fishy, and the Fried Chicken was amazing and I can't stand fried chicken (the best part it that it wasn't greasy). All of the sides were great. The sweet potato pie was just as it should be, though the crust was a little dry. However, the flavor of the filling tasted just like a sweet potato. We will be returning!

text: We were desperate to get out of the city to go to an *ahem* bigger city. It was my birthday and I was more than excited to stay at this "luxury" hotel. We choose the location because of the view and the proximity. Our first concern was parking. $18 dollars a day with no in and out privileges. We opted to park (for free) at the Delmar loop and take the light rail, buses, hotel shuttles and taxis if we needed. Second: We were able to check in early by some miracle but were forced into the South tower for North tower prices. The room was tiny and the air conditioner was so loud it woke us up every time it went on. The view in the upper left corner of the window was awesome, watching the lightening dance around the arch was impressive, the view of I-70 however, was not. Third: The public transportation in St. Louis is great, we had one of the best bus rides a person could as for, everyone was very helpful. Since we didn't have any cash on us we opted to call the hotel shuttle for the ride back, they said they would be there in 10 minutes. As we were celebrating our good fortune a fellow Budweiser tourist overheard us and said that he had been told 20 minutes and that was an hour and half ago, so we shared a cab. We called/asked for a shuttle 3 different times and each time either one wasn't available, one broke down, or we juuuuust missed it. Oh, and you are not allowed to call for a shuttle from your room you must go down to the lobby and call on the special black phones. We saw the shuttles, mostly parked outside of our tower. Fourth: Yes, a rotating view restaurant is super cool, that's a given. They must bank on you being wowed by the view so as not to pay attention to the food. We expected to pay a lot of money, what we did not expect was crappy food. The duck taco was bland, the crab cake was pretty good, the salad was confusing at best. The Bombay Sapphire dirty, dry, gin martini was super fantastic! Fifth: Our room was cleaned in the normal timely fashion but they forgot the toilet paper, uhm, that's a problem. We called and waited an hour and fifteen minutes for them to bring it up. Not helpful. Sixth: It poured on Saturday night so we decided to stay in, The pool was full of bikers so we checked out the in room movies. $14.99. 'nough said. Seventh: There is a restaurant below the main floor of the hotel that we had lunch at, they also have a brunch buffet but beef tips were not on the menu for us. We ordered the portabella fries and the Cuban Sandwich. The fries looked like little kids' pressed chicken nuggets but tasted really good. The Cuban sandwich? Well, that was not a Cuban by any stretch of the imagination. After our food arrived I did not receive another refill on my iced tea and our waiter came over to the table and took the ketchup away to give to the table across from us without a word. A nice young lady who was busing our table came by and gave me a box and an iced tea to go. She was the most helpful person there. Eighth: They advertised free Wi-Fi, IN THE ROOMS. When I had problems accessing it the front desk informed me it was only in the lobby. Overall, St. Louis is really fun, this hotel was the only thing that gave us problems, we didn't even want to go back to our rooms at the end of each night. The most helpful people were the bell-hops, and the people that bussed the tables. Don't bother with the Millennium, the Drury is right next to it and it is much better.
label: NEG

text: Pietro's is a great place to stop by and grab a coal-oven pie. The pizza is thin and well-done, but not crispy or crunchy, instead it's soft and doughy. text: I've been meaning to try this place for quite some time now...and, thanks to Yelp, I finally got a bee in my bonnet to go...and was thoroughly impressed. That is to say, satisfy by not merely having options for each person, but rather, having excellently executed options. You pretty much cannot go wrong here and spend a little time reading over the menu I'm almost positive you'll be pleased. The beer list is decent but could be better. I was elated to finally find a bar in St. Pete Beach/Gulfport with an IPA on tap but was thwarted due to them running out. I was out on the covered patio watching a tropical storm blow through and an IPA would have been perfect...I settled on several Heinekens instead. The wine list was decent as well. Full bar too. The layout is a little goofy but doesn't detract from the visit. Just make sure you don't accidently walk into one of the two (side by side) women's restrooms when they are in use. text: The food was average, service sub-par. Ordered $47 worth of food for pick up, after 20 minutes, it was ready. Next day- log onto mint, and find out that I was charged a $100 tip on top of the $47 bill. First call to pagoda, some guy picks up, he says that the charge should disappear the next day, and many people have had this issue before. So that puts me at ease, a little bit. A couple minutes later, a woman calls me from Pagodas number, she asks for the details and finds my receipt, and then says that I wrote $100 on the tip, and total for $147. I tell her that thats wrong, and who in their right mind leaves a tip of $100 on a PICK UP ORDER?? She then agrees with me and says, "I thought this was strange when we put the order into the machine, and I saw that there was a $100 tip." I ask her if she can take the charges back, and she tells me some story about not knowing how to use the machine, she repeats that the problem is my fault, and that I wrote $100 on top. I tell her again, I did not, and she continues to say the problem is that you wrote 100 on the tip. After a minute of back and forth, she offers to write a check, I said, no you have a credit card machine, and you can credit the amount back to my card, she asks for my cc number and says she will try, and hangs up. A couple of minutes later, she calls back and says, I think I credited the amount back to your card, you can check. I tell her that I checked and the amount will probably take a day to post. She then stops and again says the problem is your fault, and its not hers, she repeats that I wrote 100 on the bill, and at that point, after almost 10 minutes of my life have been wasted, I just couldn't take it anymore. I said "No, the problem is that you're arguing with me! I don't know where you come from, but nobody leaves a $100 tip on a PICK UP ORDER." She repeats, this is not my problem, this is your problem. Do you have a fax number so that I can fax you a copy of this receipt? I tell her that I do not have a fax (who does these days anyway?) and that I did not write a $100 tip. She then has the audacity to ask me to visit the restaurant so that she can show me the receipt, and I replied "This is absolutely ridiculous. The customer is always right, and in this case- EVEN MORE right than any other time. I will not be visiting to see the receipt and I never order from you again. I will also tell everyone I know not to go here." Congratulations Pagoda, I actually considered making this my go to place for chinese take out, but I'm going to have to quote the yelp rating - Methinks not.

text: I have received the most horrible hair cut of my entire life at Aveda Salon. I love Aveda products and buy them often, so getting a hair cut at Aveda salon seemed like the next logical step. Little did I know that my stylist would prefer to ignore my requests and concerns, and cut my hair the way she saw fit. This stylist was not recommended to me by any friends; I chose her by chance, based solely on the fact that she was a senior stylist. After I walked into the salon, was greeted by a friendly sales associate, admired the décor and beautiful scents in the air, and sipped a cup of Aveda tea, I was asked to get into the chair in order to receive the consultation. My stylist was a beautiful lady, who listened to what I had to say very intently. Apparently, the words did not sink in because 15 minutes later I was looking in the mirror with the sense of utter horror. I asked the stylist to keep the length - she chopped my hair 4 inches shorter. I asked for long layers -she made mine short, which caused the hair to look curly and frizzy. I was so busy chatting with my lovely stylist that I didn't notice all the atrocities that were going on north of my neck. By the time I realized the seriousness of the situation, it was too late to fix anything. I chose to stay calm, keep a brave face and not say anything. But believe me- growing out a bad hair cut is no easy task. I had to wear a ponytail every day of the week for two months. I am sure it's just my luck that I chose an unsuitable stylist; and I am sure that there are many young talented hairdressers at Aveda Academy. text: You can't dislike a restaurant with a menu containing about 8 pages, 3/4 of which are dedicated to drinks. I've eaten a few times at Derek's, each time being a positive experience. In fact, I'm just recovering from my all-too-filling, all-too-delicious lunch I just enjoyed there. If you like squid, I say get the calamari. It was incredibly delicious and served with a creamy sauce rather than the traditional marinara. Also, it has a bit of spice to it that adds a whole other dimension of flavor. The atmosphere and decor are pretty great. There is a burgundy theme echoed throughout the dining space. It's reflected in the art work, upholstery and paint, even outside on the awnings. There is ample outdoor seating, which was filled with today with people enjoying food and drinks. I, however, left the house without checking the temperature and couldn't bear being out in direct sunlight while wearing jeans. Plus, I'm a wimp and anything over 75 makes me want to shrivel up and die. This is my own issue I need to sort out. One thing I really like is the fact that Derek is almost always in the restaurant. I've heard some people say he was a bit of a jerk to them, but he's been nothing but nice and easy to talk to in my experience. I like that he always knows what's going on in his establishment, and takes the time to really be a part of it. Two things of note: 1. There is always a 3-course, set menu you can order ($20 lunch, $30 dinner). 2. There is a special every day of the week typical on drinks. $5 margaritas on Monday you say? I'm there.

text: Loved the food and the ambiance. A group of 12 of us went to for a bachelorette dinner. There were heat lamps and fire pits all around the outside patio. It was lovely, and kept us warm in the cool night air. A belly dancer was making her around and around all the tables chiming and shaking. She was pretty good and the outfits were pretty. Now to the food... lovely... i got the Mashawi Combo that includes beef kabob, lamb, and chicken with tabbouli, hummus, baba ghannouj and this garlic yogurt sauce. It was all really really good. The tabbouli was my favorite, the hummus was smooth and tasty, and the baba ghannouj was creamy but had a little extra texture and a pleasant taste of eggplant (but not too much since I'm not usually a fan of eggplant... but i still really liked it). the garlic yogurt sauce was really good, tangy and cool. As for the meats, my favorite was the lamb chunks then the chicken. They were both moist and flavorful. The kabab as good too, but the other parts of the dish out shone it and I think I've had better kababs closer to home (but still very good). Some friends ordered the pepper steak and others the salmon. It all looked great and everyone was happy. My combo was huge and at $20 fed me for 2 meals so I was happy. There's plenty of other great sounding dishes. If I'm back in SB, I'd definitely try to come out here again. I'm craving the tabbouli now... Side note... it's romantic feeling but at the same time there's usually a lot a people so not exactly intimate.... they also have hooka options in the evening and looks cool for lounging later in the evening...

Sometimes they show a sports game, or do some cool visual stunts and it's something you'd expect in the lobby of a place that gouges its customers like Comcast. Diatribes aside, the holiday show, in particular, is a really nice added bonus, and like others have said and like the light show at the Wanamaker Building before it, it has become a holiday tradition for families, including mine. The whole show is much better suited for kids, but people of all ages and those kid-like too, can enjoy the show. Music is great, they feature local Philadelphia dancers and performers and as one flies over the night city skyline, it's fine holiday fun. The show has even added snow, spot lights, and better sound. Santa makes a cameo, live!, at the end. The show is featured at the top of the hour, from Thanksgiving until the second week in January. It's worth a gander, and should be part of your holiday activities. Actually, the proper holiday Center City tour actually goes like this: Comcast center holiday show, walk east through Love Park and the tree, cross 15th street, meander through the Christmas village around City Hall and Dillworth Plaza, make your way to Macy's, catch the holiday show - and let the visions of sugar plums dance in [your] heads!

text: Top 3 Fried Chicken in the city. Seriously. Really. A gas station. I read rave reviews for the chicken at Lil Dizzy's (adequate at best) and the classic over touristed and ridiculously over rated Willy Mae's (which lost most of the charm it had when Willie Mae stopped hanging around the kitchen) and laugh. Those down home style places can't come close to the fried delights under the heat lamps manned by hispanics that barely speak English at this Middle Eastern owned gas station. It sounds like I'm being sarcastic, probably because I usually am, but these are the facts. The chickens crunch and flavor is rivaled by only Coops and McHardy's in this city but for $14 you're getting 25 pieces of dark meat. ($16 for 25 pieces if you are one of those fools that don't understand true fried chicken taste and prefer white meat) No tables, obviously, but make sure there aren't too many people at your house to finish the box because like all great fried chicken and wines, it ages very well. For a party we had where we bought our favorite food from around the city, we got 150 pieces for a grand total of about $70 and made believers of an entire crowd...and that was before everybody was blind drunk. Brings back the memory of the incredible era of first few months of Chicken Box (RIP) before they went down hill and eventually closed. Conveniently, if you have to go out of your way to get here, you can fill up on some very cheap gas to get you home. A total package.

text: I have a cadre of friends who swear by the food here and love everything they make. I've been here more times than I have fingers and toes and disagree. Service is fine (it has improved over time) and the interior is pleasant, but the food leaves much to be desired. This Lemon Grass location used to be a Jasmine Thai, which had VASTLY superior food. (Anyone remember their pineapple fried rice with raisins? To die for!!) I've had just about everything on their lunch menu - the dishes I've had are lackluster, ranging from average to plain awful. Their vegetarian green curry is weak - on their menu it's listed as three stars for spiciness but it tastes barely like one star. Both their hot and sour and coconut soups are watery and tasteless. As for appetizers, their satay is scarily dry, but the sauce is okay. If I ever find myself here, I skip their "lunch special" (~$9 for a soup, appetizer, and entree) and ask for a plate of drunken noodles ($9); it's safe and dependable. I specify they be made so spicy that I can't taste them and occasionally they come close. One star for good service (depends on who serves you, of course), a clean, attractive interior, and another star for the times their drunken noodles have made me sweat. If you want good Thai, you won't find it here, nor anywhere else in King of Prussia - but DO check out the neighboring towns for amazing Thai eats. (Thai Orchid in Blue Bell, The Thai Place in Phoenixville, and Flavor in Wayne) UPDATE: Comically, I eat here relatively often because King of Prussia really has no good Thai places. Just recently I asked for my food to be made absurdly spicy and they did it, this once. I was thrilled to see them load sliced Thai peppers on ALL my dishes...

The caesar salad was sadly the same, somewhat bland, but the lamb was much better. I ordered it the same way (medium-rare), but this time they actually cooked it correctly. I cut into my first chop and could see that these were tender and succulent (the inside was pink this time). Items arrive just as you had literally ordered them. "I'd like the prime ribeye" then you will get the prime ribeye. Sides are extra but come in huge portions, big enough for two. My mashed potato side was inedible. My boyfriend's baked potato was fine, but then again, how can one mess up a baked potato. The service was amazing. I was told by the waitress that she had received a message pertaining to me, so I can only assume that my amazing service is not their standard. When Fleming's tries, Fleming's delivers. But why do they have to try? Why do they have to impress someone to serve a good meal? Tips for an enjoyable hundred dollar meal: - Skip on everything at this restaurant other than meat - Continue to send your food back until they *try* to make it right. They are perfectly capable of serving up great meat, they just need to want to try, which they don't seem to want to do for every customer. My original one star rating averaged against my revised three star review.

They make their tortillas on site as well as the chips which are complimentary. They had radishes, beef, cilantro and onion, all that you need for a great tasting taco. Then my burrito, which had all the essential burrito ingrediants, pico di gallo, rice, meat, cheese. So delightful to have authentic burrito other than places trying to pass off as such. Next time I will have to try the chile rellenos since I love those so much. The decor is what you expect, vinyl table clothes and plastic everywhere. Tiles and it was very homey feeling. text: Approaching the restaurant, one of the letters of the LUKE sign was burnt out, and I should have taken that as an omen of things to come.
