More time wasted flagging down a waiter serving another group to get spoons. Don't bother with the crab & corn bisque - there's no crab in it, about 5 kernels of corn and watery. Nice selection of Belgian and German beers. Wine pours are small. Prices seem reasonable at first glance, but portions are relatively small by American standards. Steaks are thin. Friend's burger was over done. Fries were cold (really unexcusable, at least get that right...) I had the veal cheeks which had a nice smoky flavor, but they were swimming in a watery, not very mushroomy flavored sauce. Instead of before or with the apps, bread was served between apps and main course and barely warm. The little crock of butter was sloppily prepared and messy to handle. Butter all over everybody's fingers. Just another little annoying thing that gives an indication of attention to detail. Serving the burgers on a cutting board is a clever gimmick, but they looked a bit worn and I started thinking "dirty cutting board" probably not the best presentation idea. Bread pudding dessert was very good. All in all, I can't really recommend Luke, there's better places in NO for the money. Not close to "Iron Chef" material, for sure. Would have given it 3 stars, but Yelp says 3 stars is "A-OK" and Luke was not, at least on this night. It was "Meh", so sorry Luke, it's 2 stars for you.

text: sometimes this place can be very interesting... especially when it comes to drink prices... cheap would be the word. I've been in this place when the mardi gras indians practice on sunday nights... not something you see everyday in nola, and it can be intimidating to say the least, but the amount of energy during these performances will keep you up all night... blistering.... other nights the place is filled with locals from the surrounding neighborhood, and that is fun, if you live here... I happen to be on this block. however, I don't enjoy nights where stinky people are swilling cheap drinks, and forgot to bathe in this NO air conditioning atmospere... It can be very depressing. bands are a hit and miss. The owners are GREAT people, but the employees seem to come and go too often... seems like right now, the staff is working out perfectly... I'm happy with them. I enjoy this place, many friends in there, but its only for a few drinks, never for an all nighter... usually a happy hour works great, or a krewe de vieux or good children party. wish they still had the bacon garlic oyster poboy... my landlady in her eighties tells me stories back when the original owners sold some killer food, but these days its mexican... its a hit or miss, usually a miss... but occasionally, I have a really good time there... hey, its way better than it was pre katrina... for sure.

text: Let me state that I unequivocally enjoyed my dinner at R2L. When a restaurant is located on the 37th floor of a building, you pretty much can expect that it will be a bit pricey. Although my friend and I didn't get to sit at a window, we were still able to look out at the view from our table. Service was great, our server knew the menu pretty well. We started with the grilled truffle flatbread and the rabbit nachos. Both were excellent, but the rabbit nacho was the winner. I can still remember the taste: the jalapeno mousse added just the right kick of heat, the homemade nachos were crunchy, and the rabbit was killer! Although I enjoyed the flatbread as well, I thought it had a bit too much arugula on the top. For entrees, I chose the ribeye with fries which could sound a bit pedestrian. Those were the BEST damn fries I've had in a long time. My friend had the venison with the licorice sauce, I'm not a big fan of licorice, but the venison was cooked just right. As I write this review, I'm salivating from the memories of this meal!! I would return to R2L for another meal, which must include the rabbit nachos. Yummy...

text: My friends and I used to refer to Cool Springs Galleria as "the real mall." My favorite thing was that they had a pet store so I could pop in and hug a rabbit for a while, but that store has since shut down. I can understand how not many people want to go to the mall for such a large, expensive commitment as one of their pedigree pups. I'm mildly obsessed with Cozymel's salsa (who cares if they're a chain they got it right!) so I always make sure to go across the bridge to buy some while I'm over in that part of town.

To his dismay when he ordered them they said they could not make them because he was the only one who ordered them that night (I guess they make them in big batches only) and because of the difficulty or something, I don't know. Well anyway he was really disappointed and hard pressed to pick another dish, so when they came back to take our order the owner came out with our waiter and informed my friend that they would be making the noodles special for him. He was so happy, let me tell you. And as always, they were delicious. So in summary, really good Chinese food, super friendly owner and wait staff, very accommodating and attentive. Even their non-Chinese dishes are delicious. I recommend the Vietnamese Hot and Sour Soup and the Vietnamese Style Vermicelli if you're in the mood for something different. Yummy!

text: Dearest Niche, How do I love thee? Let me count the ways. I love thee to the depth and breadth and height My soul can reach, when feeling out of sight..... .... I've been to Niche about three or four times now. Each time was mindblowingly amazing. I have tried their Prix Fixe menu + wine pairing, the 3 for $40 course menu, and the a la carte goodies as well. I must preface this by stating each time I went was with a boy...on a date....and usually for a special occasion like my Birthday or something. I could not afford to eat Niche on a regular basis, and rightfully so--everything here is a culinary masterpiece. That doesn't mean some dishes are kind of a flop sometimes....they're only human! But still. You can really taste the level of skill that goes into each dish. Each dish is made with skill and calculated precision. I never really liked pork but their pork blew my mind and changed my world. I'd put one piece of pork in my mouth and literally suck on it for a good few minutes before chewing and swallowing as to get the flavors out and savor each one. God. Listen to me. I sound like an Iron Chef critic! :) "Oooh, chairman-sama! The flavors, desu!" However....I almost took off one star because of the seating. It's kind of cramped sometimes. I get that it's supposed to be "modern" and "trendy" cusisine and they want a "modern" sort of set up, but really? I felt awkward talking to my date.... I think we were probably the youngest couple in the entire restaurant too. Me 22, him 26... everyone else was probably our parents' age. Not that that's a bad thing, well...I just wish people wouldn't stare so much at us. Not talking about the waitstaff either, haha. But it really depends on where you sit. This time we were sandwiched between two other tables of people. Last time we had a small little private area in the back all to ourselves. But then again this was a Friday night, and the last time we went, it was probably a weeknight like Wed. or Thurs. BTW the staff are SO friendly and accomodating here. They are not snobby or rude just because we're young foodies in a sea of middle aged folks. (No offense to you middle aged people...!) Anytime I have a question, they don't make me feel stupid with their answer unlike a few other places I've been to. (But could just be a few bad servers at those other places.) I also like the fact that they break down each and every component of your meal upon delivery to the table so you know EXACTLY what it is you're eating and what the word semifreddo actually means.

text: Slice is an interesting phenomenon. I have been to both the South Philly and the 17th and Sansom location's. I enjoy the South Philly location a LITTLE more because each time I have been there - it's been way less crowded than the location on Sansom ever has been (Sansom location gets a LOT of traffic). The pizza at slice is really very good. The crust is thin - the cheese is great - and there is NO grease. I mean NONE. Which I can seriously appreciate. Additionally, they have a variety of cheese and dough options - which is great for people who are vegan, lactose intolerant, or are watching their weight. The sauces taste good, and they always have an interesting combo of toppings / variety of pizza's that are great. The ambiance is simple, the service is good - the people are really friendly, but beware - they take only cash. The major DOWNSIDE of Slice is that it is a tad bit expensive. However, it's worth it. Next to Lorenzo's, and Franco Luigi's - I love Slice. Great pizza.

text: Well, golly, when a place opens 10 minutes early because you're looking forlorn at the front door, I mean WOW, that's VERY nice. Sat at the bar and started chatting with the wonderful bartender. Very knowledgeable, helpful, personable and a delight to talk to. She knows that you don't just "serve" a customer, you make the customer's whole experience. That is the difference between a good bartender and a GREAT bartender. I always wondered how a wine bar can be unique in Pennsylvania, given the restrictions imposed by the PLCB, but she explained it well. The wines are carefully chosen to provide a large variety of tastes and textures and all are available by the glass. But ...sigh.... it's still Pennsylvania and the selection doesn't quite compare to what many other major cities can offer. I had the mushroom and fontina bruschetta, a bit salty, but tasty and warm and the bread was just the right texture. Then the duck salad with spinach, strawberries, pistachios and a mint vinaigrette. The duck was tender and the salad was very tasty, and inventive. I love new tastes! Then another bruschetta, the more traditional eggplant caponata. They snuck in golden raisins to give it a bit of sweetness. (the menu doesn't tell you about the raisins) Tria seems very well run, and obviously successful since they have opened another wine bar, Biba.

text: Went here for dinner last night - we were looking for Spartaco - as it turns out it's now the Osteria but it's still owned by the same guy. First off, his Italian mom was sitting in the corner of the restaurant when we got there - the owner greeted us and brought us to our table right away. Our server came over with the wine list, bread with a fabulous olive and olive oil dipping sauce was brought over. The menu is small, with nice homemade pasta and seafood choices. Kind of what you might expect in a town next to the ocean. We started with two appetizers - bay scallops in a light tomato-basil sauce and a mixed seafood in red sauce over parmesan polenta. Both were terrific - the sauce with the bay scallops was fresh tasting and had a little bite to it. The risotto was topped with calamari, littlenecks, scallops and shrimp - delicious. Caesar salads next - excellent dressing and very fresh and crispy romaine. Then for the main attraction I had homemade canneloni with meat sauce - amazing. My friend had a delicious white fish with a caper, tomato and olive sauce and I had a taste and it just melted in my mouth. We finished that off with espresso and cannolli - what a great dinner. The service was fabulous and the owner came over at the end of the meal to see how everything was. It was great!

text: How the hell has no one reviewed the Creepy yet? Of course, the current Creepy Crawl is nothing like it used to be. It's one of those places that inspires women to look up on the Internet how to pee standing up) Now it's a nice enough bar, but it really hasn't developed a patina of character yet. I'm taking off one star for the new Creepy being blander than the old one. The huge thing the Creepy has going for it is great bands. They pull some national bands, but they really pull in a ton of great regional bands. Lots of punk, industrial, metal, and rock-ish stuff. Great underground music you won't hear on the radio and stuff. One other big detail is that they have the bar in a cordoned off area. text: Can you give negative stars? Every experience I had with Dr. Garofalo and her office staff was beyond horrid. The fact that a patient calling gets put on hold five (count 'em, five!) times should be off-putting enough to make you look for another doctor, unless you like waiting, have extra reserves of patience and don't have any health problems, ever. The first time, I was just looking for a dermatologist referral, which you would think is relatively straightforward. Think again. I was able to get an appointment after about half an hour on the phone - this wait was just a taste of what was to come. Once I went to the office, I waited approximately 30 minutes in the waiting room, followed by 20 more in the examination room. I was seen by the doctor for about 3 minutes and shooed away. When I went for my annual, I booked I think 6 weeks ahead for an appointment so I could be the first of the day. However, Dr. Garofalo didn't feel the need to get to work on time (despite the fact that my getting to work on time was contingent on her showing up) so I got to wait in the paper dress for 45 minutes for her to show up. Once she showed up, she had to get settled in, so even though I could hear her voice I still had to sit there for another 5 or so minutes. The one time I was actually sick, the office girl told me that I could come in right away. After sitting in the waiting room for over an hour and a half, I asked if I would ever get to see her. The response I got was something along the lines of why should I expect to be seen when there are other people with appointments? I said that I needed to go to class and they told me that I was SOL. Wonderful. And not even a doctor's note for missing my earlier class. The last time I went to this office, I was looking to a renewal for my dermatologist referral. This literally requires the doctor to look at my face and sign a piece of paper. I waited 45 minutes in the waiting room and decided to ask how many people were ahead of me since again, I had class. It had been a rough week and I had a lot of other things I could have been doing, so my emotional reaction was probably disproportionate to the situation, but when I was told it would be at least another hour, I had my charts be sent to another doctor and never turned back. Do not. DO NOT. go to Dr. Garofalo's office if you want to see a doctor. If you want to read magazines for a few hours though, her waiting room is the place.

text: This museum could probably be better described as an amusement park. There's a Ferris wheel on the roof (which i didn't get to ride due to some rain! Boo!), a 10-story circular slide, a big thing of *balls* to play around in, a rope swing, and mazes and *mazes* of deep-down caves, sky-high cages and installation art-type things to crawl through! I was told that this museum used to be an old shoe factory. I love factories! They also have an outdoor area where you can cool off ('cause you WILL get sweaty!), eat hot dogs and drink beer. I never thought I'd say this, but... knee pads would come in handy here.... ..as you will be crawling through millions of small spaces :) I had the good fortune of spending a few hours here with some lovely people on July Fourth, 2009, and we lost each other on several occasions, as one of us would inevitably disappear down a rabbit hole! This place reminds me of the movies Edward Scissorhands and The City of Lost Children...such a trippy place! Playing is so therapeutic...I've never been to a museum quite like this and wish San Francisco had something similar. Just think of all the awesome first dates that have taken place here!

text: Agave gets one star for strong margaritas and for good reaction to major problems. They should get no stars for the pure comedy we experienced on our visit last night. I ordered a chicken quesadilla, which was palatable but not wonderful. As I was going through my routine of scooping up some sour cream and some guacamole, a little bit of salsa and some lettuce and spreading it on my quesadilla, something seemed a little tough. I wrote it off as a chunk of iceberg and didn't think any more of it. Until I bit into it, and it wouldn't break. I pulled it out of my mouth to discover a balled-up, flattened out RECEIPT. In my freaking guacamole! And it wasn't even for my order! At nearly the same moment, one of my dining companions was working on pulling half a toothpick out of her mouth, which was buried deep inside her chimichanga. We're not snobby diners, so we brought it to the attention of the waitress in good humor, but we had every right to throw a fit. She did comp every single meal and brought us all a double of what we were drinking on the house, but come on. Maybe if I find myself in a group wanting to head out to Agave strictly for drinks, I'll go. They seem to have that side of the operation down. But I can't say I'll feel like choking down foreign objects any time soon.

text: This is a brewery that has a tasting room. BYOFood if you want to munch. But the walk to and from may take your mind off that experience as your see the operation and smell the hops and grains. They call their beers "big" for a reason. Huge in flavor and alc content. These are all solid beers w/ABV starting at 5.5 and climbing up to 11.5. I doubt you'd ever see an American Lager in here, from a keg, never a can and that's saying something coming from the land of Yingling. The 'tasting room' was nice: bar stools and a few tables. Local lads chatting away about all things beer. They have quite a selection: 2 IPA's, 2 browns, porter, Imperial Stout, just to name a few. They'll also have a guest tap or two. Pricing is totally reasonable. They also have 6-packs, pints, and (refillable) growlers for take out. Of note, the common theme to both Cigar City and Tampa Bay Brewing is that of the hassles they are having w/zoning and permits w/the various agencies, more so w/CCB. This is a great establishment, making great beer. Give them your support if you can.

text: I love this place, even though they sometimes give me funny looks. International Foods is not an entirely accurate name, because they tend mostly towards the foods of the Indian nation. Your friends will love you (more?). International Foods appears deceptively small from the outside and while it's not a huge supermarket, it does have a great selection. (Beware! The parking lot is VERY tricky.) They have big bags of basmati rice, you can buy big bags of pulses (bulk dals), and as advertised, a ton of spices. The great thing about the spices is that you can buy sizable bags for very reasonable prices (none of this McCormick's $6 for one oz of cumin nonsense). There is also a lot of fun produce, some of which you may never have seen before. There's a great variety of frozen "ethnic" food, big bags of chickpea flour, exciting packaged desserts, ice cream flavors you've likely never heard of, interesting cookware, you name it. They also often have inexpensive and tasty hot samosas at the register. Sometimes the smell of the international spices can be a little overwhelming, but the store is certainly clean enough and easy to maneuver It is crazy awesome. It can be incredibly economical (unless you get carried away like me and buy ten jars of Indian pickle ) and a great resource for those who like to cook and try new things.

Every single thing on both of our plates was delicious, and as usual, the freshness of the produce just added to the great tastes. I doubt I would take my kids as this is no basic bacon and eggs, but if anyone wants that, they can go to IHOP. text: So every so often I return to Indianapolis to visit family, and every time I experience severe culture shock. Yes, I truly belong in LA. First, I'll forgive this place for sporting a truly uninspired name. That said, there wasn't much to praise about this place. We arrive, a party of 5. Not an unusual number for a restaurant, no? Well the hostess wants to simply put a 5th chair on the end of a table for 4...and there would have been no room for us to all fit, legs under the table where they belong. An empty table set for 6 is next to the too-small table, and we inquire about using that one. No, the table that is set for six is used for parties of 7 to 8. Yeah I don't get that either, but 15 minutes later the hostess got 3 other people to put 2 other tables together to accommodate us. The place was almost empty, mind you. The table ordered a cornbread skillet to share. While it tasted good, this is way too much food. Seriously, it was like a cornbread birthday cake sliced for 6 slices. Huge. Our party had some serious eaters in it, yet quite a bit went to waste. Simply too much food. My father ordered a salad. It was not what I would call a salad, as it had one long piece of romaine lettuce on it and then some meat. Gross, and definitely a ripoff. Entrees were a mixed bag. While I cannot recall the exact names, the following dishes were ordered: 1) Hot pot fish (x2) 2) Brisket 3) Ribeye** 4) Spicy Penne in a Light Creamy Vodka sauce with chicken Hot pot fish was well-liked. Really good according to the two ladies who had it. My father ordered the ribeye, and he thought it was good, but "adequate." Nothing groundbreaking here, but nothing glaring, either. The brisket was universally panned. Brisket is supposed to be slow-cooked, imparting a very tender, melt-in-your-mouth texture. This "brisket" was deemed to really be sliced pot roast, as it was dry and chewy. The diner and his wife (she had a bite) were not happy. The penne ala vodka with chicken was also not what actually came out. There was no cream added to the sauce at all. This was straight-up red marinara sauce, not the classic pink sauce one would expect from a penne ala vodka dish. It was edible, but not what was ordered. Penne was really small in diameter, a little over-cooked, and the chicken was super dry. The sauce was NOT a "light creamy vodka sauce" as advertised, and instead was a marinara sauce. It wasn't awful, but had I known what I would be served, I would have ordered something else. Note on entrees: if you want to split an entree, they charge you $5+ to split. This is outrageous, even in Los Angeles (it happens, but it's not really common). This place is not of a caliber where this would be expected, and it reeked of pretension. For dessert, several bread puddings were ordered and split. No one was wowed; this is very average bread pudding. It had caramel drizzle on top, and it is honestly too sweet. The whipped cream on the side was loaded with confectioner's sugar and was deemed inedible by everyone. Each order of bread pudding was split by 2 people, though not one plate was finished more than 50%. This portion size was more out-of-control than the cornbread skillet. I don't like places that charge super high prices for mediocre-at-best food, while serving so much of it that much goes to waste. NO ONE could eat the portions at this restaurant as part of a healthy diet. This is also not health food. Service was slow and uneven, prices high, pretentious factor cranked up to level 12...just no. I'll waste my money on a place with better food than what I can make at home, thank you so much. **Edited to correct an inaccuracy. Ribeye is not brisket. Update: I just spoke with a few friends who recently dined here, and they had the same reaction to the penne pasta dish, though theirs didn't have chicken. Like me, they were expecting an item described as having a light, creamy sauce to actually have a light, creamy sauce...but instead they also received a chunky, tomato/marinara sauce. While not bad, it was not what was ordered. Maybe Northside Social needs to educate their chef on the menu, or maybe they should just change the menu to reflect what the chef feels like serving.
label: NEG

Look, I have definitely had fun here and have seem some good shows. But this place is very poorly run and managed with ZERO consideration to the customer experience. Every year people gripe about lousy parking, no bathrooms, expensive prices, and every year the same people come back anyway. Where else is Aerosmtih and Dave Matthews going to come in June? text: On Saturday, had my third (and final) experience at the Palace Cafe and all I can say is DO NOT GO THERE. You will be disappointed. First, some background. The Palace Cafe is an institution. It has been around for a long time, and certainly has a reputation as a traditional "you MUST go there" New Orleans restaurant. The first time I went several years ago, the food was wonderful and the service was excellent. The second time, the food was still good, but the service was awkward. This weekend, I went with my sisters and mother because my sister could not stop talking about the white chocolate bread pudding she had there several years ago. To avoid being too long-winded, here's the short version: - Waitress was rude and service was bad. Asked where my drink was (that I'd ordered 30 minutes prior) the waiter responded snottily "It's on it's way, ma'am." Received it 10 minutes after that. - The spinach salad was gritty - The BBQ'd shrimp overcooked and the sauce was uninteresting. - The oysters were the absolute worst! Sitting in a gelatinous muck and topped with dry, tasteless sawdust...er...I mean breadcrumbs. It became the running joke at the table- tricking someone into trying them and then laughing as they would almost gag trying to swallow it (Sadly, I fell for it.) - Finally, and worst of all, the white chocolate bread pudding was nothing like we remembered. There was barely a hint of white chocolate flavor. Mostly, it just tasted like egg. For being such a famous and self-important restaurant, they sure had a rag-tag group of waitstaff when we were there. Most of them were very young, and not too professional. One of the waiters looked as if he hadn't run a comb through his hair all day and the hostess was laying her head on the hostess stand between guests. Since it is such an institution and a Brennan restaurant, they're always going to have the tourists and suckers that will go there because of reputation alone (heck, we fell for it!) But, I'd hazard a guess that the locals and people who know better aren't going back. So, I'm very frustrated. Frustrated that we wasted all that money going to this overpriced restaurant. Frustrated that the service and food has gotten so bad. But most of all, I'm frustrated that I wasted precious room in my stomach for this lousy place when there are SO many more wonderful restaurants in New Orleans. Hopefully, I've spared at least one of you from making the same mistake.

text: It's kind of funny I waited until now to review First Wok. Had I done it a month ago, it would have received a 4 out of 5 from me. However, after some changes made in the last month, it has now dropped to 2 out of 5. I have been going to First Wok for a couple fo years. Co-workers and I used to go once a week until we moved into a new sight that was too far away from First Wok. As a result, I usually go twice a week or so between my two jobs and get the buffet to go. This had worked great until the above mention changes, which I will get into now. The three main buffet items I get were the General Tso's chicken, the orange chicken, and the First Wok chicken (chicken in a sauce that tasted like a combination of Soy and BBQ). First, for some odd reason, First Wok only offers General Tso's chicken on certain nights. It used to be an every other night pattern, but about a month ago it has turned into more of a "when we feel like it" schedule. This was a drag as it is really good, but as long as they had the orange chicken and the First Wok chicken, it wasn't a big deal. Second, about three weeks ago, the First Wok chicken disappeared and was replaced by Burbon Chicken. I've eaten burbon chicken before, and this does not taste anything like that. It isn't bad, but the fact that I have no idea what the sauce is made from is a bit disappointing. Again, not a big deal as long as the orange chicken is there and the General Tso's is there once in a while. Third, and this one isn't related to the buffet selection, about two weeks ago, the carryout containers got significantly smaller. This was total crap considering that they are still charging the same price as before. The old containers were enough for a full meal. The new ones, pardon the pun, are so small I'm hungry again in an hour. Look, I have perfected the art of filling these containers to the point where they just barely close, but this is crazy that I have to do this to get a full meal. It is also sad that for the same price I can go to any number of places nearby (non-buffet) and get a full meal, but I like variety, so the buffet is more of an appealing choice. The final straw was going by three nights ago. Big shock, no General Tso's chicken. Big shock, still no First Wok chicken, just the "burbon" chicken. Big shock...no orange chicken. It had been replaced by some kind of chicken I have never heard of before. I ended up leaving with a container of rice and noodles because there was nothing else available that I would eat. I really hope someone that works there reads this. If you don't want to go back to the old containters, fine. At least bring back the food that people like. Believe me, I'm not the only one that feels this way. You get one more chance, then I'm taking my business to one of the five other chineese places that are within three miles of your place.

text: On August 12, 2010 my husband and I had one of the most phenomenal dining experiences of our lives at Capital Grill Indianapolis. This experience was entirely due to the warm, kind nature of our extraordinary server, Jason Angus and his assistant waiter Alberto. Due to the busy nature of the restaurant, we were initially going to Capital Grill for the food, not the service. The service, however, is was what will make us go back! While our table was not ready at our reservation time, our hungry pallets helped us quickly forget this usually important detail. We were immediately greeted by Jason who had a happy smile on his face and a genuine expression in his voice. (Even though it was 8 pm and he had been working many long hours already.) Jason did a fabulous job of explaining the menu to us and answering all of our questions. He did not pressure us to order every course, nor did he suggest the most expensive item on the menu as "his favorite." I have to admit, I was almost embarrassed it was our first time and that we were there for a celebration. (We were not your "typical" Capital Grille guests ordering bottles of wine and lots of lobster and fillet.) Despite this factor, Jason still treated us as his most important guests of the evening. He was very honest about portion sizes and quantities, often mentioning that things were big enough for sharing. Jason was extremely attentive to our dining needs and worked perfectly with his companion Alberto. Our water glasses were always filled and you better believe they never let a crumb sit on the table for less than 3 minutes. While Jason and Alberto were extremely attentive, they still allowed us to enjoy each-other''s company &we definitely enjoyed a private dining experience. They never interrupted us and waited until after each conversation to ask us about our food or potential needs. Jason did not blink two eye lashes when I ordered inexpensive glasses of wine and he only treated my husband and I with the up-most respect. (Even though we are a younger couple.) The chocolate hazelnut cake per Jason's & Alberto's suggestion was amazing and it was even more special with the Happy Birthday message. The Capital Grille experience is still fresh in our minds, even 5 days later. This is all because of Jason, his phenomenal service and the delicious food of course! I was more than impressed and I look forward to going to The Capital Grille in the near future. I will also be entertaining guests there, now that I know about the amazing food and service. Two words: Thank you.

text: Does anyone remember a time when Cosi used to be X and O? X and O was a sandwich shop by day, and then a make-your-own s'mores and drink tasty coffee drinks, happening kind of evening. Dim lighting, lots of long tables for large parties, open late for the overzealous caffeinated pretties. Until some people started calling it "Xando" - pronounced "ZAAAANDO" - and the cringe heard around the world when someone would even suggest going there was enough to bring the evenings of tableside chocolate, marshmallows, and graham crackers to a screeching halt. No more X and O. No more Xando. No more late night. Hi, Cosi. So Cosi did it's thing. The pretties still came in looking for the old digs, but a friendly menu stating that s'mores and pizza and fondue and other former staples of X and O would still be available - just during the daytime. But what happened was this: people realized that for some odd reason, all of those delectable late-night dishes only tasted good after hours. Believe me, I tried the s'mores thing one time at lunch. You try going back to work with burnt marshmallow all over your face. Then Cosi put out free samples of their bread. By the time you were done waiting in line for your salad or sandwich, you'd already partaken in the equivalent of four pieces of bread. Oily, no grain, obviously very tasty bread. But the salad and sandwiches were quite good and you got your 10th for free. Then Cosi did the unmentionable. They downgraded their chicken. It went from actual good tasting grilled chicken to the kind of chicken you'd find swimming inside McNuggets. Gooey, sometimes unchewable, definitely not fresh or grilled, but easy to prepare. And cheaper to make. So what did I do then? Almost forgetting completely my days of latte sipping and midnight dipping, I ordered salads. And I switched from the chicken salad to a "make your own". I didn't care that it was $7.50. I didn't care that I couldn't even enjoy the free bread anymore (I had made a pact with myself that it was grain or wheat bread or I don't eat it) and I didn't care that when I did bother to order a sandwich, I noticed that there wasn't much *in* it, just lots and lots of bread! I did care, however, when a huge insect peered up at me as I was eating my salad one day. I went right back to Cosi, showed them the salad and my new friend, Buggie O'Caterpillar, and asked for a new salad. They happily obliged...and then charged me another $7.50! When I told them I had exchanged it because of an insect in my food, they were none too thrilled to hear it. And perhaps I would have forgiven the whole thing had it not happened again the very next week. Except this time it was a very small, very dark curly hair. I didn't even bother to bring it back, and only returned to this Cosi to get a coffee to go.

All of our food was bland, unseasoned and flat out boring. My shrimp were soggy...and they look to be breaded but they were supposed to be grilled. Our appetizer (the shrimp artichoke dip) was OK. It wasn't blowing me away but it wasn't terrible once we salt and peppered it. My crab cake was OK and my asparagus were just OK as well. I was supremely disappointed in the shrimp. For the money, it should be at least edible. I didn't finish them. I also got "green onion mashed potatoes"...um, they tasted out of a box. I hope they aren't but again, bland and no taste. :( I tried my husband's arctic char, which our server recommended. He got it blackened but it was downright flavorless. He ate everything b/c he can't stand to waste, but I would have probably sent it back. I wanted to speak to the manager, but my hubby was ready to go. He doesn't like it when I complain in public. I just thought he should know, so I filled out the review sheet in our bill. I hope they read it....I don't want anything in return, but I do want them to know that this is not the kind of food you want for that price. Our bill with tip was $81 and I feel like the only thing worth the cash was Kristin. She deserved a tip but I might as well have just caught my money on fire. The last time I said I should have gone to Bonefish. I should have taken my own advice or driven to Red Lobster...yep, that's right. I would have rather eaten Red Lobster than Mitchell's. :( BOOOOO :(. EDITED TO ADD: The comment card was read and the manager called me immediately. They offered me a gift card to come back, so we will be giving it another shot. I really want to have a good experience here. I will let you Yelpers know what happens. I didn't expect anything for free, but it's nice that he is making an effort. For that, I will give it another star. They deserve it. The service and management are outstanding, obviously! I am very happy with that kind of response.

If you haven't noticed the price here was more expensive, but since they raised prices across the street, you're getting more for your money here. Plus the hot bread is still just as good! 2. If you wanted to have a relatively quiet date night out in Center City, this location offers more privacy on weekends than the original. No more drunk kids interrupting your conversations! (although I was the drunk kid more often than not) Its just nice not having to grind other customers (or vice versa) to get to your seat... unless you're into that type of thing. 3. text: I was recommended to The Grotto by a colleague while in town for business. She has great taste so I headed off here with a group after work. We parked in a parallel parking spot covered in fallen fall colored leaves (don't get that in San Diego!) and were greeted by the hostess at a candle lit stand on the side entrance. There are two floors; the front room was full so we were seated upstairs. There weren't any diners up there but it was private and had a faux fireplace. When I first checked out the menu, I was taken aback. Pizzas, pastas, steaks...and sushi? But don't let it stop you!! After a disastrous PA sushi night over the weekend, I stayed away from the sushi but perhaps its good? Can't comment... The focaccia that served was pretty oily and tasted almost fried. So we kind of picked at that. But the wine menu was good. I had a Spanish Sauvignon Blanc that was good. For my main entree I had the Petit Filet with "Crisp Portabello Fries, Sautéed Baby Spinach, Country Smashed Potatoes." I asked what the portabello fries were and was told they were slices of a large portabello that were tempura battered and fried (the Asian theme came out here). I asked for the mushrooms to not be fried instead though. My dish was excellent - the meat was well flavored and perfectly cooked to order. The filet had a smoky bacon flavor. The smashed potatoes were topped with garlic spinach which was topped with the meat. I will upload a picture. My colleague got the same thing but switched the mushrooms for bok choy (Asian theme again!) and loved hers as well. The other two in our party got the Chicken Parmagian (wasn't sure why they spelled it this way?) and the Grilled New York Strip with Homefried Potatoes, Asparagus, and Truffle Gravy. They both said they liked their food, but not ask much as we did with the filet!!! Highly recommended!

I again explained that I had made the reservation days ago and that no my aging parents would not prefer to "squeeze" into a double bed as he suggested. I had requested two king rooms and that was what I expected to receive. After much back and forth, the manager and I came to a compromise and I was able to get a king room for my parents and keep a double for myself. Needless to say, not a good start to the weekend. Harrah's in Reno used to be a grand hotel. Unfortunately now, like most of Reno it is falling into disrepair. The hotel looked as if it hadn't been updated since the late '80's, the air conditioning in the casino was lacking and the unit in the room rumbled throughout the night disturbing my sleep. The bed (a double since I wasn't given the king that I requested) was too hard. Reno itself has become quite the ghost town as evident by the various boarded up businesses and casinos (se la vie Fitzgerald), I suppose proving that this once Boom Town is not immune to the weakened economy or the strength of the Indian Casinos now peppered throughout northern California. At this point, I see no reason in returning unless there is a specific event going on. And if I do, it will NOT be to Harrah's.

text: August was amazing. We ordered the four course tasting menu with the wine pairing at $90 per person. Well worth it. The meal started with a complementary egg, buttery custard(?) not exactly sure what it was.. served in an eggshell, and white wine. The first course was confit of duck leg en gelée, a mushroom salad and duck liver mousse. The second course was my favorite of the four. We had a butter roasted gulf grouper, fresh shell beans in tarragon vinaigrette and candied fennel. The flavors were seemingly very different, but worked so well to make the dish devine! The wine also went extremely well and complemented all the flavors. Our third course was a slow cooked pork, polenta, and braised kale. The pork belly was slightly heavy, but in a small enough portion to enjoy. It was also topped with a citrus salad that made an excellent balance. Our final dish was, of course, dessert! It was bittersweet crème au chocolat, caramelized white chocolate, cocoa meringues and hazelnuts. A possible deconstructed smore, if you will. It was served with a sparkling red wine. Delicious! I'm not particular to very sweet desserts, and this was quite perfect. They also brought out complimentary peanut brittle and chocolate ganache before bringing out the check. My date and I were thoroughly satisfied, with the food, the experience, the service, everything.

text: I am actually writing a review for the City of Santa Barbara -- not the airport as the other 2 reviewers have written. On our last trip to the Bay Area, we stopped in Santa Barbara for lunch. It was a late lunch and it was hard to find a restaurant open at 3pm, however, with the help of my friend who was behind his computer and was on yelp frantically trying to find us a restaurant to eat at, we headed towards the restaurant, found a spot to park and went to eat our lunch. When we finished our lunch, we walked to the car which was parked just across the street. When hubby got to the car, he took something off the windshield wipers -- it was a parking ticket. WTF????? We were not there longer than the 70 minutes allotted. Heck, we hadn't even been there an hour. Then we checked the ticket and the person cited us for parking in the spot at 2.24pm. WTF? We weren't even in Santa Barbara at that time. We were still on the road. We didn't even get to that spot until a few minutes past 3pm since we were looking for a place which was still open after 3pm for lunch. It was at that moment I decided to contest the ticket. Luckily, the police department was a few blocks away. I walked into the police dept and told the person on duty what happened. She stared at me blankly and asked "so you wish to contest this?" I said yes. She hands me a form to fill out. While there, a few other people came in to do the same thing -- contest their parking ticket. Man, what is wrong with this city? What is wrong with the traffic person they have on duty giving out tickets to people who weren't even in the city yet? Crazy!! I finished filling out the form and even gave them a copy of our receipt from the restaurant as evidence. They told me about 6-8 weeks. So I had already forgotten about this ticket until I got a letter in the mail from the City of Santa Barbara. They decided to accept my contested ticket and hence I didn't have to pay for it, but the thing is if they had hired more efficient employees, this wouldn't even have happened in the first place. But then if I did have to pay for the ticket I would never return to SB ever again and they wouldn't have received that extra star!

text: Normally, I'm like the Doug character on Weeds, "I hate f***ing chains!" But some friends of the wifeski gave us a gift card, so what's more appealing than free food, right? The wife's chicken was dry and charred, and lacking flavor. Her Caesar dressing was El Blando! I got a taste of my sons baked beans and it was déjà vu of Van De Camps Pork & Beans! text: My advise is to keep looking. My son was enrolled there for 6 months, it was a regretful experience. He's now happy to be back at his original daycare, Kids R Kids. I HIGHLY recommend you go there, it's just right down the street. The only reason I moved him was because of a conflict I was having with another mother after she hit my car. Thank God, I came to my senses! I'll try to keep this short. Small Strides is VERY cramped, there is not much room for the kids to run around & play. A few of the class rooms are a little more spacious, but that wasn't the case for my son. Be prepared to make all the lunches, have your child come home ABSOLUTELY filthy, to the point you have to change their entire outfit just to run to the store. It's bad! It's not my son or his age either. I have no problems with that at all now. They don't listen to your concerns, they just carry on w/ their way of doing things & give you a million excuses. They allowed my 16 month old son (at the time) to have 4 hour naps on a daily basis & he was only there 6-7 hours daily. So needless to say, he had problems sleeping at night. He was WAY to old for the room they kept him in. The age limit maxed out @ 15 months then he was to move to the other class room w/ his age group. He was in the baby room from 15 months to 21 months, till I pulled him out!!! There is nothing wrong w/ his development. He's developing perfectly & is having no problems "adjusting". The problem wasn't my son, it was a worker named Crystal whom I had an AWFUL experience with. From day one she ignored me, was extremely impersonal, not to mention my son HATED to be alone with her. Red flags!!! My son is so mellow and easy going. As a new parent coming in she could've attempted the "wow" factor. She is the reason my son never advanced and I'm SO mad at her for that!!! The original excuse for putting him back in the baby room was because he wasn't walking yet. I understand that. 3 weeks later he was walking & should have moved up! There are so many other minor dislikes, but that was the final straw for me. Also, be prepared to supply tons and tons of wipes. They don't use towels, apparently or hand soap. They use your wipes to wipe their hands off before & after the diaper change, that's 4-5 wipes for one change. Then they use them to wipe down tables, high chairs, etc. I've seen them do it & I asked about it. Several parents have complained. Finally, in the baby room, there is a VERY small room w/ a huge metal door that they call the sleeping room. I call it the closet. It has all the cribs in it, they blast lullaby music or white noise, shut the sound proof door & call it nap time. Remember the 4 hour naps? These little angels aren't asleep majority of the time. They look frightened and restless and like they want out! I've addressed it several times. I was told everything from, "oh, they just woke up" to "their parents want them trained to be in a crib & they just don't like it , they're adjusting." Whatever! Some of them would scream and scream, it'd break your heart. No wonder my son cried and cried during drop off. The staff over all seems very nice and knowledgeable. Just be aware that many of these young ladies are not mothers themselves and I feel they have a hard time really relating. Ryan is a first time owner, not a mother herself. I think she does have a passion for children, she just needs more hands on experience.

I'll admit I did feel a bit like I was in a museum when I saw the cooler in the back labeled "dressed rabbits" and "alligator meat." After waiting for the two or three customers ahead of me to be served, I opted for catfish steak, $3.49/lb. The prices seemed reasonable, given the freshness of the seafood and all the options to choose from (catfish fillets or catfish steak, farm-raised or wild salmon, two different types of tuna...) When I cooked the catfish two days later, it still tasted fresh. Little's Fish Company is a colorful alternative to buying seafood at a corporate supermarket. text: I will give only two compliments to 10 Arts. The first goes to Jen, who mingled with the crowd on New Year's eve. She was delightful, gracious and posed for photos for everyone. And the second goes to the pasty chef for beignets that reminded me of New Orleans. However, our dinner was an absolutely overpriced disaster. The abridged New Year's menu was eye-gougingly expensive and the quality was mediocre at best. The service was atrocious. Dishes were plopped down on our table by random runners, with no explanation as to what was being served. The waiter was never there when they cleared the plates, presumably so that he didn't have to ask how the food was. I had to flag him down across the restaurant to ask questions about my food. The portions were laughably tiny. The foie gras serving was lilliputian. When I managed to complain about the foie gras (after tracking down said errant waiter), the waiter informed me that foie gras "is expensive" and that is why the portion is small. Well no shit foie gras is expensive, but seriously the serving was approximately one teaspoon. When I think of giant servings of foie gras enjoyed by me in Chef Ripert's native France, I cringe. The entree was awful. I had the short rib ravioli. It was chewy, bitter and lukewarm. If I had not been so damn hungry by that point I would have sent it back. How Eric Ripert has amassed the reptutation he has baffles me. Maybe at one point this was a stellar restaurant. But, clearly the restaurant decided to do a half-ass job on what they presumed would be a tourist-filled New Year's eve celebration (i.e. no chance for repeat business). What is really sad, is that I know for a fact the food can be decent as we spent a week at the Ritz and really enjoyed the lounge food (two thumbs up for: fish sandwich, hot dog and lobster roll). It is criminal to charge $500 for a meal that is prepared with such disdain for the customer. But that wasn't even the worst part. The worst was waking up in the middle of the night vomiting due to what I presume to be sub-par oysters. Good thing I had asked the waiter if they were fresh. Never again... In summation, avoid the restaurant. Stick to the lounge. Tell Jen to find new employment.

text: The hotel is beautiful and is an incredible venue to hold a wedding; which is why we chose it. However, this place can not continue it's current business model and survive over the next few years. They lost thousands of dollars comp'ing us for their mistakes. In fact, their propensity to make mistakes was the only consistency in their performance. I'll leave several reviews because there were a few shining moments. Let this be my culminating moment for you to remember from my review -- as my bride stood at the back of the aisle, she stopped and waited for the appropriate music ("Here Comes the Bride") to start, and as all of our guests were standing, I had to leave my place at the front (yeah, I'm the groom) and go instruct the AV technician on what song to be played (as they played the wrong one for a bit) and when ("when" being a couple of minutes ago). This was not due to lack of preparation or guidance on our part, the AV tech was holding the written instructions in his hand when I approached him. Catering ***** (five stars) The reception dinner was fantastic! We ordered the combination plate with beef and chicken and everyone's food arrived hot and tasty, but what really set the catering apart was what they did for our guests with allergies. Our two guests who had to eat vegetarian, lactose, and glucose free meals were treated to a delicious entree that they said was absolutely delicious. They were also served fruit salad for desert and not left high and dry when everyone else was eating cake. Speaking of cake, our wedding cake was spectacular! After we got it back to the room we ate it for breakfast the next morning. The catering was the highlight of everything the hotel did. Wedding Coordinator ___ (zero stars) We dealt with multiple coordinators. One quit or got fired, another one told us that because our primary coordinator was on vacation that she didn't want to help us because we weren't her priority. Finally after being jockeyed around so much we told them we were going to leave and go to the Hermitage, the Opryland assigned a manager to do our wedding. I'm sure she's a good person and means well, but I have to say she was out of her league. Yes, she did send a lot of emails, mostly because it would take her 3 or 4 emails to answer the questions I would send in one (yes, I would have to send subsequent emails to say she hadn't answered all the questions). I could go on and on and on about how incompetent the wedding staff is, but they (the managers at Opryland) know that it is an incredible wedding venue and that you are going to use them only once (in theory), so they aren't overly invested in your particular event. Valet ___(zero stars) This has been reviewed several times and they are, of note, still an abysmal failure. A few of the staff even admitted their embarrassment of being a part of such of a joke. They have a tendency to lose your car, pull it to the wrong side of the hotel, just forget to retrieve it after you call, or sometimes fail to give you the key (for cars with push-button starts, wherein the valet can walk away and you get to wait for him to return so you can take your car out of park). Seriously, talking about the valet is like kicking a dead horse, and the fact that Gaylord employees are allowed to conduct such a clown show does not speak highly of Gaylord. ...on another note, make sure you argue parking prices. If the hotel validates parking for guest who come to eat at one of the many delicious restaurants at the hotel, then they should validate your wedding guests' parking also. I'm speaking in reference to guests who are not staying at the hotel and just need parking for the reception. Hotel Staff ***** (five stars) The bellman, waiters, waitresses, hostess, receptionist, etc... were all phenomenal and worthy of high praise. They all try so hard, and are truly sorry when it doesn't go correctly. Overall I'd still recommend it, but watch them like a hawk and apologize to your guests up front. Opryland will punt it into the stands -- bank on it. Here are some tips: Do everything with email, that way when they don't follow through, you can prove it. Make the email extremely simple for them to understand. I even did a power point presentation with pictures, highlighting and arrows and they still couldn't answered the numbered questions. Have them do a price break out every step of the way. They will do it wrong.
label: NEG

text: I had a very nice dinner here tonight. We started with the huevos rolls which had all kinds of rich savory goodness, including chicken and black bean. I've had this sort of "southwest style egg roll" before, but I thought this was nicely done. I think the salsa had some cucumber in it too, which was pretty nice. I split the Alex's salad with someone else, and I chose the cilantro vinaigrette, which was a little sweet and had an Asian feel to it. I'd definitely get that again if I the chance. For the entree, I had the salmon special. The server told us that it was Norwegian, which she confirmed to be wild. It was very good - it didn't have that overly fattiness of the farmed stuff. It came with this cold wild rice salad with cranberries in it - I think I like it better than the salmon. The sides were also great - we ordered the tequila beans and the mac & cheese. The mac and cheese were good, but I thought the tequila beans were REALLY good. Nice rich barbecue style sauce that wasn't overly sweet - although I admit not really detecting the tequila. So with one appetizer, a split salad (which was plenty), an entree each (one salmon, one prime rib), two sides, one glass of wine and two glasses of Blue Moon (mmmmmmmmm), the bill came to about $90 before tips. Louge singer was good, but I felt like I was listening to Peter Faulk in "Shark Tale." Service was good but sort of antagonistic. When asked if the kitchen had wheat free pasta for someone in our party who had a gluten allergy, the server replied, "Ha, no...this is a real Italian restaurant." I wanted to ask "so does being a real Italian restaurant mean the staff is insensitive to food allergies?" But I let the comment go. The server's attitude was pleasant enough-just overly cocky for the service provided and the venue. The pre-bussing was good, but the bus boy forgot or didn't want to replace several utensils after removing dirty ones. The food was good, but overall light on flavor. -The calamari appetizer was great. -The seared scallops on the nightly special were fantastic but the dish's sauce was a little light on flavor. -The prawn and ravioli special was excellent -The chicken Caesar was just okay -The shrimp pasta Alfredo was rich and hearty -The wine: we ordered the 3rd least expensive Chianti on the list (about $30) and it was not very good-I will never understand why restaurants put poor quality wines on their lists just to satisfy a price point. -The deserts (Tiramisu, Chocolate Gelato and chocolate cake) were all excellent, but the coffee was weak and dishwater-esque. Price: A little pricey for what you get. Overall we decided it was good enough to return, but I'm not itching to get back.

text: When my sister who's also my Maid Of Honor told me we would be going wine tasting in Santa Barbara for my bachelorette weekend I was overjoyed! We instantly went on Yelp and started hunting for the most cost effective wine tour company with great reviews. We landed at Captain Jacks. My sister called up Jack (who's apparently much easier to get ahold of when you're paying), she booked the tour for nine and we were on our way! The van picked us up at our hotel and to our surprise there was only room for 8, meaning only 8 seatbelts. Yet Captain Jack gladly took our payment for 9 girls. We get to our first winery and everything was fine and dandy, we all pile in the car to head to the second winery when my sister and I received the scariest phone call of our lives. Our parents had been in a rollover accident and they're both being rushed to the hospital. We immediatelyreturned to the hotel where they were the epitome of class and compassion and only charged us for cleaning fee for that day and refunded our money for the night. The driver from Captain Jacks was also very understanding and told us not to worry, that as long as we explained our situation we should get some sort of refund. Days later my sister called Captain Jack and explained the situation. He merely offers a $175 gift certificate for a future visit. My biggest question is why on earth would we return to an establishment who's unwilling to work with it's customers during a time of tragedy. In complete disbelief I asked my fiancé to talk to Captain Jack. He spoke to someone named Andrew who brought up Disneyland as an example. He stated that if we were to visit Disneyland and hadan emergency and had to leave, they wouldn't refund our money. He dismissed the example as a pathetic attempt to make a comparison with no validity. He then asked to speak to Captain Jack but Andrew told him he had left for the day. My Fiance called the following day 4 times with no luck getting a hold of Jack. When my Fiance spoke to Andrew again he explained that any refund would've been accepted and appreciated. I'm dissapointed that a business with zero ethics can still be in business. Please make sure your family is safe and sound in a bubble before giving this company your money because you will be left high and dry in the case of an emergency.

text: I'm getting kind of tired of hearing people compare Sugarhouse to walmart. I don't think it's a fair comparison, and I think it shows that the critic had made up their mind in advance. New carpet gets fuzz, new dealers have a learning curve, new kitchens have missteps. You can't just recreate Vegas at the drop of a hat. The marketing and hype of a casino can't match the reality of the situation They have a long way to go. The servers are far better than many casino's I've been to, and aren't your typical small casino b-team. They are far too few, and you'll be lucky to get one drink an hour. They do comp drinks to players, unlike Harrah's. The location is an island right now. It's near enough to Northern Liberties and Fishtown, but I-95 and Delaware Ave are a pretty wide gulf. They don't have enough table games, so the minimums are too high. $25 blackjack minimums both times I went. I tried the video blackjack, but after winning on one visit and losing on the other, I'd rather play at a table. I signed up for the card, but they'll only give you a sign-up bonus if you already have a premium card from another casino. I didn't try the bar or restaurant, I don't see the point, they look like stadium food. As far as the crowd goes, it's a casino. Complaining about the crowd in a casino is like complaining about hipsters in a gastropub, or whiskey faced oldheads in a dive. They're part of the background, deal with it. A local casino doesn't get to send the undesirables home on buses before dark. They also don't have to provide the all-day amenities of a gambling destination.

She barely buffed them. She forgot the base coat - I had to ask for it The whole process from start to finish took 15 minutes. Quality right there, ladies and gentlemen. My friend's polish was globbed on. It was so thick every other nail had air bubbles in it. She was too irritated to ask for a correction. My pedicure and my sister's pedicure were equally as ridiculous. The used the same dull cuticle scissors, didn't sanitize the chairs in between each customer. Repeat all problems stated above. I don't expect a nail salon in a mall to posh and luxurious. What I do expect is competent technicians using sanitary tools. I am so pissed. I will never go back again. If I could I would shut the place down. This place is a fucking joke. And yeah, I know what you're thinking. We should have just left after my friend got her manicure done. But we didn't. We were stupid and in denial. Never again... never again...

text: I can't believe anyone would give this place a bad review. The food is amazing and it's CHEAP! The line out the door that ebbs and flows should tell you something - people don't wait in line for bad food, you know? I've always been a Maximum Burrito kind of girl (rice and beans) or a taco salad with their tasty vinaigrette dressing, but I recently tried the Fish Tacos. In a word: YUM!!! I even posted up on facebook about how delicious they were and was immediately chastised by many friends for not already knowing this secret! Well shame on me, because they're now my favorite item. Try the pineapple salsa on your burrito - it's definitely one of their stand-out flavors. If I had a complaint, I would say that the place is usually a little dirty. They're so busy making burritos that cleaning tables slips to the bottom of their to-do list. Just don't go wearing nice clothes, or you may be upset when you dip your elbow in some salsa!

text: Coop's is where the locals tell you to go for the best damn jamb, and there's a reason for that. Go early if you don't want to wait but even if you have to, it's well worth your effort. Say hi to "Stella", the adorable feline and order the Supreme Jambalaya, which is the best meal I've ever had in New Orleans, probably the best in my life. Absolutely delicious, filled with nubbins of rabbit, sausage, chicken, etc...SO deeply flavorful and immensely filling with such a huge portion. Our server usually is a slightly sardonic lady with a great sense of humor, and she fits the place perfectly. HIGHLY recommended. You truly soak up New Orleans' flavor and attitude here.

text: Although the food is quite good, I strongly recommend only ever eating there in-person. As is the case with many Chinese restaurants, there is a large language barrier: it is difficult to understand what the person on the phone is saying, and the person on the phone does not always understand your order. Unlike most Chinese restaurants, Su Xing will not fix its delivery order mistakes. In one order, they forgot our rice. We called asking them to deliver the rice, and we think their response was that they would fix it next time. Whatever it was, their solution was not to deliver the rice that was supposed to be part of the meal we paid for. In what became our last delivery order with them, I requested a side of white rice. Mindful of the problems with the previous order, I asked them to repeat the order back to me several times. I could not understand what was said back to me, but I thought it sounded close. Since I had repeated the order multiple times to them, I thought they probably had repeated the correct order to me. They delivered an order of vegetable fried rice, a dish I do not like (their peas are not cooked enough for my taste), and a more expensive dish. We called to tell them the delivery was wrong. They did not fix the order, they offered no refund, and they blamed the miscommunication on me. We paid for food we didn't eat. Su Xing did not care. We will not order delivery from this place again. Due to their lack of concern for their customers, we probably won't be stopping by in-person either.
label: NEG

text: I've visited these guys twice now. The first time was for the "pre-opening" party, it's in quotes because it was open to the public which pretty much means you're open. Right? The second time was Monday of this week for lunch. For the first visit I ordered five small plates from the limited menu they were offering at the time. Mini Beef Brochettes, Scallops in Cognac Sauce, "Empanada Madness", Oyster Shooters and Bruschetta. The food was decent with a few disappointments... One scallop was overcooked and two were undercooked. They were topped with Tobiko which wasn't listed on the menu description. I think raw ingredients should be listed without a doubt. The empanadas include one cheese, one pork and one chicken. The meats were nondescript and the cheese was basically nonexistent. Oyster shooters were incredibly spicy from black pepper. I like hot food and they made me gasp a bit from the pepper. My friend just about had to spit hers out. The bruschetta was as good as any I've had with nothing really special to it. Mini Beef Skewers were tiny tiny pieces of meat, cooked well and tasty. They're served with mushroom risotto which was the best part of the meal, rich and creamy as it should be. Service on this visit left a lot to be desired. Our server returned about four times to confirm our order. She wrote it down the first time but apparently either her or the kitchen had no clue what it was supposed to mean. When we ordered Pinot Grigio from the menu she must have thought we were speaking Chinese from the look on her face. She walked away before we could explain and came back to ask again what we wanted for drinks. I order a Great Basin Icky and she was stumped again..... For my second visit I stopped for lunch and ordered "Ducktastic". Description off the menu- "Duck confit over arugula with mushrooms and roasted vegetables in hoisin balsamic dressing". Mine was served with mixed greens, not straight arugula. The roasted vegetables were cooked and seasoned well. Unfortunately the duck confit, which should be the star of the dish, was buried beneath piles of canned mandarin oranges. The oranges were unexpected from a place that claims they have a "Chef driven menu using local ingredients". Canned mandarin oranges are okay for some things. In this dish they were way off with their level of sweetness and metallic aftertaste. They ruined the flavors of everything else. Almost seems like they made this salad and said "Hey, this needs more color, let's throw some oranges on there!". The service this time was fine. Our server was prompt and polite, only stopped by when needed and had everything to us as ordered. Only comment I could make is that since we were sitting outside and it was sunny he was wearing sunglasses. Can't blame him too much as I had my shades on as well but it's still a little unprofessional. To be honest I was really hoping for a stellar meal from these guys. After browsing the menu before they opened it seemed very adventurous, maybe too much so. It's rare that a restaurant can pull of the variety of dishes that they offer and do it well. That's why we don;t see many places like this in Reno. It's worth a shot for another trip as nothing was too terrible to keep me from coming back but it won't be my first pick anytime soon.
label: NEG

text: What a disappointment. When this St. Louis spinoff first started up in Indy, it showed some real promise. But now, after several years serving the same corner in downtown Indianapolis, it has skunk into mediocrity, and that just the food. Poor, inattentive, although friendly service and watered down drinks makes it the perfect place for only high school graduation parties. Is this place in survival mode or do the owners don't care any more? If it's the former, than the only way for this place to make it is to get back to the basics - good food - great service. If it the latter, go back to St. Louis and reopen a fast food restaurant in its location. At least the food would be cheaper.

text: Figured I should review some delivery places. Really, it's more important than anything else to students in West Philly. Chinese food, like almost everything else, has one food that I always order. General Tsao's chicken. Original? No. But it gets the job done. So, just as any Mexican food rated by me primarily for its quesadillas, Chinese delivery must be rated for its General Tsao's chicken. And, I must tell, you, Beijing has absolutely the WORST General Tsao's chicken I've ever had. It's shockingly bad. I would think that something terrible must have happened the night I have it, and try it again, just to find it just as awful. The chicken is somehow both dry and pasty, with not even a remote taste of chicken. The sauce is... mildly spicy, but the only flavor is vague spiciness. Really, I could barely choke the stuff down. So why does Beijing get a second star from me? Because, in its atrociousness, it managed to help me find a second dish I could order from bad American Chinese food delivery places - Sweet & Sour Chicken. Which was adequate. So, when others ordered from Beijing, I had something I could eat. You've been warned about the General Tsao's. Only reason to buy it is if you're going to chemically analyze what it's made of, because that is NOT chicken.

text: I remember a friend of mine telling me this place was good. Why didn't I listen to her before? Located in Glenside on Keswick Ave; this is a hidden gem amongst the junky little stores that surround it. The food here is so good! Traditional Greek is hard to come by. Warm flatbread was served with the Tzatziki appetizer and we should have stopped there. But no, we each got a salad, an entree ( I had the stuffed salmon special) and TWO plates of bread. text: This restaurant boasts some of the most affordable and delicious sushi in the area. Harusame is the place to go for suburbians that would like a well prepared meal of raw fish with the works, and without having to drive into the city to obtain it. The preparation is lovely, the decor is pleasing, the service is damn near impeccable, and the convenience of having a decent take out beer selection is just that - convenient as hell. I've been here several times, and have never been let down by these talented chefs. By saying that I've been burned by unfavorable sushi experiences involving not-so-fresh fish is a gross understatement. But Harusame is never in this category - they meet and surpass my tastebuds' expectations every visit. I wholeheartedly recommend this restaurant to either a sushi newcomer, or a staunch sushi connoisseur. Make the trip down Haverford Road, and you won't be disappointed! And don't be surprised if you see me there, I'm planning some trips in the near future...

text: Bad experience with this company on two occasions, but didn't know the first experience was so bad until after the second. I'll explain. Years ago this company was hired to do extensive work on a building that was being renovated for condos. Lots of brick pointing and facade work on a building that had been vacant for many years, but was beautiful nonetheless. The bill for the work was huge, but just a few years later new residents were having lots of water problems. The roof was blamed over and over, but it was not the roof. The pointing in the rear of the building was so poorly done it was shocking. Later it was recalled that an early resident overheard a foreman (from WM Proud) on the job telling the crew to just make the first two floors look good and that no one would notice the work (or lack of work) on the upper floors looking up from the street. Turned out the whole building had to be redone, it wasn't just the back that was done poorly all of it was bad. This company was paid a fortune for this job. Before this problem was uncovered I had personally hired them to do some facade work and cleaning on a building and the consultant could not have been nicer, more helpful or accessible while I was deciding on whether or not to sign the contract. Once I signed he was gone and I was stuck with a guy who showed up when he wanted (even though it was promised that they would schedule times to perform work and show up on time). The work was started then stopped, started and then stopped. About 95% finished and then I had to beg them to come back and finish the work. I thought maybe I had just been unlucky or not much of a priority because the second job was small (although not inexpensive), but then when I discovered that the work they performed just a few years ago on the first project had to be completely redone and what had been said about only paying attention to the lower floors I felt compelled to write this review. The company has cost a lot of people a lot of money and wasted energy when it was not necessary. I will never use them again or recommend them obviously.

text: Western Cycle has a huge selection of bicycles and bicycle related items such as helmets, kneepads, spare parts, etc. Some of the brands that the store carries are Norco, Chariot, and Gore. The selection of bikes is one of the best in town. Whether you are looking for a bike to ride in parks, on the mountain trails or on extreme roads in extreme conditions, this store has got your back. Sales associates are knowledgeable and friendly. I came in for no particular reason, just to see what this huge bike has to offer, and had the most pleasant conversation with one of the sales people. I let him know in advance that at the moment I was not looking to buy a bike but would consider doing so in the future, and he was nice enough to show me store's selection and explain features of the bikes I took interested in. Prices range from fair to ridiculous. I would say that Western Cycle's prices are comparable to those at Revolution Cycle on Stony Plain road. I did notice some sales, but they weren't significant enough to be considered a steal or a great deal. Lots of sports clothes were on sale too but I didn't have a close enough look to comment on the selection.

It's also a nice place to watch a game with a group of people. We watched the last game of the Stanley Cup here. The food is good and the beer list more than adequate.

I have had both flavors, the green apple and the watermelon. I prefer the green apple, however the watermelon is jumpin' too! It keeps me coming back time after time. The doughnuts were great too, they are fresh and it's almost as if they melt in your mouth... but that could be a problem if you are trying to shed a pound or two. :)

text: Fantastic spot, heavy in my weekend brunch rotation. They serve brunch until 2pm, which is VERY appreciated on those especially slow weekend mornings. I almost always get some sort of egg scramble. There are usually about 4 to choose from. However they do run out of ingredients if you go late. Last time I had a goat cheese & mushroom. I believe lamb sausage and cheddar was another option. The potatoes that come with the scramble are also very well done -- lightly charred, diced in little pieces with a touch of heat. The pancakes are pretty yummy, espcially when you get them with the generous portions of fresh fruit. The menu (written on a dry-erase board) is constantly changing based on ingredients. They try to incorporate locally produced stuff as well. There is no cookie-cutter crap here. Everything is fresh and housemade with love. I also enjoy the melodic-sounding indie stuff on the speakers. I can recall hearing Beirut on more than one occasion. Last time I was here I lucked out and they gave me about 6 of their leftover homemade scones. I felt like a kid on Christmas. The scones are amazing. Delicate, not overly sweet and bursting with fresh fruit. For the rest of the day I drove around and played Scone Fairy. You see, being my friend occasionally has its perks. They give you a glass mug for coffee, which I think is strange, but whatever. There's RFTs to read, and I think they have the Sunday New York Times for sale. Prices are not cheap, but very reasonable for the quality. Overall it's a very pleasant laidback brunchy environment.

text: My food passport had the embarrassing omission of (real) Thai food and this place makes me regret not experiencing it sooner. However, as someone who has never guided his palate in this direction, I can promise anyone with hesitation that this is fantastic food and deserves a visit. The set-up: Small, but very nice, intimate dining area. As with any small BYOB it can get noisy, but I could still hear my table just fine. Unfortunately I could also hear the table next to us just fine since the tables are fairly close together, but it was nothing absurd. The food: We got the drunken chicken and chu chee duck and highly recommend trying these. The duck was slightly drier than I hoped (keyword: slightly) and more pineapple would've been nice but that's minor -- the sauce was disturbingly good and that was key. As for the drunken chicken, a good amount of heat and generous portions make it a must. We saw at least three people around us get it so it's a crowd-pleaser for sure. The bottom line: The prices are reasonable, the service was good and I will definitely be back.
