text: I've been in many quilting and fabric stores and have loved many of them for different reasons. I wish I could say that the Stitcher's Garden was loved in it's own special way, too. To say that the place is unorganized would be a nice way of putting it. I felt like it was the hoarder's garden. I was looking for specifically for a variety of kid's fabrics in fat quarters or smaller cuts...and found it here and there and again over there...and look down there, too. Why they couldn't have have grouped these together was beyond me. They sold several of these types of kits, and I was looking for 4 different ones. I did eventually find 4 unique sets, but it took some sorting and excavating before I was satisfied that I had what I needed. I checked out the patterns but quickly gave up when I couldn't find any sort of order or organization. I enjoy going to different fabric stores and seeing the different things that each one carries. It's almost like a journal for me. Unfortunately, this was my boyfriend's first experience in quilt shop hopping, and he doesn't quite see what the appeal is. He was also overwhelmed by the lack of organization in the store. I promised him that most aren't like this. One other observation that I have that is more of a personal preference than something they do wrong is that they rip their fabrics instead of cutting with scissors or a rotary cutter. I'm not going to debate on which one is best or anything, but keep this in mind if your preference leans to cutting. One positive thing that I can say is that the ladies are very sweet in the store. Maybe if I had asked for help they could have found the sets I needed faster and they know where every single piece of fabric is in the store, but I feel like I shouldn't have to ask.

text: We should've known better when A. they didn't have Vienna beef hotdogs and B. they had no standard pop. Don't get me wrong--I like Boylan's and was glad to see them. But I don't want a Black Cherry soda with my hot dog! Dog itself was 100% beef Nathan's, so that's good. And they did have the traditional Chicago Frankenrelish. But...the pickle was actually bread and butter slices, tossed in clumps on top. Waaayyy too much finely diced tomato & onion. And...the fries. I ordered cheese fries. My favorite cheese for cheese fries is that "cheese food" dip stuff, but I'm ok with real cheese melted on top. This was neither--it was a handful of pre-packaged shredded cheese thrown on top. The fries themselves were only warm (and very dry), so of course there was no melting happening. Husband's pierogi were frozen, he saw them come out of the Mrs. T's box and go into the fryer. I admit that my criteria for judging a hot dog is the Chicago style; for me, that's what a hot dog IS. I do know there are other styles, and I do not require that a place serve ONLY a Chicago style dog, but if you're going to do it, do it right. It's not rocket science--this isn't a French Laundry dish. It's nice that they have a good health department score. That does save them from being a one-star review. But for $18, I'm seriously underwhelmed.

text: For a restaurant with this much hype you would expect customer service superior to Burger King. Sadly - this isn't the case. We arrived on time for our 8:30 reservation and were told there was a 15 min wait. Looking around there were at least four other couples waiting - all of which had 8:30 reservations and no one in the restaurant was moving. The hostess was ditsy at her very best and had horrific customer service skills. I took a peak in the restaurant and customers tables were nearly on top of each other and wait staff didn't seem to know how to navigate themselves without almost bumping into tables. The food frankly looked mediocre. After waiting 15 mins and not ONE couple that was waiting had been seated - we left. Frankly, this is Santa Barbara, not LA - and I have NEVER waited after placing a reservation at even the most desirable LA restaurants. Poor service is inexcusable. I recommend trying the Italian restaurant across the street. The dishes are handmade and the wonderful very Italian owner actually spends time checking on his patrons.

text: Paradigm's decor is modern chic; more often than not, the patrons match. I've never had to pay cover here (unsure if they ever charge). The venue space isn't huge and it can get crowded fast, especially around the bar. As the night goes on, folks will distribute more, moving to the dance floor. As you may have heard, the unisex bathrooms have see-through doors which fog when you lock them. It's a good policy to lock the door when weeing, unless you like it when people accidentally (or "accidentally") follow you in. Friday night, the talented Aiden Scott (http://www.djaidenscott.com/) played hip-hop and funky house. He was so freaking kickass that my friends are STILL telling me how great he was. He kept everyone dancing from 11 PM to 2 AM. (Saturdays there's no DJ, but the place pipes music to keep loungers entertained.) Our server (Stephanie) was friendly and down to earth. While we were moving about, she asked if we wanted our drinks brought to the table or bar. She even suggested a tasty shot for our group. At the bar, bartenders Rory and Nani (sp?) served us. Nani offered a shot with Jameson, sour mix, and lime juice, which wasn't half-bad. Rory made a sweet pineapple upside down cake shot. Recommended as a nightspot (but not a restaurant) - check it out!

text: Rolled in for $.50 dumplings on Thursday night. First time here, after reading some mixed reviews on Yelp and elsewhere. Ordered cocktails, and the waitress promptly forgot to turn our order into the bar. We got our drinks 15 minutes later. Then the dumplings started coming out, including ones we hadn't even ordered. Some of the dumplings were very good (Sweet Potato, Bacon, & Green Apple, Duck Confit), but most were pretty blah; the dumpling skin was often thick and doughy (esp. on the 3-way pork), and the fillings lacked in flavor. Every order (3 dumplings) was served on its own plate, so we needed two tables just to fit all the plates for our order of 18 little dumplings. On top of this presentation's plain ridiculousness, its also a huge waste of water, since they need to clean all of those extra plates unnecessarily. If we'd stopped after the dumplings, this review might be 3 stars, but we decided to order some spicy tofu lettuce wraps and vegetable fried rice as well. The tofu arrived in a sickeningly sweet, gloopy sauce that was not spicy at all. The vegetable fried rice was oily and very heavily salted, completely overpowering whatever flavor the modest amount of finely diced vegetables were trying to contribute. If you go on Thursday nights and just order dumplings, you'll probably have an ok experience. But the regular menu seems over-priced, and I'm not even sure the dumplings are a good deal at full price. I probably won't be back.
label: NEG

text: My girlfriend and I recently went to this salon. We called ahead and made two appointments for 4 o'clock. When we went to the front counter to pay, the gal told us it would be $90. We reminded her about the discount from their special and she changed the price to $75. When we reminded her about the $55 we were quoted before the appointment she had to call her up to the front to confirm the prices. She then charged me an extra $10 for "opening a new color". text: If you're looking for hibachi grills with animated chefs, sexy Asian decor with dim lighting and a rotating sushi bar.... this is NOT your place. I had never heard of this place until last night while texting a friend where we should go for dinner/drinks. Her text went as follows: "*other sushi bar* has a better atmosphere & cuter with a better selection. Can be a bit pricey. Sushi brothers has cheaper wine and better tasting sushi." Of course, I went with the cheaper wine and better tasting sushi. When I got there there was a bit of a wait (it was Friday night). They told me 30 minutes, but by the time my party arrived (about 15 minutes), they were ready to seat us. This place is not cute at all. Harsh, unsexy lighting, plain tables and chairs, and a simple-looking sushi bar. But really, who cares when they have good $4 wine?! and AMAZING sushi. I had a glass of Cabernet Sauvignon, and we also got some hot sake to share. I judge my sushi bars by the tuna. If the tuna is fresh in taste texture, then they have a fan for life. Well, I got a special roll called the Tulane Green Wave Roll, or something like that. And while I HATE when they name rolls after sports or other weird things (there was a FEMA roll. why?), the roll was DELICIOUS. There was crabstick, asparagus, avocado inside, and tuna on top with lime. Didn't so much like the lime (i took it off), but the tuna had a wonderful texture and great fresh taste. I really enjoyed it. If you're willing to forgo a trendy atmosphere for some good sushi rolls and cheap wine, then this is a great place to go.

text: If I could, I'd live at the Apple store. I began my descent into computers at an early age and on a Mac. As I grew older, I became part of the PC population out of being poor and just plain outnumbered. Well, when I started my freelance writing business two years ago, I was determined to do it "right", which meant upgrading my home computer system and rekindling my love affair with Apple. I visited my local Apple store and was hooked! I recently visited to buy an iPhone. Yes, I have the iPhone. At the Marlton, NJ store, folks were camped out on folding lawn chairs during the wee hours of the morning. But when I arrived at 2:00 p.m., when the store closed to ready for the launch, there weren't very many people there: maybe 30 or so. The staff (and security) were friendly, approachable and helpful. I remarked that I hadn't seen people camped out like that since I waited on line for New Kids on the Block tickets when I was 16 and the whole staff broke out laughing. Even John "Mayor Gadget" Street had a catbird seat at another store in the middle of the night. But I decided to shop for a few hours before the reopening (I'm much too cool to sit outside a store for a phone), got ice cream, listened to the Phillies day game on my car stereo, then, joined folks in the line, which by 5:00 p.m. was growing longer. Apple staff arranged for coffee and Panera Bread to offer us free beverages and donuts while we waited! But even with the circus atmosphere (kids scalping their spots in line while local news helicopters hovered above us taking photos) Apple staff was poised, calm and helpful. When I finally picked up my box, I had a staff member offer to check me out using a mini, portable credit card machine! How's that for service? I was talking on my new iPhone in mere minutes. At any Apple store you can peruse and play with any gadget or computer with smart support and without the frustration of the "hard sell." Leave it to Apple to create products that not only are the most usable and glitch-free, but they're also the most stylish and awe-inspiring. I can't take out my iPhone in public without being asked for a look and a tutorial. If it were a man, I'd be jealous! Visit an Apple store. There's a third area Apple location on Gulph Road at the King of Prussia Mall.
label: POS

text: We went to Village Whiskey on a Friday night with some out of town friends who were dying to try it. I was warned about the potential for a big wait, so no surprise when were arrived at 8:15 and given a hour and a half wait time. Pleasantly surprised however, when they took both our name and number and were told we would be called when our table opened up. Spent a pleasant hour watching the Phillies game around the corner at Irish Pub until we were called that our table was ready. We were even seated at a table outside! Service was great - our server was very pleasant and gave us some great recommendations. I started with a Ginger Rogers, which though small, was really yummy. Later on we had Dogfish Head Festina Peche, which they had on tap. We knew we had to get the duck fat fries, and went for the Best of Philly winner - with cheddar sauce & short ribs. Akin to a religious experience in my opinion. Really excellent. The pickled artichokes were also a nice starter. Three of us had the Village Burger - nicely cooked, and juicy. One rebel ordered the Pulled Pork, which came with coleslaw and fried pickles. A BBQ snob, he gave it a solid 2 thumbs up. The rest of us were so jealous of the pickles we ordered 2 extra sides of them - crisp and not greasy! My only downside was the one, unisex bathroom, which ended up having quite a line. For a Garces restaurant this really surprised me.

text: I've utilized this uHaul on several occasions. What everyone said here is true - extremely slow, understaffed with huge long lines. My most recent rental experience was one for the record books. I reserved a truck on the website and went through a huge fiasco of trying to understand what my upfront temporary charge would be. For those that don't know what that means: when you reserve a car with uHaul, you have to pay a "deposit" amount. It is an estimated amount of milage costs, your rental cost and some various other small fees. The problem is, the amount you have to pay is different if you decide to deposit cash instead of using a credit card. This really makes absolutely no sense; in point of fact the credit card deposit is LESS than a cash deposit, as if somehow taking a little extra cash will inhibit someone who intends to utterly steal a vehicle. After spending 2 hours on the phone trying to get a straight answer about the deposit amount - which was dramatically different than what was quoted to me when I made my reservaion on the website - we went in to pick up our truck. Only when we arrived, waited in line for an hour, and finally got to the counter, we were suddenly told that because we were paying with cash we would have to have an additional for of I.D. "for security." - something like a passport, or a residential lease, etc... Of course we didn't have one, nor was it mentioned on the website, nor was it mentioned on the telephone. And the guy checking us out was the general manager, who was giving us this lecture on how we should have called him and asked about this because "people at the customer service line, they're just sitting at desks, they don't know what goes on in the stores." Ultimately I stood there and held my ground long enough that he took a student ID as a secondary ID and gave us the damned truck. But he did so with begrudging reluctance, and after 20 minutes of haggling back and forth about the issue. text: Stopped here for a late-night drink and dessert, hoping for a casual, date-friendly place for a sweet nightcap. I wont say we didn't get that, but we certainly weren't impressed and certain elements (like the price) were actually quite off-putting. The decor was kind of like a slightly moodier Starbucks: one is greeted by churning vats of (fake?) chocolate and the carefully organized gift shop by the door, a bad, vaguely chocolate-related mural took up one corner, fake quotes about the ego-maniacal Brenner covered the other walls. It wasn't oppressive, but it was certainly trying too hard. We were led to a nice little two-top pointing out on open window and our order was quickly taken. Very quickly our cocktails (good booze, well-mixed, but not worth 10 bucks a pop) were brought out and, soon after, our chocolate fondue. We opted for the Trio: a molten toffee caramel and any two chocolate fondues (milk, dark, white) served with strawberries, bananas, banana bread, marshmallows, and little grill to roast them. The chocolate was far too sweet for my taste: the white had a lovely cocoa butter flavor, but the dark wasn't that dark and the caramel had a very bland flavor. All of them hurt my teeth, their saccharine flavors overpowering the already sweet accoutrement. Those too were disappointing: the fruit was okay (I would have liked to see local strawberries, but it might be a little early for those) but the marshmallows tasted like your standard Jet-Puffed (what self-respecting confectioner doesn't make their own marshmallows?) and the banana bread was room temperature. at best, and uninspired. All the same, I would have been much happier with less, and more savory fondues with more, and more thoughtful choices to dip. I know there are entire worlds of chocolate connoisseurship, but the quality of the sweets at Max Brenner didn't even stand up to an ignoramus like me. Naked Chocolate Cafe holds its position as my favorite late-night sweet spot in the city: cheaper, better, and its Rittenhouse location couldn't be closer. 4/5 for service, a "meh" for the cocktails, but thumbs down for everything else.
label: NEG

text: It was approaching 11 PM.as I am driving near Cauesway and Veterans near construction Hell. and the thought of a steak sandwich crosses my mind so...I turn down Ridgelake and head for The Harbor in hopes they have what I want. I know they have a pretty decent menu for a bar restaurant so it's worth a shot. I get there and the parking lot is fairly crowded with cars but I manage to snag a spot close enough so I can leave my smart phone plugged in and I can run my Energy Gobbling Wi Fi Hot Spot and write this review from my laptop. I walk straight in to the restaurant portion of the establishment. It is dark but strangely serene despite music and noise of patrons coming through the door joining it to the bar. There are 7 stools at the bar along with the 4 tables. There are cops in and out ordering food and hanging out. I take a few minutes to boot my laptop and begin to peruse the menu. I decide on the Harbor Fries right away. After a while of looking I notice they have a Filet Sandwich..BINGO!..Not the rib eye I was specifically craving but certainly close enough. I order it dressed with lettuce, tomatoes, and mayo. I sit back down to my laptop and make a post in the notorious "Ancient Thead"..(It's the longest running active thread in New Orleans for Yelp..Titled "Yelp is Hiring in NOLA"). I post my response on the AT and it's been maybe 10 minutes and the cook is holding my sandwich and fries at the bar for me as I look up. My first impression is the sandwich is not Very Big I sit down and take my first bite, my next impression is the French bread is toasted very well. I pay closer attention to the bread on my next bite and decide that THIS particular sandwich is THE most perfectly toasted French bread sandwich I have ever eaten. The bread is toasted so well that the crust is very delicate and does not cut my mouth like French bread so often does. The filet is cooked medium rare like I ordered it and it is very tender as filet should be. I take a few more bites as I savor the natural flavor of the meat but decide I want a little steak sauce on it and find a bottle of Pickapeppa on another table which suits my want. I finish the sandwich quickly and wonder if the perfection that was this loaf can be duplicated or was it dumb luck that I got the best toast of the cook's career. I then begin to eat the fries.. The Harbor Fries are topped with roast beef gravy,cheese and onions. They are ok but I personally prefer the fries at the Bottom Line smothered with gravy..and I think the onions need to be grilled a bit more as they were a tad strong. Despite a few minor criticisms, I rated The Harbor 5 stars strictly on the strength of my bread. I just absolutely loved how it was toasted. I don't recall ever eating bread that was toasted so crisp it was delicate like this one before. I suspect my normal rating would be in the 3 range..but..it's about the bread..if it's this good again..then the rating will be higher..but for this one..it was perfect.

text: My lovely college friend came to town visiting from Boston and I had a major decision to make. Do I show her the greasy food Philly is known for or do I show her what all Phialdelphians know, that we are indeed a city overflowing with delicious upscale restaurants that put NY and Boston to shame. I chose the latter. I was told you have to have reservations at Amada, but we had no problems getting a table on a Sunday night at 7pm. The atmosphere is lovely. Great lighting, great textures, very intimate....perfect for sharing some food together. We of course had to get a pitcher of Sangria. Amada had three choices, but we went with the refreshing white. It was great! My friend, though she hated that it had rosemary in it, raved about it and the girl was born in Mexico. The staff was wonderful, explaining things on the menu for a tapas virgin like myself. We chose some bold choices and some safe choices. The bold choices proved to be the better. We started with goat cheese on toasts with a beautiful array of roasted vegetables. Delish and a perfect start. We then moved on to garlic roasted shrimp-one of our safer choices, but done perfectly. Next was Flat Bread with Duck Confit, Jamon Serrano, Cabrales & Date Glaze. This was an even tie for my favorite dish. It was amazing! Also worth mentioning, are the lamb meatballs with manchego cheese. Beautifully plated were the spicy potatoes. As if I couldn't eat anymore, my friend wanted dessert and since the decision was too hard, we went with two choices. Banana Torrijas, which was a crispy sweet bread with caramelized Bananas, Maple Syrup Ice Cream, Banana Anglaise. This dessert punched you in the kisser with all its flavor, but surprisingly, our favorite was the Manchego Mousse. This consisted of Sheep Cheese Mousse, Pistachio Shortdough, Apple Crumb, and Apple Cider Sorbet. The flavors in the Mousse dish were so slight, layered and complex. Honestly, I thought the bill would have been so much more considering the two desserts, and the never ending pitcher of sangria, but it was about 60 dollars a person with tip. I was happy to show my Bostonian friend that Philly has so much more to offer than cheese steaks and soft pretzels- though they may be the heart of the city. I can't wait to go back!

text: Wow, I can't believe NO ONE likes this place! It's full of junky stuff? Yes. It's also a cheaper source for those wierd alligator heads that I was once really obsessed with, haha... I bought up all sizes of them, along with claws and such and gave them to everybody the first time I visited New Orleans and also got enough to mount as showpieces throughout my home. I got over that, but it's always fun to look for random bargains on misc. stuff that you may not want. That's why I loved the La Brea Circus (Bargain Circus in L.A.) and still love browsing Big Lots for randomly sweet items. It's not the place to look for the quintessential NOLA historic pieces or authentic anything, but it has its place with some randomly cool junk! I think it's only a "tourist attraction" in that it has lots of cheap souvenirs (way cheaper than other French Quarter souvenir shops) and that tourists may just be walking that direction anyways.

text: In doing business with this company, keep your eyes wide open, This was a flat rate move, less than 10,000 pounds, out of state. The bid was not the cheapest, yet not the most expensive (Bekins). All very nice people, yet we "misunderstood" the sales contract. When the sales person was at the house, the quote for packing was estimated as 40 boxes, and she indicated that if they didn't pack the amount of boxes, we wouldn't have to pay for them. A competing sales person (Bekins) pointed out that we would need to hire a shuttle: load the goods into a small truck and then have it moved to a larger van, since the street was too narrow for a large van. When we went to the office to finalize the paperwork, right before the move (too late to secure the 2nd bidder), we were informed that the quote was "binding", that we would be paying for 40, whether they packed them or not. They packed far less than 40 boxes. Oh, & yes, we would need to pay for a shuttle, something the sales person knew when she visited the house. The excuse was that she didn't know if a smaller van and its drivers would be available on the day of the move. On the day of the move, the sales person called us, regarding the "binding" quote & kept saying "but you have the best movers", instead of addressing our "misunderstanding". Yes, that was true, the movers were the best. The bad taste was that we were misled by the company itself, not once, but twice. Moving is stressful, and you do start to worry about the other "misunderstandings" that may happen. Also, if you're getting 2 separate bids, be advised that Sierra Moving Systems, a Mayflower franchise & Puliz Moving, United Van Lines, are owned by the same company, with employees doing work at both buildings. Not exactly something you'd pick up off of their web sites.

text: We did the River-to-River 7-hour walking tour. We live near Philadelphia but hadn't spent much time exploring the city before, until our daughter gave us this tour as my wife's birthday present. The tour was a real eye-opener, showing us the extraordinary diversity of Philadelphia. Our guide, Paige, had just finished her masters' degree in history at University of Pennsylvania and was enthusiastic and highly knowledgeable. The tour didn't go to the usual places--the Liberty Bell, Independence Hall, and so on. The idea was that most tourists already know those places or can find them on their own. Instead, we explored the historic back alleys, the huge wall murals, and the lunch delicacies of the Reading Terminal Market. We now know so many fascinating places in Philadelphia--I can't wait to go back and explore more. Suggestion: Come prepared for walking - good walking shoes and a positive attitude!

text: Anyone who knows what over priced, over done and over hyped clothing stores and fashion look like will no doubt find evidence of it at any Blue Bee store (Blue Bee Jeans, Blue Beetle, Blue Bee shoes, ect.) The feeling, clothing and people this store it caters to shouts "I just moved from Dallas to Montecito, got lipo, and am now newly single after a very rewarding divorce" look. ---My bad, the lipo comes after the divorce, that's it. It is all too glittery, too "look at me, I'm wearing the same overpriced, low waist jeans my pre-pubescent daughter wore yesterday to grade school." 50 year olds and 12 year olds should not share the same wardrobe. But when they do, you'll no doubt find them shopping at Blue Bee. The staff of ALL Blue Bee stores are unnecessarily snobby and rather too proud of the crap they try to sell you. The majority of them don't know what interesting and/or flattering fashion is anyways. Just try admiring what they wear to work, and you will no doubt find nothing that in the least that entices the eye. I will argue that if you are looking for anti-sweatshop made standard tee shirts, hoodies and (some) jeans, (and are ready and willing to pay for this,) you will find them in a variety of shades and styles in Blue Bee stores. But I stress again, ignore the staff because they will ALWAYS find it necessary to sweetly remark that everything looks "super hot" or "sooooooooo, like, cute on you, omg," when you really just look like another poser or the next innocent fashion victim. Side note: Blue Bee is famous for having bi-annual, entire store sales that last 3 or more days, with discounts ranging from 50-80%, that many poor suckers will set a 5am alarm for and continue to stalk and camp outside the store until it opens. No hurt feelings intended, but the victims are usually Montecito mothers with nothing else to do but waste their time buying their undeserving, spoiled, teenage daughters new wardrobes every other weekend. You know, something to occupy all there free time. Anyone with half a brain would realize that in order to mark down an entire season's worth of clothing at such outstanding discounts the store has initially overpriced every thing you see more than what is retail norm. So it's really a big joke. Clothing stores only mark down stock that is not selling well and that could become another financial burden if not sold at all. When a store discounts clothes at such rates it usually means they are going out business, unless, like Blue Bee of course, they can still make a growing profit on all those suckers out there and even afford to do it every single passing season. So, please, take caution remember that you (your husband, your parents or maybe even your great grandparents) worked too hard for you to allow yourself to waste your cash in a place that doesn't even appreciate what it is worth.

text: A new discovery in awesomeness for the Philadelphia summer nightlife scene; for just ten dollars a lawn ticket can be purchased to the Mann's Orchestral BYOB picnic jamboree. Apparently whenever the orchestra plays at the Mann you are allowed to bring in lawn chairs no bigger than 28", any food you feel inclined to eat, and any drink you might have a thirst for, alcohol included. We went to a performance of Tchaikovsky followed by a fireworks show last night and were quite pleased, all things considered. To begin I suppose I should describe the layout of the venue. The performance area is situated at the bottom of a bowl like hill, with an artfully constructed wooden building over and around three sides of the stage to funnel the sound outwards and up. Right against the dais is a large area of seats, and behind these seats is the main lawn seating area with the ideal concert real estate. This general admittance zone extends to the top of the hill where it is hemmed in by a tree line. If you stand on this main hill facing the stage, there is a large wing to the left with levels of extra lawn seating for bigger events, and then a fence to it's left . While this extra seating does not afford any real view of the concert, the view of the city skyline that can be seen from there is breathtakingly spectacular. If you were standing on this extra seating hill, at the top is a tented restaurant area. On the side of the tent farthest from the stage is another small patch of grass ringed on two sides by tent walls, and then on the third by a chain link fence with dumpsters beyond; This is where I was able to find open grass to sit, and the only view was of an abandoned factory. I know what you are thinking: "How can he give this place five stars when standing outside the property line would have let him hear more musical notes than where he sat?" (during the 1812 overture we listened to the dishwasher's clattering silverware in lieu of the cannons) The reason is because I arrived to an eight o'clock concert at 8:20 and understand I got what I deserve, so next time I will be much earlier. Plus, I can recognize greatness even when I prevent myself from experiencing it (the far corner was a big party anyway, so there was some consolation). P.S.- We may have been in the absolute worst possible seats on the grounds for the concert, but when the fireworks went off afterwords they were directly overhead. Suck on that, front row center. -Also, biting bugs were out in force.

They were advertising happy hour prices on some sushi appetizers such as spicy tuna roll(6 pieces) and salmon rolls(6 pieces), plus a few others at like $5 bucks each and beer was like $4 bucks each. The spicy tuna was pretty good and overall it was tasty but definitely not the best I had and for the price, can't really complain much. The three of us ate enough as a teaser before dinner later, so it came out to about $35 bucks including food, drinks, and tip, which isn't bad. The waiter at the bar was friendly and responsive so no complaints there. The place is huge and has high ceilings with a second level which I think is more expensive for the VIP types. There are large paintings hanging on the wall and the overall decor was pretty decent but of course the atmosphere was pretty dead on a Friday night. Overall, I would come back again but only during happy hour prices, otherwise I can sense this is another overpriced fancy sushi place in downtown historical Philly.

text: If you are in St. Louis, and you are drinking that swill they call Budweiser, or anything in general from Anheisser Busch, well, you know nothing about good beer. Morgan Stree Brewery is a nice little micro-brewery down in Laclede's Landing. The hotel I'm staying at this week is giving out coupons for a free beer from Morgan Street, so being a lover of all things barley, hops and water I made the short jaunt down the street to Morgan Street. It was pretty empty, then again the Cards and the Blues play tonight so that would attribute to that. Being smart I decided NOT to ask them to put on the Red Wings game for me. With the Blues about to get swept, and the Wings handling business as usual I decided NOT to make St. Louis fans jealous. So, on to the real business after getting sidetracked as usual. I ordered two pints (one at a time) of the Steam Lager and the bacon wrapped meatloaf. First things first, beer. A nice hoppy beer. Not as hopped as a Boston Lager would be, but a great balance you would come to expect from a nicely brewed craft beer. Food, food was great. Bacon makes everything better, and while the meatloaf could stand on its own, I'm all for the obligatory adding of bacon to food products. Lots of people would criticize meatloaf, but this was really good. It came with a side of home fries, grilled tomatoes and had a nice sauce with it. With more trips in the future for me Morgan Street Brewery is most likely a place I'll have to visit every trip. I definitely recommend stopping by if you get the chance, you won't be disappointed.

text: I was so so looking forward to this place after reading the reviews, because I loooove hot pastrami sandwiches, having enjoyed them everywhere from the Togo's chain of my youth, to the classic New York City deli offering at Katz's on the Lower East Side of Manhattan. Pastrami should be savory, somewhat salty, yes, because it is a cured meat after all, and it should also have a sweetness and richness from the de riguer fat that the best pastrami should come marbled with. Unfortunately, I found the hot pastrami at Country Catering to be strangely bitter and overly salty. The french roll was stale and hard at the edges, and I don't think that was from having been toasted or grilled. I had asked for everything but mayo, and was disappointed to find only a few shreds of grilled onion. I would have preferred fresh, and a solid portion of them. The coleslaw I chose as my included side dish was good, but could have used an addition of of tartness to balance out the sweet mayo dressing and raisins. But the green and red cabbage combo was pretty and overall it was nice to have a side that was apparently house-made, and not just some goopy stuff out of an industrial plastic gallon jar. I will give them another chance. It's obviously a very busy and popular place at lunchtime. I was impressed to see about 6 deli staff (including the owners, whom I recognized from the Yelp pics) efficiently taking orders and preparing food. The service was friendly and fairly prompt, the store clean, and there were several inviting tables outdoors and a few inside. Nice selection of cold bottled drinks too. And the meat counter offered some good looking cuts I would be tempted to lay down some dough for. Excellent quality meat does not come cheap. But that pastrami, I'm scratching my head still. Next time I will try the tri-tip or BBQ sandwiches.

text: The best thing I had at A La Maison was a delicious bottle of Pinot Noir. That's a pity, considering the restaurant is BYOB. French restaurants are rather rare outside of downtown, so I was delighted to come back from a four month absence to find A La Maison had opened up in my old stomping grounds of Ardmore. I'm a huge fan of French Bistro food, as I worked in one for several years. I brought my wife to A La Maison Friday night, which took some persuasion as my wife doesn't share my love of French food. She just doesn't understand what all the fuss was about. I assured her that she would have a revelation once she had it at a good bistro. Unfortunately, A La Maison is not a good bistro. The decor is sparse but passable, done on a budget but reasonably tasteful. The wait staff was friendly but unpolished. They would benefit from acting slightly more formal and brushing up a bit on their knowledge of the menu. The menu was essentially standard bistro fare, except for an interesting looking smoked salmon tian. I ordered that as an appetizer, only to be told that they were out of it. (At 6:45 on a Friday?) Okay, I'm not that picky, so I went with the pate, to be followed by the nightly special of steak Diane. My wife ordered the house salad as an appetizer and the roasted salmon Dijonnaise as a main course. The pate came with a spot of mustard, some cornichons, and toasted baguette slices. The baguette slices were hard as rocks, so I used the house bread instead. The pate itself was reasonably tasty but not memorable in any way. My wife's house salad was imposingly large, with a light-tasting vinaigrette, palm hearts, pine nuts, and a few other knick-knacks. Like the pate, it was unremarkable, even a little bland. The more glaring problems began with the main course. My wife's salmon was expertly cooked, but it was under-seasoned, and the sauce was sparse and wimpy tasting to boot. It came with sauteed Swiss chard. Technically there was nothing wrong with the Swiss chard, except for the fact that apparently nothing had been done to it other than throwing it in a pan. No shallots, no wine, no vinegar, and no spice of any kind. Hey, Swiss chard is a nice vegetable, but you should at least TRY to do something with it! Similar problems plagued my steak Diane. I had been told it was tenderloin, but I was dismayed that I received the top of the head from the tenderloin, which is the least tasty part. For $28, I would expect a better cut. Just like the salmon, the sauce was sparse and underwhelming. The accompanying mashed potatoes could have come from any diner in Philly, and the spinach was a clone of the Swiss chard, i.e. badly in need of something else to give it a kick. In fact, that was the problem with the entire meal. Nothing had a kick to it. The things that make French food so special, the rich stocks, gobs of butter and cream, wine, fresh herbs, pungent shallots, all seemed to be missing or used extremely sparingly. This isn't rocket science, guys! It's just as easy to make a knock-out batch of creamy mashed potatoes as it is to make a bland batch. The final verdict? As much as I wanted to like A La Maison, I had to agree with my wife's judgment: Not Worth The Calories.

text: "The Corner" in New Orleans should rename itself "Lame Rip Off." I was drawn in because the sign said "Breakfast Served All Day" and it had large windows and antique tables. Looked like a winner. But the first thing I noticed when I came in was sports flags all over the ceiling and a staff dressed in the black and white jerseys of football referees, complete with whistles. The stripes of their uniforms, along with their demeanor, made them seem more like prison inmates. They were sad, lost, miserable souls without a smile to be found, numbed by it all as 80's pop hits, such as Steve Winwood's "Roll With It" blasted from the stereo over the practically empty restaurant. I'd also noticed a sign saying "We serve bottled water only," which I took to mean something like "Our glasses of water are fresh, right from the cooler, not from the tap." But I found out the truth when I asked for a glass of water from the waiter, who had all the excitement and enthusiasm of the perpetually bored cartoon dog "Droopy." "You gotta buy a bottle o'water, Chief" he said. Translation: this tourist trap, corporate chain like blight on the otherwise shining city of New Orleans will not serve you a glass of water. They make you pay for an overpriced bottle. This should have been my clue to leave, but I wanted to give this place a chance. It was right on Jackson Square in the center of a city with great food all around. How bad could it be? Undaunted and determined to attain the breakfast I so desired, I ordered an ice tea. Then I looked at the menu. The prices seemed reasonable, at first. "What do these come with?" I asked my server about the eight dollar omelettes. "Nothing, chief" he said. "There are sides right there." He pointed to the lower section of the menu, which showed home fries for $4 and toast for $2.50. In other words...you pay $8.00 for a tiny omelette that comes with nothing. Then you have to pay another $6.50 for toast and home fries. At this point, I probably should have paid for my ice tea, cut my losses and gotten the hell out of there. But I was hungry and a bit hungover. I figured, at the very least, this place would at least provide me a good meal, despite prices that were comparable to room service at the Westin. When the 'omelette' arrived, it was a thin strip of egg over the 'toppings,' each of which I was charged an extra 1.50 for! The 'home fries' were those cheap, crispy, frozen, plastic like ones that you get only in the cheapest of diners. And the toast had all the freshness and authenticity of Wonder Bread. I took a couple bites and decided not to waste my appetite, bite the proverbial bullet, go somewhere else and call this a valuable lesson. When the bill came, the total was $22 (gratuity had been included). Twenty two dollars for a cheap, lame, pathetic excuse for a breakfast. To the owners of The Corner: Shame on you. To everyone else: New Orleans, La. is filled with great restaurants, some of the best I've ever eaten in. But if you ever find yourself visiting there do NOT, by any means, ever eat at a restaurant called "The Corner" at Jackson Square.

text: At 75% Irish I usually find myself having a profound and utter distaste for off Irish pub's. But I found this Kelliann's (I feel like the West Philly one could be another story) to be a chill little pub. It might have been the random and fun crew that I was with, the Bacardi mask that made the rounds, The round of Irish Car Bombs, or the Madonnathon on the jukebox courtesy of Big Drew doing the the talking. But I'd even say it's perfect for a good weekend gathering. The bartenders definitely hooked up some spot on service. The beer varieties were good and plentiful. And even though I don't really get the fuss behind sliders (they look like White Castle) the food did look mighty tasty. The bar has a colorful group of regulars that like to dance to random songs too. I think I'll be back.
label: POS

text: I have to agree that this library is much better than many other libraries I have been to in the past. CC library has a helpful staff and a very wide selection. They have reading lists for school and other great educational resources especially for high schoolers and college students. This library also has a large section entirely for children, with computers and a special reading area for stories. CC library has so many great things to offer: they also have a great audio/visual section full of popular CDs, many TV series, movies, and workout videos and documentaries. Their magazine section is very large. They have a graphic novel section and a small area for young adult books. The library is really developed and a great place to come and find a book to read. One small problem is that oftentimes the library doesn't carry some material. You might have to put some things on hold, but they do come in quickly.
label: POS

text: My friends and I came here because we were hungry for breakfast and didn't want to wait in line at Cafe Du Monde. The service was awful - the waitress had an attitude the whole time. Their waffles were cold and undercooked. The grits were tasteless and had a film on them. The hashbrowns were like canned potato strings. The omelette was the only thing that was any good, so I shared with everyone else. I was very disappointed with our service and food for the price! Next time I will wait in line at Cafe Du Monde.
label: NEG

text: This is my go to spot to get a fresh one. I made the pilgrimage back in college and have renewed my faith in this good barbershop. Upper Cuts are the same people that own the upscale Shaving Grace Barbershops in Malvern and soon to be in Doylestown. The best part about Upper Cuts is that you get the same shape up for only $15 compared to the $35 at Shaving Grace. I have received cuts from 3 different barbers there and prefer to go on Wednesdays when the owner is there. They still do hot foam straight edge shaving on the back of your neck and the chairs appear to be from the 1960's. A little side note on real barbershops compared to Supercuts, Hair Cuttery, etc. When I lived in Ardmore I frequented the Hair Cuttery on Lancaster Ave. One lucky day I was get my trim on (1 clip faded up with finger length on top) from a woman who had yet mastered the English language. She was using a clip on top and as you can imagine the clip fell off and she clipped me. Almost down to the skin. She shouted out "You no pay, You no pay" but the damage was done. I was doomed to spend the next 2 months growing out an Uncle Fester cut. Never again would I frequent such an establishment. Moral of the story- Friends don't let friends go to a chain "barber shop".
label: POS

text: KC's Pastries does one thing right: the custard filled pineapple buns. I'll forgive the employee's incompetence at correctly wrapping the buns in the bags. Heck, I'll even forgive the same employee for grabbing the buns on display with her bare hands after forking over the change. Why? Because those custard filled pineapple buns are THAT stinkin' delicious. End of story.
label: POS

text: Agree that I wish there were negative stars. This is the worst leasing experience my fiance and I have ever had. Among a host of other issues - they made several false statements to us regarding the condition of the unit when we were looking. They advertised our unit as having a "working fireplace" and a whirlpool tub. Once we moved in turned out the whirlpool tub did not work at all. When I reported this to the management company - their reply was to "use it as a soaking tub." When we tried to use the fireplace in the winter (with the flu open) the chimney was so dirty that our entire unit completely filled with smoke. We reported it. They said it was fixed. We tried to use it again - smoked out again. Since we gave notice that we are not renewing, they have been showing our apartment almost everynight - up until 7 pm. When I emailed the owner, Alyson Herman, to ask her to keep the showings before 6:15 (reasonable I think) she threatened "action for breach of contract." Claimed that the leasing agent never said anything about giving 24 hours notice and stated that according to the lease she was only giving us notice as a courtesy anyway. These people are the WORST - there are plenty of awesome landlords in Philly so save yourself the drama and take your business elsewhere.

text: Lolita wasn't at all bad, but it just wasn't a stellar, wowing experience. The service was all right - server was not the friendliest Ambiance was the best part of the meal - I like the small intimate space and it does feel casual yet refined. Food was ok. I had the salmon with a corn salad. The salmon and corn salad were good, but I didn't like the sauce it came with (can't even remember what it was - something with heart of palms I think). Guacamole and chips very good. My friend had the ceviche special. I didn't ask if she liked it but I don't think she loved it. I do like that it's byo and the prices are pretty decent.
label: NEG

text: Southern,Yes. Great, No. You walk into this place on one of the most touristy streets i have ever been on, and you feel the grit of a BBQ joint. It has the ambiance of a place that is going to put out some ridiculous meat. There is a a menu above a steam table where they keep all the food. The smoker is right behind the people slappin meat on plates. I felt like I was goin' to do a little two step while I was waiting for my grub. I was excited. My taste buds were standing like little erections cuz it smelled so damn good in there. I order the a combo plate of pulled pork, pork ribs and brisket. Sides of creamed corn and mac n'cheese. The pulled pork was heavenly. When I got the front and ordered he ran out of pulled pork so he turned around and pulled a football size pork shoulder wrapped in foil from the smoker and proceeded to pull it apart with his hands. It crumbled and steamed like crazy. My taste buts were fully erect and ejaculating at this point. He chopped my ribs and sliced my brisket; and slopped the corn and mac into containers. Got the grub back to the hotel and started to satisfy my eager buds. Like I said before the pulled pork was tender and juicy and creamy and tasty. Awesome. The ribs had a thick skin on them like beef jerky. I had to peel it off so i could eat them. Ultimately i couldn't eat them. They were too dry and were getting stuck all up in my grill. I needed 20 minutes of floss time to get the grill back to normal. The brisket was like dry roast beef at a cheap buffet. The flavors were nice, but so dry I couldn't eat it without saucing them up so much I could no longer taste the meat, only vinegary sauce. The sides were not good. The corn was like grade school cafeteria corn. Grey kernels cooked in milk and sugar. Mac n' Cheese could have been good if it had salt and saucier sauce. Bland, dry Mac is no good in my hood. In the end my buds went limp and did not get their happy ending. So, sad.
label: NEG

text: I have never actually gone inside Golden Dragon - we found this place online and always get it delivered. I LOVE the food here! It is never greasy like a lot of Chinese places tend to be. The fried rice is fantastic, one of the best ever! I've had the sweet and sour chicken and sesame chicken before - both absolutely yummy! The breading on the chicken doesn't overpower the meat like it does in other places. The spring rolls are great too! This is def. becoming one of my favorite delivery places!
label: POS

text: I have stopped into Maria's twice now, and both times I was disappointed. I actually can't comment on the food because I never stayed long enough to eat. The staff and bar service have just been unfriendly. I didn't want to spend my money at an establishment where no one would even crack a smile. I know people sometimes have bad days, but this was the case on BOTH of my visits. My last visit Isaac and I pulled into a desolate parking lot, granted it was only turning 5pm, so maybe we were early. When when we pulled up the server was outside smoking - an immediate turn off for me. I loath cigarette smoke. We went inside to have a drink at the bar before we ate. The bartender was lacking personality, so in his usual style Isaac tried to lighten him up by cracking a joke or two...there was no response. Isaac and I looked at each other, and knew it was time to go. For me the whole experience was rather depressing. I might give Maria's one last try, but honestly, it will be hard for me to forget my not - so - hot previous experiences.
label: NEG

text: I want to like SEPTA. I want to appreciate SEPTA. I've tried so hard. But living with SEPTA is like having an abusive boyfriend. He leaves you stranded when he says he is going to be there. And when he does pick you up, he can only manage to drop you off in the general area of where you want to be. He doesn't cost that much, but you'd gladly pay more for better treatment. I'm sure SEPTA is doing what it can with the finding it gets, and I think it's terrible that Pennsylvania doesn't recognize that an efficient public transportation system is extremely important to everyone, not just those with low incomes. But honestly, using SEPTA is a nightmare. If you rely on the bus system to get to work, God bless you. Some bus routes run regularly enough, but most are consistently running late--if they show up at all. I have had in service busses blow right past me on more than one occasion. I have waited for upwards of an hour for a bus. The subway system is utterly useless. We need more lines. Why isn't there a subway line running up and down Columbus? Why isn't there a line that goes up Passyunk? Why isn't there anything but the Orange Line servicing North Philadelphia? And what the hell are we doing with all of these trolley tracks? The regional rail is wasting money. If we modeled it after PATCO and eliminated the conductors we could save a lot of money. Sure the elimination of jobs will be devastating to some, but I think in this case it is for the greater good.
label: NEG

text: Smells like moth balls. The little bar upstairs is pretty ok. Prices too high. And I would like them a WHOLE lot better if they would be considerate enough to post a sign asking their patrons to park in the ample parking available from Elizabeth's and not take up all the spots of the people who actually LIVE in the area.

text: You know when you enter an establishment and feel that, even in the low light, everything inside has a layer of filth on it? Welcome to AMC, the first movie theater I've entered that smelled like high school gym class locker room; next time I go (only out of laziness due to proximity) I'm bringing a bottle of Febreeze to hose down my chair ahead of time. I love dive bars so I'm cool with a little grime but this place was just funky and not in a Bootsy Collins way. Two stars for stadium seating and decent sound. Hopefully as the tedious construction on this mediocre mall nears completion they'll send in a team of cleaners to chip away at the filth.

text: Noodle salad! Great convenient location when out shopping in elmwood or before a movie makes this solid sushi place definitely worth a try. As a vegetarian they have some good options including the spring roll. However unlike the spring roll at the kyoto in uptown this one comes with crab, so make sure and specify without if you are a veggie.
label: POS

text: After walking by for years, and hearing countless self-proclaimed "night life experts" praise Monk's, I decided to brave the "place to be." I had a large party with me. We dutifully tried to make arrangements earlier in the week for a reasonable, less-trafficked hour on Saturday. We were told that no reservations were taken. That said, we entered earlier than planned, and by the snippiest, rudest hostess I've seen in my life, we were told that not only would it take at least 2 hours to get seated, but that our party would be split, and the second seating would be 90 minutes after the first. When we inquired further, we were brutally reminded to "call ahead next time!" What kind of joke is this? When we evaluated how to proceed in the bar, we were very much in the way, and treated rudely by other staff. Fed up, I walked out, and decided that my night would be exponentially happier spent on the sidewalk than here. Shortly thereafter, I was met by the rest of my party. I'm an atheist to Monk's holy beer bible. I'm smart enough to know where to get all of these beers elsewhere in the city. Moreover, I don't care whether I'm in Studio 54, The Century Club, or the hottest spot in Miami, NOBODY is treating me or mine like that. Monk's, you're a bridge & tunnel amateur night hangout. I can drink your brews elsewhere, and I can eat your recipes in copycat bars that respect my dollar. Others may love it, but I never needed a "soup nazi" to make the soup taste better... I like what's genuine, respectful, and truly good, and I will never return.
label: NEG

text: RIP OFF. Admission, lunch for 2 toddlers, my wife, and I=$62! It really is a great concept, but the owners of The Little Treehouse fail to pull it off well. We pay $100 annually for the Please Touch Museum, and they offer tasty food for reasonable prices too! The proprietors are trying to be somewhat gourmet, but falling flat and overcharging for it. My wife's 9 dollar grilled cheese? Meh. And it seems like they could've packed more fun equipment into that big room; you get the impression, especially after signing a waiver upon admission, that the owners are petrified of getting sued. So they went out and got boring hippie equipment. One slide that rises a towering two feet off the ground, for example. The owners of this place must be making a killing, however we do not plan to continue to stuff their pockets in the future.

text: We went here because we got two free passes from some guy on Bourbon Street. I'm sad to say that it wasn't that great. The dancers looked bored at best and the clientele was shadier than I am used to. There was some major full-contact going on, but I didn't find the girls that appealing. I think that the best part about this place is the outside - there is a pair of mechanical legs that swing out from the building. All cute and burlesquey, clad in fishnets. If you get a free pass, check it out...why not? However, I still think that you can have more fun down the street at Temptations.

text: Wether you're there for brunch, lunch, or dinner prepare for an amazing meal in a unique and calming atmosphere. The eggs benedict and mimosa combination always make the rest of a Sunday for me. And during dinner try the escargot... it is intense and a memory maker of awesome proportion. The cheese plate and a bottle of wine will start your night off the right way. Wether for a date or a nice dinner with some other food loving friends this is a must do on your new orleans culinary experience.

Drinks aren't exactly cheap but they have an awesome beer drink that's blue moon mixed with some raspberry stuff with an orange slice, amazing but $7. Plan on going there again though.

text: Holy crap, mindblasting. I was in town for an Ultimate Frisbee tournament at UCSB, and heard about this place incessantly from local players. After our tournament ended on Sunday, we moseyed on over, and got into the huge line. A little bit later, I walked out with a Monster Steak Burrito. SPECTACULAR! PHENOMENAL! TIMEWARPING! WIGGLEWORTHY! I wish I had eaten all my meals here. I could imagine someone getting tired of this place if they..lived here. But if I am just visiting, why go anywhere else. I sampled other people's meals, and they were great too. Awesome nachos, super quesadillas. The only 'problem' with this place is that they don't have carnitas. COMPLETE THE TRINITY FREEBIRDS!

text: You would think that the very nicely appointed rooms would have sold me. Or perhaps the view or the complimentary bike use did it. Nope, it's none of those things....it's their hospitality. Picture in your mind's eye that I'm being driven here really late at night...I'm really groggy and seriously have no idea where the hell I am. The car comes to a stop and I'm told to get my stuff....as I clear the concrete eye bunnies to get my bearings I pack a bunch of random things in a flimsy plastic bag. As I take a step outside my bag of crap bursts open on the very steps leading to the front desk. ARG! I stand there in my pj's (forgot to mention that) looking like a complete mess, now like a bum. I am befuddled by my luck and stare at the mess at my feet absentmindedly as a large coated figure walks my way. I look up and it's the door man smiling at me in that kind of warm fatherly way...."excuse me sir, would you like some plastic bags for that?" There...that was it....that's all it took..... LOVE THE FOUR SEASONS!

text: Ok foodies, If you are in between Clearwater or Tampa or you don't know where you want to go? head west on Hillsborough or East on Tampa Rd (same thing) and when you get in the middle, check this place out! text: I nominate Fast Wok as one of the best dives in Indy. The place is a little dirty, and the rules and regulations posted on the walls (e.g. Limit 5 napkins per dinner) gives the place a "Soup Nazi" vibe. But the food is delicious and it's a great bargain. Vegetarians are kind of out of luck. There are only two meatless items on the menu and they're both side dishes.

text: Maybe I just got a bad meal but I thought it was way overpriced and not great. The burgers are so thin that they don't even bother asking how you want yours cooked - it's just brown all the way through. The bun was a little soggy and the cheese wasn't melted. Their cups of chili looked really good so I asked for the bacon cheese burger, a fountain drink and some chili. The chili came on my burger, not in a cup. It is a side but I thought it was weird that they didn't clarify and as a first-timer I didn't know enough to be specific. The chili was pretty good though. The sweet potato fries were just ok. I got a lot of charred bits and I thought they were overpriced. We ordered in but they still brought us our food in bags. They did the same for the other people who ordered in. Even McDonalds puts your burger on the tray. All in all, I just don't get the hype.

text: I had been waiting for a beautiful day like today to take Emma to a local dog park. It needed to be fairly close by and fenced in. I found Pretzel Park. Parking wasn't too bad since it's a few streets back from Main Street Manayunk. The area wasn't huge but big enough for the consistent flow of dogs (maybe 20 or so). There are bags and some water provided. They're taking up donations for bricks in order to install a human/doggy water fountain there. The dogs and humans were quite friendly. My only beef was that the walls are pretty low, especially the stone one that borders Cotton St. My jack russell (who can't be trusted off leash) could easily jump up there. All of the other dogs kept her busy so it wasn't a problem. All in all a good park. My pooch will be sacked out for the rest of the night!

text: Two words: mall pizza. If you enjoy canned mushrooms and olives, and don't feel like walking the extra block to Liberty Place to get Sbarro's, then by all means go to Joe's Pizza. If you want something that actually tastes good and has fresh toppings, try Pietro's.

text: I have now been to Surly Wench well over a few dozen times. They just opened up a whole new room with a bar inside and plenty of couches to relax on. I always start a tab and am always surprised to get my bill because it is always cheaper than what I thought I would be paying. I have eaten there a few times and the food is soooo good. I recommend the BBQ Burger with crispy tater tots. Yum. They also have potato tacos and fried Oreos which I hear are very tasty. The doorman there is always pleasant and so are the bartenders except I have to agree with a comment below, there is one rude bartender, I wonder if we are talking about the same lady. There all always live bands or DJ's and this bar is never boring. From burlesques shows to guitar hero nights to 80s dancing, it's a must "stop by" if you are on 4th Ave!!

text: If I had a baby, and this baby tasted like Iron Barley, then I would eat my baby. The food is INCREDIBLE. The service is SPLENDID. You can spend 20 bucks, or you can spend 60 bucks. Either way, you will leave fulfilled. I went yesterday. I had a mexican cheese appetizer. They served it on a skillet. I thought "oh gross, reminds of when I was in college and worked at applebee's and we served these wicked bad 10 dollar steaks on sizzling skillets. what have i gotten myself into?" Best. Cheese. Ever. It's a fried cheese, served up with some tortillas and pico and the best freakin tequila lime sauce IN THE WORLD. I actually used my finger to wipe up the plate and continue to lick up the sauce, long after the appetizer was gone. What can I say, I'm the classiest. The portions here are huge, fresh, and full of quality ingredients. The servers here are amazing at what they do. My server last night spent ten minutes rattling off the huge list of nightly specials. Watermelon salad? Check. Seafood risotto? Check. The list went on...and on.....and on. I want to go back and eat it all. I want to eat until my entire body goes into convulsions. Yes. You NEED to try their desserts. They are strange. They are enticing. They are delicious. They might be Satan tempting you from his lair because I was incredibly full after dinner, but I managed to scarf down my entire Peanut Butter Blaster Pie. Best part? Go in here and ripped jeans and flip flops, or a suit, and you'll be good.

They were so busy and she didn't get annoyed with me needing variety of 1/4lb thinly sliced meats. The selection is great for the deli meats and assorted artisan cheeses, and the service cannot be beat.

text: Nashville's answer to all the sports you played back in the day. They offer up sports like Flag Football, Basketball, Kickball, Softball, Soccer, and Volleyball. Though on the other side of the coin, since there are more seasons throughout the year, there are more chances to play and win a specific league. Most events are "alcohol friendly", and some people consider the activities more social then competitive. You even get a couple of "free pitcher" vouchers at each game. The scheduling of the games can be an issue during weeknights as some games can start as late as 10pm. Overall not a bad option for those that enjoy a good time while playing sports...

text: Okay, so I wasn't intending to be 'that woman with her kids' at such a nice place. But the wait at P.F.Chang's across the street was insanity. And we were all starved. And it was raining. And I was pushing a stroller. So I pushed it back to the hotel and did a quick text to get the number for Acacia and they were able to get us in... Holy gracious. The manager was so fantastic, I don't even think he would have cared if my kid had stood up on the table and thrown poo. Okay, maybe he would have. But he was very accommodating, and being in the industry, I know the gasps and groans I get at some establishments when I show up with two wee ones in tow. (I dine out a lot with my kids so they know how to eat and how to behave. Still, as soon as we sat down, the old couple next to us asked to move tables. Maybe she was expecting a hurled poo?) Anyway, the staff was LOVELY and so wonderful to us... we had about six servers, plus the manager, couldn't keep them all straight. But we were never ignored and they engaged my three-year-old a great deal. He loved the ribeye steak frites. My 8 month old loved the mashed tatoes. Me mumsie had the lamb - kind of wish I had ordered that, it was so fantastic. But I can't make myself ever order the same thing as someone else. Major hangup. And then I get food envy. Beet salad was awesome to start. I agree with Brooke - desserts are sort of forgettable. We took one back to the hotel room - a chocolate walnut roll - and it was like any boring bakery roulade... blah. Skip dessert and get another glass of wine. Great selection.

text: South Street is GREAT! My friend "Little Joe", whose dubious job it was to drive me and my crew around for three days, suggested this place, and he definitely knows what he's talking about. The service was friendly, the prices were reasonable, and the food was really good! Admittedly, I didn't go the adventurous route, I had the fried shrimp and they were pretty good. Little Joe had the fried catfish, and it looked delicious! As with most restaurants in Nashville, this place is hilighted by its fantastic sides. I had the sweet potato caserole...are you kidding me? marvelous! Another friend had the tater tots, and while I'm not usually a fan, these were nothing like those soggy little potato cylinders they served in my elementary school cafeteria. These are more like little fried mashed potato clumps, and they are superb! Overall, I was super-impressed by this restaurant, and I'll definitely stop by the next time I'm in town.

text: Just had lunch at Dixie Picnic with some friends and it was great. I ordered the muffaletta and it was darn near perfect. A very tasty olive relish smothered over a nice layer of meat and cheese on the traditional muffaletta loaf. The loaf itself was light and flavorful with a great just-slightly-chewy texture. I could have handled it being toasted a little more, but that's picking nits. One friend ordered the crab cakes and the other ordered the chili and conrbread, and both were very satisfied with their lunches as well. On the way out the door I grabbed a piece of the Key Lime pie and it was really good as well. Light texture with a healthy amount of lime zest and a moist graham cracker crust. A little bit sweet for my personal tastes (I like my fruit desserts on the tart side), but I would order it again. Will definitely be going back for breakfast and lunch.

text: Wood fired brick over pizza at it's finest, and there is no comparable pie in Reno-Tahoe. Prices are reasonable and certainly cheaper than most Round Table's. The interior is clean and modern and there is a good vibe in the place since the pizza chefs are on display doing their thing. They have wine specials on certain days of the week, which means you should call ahead to determine which day has the best deals. On the day we went it was half off all bottles of wine. A killer deal for sure! It's never terribly busy which confuses me since the pie is so choice. The only thing keeping me from giving them 5 stars is the sometimes lackadaisical service. The help is friendly but they do need to be reminded to refill drinks and check in after bringing food to the table. This is a 4 star place with 5 star potential. Kudo's to the franchisee for bringing Brooklyn's most famous pizza to Sparks.

text: Michael's review seems to have been suppressed. Allow me to syndicate his review: A friend had seen this new Mexican restaurant with outdoor seating and was eager to try it out. So after driving & walking around trying to find it, we finally settled in to a nice outdoor table. And what a huge disappointment it was! The simple summary is that the highlight of the meal was the chips! Or, as I told the server: the food displayed a fundamental lack of understanding mexican cuisine. Consistently bland and heavy, as if cream & cheese were substitutes for onions, garlic, cilantro, chiles, etc. The guacamole seemed to consist of nothing more than mashed avocados. The tomato salad had few tomatoes and was drowned in dressing. The vegetable tacos were nicely sauteed, but had little flavor and were wrapped in raw tortillas. My friend had the sweet potato & bacon enchiladas, and was willing to give them a C- until he tasted his main course; then he said "F". And the drinks? The watermelon margarita tasted *nothing* like watermelon and had no hint of pink in it. But the real treat is when you ask for a special tequila in the margarita -- they charge $16 each for these small drinks!! OK, so maybe I'm the wrong person to ask: I've been eating mexican food since I was 3, and have enjoyed restaurant, street and home cooking in Mexico. But there is much, much better Mexican food here in Philly. El Vez is noisy & expensive, but the flavors are solid. Tequilas is expensive, but the food is good. Veracruzana has zero ambiance, but has good food and is cheap. Even Cantina, which I don't think is very good, is better than Azul. Casuelas, Lolita.... too many options to pay high prices for bad food.
label: NEG

text: I am not sure if I can accurately capture the essence of D'Angelo's. When you walk in, it is dark and ambient. An instrumental version of Moon River was playing in the background. Amidst tons of Italian options, I was a little hesitant to try this place out at first. It is not dripping with trend, it is not in South Philly, and despite being on that special restaurant row of 20th St. between Spruce and Locust, I have not really heard much about it. D'Angelo's is a classic dining experience. The staff will take care of every minute detail. My lasanga, not something I usually order, was massive and I ate the whole thing! So delicious! Side note: This sounds a little odd, but I really appreciated the carpeting too. It kept the noise levels down. We had a lovely nook on the second floor, overlooking the tree-lined street. I can't wait to go back.

text: Ummmkay. I am a literary geek. I love me some documents, I love museums, I love the smell of old books and I think the most wonderful place in the history of mankind is where I learned to read, the Elsie Quirk public library that smells like a century of pages turning under children's fingertips. And I thought I would love the Karpeles, I had it at the top of my list. But...I felt very let down. I don't know exactly what I was expecting, but the museum didn't compare to whatever it was I had in my head. The manuscripts are mostly copies of famous manuscripts, and there aren't a lot of descriptions in the museum to explain the DATE of the manuscript or the immense importance and why I should be looking at it through a little glass case. There are just some random quotes drawn from the exhibited text, and that wasn't enough for me. They have a few neat pieces, like a part of the Torah on deerskin that they state is 350 years old, but the whole place just feels a little bit sterile and derivative. For a document library, there were very few facts and even less real information, which is what I was craving. Instead, I looked very quickly over busts of heads with no name tag. Who are you, head that looks a bit like Benjamin Franklin?? And copies of manuscripts and music. It's just off. I hope that makes sense.

text: DON'T make the mistake of limiting your South Philly taco intake to La Veracruzana and La Lupe. Los Taquitos de Puebla is too good to miss, and just as the cuisines of Puebla and Veracruz (neighboring states in Mexico) have marked differences, not least of which are the differences in local agricultural products, no two South Philly tacos are exactly alike. I had an order of tacos al pastor, cooked on a kabob-like rod and containing a unique blend of seasoned beef and pork. They were served up with delicious nopales (a popular cactus dish) and two fabulous salsas. Go for the roja! Go for the fire. An order of cebollitas preparadas (little grilled onions, seasoned) can really round out a meal, especially if you can share them with a few friends. And for your drink, grab an agua de horchata: a milky, rice based drink made with cinnamon and lime. Sooooo good. It's pretty rare to find "real" homemade horchata these days. I didn't ask if theirs was the "real deal" at Los Taquitos de Puebla, but I certainly found it convincing enough.

text: If I could rate Nunzio's -5 Stars I would. For a place as presumptuous as this, one would expect 1st-class attention to service and customer comfort. Fahgettaboutit!! When our group of five arrived at 7pm on Sunday the entire front of the dining area was empty, but for a boisterous group of 20+ sitting at a combined long table squeezed into the narrow left side of the front of the room. As a result of the pitched ceiling and 1/2 wall surrounding the table, the noise emanating from the group was deafening and echoing off every wall (hence, every other guest having been relegated to the (quieter) rear of the dining area.) When the "Hostess" attempted to sit our group at the closest table to the noise we asked to be seated at the furthest table away from it. She said: "Don't worry, they've already received their bill. They are leaving. And anyway, that other table is too big for your group. I have to save it for a larger party." Twenty minutes later, not only had the noise NOT left, they had repositioned themselves 5 feet from our table and were yelling at each other louder than Eagles' fans at a Dallas game. It fact, it was so loud, the waiter had to literally yell the "memorized" entrée list and walk around the table to be heard. During this ordeal, no one bothered to ask us if we would like to relocate to the "quieter" location. Once the orders were placed service was slow and 1/2-assed. Slow, despite the fact that now the joint was 2/3rd's empty and 1/2-assed because since the waiter had no assistance, when he brought 3 of the 5 entrée's out, he then had to march back to the kitchen only to reappear 3 minutes later with the remaining 2 entrée's. Do you know how pathetic it is to sit and stare at food waiting for the rest of the table to be served? Apparently simultaneous food delivery is beyond the scope of service there. It is also apparent that the management places a higher importance on how "pretty" the food looks than on the comfort of it's patrons. Oh, and that quieter table with 6 settings which our group of 5 was too small for? It remained empty for our entire 2 hour dinner ordeal. Clearly this place is way past it's prime and should be avoided at all costs. I can only hope that this review costs them many lost customers since the $175.00 we wasted there will be the last from my group.

text: Terrene definition? mundane... by Mr. Tasty Our first experience at Terrene was quite a disappointment. Even though the staff was friendly and accommodating enough, the interior had the feeling of a 60's Famous Barr in-store eatery. The outdoor patio was pleasant but was missing the calming sounds of a water feature. We started with the small plate frites-hand cut fries. I believe the oil they were fried in was old as the fries were oil soaked through. The accompanying white cheddar ale sauce was a welcomed tasty dip for the frites. Moving on to the big plates we ordered the hanger steak, the lamb pot roast and tofu tacos. We asked the waitress about the hanger steak as we unaware of this cut of beef. She told us this steak was located on the diaphragm of a steer. She said it was a flavorful and tender cut. My wife ordered it cooked medium well. The steak arrived but was tough and chewy-not at all flavorful and tender like the waitress had described. Upon returning home and a quick Google search we learned that a hanger steak can tough and chewy if not ordered rare to medium rare. Had we been informed of this my wife would have ordered medium rare. Needless to say, the hanger steak was a disappointment. If you order the hanger steak please heed our warning as the staff will not. The vegetables that came with her dish also came complete with stems. I ordered the lamb pot roast. The lamb was perfect, tender, juicy and flavorful. However, they serve the meal in a bowl and the Yukon gold mashed potatoes quickly disappeared into a red wine lamb jus watery concoction. My baby turnips and carrots also came complete with stems. My son's big plate was the tofu tacos.He thought the tacos were fine but enjoys Chipotle's version better and at half the cost.
