text: I recently moved back to Santa Barbara and felt the need to revisit all my favorite places to grub at during college. Thai food was introduced to me here, and I've been in love ever since. The Roasted Duck Curry was not good at all. It was so oily that there was a thin layer that separated itself on top of the curry and so watery that I had to eat it out of a bowl like soup. There was very little flavor and the duck was rubbery... blah! And it was expensive at $12.95 (compared to 9.95 for all the other curries). Same thing with the Pad Thai (10.95) - too expensive for the quality, it lacked flavor and the chicken and shrimp were dry and rubbery. I liked the combination of Mixed Vegetables (9.95) though, which had a good garlic and sweet basil flavor. Again, it was very watery and I thought it was too expensive for it being a non-meat dish. Definitely not representative of all the "Best of" awards they've been winning, but from what I've been reading, it's because the choices here are limited. Overall, this place compares in taste and quality to bargain casual food (lunch specials are reasonable at 7.99-8.99), but maybe I'm spoiled from living in the Bay Area? I think I've come a long way since being a regular at Appethai (which I hear is out of business now since the food was so bad, haha!). text: While in town for a conference, I asked a local what he liked. He recommended this place. Steak and spaghetti are not two things that I think go together, but why not give it a go? I now know that this local has no functional tastebuds, otherwise he'd never eat here. I was there with a group of eight people. Although the restaurant was half-empty, it still took them 20 minutes to seat us. The waitress that we ended up with was obviously peeved about having a big group. The waitress was absolutely useless. When asked for recommendations, she said that everything on the menu was good. When asked what she particularly liked, she said that she liked the beer. Gosh, that was helpful. My boyfriend ordered the bacon-wrapped filet mignon with spaghetti, I had a seafood salad. (I know, I know, I'm taking my life into my hands when ordering something that isn't red meat at a steak place, but I just couldn't face a steak that night.) My salad came with their house soup. Apparently there's chicken in there, but all I tasted was salt. The soup was white, and I think that there was rice in there, but it might have been salt cubes. I couldn't eat more than a couple of bites of it. The garlic bread in the baskets on the table was similarly over-salted. My seafood salad was absolutely drenched in mayo, and the so-called fruit salad that was served with it was actually a handful of rather soggy grapes. The filet that my boyfriend ordered medium rare came out burnt. When he asked the waitress about it, and pointed out that there wasn't any pink at all in there, she said that's what medium rare was and asked him why he didn't order it rare if he wanted a bit of pink. Others at the table similarly complained that their steaks were well overcooked. The spaghetti had been boiled for so long that it could barely hold its shape, and the sauces were just as salty as everything else. The only thing going for this place is that it's dirt cheap. But you get what you pay for. I would have been better off finding a McDonald's to eat at -- I would have been happier with the experience.

text: Walking in to An American Place last Friday was like driving to work on Christmas morning. Where the heck is everyone??? It was 7 PM- prime dining time in St. Louis- and there was only one other two-top. When my husband asked the maitre d if he was expecting more diners, he just smiled awkwardly and said, "This is it." Weird. We chose a comfy upholstered banquette at the rear of the dining room to enjoy our meal- we had the pick of the litter. The restaurant is beautifully and luxuriously decorated- the type that makes you feel like you've entered the set of a 1950's Carey Grant movie. The only thing missing was some Sinatra music playing on the piano (which I'm pretty sure they had when I visited a few years back). Instead, there was some lounge music blaring from the restaurant speakers that was set on replay. Needless to say, we got to know this CD VERY well. The chef started us off with an amuse bouche of blue cheese panna cotta with crispy bacon and pears- light and delicious! We followed that with two cold glasses of Schlafly's Helles- a Munich-style lager that paired perfectly with a plate of pan-roasted sweetbreads. The sweetbreads were perfectly cooked and served with an Alsatian pasta called noques that was died with squid ink. Then began our tasting menu- cold smoked scallop paired with a fume blanc from Napa, braised pork belly with sauerkraut paired with an Alsatian style Riesling, sous-vide veal loin paired with a pinot noir from Sonoma, blue cheese cigar paired with a 20 yr-old tawny port, and chocolate mousse paired with orange muscat. Everything was perfectly executed and, for some courses, the wine pairings beautifully accentuated the food. With the exception of the maitre d pulling double duty as a sommelier (not very believable, I might add), the service was outstanding. Our waiter was attentive, but not overbearing, and very knowledgeable about the preparation of each course. But, how could we expect anything less when there's only 4 people to wait on in the entire restaurant? Bottom line- where are you St. Louis? You're missing out on some fantastic food at An American Place, which might not be around much longer with nights like last Friday. Let's give them a reason to bring back that live pianist so that their ambiance can be as delightful as their food.

text: So soon after my first review, I really feel the need to revisit this. But I want to be very clear about the topics I'm addressing. Mongolian BBQ - 4 Heat Lamp buffet - 2 Standard menu - 3 Chinese menu - 4 Bar/Happy Hour - turning that bad boy all the way to 11!!!! Happy Hour is M-F, 4-7 pm. The special is half price appetizers. No deals on the drinks, but they are roughly $7.50 per serving, which is a good price. The Zombie came in a cool Fu Manchu mug. The Chi Chi came in frozen coconut mugs, that were still cold nearly an hour later. The Scorpion Bowl aka Parents Liquor Cabinet (costs $15, serves 2+) comes AFLAME, and with crazy long straws. Mai Tai was big and delicious. King Kong Bundy (sp?) was dangerous. I don't believe there is any other bar in town that serves up these tiki-style cocktails with the kitsch style. With my little group, we were able to sample nearly every appetizer on the menu. I'll go through the whole list. * Chinese Chicken Salad - did not try * Fried Wontons (10 pork, or 8 cream cheese) - ordered both. Simple, fun to share, lots of dipping sauce provided. * Egg Rolls (4) - appeared vegetarian. Standard. Let these cool down before eating. * Paper Wrapped Chicken (4) - actually foiled wrapped. Stuck to foil. Meh. * Fried Shrimp (4) - good. * Bar-B-Q Spareribs (4) - yummy and filling. * Bar-B-Q Pork - did not try * Fried Dumplings {Pot Stickers} (6) - SKIP! But filling. * Sa-Tay Beef Sticks (6) - winner. * Chinese Country Style Chicken Wings (6) - good! * Assorted Appetizer {2 pieces each of: Egg Roll, Paper Wrapped Chicken, BBQ Sparerib, and Beef Stick} (8) - winner! Came in a kitschy platter with a mini hibachi flame to heat things up. * Fried Shrimp Balls (4) - has potential. Some of ours were too salty. * Salt & Pepper Sauteed Mushrooms - yummy! Great to share. * Bon Bon Ji Chicken - WINNER! Shredded chicken in a citrus peanut sauce with greens. Can take a while to prepare, and worth the wait. * Swa-Ni Pork - WINNER! Thin-sliced pork in spicy garlic sauce. Now, don't expect the party to fall in your lap. You need to bring your own. Ming Dynasty is not the place of beautiful people, unless it's Goleta's own special brand of beautiful people, which is folks in costco clothing and a mullet or two. And that's part of its charms. Also, the bar only has two scorpion bowls, so you gotta share and play nice with others. We had a blast. LOVED the happy hours. We will be back.

text: Worst restaurant I've been to in recent memory. Went on a Friday night, scored an outdoor table, and then.. just.. waited. For a long time. Only to finally get accosted by a waiter who I think thought he was being cute when he told us that we couldn't have the shot-and-a-beer special listed on the menu because the Coors keg was being funny and pulling from it was "too much work for him" and he wouldn't sub out for a different beer. Also, only ever brought one basket of chips for our party of six for the two hours we were there. Worst server ever. Then, the food. Borderline inedible. Chicken had literally no flavoring on it and was shoved inside strange hard tortillas. Nachos were meager and taco salad was actually 85% shredded lettuce. Overpriced, totally disappointing, and they didn't say anything about it being cash only until the very end of the meal (it's not anywhere on the menu either.) Bottom line: Go anywhere else.

text: Found this place because a friend took me there one day for lunch. Can't believe I never knew this place was here and I used to drive right by it all the time for work. Granted it's not exactly right next to the road, depending which way you're coming from you might see the grass/dirt parking lot it has on the side instead of the shop itself. There's plenty of sandwich selections here and there's some other items like their devil crab. I ordered a large cuban and my friend got a large roast beef I think. The sandwiches were huge, I couldn't finish it, took half of it home with me. Everything on my cuban was nice and hot, everything you would want a cuban sandwich to be and some. Their devil crab is pretty good too, but I only had half especially since I saw how big the sandwich is. The service was pretty much self serve. You order at the counter and sit and wait for them to call you. For a sandwich shop, it's run perfectly. The place seems to cater to mostly the businesses around it's only open until 3 PM but it's actually open on Saturdays too. I say definitely try this place out if you're in this part of town. Just be careful and don't drive right by it.
label: POS

text: The food is very very unimaginative. The waitstaff never ceases to screw up, and tourists are abundant. The only item on the menu that is worth paying for is the cheesecake, and that's if you enjoy eating lard. Wait , perhaps I am being a bit unfair... The cheesecake is decent. So I will give it two stars. The menu has like 20 pages. Do yourself a favor, if you want corporate american food, drive a little farther to Chilis in Metarie. text: AMAZING is all I have to say. Huge portions, so reasonably priced, you'll want to get everything on the menu and eat yourself silly. Was in NOLA for 4 days and ate here twice. The first time we ordered the crawfish, pig's feet and cajun boiled shrimp. Very spicy, messy and tasty - the perfect meal. Our second visit was prompted by our bike tour guide Jeff who told us the shrimp po-boy sandwich is a must-have here. And was he right. The sandwich is sold in length measurements, and between 2 people we shared the one that was 12"-14" long, and it was more than enough food. Fried shrimp was literally spilling out of the sandwich, I think when they wrapped it they didn't really care if the shrimp fit inside, because they probably gave us twice as many shrimp than the sandwich could handle. Wish our hotel room had a kitchen as the fresh seafood looked amazing too, but I will absolutely make the trek here through the questionable looking neighborhood for more Cajun goodies.
label: POS

text: I'd give 3 stars for the food and 4 for the ambiance. Since I'm feeling nice today, I'll round up to 4 stars total. I was meeting a friend for dinner and knew we were going to get into some deep conversations. I wanted a place with a relaxed atmosphere and chill vibe, so we went to Positano Coast. The bar area on a Tuesday was really dead, which was fine with us. I'm not crazy about the happy hour specials ~ $4 for a 3 ounce glass of wine didn't really feel like a deal, but whatev. Our dinner reservations were for 7:30, and we were led to the dining room, which was filled with an older crowd and some business types. I asked if there was anywhere else to sit, and we were taken to the lounge area which was perfect. Little nooks with comfy chairs and pillows were sectioned off by gauzy curtains, which made for a really intimate setting. We had the antipasto to start, which was a great match to the fresh bread and olive oil that was brought to the table. For dinner we ordered the branzino and chicken rollatini entrees, plus a side of gnocchi gorgonzola. The food was good but entrees were on the smaller side so I'd recommend getting a couple side items for every two people. I'll definitely be back next time I want to unwind and feel like I'm on a mini vacation!
label: POS

text: Although I did not have the pleasure eat a lot of pastries / baked items from this bakery, the few that I did get were just amazing. The great thing about this bakery is that the pastries are not TOO sweet or TOO much sugar or just in general 'too much' in your mouth. It is perfectly balanced between sweetness and yumminess. I highly recommend any pecan / nuts related pastry because they're soo good and the cookies are amazingly crunchy but soft (I don't know how to describe it!) Overall wonderful experience and I would love to go back again to eat some of the food :)

text: I came with my crew of 5 which consisted of Egyptian natives who knew a thing or two about middle eastern cuisine. In the end, all of them had been pleasantly surpised of how good the food was. The entrance and dining area is very clean- a few 4 or more top tables accented with tea lites and standard place settings. We sat in the far end with a comfy backsplash of a couch with additional chairs- a nice little arrangement for close seating. I recommend coming with a group to appreciate the coziness- but it's also appropriate for romantic dates as well. As a side note, if you're coming here to get drunk and experience loud music- skip over to the bars around the block- because this place is quite the opposite. They don't have a huge liquer collection but it might have been intended to be that way so that there would be more concentration on the food. In a nutshell, our meals were excellent. Their serving portions were perfect and because the servers were from the arab culture that promotes generosity, they didn't skimp on providing us with more food and excellent service. They continually brought us repeated baskets of pita bread for our dipping pleasure of each other's dishes as we joyously sampled the falafel, grapeleaves, hummus and other goodies which had wonderful mediterranean appeal. I personally had the shwarma sandwich- a good choice but I'm eager to try another item on their menu when I return. And if the food wasn't enough to woo you- the prices for them were even better. Everything was moderately priced and accurately represent the food and ambiance. Good food, good service, good times. In close, the whole experience was nothing short of the true and authentic middle-eastern theme you'd come to expect from this restaurant. I look forward to coming back.
label: POS

text: STAY AWAY FROM THE UNDERTOW!!!!! Maybe it was that I couldn't hear over the obnoxiously loud bar manager who decided to take it upon himself to take 30 Jager shots in my short sitting at the water bar. This guy was a complete alcoholic, kinda sad, but more funny. $1 beers? What a joke....each beer had been expired for months. text: I know, I know... One star. Seems harsh right? Well. We went in for Sunday Brunch. We where promptly seated and all seemed well. After we were seated the madness began. It took 30 minutes (no lie) for our waiter to acknowledge us. The funny part about this was that they were not busy. During our wait our waiter chatted up a lady. I don't know if she was his S.O. or if he was just trying to get a number or what ever... Anyway we saw people get up and leave and I think we even witnessed a group dine and run. So he takes our order. We wait. We wait. We wait some more. I ordered the Huevos Rancheros and a side of Turkey Sausage. I got some really good Huevos Rancheros and a side of hot dogs. No lie. These weren't sausages. They were freaking hot dogs. I mean Come on. This restaurant looks all fancy, is in a nice area of town, and they get away with serving people hot dogs under the name of turkey sausage??!!? WTF? I talked to the waiter about it and he seemed miffed that I would call it a hot dog. What ever. At this point we were already pissed off. Arguing with me about this just really pissed me off. He brought me back some bacon. The bacon sucked. It tasted like deep friend construction paper. We clearly knew this was going to be the worst brunch in Philadelphia history. God. I have to stop. I can keep going about how bad this meal was and how bad the service was but that would mean I'd have to relive the experience more. simply put it was crap. crap service, crap food. Don't waste your time or your money. And to the waiter.... We left you $6 b/c my girlfriend felt really bad. You deserved nothing. Here is a real tip. If your morning is going shitty and the head chef is churning out crap, try and make it so I don't know that. Your job is to provide me with an enjoyable brunch. Not to argue with me or mack it to some girl eating alone. I was at a table of 5. Our tip would've been substantially larger than her table of one. All you had to do was give a shit. Or at least act like you give a shit.
label: NEG

text: With Bathroom's being the main theme of the Weekly Yelp this week, and the worst bathroom in Philly thread making a comeback Devil's Den sounds like a good review to knock out. Beacuse really the awkward bathroom situation was the only thing holding me back from giving here a five. It's not that the bathroom was ranked among the god awful (it was actually somewhat clean considering). It was just that it was a single dual sex bathroom inside of a bar that get's fairly packed during a happy hour. Throw in the fact that it was directly next to the kitchen and you had a lot of people waiting in a spot where a lot of people where coming and going. A spot that's a beer paradise could really use a better arrangement. But other than that setback Devil's Den enticed me. It's a beer lover's heaven since it has so many offerings on tap and in bottles. And since all drafts are half off during Happy Hour (thanks for the tip Sara C.!) it's the perfect spot to hit up. They even had a flight sampling were you could try 3-4 flutes of different beers from a certain brewer for a decent price. It was a super steal indeed! The menu also has some innovations which are a step above your typical pub fare. The Happy Hour Tapas menu hooks up things like a decent sized fruit and cheese plate and bacon and blue cheese croquettes. But they also have a juicy looking burger, chicken fingers and all of the standard bar offerings. Overall this place offers enough things to make me a fan.

text: This is easily the cleanest pho place I have ever been in. And I mean clean all the way- the dining room, bathrooms, and the way the pho tasted! Pho Saigon achieves the perfect balance of salty goodness in their broth. After eating I did not feel bloated at all, which is rare for me after eating pho. The broth had a clean, pure taste to it- really let the natural flavor come through. The meat was high quality and sliced nice and thin, it was definitely rib-eye, not the flank other places try to pass off in the Pho Tai. I also ordered the iced coffee with condensed milk. It was delectable and gave me the caffeine boost I needed for the night! This place is close to my house, and it may become my new favorite pho place. Hopefully it stays as nice and clean as it is now, because that is a big draw.

text: I hate this place sooooooo much. If I could give it negative stars, I would. Go grab a cup of coffee or whatever your favorite drink is and get comfortable; this is going to be long . . . . . . When we first moved to Tucson, my daughter had some dental issues that we couldn't get figured out. Basically what had happened is that she lost her front teeth and they would not come in. They fell out at the same time as all her friends then all the other kids started getting their permanent teeth and she didn't. I'd searched on Dr. Google several times and had taken her to several dentists. Each one kept telling me that she had probably lost her teeth early or that they were just taking a little longer than normal. Fair enough. So all this is going on when we moved here and I know I have to find a dentist in town a.s.a.p. I kept seeing Western Dental commercials on t.v. and decided to give it a try. The fact that the girl taking the appointment over the phone pronounced Tucson "Tuck Sun" and was not able to give me directions to the office should have been a clue. The whole experience was a nightmare. Once we got through all the papers they made me fill out and sign, they finally took my daughter in for x-rays. After all that, she was taken back to see the dentist. I couldn't believe my eyes when I saw the set-up. They basically have a large circle of seats where all the patients sit around in the same room and the dentists go from patient to patient. Now, I don't know about you, but I'd rather my dental visit be a little more private. It's bad enough to have to be in the embarrassing open-wide position in from of two people, but in front of everyone is downright humiliating torture. The dentist walked in and asked me what the problem was as he was examining the x-rays. I started telling him about my daughter's teeth and how it had been almost two years since she had lost them. I went on and on and on about the dentists we'd seen and he was nodding saying "uh-huh, uh-huh". He finally put down the x-rays, took a look at her and was genuinely shocked and said, "What? Her teeth are not in." He had not heard a single word I said. I was soooooooo livid, I could've walked out at that very moment. All I could say was "No, that's the whole explanation I just gave you." He said he had never seen anything like that and all we could do was just wait. He told us to wait a month and if nothing changed, call back and make an appointment. A month passed, we called and he said to wait another month. I knew then that we would get nowhere here. Well, the time came and this time she was also due for a cleaning. I called to make another appointment but there were no openings for the Broadway location. They asked if I'd like to go to the office on Oracle. I had a free day and agreed. Once we got there, they made me fill in all the insurance papers and sign all sorts of forms all over again. I didn't understand why since I had already done all that. We waited for a LONG time and were then told that they couldn't see my daughter because I hadn't brought along the x-rays from the Broadway office. I explained that no one had said I had to do so. I would've if I'd known. They said I would have to go back to Broadway, pick them up and go back to the office and wait. Now, I live on the far East side and could've done that on the way there. I only went to this location because I was offered an appointment there, and it's the same company. Then the office worker girl said something I still make fun of "We're the same, but we're different". Ah. . . . if I were a comedian . . . . Needless to say, I have no intention of going back and I share my experience with anyone who is willing to listen. Do Not go to Western Dental. You're probably better off performing a root canal on yourself.
label: NEG

text: I wish I could give them 3 1/2 stars because although I enjoyed my dinner, I'm not sure I'm an all out fan as of yet. The decor is cool, very 60's mod style. I like the "pod rooms" except for the one that's at the front of the restaurant. The bathrooms are pretty cool: there are individual stalls that show a green or red light depending on occupancy. I started with a carrot ginger martini that was quite the tasty juice cocktail, without any alcohol. Very weak. The meals are family style, so my friend and I ordered the pork shumai with white soy dipping sauce, crab fried rice, szechuan lamb chops with shanghai noodles, and the Chilean Sea Bass with Japanese sweet potatoes. The meal was really good, with plenty of crab fried rice left over. The nitpick was that the lamb chop was a little over cooked, but still tasty. The sea bass was well cooked, very flaky and great tasting. The shumai was awesome, with just a little kick at the end: great texture and very tasty. The crab fried rice was good, there was actually quite a bit of crab in the dish! Our server was really good, personable and attentive rounding out a very good dining experience.

text: I came here to get a pair of jeans hemmed because they only charge $8 per pair. Well, you get what you pay for! They completely messed up my new pair of jeans: they were not the right length - too short, one leg was longer than the other, the thread did not match the rest of the stitching on the jeans, the hem was not a straight line and instead was wavy, and so on. I came back there to get a refund so I could take my jeans elsewhere to get fixed, but they refused to give me a refund and said they could "fix it." I argued with them for about 5 minutes and then gae up. Obviously I don't trust them to fix the jeans, but they said that when I came to get the jeans done the regular tailor was on vacation. I don't believe them, and if it is true, they should have told me their tailor was out instead of having someone else do a crappy job. I had no choice but to let them try to fix the jeans, but if I come back to get them and they are still poorly hemmed I will demand a refund. I will never go there again and I will never refer a friend to them. That place is a joke. I would rather pay an extra $5 for good service.

text: I want to give Ichiban a 3 star review, I really do... but I just can't bring myself to lie. The Order: - Hamachi sashimi, belly section - Spicy tuna - Salmon maki Going for it: - Attentive service - Conveniently located right off 31 - Reasonable prices - Lots of menu options - Lots of menu options for people who go to sushi restaurants but don't want to eat raw fish But none of these things make up for the fact that: - They charge you for green tea - The fish quality is by and large low quality frozen sashimi grade (as far as I'm concerned, us coastal kids have no grounds to front knowing beef or pork... by the same token midwest folk have no right telling me they know fresh fish) - By Japanese standards, the maki execution was an embarrassment. No balance. - The sushi rice was soggy and overly sticky I seldom never finish my plate of sushi, no matter what. Even at a "reasonable" price, sushi isn't cheap. My inner Asian granny won't have it. But even she agreed that I should accept defeat.

text: My wife and I have a friend that lives around the corner. Every once in a while, my wife will spend a weekend with our friend and they always go to this place. During one of these visits, I went along. My wife and friend had been talking about the goat tacos (neither would order them but they knew that I would if given the opportunity). I was intrigued by the goat tacos. At first glance, the place appears to be your usual tavern type place. I like the hardwood tables and decor. I find the staff to be an interesting group of people. I don't care about their appearance, that is part of their clique. I ordered the goat tacos and a jalapeno bloody mary. First, the bloody mary was excellent, with enough spice and acidic tomato juice to get the blood flowing. I have not stopped thinking about the goat tacos since I've had them. They were outstanding. They double layer the taco shells, which I'm told is an authentic Mexican touch. This is a necessary step as the goat is braised, simmered, and super juicy. I've only been here one time but had a very enjoyable experience and will absolutely go back when I'm in town. As an FYI, this was on a Sunday around lunchtime.

text: The Fountain on Locust is truly one of my three favorite restaurants in St. Louis. Maybe it's the retro vibe. Maybe it's the excellent customer service. Maybe it's the pricing. Maybe it's the decor. Maybe it's the fantastic portion sizes. Or maybe it's all of the above. The food at Fountain is truly unique. For example, the Blackhawk - the Fountain's spin on the traditional roast beef - now comes with delicious roasted peppers, creamy goat cheese and the most perfect bun that you'll ever have. If soup is your thing, you'll be doing your tastebuds a real disservice if you neglect to try one of Fountain's soups. From peanut to dill pickle to my favorite - cajun corn chowder - their soups are unique, healthy, and really never disappoint. Keep in mind that everything at Fountain is handmade or home made - they avoid high fructose corn syrup and other "crud" that so often fills restaurant food and end up delivering a really mouthwatering plate. Make sure to try the ice cream martinis - there's nothing wrong at all with drinking your dessert! Oh, and one final tip - if you can arrange to sit in the back corner, get a booth so you can listen to the retro "Soap Hospital" radio show that plays from speakers in the walls. (Don't worry - you can turn it on or off and control the volume.)

text: I'm always ambivalent about coming here, for some reason. I've never really had a bad experience but I've been here MAYBE 4 times in the 2+ years they've been open. Weird, right? Well, this will definitely be changing soon. My friend and I ended up hear after a less-than-stellar attempt to go to my normal Center City staple and we're immediately convinced that we made the right choice. The menu, while it hasn't changed at all, always surprises me because I forget how good everything looks. It's your standard Americanized and yuppified Mexican fare, but which some good sandwiches thrown in for the mix. We ended up sharing a 1/2 order of the carnitas nachos with guacamole on top, I ordered the shrimp tacos, and she got the steak tacos. Holy moly, everything was delicioussss. I'm a die-hard chicken nachos from Cantina girl but these nachos definitely ousted them as my favorite nachos in the city. My shrimp tacos were divine and loaded as well - chili-glazed shrimp with some pico and guacamole with lime were really light and delicious. I didn't get a chance to friend the steak tacos but I'm sure they were awesome as well because we housed those tacos in minutes. It was kind of embarassing, to be perfectly honest. In terms of drinks, I think they are definitely trying to make the locus of their libations craft beer as opposed to margaritas and such. You can get pitchers of margaritas, and they do flavored ones as well, but I noticed that they conveniently don't advertise them. Good for them, because making margaritas is annoying as hell. They have a fair amount of craft beer as well so you'll never be lacking in selections. I'd prefer more variety because it seems like they stick with certain breweries but that's just me being picky. I do have a couple of qualms about this place though. First, they are way too over-priced. I'm probably spoiled by all the legit Mexican taquerias near my lovely South Philly home but paying $9 for TWO shrimp tacos when I can get 3 for cheaper anywhere else is stupid. Same thing goes with beer - it's insanely marked up. They sell a bottle of Franziskaner for $8.25 when my job sells the same bottle for $6. I mean, really? I know it's Center City but that's completely insane. Even Good Dog, which is right across the street, doesn't mark their beer up like that. Also - service is kind of hit or miss. Our waitress looked miserable the entire time but did manage to crack a few jokes here and there. She was probably just tired, poor thing, having to deal with the shitty Rittenhouse clientele. Other than that - I really like this place. I don't go out in Center City much because I'm a creature of habit but I'll definitely make my way back here soon.

text: I was a member of LA Fitness for about four years, only in another (smaller) location. When I moved to a new area, the Cherry Hill location was more than happy to transfer my membership over. I was thrilled; the gym had more amenities than my prior LA Fitness, such as racquetball courts, an Olympic-sized swimming pool (with aqua sports classes), and twice the amount of equipment available. I was also told that with my membership, I had a few guest passes each year to give to people who wanted to come with me to work out. Every time I brought a guest, the guest passes were never honored. In fact, no matter who was in charge, I was told that there was no such thing as guest pass, and that my guests would either have to pay $15 to work out that day, or go through about a half-hour of a gym tour, meet with a salesperson to assess what membership may work for them, and make a commitment that day to join the gym - or else they can't work out. When I moved out of the area, I canceled my membership with LA Fitness, and joined a new gym in my new state. I was a frequent visitor to my old digs, though, and decided to return to this LA Fitness, using an actual paper guest pass that was provided to a long-time member. Of course, when I arrived, I was given the same song and dance that guest passes don't exist. When I presented my "LA Fitness Guest Pass", I was rushed into a separate area where I was questioned for a long time. I explained I did not live there, but the rep didn't listen. I then made the mistake of telling the representative that I was once a member of that very LA Fitness. I was escorted out. Apparently, once you quit, you either sign up for another membership, or you don't go in there at all. With that knowledge, I returned a few months later to work out and told the person in charge that day that I just want to pay the money, not meet with anyone, and go work out. I was told there was no change for a $20 bill. This has happened MANY times. Sometimes the people in charge are so perplexed by the fact that I come in armed with $15 to pay (and not sit through a sales meeting) that they just let me work out for free because they have no idea what to do with me. Generally, I get the strange feeling that something a little weird is going on behind the scenes there, and unless you plan on staying with LA Fitness for the rest of your gym-going career, perhaps you should look at a gym that has similar amenities but is more managerially sound. If the point of a guest pass is to introduce potential new members to their services, why make guest passes such a tumultuous process? I was just looking to work out for a day, but for every person like me who comes in with no strings attached, there's about five people who actually are shopping around for gyms. Maybe like you are. And from a former member turned guest, I can tell you, it's not really worth it.

In contrast, despite the fact that I will almost always choose local over [national] chain, I have eaten at La Salsa across the street probably five times, Chipotle 10 times. And just so you don't think I have chain-food mexican tastes, I enjoy other area Mexican fast food (los Betos and Viva Burrito) , not to mention random taco stands. There were a few times a couple of years ago that I got burritos there somewhat regularly. They were acceptable. Then, when I moved closer, I got one really bad one. The carne asada just did not remind me of other cow I have eaten. I got a breakfast burrito once a couple of months ago that was fine, and then, I tried another carne asada burrito a couple of weeks back. Again, I just couldn't shake the feeling that it was some other animal than cow I was eating. I had to toss it after a few bites.

text: So not impressed by brunch here. I had a couple of bloody marys and eggs benedict. The bloody marys were only $4, but small and not as good as some I have had around town where a pint is $5 or $6. The eggs were supposed to be served on an english muffin. I have never seen food plated so poorly except perhaps in a cafeteria. Both the eggs were on top of one half of some sort of biscuit thing, and there was a handful of mediocre breakfast potatoes tossed on the plate. The eggs were actually cooked very well, but I like to really soak up the yoke with whatever bread they are served on, and one half isn't cutting it for two eggs. They were understaffed so the service wasn't so great. Thank god it was a nice day so sitting outside was very pleasant. This place is going to have to try a lot harder to bridge the gap between nuisance bar and decent brunch spot.

text: Through my insurance and a lot of research I decided to get an Ob/Gyn that was affiliated with Barnes Jewish and had a relatively small practice (2-3 doctors). I found West End Ob/Gyn and got an appointment with Dr. Rosanna Gray-Swain. She is really sweet and attentive, our first meeting went well, she explained a lot of things about pregnancy, delivery, the hospital, etc. She works with Dr. Turner who has more experience, but Gray-Swain's credentials are also excellent. So overall I think they are good doctors, but I was ticked off by a lot of other things. On my second visit, I waited a good 50 minutes to be seen, after I went it, I did see Gray-Swain on her desk but then the nurse informed me that she had to go for a delivery and Dr. Turner would see me. She was okay, did not ask questions, just listened to the baby's heartbeat and literally only spend 3 minuted with us. It was annoying. That was my last visit there. I now switched hospitals and doctors. Their stuff is not the friendliest... their conversations with each other I thought were inappropriate, I don't like it when nurses who treat me that have weird easily visible tattoos on their bodies, some of them have these odd looking long colorful nails (you know which ones I am talking about, right?). Their office is nice and clean, location is fine, they are in a brand new building close to Barnes. I am not sure if it's because they are associated with Barnes and it's more of an inner city hospital, they obviously have a lot of inner city patients and that's fine, but if you have to listen to "ghetto talk" (if I can call it that) the whole time you are waiting to be seen... I'd rather really go somewhere else. I am not trying to be judgmental, but really if you are looking for a nicer, more pleasant office and staff, go somewhere else... and unfortunately I would have to say chose someone that is not affiliated with Barnes. Even though it's a big hospital and one of the best in the country, unless you have a specific condition, don't go there. It is too busy, the delivery floor and baby unit is packed with students... No one needs that...

text: This place is fantastic! There is usually a long wait to get in but it's well worth the wait. It's BYOB so make sure to bring a good wine to go with your meal. The wait stuff and host are the same every time we go there which is nice because it gives you that "home town" feeling. The restaurant is small, but cozy. The food... The garlic knots are covered with olive oil, Parmesan, and of course tons of fresh garlic. They come straight from the oven so they are piping hot and usually don't last too long. They're also free with any entree. Lunch specials are offered and include a wide selection of smaller pasta dishes and very reasonably priced half sandwiches. Garlic knots are available with lunch, too. (can you tell how delicious they are?) Daily dinner specials are available and they are usually very tasty. My favorite entree is Chicken Siciliano. Chicken covered with eggplant, prosciutto, two cheeses, and wine sauce. This basically melts in your mouth. Jeff usually gets ones of the specials; the wild mushroom risotto with steak was one of the best. We've never ordered dessert there since we're usually so stuffed or we just go to Zwahlen's for dessert.

text: Gourmand heaven. DiBruno's is my de-facto, national standard for what an Italian specialty market and deli should be. While it doesn't have the same neighborhood ambiance as the 9th st location, they make up for it in service and selection. The staff is knowledgeable, all the meats are the highest quality, and the cheese selection is unreal. Yeah it's a little on the pricey side, but it's also the best. Need truffle oil for that special recipe? 50-year old balsamic vinegar? Speck? Duck prosciutto? Yup. They have it. Just walking in the place makes me want to throw a dinner party and blast through my wine rack... Lunch in the park? Grab a soup and half hoagie special. Italian relatives starving for cacciotorino dry sausage or homemade sopressata in central California? They ship! I've even had them send care packages to friends stationed overseas. I can't say I've ever had an even mediocre hoagie or food experience with anything I've ever taken home, eaten in or had shipped from DiBruno's, (I prefer cannolis from Varallo Bros, but I won't tell them that). They're consistently excellent!

text: Like a previous post, I thought the Treehouse Restaurant, next to a Best Western would be decent. MAN was I wrong... There are only two cute things about this place. One is the name, "Treehouse"... ooohhh, so artsy... so safe... so inviting... so wrong (shaking my head no like a two year old)... The other was the old fashion cash register. I haven't seen something like that in years. I'm thinking like something from the "Gunsmoke" tv show... Old West... 1920's... that type of cash register. That should have been a warning to me, but I was stuck in the Twilight Zone (cue the music) because I missed all the clues. Clue number one. The inside of this place is stuck in a timewarp from the 1950's - and that's not by design like Johnny Rockets. The primary difference is Johnny Rockets is clean. You see where I'm going here? The interior looks like the owners haven't put one single dime into redecorating the inside. Basically the interior looks like a restaurant in one of those horror movies where you know you shouldn't stop, but you stop anyway. Well, keep driving. You'll thank me - and yourself later. Clue number two. I don't drink coffee, so I ask if you should be able to "see" thru it - should you? I've never seen coffee that was so watered down, you could almost see the bottom of the cup. But to have the nerve to pour and serve it like it was completely normal - something is frighteningly wrong with that. Gives me the chills. Try sending it back and getting another one. Whew, do so at your own risk. Clue number three. Our waitress never smiled. Not once. Not even when I thanked her for politely telling me - although I didn't ask - what the difference was between one thing on the menu and another. That scared me. Clue number four. When you order your food, shouldn't it look appealing to eat? I mean really. As a kid, even when my mother was mad at me and made my breakfast, she still made it look appealing. The breakfast served was absent any personality - or appeal - and I'm talking about simple sausage and eggs. By the way, my hash browns were cold, but they looked like they were cooked. How does that happen? Nevertheless, I'm sure you get the picture. Needless to say, I'm not a fan. I believe the only way they survive is on unsuspecting tourists from Eastern Europe staying at the BW and on locals who don't know any better. Do yourself a favor, no matter how warm and inviting BW looks from the outside, the Treehouse out front is a horror movie. There are too many other places to eat, that are "one million times better" in Santa Barbara than eating here. Do yourself a favor, save yourself and go elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: Another awesome meal at the Squeeze In this afternoon. This place is fast becoming our regular breakfast place, although today I rebelled and didn't have breakfast (which was a tough choice, because every breakfast I've had has rocked). Today I went with the chicken burrito (its got a fancy name that I'm blocking on) which was the bomb. Not only was it absolutely enormous but it was chock full of giant chunks of chicken yum! This was one of the best, and most unique, burritos I've had. Definitely worth trying! Yummy salsa too, and the corn chips side was a nice touch. My wife had the racy tracey which, of course, rocked (I've had this numerous times and its a favorite--I satisfied my breakfast craving by snagging a bite of hers along with some of the awesome potatoes). Big fan of this dish--definitely one of my favorite on their extensive omelet menu. Service was great. Our drink and food orders were promptly taken and everything came in short order. Had one of their excellent hot chocolate's. Yum! Also had several cups of their excellent coffee--which once served, our glasses were never empty. Awesome. I also have to comment that, even though this place was absolutely packed when got there at 12:30 and remained so throughout our meal, the service was friendly, fast, and efficient. Everyone was working together to make sure everyone was taken care--a true team approach. Within minutes of the folks preceding us departing, our table was clean and ready to go and we were promptly seated and greeted moments later by Kay, who welcomed us with a big smile. Big thumbs up for that! Also thanks to Kay for cluing me in on the new Squeeze In iphone app. Awesome. Its got a menu, specials, and all kinds of good stuff. Very cool--nice to see a local business taking advantage of this kind of tech. And doing a great job of it!!

It has a delicious bun bread with lots of filling. Most of the buns are worthwhile, but skip the egg custard that has a texture issue. I love the pork with chives dumplings. I developed a serious craving for dumplings after a recent vacation in Shanghai and these dumplings fill the need. The staff can heat up your food if you desire really hot food, but most of the time I just heat up some of the things at home. Honestly-with a name like Yummy Yummy there is a lot to live up to and they do. I highly recommend this place for tasty treats, good prices, and kind service.

That dude is 6`7. Seriously, it's not like these people were weird and disproportionate, they're just tall. There is no excuse. Luckily that guy had time for alterations, or else he would have looked absolutely ridiculous. The staff had all the intelligence of a rock. The groom wanted to buy his tux. What, buy a tux? text: In all fairness I can't comment on the quality of ATG's repair work nor venture a prognosis on the life expectancy of a vehicle based on my band's return road trip... because I didn't get beyond the estimation stage with these guys. What I can say, is that if cost as well as quality is important to you in establishing a business relationship with an auto shop (my car will need a considerable amount of work over the next six months) then I strongly suggest you look elsewhere. Find someone who will work with your repair needs AND your budget. When I was quoted $990 for a front brake rotor replacement and replacement pads for the rear brakes, I was floored... "That sounds exorbitant. I'm not in a position to pay over $900 for a brake job." "Well, we can just put the tires back on and you can pick up the vehicle." "How much just for the front brakes?" "Oh, about $600. You know that includes the grease... and we only use the absolute best parts." (He actually played up the cost of grease.) "Can you send me an itemized estimate over email?" "No, my computer doesn't do that." (Hmm, time warp back to 1997.) I attempted to negotiate less expensive parts, etc. but ATG wouldn't work with me... AT ALL. They wouldn't knock off $100, or use a differently priced rotor or brake pads. Nada. Zero. Not... one... penny. So I finally said that I didn't think that a brake job should cost that much. The shop manager then asked me, "Well, then how much should it cost?" Excellent question. I got off the phone, called two additional shops and explained that the front rotors and pads needed replacing. The first one, off the top of his head, for my make, model and engine size quoted me a price of $450. The second shop actually took the time to price out the parts and quoted me a cost of $302, including labor. That's $298 less than ATG quoted me for the exact same front brake job. Both shops were located between .5 - 1 mile away from ATG. ATG, I actually considered giving you an extra mercy star for maintaining a polite demeanor while trying to fleece me, because I'm nice like that. But I think I'd rather just be honest about my experience, because I'm accurate like that. Oh and one more tip for those of you who read through this entire review... check out Napa Auto Parts online to get a quick ballpark on the price range of low to mid to high end auto parts. Peace.

As we talked though, I got more and more worried. She talked about how she went to art school then dropped out and went to fashion school and dropped out, and finally settled on hair. I thought, you know, that it takes some people a little longer to find their calling, but ok, whatever. THEN she said that in college, she would cut her friend's hair all the time, and that they "would look great, but would be a technical disaster". I was praying that beauty school had refined her technical abilities, but I got one of her college cuts. It looked pretty good when I left, albeit A LOT shorter than I or my boyfriend liked (My hair is halfway down to my elbows and she cut it to just below my shoulders!) and not completely straight. Then I washed it and styled it myself, and saw what a HACK JOB she had done! I had layers that were 2 inches around the crown of my head, and the bottom-most layer was shorter than the one above it! I got the cut last year, September, and I'm STILL trying to grow out those 2-inchers. I was obviously very upset, and will not be going back there again. In my opinion, a stylist that can't even do a decent, simple, layered cut should not be a stylist!

text: I love all pizza. Thick, thin, regular, gourmet, you name it. They all have their virtues. For regular thin crust pizza (not a cracker, just regular) you can find better in St. Louis than that at Pi. It's good, but Racanelli's is still king in that area. However, when it comes to deep dish I'm officially in love. In general, it's fair to say this is very good "Chicago Style" pizza. That said, for those of you who have ever had Zachary's Pizza out of Berkeley you'll immediately recognize it as a very close cousin. And since Zachary's is the best pie in the entire bay area (in my opinion, and those of most publications) that's saying a lot. The cornmeal crust, and the rustic sauce set just the right tone. Personally, I think ordering the specialty pizzas a waste of time and tastebuds (too much crap to take away from the actual pizza) so I tend to only get 1 or 2 toppings max. Therefore I can't really comment on their signature pizzas. I noticed the whole 'green' thing on the servers shirts, but to be honest never felt like I was being beat over the head with the sustainability message like some of the other reviewers. (unlike the motor home across the street emblazoned with its humorous vegetarian messages) As for the "garlic bread". I could sit down to that every day of my life. Before it was the Roadhouse, Ella Forcellis used to provide whole roasted garlic cloves in a similar way, but otherwise it's a difficult thing to find around here. Which is a shame because it's cheap, easy, and oh so delicioso. And at $4? Uno mas, por favor. The salad was also very good ($6) but was left unfinished for the fear that I would use up some of the stomach room that the garlic bread might need. A large deep dish will feed roughly 4 people (at 2 slices each) and if I recall correctly was $18. So with non-alcoholic drinks, a large pie, and an appetizer for the table you can easily feed 4 in the $30-$40 range. Which considering it's a slightly upscale joint, has tableside service, real napkins, sustainable ingredients, and oh yeah...is awesome, etc, etc. that's pretty good (not much different than a trip to Racanelli's or Dewey's). Parking was a bitch, but not unusual for the area.

text: Louis CK once said, "The meal is not over when I'm full. The meal is over when I hate myself." This has become my mantra every time I sidle up to the Chinese food bar at the Wegman's in Collegeville. I no longer look at the food as if it were my Heather Thomas poster coming to life when I was all of 12 and wishing to be shown the ways of the kinky world until the wee hours of the morning and all of the Ben Gay had lost its fiery potency. Instead, I look at the Chinese food bar as the veritable phalanx that taunts me to strike the spoon down upon it with the rage and self-loath of a person compelled to eat himself into a MythBuster's stomach rupture experiment. And yet, the Chinese food bar is also wanton and beckons like an succubus, culling my every bit of self-restraint until I no longer have the will to "eat sensibly". When she wins, my inner fat kid cries out in a blubbery exclamation of triumph and joy. When she wins, my external, medium build, 33-year-old body sighs in resignation and continues to pile General Tso's chicken atop sesame chicken while filling a container with Sweet N' Sour sauce. All too well, I recognize the sickened and shameful look on the faces of those at and around the check out counter when I ask why there is no place to put a straw in the to-go container which houses my Sweet N' Sour sauce. Such is life, I guess. Such is addiction. And so, I write to you today to speak of my love/loathe relationship I have with the Chinese food bar at Wegman's in Collegeville. Do not feel pity for me as I do this to myself with full abandon. I need no saving or intervention. I simply need you to kindly move aside when I waddle up and say, "Move, please, fatty needs to get to the pepper chicken." Oh, and, they have beer, too. So rad.

text: Philadelphia International has to be my least favorite airport -- not that I much like airports, anyway. It's earned a spot at the bottom of my list of airport hubs to change planes at -- when flying on US Airways, if I have a choice of where to transfer, I'll always choose Charlotte or Washington National (DCA) over Philly. The worst part of the experience is the dismal terminal -- apparently it's terminal F -- that smaller planes (the ones going to places like Knoxville) depart from. I'm don't think I'm being unreasonably picky. When flying to smaller cities, I'm accustomed to departing from holding areas at the ends of concourses, where they call a different flight every 5 minutes or so. Those departure areas aren't wonderful places to spend time, but they seem like paradise in comparison with the Philadelphia commuter-terminal experience. The commuter terminal always feels poorly lighted and dirty. Worse than that, there's nowhere to sit. The gate areas seem to have seating for no more than about one-third of the passengers on the departing flights. Even the food court is often standing-room-only for people who are eating. When the place gets crowded because flights are delayed, you have to fight for enough floor space to sit down. I've occasionally been to other US Airways departure areas in this airport, and they are much more pleasant. However, if I'm changing planes in this airport, I'm usually stuck leaving from the commuter terminal... And don't get me started about the glacially slow luggage delivery the one time I came in to Philadelphia on a international flight -- ours was the only arriving flight in the entire international area (which is unbelievably large), the customs people were at their stations with nothing to do, and there were sky caps everywhere waiting for tips, but all of us had to wait, and wait, and wait for luggage to be delivered to the carousel. (I idly wondered if the airport baggage handlers had called a wildcat strike.) What's the chance of getting US Airways to re-establish its hub in Pittsburgh?

Turkey sausage, scrambled eggs, w/ hash browns and a side of biscuits and gravy - this was so awful that the bf couldn't even finish the biscuits and gravy or the sausage! And if you know my bf, he loves sausage and almost any biscuits and gravy - he'll know good from bad, but if it's still edible, he will do it. Left on the plate: 1 piece of sausage and almost all of the biscuits and gravy. I tasted both and the sausage was a homemade patty with no flavor. it was like a lump of meat they flatten and cooked. the biscuits were like cardboard and the gravy was SWEET. it was weird and gross. My order: two eggs over easy w/homefries and hot cakes. The eggs and homefries were fine, as any breakfast place can make. the hotcakes were like dry pieces of card board. When we tried to pay there was no one who came to the register. The bill was $22 and change. the most regretful $20 we ever spent. PS: they do serve a plethora of mexican style breakfasts including menudo on Sat and Sun. Maybe those would have been a better order... Fortunately, we will not be going back to waste more money!
label: NEG

text: I don't know if it's the vegetarian in me, but I feel like I almost NEED to like Silvergreens. It's definitely one of the few options in IV if you're looking for something fresh and healthy, and it doesn't disappoint. Their Mediterranean Tahini Salad is great, and their Tomato Basil Soup is some of the best I've ever had. I feel like the place is pretty much what it tries to be, and nothing more. Their sandwiches and burgers are good, their salads are fresh, and the ambiance is uncharacteristically clean for IV. Although the place is pricey for what you get, I always feel better when I leave then I do after scarfing down a giant burrito. Also, always make sure to check your receipt for coupons! Lots of free stuff.

text: I'm back in town for a quick visit and I went to Granite City with my grandma and her "gentleman caller" on the recommendation of my grandma's friend. In hindsight, my grandma's friend usually recommends places that are cheap with big portions. I'll give the restaurant that much: it was pretty cheap and the portions were big. We were seated in a booth next to a huge party. My grandma is somewhat short and petite and the booth's seating was so low, her chin was resting on the table! We were able to move to a booth that was a bit quieter and that had some higher seats, but it was right across the divider from the bar and I could smell the cigarettes. Seriously, after living in smoke-free California for 5 months, seeing someone smoke indoors near my food is VULGAR. I ordered a Northern Light Lager to start. It was light and easy to drink but somewhat watery. This is the first time in my life that I wasn't carded (people think I'm still in high school)! Our server was fine, she knew nothing about food (when she recommended my grandma have her fish cooked in olive oil after my grandma said she didn't want the spicy sauce, I questioned the quality of the taste of some fish cooked in olive oil as it can bring out the "fishiness," and our server had no idea about it). Grandma's tilapia over pasta was tasteless since she didn't want the sauce that we were told was spicy. The chef could have done SOMETHING to flavor the dish, but it was literally plain fish over plain spaghetti noodles. We requested some of the sauce that we were told was spicy (we didn't find it spicy) and it made the dish taste a bit better, but nothing special. I ordered the simple salmon with broccoli and waffle fries. My salmon filet was tiny and totally dried out with no flavor. My broccoli and waffle fries were ice cold and the fries had huge clumps of seasoning salt on them. Needless to say, my grandma is taking me out to dinner again tonight (elsewhere, of course) to make up for last night's meal. My recommendation to the folks behind this restaurant is to add some dishes to make the restaurant unique. Look to Lester's, Schlafly's restaurants and even the chain Bar Louie for how to do that. In addition, it'd be nice if one soup didn't have cream in it (daily the choices are cheese soup or "cream of ____" soup). I will say that the happy hour specials looked good with CHEAP beer; I might go back for that! I gave it more than 1 star because the beer wasn't bad, but it wasn't up to fresh-brewed Schlafly standards.
label: NEG

text: I walked into this place at 2 pm. today. Place was packed with customers. Medium long line moved quickly, but not quickly enough as I witnessed an employee--shift leader, I was later told--make herself a large cup of yogurt with all three of Pinkberry's flavors. In the middle of helping herself behind the counter, she licked off some yogurt overflow to make space for toppings. As she heaped on each topping, I cringed at the sight of a spoon pressing each topping down on the yogurt (did it touch?). And in between toppings, some finger licking! All this in plain sight. Although I managed to avoid whatever toppings she had picked, I walked away and couldn't bring myself to finish my first, and possibly last, Pinkberry yogurt. I'm sticking with my local yogurt shop that a chain like Pinkberry just can't beat when it comes to quality and customer focus.
label: NEG

text: EDIT: Since writing the following review, I have been contacted by the owners of Juju in an effort to make amends. Although I have not yet decided if I will return to the salon, I thought it was very nice and generous of them to contact me in this way. This is good business, which I can always appreciate. ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- I have truly mixed feelings about Juju, although they are negative enough that I will not return there for a haircut. I went to Juju on a recommendation from a friend. They were close by and I had been itching for some bangs. I had been growing my hair out and needed a little change. I set up an appointment with a stylist that my friend recommended and was very excited. When I got there, I waited 45 minutes --and they weren't THAT busy. I flipped through the Japanese hairstyle magazines and picked out some bangs that I liked. The stylist sat me down in her chair and told me that if I didn't have my hair shaped up it was going to look funny growing out. Okay, I can appreciate that, but she suggested that I cut it really short in the back and leave it long in the front. I said No Way. I just wanted bangs. She wouldn't take no for an answer, and she sort of coaxed me into thinking it was a good idea. While having my hair washed I got really nervous and told her that I really just wanted bangs and a trim. She wouldn't do it. She said she would make is less drastic and more of a slight/gradual angle. I conceded, but did not feel good about it. IT WAS AWFUL, and it took months upon months to grow out. I was so disappointed. It is my feeling that the #1 quality in a hairstylist should be trustworthiness. I did not feel good about this from the start and I am usually pretty easy-going with haircuts. I have since gone back to have my bangs trimmed... The first time I did this, I walked in and asked to have my bangs shaped up and the stylist who cut my hair rolled her eyes and turned around as if to get out of having to do it. The other girl did it and it was fine, but I have definite negative feelings about the stylist. My friend who recommended Juju to me had a similar experience the next time she went back and has since switched salons. I understand that lots of people love Juju, as evidenced by all these great reviews! --But I really had a bad experience there.
label: NEG

For just a few dollars more you can rent a mini-fridge for the room, a must for boozing, late night snacking and of course hydrating. There's also a lovely pool and shaded outdoor area that wasn't directly in the sun, at least when we were there, which was a pleasure to take a dip in. Finally the hotel staff seem very cool with, say people coming in at 6 in the morning from the bar, so I always have love for a place with no judgment!

text: My boyfriend and I are out of towners (from northwest Illinois) and I had booked reservations for this restaurant sight unseen. I can't say we were anything less than thrilled. From the valet service to our waitress to the food to the view from the rooftop -- everything was perfectly on-point. It didn't hurt that the Cardinals won that evening and we got a beautiful fireworks display. The food was fantastic -- don't miss out on the steamed mussels appetizer. My boyfriend got the pork chop and I got the steak au poivre and we kept sneaking bites off each other's plates because everything was so tasty. Those bacon-bleu cheese twiced-baked potatoes are a dream come true. The waitress didn't balk at taking our photo a few times up on the rooftop and our valet didn't mind us getting into our car a few times and watching it while we took a stroll. Great service, great views, great food. I think about going back there all the time!

The pizza brings a harmonious balance of crispness on the bottom and chewiness on top. This was only my first trip to Stella but I look forward to trying it again and would recommend it to others in the area.

The wait staff rushes you through, the tables are usually sticky and the place looks like it could use a good cleaning. The food is edible, but certainly nothing to savor or keep you coming back. I've never had anything but breakfast, but I would think the lunch, dinner, etc. offerings are pretty standard as well. text: The food.. the fucking food. Ugh. Had the shepards pie.. someone really just wants to make sure that the stereotype of English food being terrible lives on because it really wast he most blandest, worse thing I have eaten in pie form. The Guinness was good, but really, that's the only thing that makes this place anything remotely Irish in terms of pubs. And even then, I'm sure just picking up the Guinness from a market with some corned beef will make you more Irish than this pub. Service was very spotty. My server was spread way to thin.. Which shouldn't say I was pissed off at the wait staff.. That's something management needs to sort out. It was a late start for hitting the bars. A lot later than what I'm normally used to. So getting in there and seeing groups spread themselves out over more tables than they needed and hogging up the room was a bit of a mess. Ended up going to the back area sit down/dinning area. Then when we do get a table the leg was wobbly as hell. Guess the table had one too many spilled Guinness as it was very unstable. Telling the waitress this when ordering the drinks she said she would get on it to get it fixed. Comes back with the drinks and forgets all about the table situationn... which made having beer on the table something of a no no. That's like asking someone who has greasy/slippery fingers to hold some glass bowl. They will more likely make more of a mess. Ordered food... it was terrible and only when she did her "how's the meal" did she notice that i made a poor attempt at leveling the table and realized that she completely forgot about the table situation. Over all, I really didn't like this place. The beer was good. That's about it and that's not saying much as beer is good anywhere as long as you have refrigeration. The atmosphere was way too crowded. The noise level... I dunno why bars feel the need to blast the music, especially in a sit down section, to levels where you can't even communicate with the person sitting across from you. Oh hey, just cause you play U2 endlessly doesn't make you an Irish Pub. So as I sit here at work killing time on the internet looking to my past months adventures, I have to say that this pub and that night was a rather low point. Screw that place. No way will I ever be back in that bar again. Terrible.
label: NEG

text: Oh man, the Supreme. Let me start off by saying there is no contest really between this grocery store and any other in the area as that Fresh Grocer is just ridiculous in its set up and way too small for servicing the University, not to mention all of us living off of its multiplier effects. All other groceries are internationally oriented and really great, but when it comes to one stop shopping for all your usual needs, Supreme sort of has a monopoly on normal shopping. But to call it "normal" is an understatement. Specifically the meat section which resembles the Mudder museum. I don't want to be offensive to anyone's eating habits but this is the first place where I saw the intricacies of cow tongue up close--where I could feel it's texture through a thin layer of plastic wrap. Dems HUGE. After picking out everything you need (I love that they have Mineral Agua there!) you are so psyched you got all of your needs in a one stop shop scenario and you head to the check out--here's where the games really begin. Typically all of the check out belts are out of order. Not only does this make the wait particularly long, but then you start talking to your friend while you wait for the guy in front of you to shuttle all of his foodstuffs down the belt until you here someone shouting at you. Oh, yes, it is your turn now. you ridiculous talker. How could you forget to start moving your groceries down the belt? Anyway, the checker will always get over your grocery moving ineptitude and chat you up and before you know it, you have everything you need, and another experience at Supreme is over. Just stay positive because really, where else are you going to go?
label: POS

text: There is certainly no shortage of musical equipment stores in the greater Nashville area, but for drummers, Fork's is our Mecca. This little shop has everything you could possibly need, from a huge selection of heads to new and used snares, full kits and crazy little percussion items. Fork's is on 12th South right next to the more guitar-centric Corner Music. Fork's has a really friendly staff that won't sneer at you in that all-too-familiar Guitar Center way. These guys don't seem to care how good you are or what type of music you play; they just want to help you find the item that you're looking for. When it comes to musical equipment (especially drums) prices are going to be comparable at most every place. The difference at Fork's ist that you'll be supporting a locally owned shop with a staff that actually cares. And as many times as I've been in Fork's, they never seem to be out of the basics (heads, hardware, sticks, et cetera). Only problem is, every time you're in there you may be tempted to buy shakers or cajons or djembes or God knows what other kind of crazy world percussion items Fork's has in stock.

text: THANK YOU Yelp! I came to Reno a couple of weeks ago for a basketball tournament. I had a break in between games and wanted to get something good and decently light. Sup was basically rated as the best place to eat in reno. The bf and I split a pesto turkey sandwich and a bowl of chicken enchilada soup. It was perfect! They even split the sandwich for us and gave each of us our own little side salad that even came w/ strawberries! The sandwich was delicious and a decent size. Having the soup, sandwich and salad caused me to have leftover sandwich. I can see how seating can be a problem. The place is small but if you are just coming for a quick (take-out) or a nice little lunch definitely check this place out.

text: What used to be a fairly uneventful and empty waste of space (called Semolina Pasta) is now a very popular Zea restaurant on the West Bank. I've had the fortune of visiting home last week and got to catch up with some girlfriends at Zea. Parking is super ample because it shares the same lot as the Palace Movie Theatres. I definitely recommend lunch during the week; as crowded as it is, the prices are wallet friendly! The wait was roughly 30 minutes, but that's because we rolled in at noon. When we were seated, we noticed that there was a cold ass draft because we were sitting right under the vent! Don't sit in the back if you want to avoid getting chills. Anyhow, I tried their platter of the day which includes a protein (Thursdays - sliced lamb with mint demi-glace) and two sides (Thai snap beans & Zea potatoes). The price is perfect (about $11) and the portion is too huge! The lamb was overcooked and dry and the sauce used to mask that dryness wasn't very yummy. The Thai snap beans were sweet and crisp, while the potatoes were just lame country style potatoes, super deep fried. One friend ordered the Ahi tuna salad which is basically a seared medium rare ahi tuna steak on top of greens with some funky shaped deep fried wonton chips and dressing....it looked SOOOO good I wish I had tried it. Madison was our server and she was extremely professional (even though a knife was dropped - no injuries!) and super duper nice and always smiling....she definitely rocked our lunch! I'd definitely return here if I ever come back home - Zea is affordable and the atmosphere is definitely welcoming.
label: POS

text: What was done well: The atmosphere in the dining room was intimate and relaxed. The staff was very friendly and attentive. The truffle fries were delicious, and my date's chicken sandwich was also very good. The coleslaw was a bit mayonnaisey, but the green onion was a very nice touch and complemented the sandwich's flavor well. My chipotle burger was decent, but I thought it was a notch below some of the other gourmet burgers around town (see, e.g., the Luke Burger). The Martinis were good, but a little on the pungent side. After I asked the bartender to make them with a little less vermouth. What was Bad: The Cajun Scallop Salad. There were two important things which were wrong with this dish. First were the scallops. I know they were billed as "blackened and seared," but they were more than undercooked. They were mushy and lukewarm in the middle -- in short, totally raw. Second was the level of spice for the salad. I'm no prude when it comes to spice -- I probably put more tabasco on my red beans than most of you. But this salad was so hot that any of the other flavors of the salad were completely overpowered. The jicama? It might as well have not been included. The honey chipotle pecans? They might as well have been cardboard. In light of the $17 price for this dish, you expect more.

text: Call ahead and find out which day(s) of the week that the meat man is in the back of this small store cutting up a dozen or so whole fresh lambs that are hanging in the big walk-in refrigerator. Not particularly cheap, but who else in Tucson has entire lambs and will cut them to order? It's like being in a Mideastern bazaar! I'd sure love to get a whole lamb to cook on a spit-turned roaster! My husband's gyro platter was pretty good, but that was the first time I've eaten gyro. He did say that while it was pretty good, he's had better. This place advertises being "group friendly" on their website. We were a party of 8 seated at a TINY table with barely any elbow room. I was rubbing knees with the two people on either side of me. Not comfortable at all. Add 8 entrees, appetizers, and drinks to the mix, and well...none of us were able to relax. Zorba's Taverna in Fairmount has waaaay better food for about the same price. text: I'm surprised there aren't any reviews on this place, yet... whatever. I'll do the honors. The Crack Fox is a small bar/venue in downtown that caters to a different crowd than the bars a couple blocks away on Washington. Whereas you'll be listening to pop-rap or cover bands up *there*, at the Crack Fox you'll most likely be listening to some obscure industrial or electronica. On Washington, it's button-up shirts and tiny, black dresses, but at the Crack Fox, it's often see through mesh shirts and leather dresses. You starting to get the picture? It's an alternative club, in the truest sense. The decor is all dark-red and black, making for a good match with its clientele. Carrie, the owner, is a real fine lass, and she holds great events through her own production company (Conspiracy STL) and others (Subversion, Rapture, etc.). The cost is always reasonable, and the drinks are as stiff as they need to be. Some of St Louis' top alternative talent plays here, but that also bring me to the reason I can't give the Crack Fox a 5-star rating: the sound. It's not *horrible*, per se, but it's just mediocre enough that you'll probably make a comment about it. With some bands, it's not a problem, but if there's a drum kit up on stage, there might be problems. Overall, though, you SHOULD go to the Crack Fox. It's one of St Louis' best bars, and unless you're a complete douche, you'll enjoy it! UPDATE (9/8/2011): After coming here a bunch more times, I'm changing my rating to 5-star. Although the gripe about the sound is still there, it's less of an issue after they upgraded their stage setup. New sound equipment, new lights, etc. Sounds and looks better than before.
label: POS

text: NEVER AGAIN!!! Actually, I'm pretty sure I said those exact words several years ago when I was last at Mad River. However, it was my sister's 23rd birthday, so I had to suck it up and go with the program. We arrived around 9 or so on Saturday night, thinking the bar would be relatively empty since the Phils game was postponed. Not so much. There was a Penn State alumni event going on, so the place was packed and we had to wait in line in the rain. We should have known right then and there to cut our losses and go elsewhere.
