text: I really wanted to like this place. I went there for a manicure and pedicure and I can easily I will not go back. I am sure others may have had great experiences, but I can only attest to what happened to me. The first time I tried coming here, I made an appointment for the Tucson shop. When I got there at my appointment time, they told me they did not have my appointment. After waiting a bit, they called the call center, and it turns out they erroneously scheduled me for the Denver school. I decided I'd give them another chance, so I agreed to come back the next day. On my second attempt to get my nails done at the salon, I got a student who seemed very nice, but so tentative! It was like she was scared to touch me, and this made for a verrrry slow manicure. And a very ineffective one. She was afraid to push the cuticles back and afraid to cut my nails, so that by the time she was done with all that, it didn't seem like much had been done. She then went to go prepare the self heating seaweed mask for my hands. Before she put it on, she made the comment that it was very hot, hotter than usual. In fact, she said the mask was so hot it seemed like it was melting the plastic tray that it was in. And despite all this, she put this mask on my hand, and the instant it touched me, I pulled back in pain. Yes-- it was that hot. Even after we washed it off with some water (which only made it hurt worse because the self heating properties of the mask is activated by water), my hand still hurt for the entire manicure. After all this, I still stayed and got my nails painted. It turned out pretty sad. I realize this is a school, but I would have done a better job painting my nails myself. It was clumpy and a lot of it ended on the sides of my nails and on my cuticles. Since it wasn't cleaned up right away, while the polish was wet, when she tried to clean it (after the polish had dried), it marred the already set polish that made it on the nail. Not a pretty sight. Definitely did not look like I had a "manicure" done. The pedicure was a little better, but still very tentative. Luckily the polish went on fine. The instructor came in and I told her about my experience. I don't know how the grading system at Aveda works, but the instructor gave the student all perfect score, even after I told her what happened. When I went to check out (3 hours later), I mentioned my dissatisfaction to the woman who checked me out. She offered me a free manicure at the same salon, which I turned down. My overall opinion is that if you want a professional job, go to a professional. If you go to the Aveda Institute, you might get lucky, but then again, you might not.

text: Yes, we did do more than eat and drink while we were in town. We went into a few shops and this was my fave. Highlights: - Really cute, fun and nice stuff: trendy but not tacky or made with cheap material - Great feel to the shop: open and welcoming. It felt kind of like an upscale urban with less t-shirts and gag gifts and better selection of clothes. In the window was a chair that had a seat made out of different ties woven together: pretty cool. - Super nice girls working there: very helpful, were there when you needed them to grab you a room or another size, but weren't pressureful, and gave you their opinion when you wanted it. On this alone I'd give the store a high rating, as it's rare to find these days. To see the rating deal, when we left the store and they said thanks it seemed like it wasn't just a "buh-bye" line and they genuinely appreciated our business. - Dressing room was fun: a square area surrounded with dressing rooms given privacy by thick drapes and complete with a fuzzy chair inside em. - Prices: everything was super reasonable. Cute tops from like $30-50 and lots of dresses for way under $100. I go into a lot of great looking stores where I love all of their stuff, but the thrill stops after I look at the price tags and everything--even a tank top--seems to be over $200. Lowlights (my flip side to highlights): - Not everything looked as cute on me as it looked on the hangers. :-O - Sizes and cuts weren't consistent: some mediums fit me and some didn't, but that happens in most places. In trying to be different, the cuts didn't always work--at least on me. I'll stop in here again for a little girly shopping time if I'm passing by to see what they've got.

text: This makes me very sad to write but I must let others know of the most awful experience I had, at what use to be, the best sushi place in town. We ( a group of friends) have celebrated many birthdays and evenings out at Miso. We always received awesome sushi and awesome service. The place always had such a nice atmosphere. Expensive? Yes but nice. We decided to celebrate my birthday at Miso. We made a reservation several weeks in advance for the fancy table/ area in between the upstairs dining area and downstairs dining area. We ordered our favorite sweet potato appetizer. It came out quickly but the sweet potatoes were crunchy- not in a good way. Then we ordered sushi and it took 45+ minutes to come out (normally it's much quicker). Our favorite sweet potato roll contained more crunchy sweet potatoes. Not good, especially, for sushi that took so long to come out. We typically order two rounds of sushi. The manager came to our table as were just finishing our first round of sushi and started removing plates and drinks w/ out even inquiring as to whether we were finished. We stated that we were ordering more and he said no! There was another party coming at 9 and our table was needed. We told him that the sushi took forever to come out and then was not good. He argued w/ us about that and made no apology. He basically told us to leave! He took a drink that was only half-way gone (and their drinks are $8 a piece). We told him this and he denied it and blamed our waitress and made her come back and apologize for it. He stated that he had already taken it off our check because it was my birthday (we were holding the rather large bill and the drink was on it). The waitress seemed humiliated over the whole thing. She didn't have time to do the customary b-day cake which was fine. This whole situation could have been totally avoided. The place was practically dead (which is very unusual for Miso on a Friday night) and there were empty tables and the bar was empty. They could have offered us another table. Instead, the manager was rude and ruined my birthday evening. He made no apologies for over booking our table. He offered us nothing. Instead, he lied about the drink he took, he argued w/ us over the bad sushi and he ruined a fun evening. We had planned on ordering more sushi, desserts and more drinks (which would have been a whole lot more $$$ for them). What an awful experience. Based on the crowd word is getting out that Miso is no longer a hot spot for good sushi and good atmosphere. EDIT- Response to the owner: We made our reservation on Oct. 20 for Nov. 5, more than 2 weeks in advance. We were contacted on Nov. 2 about the private party (thank you cell phone call logs). We were told that another party had reserved the bamboo lounge for 9:30, not that the entire bottom floor would be booked. None of your staff mentioned the other party once we were in the restaurant until 9:10 when the manager very rudely told us that we were not allowed to order more food. He did not offer us a table at street level - we wanted other accommodations, but he simply told us that we had to leave. We only go to Miso on Friday and Saturday evenings during prime dining hours and it has never taken 45 minutes for our sushi to arrive. Was our service and food so lousy because you were all preparing for this private party? Was the president in town or something? No one apologized for the delay in our food. The manager didn't apologize for taking the drink (but he did lie and blame it on the server, making her apologize for it). He didn't apologize for the lousy sushi. He didn't apologize for us getting bumped for another party. And you still haven't apologized for the experience we had. It's your response that continues the most troubling issue we had at Miso, but there is a silver lining - your response captures the rudeness of yourself and your manager better than my review ever could. Was my review one sided? Of course it was, that's how reviews work. And now that you've had your chance to respond, it's not that one sided anymore, is it? But you weren't really there to witness any of this. You're basing your side of the story on what your rude manager has told you - your manager who has an incentive to tell you the story in a way that puts him in the best light and keeps his job safe. Thank you, again, for helping me replicate the attitude of the manager who was working that night. It helped me prove my point.
label: NEG

text: Ok, its time this place stops getting raves and attention from food network and the various other media outlets that praise this place. First off, I know good bbq, and this aint it. The service is terrible. You'll wait upwards of an hour for your food, and the wait staff could care less. Tip, if you're smoking meats, you smoke alot so you know you can handle the lunch time crowd. You don't smoke one rack of ribs, then smoke another when that's done. You're doing things ass backwards. Second after an hour, the food arrived cold. Are you kidding me? I thought surely the wait is justified because were going to get some hot tasty ribs off the smoker......Nope. Onto the Food. They actually make cole slaw that is dry. How is that possible.....ask them. The baked beans were completely tasteless and devoid of any brown sugar.......a necessary ingredient in BBQ beans. They somehow managed to muck it up. Third........portions are small and prices are high. If you pay 14 dollars for a rack of ribs.....you want a rack, not a rackette. All and all this place is garbage. I imagine it gets a lot of attention because its in the ninth ward, and it's some people trying to do bbq in new orleans. I know new orleans isn't known for bbq, but it is known for good food, and this place falls way short of the mark. You want bbq in new orleans, head out to vets, and go to corky's.....its a franchise, but at least its good and consistent. Every local I talk to, thinks the joint is terrible, they don't go, and maybe they're onto something.

text: It's the day of "I want to love this place" reviews. I would have agreed with the other reviewers until recently. But of the last half dozen times I've gone here to do laundry at least one washer or dryer was broken, which you don't find out until after the cycle is meant to be done - UNLESS someone is kind enough to run home and make a note to tape up saying it's out of order. Then the extra trip and extra wash/dry. So money and time lost. It's only laundry, but WW ranks up there in price: a dollar seventy-five for a wash or forty-five minutes of drying. Additional fifteen minute increments of drying are seventy-five cents, I believe. Now I'm hoping their latest problem is only a glitch that will be gotten beyond. text: For my 100th review, I thought it should be special. What's more special than my favorite meal, at my favorite restaurant, in one of my top 3 favorite cities. Manale's is famous for their BBQ shrimp. Are you thinking shrimp slathered with BBQ sauce? Well, you're wrong. BBQ shrimp are shrimp baked with the heads and shells on in a mix of butter, Worcestershire and a host of other spices. I guarantee you've never tasted anything this good (although Drago's char-broiled oysters run a close second) in your life. Served with perfect New Orleans French bread (paper thin, light crust, soft, airy bread on the inside) for sopping up the sauce, this is a New Orleans staple that was originated at Manale's. In addition to the BBQ shrimp, there are other reasons to visit this New Orleans establishment as well, like the oyster bar where I once challenged a 10 year old kid to eat a very large raw oyster. He did it so I had to as well, and I hate a large raw oyster (yet tiny ones are a gift to the world). Good stiff drinks in the bar as well as oysters to die for and shuckers who win contests. Seriously. When you go to the dining room, it's like stepping into another decade. It's got that old school Italian feeling. I expect to see Carlos Marcello surrounded by his people at a back table. OK, not really since I wouldn't know Carlos Marcello from Tony Soprano...but you get the idea. The waitresses are all of that older, steak house variety. You know the kind, weathered, hardened and not about to take any crap, but still wonderful, attentive and knowledgeable because they've been there since the joint opened. The Italian-inspired menu ranges across everything you can think of and all the New Orleans classics as well, but you know, in the end, it's all about the BBQ shrimp. And that might just be the best meal on earth.

There are also cool historic things back the Crick (how I've always referred to it), like an old time paper mill (still operating for touring purposes), the finger bridge and covered bridge, a statue or two, some ancient looking ranger houses, and informative plaques randomly scattered throughout. Some of the Public Parking: http://maps.google.com/maps/ms?ie=UTF&msa=0&msid=210485173569154004813.0004ab1a442bac0939b52 Some (but by no means all) spots worth checking out: http://maps.google.com/maps/ms?ie=UTF&msa=0&msid=210485173569154004813.0004aadd7a2e577157193

text: Food: * Ambiance: * * * Service: * * Cost: * * (more stars means more for your money) Dress: Casual/Business Casual I have to say I don't like this place and I even gave it a second AND third chance since I don't believe you can judge a place by just one visit. I think it was nice to have another big restaurant hit Broad Street and I was excited to know it was another "meat" place and even more excited to hear it was backed by rich Ted Turner. Now I know better and Ted Turner didn't put enough money into this place. Despite have a great location, the food was terrible. I know 3 people who got food poisoned and I even had a tinge of it as well. The food is not spectacular and you can get it elsewhere in the city cheaper and better. Their most unique item is probably that they offer bison, but take it from me, you're better off just going to any of the Midtown diners and grabbing a bison burger at their joints. It's just as tender and tastes better for much less. Everything else on their menu is typical American fare that you can find some variation of at any family restaurant chain. For just a little less, you can get the same at your expectations just a few steps away. In terms of the place, they do have ample seating from the looks of it, but their service is bad and it seems at times understaffed. Even if half the place is empty, you might wait 15 minutes for a seat sometimes because they don't have enough waiters. I like the decor with the giant moose head and pictures, but it's not enough to win me over. Steaks are sometimes dry or cooked improperly (not what you ordered) so at times you might get what you want, but who wants to play the luck game when it comes to wanting a nice juicy piece of meat? Service was horrible and maybe it is because they seem understaffed, but I barely got the time of day usually. The waistaff didn't check up on me and we had to yell to get any service. I want water when my glass is near empty and if my steak is dry, you better hand me the A-1 sauce. I'm not going to lie. It's only a few bucks above the average of what I'd pay for this type of food and if you are lenient, it's not a bad place to eat. But for the money and the expectations you go in with for a place with their decor, backing, prices, they should offer more in terms of service and quality. I don't find this place acceptable at all and don't plan on going back after my 3 visits. In summary - PROS - sweet location, boasts bison meat CONS - service, not good enough for the money, food quality, inconsistent steak performance, get better food elsewhere cheaper

text: This place is passable as a Moroccan joint. The decor is pretty low-budget but it fulfills the middle-eastern vibe you'd expect from a hookah bar/restaurant. The waiters are friendly and helpful. Unfortunately thats the extent of the positives. On paper this place looks great. A hookah bar? Cool! A Belly dancer? Why not. A live DJ? Sweet. A 10 course ROYAL FEAST? OH HELL YES. Don't get too excited though, for things are not as they seem. The hookah bar fulfills its role, the shisha is a bit expensive ($20-25) but the waiter was pretty generous with it so I'll let that go. The belly dancer though is quite the trip. We were there over the course of 4 hours, from 7-11, and the dancer came out twice for 10 minutes each. Sure she danced with a sword for part of that time, but COME ON, if you are advertising belly dancing in big capital letters I'd expect a bit more. The DJ however was as promised, and he played, and he played, and he played. Think loud trance music, nothing middle-eastern mind you, just trance music. LOUD. Now I've been known to get down every now and then, and I enjoy the trance, but when you are trying to chill out with a hookah by your side its not what you want to hear. And finally we come to the royal feast. On Fridays and Saturdays, as mentioned by previous reviewers, you are required to order the feast, you have no choice in the matter. Again, on paper the feast sounds amazing. For 25 dollars you get 10 courses, thats a sweet deal by any standards. Unfortunately the sad reality is it is not 10 courses at all. A few of the dishes are combined into 1 dish. So even though the baklava is separate from the fruit salad on the menu it is in fact just a small pastry that sits on top of said fruit salad. But hold on, it gets even better. 3 of the main courses of this feast are combined on 1 plate. So instead of 3 separate savory delicious dishes you have a plate with a couple sausage bits, 5 or 6 pieces of lamb, a few veggies and a sprinkling of couscous .. FOR 4 PEOPLE. Thats right, the real kicker was we had 4 people who had ordered the feast and we shared 1 central plate. So in reality that small plate of meats and vegetables had 12 courses on it. It blows the mind, really it does. On the plus side, the food had substance to it, and even with the small portions it was rather filling and tasted fine. I should also mention that based on the quick turnaround and lack of heating I suspect the food was cooked in advance, although I have no way of confirming that. Overall it was an OK experience. Not horrible, not great. But I do wish they would be clearer on what they are offering, I feel on some level that they misrepresented their menu.

text: What a disaster in a pretty box! As we pulled up in the torrential rain, I was excited to be getting somewhere where we could watch the football game between the wedding and the reception. I should have known something was up when there was no one directing traffic through the port-cochere and no one to help us with our bags. We finally got a somewhat covered spot, though the wind was blowing the rain under in sheets, and proceeded to unload our bags ourselves while still wearing our formal wedding gear. Fun times. So we waited in the lobby while Keith checked in, and then proceeded to one of the two elevators, and up to room 326. The set up of this hotel is not that user-friendly - the elevators are at one end, and you have to traipse all the way down the hall if you have a high-numbered room. If there were a fire, you'd literally have to go the full length of the hallway to the stairs... Anyway, we get to the room, and the keys don't work. Keith goes back to the front desk who advises him not to put it near a cellphone. Ok, while that will disable the keys, it doesn't do it that quickly. So as he's walking back with the "fixed" key, a woman is walking practically alongside him. He stops at 326 where the rest of us are waiting, and so does she. "I think this is my room," she said. Oh, really. Well, we tried Keith's key, and sure enough it worked, and sure enough, the woman's husband was inside. Thank goodness he was dressed! So Keith goes down to the front desk to get us an unoccupied room. We wait since we don't want to haul our luggage until we know where we're going. The man and woman came out a few minutes later to say that he'd gotten a call from the front desk and apologized saying that they thought they'd put them in 235 and that they would reduce the rate on the room. So we headed to 235 because sure enough, that's what they gave Keith. Jokingly, I said "make sure you knock a few times first" to Keith when we arrived at the door to 235. Well, good thing he did, because there was a guy asleep in his pajamas in this room, and he was none too thrilled that we'd awoken him. So at this rate, I'm livid, and so are the rest of us. We take all of our luggage down to the front desk and drop it in a pile in front of everyone else when Jimmy says "This is the most embarrassing hotel experience I've ever had!" Fortunately, that got their attention, so Keith could quietly say "yeah, that one was occupied, too. Is it really too much to ask for an unoccupied room?" Everyone cleared away from the desk. The Bellhop was so scared that he walked briskly away and left his cart, so I stole it for all our luggage. Finally we here "Ok, 220 was just cleaned, so I know it's open." So we head to 220. And yes it was open. And it was a decently nice room. The front desk called when we'd been there about 15 minutes to ask if the room was acceptable and to offer a $20 discount. Then they called again 10 minutes later to ask the same thing and offer the same discount. Clearly, there were communication issues at the front desk. When we took the shuttle to the country club for the reception, it got us there directly with no issues, and even a polite hello and goodbye from the driver. Best service we got from Normandy Farms all day. At the reception we learned that they wrong number of rooms for 2 members of the bridal party, so it wasn't just us. The bed ended up being quite comfortable, though I woke up stuffed up, indicating that the air was too dry or the place was moldy and activated my allergies. The brunch buffet was extensive and most of it was quite good, though the stuffed pancakes were not in fact stuffed with blueberries as advertised and were extra mushy as if uncooked in the middle. The salads were great, and I was impressed by the fresh oysters. So Normandy Farms, you get one star for comfy beds and one star for brunch. Service was atrocious. If you stay at NF so you're to Blue Bell Country Club (I can't imagine any other reason to stay), at least get the brunch so you don't leave with such a bitter taste in your mouth.

text: (My first review of this place was 5/2008 - I gave them 5 stars at the time. Did I mention it is BYOB?? Can it get any better than that? Yes. The sashimi and sushi is literally without a doubt a five star palate retreat. We always find ourselves going there and instead of ordering the rolls we know we like, we actually live outside our bounderies and will ask the friendly staff what they recommend and 5 times out of 5 times they will recommend what is on special. Special meaning soooo fresh it's a sin not to try it because you're missing out! We had sea urchin flown in from japan and received that very morning it was alive and still breathing, OMG it was soooo good. The owners recommended we try it, the staff recommended we try it and I am sooo happy we listened. We also had other recommendations of Sashimi and the filets of raw fish were so fresh and delicately sliced it was as if we were biting into pieces of buttery goodness. Like I said, when we go to Oh Yoko! we never order our usual rolls, we live a little on the wild side and order whatever they recommend and it's worked out for us still 2 years later. If you want to taste what real sushi and sashimi should taste like than this is the place. I grew up in a household with a father who went deepsea fishing every weekend so I know what meat just minutes out of a fish should taste like and Oh Yoko! does a really good job meeting up to that. It's a sin to have anyone try to rate this any lower than 5 stars. They are the friendliest bunch of staff you'll be soooo lucky to have met and I am honored to have been introduced to such wonderful food. I hope they live long and prosper.

text: Still love this place. The shop continues to bring in great yarn. Sure they've got their standards - even the standards go above and beyond! - but I like that Craig and his staff will stock things you don't see every day like the Tussah Silk of last season or the single-ply roving from Columbia Stock Ranch this year. The staff are always coming up with great, modern patterns that keep me excited about the craft. I'm also greeted by name - which means I'm there too often - which is so pleasant when I've had a crappy day. I'm always impressed with the customer service. I also like Craig's philosophy on how he chooses to stock his store: sure they could carry items similar to what you find at the big-box craft stores, but then Loop would be competing with them on items you could ultimately find cheaper at places like Wal-Mart. Loop is a place to come to find yarn that is what it was meant to be - natural or mostly so. It is often hand-dyed, kettle-dyed, etc and comes from companies that offer unique choices for all your special projects. The prices don't reflect arbitrary numbers used to turn a huge profit, they reflect the care and artistry that goes into many of the products at Loop. And let's not forget that Loop has a staff that needs to be paid and rent on South Street ain't cheap either. Lastly, the classes are great as well and tend to correspond with what is popular in knitting at the moment (ie: learning to knit the February Lady Sweater). You also can't top the awesome folks that Loop brings to the shop for trunk shows, classes, or meet-and-greets. And who doesn't love a place with a monthly Stitch Party!?

text: I remember going to the Silver Legacy on opening night. It was back in 1995 and believe it or not they even had rooms available. It was jam packed and unbelievably easy to get credit. The first time I was able to open a line of credit without having my credit checked. Those were the good old days. Well here we are 11 years later and I still go to Silver Legacy whenever I can. When you arrive at the Silver Legacy, you are given a choice to self-park or valet. I recommend valet especially on the weekends. If you self-park, you will spend your time going up each floor looking for parking with 50 or more other patrons only to find yourself on the roof and having to turn around and drive back down. Why? Because there are no spaces available. Believe me, I have been there; done that. Once inside you will find yourself on the midway filled with shops, restaurants, and of course the slot machines. One thing I really like about the Silver Legacy over the others is that they have a wide variety of games from The Munsters all the way to the new Party Time / Jackpot Party. If you like table games, they have the usual Blackjack, Poker, Roulette, and of course Craps. In fact, the Craps games downtown offer the 3-4-5 odds, which in theory gives you a better chance in walking away from the table a winner. But the key word of course is CHANCE. For more information, ask your friendly dealer. After all the excitement of gambling, you probably will be hungry. My recommendation would the Sterling's Steakhouse. The atmosphere is elegant and the food is delicious. Adjacent to Sterling's is the Oyster Bar where you will find some of the best Bloody Mary Oyster Shooters. The price is right and the seafood is excellent. Finally, if you are staying at the Silver Legacy, you will be treated to some of the nicest rooms in Reno. The Silver Legacy is the tallest building in Reno and if you are lucky to get a room on a higher floor, you will have some of the nicest views of the mountains and city. text: Do you have a Honda or an Acura? If not, you'd wish you did so you could just take your car here and let them work on it. I'll share a story and maybe you'll take your car here too. I have a 1997 Honda Civic EX. I love that car, yet I also hate it. I've taken it to other shops before but I always feel like they just "figure it out" because they don't really KNOW my vehicle. I also feel like other shops just fix whatever and don't really inform me of what the problem was or help me understand how it happened. So my car was leaking oil so I took it in to Accurate Automotive after my boss said he took his cars here for the past 15 years. So I drop my car off at the lot and I call them the next day. I spoke to a guy (I this it was Troy) and he was really honest with me. He told me "you've got a leak somewhere, that's for sure. But really, you're burning more than you're leaking. My advice is to just add a quart of oil every month because it's just not worth it to take the engine apart and find the leak." I was shocked! I loved how honest he was - and the fact that he wasn't looking to make a bunch of money made me even happier. I feel like their motivation was to keep my car running well but also keep my costs down. Perfect. I then begin to rattle off everything that has ever been told to me that was wrong with the car - and he said he'd take a look at everything. I received a call the next day and he informed me that my ignition coil was burned out and it was due to some other shop replacing my wires (the ones that go to the spark plugs from the distributor cap/rotor) with ones that are not good for Hondas. I told him to replace everything and then he told me it would be ready the next day. I go in the next day and my car is ready before he told me it would be. He then came out himself and showed me the old parts from my car and exactly what was wrong with them. He explained to me everything and I felt like I got my money's worth - and then some. He really knew Hondas. This place specialized in Hondas and Acuras. If you have one of these makes I highly recommend this place.

text: This is now named Home-style Beijing even though the receipt still says Green Leaf. I went there today with my wife and teenage daughter. Though not specified anywhere the lunch specials were not offered on a Saturday. That was no big deal. 12:30 on a 72F. sunny weekend, it was deserted when we arrived. We ordered the scallion pancake as a sharing app (reminiscent of the Thousand Layer Bread at Rangoon) and also the pot stickers (but asked for them steamed, instead of fried.) We were probably being a little too health-conscious. The dumplings were water-logged, and so masked the flavor of the gingery ground pork. Also the squirt of hot water in your mouth when you bight into a dumpling is not particularly pleasant. My daughter is the least adventuresome of the trio, and ordered pan-fried thin noodles with chicken. It was an somewhat interesting dish, with a curiously seasoned brown gravy over the usual bamboo shoots, mushrooms,carrots and onion. Perhaps a hint of five-spice powder. I ordered the Mao's Pork belly with a little trepidation, as pork belly can sometimes be pretty fatty. It was not, but as advertised, it was pork in a sweet sauce with peppers (bell and dried hot.) Not a bad dish, and enough to share. You would definitely want to order dome kind of veggie dish along with it though. What killed the meal for us was my wife's dish, double-cooked pork. When it arrived, we were wondering if the waiter had brought the wrong dish. Was that tofu ?? Maybe eggplant ?? The shiny, flabby squares certainly did not look like any kind of pork we had experienced prior. Upon close inspection, there were tiny ribbons of meat along the edges of SOME of the squares. Sure enough, they were pork. The lion's share of the slices were PURE FAT. Though it took a long time to get the waiter's attention (as it did later to get our check, despite the fact only one couple arrived during our meal) when we asked if this was normal, he assured us that this was the way they make it. Now I realize this is touted as authentic Beijing cuisine, and maybe it is. But when you also have Wonton Soup and Sweet and Sour Chicken on your menu, I think it might be nice to apprise an obvious Western family if a standard dish like "Twice Cooked Pork" varies THAT widely when prepared to authentic Beijing standards. The waiter asked if he should take it off the bill. We though they should take it off the freakin' MENU, but said yes, only because it was inedible. It was like lightly sauteed fatback. Maybe it was a purely unlucky choice, but IMO, unless you are specifically known for REALLY off-the-wall authenticity, it should be the waiter's duty to inform an unsuspecting diner if a dish may potentially be unappealing to even above-average tastes.
label: NEG

text: J-Bar is probably my wife's favorite restaurant in Tucson. And that's not a bad thing. There is much to be liked about J-Bar. The appetizers are great (especially the nachos!), the entrees are flavorful (try something of the Recession Busters menu) and the deserts are unique and delicious (yum!). There really is just one thing that keeps me from giving J-Bar a 5-star review: the waitstaff. I don't know if their sections are too big or if their training is lax or if we just happen to continually catch the one bad one that night, but we've never had a waiter/waitress who is even decent at the job. Giving a table time to peruse the menu before ordering is one thing, but making people wait 20 minutes to order is another. On our most recent visit, we waited about 20 minutes to order, another 20 minutes to get the desert menu after we were clearly finished and 15 minutes after desert was finished to get the bill. We were really thankful that a separate person came through the room with water or we'd have not had anything to drink for most of the meal. text: Riverside Village is one of the fastest growing neighborhoods in East Nashville and is already home to some amazing local businesses. It's located at the corner of McGavok and Riverside, placing it on the outskirts of East Nashville in the Inglewood neighborhood. Although the number of places here is small, Riverside Village packs a walloping punch. Probably the most notable business here is Mitchell Delicatessen, which has quickly become one of the best Deli's not only in its neighborhood, but in the greater Nashville as well. Castrillo's is the place to grab a pizza or, my favorite, some amazingly delicous wings. You can grab a hot cup of joe or some freshly made baked goods at Sip Cafe and either take it to go or enjoy it in the courtyard. The newest addition thus far to Riverside Village is Watanabe, a cozy sushi restaurant with some amazing potential. There's also a music store of the lesson type variety (East Nashville School of Music) as well as a handful of other small businesses. One of the greatest things about Riverside Village is its sense of community. All the businesses here share a common courtyard full of picnic tables and chess boards. There's a community garden that's lovely in the warmer months and Mitchell's even uses the herbs that are grown here in their delicious food. A downside is that there's one tiny parking lot that is shared by all the businesses. Since word of mouth began to tell about the amazing food that can be found here, parking quickly became a hot commodity. During prime times of the day it can be quite difficult to get in and out, so if you're going with friends carpool.
label: POS

text: We consider this our neighborhood pizza place. Honestly, it's not much to look at and we've only eaten in once, but the food is very good. The pizza is fantastic and we almost always get the Hawaiian (pineapple and ham) along with fries and cinnamon sticks. Most of the menu items are pretty good including the sandwiches. The fries are always hot and good too. The decor leaves a lot to be desired. This is basic bar and grill stuff with laminated tables, metal chairs and plywood style "booths." They also have several pool tables and often host pool tournaments so if you're eating in be prepared for rowdy pool players at times. text: This restaurant is a staple for the college students of Swarthmore, but it's not because the food is of an even remotely memorable quality, because the prices are extremely fair, or because the service is at all good. It's because they deliver and are open relatively late (midnight all week). Desiring something to tide me over until tomorrow's lunch since I'd been writing a paper all day and had consumed literally nothing but an energy bar since I woke up that morning, I called Appetito's, pretty much the only place that could provide me with anything more than a bag of Doritos at 10 PM on a Thursday on Swarthmore's campus. I ordered a Student Special ($7.50 for a large pizza) for my boyfriend, and for my vegan self ordered curly fries and a vegetarian pita sandwich, which wasn't on the menu, but wasn't a very hard order to request: all I said was that I'd like everything that's on the Vegetarian Pizza on a pita bread, minus the cheese. If you work in the food industry, this is REALLY a simple order to take, which I can testify due to my four years' experience working as a server and taking FAR more complex orders successfully at a much more busy hour (again, this is 10 PM on a random Thursday). I made sure to read off each topping on the pizza so that they knew exactly what I wanted: MARINARA SAUCE, MUSHROOMS, spinach, broccoli, onions, green peppers. I repeated this twice. All was good, I paid with a credit card, and waited the requisite hour or so that it ALWAYS takes to get pizza delivery at Swarthmore, no matter how simple your order. When they arrived with my food, everything seemed to be off to a good start. The pizza was piping hot and fragrant in a good way, that much I could tell from holding the box. Once inside my room, my boyfriend agreed that the pizza was very hot and surprisingly tasty for a local pizza joint (and he's New Yorker!). My curly fries were hot, crisp, not oily, and the only complaint I could really have about them is that they somehow tasted a little burnt. Then the sandwich. It was cold. Not a good sign, but I could deal. Maybe they mistakenly thought I wanted the toppings cold. Unraveled the sandwich. It was pita bread covered in raw spinach, raw broccoli, raw onion, and a slice of raw tomato. Are you serious?! For $5.25. Absolutely confounded as to how they could have though that any living human being would want a pile of raw vegetables on a dry pita bread and furious because the two things that would have actually made it a sandwich, the tomato sauce and mushrooms, were missing, I dialed Appetitos back. It rang and rang and rang, despite the fact that it was only 11:08 PM and they close at midnight. I called them for over half an hour straight, nonstop. And no one answered. Thanks for my overpriced pile of inedible vegetables, I really appreciate it, and THANKS FOR DOING YOUR JOBS by answering the phone during your business hours so that, if you didn't have the decency to remedy your error, you could at least APOLOGIZE. I'm still hungry. :(

text: There are no Bob Evans in or around NYC and California doesn't have any, either. It was with some trepidation that I accepted my coworkers invitation to grab lunch there while at a conference. From the brief description he offered, it sounded like a faceless corporate version of a standard greasy spoon diner. It was! So we roll in, grab a seat (five dudes cramming into a booth is an unfortunate and inelegant dance), start the never-ending flow of cheap, hot coffee, and peruse. All diner standards were there: eggs, home-fries, grilled cheese sandwiches. The OJ's decent and the coffee's inoffensive. The corporate backing is good for one thing: it allows some experimentation with menu items in traditionally close-minded environments. My tuna melt came with dried cranberries in it, a welcome tart addition to the usual flavor. One of the dudes got pancakes stuffed with vanilla cream cheese and topped with caramel and pecans. Decadent, beautiful, creamy, delicious heart attack. A pulled pork sandwich was a bit too dry. The burger was a mess; hence, satisfactory. In the joint's favor, the price was low, low, low (50 bucks for food to fill five fellows). Also, it's a damned fast food joint, so it's not like one could be disappointed by the health standards of the fare. They do have a scanty selection of healthier items (limited to the salad and 'swap veg for meat in entrees' categories). Would I go there on my own? Nope. If I'm feeling passive though, and know that I'll have an opportunity to exercise compulsively in the next 48 hours, Maybe.

Well, that was a bummer but no big deal. So we go on to order the fois gras. They were all out. None. Ok, that stuff happens. So we ordered the duck liver mousse on the recommendation of our server. text: It had been quite a while since I had been to Catelli - and decided it would be great for Valentine's dinner. I was expecting a bit less because of the day-- but over all, especially in food department, they came thru shining. We check in and had about a 5 minute wait for our table - no big deal given it was Vday. Our waiter greeted us, noticing we had drinks already. He was very friendly and chatty - though for the rest of the evening, he seemed to always be about a step behind. They had a set limited menu for Vday -I knew that going in, but the selection was large and there were also 4 specials. I didn't have a problem finding something I wanted- and my guy was overwhelmed with the selection and specials. I started with a cream of wild mushroom soup which was completely delicious and he got the lobster bisque which he describe as 'like silk, wonderful'. We went on to apps- I am VERY particular about eggplant- so ordering the eggplant rolletine was a fence sitter, but WOW - done to perfection, I mean perfection. I rarely say that about eggplant. He got the seafood ravioli special as an app and loved every bite. For entrees he went with the veal chop, which he said was done perfectly and he didn't need a knife...served over lobster mash potatoes. I ordered the Ravioli in a pepper blush sauce, which comes with lump crab meat that I ask them to hold off (being a veg) they had no issue with that, in fact they brought it out on a separate plate so my hunny could enjoy it : ) The sauce was excellent and I enjoyed going in with the fresh baked bread to finish it off. The dessert tray came and was full of a ton of things I love... but at the waiter's suggestion I skipped the creme brulle, the crepes and the key lime tart and I went with banana bread pudding, since I love banana and bread pudding. We ordered coffee also -- which came right away - unlike our dessert. When it finally came, it was sadly our only food disappointment of the evening...all I could taste was cinnamon, fresh shaved cinnamon, but it took over the whole dessert. I could not get a taste of banana or creaminess that is usually in bread pudding thru the whole thing.. My second cup of coffee never came - and our waiter didn't realize it until after he brought our check, ran our card...etc.. So the waiter being off and the badly done dessert kept this from being a 5 star experience for me, but over all I truly enjoyed it.

text: Freshberry is a copycat company jumping on the yogurt bandwagon craze largely started by Red Mango and Pinkberry. "healthy" nonfat yogurt with fresh fruit toppings, a trend that came from South Korea (koreans prefer less sweet desserts, so the yogurt was traditionally more tangy than sweet and creamy). Freshberry's yogurt tastes just like plain old fashioned soft serve yogurt, not the newer "healthy" active culture yogurt that's so trendy right now. They do offer more variety of flavors and toppings (they also offer the candy toppings). They don't offer my favorite topping, mochi balls (but I think they will as soon as they find a supplier, as they've indicated they keep getting asked for it). I thought the yogurt was too sweet and too soft, not cold enough. It came out of the machine sort of half melted and didn't hold a stiff peak like I prefer. Positive notes. It's bright and clean inside and the staff are extremely friendly and helpful. also, a note on the "healthy" claims. A 4oz serving is over 100 calories. I believe the smallest serving is over 4oz, largest one well over 3x this. add on 10-100+ calories per topping. (candy toppings generally add on the most, and fruit varies greatly) and you're looking at 400 calories easily even with the smallest serving on the menu. So be careful and enjoy as a treat, not as a healthy snack. They also aren't rated for the live probiotic cultures that are promoted in the product.
label: NEG

text: Mitchell Deli is the newest addition to the burgeoning little district at McGavock and Riverside in East Nashville. This place is brand new, but it's already completely won me over. Mitchell Deli was opened by local chef David Mitchell with help from Julia Helton, formerly of The Family Wash, in March of 2008. In addition to offering a huge and diverse selection of sandwiches, this deli also sells fresh produce as well as meat and cheese by the pound. They offer a salad bar as well as breakfast by the pound in the mornings, and their soups and fresh fruit are exceptional. Mitchell's sandwiches are incredible, and I personally opt for either their Ruben or Muffaletta, both of which are piled high with cold cuts and spicy fixings. The prices are completely reasonable, especially considering the quality. Seating inside is somewhat limited, but there are plenty of tables out back on the patio. Mitchell has already proven very popular amongst the locals, and something tells me that people will probably come from far and wide to sample this tasty little joint's cheeses and locally grown organic produce. This area, at the southernmost part of Inglewood, is growing rapidly, and Mitchell looks like the best spot to grab a casual lunch. The staff is friendly (but constantly swamped), and I guarantee you can't just go once.

text: Alright, alright. I've already reviewed one Stephen Starr place today, so we'll skip the rant about business tactics and degradation of food costs. Let's begin... *Makes fart noise with mouth* A disappointment is what this place was to me. For all its showiness and stylish creepiness (2 way bathroom mirrors looking into the bathrooms??), it just could measure up to other places nearby. Let's look at the positives, first. 1.) The Look Physically, it's a damn beautiful space. It's like a 50's diner that took all of its best qualities with it into a time machine bound for the 2000's. The colors all pop and exude fun. The shag carpeting on the ceiling at the bar is interesting and eye-catching. Most of all, the seating stands out. If you're lucky enough to grab one of the tables with swinging chairs, do so without hesitation. It'll help take your mind off the food later. 2.) The Service Fast and attentive without being over-bearing, the service staff really excels here. I did have problems with some plate crowding, but its my own damn fault for ordering so much food after I requested a 2-top just for a swingy chair. 3.) The Drinks Continental Midtown boasts a very creative drink list. An entire section of the menu is devoted to specialty martinis. I know it's been harkened to a lot on this site, but the Buzz Aldrin is an amazing concept for a drink. Wow, that was glaringly positive. I guess it's time for an appropriate counterbalance. Here comes my lone negative... 1.) The Food Now, it is entirely possible that I picked each of the worst items on the menu, but even so, they should still be decent to even be on the menu. To start, I had the humus with pita. With such a simple dish, I've become accustomed to chefs trying to play with the humus a little. Truffles, garlic, and red pepper come to mind. But Continental Midtown offers a plain garbanzo bean humus, something I could purchase in a supermarket for a lot less than this restaurant's pricing. Next, I went with the crispy calamari salad, having had great experiences with fried calamari in my time. What I got was unpleasant. The menu didn't lie, it was served over arugula with sesame oil among other embellishments. However, the smell of the sesame and the taste of the peanut oil the calamari was fried in overpowered everything else. I'm sorry, but your fryer oil should never overpower the taste of what it is frying. In the end, my dish smelled like a skunk and tasted liked peanuts. Finally, I decided to end with the menu's sole sushi plate, which I think was a spicy tuna roll (it's been a while). This was actually very good. But that in itself leads to more questions, like: Why does a non-Japanese restaurant fail in every piece of its menu except for its only sushi roll? Sheesh. Sorry about the rant, but this is my first overtly negative review, and I had a lot to complain about. Overall, Continental Midtown fails in my eyes. It is aesthetically pleasing, but the fact of the matter is that I decided to go out to eat; to have someone else prepare a meal for me knowing full well it would cost me. Tragically, the preparer of this meal did not hit the mark. At the end of the day, what is a restaurant if it can't feed people into satisfaction?
label: NEG

Out of the baked goods I really enjoy the nudos very much, which is sort of a hybrid of brownie-cookie, with crunchy edges and chewy innards. text: In many ways, Ting Wong reminds me of many of the New York Chinatown restaurants my parents took me to as a wee lad: Good Cantonese rice and noodle dishes, borderline sanitary conditions and surly service. Stands to reason since this is the Philly annex of the Big Wong chain. We usually do takeout here after church since they make the dishes that my kids like. We normally get the Three Treasure Rice platter, which is sliced roast pork, pieces of the soy sauce chicken and a runny fried egg with green veggies and rice. The yolk combined with the sweetened soy sauce makes for an nice dressing for the rice. My daughter likes the Slippery Egg and Beef Rice, which is an egg sauce thickened with corn starch. Also recommended is the curried octopus with rice. If fishiness is your thing, then get the Fried Rice with Anchovies and Chicken, a HK comfort food. I've gotten the Dry Sauteed Beef with Rice Noodles, but recently it's gotten doused with too much soy sauce and was just plain bland. Same blandness for the Singapore Noodles (really should have a bit of a kick, you know what I mean?). They are known for their congee or rice porridge which is made to order. Get their chicken congee, which features de-boned slices of their soy sauce chicken which is arguably their best deli meat. However, you may want to hold off on getting the fried dough sticks (yu tiao) which usually accompanies the porridge. It usually sits high on a shelf uncovered and I know there are winged creatures buzzing through the restaurant. And yes, avoid the bathrooms if you can. Very NY Chinatown. And the surly waiters, too.

text: On my recent trip to Nashville, we ran into some trouble finding places to eat/drink. I combed over Yelp extensively, even posted a talk subject hoping to find some help with my specific needs. (I don't like country music, don't care for touristy spots, and wanted to find genuinely good food for a decent price, much like I can at home.) After all the searching, we ended up hitting a few well reviewed spots, and I am beginning to think my taste buds must be really different from everyone else's. We went to Eastland on our second night in town. The space was very cute, home-y with an open kitchen. We opted to sit outside (in the backyard, if you will...) The weather was nice, and even though our server looked to be busy, he greeted us promptly. We both ordered a glass of wine, me a sparkling, him a red. His was much better than mine, I must say. (Believe me, it's hard for me to admit. I am used to being the ordering professional.) There was something odd about the wine list, though. The prices were actually in favor of ordering by the glass opposed to ordering by the bottle. (Only a few dollars more, but at every other restaurant, you save a little by ordering the bottle. That way, you not only spend more, but the restaurant saves by not having open bottles sitting around for too long.) Since we had a late lunch, we opted to order three appetizers and a side to share, plus the complimentary bread, served with the odd but acceptable combination of traditional dipping oil infused with cilantro. We got the pizza, the goat cheese brulee, the crab cake, and the jalapeno mac and cheese. Mediocrity seemed to be the running theme. The crab cake tasted just like every other version (except for Blais' at Home....I don't think I need to go into that again, but my mouth is watering just thinking about it.) It had way too much filler, not nearly enough crab. The pizza was decent, competently done, with accurate flavors, but it wasn't something I would recommend. The goat cheese brulee was odd. It was a lump of goat cheese on a plate, then hit with a torch and covered in honey and a balsamic glaze. It was served with what looked to be the pizza crust, sliced with no toppings, roasted red peppers, yellow peppers, and tomatoes. A bite of just the crust and the goat cheese was way too sweet, but pairing it with the roasted tomatoes overpowered the other flavors. (I liked the tomatoes, their flavor was just too rich for the goat cheese.) The mac and cheese was the saving grace of the meal, though it was so hot and bubbly we couldn't even eat it until we were full from everything else. (I know that isn't a real problem, but I want to be able to eat things within twenty minutes of them hitting the table. This was too hot to do even that.) After a couple of bites of the perfectly spicy and rich pasta, we took that last piece of pizza and the mac and cheese to go, and paid the bill, which came to $50. Reasonable in the price, but we didn't order main courses. Bottom line is, I would probably enjoy sitting at Eastland's bar and having a cocktail, but wouldn't choose to go back for dinner.
label: NEG

text: Wow, what an awesome place! One of my husband's coworkers has been nagging us forEVER to come here, and when the company boss showed up in town last week and wanted to take everyone and their wives out to dinner, we finally decided to take the recommendation. We're so glad we did! The service was really great. Our server was Clayton, and he was extremely friendly and patient with everyone while we poured over the beer menu. The manager stopped by twice to make sure everyone was having a good time, something we were really impressed with; both times he was very friendly and seemed genuinely interested in knowing how we liked everything. Usually managers in other restaurants pop in for about two seconds with a short "Everything okay? Great!" before they vanish. Another thing we enjoyed was that we happened to show up on what was apparently open mic night. (Tuesday.) It was just a really cool atmosphere, and we were amazed how many people showed up with instruments waiting to play. Dinner AND free surprise music is about as good as it gets. The only downside is that the chicken portion of my chicken sandwich was about as dry as it could possibly be without being wood. My fault for ordering a grilled chicken sandwich (Chicken a la Dunderbaks, I think) in a German place, I suppose, where everything else on the menu is various sausages and such, but it was still disappointing, and I didn't eat it. It was too difficult to chew and swallow. I didn't comment on it, though, because everyone else was having such a good time and RAVING about their food. (We were a party of nine.) I had a taste of several other dishes people ordered and everything else seemed amazing. I'm actually writing this review right now because my husband called from work and asked if I'd bring him one of their Schnitzel sandwiches for lunch. We ordered a $4 basket of Billy Goat chips (which neither of us have ever had), which comes with an onion sour cream dip in which I detected a dollop of horseradish . . . quite tasty. The chips were fine . . . just homemade chips. I make them. Very salty. We chomped on them while perusing the menu. It took a while to get the food. I got the $8 brie and turkey panini (sourdough bread) that comes with peach jalapeno preserves and slaw. There were no panini grill/press marks on this, and the bread was mismatched, so it didn't eat well. Tried the preserves on the sandwich, and they were a nice addition, yet somehow not required. The spinach would have been a lovely addition had there been enough of it. I'm not a slaw fan, but this was way under-dressed crispy, crunchy purple and green cabbage with carrots. Better than many I've had. Miss C. got the $5 small cheese pizza. She said it was fine. All in all, nothing stellar. How many chances do you give a restaurant? For $35 for a lunch for 2? As a side note, one of my sons has been for lunch, and got the pulled pork sandwich . . . he couldn't eat it. Evenso, we took plenty of food home. Don't know if it will be consumed.

text: Yesterday was my second trip to this savior of a spot in the Rttienhouse Square disctrict of Philly. I was wandering around for an hour a few nights ago, just wanting a nice divy spot for a beer and was surrounded by these young professional (and older) having "happy hour" at these fancy places around the square, feeling very out of place. I had been to this place a year ago but couldn't remember where it was and was devasted and defeated. I called my boy back home and had him google it. I went the next night. Yay! First time about a year ago I was introduced to a canned IPA by 21st century brewing at this spot. My boyfriend and I had not yet seen this phenomenon and were practically sh@%ting outsevles in excitement. We took pictures of the beer can. We giddily asked our server for another. It was heaven. then we looked over at the table next to us and saw what looked like incrediably delictable burgers. Found out they were the Good Dog burger, a patty stuffed with cheese. Oh my god. We'd just eaten and were prepared to shoot oursevles in the feet (or more helpful, regurgitate previous meal.) I love the multiple floors, sorta loud divy feel downstairs, but less noisy options of upstairs. The bar has a cool set up and feel. Not sure how to explain it, but walking inside I knew I was home. It reminded me of spots in Portland that feel *safe*. My second visit last night had me drinking Caldera IPA in a can, another awesome canned micro, and being presured by my boy across the country to order the burger. I wasn't hungry but I mean, I HAD to. So I did. For him. For good burger lovers everywhere. Boy am I glad I did. First I LOVE that its served with a mix of regular fries and sweet potatoe fries. Both awesome. Love sweet potatoe fries. The burger was huge and the fact that it was filled with cheese was what made it *special*. Otherwise the flavors were a little strange. I don't remember the type of cheese, but it was a stinky blue type (which I love) but didn't quite go with the french onion soup tasting onions on the burger. The aoli type dipping sauce had good flavor. It's certainly worth trying.... Any and every time I visit Philly, I am coming to this bar. I haven't yet gotten drunk here, so that will have to be in order for the next visit. And definitely some more of those fries. Thank you for existing in this otherwise ritsy (?) section of city.

text: check another one off the list!! A friend and I went to miro district for dinner last night and had a lovely meal! the service was great, and our waiter was accommodating and helpful with suggestions. i had E. My friend got the crabmeat beignets which were fluffy and the right amount of sweet (not too much) to go with a savory beignet... we both felt a little cheated like we were getting an airy crabcake. the flavor was good though. the bread basket included tiny corn muffins, biscuits with dots of orange jam (i think), and slices of baguette. i chose the salmon with pistou, red potatoes, spring peas, and chervil. it very good and interestingly paired well with my wine.... it was a little salty, but cooked well, and the plate was warm which i love. My friend again seared his tongue on the chicken pot pie right out of the oven (the beignets had come right out of the fryer! haha), but after a few minutes we both were able to appreciate the homey chicken and dumplings flavor. we agreed it was on the light side for a pot pie, more brothy and not overwhelmingly rich or creamy. he got a glass of Coppola's Director's Cut Zinfandel which was much richer than my glass but perfect for dessert. all of the desserts sounded good to me, so to go along with the rest of our meal i chose the most southern, Apple Pan Dowdy a la mode. YUM!! it was like a baby apple pie, complete with a small lattice crust that was crunchy and flaky. they know how to make all different kinds of great dough here! the apples were warm but not mushy, and the vanilla ice cream was in the perfect amount and high quality. i would love to come back as i enjoyed the food and the atmosphere, the bar area looks cool with a lot of outside light and black and white checked tile floor. i want to try the pork chop with ginger, thyme, sweet potatoes and spring veggies, the steak frites (smelled like wonderful steak grilling when we walked in!) and the chicken adelicia with fontina and tomato chutney aioli. and of course i want to try all the desserts. :) particularly the chocolate sheba, described by our waiter as a fudgy thing with dried fruit and nuts.

text: I have to disagree with the "overpriced" reviews about Harris Teeter, I would be willing to bet that if you walked into the store with a pencil and paper and jotted down the prices of the store brand milks, eggs, bread, flour, sugar, water, tea, canned vegetables, etc. you would find that they are as low or lower than you will find anywhere save a 50 case pack at costco or sam's club. Of course nearly every supermarket is the same. A can of Del Monte green beans is a can of Del Monte green beans no matter where it comes from. The test of a supermarket is really in their specality and store brand items and this is where Harris Teeter excels. If you buy their product and you don't like it you can return it for a full refund plus they will give you a national brand item for free. If you buy their seafood and you don't like it you can take it back and they will DOUBLE your money back. That's pretty impressive. And for those people who don't realize it the prices of Milk is set by the state dept of agriculture in that it cannot be sold for less than cost. And Harris Teeter owns their own dairy farm which means they can sell milk a the absolute lowest price, a Gallon of HT milk is 2.19 thats cheaper than wal-mart. And while Kroger may have lower prices they also have lower quality products, especially in the meat/seafood and produce departments. Test it out, walk into any kroger at 6pm at their busiest time and close your eyes and pick up a pack of strawberries or raspberries, and then do the same thing at Harris Teeter. And while most people can agree that kroger is a much larger chain store that may have some super cheap items saving 5 cents off a product isn't worth me waiting in line 20 minutes to save it, at Harris Teeter i've never waited more than 1 minute before someone was scanning my groceries even at most busy of times they always call someone up to open a new register and that is worth an 10 cents to me.

text: Started off a 7-bar pub crawl on Saturday at "The Mack". It was a little after 3 and none of us had eaten lunch in anticipation of the steak sandwich, which was vouched for by a Southampton native. With the spectacular storm brewing outside we prepared to hunker down for some pub grub and brews. Three ordered the steak sandwich and I went with the 1 lb "Man Burger" (I knew I'd score some of the steak from my petit bride). The burger was fantastic. If you've read my recent O'Connell's burger review you'll see I was none too fond of their offering. The Mack's burger blows O'Connell's burger away. Ironically, O'Connell's was just named the number 1 St Louis area burger according to the RFT. I challenge anyone to try them side by side and prefer O'Connell's flavorless bloodbath of ground-beef. Anyway, huge props for this massive, tasty cheeseburger, nicely priced at $7.50. That all said, I should have gone for the steak sammy, as was the original plan. From what I tasted of my lady's sandwich, it was the best cutlet of steak I've had in all of St Louis. Yes, it was better than anything I have tasted at Tucker's Place (and I've had a steak or ten there). Trimmed of fat and gristle, the 5 chunks of perfectly-seasoned steak served between two pieces of cheese garlic bread were a steak-lover's dream. At $9 for the sandwich and side, I'd challenge anyone to find a better or larger cut of steak in the land. I have had dozens of mediocre steak sandwiches in my day. You know the ones where you take a bite and the entire piece of steak comes off in your teeth as you try to bite through the sinew and gristle, then inevitably have to spit a chunk of it into a napkin because there's no way it's fitting down the gullet? None of that here. I would estimate that the total weight of the 5 chunks of steak after cooking to be around 16 oz (or more). This is a bargain by anyone's standards. Golden Tee on the widescreen. SilverStrike antiquated 2007 version. Nice side room for steel tip darts (5 boards). Friendly staff. Several flat screens. Bon appetit!

But then I as I walked in further, I noticed that it was La Colombe self serve, a la WaWa or 711, meaning that if you're ambitious enough as you might be at Wawa, you can mix and match your own caffeinated coffee concoction. Only for extra measure you can add on that extra shot of espresso. Difference Maker #1! But sometimes when your at a coffeehouse you want to say screw coffee, espresso, etc., and get something slightly different. So far, again unless it's Cafe Ole, most La Colombe coffeehouses have been somewhat limited on those options. Yet Euphoria hooks up some pretty awesome bubble teas and smoothies. Difference Maker #2! On it's own Euphoria didn't have the greatest outdoor seating, but it's part of the Piazza so not a problem. and The Piazza attributed to it having free wireless minus a problematic connection. and meanwhile the indoor area was pretty solid in it's own right, and hooked some a great variety. While the Piazza is by far the best outdoor location to accompany a La Colombe coffeehouse, I can't really credit Euphoria for it. And there are plenty of La Colombe house s that deliver a similar indoor vibe. So while it's not quite a difference maker on that category, it is beyond solid! and thatgains Euphoria another euphoric fan!

text: This was great fun. It isn't terribly clear what the protocol is, but basically you give donations for whatever food you want. For our morsels, we offered five bucks ( one plateful). Outside, we discovered what seemed more like vendors with desired donations listed per item. Be warned that the fried bananas ( plantains) take FOREVER FOREVER FOREVER. They are totally worth it. Order them and then go sit to eat the other food, and send someone back to check periodically on the progress. The deal is that a man will ask you how many people you want to feed, you tell him, then he tells you Joe much to give ( he can change for a twenty), and then he gives you a number. Silly me thought they would call me quickly, but no- you have to wait until the paper bag bearing your number re- appears in the tray next to the man from whom you ordered. It takes awhile. Like 40 minutes, in my case. Totally worth it. Also, there is a group of ladies making green paw-paw salad, and it is killer. Spicy, sweet, sour, umami- you name it. The sanctuary is lovely, and itnis generally a happening, happy place. No booze!! Please respect the house rules.

Parking was a pricey $26 a day. Conference rooms were so-so also, they could use an update. No WIFI anywhere. For business travel or personal travel, I wouldn't recommend the Ritz. text: For anyone who has been to a big zoo, like the one in Calgary or Vancouver, you might not think too much of the Edmonton Valley Zoo. But it's still a cute little zoo, and offers its own kind of fun. Summer, of course, is the best time to go, but I recently went on a warm fall day, and I enjoyed walking through with barely any crowds. There is a train ride and merry-go-round for the kids, pony rides, and different shows and demonstrations on throughout the day. (I was sad that I exceeded the height limit for the pony rides.) Be sure to go in the morning or early afternoon, as that's when all the shows take place. Their Birds of Prey flight demonstration is really cool, if you can catch it. I've never seen a real owl so close up before, and it's absolutely amazing how silently they glide through the air. Also catch the elephant show if you can, where they introduce Lucy the Elephant to you. She's quite famous in Edmonton, because she's a painting elephant (she can paint with her trunk)! They also have lectures on frogs, and teach you how the frog species is becoming endangered. There are paddle boats, but those are closed now due to colder weather. The petting zoo was also closed too when I recently went. The last time I went in the summer however, they were open and I saw a guinea pig giving birth to her babies in the petting zoo barn. My favorite things about the zoo though, are the red pandas and the prairie dogs. They are all so unbelievably adorable! You haven't seen a prairie dog until you've seen it yawn and stretch like a house-cat. I'm telling you, I cracked up so hard I think I scared the poor things into their little holes. So it may not be a big zoo, but it's still a fun place to spend a free afternoon. You can visit the animals, and learn something new!

text: All in all, a very enjoyable evening at Om Modern Asian Kitchen in Tucson. First of all, I was glad to see that they had complimentary valet service. I have been to this location before and parking can be a challenge so this was a big plus. This restaurant appears to be is a well kept secret as I was there on a Friday night at 7pm and there were only two other tables occupied at the time. We decided to go with two of our standard rolls that we usually order (Caterpillar & Vegas) for comparison and two rolls we hadn't had before (Spicy Salmon & Kamikaze). Everything tasted fresh and was well prepared. I usually use a pretty good amount of soy sauce and wasabi with my sushi but really there was so much flavor, I ended up using hardly any. The edamame was prepared well and so was the miso soup. Sometimes miso can be very salty and have not much other flavor at all but this was not the case here. At first, the rolls might seem pricey but I assure you, it is worth it. Great flavor and a generous amount of sushi were in the rolls that we had. We also tried some nigiri going with Fresh Water Eel, Red Snapper and Yellow Tail. Honestly, it was the best Fresh Water Eel I have had. The server did a great job of keeping our waters and ice tea filled and helped us out with our menu choice. She and everyone else including the hostess and manager were also friendly. Total bill was about $63 before using my Groupon but I will be fine paying full price the next time I go. I hope more people will check this place out. It was one of the nicest Sushi places I have been to in Tucson.

text: The Edgefield Restaurant is a sleepy little meat and two right at the five points intersection in East Nashville, next door to the infamous and most snobby Bongo Java in town. None of it is gourmet, but you don't go to this kind of place for gourmet, you go here for comfort food. I would recommend the fried chicken! It is very...comforting, in the sense that after you have finished eating all you can worry about is where you are going to lie down to take a nap.

I don't want to state that Japanese Sushi chef do better because I had uneatable Sushi experience by Japanese Sushi Chef in Bronxville, NY. It doesn't matter Japanese Sushi chef do better but they should know what good Sushi is. Especially I was disappointed by Nigirizushi in Sakura. The fish has to be fresh! When our Nigiri plate came, It smelled. Fresh fish should NEVER smell! Wait was very long and even when we got the table, it took very long for food to come around. Poor kid with us, starting to say "I am hungry!" "I am hungry!". I was very hungry as well when Sushi arrived. It was eatable but wasn't good. I will never serve that to Japanese. I learned not to order if I suspect that Sushi is not care well, then only order rolls. Rolls with cooked stuffs like Tempura with Avocado, cucumber. For fish, marinated fish or spicy ones that killed fishy smell and vinegar or lemons cooks the fish. Most of the restaurant marinate fish is to disguise its freshness. Last result to make fish eatable. Safest Sushi choice would be eel, Tempura and some veggies like cucumber. Rolls are becoming and treated as Burritos in America. I get the tortilla soup, which is a simple, tasty broth with onions, tomatoes, and strips of crispy, salty tortilla. yummmmmmm. That's usually my staple and sometimes I splurge on the chicken taquitos and my friends always find something new on the menu. It's a small little diamond in the rough restaurant that you miht just pass by before finding it. It's a BYOB place (which living in Philly I'm kind of getting use to.) but, they do offer a complimentary margarita or glass of sangria, just to start you off right. text: When my Aunt and I stopped here to dine as we searched for some new Mexican places in Brandon, we were intrigued as we entered the restaurant because it's so open that you can see almost every customer inside dining just by walking in. Even booth's are wide open, leaving people staring at you frequently, which can get a little awkward for some. The tortilla chips tasted pretty awful, which I think is an important part to eating at a Mexican restaurant. People don't normally order appetizers so the chips are usually what they want to hold them over to their main course. We dove right into the food. I had some tacos de carne asada, which is one of my favorite dishes to order at Mexican restaurants. They came out with more steak than I could ever imagine, and for the most part, the steak had no real taste to it. There was no real flavor, leaving it like a bland piece of meat. I recognized the tortillas from the grocery store, and the refried beans tasted like Old El Paso beans, straight out of a can, which really is not that great of a quality, and certainly not authentic like Estela's claims to be. The food was so bland, that I actually got full before I could finish the meal, a rarity for me since at Vallarta's I can eat and eat until I eat everything on the plate and all the tortilla chips without noticing how much I've actually consumed. All in all, it was agreed that nobody in my family will likely return to Estela's for dining in the future.

text: My girl insists that we need a quality meal before going out drinking (again) so we stroll in and are able to make a 9:30pm reservation for their NYE prix fixe dinner ($65). We ended up eating cheeseburger po'boys prior our 3 hour nap before going to dinner, so none of us were that hungry, but the food sounded and looked really good so we had to enjoy it. Amuse bouche was a pureed cauliflower with chives--pretty much like an extremely creamy mashed potato. It was nice, but more of a side dish or soup not an amuse bouche (it was 4.5 bites btw) Next was 3 little salmon and tuna rolls stuffed with cucumber and a creamy sauce and yuzu vinegarette. Really nice and refreshing..the salmon was quality and the taste of the cucumber & yuzu was a nice balance. One of my friends ordered the kobe short rib instead and I just had a bite--OMG sooo tender and delicious! The salad was amazing! I asked about it and there were zucchini and squash which were flash cooked in chicken broth and then put atop some kind of field greens. The dressing was nice and light, creamy, but slightly tangy...so tasty! For my main meal I had the snapper topped with clam and shrimp dumplings. The snapper had some red bell pepper on top and then was topped with the clam which was sliced thin. It didn't really have much flavor to me, pretty bland. The dumplings were really trying hard to be Asian, lots of ginger, some kind of soy sauce based sauce, but the skins were a bit overcooked and the shrimp was a tad salty. I was sad that meal was so blah :( The dessert was also disappointing..strawberry something or the other, pretty much a shortcake with creme fraiche layers, but not too good. So boring, I can't begin to explain it. Anyway, since we got to our rsvp late and we wanted to ring in the new year near Jackson Square, we told the waitress about the time constraint and she did an excellent job of bringing the dishes at a timely rate, but not rushing us at all. They had balloons and hats at the tables and it was really nice, not tacky or cheesy at all...plus then the boys had hats for later! Overall I liked the place and would consider it again for a regular meal.

The short rib dish literally falls apart once you try to eat it, it's so tender. Their appetizers are amaaaaazing. Oyster lettuce wraps? NOMNOMNOM. When you're a college kid, you don't mess with this stuff. Amazing. Dessert. Yes. Oh my. Now normally when you think cotton candy you think of fairs and what not. Here, it's literally a MOUNTAIN of sugar and brings you back to childhood. The freshly made donuts are one of the best desserts you will ever eat, especially with the trio of dipping sauces it comes with. Strawberry shortcake? Why yes, I will eat you. It's so light and buttery, but doesn't make you feel guilty at all.

text: I took my sick female corgi here for emergency care at 6:00 AM. The first vet after looking at her and bringing me in for a consult said she was in bad shape, among other things her heart beat was very high. She gave me a price for her care - $1,500.00 to $2,500.00. I signed this agreement and left. The next vet on duty (change of shift) called me saying she was going to try a different method, she did not mention the price was going up, higher than $2,500.00. I agreed verbally. Later on that day around 4:00 PM, I spoke to the vet and was informed that I had a choice to make. I drove to Gwynedd, saw my sick corgi on oxygen and knew what I had to do....sadly, put her down.....Now comes the bill in the mail....the invoice was slightly over $3,000.00 for her care. I am still paying it off through Care Credit. This is the issue I have with Gwynedd , their vets will pose what their care is and if that doesn't work switch care as the prices keep mounting. There are not price lists given to you so you are aware of what the charges may be. I was upset that I was never told the cost of care by the second vet would be another $500.00. Be prepared to bring a big fat wallet with you here.
