text: I have dined at Janos several times in the past and had enjoyable and memorable experiences. However, last Saturday evening, while the service was great, the food was extremely disappointing. First, the restaurant has a lovely ambiance with beautiful views of the city lights. The service staff was very competent, friendly and attentive. If only the food measured up to the quality of the staff, this would have been a 5 star review. The complimentary amuse bouche is a very nice touch in any restaurant for setting the tone of the meal. While the Scottish Salmon gravlax was house-made, the dish was thoroughly ruined by the sausage bread pudding on which it was served. The pudding was inedible and foreshadowed the meal to follow. The next course was a sweet potato and smoked chili soup. The soup was presented elegantly and hot, which was promising. The corn flan in the soup was tasty and a creamy - a highlight of an otherwise watery and lack luster soup. (Both my girlfriend and I thought it strange that the restaurant did not offer any salads on the menu, which would've been a betetr option than the soup.) The next course was a stuffed quail breast wrapped in bacon served with potato gnocchi. The stuffing was dry and unflavorful, the quail non-existent and the bacon was crispy though. The gnocchi were raw in the center. My date ordered the beef short rib for her dinner entree. While the short rib was tender, the dish just hit a single note. My dinner entree was the Colorado rack of lamb. Two lamb chops were properly cooked, but overwhelmed by the Kalamata olive sauce. The polenta was creamy, but was cold. The highlight of this meal was the cappucino ice cream with chili hot fudge sauce. While the ice cream was rich and creamy, the chili hot fudge sauce was grainy and served at room temperature. The coffee service was elegant. Cream, whipped cream, lump sugar and sugar substitutes with a rich, bold coffee. Chef Janos was in the dining room touching the tables and greeting certain guests, which is always nice to see. I will most likely not be givining Janos another try until I see better ratings on Yelp. There are other resturants in Tucson to be enjoyed for a better experience.
label: NEG

text: this is my favorite bomb ass new york style pizza joint outside of new york city. i still cant find any place here in vegas or any other place that ive lived (i.e. austin or san francisco) that tastes as good as the pizza at this joint. everytime im in town in reno, i ALWAYS venture out to this pizza place. this place was a small chain in the past, with locations in both tahoe and reno. i used to go to the location in south lake tahoe about 20 years ago, and would eat at the location for most of my life in reno. the reno location hasn't changed that much at all, except for moving across the street to a bigger location and changing the name from new york pizza to NU YALK pizza. they still have the big screen tv dedicated to new york pro team sports games, and a lot of the original new york business advertisements..i.e broadway shows, new york magazine. i remember always getting New York brand seltzers (remember those small bottles!!!) when i saw the name change, i thought oh no, new recipe, suck ass, but when i took a bite of their pizza, still the same recipe. so why have i been eating this pizza for so long and dont think no other place out there makes it the same... their sauce is phenomenal, very tangy and has a little spice (although id prefer more, its just right so that everybody can enjoy it). they dont skimp on the sauce either, they add a lot. it also is just enough so that it doesnt ruin that t really thin and crispy crust, if you're lucky you still see them hand toss that dough in the air. they also add lots of cheese, and sprinkle pepper and oregano all over it. i usually order their supreme pizza with all the ingredients such as olives, mushrooms, meatballs, pepperoni, bell peppers, etc. lately, i have been ordering a pie with just pancetta and mushrooms. oh its so damn f#ckin good, to see all those mushrooms and red/brown spicy/salty pieces of pancetta causing you to see a shiny oil sheen all atop the pizza. ive had requests from other former residents here in vegas to freeze pies and transport it back up here to vegas. it is that good!!!! If you don't go with a large group of people, you can order pizza by the slice. the slices are bigger than a standard paper plate. i remember eating on the portions that hung over the plate as i was being driven in the car when i was a little kid. i dont recommend ordering a small or medium pizza b/c the crust wont be as thin or as crispy b/c they really load up the pizzas. get the slice instead, unless you get a large or x-large. oh yeah, you have to try their calzones. get the meatball calzone...whew its like eating a football stuffed with hella sauce and meatballs....when you first take a fork and knife to this thing, you see hot steam and sauce spew out of the crust. when you take the calzone for take away, they use a wine box. i think the last time i ate there, it took me 3 days to finish that thing...i cant wait to go there....two more weeks!!!

text: I am a bonafide California girl and most East Coast taquerias put me off, usually because of the prices. Usually I wouldn't give an eatery that I primarily use for take-out as a 5-star, but I have been in search of an AUTHENTIC Mexican place that serves up great mexican dishes at reasonable prices. This place is my new favorite spot with authentic Oaxacan-style mexican food, where you can be completely full (and even have leftovers) for ten dollars or less. They have everything from tacos to tortas to burritos to enchiladas to sopes. I haven't found sopes since I left California, those thick pueblo corn tortillas topped with shredded chicken or beef, sour cream, lettuce, and salsa. The mole burrito is amazing and also try the pork & pineapple burrito. For dessert try the carmelized plaintains in sweet condensed milk.

text: Being a fan of all that is breakfast, I had to recruit my girl and head to the much talked about Pancake Pantry(PP). 45 minutes in line later (you don't wait in line at the waffle house - you might already know where I'm going with this), we find ourselves being quickly ushered across the restaurant floor to be squeezed at a table nuzzled a sparse 6 inches from our neighbors on both sides. Hello, New Unwanted Friends(at Waffle House you can have your own booth and enjoy the company you intended to enjoy). At this point I'm thinking they must bring grand portions of the most divine breakfast culinary treats and feed it to you while an attendant under the table cleans your feet with a warm towel and then gently massages away until your feet are happy and relaxed. Reality comes crashing in as I realize there is only room enough for my legs under the table and the menu consists of your stereotypical breakfast fare with astronomical prices tagged on(12 dollars will STUFF two people at the Waffle House). A brief synopsis: sausage - looks fresh from a microwave, hash browns - large cut and flavorless, eggs - McDonalds does it better, pancakes - i'd rather make them myself, mushrooms - from a can(seriously, ick) I wasn't really sure what I was paying for here. It wasn't the ambience. Perhaps I was paying for sidewalk space while I waited for over-hyped, poorly prepared, over-priced cafeteria food. I thought of giving the PP two stars for serving breakfast in a town with a shortage of breakfast joints, but then I once again remembered that you could walk into a Waffle House and not wait, know what to expect, get decent service, not get packed in like cattle, and have food that competes with the PP for a third of the price. Perhaps I'm a little grumpy in the morning...
label: NEG

text: This was the oddest winery I've ever been to and one that I don't plan on returning to. They have a confusing bottle cap system to use for the tasting that they don't explain when you arrive. I provided my passport and the gave me a sheet of paper with the wines they offered listed on it and 5 bottle caps. My MMM (Main Man Muncher) provided his passport and just followed off with me. One table had red wines another across the room had whites. If you are only limited to a few selections, I'd much prefer the wine to be poured at the same station so to better assess the selections and so that I don't taste a sweet white then a dry red. Anyways, we go to the white table first and try a wine. They ask for the wine money and I had no idea what they were talking about. Bottle caps, said the lady pouring the wine. I had mine, but after getting his passport stamped my MMM had to go back and collect his bottle caps. Don't know why they didn't tell him to take them with him when he got the passport stamped. The wines were alright. Some were tasty, but nothing that wowed me. Like many of the wineries on the Brandywine trail, the cost is greater then the quality. Lastly, the bathroom was one of the creepiest I've ever been in and the sink was on top of the tank using recycled tank water. Thank god for the bottle of hand sanitizer in my purse! I'm all for going green and the sustainability thing, but that just seemed unsanitary to me. One winery that I do not plan on returning to.
label: NEG

text: I should be fair and honest up front. High marks go to the staff that helped me with the issues that continued to present themselves during our short stay. I believe they did their best with the resources they had. That said, I am forced to suggest that you avoid this hotel for one huge reason - amazingly filthy floors in the rooms. I can honestly say they were so dirty I felt that there might be a health risk. More below... I choose to book this hotel based on high reviews on Trip Advisor. Since we were travelling with our 11 month old so, when booking I requested three things that were needed: a fridge, a tub and a king bed. We booked an executive room and these items were confirmed in my reservation. Upon check-in I immediately noticed that we only had a shower stall, so I reported that and we were moved to a new room. Not on the executive floor (where the executive lounge/workspace was), but a suitable room. Only a mild inconvenience and short disturbance. Once in the new room, we discovered a toilet that sounded like a jumbo jet's engine when flushed. We were off to dinner so I reported that at the front desk and they said they would have someone look at it while we were out. Upon our return at about 10pm, I checked in with the desk about the toilet. They called and spoke to the repairman who said that it was broken but they did not have the part necessary to fix it. They asked if I wanted to moved again, but they could not find a suitable room while I was waiting. It was already past my son's bedtime and we needed to give him a bath and get him down, so I said I would call them shortly from the room and in the meantime, I asked that they try and figure something out. Once back in the room, my wife found the tub to be dirty (pubic hairs from a prior guest). Our frustration level was rising, but we had to get our son to sleep, so she washed the tub herself and I knew I would mention it when I called down. When my wife picked up our son for his bath, we found his hands and feet to be black. We considered the day, where we had been, where we might have put him down, etc. and were confused. Then we considered the room. I grabbed a white wash cloth from the bathroom and a simple, light swipe across the floor revealed it to be filthy. A black streak was on the cloth. I checked multiple places in the room and found the same condition. Finally, I called the front desk. At this point, I explained, we had been given the wrong room and a new room with a broken toilet, a dirty bathtub and a floor so dirty we could not bring ourselves to take our socks off, much less put our son on the floor. My room was comped at that point, without hesitation I must add, and I was offered another room. My concern now, however, was that no one knew anything about a carpet cleaning schedule - I wanted to avoid the same issue in a new room or just leave that night. It was suggested that a go into the other rooms with the person in charge of housekeeping and choose my room. She escorted me into three different rooms, all of which I found to have dirty carpets as well (I used the same cloth test in each room). It was after 11pm and I knew we would not complete our 3 night stay at this hotel, but did not wish to uproot my now-sleeping family. When morning came, we packed up and left this hotel. I must again say that the staff was very helpful and understanding. In fact, a few offered that they were as disgusted as I was. Of the number of people that helped me, thank you to Tiffany and Theresa (I might be confusing this as actually being one person - whomever seemed in charge behind the desk that night) and the rest of the desk staff, and Bertha, the housekeeper. However, no amount of customer service can clean a carpet or get my to put my son on the floor of that hotel ever again. I should add that we wondered how often this floor condition might be the case in other hotels and we just never noticed. Well, our trip included two more hotels, neither of which had this issue at all.
label: NEG

text: Hospitals freak me out (you know, that whole association with sick and dying people), so the fact that I'm giving St. Luke's a solid 5-star rating really is a big deal. When I got pregnant, the first thing I did was look for an OB and a hospital that would be a good fit for me & Justin. I had had my heart set on a midwife and a home delivery, but since midwives are just starting to come out of the woodwork here (for shame, MO, making midwifery a felony for so long!), it looked like a traditional OB and hospital birth were the only options. I found Dr. Janet Matuszek and was delighted to see she delivers at St. Luke's. St. Luke's has a great family-centered, pregnancy-as-wellness approach to maternity care and I was very keen on being treated as a healthy person rather than some patient suffering some terrible malaise. When it came time to give birth, things could not have gone better. I had preregistered at the hospital so I didn't have to worry about filling out paperwork while breathing through contractions. Since I planned an unmedicated birth, I was granted one of two rooms with a jet tub rather than just a shower--and I was glad to use it for about seven hours. The nurse who tended to me during labor, delivery and briefly afterward was fantastic--very supportive of our birth plan and my decision to give birth without the assistance of drugs or other interventions. I felt that the staff truly honored our wishes and it was so nice not to have to fight to do things outside of normal practices. The nurses and house pediatricians who tended to me and my new son were nothing but warm, friendly and professional throughout our 2-day stay at the hospital. Being treated as a healthy individual and being an active participant in directing my care were my top priorities--St. Luke's exceeded my expectations, much to my relief. The comfortable, spacious (for a hospital), private room was just an added bonus! I hear there's a birth center going up in St. Charles soon (hooray!) and I'm still very interested in a future home birth, but to be honest, I had such a great experience at St. Luke's, I would seriously consider returning for any future babies I might have. Now THAT'S some high praise.

For my entree, I had a lobster-brie flatbread(aka pizza), and tasted pretty blah. The crust had more of a naan taste than 'flatbread' or pizza, and the topping of lobster-brie had no seasonings whatsoever. It felt like it would make for a nice party hors-d'oeurves, naan with a lobster-brie dip, but I didn't think it made for a good dish. All in all, the restaurant is very so-so, especially given the prices. While I didn't have a full-priced $25-$30 entree, my friend did and was not pleased. text: Avoid this place at all costs. I'm pretty skeptical of reviews where someone hates everything about a restaurant. I don't care that much, personally, but it certainly doesn't help the experience. Our waiter seemed like he wasn't trying or just didn't care anymore. He did stop by often to check on things and our food came quickly, so that was something good. THE FOOD. If someone made a TV show that put an 8 year old in charge of a busy restaurant without letting customers in on the joke, you'd have Rigazzi's. We started off with a salad. My gf got house dressing on the side. I did not. I would say roughly 40% of my salad consisted of salad dressing. For background, I put what some people have said is a disgusting amount on salads. I couldn't eat the Rigazzi's salad. I ordered the pizza + 2 pastas lunch special. The pizza came on what looked like pita bread that came from Schnucks. Ingredients on the pizza looked fresh though, and those tasted fine. Next was what was described as some kind of lasagna, but had corn, green beans, peas, and mushrooms in it. The taste, though, was almost entirely garlic. I would guess roughly 5-10x more garlic than is normal or expected. (FWIW, I love garlic, too). And lastly, the ziti. I haven't had Chef Boyardee canned pasta in years, but after a bit or two, I thought I was eating Beefaroni. I ate the pizza, but couldn't stomach the ziti or lasagna. I take everything home from restaurants, even if I think the food is kind of lousy. I let my waiter toss both the ziti and lasagna. I would be lying if I said I didn't enjoy the experience, though. The look of the place, insane pricing for what they serve, and the star of the show, the food itself, all provided for an amusing evening and made me thankful for average, cookie-cutter Italian food I've had at places like Favazza's. I'm looking forward to my next trip to the Hill to try another Italian place. It's all uphill from here :)

text: Chad and I visited this market on Sunday and it was even better than the last time. I did get some lovely rhubarb, but our August visit was definitely an improvement. We decided to leave our apartment as soon as we physically could- no breakfast this time. The trick is to show up as early as possible so you can get first pick of everything. I know, it's hard to be somewhere on Sunday at 10 am, but this is worth the effort. Because we slept in, we drove this time around, which was faster than taking the bus like we did in May. I kind of hate mentioning that because I'm anti-car when it comes to city errands, but SEPTA always manages to screw up timelines. So the first thing I noticed when we got there was the smell- it was glorious. And then we I saw the Sweet Lucy's truck. Ummm... how did I not know about the Sweet Lucy's stand at the Headhouse Farmers' Market? Not sure what their offerings were, because we opted for mexican food, but we'll definitely be hitting them up next time the cravings start. So the other hot food vendor is Los Taquitos de Puebla, which makes the best effing tacos al pastor I've ever had. These are even better than the ones served at their restaurant, I'm not sure if it is due to the rapid turnover or because it is just fun to eat outside on fancy marble stairs. Either way, I recommend ordering them with the green sauce. Joe Coffee Bar has a stand here, too, which is great for Chad because he has a caffeine addiction. In addition to beans, Joe serves up hot and iced coffee, which I still think kicks La Colombe's ass. So, on to the produce. We bought about 5 pounds of tomatoes for $10 and they were absolutely amazing. We have eaten tomatoes every day this week and it has been marvelous. We also picked up some delicious apples, including one of a very tart variety which I am enjoying right now. And, finally, a cantaloupe, which made our entire car and apartment smell like melon before we even cut it up. It was divine with the La Quercia prosciutto I picked up a couple days before. We also purchased a ball of fresh mozzarella on the way out, it was some of the best I've ever had. The are also salsas, honey, baked goods and meats, which I have yet to try. The only thing that would make the market better would be a ban on strollers. Seriously, there is barely enough room for people in there.

text: I didn't sit at the swings at the bar. For my entree, I chose the pan-seared scallops special with yucca mashed potatoes and green beans and left nary a bite on my plate. The scallops were good-sized and nicely seared and while there wasn't anything totally unique or amazing about the sides, they were definitely tasty. I didn't try anyone else's dishes, but there were few leftovers to cart home, so that's a good sign. Those who know me know that I'm a dessert junkie. This night was no different and we ordered the brioche bread pudding to share. Like I said, I usually eat more than I should, but this bread pudding just wasn't doin' it for me. One bite was plenty and sadly forgettable. The good part about that was it meant I didn't totally overdo it. :) I'd put Boogaloo at 3.5 stars right now. It wasn't outstanding, it wasn't great, but it was definitely *pretty* great. I loved the atmosphere, our server and some of our food, and I see from other folks that some dishes and some nights are better than others. I'd be happy to head back and try more of their offerings. text: This architectural landmark in Tucson has quite a twisted history...the fourth replacement for the original church of St. Augustín de Tucson (founded in 1776), construction began on the new cathedral in 1897 under the supervision of two French-born bishops (Salpointe and Bourgade), who envisioned a Gothic structure with two pointed spires (which were never completed due to lack of funds). For thirty years, the church stood unfinished, with bare-brick walls, until American-born Bishop Gercke decided to finish it in the Mexican baroque style. Inspired by the Mexican Catherdal of Querétaro, the sandstone façade and mission-style towers were completed in 1928. Structural deterioration prompted a restoration in 1966 under Bishop Green, who demolished everything except for the facade and the twin towers. The new building (completed in 1968) sadly is a product of its age...industrial acoustical tile, kitchy folk tapestries adorn the clerestory, a giant floating Jesus looms over the altar, red kitchen tile lines the floors and ceiling mounted florescent lamps cast a dull pallor over the interior. text: I really, REALLY wanted Monkey Burger to be 'as good as it gets', but it was probably the worst dining experience I've had in Tucson. I'm sorry Monkey Burger, I am. I was super excited to walk in and see Roy, the old manger from my favorite burger joint in Tucson, Burger City on 6th Ave. Do you remember Burger City? They had an awesome menu of burgers and sides, and the proceeds went to benefit ArtFare, a downtown not-for-profit benefiting the art community. They had this buffalo burger that was to die for...probably the best burger I've ever had. Burger City closed last summer and never reopened, a huge loss for downtown Tucson. Roy told me that Monkey Burger was supposed to be similar to Burger City, which got me super jazzed. The menu is laid out the same way, the prices are pretty much the same and they still have that super popular roasted corn on the cob. I was sure this place was going to be my Burger City replacement, but the food completely misses the boat and the service was worse than ordering up at a fast food joint. I ordered the South Shore (five spice patty, jack cheese, shredded lettuce, ginger BBQ glaze, pineapple relish) and sweet potatoes fries. My friend ordered Chef Mattie's Monkey (roasted poblano peppers, sautéed mushrooms and onions, lettuce, tomato, bacon, cheddar and swiss cheese). We took our number to a table and almost immediately some guy came out and said, "You got sweet potato fries? Did you want them now because they're done?" Let me pause a moment and say that I happen to think I'm a pretty good cook. So when I go out, I'm choosing to spend money on a great meal, but I'm also looking for a good experience, and that starts with great service. The runner was so standoffish and it just got worse from there. The sweet potato fries were cold and it was evident they had been sitting around. If there is one thing I hate more than bad service, it's cold food. I'm a firm believer that hot food should be served hot. I tried to flag someone down to tell them the fries were cold, but there was nobody insight, and that is the problem when you order at a counter...you never see anyone again. I went up to the counter, told them the fries were cold, and the woman said, "I'm sorry let me take them to the back, they reheat really well." WHAT?!?! I don't want cold and reheated fries. I told her to just take them back. She insisted though that she would have the guys prepare a new batch. Meanwhile our burgers arrived and I was ready to find some redemption in the form of a juicy patty and awesome toppings. Not the case. The burger was dry and cold, the pineapple relish was mushy and flavorless, the bun itself was soggy, and the glaze (which by definition should coat something!) was served in a little cup off to the side. Sweet potato fries came back out, just as cold as the first, which left me thinking that Monkey Burger prepares pattys and fries and stores them under heat lamps until they are served. This is probably super efficient for a place that gets a lot of foot traffic, but it greatly reduced the quality of my meal, and left me feeling like I should have gone somewhere else for lunch. I'm giving this place two stars because my friend's burger was slightly better. I know they're new, and I want to say I'm willing to give them another shot, but I was so displeased with the entire experience, not to mention it set me back $25 for two people, and what do I have to show for it in the end? I'm still hungry for something else Monkey Burger, hungry for something better.

text: WINNER: Best Carne Seca IN THE WORLD RUNNER-UP: Best Cheese Crisp Although there are now other branches of El Charro in town, stick to the original downtown. It's an old building with tile floors and warm dcor. If the weather's holding, ask for a table in the open air courtyard. If there's a wait, don't linger in the front; wander to the back bar for a drink and some chips and salsa, which are solid: they use the thicker corn tortillas for their chips, and they're not too salty. The salsa has a nice smoky flavor (maybe some chipotle chilies?). Don't fill up, though, because they also feature the second-best cheese crisp in town (order it with green chiles). I cannot rave enough about the carne seca (see: my last meal). It is seasoned, sun-dried beef, kind of like pulled barbeque without the sauce. A lot of people are turned off by its dryness (what do you think "seca" means, anyway?), but drying it allows for a full absorption of the spices, yielding an amazing meld of flavor in the meat. If you truly, truly love beef, you must have the El Charro carne seca experience; it is Meat of Heaven. There is a special carne seca dish on the menu, but I prefer it in burro form, mostly because they use delicious tortillas as well. My other meal recommendation is to get the charro beans, cooked whole in meat bits, which are far more flavorful than their refried beans. Perhaps it was the opening of other branches, but I will note that the quality of El Charro has decreased somewhat, hence the deduction of a star from what used to be a 5-star establishment. For a nicer restaurant, the service is lacking, often downright bad. The margaritas are wildly inconsistent: granted, this is a consolation that they are being made by hand, but even at the same meal you can order one that tastes like straight tequila and the next will be no more potent than an Icee. (I advise sampling their amazing prickly pear margaritas if you like sweet things, and don't be afraid to send it back if it's not up to standard.) Their prices have also jumped in recent years. Considering the quality of the food, I would not challenge this except for the lack of consistency (and the service). Still, this is a must-visit if you're on Tucson holiday.

text: Mckay's is the best used book/media store I have EVER been too and it is hard for me to understand why anyone wouldn't like this place. First of all, it is one of the biggest stores of its kind, at least that I've seen. The building is the size of warehouse and its inventory is staggering. The first thing you see when you walk in a counter where you can sell them items, which is great since a lot of places make you walk past all their merchandise first hefting your bags of goods. If they accept your items (which they almost always do, unless they're in bad shape or they already have too many duplicates) you can either get a store credit or receive cash. I can't come here unless I have a lot of free time because it is incredibly easy to spend HOURS browsing their merchandise. The bulk of their store is made up of books in all varieties and topics in both fiction and non-fiction. The rows and rows of books are broken up into sections by general subject matter. Each cubby is then divided alphabetically by author or sometimes title for non-fiction. I will admit it can be kind of chaotic if you're searching for something in particular. It's very easy for the books to get out of order and with such a vast inventory, it can take awhile for the staff to get things put back into place. My best suggestion if you're looking for a particular title, author, or topic is to ask one of the employees who can look it up in their computer system. (A used bookstore this size with this amount of product with a digital database?! YAY!) Otherwise I just like to wander around the aisles, picking up books that interest me. Their selection is pretty varied, you can even find textbooks here, but there is a weirdly disproportionate amount of used bibles, 'life guides' and other religious reading hoo hah here. I guess that's what comes of living in the bible belt. They do process a lot of merchandise, so their stock gets replenished very frequently. The rest of the store is comprised of all the rest of their used media. You can find video games from most every system here (they even sell used game systems if you need one), and they even have some newer titles. There are used computer programs and games of all varieties as well as books on tape and CD. Their used music selection is fairly extensive and divided up by genre and author. While they mostly carry single CDs, they do have some decently priced boxed sets and a limited selection of vinyl. And if that's not enough for you, they also carry movies on VHS and DVD. Their pricing is pretty awesome, if you're selling to them, they offer the best prices in town. I can usually walk out of there with a handful of books for under $10. You can even find newer hardbacks here for fractions of their original pricing. Same goes with the rest of their media. People treat this place like a library, and with its size and high narrow bookshelves, it is easy to find yourself speaking in hushed tones. It can be hard to maneuver around people in the tight aisles of books, and if there's too many people here I get claustrophobic. It's located a short drive out of town, just past the Charlotte Pike/White Bridge Road intersection and is very convenient to I-40. Their hours are pretty good, I prefer to go on a week night when there's less people.

text: OK, so we use to love Bistro Zin. When it was changed to Zinburger a more kid friendly place we couldn't wait to visit. Well, we went today and the results were not good. We asked to sit in the back patio and even though the back had several large tables open the hostess did not want to seat us there saying that it was "practically full." She offered the front patio but we do not like eating so close to the parking lot. So we ate inside. I asked for a table along the wall so the kids could sit on the bench seating. The hostess offered us a table closest to the entrance without bench seating. I asked again for a bench seat seeing several tables still available and she then took us to the back of the restaurant to sit along the wall. Before being seated the first hostess asked if we needed a high chair and I said yes. She sat someone else and the next hostess asked if we needed a high chair and we said yes. We were seated and about 10 minutes later our waiter asked us if we needed a high chair and we again said yes and about 5 minutes after that we finally received one. Though we had a bit of an issue with the Hostesses, everyone was polite, had a nice smile on their faces and our waiter was competent, friendly and attentive. The interior was much different than the dark Bistro Zin. It was very clean, bright and IKEA like.I feel they missed the boat with the interior. Instead of clean, stylish and sophisticated it came across as sterile and boring.They had a cheesy pastoral photo mural of cows on their west-side window wall. The windows shades were interesting. Though up, we could see that it would have matched the mural. The food itself was certainly not bad. We knew going in that it would be a bit expensive but we were sure that the quality would be there. The burgers were large and juicy and the toppings were interesting and plentiful. The fried Zucchini was tasty and so were the fresh cut fries. The Sweet Potato chips were on the other hand very bland. Their milkshakes were very large and tasty. We ordered chocolate shakes even though they were not on the menu. Here's the rub. We found 4 hairs in our food! I found one and put it too the side saying it is long enough to make me continue to enjoy my juicy burger. At first I thought is was just a stringy part of the cheese but it was a hair. I bit into the middle part of the burger and I found another. I had enough. I quietly told my party that I cannot eat anymore and another person in our party explained that he too found a hair in his fries. Upon further inspection he found another. The waiter understood and sent his manger over to speak with us. She took the food and came back understanding why we would be turned off by the food but it wasn't hair but rather part of the "palm pick" A toothpick like item made of a palm leaf tree like substance that held the big meaty burger together. She said that it shreds apart at times and could look like a hair. I told her that it could not have been that unless they rub the pick inside the burger and throughout the cheese. We then showed her the hair in the fries.She understood and comped the whole meal. She assured us that this is the first case and is not typical of their food quality or service. I tend to believe her. Thankfully none of the hair were the short and curly type but it did kill the experience. I doubt that I'll ever go back but I cannot say that other's would not enjoy it. Zinburgrer lost a star for the hostess, a star for the price and a star for the hair.

Whipped made 12 yummy little cupcakes which I could have scarfed down right then and there (they were perfect) but I managed the urge to stuff them all in my mouth. text: Worst. Food. Ever. This is the poor man's Carmines. This restaurant made me realize I can never leave New York, because it's just not the same...anywhere. Buca di Beppo...we came up with many nicknames for this place during and after....but anyway, the place is ridiculously over-decorated. One room was hardcore Vatican with a bust of the Pope in the middle of the table spinning. Mmmm. Little much. The palce is also hardcore topsy-turvy we had to walk through the kitchen just to get to our table and good luck trying to find the bathroom and then your way back to your table. But let's cut to the food shall we?? Tasteless. Tasteless. Tasteless. So bland. i couldn't add enough salt and pepper to my food. At one point I just gave up. Our guy friends ordered the Chicken Marsala and they were immediately complaining that it tasted like the chicken was soaked in maple syrup. They can be a little dramatic so I tasted it for myself. Ummmm....yup--really?!? Maple Syrup. So sweet! Chicken Marsala is not supposed to be sweet! So they sent it back--yeah we were those people. Our waiter came over and even the manager, who was like "yeaaaahhhh....it is a little sweet." CHICKEN MARSALA IS NOT SUPPOSED TO BE SWEET!!! Blech! I guess the best part of the meal was the caesar salad and that even was subpar. We couldn't even get the beers we wanted---our waiter came back 3 different times like "ohh, yeaah--we're out of that...uhhuh we're up to that too...and oh yeah--that one---seems like we don't have that either." Terrible. Terrible. Anyway, some people really love this place, but I'm not willing to give it another try. My stomach didn't recover for a good 4 days afterwards. Mmm. Oh no. Never again.

And if you have room afterwards, I suggest a trip to the dessert rooms. Each dessert room is its own little alcove, providing a nice private ambiance.... and the desserts aren't too shabby either. Needless to say, I am a fan and I make a point to always go to Bern's when I have the chance.

text: What can I say about Joe Pesce? I came with a small group for happy hour and we asked to be seated outside. We were given dinner and drink menus, but no mention was made of their happy hour except when we asked the waiter. He only mentioned drinks and didn't say anything about the appetizers that were $4 a plate, until someone else in our group mentioned it. Ended up getting two plates of $4 calamari. Perhaps the $4 should have tipped us off, but it was not good. The squid was very chewy and bland, and the breading lacked seasoning and flavor. The marinara sauce served on the side tasted like a crushed tomato in water.. bland bland bland. Given that this is a seafood restaurant, I expected something better. Not breathtaking, given the price point, but at least something edible. Service left something to be desired. They brought out the appetizers.. but didn't bring any utensils. Are we supposed to eat calamari with our fingers? They brought out the drinks, then failed to bring napkins. I felt like we were being rushed.. yes, we did sit there for almost two hours, but the restaurant wasn't busy at all PLUS we were sitting outside, so I didn't appreciate the pushy waitstaff. The waiter also told us the wrong price, saying that beers were $2 a pop. Someone then ordered two Coronas, only to find that they're $5 each. Yikes. They also screwed up our bill, charging us for beers that nobody had ordered and completely leaving off the calamari dishes. I most likely won't be back.

text: I was so hyped up to come here last night for dinner. It looked so beautiful inside and located on a quaint side of town. My friend and I have been craving guacamole for a long time, so we wanted to see what the whole fuss was about. Now we know. It was really neat to watch the waiter make our guacamole in front of our eyes. We got the guacamole special which was the guacamole on the menu plus some extra ingredients, which for us were truffles and manchego cheese I think. Cilantro and some jalapeno are mashed into the guacamole; don't be afraid of the jalapeno, you won't feel the spiciness. So this is one of those places where if you sit in the dining room, you won't be able to take advantage of the happy hour special. Lame. I'm not a tequila fan, and even after a drink here I'm still not a tequila fan. We got the enfrijoladas to split between the two of us because we were determined to finish our guacamole and we were limited to veggie and fish options due to our dietary restrictions at the moment. They were alright. I expected seeing more, erm, exotic vegetables inside as opposed to seeing mixed vegetables which I can easily get from the freezer section of the supermarket. And service. Really, now? I see you giving other customers better service, what the hell? Biscotti with the check, really? Well we never got one, thanks very much. We barely saw our waitress and when asking them for advice, I never got any. Never want to go back. Really, a meal that looks like I could have microwaved it myself, happy hour limitations, and curt service. Awful. One star experience, another star salvaged for guacamole. You let me down Xochitl. You so-cheet-ed me. Have a good life.

text: Ricci's is a tough call for me. They are cheaper than Sarcone's and closer to me than Chickie's, but I'm just not impressed with their sandwiches. This is a tried and true hoagie shop, and their dual assembly line set-up promises fast service (as opposed to what can be a very long wait at Sarcone's). It's not bad, I just haven't fallen in love with it. What I've noticed, by virtue of living close by, is that the clientele seems to be disproportionately black in an otherwise not-very-black area. I haven't the slightest idea why that is, or if maybe I just don't see the whiteys (they all look the same to me), but there it is. text: How I long for the days of a $10 cut. And $60 highlights. Sigh. My two most dramatic hair moments involve the Chop Shop....and in good ways. The first time I went to the Chop Shop was after I dyed my hair red. My boyfriend at the time convinced me that deep red was a great color for me....so I gave it a try. And you know what, he was right! It was a great color for me. For three days. Then it faded to this awful orange. I was horrified an immediately tried to get it back to normal but at the time I didn't know you can't go from red to blonde. (silly, silly, girl.) Luckily my hair was salvageable and I have the Chop Shop to thank! Fast forward a year. I go in and see a different stylist who literally chops my hair off. At least 6 inches.....I went from below shoulder length to a bob. Up until that point the thought of short hair like that horrified me.....but it looked SO good. Now, another girl may have had a panic attack right then and there in the chair but I didn't. I'm glad the stylist pushed the envelope and took a chance. Secondly the rooms have a kitchen area or even a full kitchen which is extremely helpful if you have to stay for a while. The best thing though is that the rooms are super spacious and clean and open up to the courtyard which is furnished with tables & chairs to hang out. I truly recommend staying here if you do not look for the typical Hotel accommodation. BTW: the couple running this place is very friendly and helpful. They totally made me feel welcome and at home especially since I had practically moved across the world and didn't know anybody.

text: My first and only experience had my party waiting a ridiculous amount of time for service. When a waitress finally showed up, she took our orders and 5 minutes later came back with a question about the order, indicating that she hadn't placed it yet. When we realized our hour lunch was going to take longer (we had to get back for a meeting), we asked her to have the lunch boxed to go. She came out with 4 of the 5 lunches. She then realized she forgot to put my order in. She ran into the back, then returned saying the kitchen said they could make my lunch in 2 minutes. So we waited. 10 minutes later she came out with the forgotten lunch and a revised bill. What did we get for the missed order? She took the drinks off the bill. First of all, only 2 of the 5 of us ordered drinks, and they totalled $5. Second, I had water yet I was the one whose lunch was forgotten. So basically, for that big of a screw up (which caused us to be really late for the meeting), 2 people in my party got a discount on their lunch and I got nothing for a lunch order that was never submitted. What kind of customer service is that? It's not even logical. I can't imagine ever wanting to go back after that.

text: Okay, I've tried El Fuego three times. I had no desire to go back after the first time, but it's a block away from work and people rave about it, so I figured I just hit an "off" day. The first time I had a burrito, second time tacos and today a quesedilla. I've had way better, even in Philly. I think "meh" pretty much sums up the taste of the food. Everyone points out that it's fresh, which I suppose is usually better than frozen, but if it's lacking in flavor and not prepared well, it doesn't do much good. The service was okay, I guess. The girl who took my order today was completely confused when I asked for a cheese quesedilla. Apparently you can only get it with meat or veggies (read: a couple of peppers and onions) and she put beans in it. I'd never had a quesedilla with beans in it but I thought, "what the hell, I like beans." I think my biggest problem with this place is the sogginess factor. They don't use a slotted spoon to drain the beans so you get a bunch of water in your burrito/tacos/quesedilla. It makes it very messy, and just plain unpleasant to eat. And what's with the loud dance music? It makes my head hurt and I sure wouldn't want to eat in because you can barely talk to your friends over the music. Maybe I'm just missing something, but I'm just not getting the four and five star ratings. The main reason for the second star is that they serve Jarritos sodas. That would only be better if they served the Jamaica flavor. Would it kill them to offer nachos? They have all the ingredients but don't serve them. I have to say I love some good nachos, so if they put them on the menu they might be able to redeem themselves to me.
label: NEG

text: My first dining experience at Yemanja Brasil was many moons ago and, trying to impress my now fiance, I ordered some vegetarian dish. I was blown away! After getting warmed up with a Caipirinha, make that a double, i ordered the national dish Feijoada de Ogum. When they came out with a plate AND a big ol' bowl of meat and beans I was very excited to say the least. My plate was packed with rice, collard greens and farofa. The waitress kindly explained that traditionally the beans/meat is ladled over the rice and eaten that way so I dove right in. It was delicious! My lovely fiance had her favorite, the vegetarian botafogo which is very delicious and if you're a meat eater, you wont miss the meat at all. It's got so much flavor and a delicious potato salad that goes along with it. I may just have to order that next time... The service was somewhat lacking towards the end of our meal but we were eventually taken care of by the owner. We were seated by the door to the outside patio and the constant traffic detracted from the environment. I also have a beef with the mixture of benches and regular chairs where we were seated... I just cant seem to get comfortable in that kind of setting. All in all its a very good experience and would highly recommend it!

text: I grew up going to this place as a hang out spot. I'm just old enough to remember Roy Rogers, the drywall tunnel that is now Kmart, the fountain/stairs where GameStop is, JCPenney in the basement, the boardwalk fry covered columns in the Gallery I food court (pre-Gallery II), the ORIGINAL Tiffany's bakery location, The Strawbridges' bakery and food court, and the BACK entrance to the 8th street El stop. It really was cool when I was a kid... so young my mom had to take me. Since 2001, I've had nothing but complete disdain for this place. It's an embarrassment. I hate seeing tourists in there when there are much better shopping options nearby. I think the damage is done. Short of a complete shutdown and renovation I don't see it ever making a comeback. It's good to see that Tiffany's is still around though. Overall, it's a homeless haven now. I'll always have those fond memories of the 2nd and 3rd floors of Gallery I. It was like a nightclub for kids. Beautiful girls working at every store (that mattered), prices on sneakers and clothes were negotiable, rappers and sports stars would stop in at times, and I always ran into someone I knew. Circa 99-00.

text: There are 4 really good tasty burgers in the St Louis metro: The Hilltop; Carl's Drive In; Cousin Hugo's and The Village Bar. They are all excellent in their own right. text: Yuck. HIGHLY disappointed. used to hit up Scotty's in Bloomington all the time when I was in school. Somehow I don't remember it being as overpriced and underwhelming as it recently was. It was actually so poor it is why I'm on here right now bc it inspired me to finally get on Yelp and stop being a lurcker and just post something myself already. We went on a Thursday, around happy hour time. good crowd, competent and attentive server. liked the personal tvs at each table. Boyfriend's draft beer had too many bubbles in it. but whatever, he ordered cheap beer and maybe should have gone with a microbrew instead. So if I had to give stars based on only those elements, maybe 4. But definitely sticking to "1" for the food. I know a good burger and I will pay good money and travel a good distance for a good one. this was most decidedly NOT that, not comparable to Capital Grill or Harry&Izzys or 14 West or McCormicks where their prime burgers are even less expensive to begin with! and it truly paled against any of the local (and cheaper!) awesomeness like Barringer's or Bub's, or heck, 96th street burgers right down the street, where they all always deliver the whole package--beverage-burger-fries/rings--deal spot on right. Everytime. Scotty's really likes to push the build-your-own-burger where even the condiments are an extra 75 cents. Our server's every other sentence promoted that. I had the bison burger cooked medium well on a ciabatta bun. Onion rings on the side. Ciabatta bread was so dry and stale it was unsalvagable-- even with bandaids mayo, ketchup, nothing worked. it wasn't even toasted and it literally just crumbled in your hands... i ended up having to eat a carb-free burger with fork and knife. Also, my patty was not medium well, it was well-well. I asked for pickles and got 2, which they brought to us ever so ceremoniously in a small container sitting on it's own little plate. for TWO pickle slices?! I mean, you had to laugh. what, do i have to cough up another $0.75 for 2 more? is it that too much to ask? I got 5 small soggy cold onion rings for my $2.50 upgrade. My friends, Hardees has better onion rings. steak n shake has better onion rings. you get my drift. AGAIN, i don't mind the cash, just could you please just make it so i'm paying for something reasonably half-decent! Boyfriend ordered the Indiana Prime burger, cooked well, w/ cheddar cheese and bacon. w/ potato soup as the side. His bun was okay, burger was medium--- NOT well, as he'd requested his. Cheese was a ghost of a slice, as if it had melted completely away before it got to the table. Bacon slices were limp and chewy. Meat did not taste any better than any other ol ground chuck patty. Soup was goupy and flavorless-- he said even crappy foodservice Outback's is better. So the check came and our two sandwiches came out to about $15 each. For all that you have just read above. and that's that folks. FAR TOO MANY other great burger joints around town than to give this one a second chance.
label: NEG

text: This is one of the last great generalist used and rare open stock bookstores in the region. The proprietors are real bookmen who know books, the book trade, and their customers. Bravo.

text: Having Rolling Hill Park as an asset makes me so happy to be a resident of Lower Merion Township. This property could have easily been sold off to developers for millions upon millions of dollars, but the township transformed this historic property that changed hands many times in to a world class park. I've been exploring Rolling Hill Park ever since the summer of 1996, and it came along way since then. Rolling Hill Park was bought from the Pew family in 1995, and transformed in to the park that we see today. Let me give you a brief overview of the park. The first mill was built in 1764, and transformed in to a huge mill at the lower end of the park along Mill Creek. Throughout the lower portion of the park, you will find 4 stone ruins of the mill workers dormitories. On the upper portion of the park, to your left hand side, you will see a stone building in ruins and a concrete silo. These along with a pig stable down a little further are what remain of the old farm days of the property. The upper portion changes hands a few times from a farm to a residence and then was bought by the Pew Family (founders of Sun Oil Company, you may know it as Sunoco) after the Stock Market crashed in 1929. The highlight of the property was a large modern mansion that was built by the last owner. The Pews built a lot on the upper portion, including a large pool. This pool was filled in, and the pool house ruins were there to explore in 1996. Now in it's place is a set of bathrooms built in the same stone style, and you can still see the outline of the pool in stone. If you walk straight down the main path, to the large clearing you will see a lot of steps and stone blocks. This is the remains of the old garden that was in front of the mansion. The old mansion was being dismantled in 1958 when it burnt down, and none of it remains today. Now back to the park. The park is beautiful. You have what I believe is over 100 acres to explore including all the old ruins, many paths, and very interesting historic relics from the early 19th and 20th century still around. You can go down to Mill Creek and sift through the water to find tiny broken pieces of pottery from the days of the mill workers. Every time I head to Rolling Hill Park, I always find something interesting and brand new to me. You have more than enough room go explore and never see someone else your entire time, which is why Rolling Hill Park is so special to have.

text: Tria...Tria...Tria....my old watering hole. I have spent many a nites and many a paychecks...and it has always been worth it. I came to Tria a few summers ago the first time, it was a long long evening and ended with last call. With among the last beers my brother & I had we decided to get some cheese which came with ultra ultra tasty honey. On asking our chirpy waitress (how she had a bounce in her step and energy in her voice at the end of a Saturday is beyond me) where that honey came from she asked us to write the question and told us Jon will get back to us. Sure enough the next morning I got an e-mail from Jon (with my correct first name-a big effort) giving details on the honey. Also since the honey was sold in 5 gallon jars from a beekeepers house in Flourtown, PA he offered to sell a smaller quantity. I showed up at Tria the next evening and walked out with a pint glass filled with honey & covered with saran wrap (it looks suspiciously like beer on the street :-o). Long story to illustrate the wonderful service. Tria sells Wine, Beer and Cheese. In addition it sells simple snacks such as sandwiches. The beer selection on tap (and in bottles) is outstanding, they do tend to have a couple of local beers on tap, apart from Allagash white & Dogfish head. If you are around here Christmas time I would highly recommend the Saison Dupont Christmas Ale (Avec Les Bons Vaeux de la Brasserie Dupont). In the wines I would recommend the Vouvray, it is a spectacular wine from 89. (If you are in a group skip the glasses and get the bottle, really reasonably priced). I liked the way the menus are organized (Food, Cheese, Wine, Beer). The tria are organized according to taste, for instance zippy whites. The food is delicious, even simple things like the white bean spread are really good. The cafe itself is rather long with some tables in the front and along the walls. There is some outside seating in good weather months. I preferred sitting inside if I could get a place. This is not a place for huge groups, best as an intimate setting. To give some history on this place, it used to be the Alaska ice cream place before it became tria, so think ice cream place converted to bar, how large could it be. That said the interiors are spectacularly done and this place could hands down compete with one of those places from New York. A newer 'branch' of Tria has opened on 12th & Spruce, it can fit a larger group. I went there as a party of 8 last summer and they were able to seat us upstairs. While I like the original Tria, the newer Tria has a bit more space and the windows can be opened to the street so has a bit more Bistro like feel to it. There is an upstairs seating which is pretty cool. While there are other options which have opened up of late in Center City, Tria was a great start in the Rittenhouse area and continues to be a great place to get good wine, beer and cheese. (And no they do not, I repeat do not sell cocktails, other assorted drinks). The servers are among the most friendly people and it is a lot of fun just sitting at the bar watching them wipe the glasses. Overall I have not given it a perfect 5 since it does not have any sort of happy hour and personally I would like to see some more non-American wheat beer (Sorry Schneider Weisse is not the only representative German beer). PS: Words from the wise, do not end your night with the African Mead (regardless of if it is only 3oz) :-o).

text: Wow, so I get to be the person who gives The Sultans of Schlep their lowest star rating. A couple of weeks ago, I was looking for a mover to help out with a craigslist purchase of a heavy, high-end bedroom set, so of course the first thing I did was Yelp. The Sultans of Schlep popped out as a moving company with outstanding reviews which, like, never ever happens, so I dropped them an email asking for a quote, and left my number as well. I get a reply from Tom two days later, which is a little on the high side, but I'd rather pay more for peace of mind than risk a craptastic move. Two days later, I email back, confirming that I'd like to go ahead, and could he please call my boyfriend to schedule a move for sometime this week. The next day, we haven't heard anything, so my boyfriend calls referencing the email and leaves a message. Another day passes, still nothing, so we call again, but calls just go to voicemail. We eventually scheduled our move with another company I dredged up from craigslist, which actually turned out okay, but to this day I never heard back from Tom, either in response to my email or to the voicemail message that was left for him. More like Sultans of Schmegegge if you ask me. Two stars because, FWIW, they didn't break anything. Edit: In response to the owner's comment below, note that I mentioned that both an email and a voicemail message were not returned. Additionally, I had provided the desired time frame of my move in my initial August 5 email, which was the only one to which I received a reply, so Tom could have told me then that he was going to be out of town. This isn't just a criticism of the company's attentiveness to voicemail, but email as well; I would say that responding to customers is a pretty important criterion for rating a business. And the curious fact remains that I received a response to my Yelp comment within minutes, and yet my August 9 email - and August 10 voicemail message - were never returned. What is true, though, is that this won't happen again, at least not for me. 'nother edit: Well, maybe next time a potential customer requests a quote and provides a time frame which coincides with a stretch when you're going to be out of town, it wouldn't hurt to mention it when you first reply. text: Being from Philly I have had my fair share of cheese steaks. Tony Lukes if by far my favorite. Once you pull up out front you get the nice feel that you are about to sink your teeth into a nice juicy sandwich made the Olde Philly way. Today i decided to take a friend, who has only been to Philly a handful of times, to this place. I got the roast pork Italian with broccoli rabe and sharp provolone, which is my favorite thing in the whole world. She got the classic cheese steak "wit" and instead of cheese whiz, which is not the classic way, she got it with provolone. My roast pork was fantastic. The mildly spicy pork with the slightly bitter broccoli rabe and the provolone were like a symphony in my mouth. Besides Glascoes fried chicken and collard greens I would want this to be my last meal on earth. My friend enjoyed her cheese steak although she could not finish it. She even put mustard on the steak at the end which i thought was a little weird but not terrible. When you have a great cheese steak you don't need to add anything to it. Service was just like it is at any cheese steak spot. As long as you know what your ordering and are prompt with your delivery they are very friendly people. Location is nice, right near the stadium district and right off of I-95. If it is your first time having a cheese steak in Philly go to Tony Luke's. Don't go to Genos or Pats, they are not good and they are like the Burger King and McDonalds of the cheese steak world. Stick to Tony Luke's and you will not be disappointed.

The set up here is interesting because they have two big long rooms and they don't have a big hall between them. It's a waitress station. text: I give Procini only 4 stars because of it's lackluster ambiance, but the food was so phenomenal that I could have been eating in a cell block and not have minded much. My entree was spaghetti del mar and I found myself practically licking the plate! It tasted so incredibly fresh. The sauce was sweet and light and delectable. The portion was certainly not huge, but I am someone who prefers a portion size that is meant to be eaten in one sitting and doesn't leave you feeling bloated. Like many BYOs, it is a teeny tiny place so don't come unless you're ready to make friends with your neighbors. The service is intimate and friendly to the point of being familial. As long as you know what to expect as far as decor and space issues go, I don't think you will be disappointed with Porcini. Magnifico!

Temperature wise, it was scorchingly hot which seems to be a common theme with pad thai. It was a very good dish with lots of flavor, zest, and spiciness that I always appreciate. It was a satisfying meal. The next visit, I had sushi. I got an unagi roll, volcano roll, and spicy crab roll. The volcano and spicy crab rolls were excellent with great presentation and flavor. The unagi roll was alright - I think next time I will get unagi 'Sushi a la Carte' as the roll (six pieces) didn't blow my socks off. The meal was satisfying, although with sushi I always feel like I could eat more (and more, and more...). I would certainly suggest this restaurant to anybody who lives in the Bellevue area. My recommendation would be to shrink the menu to a few good dishes and cut down the dining space so the customers can actually be served. text: Easily in the top 20 meals I've had in my life! We had a party of 12 which was wonderful because a) we got to sit in the private room and b) I got to try a lot of different items from the menu. Did I mention there's bacon involved? - Redfish: my sister aptly referred to it as "fish from heaven." Perfectly cooked and nicely seasoned. Light and airy but substantial at the same time. - The alligator sausage and shrimp cheesecake: the bartender at our hotel warned us that this dish would "change our lives." I don't know that I'd go THAT far, but it was pretty awesome. Very rich, too. Two for our large table was one too many. - Fried chicken: Through some glitch in the Matrix, I wasn't able to try this one (how did I miss that???) but everyone told me how it was the best fried chicken they'd ever had. The only thing that was just ok was what I had ordered: the paneed duck. It was sort of a duck milanesa. Great texture and interesting sauce, but compared to the others (all of which set the bar pretty high) it fell short. Nice wine selection- with prices that I thought were more than reasonable. Mixed drinks were great as well- and also decently priced. I'm going to dream about this place.

text: so our third and final food destination on our little excursion to santa barbara was to have breakfast at tupelo junction cafe which YELPERS seemed to agree -- had a tasty breakfast alternative to the OC and for that reason i had to try it. the decor was the first thing that caught my attention. very earthy. very clean. very updated. very spacious. it felt like i was eating on the patio in the countryside somewhere but i didnt have to worry about bugs or fleas. perfect for me. we ordered the apple beignets which came in high regard, the vanilla french toast, and the crabcakes. of the three -- the crabcakes really impressed. if you like that overly breaded crabcake that most places serve, then this is NOT the crabcake for you. but if you're like me and you wonder why crabcakes dont have more crab in them and wish they did -- then you'll love these. the only other crabcake that i can remember eating that left a lasting impression on me was over at HOUSTONS restaurant but those were flakes of crab inside the cake and it cost like 30 bucks for 2. here for half the price, we had shredded crab meat waiting for us inside the cakes and it was just as tasty with the avocado salsa and poached egg on top. MMMMM.... im a crabcake lover so i definitely could appreciate it. other than that the vanilla french toast was okay. kind rich but it had a good tarty berry sauce to it. the apple beignets were tougher than i thought they would be -- pretty much 4 deep fried oversized donut holes but if you like apple butter then you might like this as well because they had a real nice apple butter sauce to go with it. im sure we could have ordered something else better to come away with a better impression of this place but the crabcakes are reason alone for me to try this place again. oh yeah and the all female staff with their clean cut outfits were pretty easy on the eyes as well. in case, you end up going and seeing a bunch of guys having breakfast there and wondering why they're not over at the locak IHOP instead pigging down pancakes. thats why.

Our service was mediocre, someone forgot to order our appetizers, so we missed out on those - no comp or offer for even a coffee to make up for it. However, the food was good - we tried the Chicken Imperial and the Shrimp Scampi, both of which we would order again. I would definitely go back, it was a nice casual atmosphere where we could have a decent meal and watch the game. Updated in July 2009: Went back and was very disappointed. They always seem to not have enough servers, they changed their menu (not nearly as interesting as it was) and now they are closed on Saturdays. The only reason I would go back is if I wanted to take advantage of their outside deck.

text: I sit in an airport terminal receiving messages about a broken aircraft, but I am content. What a happy moment when I realized my favorite layover haunt from IAD is now in PHL, and in an expanded form. Not just a wine bar, but a larger seating area plus outside "patio" overlooking the Philadelphia Marketplace and the peoplemovers. Yes, you *can* get a cheesesteak there, but it's overpriced and not as authentic as it should be. There's the Independence brewpub, but beer + food can make for rougher flying in cramped and strapped-down conditions. Ah, but wine and small plates is perfect. I skipped the salad this time and went for a full bowl of chorizo and chick pea chili. It was excellent--rich and spicy, served with crostini, and complemented well by the rich "Autumn Flight" of white and red wines. I also found a new favorite wine in that flight: a Columbia Valley red blend that was aggressive and tasty as hell. Yeah, I'll have a second glass of that. The snacks and salads were updated since my last visit, and all looked good. It's expensive, sure (a real dinner would have paired the $12 chili with at least a $6-$8 salad and maybe something else), but shit, it's an airport: you're once again trapped inside a crowded but strangely limited shopping mall, forced to pay whatever prices and eat whatever crap the local port authority deems kickback-worthy--and people with guns threaten you if you complain too much. At least this establishment is a place you'd want to patronize outside of localized martial law! It's less crowded than the IAD location, and has the same comfortable leather seats. I'll call this 4.5 stars, because the lack only one amenity: a stylish but legible flight status screen.
label: POS

text: Ok, I'm not quite sure about this place. The food is good. The location (right on the river) is great. But the service sucks. I've eaten here 2 times in the last 2 weeks (once for lunch and once for dinner) because I like their philosophy and location but each time had its flaws. My first time there it took ages to get our drinks, then the waitress handed us the check before we even finished our meal, she never even asked if we wanted another drink or some dessert. I went there again tonight after having spoken on the phone with the chef. I'm a vegetarian and the chef was very nice in telling me to come down and ask for him and he'd make me something special. Well, he did come over to our table and was again extremely nice. He made me a wonderful fried polenta with a portabello mushroom sauce (this was not on the menu). He also told me son he would make him "the best pizza he ever ate"..and if not it would be on him. So yes, the food was good, but the chef never came back over to our table to talk to us. Several times he came outside and looked around but never returned to our table to see how things were. I thought that was rather weird. Plus our server was extremely slow, never came back to check on us, forgot to get the drink my son ordered and took a ridiculous amount of time to bring dessert to the table. The place was not that crowded, so there really was no excuse. So, yes, the food is decent and I want to support a small local restaurant that gives back to the community but until they learn how to treat customers better and improve on their service, I'm not so sure I can recommend this place.

text: I'm a big fan of this place. Good place to watch a game (or games) or to just grab dinner and beers with friends. The Carolina barbecue pork sandwich is top-notch. I haven't found better in Philadelphia. Their fries are great, too, including the Old Bay (aka "Crab") fries, though I do miss the cheese sauce from Chickie's. Their cheese steaks are good, but they're not getting on any "best of Philly" lists. text: I really wanted to be able to rave about this place. I love French cuisine and French inspired cuisine and was excited to try it. I had the Croque Monssieur. It was okay. Edible. Nothing amazing. Looked like a grilled cheese with ham on it. I've had the same thing on beautiful, long slices of artisan bread with browned, all but burnt cheese at the edges and lovely baked ham. This was not that. No attention given at all to presentation (other than it being sliced evenly down the middle). French fries were limp, not crispy at all. That dish was $7.95. I then was forced to buy a 1/4 lb of cookies (they only do them in quantities that small) instead of just a few and it cost me $5.49 for some forgettable cookies. Again, edible - but, forgettable, too. Ambience was so-so. If you sit near the counter rather than in the dining room, there's a nice view of Udall Park. I'll not be going back. I recommend Ghini's/Le Baguette instead.

The waiting area is very, very small, so if you're bringing small children in here you'll need to make sure that they're not running around getting in everyone's way. There are only 3 or 4 chairs; however, it's never been crowded when I've been there. I almost never have to wait more than 5 minutes to get called back to begin my exam. I really appreciate their effort to keep things moving. The staff who work in the frames/ materials area are friendly and easy to work with without being overbearing; they let you try on frames without breathing down your neck (something anyone who follows my reviews knows that I haaate). Going here is a pleasure.

text: This place is under new ownership (new name is Meun Fan Thai Café) and is on the verge of becoming my new favorite Thai restaurant in SB. Very much looking forward to trying the new place in Goleta also from the former owners of Appethai. But Meun is going to be hard to beat. Love the Chicken Satay (great peanut sauce). Also love my favorite Thai dish, the Phad Thai. Just the right amount of sweetness for my tastes. The garlic pepper-shrimp is also very good (although the garlic-pepper pork was a little boring last week). But the most shocking thing has been the fried rice. Best fried rice I've ever had (my wife and daughter agree). Not the least bit greasy, and has a wonderful, perhaps slightly onion flavor. I don't eat fried rice very often, but love this dish. We've been three times under the new ownership. The service has been a little slow at times, and they appear to be understaffed if it gets too busy. But the staff has been pleasant, and the quality of the food has made it worth the wait.

text: Yes, an awesome vet within walking distance. This is a good thing. I came home earlier this week to a sick cat. Basically, he had gone on hunger strike and it was starting to worry me. After seeing him (Earl Grey) not eat for 3 days, I decided it was time to call in a specialist. Being that my old vet (Penn) is now a big cab ride away, I yelped it up and found Queen Village Animal Hospital. I called in the evening and they were closed. I knew this wasn't a dire emergency and it was able to wait until morning. They promptly returned my call the next day and were very interested to meet Earl and get him on the road to recovery. As luck would have it, it was their late night (Tuesday) and I was able to get the last appointment. Score! We got there and I was greeted by the friendly yet firm receptionists. I had already had Penn fax over Earl's vet records so they had his stuff set and ready to go. We were seen promptly and Earl got an exam and they determined that he had a minor fever and some dehydration. They attributed his condition to post move stress. They gave him an injection of fluids and told me to cater to him a bit more until he adjusts to the house. Aces to this place for the staff and the facility. They were very helpful and very interested to know about me and my animal so they could provide excellent service. This place will be my vet. Apparently they are used to taking care of cats with attitude problems.

text: I called around to numerous moving companies around Nashville to find a good price on movers to help move my girlfriend to her new townhouse. All My Sons had a great price, and I had seen their trucks driving around Nashville regularly. So, I hired them to come meet me at her apartment and help us move. To "cut to the chase"......DO NOT USE THEM!!!! It was the worst experience I have every had moving! The movers were two lazy thugs that looked like they had just broken out of prison. THERE IS NO WAY I WOULD HAVE TRUSTED EITHER OF THEM! Just like most moving companies, you have to pay by the hour for the move - which is fine. But, I didn't expect that both of the movers would each take 20 minute craps in her bathroom, nor did I expect them to take the time for personal calls and send text messages the whole time they were moving our things! I felt like I was a manager for All My Sons, since I was having to tell them to please stop talking on the phone and to show some sense of urgency in getting our things moved since I was paying by the hour! It was ridiculous! On put a wonderful ending to this excruciatingly painful experience, the MOVERS ASKED FOR A TIP WHEN THEY FINISHED!!! Are you kidding me? I like tipping well for people that work the butts off and get things done in a professional manner, but these guys must have been joking! The next time we moved, we used TWO MEN IN A TRUCK - WONDERFUL EXPERIENCE!!! They cost a little more that All My Sons, but they are well worth the additional cost per hour - especially since they end up being cheaper when its all said and done, because they are focused on getting the job done! By the way, I gave the Two Men in a Truck movers a $100 tip, just because they worked their butts off and were very professional! It was the first time I was sincerely happy after paying over $500 for a service. Once again - DON'T USE ALL MY SONS!!! Trust me, you will be extremely disappointed and frustrated!

The server asked our thoughts, and when we said that the food was mostly good but the portions were small for the price, the look on his face said that he hears this complaint regularly. We're well aware that quality fish is expensive, especially in Indianapolis, so we're happy to pay for good sushi. text: I've wanted to visit Cochon for a while, and since I believe in ordering to a restaurant's strength, I always planned to choose among the signature pork dishes. My plan was frustrated last week when I was taken here for a surprise, romantic dinner. Cochon was an excellent surprise, and the setting served up romance, but I just wasn't in the mood for pork. I worried it would be a mistake to eat here without trying the pork belly or pork loin or suckling pig. The waitress confirmed my worries, and suggested the pork loin. I didn't listen, however, and had the Magret Duck Breast. I was not disappointed. The duck at Cochon was crisp on the outside, and a perfect medium-rare inside. It also stood out from many other duck entrees in the city, in that it wasn't covered with a sweet, fruit-based sauce. There were small hints of pomegranete, but it was never overpowering-- a great step away from the gooey orange sauce that frequently drowns the duck. The best part is, it is served with a white bean ragout that is peppered with pieces of pork! I was able to enjoy the duck and sample some of the pig-based menu. Delicious. I'm still thinking about this dish a week later.

text: We waltzed into this former Mexican fast food joint at about 6 in the evening. We ordered the Hot and Sour soup and and the beef with black bean sauce. What's odd is that it hasn't been for about 10 years and they haven't done a thing to convert the place to anything resembling something Asian in nature. Pay them a visit if you're poor college student that doesn't mind paying little to no money for little to no atmosphere or flavor. There's also a drive-through window. Go figure.

text: Eeek indeed. Before I explain the eek let me say that I love this little part of Samson Street that stretches from Broad and West. Was sad to see the Oyster House close. text: Short review and long review. Short: Be prepared to be upsold and talked down to. High-end selection for road and XC MTB, but limited. Attitude was the big turn-off here.
