Long review: Took my bike in to have bottom bracket looked at and, without looking at the bike, the mechanic on duty told me it wasn't my bottom bracket. Told me to re-do my dropouts then re-try. C'mon. I'm not that big a dumb ass. Did it anyway. When that didn't work, he told me it's probably my seatpost and 10 other things not in the BB area, except the noise was quite obviously from there. When he finally rode it himself he conceded its the BB. Rather than saying they can fix it, though, he says: "What you ought to do is get rid of your bike and get that Trek Commuter over there." This came after he insisted to the previous customer that his wheel was crap and its time to upgrade to something way more hardcore than the customer wanted. He told me he'd fix my BB and call me in 2 days. 4 days went by without word, so I went in. He told me he broke my rear derailleur hanger dropout. 1st of all, the bike was shifting fine when I took it in, and I have trouble seeing what the rear drop alignment has to do with a BB that creaks regardless of if the bike is being pedaled or not. Second of all, its a 1994 Cannondale. Not easy to find replacement hangers. After inquiring at length why they were messing with the rear der, they said don't worry about it, they'd take care of it. Wasn't happy. Came back in about a week later, asked for my Cannondale and they said, "Ooh, bad news: we broke the derailleur." I was beside myself, but when I asked how they could break my bike twice, they looked confused. They were referring to a different Cannondale...that they broke. Finally go in to pick up my bike and they try to charge me for the rear der hanger. This sparked a whole run of attitude about how my bike is too old, that I should expect things to get broken (the hanger that was on there was a replacement that wasn't as old as the bike), and that I shouldn't be upset they were trying to make my bike better. I wouldn't be upset by that except I didn't bring it in for a rear der adjustment and I don't believe that had anything to do with the BB, which they initially argued had no problem to begin with. In the end they charged me for just the labor. But the whole interaction combined with seeing how they treated other customers and hearing how they broke another bike is enough to make me sit here and type this review.

text: I have visited Villa Barone probably about thirty times in five years, and each time, I was astounded by how delicious the food is, time after time. The portions are generous, the red sauce is zesty but not spicy, the cream sauces are thick and not milky, and the pastas and meats they're prepared with have yet to disappoint. What is unfortunate, however, is the restaurant's rule of no substitutions. You can't substitute a soup for a salad, for instance. And not only are they strict about this, they seem to be very taken aback by any questioning of a possible substitution. So for those who are totally content to order exactly as is, and never vary from the menu whatsoever, you've found an Italian restaurant that you're sure to enjoy. But for those, like me, who sometimes need to eliminate an ingredient (due to allergies or just plain dislike) or wish to do something a little different (the salad comes with dressing and they won't take it off, so I prefer soup as I do not like dressing), just proceed with a little caution. text: I love the bagels at Manhattan Bagel, they are always fresh and are the chewy New York style I prefer. Manhattan Bagel offers a good variety of bagel flavors. They also have quite a few sandwich options (on bagels or other bread) and plenty of flavored cream cheeses. I haven't ventured much past the old standby of a bagel with egg and cheese--they fix the eggs fresh on the grill so it takes a few minutes more than places that fix eggs in a microwave, but it is well worth the wait. Unfortunately, they do not offer pepper jack cheese but if you get the bagel on a toasted jalapeno cheddar bagel that's almost as good! The cinnamon buns look much better than they taste--the new bagel poppers are a better choice. Be warned, they are *bagel* poppers. Don't be confused by the resemblance to donut holes, these are chewy like the bagels. If you like a sweet bagel, the poppers may be your thing. My only complaint about this location is the TV is always on and almost always too loud for my taste. Otherwise, this might be a decent place to sit and hang out for a little while. During busy times of day parking can also be a challenge but the spots in the parking lot usually turn over quickly and its not too bad a walk from the grocery store parking lot.

text: Monk's is located at 16th and Spruce, and it's a nice little Belgian beer bar and restaurant. If you go, I suggest that you order the mussels and, of course, Belgian fries. They have several varieties of mussels, and they arrive at your table in their own cute little pot with handles. The real draw, of course, is their beer selection. They've got a very extensive selection of Belgian and imported beer. I really enjoy this place and have gone with friends on more than one occasion. I just have to be prepared to spend a lot because they are pricey. This place has two drawbacks, though. First, it's pretty tiny, and it is always (and I mean ALWAYS) packed. So it's tough to get a table or place at the bar. You're best bet is to go on off hours, really early for dinner or something. But it'll still be crowded, just less so. Second, the staff is pretty snobby, although I'd say the bartenders are more snobby than the regular waitresses. Case in point: I went to the Philadelphia Craft Beer Fest over the winter, which featured well over 100 beer brewers. Each person got a 4 oz. glass with a 2 oz. fill line on the glass, and you went around and got 2 oz. samples of as many different beers as you want. Now, I know my beer. So I went to the Monk's table and ordered their sour ale. And the stuck-up chick working there told me that I should take a sip before she gave me the whole 2 oz. because she didn't want me wasting their good beer. Come on. First, 2 oz. is seriously 2 sips. Second, they were there to give out unlimited free beer for the night (well, I paid for admission, but still...). Third, that was SO condescending to assume that I don't know what I like. So that turned me off. And the bartenders in the actual restaurant can be just as stuck-up and condescending for no reason. In all, I am a much bigger fan of Eulogy at 2nd and Chestnut. They have 300 different varieties of Belgian and imported beer, the same food (just as good), but without the attitude. However, Monk's still has some great products, so it's not horrible. I just prefer to go elsewhere when I can.

text: I like going out to dine in fancy places and I really don't mind paying extra for a nice dinner. And also I expect high quality service and delicious food to be served... We had some things to do in St. Pete and after reading a very good review in local newspaper (http://www.tampabay.com/features/food/restaurants/tampas-chart-house-takes-seafood-upscale/1130308) decided to try this place for a dinner. BTW, now it is called "Chart House" and the fact that the owners did not bother to make changes in Yelp's profile can tell you a lot how the restaurant is run. Poorly. Food. - Worst Oyster Rockefeller I've ever had. Imagine six tiny fresh oysters warmed in shell and covered with onion + frozen(!) spinach + separated-cream-and-cheese glue for 14.99. I did not even know oysters can be that small! Onions overwhelmed the taste and smell. It was like eating onion soup served in a miniature sea shell. Oh, have I mentioned that there was no seafood fork with oysters? And I had to use my full-size dinner fork (which was bigger then the shell). Just like eating with a ladle from a ramekin! :) - Best of Shrimp entree was good. I especially liked the crab stuffing which seemed to be the only one really wow-food in my expensive dinner. And I also managed to get plantain chips (from tuna appetizer) as a side even though they were not on the menu. I like plantains very much. That is ONE STAR in rating. - For the dessert I had cinnamon with something that looked like cooked sliced apples and whole dry cherries topped with more cinnamon and a scoop of ice cream. I could not tell you was it vanilla or caramel ice cream because everything I had in my mouth was cinnamon. - Clam Chowder was just a soup. Not bad, not great, thick and chunky, with a good seafood taste. - Prime rib was good. Potatoes were fine. - Mud pie was a piece of coffee ice cream (no pie crust) topped with chocolate syrup. You can definitely have all that food at twice less price in hundred different restaurants. Service: When you arrive there's the sign outside "valet parking". And no valets on the sight. :) Do you think anybody rushed to take care of us?! No. We were sitting in car for a while wondering what to do next - honk the horn or just park by ourselves when a guy with cleaning supplies in his hands came out. Lovely beginning, we thought... You do not need reservation for this place. First of all, because the restaurant is huge, there are plenty of tables, indoors and outdoors. And it is almost empty because people simply don't come back there. Second, the hostess does not bother to read your on-line reservations form and your requests at all (OpenTable, pay your attention to this fact!). I've asked to be seated outside far away from the entrance door. Showing us toward the table the hostess asked where we'd like to be seated (outside or inside) and chose for us the nearest table to the entrance. Next to a table with a loud company. Cute. In the entire empty restaurant she could not find a quiet place for a couple! Because she even did not care. I've deiced to choose a table by myself... And the winning prize goes to our waiter! My husband decided to go with the pre-fix menu (soup or salad, a choice of entree and a dessert) of three courses and I ordered an appetizer, an entree and a dessert so none of us would ended sitting without food. It turned out it was too complected for this restaurant. ;) The waiter served only my appetizer. I had to ask for the soup my husband ordered. It was brought within several minutes. Enough to make my hot appetizer get cold. But it was not good anyway so nothing could hurt its taste. Would you believe that he same thing happened to our dessert?! I was speechless when again our waiter served only me with my dessert! And again I had to remind him about my husband's food and again he brought it within a while. Deja vu. As soon as the sun went down it became impossible to sit outside because of huge flies. So we really had to finish our dinner in a hurry. So at the end I was so glad our dinner was over! On our way out we decided to take several sweets with us. Usually in pricey restaurants they have cute chocolates wrapped in nice paper with restaurant's name on it. Chart House has round ribbon candies. Pathetic... Update after I got a manager's reply to my post: Hi Craig! Thanks for reading my feedback. I've noticed you'd made changes on Yelp's profile, it's good. However, I believe that rebuilding the facade and changing the name of the restaurant doesn't make it "a new store". Honestly, it is a lame excuse. Good luck with fixing your kinks!
label: NEG

text: try the tuna bimbambob - its fantastic. tasty and healthy. i eat here often and i love all the food i have tried. great quality. i have gotten used to the seat yourself thing, haha. the countergirls are always nice. tip - for take out call ahead. lunch is busy.

text: How is it that I haven't reviewed Reid Park yet?! I'm there at least 3 times a week! I'm usually "in the zone" when I'm at Reid, so I'm sure there are amazing attributes that I run by (literally). I use the path, which in distance is almost like running a 5K, for training runs. I use that word "training" loosely, because let's be honest, that marathon I was going to run this year, praahhhhhbably isn't going to happen. Sort of like the marathon I was going to run last year. It's all good though, when I'm at Reid I tell myself I'm in training and that usually helps me get around just a bit faster! If you choose to take the outside path, the longer of the two, you wind up running/biking/jogging/dog walking....by a lot of traffic, but I find that the whiz of the cars by my side motivates me to move faster. Whether it's their speed, the proximity of vehicles or the sheer fact that I don't want to die, I find myself moving really fast on 22nd Street and Broadway. There is a great little hilly portion on Broadway at the corner of Alvernon. It can get dark at night, but it's great training for the calves! My only complaint is the water situation. There aren't many places to stop for a sip, and it takes like butt. I mean, it's not THAT bad, but it's usually warm and has a weird aftertaste. I bring my own water for after, but I wish there was a better option for when I'm on the path. Ah well. It's a park trail, it's not like I'm out running a marathon somewhere.
label: POS

text: I attended a wedding reception at the Franklin Room recently. It boasts that it's vintage and unique and will provide for a lasting experience. There was, however, nothing spectacular about the reception that made me think, "wow, the Franklin Room sure seems like a great place for a wedding reception." Granted, its close proximity to 3 or so churches in the area make it a very convenient place to hold a reception. Convenience for parties that leads to assured business for the venue should not lead to complacency, however, and that is just what this experience felt like with regard to what the Franklin Room has to offer. First and most disgustingly, may I point out the level of cleanliness in the women's bathroom. Upon closing the top lid on the toilet seat, I noticed that I must be the only person who has that habit of closing the lid b/c the back of the bowl was completely filthy. It was unbelievable that in cleaning that place, someone hadn't thought to close the lid and clean the top of the toilet. It's not like it was just a little filth either - it looked like it hadn't been properly cleaned in over a month. If that wasn't enough to make me lose my appetite, the food sealed the deal. Stale rolls, canned potatoes (trust me, if you've even eaten those little canned whole potatoes, you know them when you see them), a soggy salad, and mediocre entree meat (it appeared that they were taking thick cut deli meat and throwing it in gravy to heat it up). I haven't seen salt passed across members in a table so much in a long time. I really hate to give such a poor review b/c the wedding itself was simply gorgeous. The wedding itself was simply gorgeous, and it seemed very obvious that the bride and additional organizers really worked hard to make sure everything was perfect. As a result, the gaffes with the reception seem very one-sided (and that would not be by fault of the bride's planning). I understand that some people don't necessarily care about the food at the reception given that the celebration helps create memories of the bride and groom's first moments together as husband and wife. There is a huge problem, however, if instead of thinking of their time together, I've called other friends who thought the food at their reception was bad to tell them not to fear b/c the food I had just eaten made their wedding reception seem like a gourmet affair. AND the bathroom - that's just inexcusable.
label: NEG

text: I was one of the people in line for the new iPhone4 this morning. Let me correct that, I was one of the people that casually strolled over to the line where people had been waiting at since last night and expected to get an iPhone4 today without having pre-ordered it. (blushing) In my defense, Italy was playing today and I couldn't miss it. Anyway, we got there and stood in the long line. Within a few minutes, the Apple crew was out handing out umbrellas to be used as parasols and bottles of water. We waited a few more minutes and an employee came out. He explained how many iPhones were in stock, how many were already reserved, how many people were there in line to just buy some and pretty much said that we probably wouldn't get one. He explained the chances to get one tomorrow and how to go about it. I appreciated that they even said anything. They could've just let us stay there at our own risk. I thanked him and we left. I reserve the last star only because I didn't get what I went there for, which I realize is my fault . . but still.

Since our Anniversary is in December, we also had the treat of listening to live caroling while we enjoyed our meal! I loved that on a Saturday night, everyone was dressed to the nines! I did not feel out of place in my cocktail dress, and my boyfriend fit right in with his shirt and tie. There is an outdoor patio that is gorgeous, and reminscent of the sea, and on the crisp night, the atmosphere couldn't be more beautiful. Do not be afraid to try anything on the menu! Trust me, any of the foods will excite your palate. This is definitely the finest retaurant in the area, with delicious food, service, and ambiance.

text: I came here mainly for the roti canai which I was craving and hadn't eaten for years. I'd been to the Penang's in Boston when I was in college several years ago and remembered it being decent food but nothing great. This visit fell short of my even already low expectations. The roti canai was fine and I gobbled it up. We also had the oyster omelette as an appetizer, and the ratio of egg to oyster was too high. For entrees, we shared the mango chicken, the fried squid, the malaysian buddhist, and the malaysian pork ribs. In Boston, the mango chicken was reliably tasty, but this time, the chicken was dry and stringy. The fried squid we sent back because we were sure they were old pieces of squid double fried in month old oil. It was that bad. The replacement was better, but still, the squid was too tough. The Malaysian buddhist was a vegetable dish that had a way cornstarchy, coagulated consistency, but otherwise the flavor was fine. The pork ribs in flavor and texture were good, but there wasn't much meat on the plate. Our waitress was great, however, and very helpful when we weren't happy with the squid. If I ever come back here, it will only be for the roti canai.
label: NEG

text: I am not a coffee snob, but there are WAY better places to enjoy a cup of joe on Main Street. First we'll go with positives: 1. It is a great place to study, meet a friend, or kill some time. 2. The staff and owner are very friendly. 3. They take credit cards. 4. Open later than La Colombe and Mugshots. Unfortunately the bad outweighs the good. When Bucks closed I was a little sad. I work on Main Street and Bucks was always so convenient (I am completely unable to carry cash for some reason). But then Saxby's opened and it seemed that little changed. Within the first month, however, things did change... First of all, the owner has definitely been buying less food. There used to be sandwiches and salads from Le Bus, yogurts, hummus and pita, granola and trail mix, and a wider variety of baked goods. For those of us who work on Main Street these lunch items were so convenient! Slowly the treats began disappearing. They do have soup (made by a small local business), but I'm not always trusting of the freshness. I also ordered a muffin and was really disappointed when I got back to work and found that the muffin was at least one day old. TOTALLY STALE! That was the last straw for me. The coffee is alright, but I'd rather go to Mugshots, La Colombe, or even Starbucks.

We all split the vanilla soaked french toast (which wasn't part of the prix fixe) and it was excellent. The corn and crab chowder soup was yum. The Loie burger was tasty and done the way I'd ordered it, although I was expecting more horseradish in the mayo. It had just the right size bun (supersize burger buns are my pet peeve) with doubled fried fries on the side. I'm a fan.

text: The best thing about this restaurant is the location. There were two of us in our party; it was about 7:00 PM when we visited. When we arrived, we were offered a table outside. We went outside, where we found our table with no chairs. The man who seated us said this would be no problem; he'd be right back with chairs. A couple minutes went by; then five more and no man or chairs. Finally one of us went to get our own chairs, at which point a different staff member hastily went to get us some chairs. We sat down and were greeted by a four panel, plastic covered menu. After reviewing the selections we chose, but the waitress who had taken our drink orders was nowhere to be found. After fifteen minutes or so, she reappeared, with the drinks, but without the water we had requested. She took our orders and this was the last time we'd see the waitress until the very end of the meal. Surprising me, the food came rather quickly. I was greatly disappointed when I found that the food had ALL been deep fried. The order was correct, though; it must have been our selections. Five minutes after the food appeared, the initial staff member checked on us. The waitress reappeared well after we had finished and asked us if we wanted any food to take home with us. We both declined this offer and the dessert offer. She left to get the check and was gone another fifteen minutes. When the check finally came, we gave her cash, waiving any change, since it would have probably been another fifteen to twenty minutes wait. The location was great; near to hotels and fairly close to both the Warehouse district and the French Quarter. The food was below typical bar fare and the service was lacking. I don't plan on going back, and honestly, would not advise others to visit.
label: NEG

text: Horrible service, and the drinks weren't good enough to make me overlook it. Six of us visited AG last night for my friend's birthday. Three of us ordered cocktails, while the remaining three were boring and ordered beer and wine -- it wasn't a complicated order at all. It took us longer to get those drinks than I've waited for some food. And, the waitress forgot the birthday girl's long island -- even though we all witnessed her writing it down. We ordered, waited 20 minutes and she comes out with five of the drinks, turns to my friend and is like, "Wait...what did you get again?" Usually I don't get too heated about slow service, but the bar wasn't even that crowded -- no one was standing, there was an empty table in the bac and the patio was closed. And hello, 20 minutes for two beers, glass of wine (you just have to twist the tops off and pour!) and two cocktails? Unacceptable. My coconut mojito was delicious and refreshing, but I can't overlook the serviced offered by that heinous troll of a waitress. I was going to steal some of their glassware to make myself feel better, but alas, there wasn't a clear opportunity. So we paid and ditched the goose to enjoy the rest of our evening on South Grand.

When I order from takeout taxi, it's listed as La Tolteca. there's also a La Tolteca in Fairfax shopping center. but after the confusion, i do recommend the food, and at least once a week the have a Mariachi band.

text: I will admit to a bias against this restaurant because it replaced Thai Royal House, which was awesome and I miss it. I did have hopes that Sushi 7 would be good enough to make me forget about the tasty Thai food I used to get, but it was not to be. The sushi is not horrible, but not good either. Everything has far too much rice...some rolls you can't even taste the fish. The selection of long rolls seem aimed at those who prefer things bland...over half of them are smothered in avocado or crab meat as if to disguise any fish taste you might experience, and the hand rolls are basically rice cones with a dab of fish topping. Husband says that the nigiri was fresh-tasting, so that is one bonus. The service was the best thing here...the chefs were fast and attentive, and the servers were quick to refill drinks and clear empty plates. I did not care for the atmosphere, the music (an unfortunate mix of top 40) was too loud, and TVs around the bar were playing sports as well, giving a sense that you are in a sports bar instead of a sushi bar. If you go, I would recommend the Hana or the Sweet and Hot rolls and the Ocean Star hand roll...those were the best things I had, although nothing I ate surpassed Sushi Pier for the same price.

text: I've always been jealous since most consignment shops seem to only feature ladies apparel. Well, along comes Flip to change all of that. I was in when Flip first opened, and the owner was very friendly and open to suggestions. He even asked for my contact information to put me on their e-mail list. I don't know of any other men's consignment stores, and Flip only carries the good stuff -- a list of brands they "flip" is on their website including Prada, Banana Republic, Ben Sherman, and 7 Diamonds just to give you some idea. If you don't want to wade through the dreck at Goodwill or other thrift stores, come in to Flip where everything is high end, in good condition, and well organized.

We weren't greeted by a host until waiting for at least 10 minutes at the entryway (we had a reservation), the menu was pre-ordained (no options), the food was uninspired (paella, lemon cake...) the service was incredibly slow (took us almost 2 hours for 3 courses), and the ambiance felt like a hotel restaurant in toledo (bright lights, 80's art, fake plants, etc). Restaurant week is supposed to be a great way for restaurants to reach out to diners that had been waiting for a reason to try them, and by giving US a bad experience, we will not be back, or recommending it to others. Big disappointment.

text: After a happy hour last night, six of us headed to Roxanne in Clayton. It had been several years since my last visit, but I remembered a large menu, packed restaurant/bar, and well-cooked food. That is not what we experienced last night. We walked in around 9pm and the place was near empty. A DJ was setting up in the hostess area, and we were quickly seated to a table. Drink service was quick, but when asked about house wines, our waitress admitted that she had no idea how they tasted. Maybe beer would have been a safer choice. The menu consisted of appetizers, salads, sandwiches, and some entrees. Not much variety here. The burgers were well received, as was the macaroni and cheese. My sister and I split a house salad, which was decent, and a ham and smoked gouda toasted sandwich. The cheese on our "toasted" sandwich was not even melted, and our seasoned fries were limp. Taste was decent, but given the fact that we were some of the only diners there, I was expecting better. The DJ started blasting music around 9:30pm, which made conversation at our table difficult...it seemed that he could have turned the volume down, since: 1) we were some of the only people there 2) there is no room to dance 3) there was no one attempting to dance. Overall, I was very disappointed, and do not plan to go back unless I hear in the local foodie news that drastic changes have been made.
label: NEG

text: If you are ever in Reno or Sparks you gotta try out this place. We found out about this place in our dining guide we got from our hotel. We thought we would try out the lunch buffet. The sushi bar was huge. I would say it would fit about 50 people. Our chef was very nice and kept asking if we wanted anything else. The waiters were also very nice and by far the best service we gotten at any sushi place. They kept refilling our water without us asking. They kept checking in on us to see if everything was okay. GREAT SERVICE. As for the food, IT WAS GREAT AS WELL!! All the fish was so FRESH! You can taste the difference between fresh fish and not so fresh fish. The lunch buffet was definitely worth it. The menu had such variety of hand rolls. If you guys know hand rolls, they can get pretty expensive. So it was so worth it. We probably both had about 8 hand rolls each. I would definitely come back again!! GREAT SERVICE, GREAT FOOD and the price is affordable. Lunch buffet is $15.95 and dinner is like $20.95. What more can you ask for?
label: POS

text: I went here because my boss had some list of the top burger places to go before you die. I think this was #4. The first night we went they were already closed. The next day we went for lunch. I had actually had lunch already, so this was a second lunch at about 1pm...right after my first lunch. I wasn't very hungry but I had to try this $16 burger, so I did. Let's just say I finished it all. It was the thickest burger I've ever had. The meat was of very high quality. I ordered medium well and it was cooked perfectly. The fries were also very good. I'm not a great burger critic but it was certainly a very good burger.
label: POS

text: Meeting friends and catching a bite before the Hockey game brought us to this little gem in Layfayette Square. Sitting directly across from Sqwires, it's not hard to miss. Being a Saturday night, there was ample street parking, along with a free parking lot across the street. There is a great selection of Micro brews and pub grub, with a friendly bartender quick to make some suggestions if needed. With that being said, everyone there was friendly and warm. We even starting chatting with some of the patrons at the bar. It just tops off that "neighborhood bar" type of feel. Growlers. text: Part I: I really wanted to fall in love with this dealership, and I did... at first. I've always been a domestic manufacturer kind of girl when it comes to cars. Hell, my father was a UAW (United Auto Worker) with the Ford plant in Gary, IN for over 30 years. He always drilled into the family to "buy Amercian", yadda, yadda, yadda. I should have heeded his advice but no, I had to learn the hard way. About a year ago the hubby and I took a ride over to Lexus of Chester Springs ready to make a purchase. We had just attended the Philly car show in February and of course we were all starry-eyed over the thought of a new car. Mind you, I had an '06 Pontiac that was completely paid off. What did I "need" a new car for? But that's neither here nor there at this point. We test drove a 2008 IS250, which was sweet, but then I found out that there was a faster version, the IS350. Sold! We were offered more than expected for my trade-in and the hubby used his skills to negotiate a reasonable price. We left the dealership deliriously happy that day, and I'm sure many of the police officers in Chester County were salivating at the thought of issuing me a speeding ticket in the near future. Unfortunately, this is where the bliss ended. Two weeks ago I was in a parking lot sitting in the car with the engine idling. Suddenly, the car started idling really rough; it was shaking and the RPMs were hovering at 0. I turned off the car, gave it a minute, and then tried to start it. No success, it would turn over. I knew it wasn't the battery because all of my accessories worked just fine (lights, stereo, windows, GPS, etc), and I had plenty of gas. I was at a loss, but good thing this happened only a few miles from my house. The hubby came out to meet me where I was stranded and agreed we needed to call for a tow. Here was my chance to use Lexus Roadside Assistance. They were great; a tow truck arrived within a half hour. The car was loaded on the flatbed and was on its way to the dealer. The towing company called us at home after to car was delivered to the dealer. Perfect. The next morning we went to the dealer since the car arrived after business hours and we wanted to talk to the Service Dept about what I experienced. The Service Advisor had no record of my car ever arriving the night before. I felt nauseous. My hubby just about popped a vein in the lobby and demanded that they find my car. He and the Service Advisor walked outside and found the car on the side of the garage, which was a HUGE relief. Only problem was that the key fob was not put in the night-drop, which is why the Service Dept had no indication that a car had arrived after-hours. Just to get things moving along, we gave the Service Advisor our extra fob and asked him to call us when they determine why my car broke down. In the meantime, I called the towing company to ask about the key fob. The driver of the tow truck said he couldn't find the night-drop so he left the key fob on the BACK BUMPER of my car, out in the open, in plain view. I guess it was a good thing that the car wouldn't start, not like anyone could have stolen it without a lot of effort. By mid-morning the Service Advisor called my hubby and informed him that upon initial review of the car it appears that a mouse made its way under the hood of the car and chewed through the wires that lead to the engine. I had never heard of such a thing, but what do I know? We were also told that this would not be covered under the warranty and could be pretty pricey depending on how extensive the damage was and the time/labor to rewire the car. All I could think was, "Buh-bye bonus that just appeared in my paycheck last week." A few hours later the Service Advisor called again and said their initial diagnosis may have been a bit premature and it was actually a valve spring within the engine that broke. The engine would need to be removed from the car, taken apart, and then repaired. At least this particular issue is clearly a mechanical malfunction (probably during manufacturing) and would be covered by the warranty. The parts were ordered and were expected to arrive the next day. Supposedly an engineer (or someone along those lines with that type of knowledge/expertise) from one of the Lexus US offices was informed of the broken valve spring and wanted to look at the engine to determine if there are any design flaws (whatever, it meant a lot of nothing to me at this point - I just wanted the car repaired). He was expected to arrive the same day as the parts. Stay tuned for Part II...
label: NEG

text: After hearing about this place opening I thought to myself i will give them 2 weeks to get everything in order before finally going in. After working in the food industry for the better half of 10 years now i know that judging a place the first week it opens is downright cruel. No matter how many soft opens or numbers you crunch there are just some things that can not be accounted for, and I typically will give a place 2 weeks of being open to the public before going in. That being said, i waited 3 weeks and figured it was finally time to give this place a shot. I was thrilled beyond belief to hear of a place opening close to me that would be similar if not better(from what i was told) that the foodery. guess what, it was not. At first glace the place looks fantastic, I will give credit to who ever designed the interior. It is a warm, comfortable place with a fireplace and plenty of seating with enough space in between not to feel cramped. After stepping in the front door, I saw the magical luminescent glow coming from the beer coolers and was taken directly there with almost a supernatural force as i could feel myself almost drooling at the selection. Everything was well organized and divided and fully stocked with an amazing selection. but where are the prices? can i scan them myself? can i look them up on a touch screen (like at the foodery)? is there a printed list of prices somewhere? does the kid behind the counter know the prices? no, no, no, and no. Actually, the kid behind the counter didn't even know what kind of beer i had brought to the counter to price check, let alone could he have offered ANY suggestion at all. completely useless in the way of beer knowledge. I brought 4 bottles to the counter, all of which i have had before and loved, to check on the prices which i could not seem to find anywhere. after scanning the first one i thought, well, that is a little high...over a dollar more per bottle than we sell it at the bar i currently work at, then the second one, a hitachino white...7.75 for the bottle. I thought that it was wrong so i had him check again, i was not wrong. I was stunned. I wanted to take out a rape whistle and scream for help, how could they do this to a loyal customer base from bella vista? I took the other two bottles back and settled on water, the prices were down right criminal. not only is the foodery VASTLY cheaper, but the staff is super friendly, always helpful, very knowledgeable, and always willing to help make a suggestion or assist in putting together a mixed six with suggestions from other beers you have liked in the past. this place totally dropped the ball of ANY of that. I will admit that there is a HUGE problem in PA in general with the taxes, and the LCB, and i realize that some of the stuff in there is hard to find, but when i buy 6 packs of PALM in NJ or DE and only pay 7.99 for a six-pack, i sure as fuck am not going to pay 4.25 for a single bottle! The markup on their bottles is flat out offensive, charging MORE than almost any bar even in center city or rittenhouse for something that I'm taking out? you have got to be kidding me. i will NEVER buy beer there until they take their heads out of their asses and their fists out of their customers asses and rethink the prices on almost their entire selection. in reflection, If i have to buy beer in the city i will never go to hawthornes, and i would suggest unless you want your wallet emptied and experience bleak and bland to stay away. For now I'll stick with the foodery, who still have slightly high prices for some things, but are still more reasonable than hawthornes, plus what the foodery lacks, which is not much they make up for it in other aspects...LIKE CUSTOMER FUCKING SERVICE.

text: Upon entering I couldn't help but notice a few business diners on their lunch break, several MILF's with her tea sipping friends, and AARP patrons all dining here. text: Being new to yelp, I'm figuring things out as I go, and I've decided that I'm only going to write a review if a.) no one, or very few people have reviewed it, or b.) what everyone else has said is directly opposed to what I have experienced. Mosaic falls in the latter category. Mosaic is f-ing terrible. I went there, roughly a month ago, for a friend's birthday. Though we had reservations, we had to wait two hours for a table. Only after I complained, did an owner/manager come to speak with us. He apologized, stating that the tables weren't turning over at their regular rate, and said that he'd comp us some starters in apology. Great, sounds right to me. Then we had to wait an additional 45 minutes (I complained around the 75 minute mark--take that math!) before we were seated. They actually sat us at a ridiculously small table in the corner. There were seven of us, and the table was initially set up as a four top. Once seated, the waitress came over and got our drinks and the promised complimentary dishes came out. The food itself wasn't that bad. It was unimpressive, but, I've had worse, so I won't necessarily complain on that front. But just a word of caution to any would be restauranteurs reading: if you're going to charge me $7 for something you tag as "truffled frites," make sure you don't give me fuckin' Steak n Shake fries with cold truffle oil on top. (Epicurean note: truffle oil isn't actually made from truffles--its just a cheap way for restaurants to bump up prices. You're welcome) Anyway, after the "meal," the check comes to me, and I notice that they didn't take the initial starters off of our bill (roughly, $50). I pull the server aside and ask her why the amount wasn't taken off, and she acts like I'm trying to rob her. "I was never told anything about free dishes. You may be mistaken." Yes, you're right tapas wench, somehow an order was placed before I sat down, an order which you brought out, and now I'm trying to screw you out of $50, just because I want to come back and buy 1.6 pitchers of your terribly overpriced excuse for sangria. I eventually found the owner who promised us the dishes, and cleared it with him--but considering I had to wait 2 hours to eat, waiting another 10 minutes didn't help matters. BONUS: While we were waiting for a table I went outside for a smoke, and a group of girls came out, in which I heard the following conversation. Tiffani* you should TOTALLY ask that dude for his number, he's super cute. UGH, as if Steffi*, he's a VALET. Maybe if he, like, OWNED the restaurant. Now, i have no problems with a little snobbery; hell, I unfortunately will admit that I popped my Lacostes back in college (I've grown a lot, i swear). But these girls were exactly the type of people that saturated Mosaic that night--faux hipsters that lease BMW's and over spend on their Discover cards so they can feel like Sarah Jessica Parker and crew. I wanted to slap them, but there were four of them, and I have a proven track record of losing fights to chicks. *-all names are theoretical examples of what I expected, however I have a sneaking suspicion that I am 100% correct.
label: NEG

text: People are lined up on the weekends to get in this place. I don't get it. It's over-priced and mediocre. I had the buttermilk pancakes and while they were good, they weren't special- no better than IHOP. The big fail on this trip was the ham and cheese omelet my daughter ordered. The eggs were undercooked and appeared to be from a mix- that unnatural yellow color is a dead giveaway. And the cheese- wait for it.... was american! American cheese isn't even really cheese! Pasteurized processed cheese food a great omelete does not make. C'mon! For nine bucks I expect cheddar. The service was equally disappointing. The pancakes and omelet were served on the same plate, and since my daughter didn't want syrup on her omelet she asked for a separate plate which appeared to tick the server off. When I paid, the cashier asked me if everything was OK and I said "yeah, OK is about how I would describe it", which got no response at all- she obviously could not have cared less. So go stand in line with the rest of the sheep if you want, but I'll go to Cracker Barrel and get a better breakfast and save some $ in the process.

If you're willing to test your Korean food-making skills (hel-lo, youtube!), you can grab your ingredients here. You can get other Asian ingredients here too. Pricewise, it's expected that it's going to cost a bit more considering its accessibility. So, unless you're willing to drive to the Bay Area to get cheaper items, you'll just have to settle! If you're just too lazy to cook, you can grab some chop chae (korean noodle w/ veggies) or ghimbap/gimbab (Korean sushi, almost like Japanese sushi futomaki) to go. text: Holy crap, this place is spectacular. I have been here for the omakase many times over the years and am always blown away. I have been to comparable (and sometimes more expensive) restaurants in other cities and with the exception of Nobu in NYC, which is pretty similar in its awesomeness, there is just nothing that competes both in terms of food quality and quality of service. If you are ordering a la carte, I highly recommend the ishi yaki bop with kobe beef (or, if you are feeling really really decadent, upgrade to wagyu). It is a singular dish - extremely yummy, and something you can't get anywhere else. I have also heard good things about the Sea Bass. They have a great selection of sakes, some of which are Morimoto house sakes, and they are great at matching you with a sake based on your preferences. Morimoto is not really known for its dessert, so I wouldn't recommend coming just for dessert, though. That said, let's get on to the important part: the omakase. First of all, paying more really does make a difference. The most expensive omakase grade is completely worth it - I find the $80 to be a bit lackluster by comparison. The same goes for the beverage omakase. I have tried both the general beverage omakase and the sake omakase and in both cases, they have been superbly matched with the courses (this is particularly true for the more expensive courses paired with the more expensive beverage omakases - at lower levels, it's more like some tasty drinks and some tasty food but they aren't perfectly matched up). Even better than there just being fantastic food, I have almost always had superb waiters who are familiar with the food I am eating, as well as the drink pairings (they either selected the pairings themselves or have tried them) and can talk with us at length about what we are eating. It is worth noting, for the lady who gave the place 3 stars because she didn't love one of the dishes, if you are honest with the waiter when he asks you how you like each course, HE WILL BRING YOU ANOTHER COURSE. They don't mind. They know you are paying a lot and want you to be happy with your experience. I have found Morimoto to be nothing but pure class. One time, a bug got in my glass of sake 2/3 of the way into my carafe and in apology, they brought me an entirely new, full carafe of sake. If you are really into food, you will have a great time doing the omakase. I have had a particularly good experience with a server whose name is, I believe, Dan? (he has a birthmark on his face) SO AWESOME.
label: POS

text: My chain broke on an afternoon where it was pouring rain, and since Breakaway Bikes was the closest bike store to where this happened, I stopped in to get a new chain. The employee said, "Well, putting a chain on takes time, and it's work, so..." but I was already out the door, cursing myself for not having my tools on me. I ended up walking to Trophy Bikes (in the rain) and paying fifteen bucks for a new chain that they installed for me. In five minutes. Suck it, Breakaway. text: Cube Libre was a pleasant surprise in Olde City, Philadelphia. The food was very good: we started off with a Ropa Vieja Arepa, which was amazing. I then had the Ropa Vieja entree, which came with fluffy steamed rice...the tomato-based beef stew was great and full of flavor (although, it could have used just a little less salt). The rice was plain, but a good way to clean the palate since there was so much flavor in the stew. The dish also arrived with plantains that were cooked to perfection and were just the right amount of sweet. The ambiance is lively and the decor gives a sense of Cuba at night. I would definitely recommend this restaurant to anyone in Philly or those who are visiting. It's located in a nice and safe area lined with other restaurants and bars, so it's a great place to have an evening out on the town.

text: I live just down the street from Seamus here in Dogtown, and we go there just about every other Thursday for Guinness and Buffalo Chicken sandwiches (the perfect combo). As long as you aren't expecting anything too fancy and just want a casual dining experience with good food, you'll love Seamus. You definitely get the authentic Irish Pub feel, here, which is fitting as it is at ground zero during the huge annual Dogtown St. Patty's Day Parade and mayhem. In the past few years they've really expanded their back patio, which is a great scene in the summertime. They close it up in the winter and it's great then as well. Always plenty of tv's for watching either the Cards, Blues or Rams totally stink it up. They always seem to be in the discussion for best burgers in St. Louis, but I'm a creature of habit and stick with the grilled Buffalo Chicken sand. It's excellent. They actually do salads quite well (try the Greek dressing - it's the best). Only thing I haven't liked there is the Philly, which was inexplicably like thickly-sliced roast beef w/ cream cheese if I recall correctly? Was not good. Anyway, always a good crowd on hand and yet never a long wait. Friendly staff and good service.

text: They have A LOT of work to do. I can understand there will be hiccups on opening night...but this many after they had been open for a few weeks??? Come on now! Is that what soft openings are for - to work out kinks? First off I walk in and it was crowded, but not ridiculously crowded (like I had expected). I asked a couple waiting by the door if they were waiting for a table...they were. I didn't see any sign of a hostess stand or anyone who looked like they were trying to keep a list of those waiting. Next thing I know there is a girl standing in front of me just staring at me. No hi/hello, how are you?, may I help you? I asked do you work here...can I put my name in for a table? She then replied all the tables are full (really? I hadn't noticed). I then say, are you taking names? To which she says no, I don't think so (cut to confused look on her face like I was asking her a really difficult question). She then turns to another girl and asks if they are taking names. They aren't, so I then say well I will be sitting at the bar will you come get me when a table is free? Finally! I got some sort of assurance that I would actually be able to eat that night. For real? There was no organization whatsoever. It was like these people were specifically hired b/c they had absolutely no experience at all in the restaurant business. My second gripe comes with the table service. This I guess goes hand in hand with the reception I received. There was no organization. Two servers asked to take our order. Both were very nice but I haven't had that happen in a long time. The service was very slow. Now I am not sure how many servers they had on, but it really wasn't as crowded as it could have been. Along with the delay in receiving our drinks, one of my friend's ordered a beer which never came. We had at least 5 attempts at them serving us food that wasn't ours. We even had someone try to serve us food while there already were plates in front of us. Really? Number your tables dammit. Or have the waiters/waitress server the food they took the order for. WOW. My last gripe is the restrooms. Co-Ed restrooms are not my favorite....especially when it's not just the sinks that are co-ed. I mean I really don't like walking into a bathroom in which all the seats were up. Seemed to me like a cheap cop-out rather then a "hip" solution to a small space. I do have to say the bartenders were very on point! They immediately noticed when someone new arrived to the group and when our drinks were running low. Very attentive. The food: good, not great. It definitely has potential in that area. I would hate to see a decent chef's hard work be spoiled by poor service and a poorly run business, but wouldn't be the first time I have experienced that. I had the Good 'Ol burger (I think that's what it was called). Tasty and perfect size for me. Fries were awesome! We even ordered a second round, even though we knew it would take forever.

text: This past weekend on my first trip to Philly, bf and i decided our trip would not be complete w/o trying out a Philly cheesesteak. nevermind that i try to eat a vegetarian diet, our local friends set out to help us accomplish the goal. our friend remarked that this wasn't his favorite cheesesteak place either (he prefers tony luke's), but that this place was good as well. we arrived about noon on a weekend and the line was wrapping around the shop, so we figured, hey - it must be good! the line was long, but it moved very quickly. within 10 minutes we were up to the counter. we're the kind of people who usually don't carry any cash, and just use debit/credit cards. this place is the kind of place that doesn't accept said debit/credit, only cash. usually there is some sort of sign to point this out, but here i saw none. luckily, it wasn't a problem this time. bf ordered the whiz wit, and i got the prov wit at the first window, and sodas and cheese fries at the second window. this place is kinda pricey when you consider that it's fast food. $25 later we dug into our food while standing across the street (it's outdoor seating on a few picnic tables only). the prov wit gets my "A-OK" vote, but i can understand why others wouldn't like it. the meat was sorta dry, there wasn't much cheese and there was a lot of bread to the cheesesteak -- however, when i eat meat, i prefer it this way. the cheese fries were flavorless and extremely salty. i'm glad i tried out a philly institution, but prolly won't be back.

text: I had to go to the ER this morning, only the third time ever in my life, thank you very much. What can I say, I'm a klutz! The hard and icy snow piled up so high along the streets and parking is pretty crappy, so when you do park along the side and bring your utility vehicle up onto the hard packed snow, do not underestimate your first step out of the truck like I did. Little did I know that under several feet or so of snow was a drain, if I had parked a little further back or forward I would have been fine. Expecting to step onto the hard packed snow, I stepped right out and my left foot and leg went slamming down to the drain grid. At that I then lost my balance and went sideways. I see you laughing, but ouch! It was painful yesterday and last night I could barely sleep it hurt so bad, when I awoke this am. the pain was twice as bad as I tried to apply pressure to the foot. Being the stubborn fool that I am I waited for hubby to leave for work, called my own work and then drove myself to the ER using one foot. Am I your hero? The ER waiting area was empty and I thought joy, joy. Checking in was as quick as a wink and I only waited about ten minutes before being taken back. Yikes why did I come here today? I saw how busy they were and it wasn't even 7:00am, so I said no to a bed that was offered to me and said I was fine in a chair after hearing all beds were full in both the hospital and the ER. During my time there I watched ambulance's bring in patients who were registered right there in the hallways from the stretchers they were brought in on. Some of these patients stayed right there, because there were no rooms left. Maybe they would have moved me along a little faster so they could have had my room, if I had agreed to one. Two hours I waited for a simple foot Xray, it did not even require the ER's time, it was a matter of calling an Xray tech to come and get me. After seeing someone brought in who fell on the ice and get attention right away, I started to get angry, but I started to cry too. I finally said to a Doctor passing by that it has been two hours and no one has seen me and I would like to leave and go elsewhere, since they were so busy. Dr. Jack did not catch his last name, grabbed my wheelchair with fury, swung me around and down corridors in a very rude and malicious way! He was so ignorant in the way he talked to me and handled my wheelchair. Two techs were standing there talking, doing nothing else, had no patients and I was seen right away. They were very nice. Turned out I have torn ligaments and tendons, no broken bones and I'm in a show boot and on crutches for the first time in my life and hopefully the last. They prescribed me heavy duty narcotics, but I'll pass on those. This is the closest hospital to my home, I tend to drive three times as far to go to another hospital, for the couple of times I have had to go. I have heard nothing but horror stories of St. Mary's, but hubby has been admitted here several times and I thought it was okay, not as good as others, but okay. I wonder how they will open up beds in the hospital for the heart attack patients just arriving. Do they go by who could have been released two days a go and their insurance is just being milked? Do they weigh the insurance of the new patients arriving or do they really care about who needs the most care? The way they handled the patients coming in and out was unbelievable. Most were pacing like hello, what is going on here with my care. Instead of standing around for a good half hour talking in huge groups when the shift changes, keep on moving to take the few minutes of care you need to for the many fall victims who came in and the burn victim. Get us in and out to free up your space and time for the seriously ill. I lost two dear friends in this hospital, one was a diabetic who had fallen and was in for injuries and treatment, he ended up with pneumonia and died, another was in after a stroke, he was to be released and go into therapy in two days, he got pneumonia and never did leave. I am not a fan of this hospital. I give kudos to Michelle who fitted me with this awesome blue boot (not) and crutches and taught me how to use the damn things. She was awesome.
label: NEG

text: Came here with my Vietnamese girl (Ha) after finding out the local Italian restaurant (California Pasta) was shut-down. Boy did I wish it wasn't. The Decor itself in 'Saigon In and Out Vietnamese' was great, the servers were pretty good, and the menu seemed fine. They had a Vietnamese style Crepe special that had Chicken (which according to Ha should have been Pork Tenderloin or Pork Belly), Bean Sprouts, and various herbs ($10). We shared that as an appetizer and the size of the Crepe was generous, but they were a bit stingy with the Lettuce required to eat the Crepe. We drank Mango Smoothies which tasted ok, but the horror began when I ordered a something I generally have at Vietnamese places with a generic name, Rare Steak Pho. The first thing I noticed was the broth, it wasn't clear and smelled like Miso. The broth is the single-most important component in Pho, and this one was an epic failure. For $9, which is insane for Pho, I expected much better. I guess I was paying for the nice plates the Pho was served in? Ha wasn't thrilled with her Rice Vermicelli with grilled beef either. Noodles were dry even with the addition of Fish Sauce. All in all the total came out to $40 + tip. I think Santa Barbarans need to head down to Westminster, CA (with cash since most places down there are cash only) and be amazed at the Authenticity of Vietnamese cuisine there. You'll save money too!

text: Oh how I miss Trim... I need a haircut and now live hundreds and hundreds of miles away and so there's no chance that Merril will be able to work her magic on my locks. text: I'm super bummed to be writing a bad review for this place. I was so stoked to go here because I was attending the Jane Austen conference across the road and have been experimenting with eating early 19th century as much as possible. I thought I'd found the one restaurant in existence appropriate to the Jane Austen diet. I was excited. The ambiance is wonderful with the waitstaff in costume, the pewter mugs etc. The beer was great although possibly different from what I ordered. The beer recipe was supposedly "spruce beer" which while delicious it was not authentic "spruce beer." Either they brought me the wrong thing or they just pretty much named an ale variety "spruce" to give it a more authentic feel. The bread was really good and did have an authentic taste to it. The mini muffins were supposedly a Thomas Jefferson recipe. I'm assuming that's Jefferson's cook's recipe since I can't imagine 18th century plantation master really did his own baking. The soup I had was pretty good though not authentic to the colonial era at all. They also brought me the wrong one first and then it could have been hotter when it did arrive. Also the portion size was miniscule for $9. My lunch companion ordered some elaborately named salad which turned out to be chef salad and pretty mediocre at that. Our total bill for one small soup, large salad, bread, one beer and gratuity was nearly $50. That is really ridiculous, even in a tourist area. The JASNA group were having a prix fix meal here on the last day of the conference and it was $95. From what I saw of the service and food quality, I really hope they got their money's worth but I doubt it. I'd like to come back here sometime when I am hungrier and have more money to try some other things on the menu. It's kind of a bummer that such a potentially amazing place has the feel of a tourist trap.
