They have the usual diner fare (think burgers, salads, fried foods, and sandwiches) with a slightly more upscale twist. Many of the salads and sandwiches are well thought out, and very tasty. Service is so-so, except for one male server with salt-and-pepper hair, who is great! I always stop at this place for a quick bite whilst shopping. I love a place where they are not afraid to put brie cheese on anything. (:
label: POS

text: So I came in looking for a mesh shirt to wear to Dracula's Ball. I thought I had found my match, bought it, then went home, tried it on and it didn't work. The worst part? I looked at the receipt and it said they had a no-return policy! Precious money down the drain that could have been well spent elsewhere!
label: NEG

text: I liked Eulogy because: When two drunk Italian bros walked in asking for Grey Goose, the bartender and everyone within hearing range gave them unimpressed judging looks. The bartender also told them there was no way Eulogy EVER carries Red Bull. My kinda place--that also happens to carry all the awesome Belgian beers I miss so much. I didn't like Eulogy because: At 10:50p when we asked about frites, we were told the kitchen closed at 11. Come on, guys. They just sent out some frites. Are you telling me there aren't any leftover back there!? Damn you, Philly, for shutting everything down at 2am.
label: POS

text: My review is unfortunately light, and based on one bad experience and boring pizza that included green peppers when I ordered without. Even after picking them off, just boring and certainly not a deal. I'm not going to give many pizza places like this high marks, most are the same boring generic thoughtless things.
label: NEG

text: The food at this "neighborhood Applebee's" is average, just like every other Applebee's I've been to. Like every other Applebee's, it has plenty of parking, is reasonably clean, and totally devoid of personality. I ordered a randomly-named burger (~$9), maybe the Super Loud Burger, the Melting Western Burger, the Atrocious Tragedy Burger with Uncle Henry's BBQ Sauce, or maybe the Brewtus Steak Burger? (Whatever it was, it wasn't anything special.) While our super-friendly server (whose name I forget) took our orders, I noticed she was wearing a button that read something like: "WE CARD BECAUSE WE CARE". I asked her where I could get one and she said she'd look into it. During the meal, she stopped by to give me my very own button, for free! That's special treatment, and it earned her a nice tip. (I wore the button to a Halloween party later that weekend which somehow ended up being pinned to a cute partygoer who I never saw again.)
label: NEG

text: Mmm... Tierra Colombiana! So fresh, so good, so fun to say its name. The entrees are good for the price, although the meat tastes kind of cheap... maybe I should go for things that are more stewed/long-time-cooked than not. The black beans, salsa and sweet plantains are amazing. Mixed together with rice and lemons - I would rather just get THAT for an entree.
label: POS

text: Oh no! I just got a note from the owners that they're doing a big going out of business sale and will be website only after the end of their lease. Boo hoo. Reno, you really don't know what you had with these ladies and their two wonderful businesses. They really were too good for you.
label: POS

text: First of all, let's state the obvious - this space is ginormous, and from the moment you enter it's easy to note the spot as a little, well, *vast.* That said, it seems like the current modus operandi is keen on attracting both pool fans and ping pong nuts and as someone who doesn't play a ton of either these days, was fun to pick up a paddle and take a swing at a game or two. If you look around, there's a hearty brew supply happening, a stage area, and a sea of flat screens should catching the game pique your interest. When we were in, the place was comparatively empty, but it was a Monday, they haven't been open particularly long, and they seemed amped and optimistic about where things are headed. Besides, it's nice to break a sweat and follow it up with a frosty one now and again. I'm sure that won't be the last time that happens.
label: POS

text: This place had kind of a weird diner-ish decor, but the food was excellent and the kitchen stayed open pretty late. Fried Craw fish was a great appetizer and the BBQ shrimp was fantastic.
label: POS

text: I had first gone to Misos once after a friend of mine's wedding. After the reception several members of the wedding party, friends, and I decided to continue to keep on celebrating. We did not feel like getting in the car and driving some place, and since the wedding took place in downtown Clayton, we figured that we would go to a bar where someone showing up in a suit or a nice dress would not look way out of place. Thus, we went to Misos. Misos is a cool place. We did not eat or anything being that we had eaten at the wedding, but we did drink. When walking into the place, take the stairs down below, there you will find a really neat set up with the bar. Down stairs is a really neat lounge. The night that we had gone there, the part that I was with ended up being the only people down there, so it must have been a slow night. But it was still fun. If someone came down there I bet would expect the Rat Pack to hanging out down there with us. Anytime I'm wearing a suit and at a bar, I figure I should just as well play the part up so I was drinking martinis that night. They made them well. The bar is nice. The bar and seating area has nice mood lighting and lounge furniture to relax on besides your normal table and chairs. Since the only people there was the party I was with, there was a nice hum of voices floating about but not so much that you had to shout over everything in the room. Misos is a relaxing place that I enjoy going too. When I go there, since the bar feels hidden away, I feel as though I'm walking down into a speakeasy, knowing the secret password, which is always fun.
label: POS

text: Overrated - I have tired this one more than a few times, as I keep hearing that P. Solis is the best. I am usually all about the small hole-in-the-wall joints, but not this one. I will give it to the guacamole. but other than that, by no means the best in town. Crowded - slow - costly - okay at best. The fajitas were actually the worst that I have ever had.
label: NEG

text: Ain't gonna lie, the service is 4 stars but the crowd control and wait is 1. They closed off the exterior door, so you have to walk through the book-store. At 10:30, the line was all the way to non-fiction... and that ain't no lie.
label: NEG

text: Yep, this is a cash-only establishment. The service isn't fast, but we weren't in a hurry. I can see how it might annoy some. The menu tried to be a little too creative for what I had in mind. I love Mexican food. I was craving carne asada, beans & rice, or other more traditional food. I wasn't in the mood for burritos with portobella mushroom or organic beans. On another night, it might have been an interesting menu, but this night it just didn't do it for me. But the big problem was the salt. The salsa was so salty I couldn't eat it. I ate plain chips. In their defense, my friend LOVED the salsa. She loves salty food. My burrito was a big wet affair--there was no way you could eat this thing with your hands. But it too was salty. I ate what I could and felt awful afterward from too much salt. UPDATE: went back with another group (not by choice). Again, the food was far too salty. there wasn't much flavor, either--other than salt. It's simply not good food at all.
label: NEG

text: I have been to Lolita twice, and walked out twice because of the horrid attitude of the tall male host. Walked over to other other mexi-themed restaurant across the street where I always get great service. Will never go back.
label: NEG

text: We made a stop at the St. Charles Ave Voodoo again last night. I have been there many times since my 2008 review and it's usually a pretty good experience. Hence I'm upgrading my 2008 two star review. Last night two of us split a brisket platter and a loaded baked potato also with brisket. Both were good, I wouldn't give it five stars but a solid four stars. The meat is usually nicely smoked but not too smokey. I do like their mojo sauce that is a very traditional type sauce. There is one I think is called crystal something and it was way too hot for me (I'm assuming it has Crystal hot sauce in it) and they also have a vinegar bases sauces which I don't like. Their side dishes are usually pretty good. We had mac & cheese last night and corn pudding, both were fine. I do wish they would open a Metairie location. There really are no decent BBQ options along Vets.
label: POS

text: I've been to this Salvation Army store a few times before and have managed to find a couple of nice things, and today I dropped in looking for a table. They had LOTS of tables, but the PRICES! Egad, it was enough to hurt my eyes! I could buy crappy veneer furniture cheaper at Wal-Mart than here! The high prices may explain their pretty good selection of furniture--because really, who wants to pay $300 for a used dining set in questionable condition? Apart from their good selection of ridiculously priced housewares and furniture, they have a pretty scant selection of clothing, which is very poorly organized. Overall, I would say stop by here if you are looking for furniture and don't mind paying above-average thrift prices; otherwise, don't bother.
label: NEG

text: I'm not going to bash the place. I'm just going to state the facts. I went in for lunch wanting a salad. I ordered the $8 beet salad. The place was completely empty and they had one person working in the kitchen behind the counter. He said they only had spinach left for the base, that was fine with me. I received my salad. There was spinach, canned beets, and canned string beans. A vinaigrette sat on the side. $8 for canned beets and string beans..... hmmm? Maybe I'll get a sandwich next time.
label: NEG

text: Some of the best Indian South Jersey has to offer. Creative, fresh regional dishes. The service problems seem to have been addressed - and the portions seem to have gotten smaller in the last year ( the Thali is minus a few dishes) but the food is always right on. Save room for the rice pudding !
label: POS

text: I'd say 4.5 stars, really. This restaurant single handedly gave me faith in St. Louis dining. It was authentic and excellent. The service was pretty good, considering that I was in a group of 11. The food still came out in a normal amount of time and everyone was happy. We started with the tamale and the yuca fries. The fries were spot on, with a parmesan aioli. However, I highly recommend using the free chimichurri sauce as a dipping sauce. The complementary plaintain chips and chimichurri and ceviche-style salsa are out of this world. One friend wanted to cancel his order and just eat that the whole night. He is glad he didn't in the end. The steak recommended by the waiter was a stir fry of sorts that was in a delicious sauce. The tilapia entree surprised me by being fried, but was tender and delicious nonetheless. I think to top it off, we ordered every dessert on the menu and passed it around. The flan was creamier than most and the rice pudding was outstanding. Really, you can't go wrong here. Don't forget to try the pisco sour! Tasty, but strong.
label: POS

text: Long gone are the days of my wildly expensive nights out (and my 27 inch waist!) My friend and I were just lamenting that no one our age wants to sit at Le Bec Fin for a crazy gastronomic $300 extravaganza. Seems that Meritage feels the same way. New menu, new chef- new owners (?). $36 bottles of Sauvignon Blanc "wine of the day"+ a menu of a zilllion $6 little dishes plus more substantial dinner entrees such as seared scallops. We ordered a bunch of little plates. The five course tasting menu looked delightful - $39 + you could add the wine pairs for like $29 (?) but would have to wait for another night. Scallop special of the night was paired with short rib ravioli. Interesting. Three tater tots appeared- I was totally taken by surprise by the silky, creamy inside- no school cafeteria tots a la Napoleon Dyanmite here! Wild mushroom risotto- I don't even want to think about the butter and calories in this rich dish. YUM. Expecting a bit more from an ex-Chinese fusion chef, the dumplings fell flat. Shrimp dumplings- bland blobs- not super hot. Pan fried pork dumplings- no wow factor. I told my friends we would go to a dive Chinatown joint for our next dumpling outing. The night we went, the restaurant was filled with a 60-something crowd- then, a slightly younger crowd came for the later seating. The bar, on the other hand, was packed with all ages - pretty rocking at 7 pm happy hour. I really liked this warm, cheerful place. I hope the new menu will make this place more accessible to a larger clientele. Service was fine- very attentive- sometimes a bit more talky than necessary. They were trying very hard.
label: POS

text: just cause I put five stars don't expect the world of this place. It is the perfect dive! 90's music, a dude in the back on a piano taking requests and all drinks are served in a plastic cup. 5 star dive!! Had to come here being it was the oldest Bar in New Orleans!
label: POS

text: One of the few places in NOLA that has vegetarian food. YAY! We went here on a sunday night and the line was out the door, which I guess was good sign. We had a 20 minute wait and then got a really nice table by a window. The waiter came by and asked if we wanted Hurricanes. We decided that we had had enough alcohol for the day so stuck to iced tea and water. To start with, they brought out a nice 1/2 loaf of warm french bread. For our meals, I got the vegetarian gumbo and my husband got their veg dish of the day which was beans and rice. Both were yummy.. We also ordered a side of garlic mashed potatoes which were very garlicky and a corn thing which was quite yummy. I felt that the portion sizes were kinda small and I wasn't completely full. For dessert we got their warm bread pudding. It was nice but we're not big fans of whiskey so we weren't too thrilled with the whiskey sauce. If I go here again, I'll ask them to get it without the sauce. Would definitely go again. I want to give this place 4.5 stars..
label: POS

text: I hate giving only two stars to a relatively new local business, but I honestly can't bring myself to say that my brunch was "A-OK" the other day because, frankly, it wasn't. Two seems rather low though, considering the cozy, inviting décor and the extreme friendliness of the staff. I think two and a half would be more appropriate. We arrived to a mostly empty restaurant at around noon on a Saturday. A friendly gentleman (the owner?) seated us by the fireplace, which was lovely as we had just walked through freezing winds to get there. The prix fixe brunch is $14.99 and includes coffee and orange juice, a starter course consisting of fruit with mint yogurt dressing and a homemade muffin and finally, a choice of about eight or so main dishes. The fruit salad was mostly melons with a couple strawberry halves. My first bite of melon was slightly prickly, but I decided to try another piece in hopes that my first was a fluke. Unfortunately, I was met with the same results. Moving on to the (apple chocolate chip) muffin, I took a couple bites and decided to save my calories. Except for the very center, the muffin was extremely dry. I was hopeful that the main course would somehow rectify the situation and make our freezing trek through the Collingswood tundra worthwhile. My chicken crepes arrived as did my dining companion's quiche du jour, which contained lobster, spinach, mushrooms and cheese. Both dishes looked promising but fell flat in taste. I did enjoy the consistency of the crepe itself, which was perfect, but the tiny cubes of chicken inside left much to be desired and the overall taste was very bland. The most noticeable flavor was the red sauce ladled on top of the crepes, which completely took over the rest of the ingredients. The quiche was somewhat better, although my bite allegedly came from the "tastier quadrant." Brunch was disappointing but I would like to give Bistro AmericanA another try sometime nonetheless.
label: NEG

text: This Lone Star's kitchen turns out standard putrid fare: their chopped steak ($9) is a dry listless slab of meat, neither fresh nor juicy and the grilled shrimp entree (also $9) is scary and to be missed. The sad fact is that they're making everything right, as Lone Star Corporate would have them do. (The Conshohocken location is junk too, and thankfully closed, last I checked. They used to have peanuts littering the floor - for ambiance - but I think many locals were thinking, "what's going on?") There's plenty of space, so I've had group lunches here twice - one time too many. Is there any reason to go back? Hell to the no. Even if you LIKE overpriced, inconsistent chain steakhouses, just go to Outback down the road.
label: NEG

text: This review is about the Adelphia House, one of the apartments that falls under the management of Philadelphia Management, so in effect, Philadelphia Management has screwed up. Way to go, Philadelphia Management. Adelphia House: This place sucking sucks. It is so incredibly brilliant at sucking that all I can do at the moment is use "suck" in various ways because the word that rhymes with suck just seems so crass. The place is tiny for what I'm paying, but I thought, "Hey, it's a decent location, at least it's not some place on Kensington somewhere." That's what suckered me in I think. Because of my foolishness, and the fact that I had no idea about Philadelphia 6 months prior. The leasing office and all of its staff will ignore you if you call about the various things that go wrong with the apartment (sink doesn't work, stove doesn't work, shower doesn't work, mail isn't arriving). If you call them out on how you're being ignored, they will pretend they didn't get the call/voicemail/email/telegraph/smoke signal/etc. I was without a stove for a month. A month! And after a month of bitching to the office every other day about how my stove blew up on me (that's right, you read that correctly, it blew up), they finally replaced the stove. And then they attempted to appease me by saying I would get money back (very little I'm sure since they didn't specify how much) on a month's rent. That was four months ago; still nothing. The security guards (not all, some are cool) at the front seem oblivious as to who lives there and who doesn't, which would explain why there are what appears to be various homeless people walking around on my floor yet I never see them do anything other than sit outside during the day. Granted I don't know if they are actually homeless people, and I shouldn't judge a book by its cover and whatnot... But I've never read a book that I liked that didn't have a nice cover. Any benefit I get from being located in a decent area (Center City) goes out the window with the completely inept services provided by this horrible establishment. I've never met a group of people who are more quick to blame someone else (including me) for issues that they are supposed to take care of. They are also incredibly good at pretending that they're going to make phone calls or send emails. Unless they actually are making phone calls and emails, then it's clearly Philadelphia Management's fault for not stepping up. And now that I'm trying to break my lease because they are not meeting their end of the bargain, but they are going to end up keeping my security deposit for something that wasn't my fault (the ceiling falling apart because the apartment above me was leaking, the carpet that wasn't replaced, etc). Don't let the decent looking lobby fool you. This place is as close to a criminal establishment that's being run legitimately that I have come across to date. And I can't possibly believe that Philadelphia Management doesn't know about everything happening here, which means they are just as culpable for how horribly the Adelphia House is being run.
label: NEG

text: I am not an Applebee's fan. I have been to this one twice though - once I was dragged here by my inlaws - who LOVE chain restaurants. (I guess they make them feel "safe"), The food was marginal and the service was, of course, by disinterested teenagers. Not my idea of a good time.
label: NEG

text: You get two stars for being the only department store to remain in New Orleans. You would get one star for my experience with how your customer service is handled. My story goes like this: I called to see if they sell my hair relaxer, which is expensive and somewhat hard to find (Phytospecific Index II - if you see it a Walgreens, it's counterfeit!). I was told yes, gave my name, and hung up. After a cab ride in a torrential rainstorm, I arrived only to find the sales associate sold it to someone else! What was the response? A sad shoulder shrug and an apology that was so insincere, I thought I was at the DMV. Now, I sell crap for a living, and so I knew there were other measures that could have been taken. I asked if another of their locations could ship one to me. I was told it was too late, although it was still early enough for a store on the West Coast to send one to me. So she calls Chicago instead. Finally, after other associates advised the manager, I'm offered the version of the product I don't want at a 25% discount. To describe this offer? Well, it's like saying, we're out of tofu, but we'll sell you a burger on the cheap to get you out of our hair. To credit the manager, she did give me her card and said there would be a reprimand, but just encourages me to purchase my beauty items online. I'd like my tax dollars to stay in town, but this episode was a huge deterrent.
label: NEG

text: Watch next January for the Taproom's premiere on "Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives," even though it is none of those things. It's an amazing neighborhood bar tha happens to serve damn fine vegetarian and vegan food along with some local classics (get the smoked coconut club sandwich - it's astounding). They also feature incredible boutique beers - and the nicest staff ever. Parking is plentiful and the neighborhood is blooming. I've brought dozens of people to the Memphis Taproom and all of them have loved it.

An old shoe would have more flavor. Good thing it had onions and tomatoes or I might as well have been eating a shoe. The fries, root beer, and service were good tho. Also, I hate that it cost $30 for the two of us to eat lunch. It's burgers for crying out loud. Strike one!

text: My BF and I visited Philly cuz we wanted to see the liberty bell. We arrived at probably 6am and we were hungry. By chance we happened to park next to Morning Glory Diner. We noticed that it received a lot of awards so we decided to check it out. I don't remember what my boyfriend had, but I had the breakfast pizza. At first, I was intrigued when I saw it..but when I tasted it...it wasn't as good as I thought it would be. I was expecting it to have some tomatoes but it didn't. Instead it had caramelized onions which to me made it taste a little weird...don't get me wrong I LOVE ONIONS but just not this time. Although I don't remember what my BF ordered, all I remember was it falling apart because it got sooo damn soupy! I felt so bad for him because he felt like vomiting. So all in all, we did not have the breakfast experience we were hoping for but it was a cozy place and the service was ok.

text: We eat here every Thursday. We started eating here a few years ago and the food here is incredible. We usually sit at the sushi bar. Brian is a great guy. He is very friendly and make great rolls. I recommend ordering the Stuffed Tomato. It is spicy live scallop that is chopped and rolled inside 3 different types of fish with ponzu sauce and topped with tobico. They have a roll of the day that is only $5. Anyone who enjoys eating sushi will love this place. Their cooked Japanese food is excellent as well. Update: I just had another great meal with my wife. We sat at the sushi bar. I have to say that the fish was delicious. They are getting their fish from a new company and you can really taste the quality. The yellow tail was excellent. The are also using a seaweed that is super crisp. If I could give 6 stars I would because this place is even better.
label: POS

text: We frequent NOLA regularly, and part of the joy of roaming the city is finding great, new restaurants to enjoy. All of us work in the service industry We tried Nosh today before debarking back home. Unfortunately, this one was NOT a keeper. We came in and placed our order of 7 sliders, 4 beef, 2 turkey, and 1 buffalo, a side of mashed potatoes, and some tater tots, with 3 drinks, Total of 30$. Sliders shouldn't take terribly long to prepare. It took FIFTY minutes to get our order. The restaurant had one 8-top, and one 2-top besides ourselves in there. The food was sub par, meat was fairly dry. The "mashed potatoes" were dry, unbuttered, and unseasoned. The best thing we had were the tater tots - which are pretty hard to mess up! Do yourselves a favor - "Nosh" some food elsewhere!

text: The Creole Cottage is owned by a mother and daughter duo who perform magic on furniture. The cool thing to call this is upcycling. Upcycling is where you take nasty ratty crap and make it gorgeous. They update their website all of the time which details all of the pieces in their gallery. This furniture is cheaper than what you would find at Target or possibly WalMart, and far more beautiful to say the least. I don't think I can type enough praise for The Creole Cottage.

text: This has my favorite sandwich in all of St. Louis and that is saying a lot. The bread is always fresh and the meat is plentiful. The person I used to go there with always got a Gyro and raved about it. It is a little expensive for a sandwich but completely worth it. I was never hungry after eating and always satisfied. I cannot say enough good things about Zoya's and the people who work there!

text: Awesome place! I go there every Sunday for the half-price specials. I confess this place may land me in debt, but it's so hard to keep away. Totally yuppy, but I guess that's me. I'm awful at names, but now I'm finally remembering some of the staff: Brendan, Chris, Danielle with the cute tongue stud and overbite, Staci (never met a more cheerful person, even when talking to extra picky customers). Anyway, go and talk to them; they know everything about wine, beer and cheese.

text: My wife and I ate here for breakfast this morning and I have to say we were pretty disappointed. Both of us live in Reno but haven't been to the Coffee Shop in quite a while. Unfortunately the prices have gone up and the quality of food has gone down. Perhaps the Peppermill is trying to offset the cost of their enormous remodeling project, which by the way is very nice, but its too bad that the food quality suffered. I do have to say that the service was great. There are so many other coffee shops and breakfast joints in town that have better food, for the same price or cheaper.

text: GREAT NEWS FOR THOSE LOOKING FOR A SUNDAY BRUNCH! Le Castagne (a fabulous lunch and dinner place) has just started serving Sunday brunch. I had a divine crabmeat and asparagus omelet with yummy home fries . The pastries and breads were delicious. Anyway, I've long complained that Center City does not have enough Sunday brunch restaurants, so this is a very welcome addition. It's somehow classy but comfortable at the same time. Great service too.

text: The only reason I give this place 2 stars is that I think it's trying to be something that it's not - in other words, it attempts to be a trendy posh Asian eatery, but the dining experience more closely resembles eating in a giant overly decorated warehouse. The food is NOT authentic, that's for sure. In fact, it's more like Asian fusion, only that it's not particularly good at any of the types of Asian food they try to create, be it Korean, Chinese, Thai, or anything else. BUT, for people who can't tell and/or don't care about the authenticity of their ethnic food, this place is pretty good. Food is not overly greasy, seasoning is flavorful, and the presentation is visually pleasing. Generally, I've found that people who know nothing about real Asian food love this place....food purists and authenticity snobs (like me) trash it.
label: NEG

text: I'm leaving this four stars, but barely. I'm leaning towards three. We arrived on a Tuesday evening when we were literally two of six people in the entire restaurant other than the staff. Perfect to accompany a drink. I wonder how successful this will be on a really busy night, as it seemed like a project even on this slow evening to keep it fresh, made properly, and in front of the guests. The Bahn Mi is as good as everyone says it is. Go on 3/5/2010 for lunch and get your free one. My guest didn't like it that much and said he has found better, and fuller, sandwiches in chinatown, but I haven't so this is one of two dishes we had that saved the four star rating in my book. I would have eaten this entire thing myself. Charred Octopus was disappointing. It was a large portion, it was very tender, it was even well seasoned and presented, but there was NO char. If it was 'octopus salad' it would have been perfect, but we really wanted to taste a touch of acrid char against that delicious tender octopus. With the Chef in the back, no excuse on this one. The Wonton Taco was the other smash dish that saved the four stars for me. The SUPER crispy airy wonton filled with the perfect blend of shrimp and seasoning was top notch. This dish was so good I could have eaten another portion right away. Five stars on this dish. The suzuki shashimi was tasty, with good size portions of fish, a nice portion of pommelo (a citrus similar to pink grapefruit) and tapioca pearls with various seasonings. It was, however, a pain in the ass to eat. Chopsticks were useless as the citrus was too delicate and tapioca pearls scattered like, well, pearls. Trying to stab it with a fork resulted in similar self-destruction. In the end the only successful way to get this food in your mouth the way it was presented was to quickly scoop the portion up and stuff it in. This may, or may not, score you points with your date... The lobster sashimi was more garlic tomato salad than lobster sashimi. My guest was annoyed, as the overpowering garlic and seasoning in the pile of tomato salad that covered the lobster pretty much occluded the sweet taste of most of the meat. I agree, and would not order this dish again. The ice cream flavors of the evening were kit-kat and burnt marshmallow. Apparently whoever was in charge of charring and burning things didn't make it in that evening, as my burnt marshmallow tasted like vanilla soft serve, and that was it. I did get the kit-kat in the chocolate offering. These cones are fun, and I'd order them again happily regardless of the flavors. As I wrote this it hit me the inconsistency in the intensity of flavors dish to dish. I've mentioned before how I felt the truffle taste in the edamame dumplings is weak, which echoes the burnt-marshmallow in the cone, yet we are uber-garlicked on the lobster sashimi. The espresso at the end of the meal had that same intensity disconnect. It was very good, and we both LOVE strong espresso, and this was so strong that we were remarking that we could still taste it walking back to my car. It completely cleared away any flavor afterthoughts of the ice creams. So I'm still telling you to go. Try the Bahn MI, absolutely try the wontons, get the ice cream, and yes, get the espresso. Beyond that, you're hit or miss.

text: This is the first gallery I've seen in Edmonton that sells fine First Nations art (maybe the only one?). It's an authentic art gallery, so you won't find items like tacky dreamcatchers and mini-totem poles as you would at stereotypical tourist shops. The Bearclaw Gallery has the real stuff, some of which rivals the fine art in BC, where there is a huge Aboriginal art market. Since coming back from Vancouver, I hadn't seen any soapstone carvings until today when I stumbled upon the Bearclaw. (Soapstone is basically a rock material used in art carving, and typically has green to brown hues depending on its mineral content; it's very common among Inuit art.) They carry quality art by Aboriginal and Inuit artists, including paintings, silkscreen prints, sculptures, and soapstone and antler-bone carvings. I was surprised to see a strong Northwest Coast influence here; there are lots of wooden carved masks. They even have authentic hand-carved silver jewelry here! (If you've never seen one of these, you have to visit the gallery to at least look at them; they're unlike any jewelry you've ever seen before, and that's an understatement.) The prairies First Nations art tended to be more dominant in the paintings and prints. Famous artists include Norval Morriseau and Daphne Odjig. They have smaller items too, like beautifully beaded jewelry and accessories, moccasins, and dreamcatchers. These dreamcatchers are unlike any you've seen though; they're huge and authentic, not mass-produced somewhere in China. Although there's not quite a market for Aboriginal art here in Edmonton yet, I think it's great that the Bearclaw Gallery is here. If you're an avid art collector, this place is a must-see.

text: Over the past three years of living in the neighborhood, my biggest complaint was that Cherokee went dead by 8pm. And while I don't mind a walk up to South Grand to hit up a bar, I wanted something closer, more chill, and less smoky. And here we have Foam. Not only does it fill some of the huge nightlife gap (although between here and Off Broadway, I feel pretty well covered on the no-smoking Cherokee area venues), but it also opens at 7am for the workday crowd. It's a great work environment, for when I need to get out of the house for studying, and it's a great place to run into friends and neighbors. It's even the place I've been looking for to have a beer and do some knitting! It's sounds goofy, but the lighting is just right for crafting at night. The design of the space is fantastic, understated and stylish. It's striking, but it doesn't wallop you over the head with kitch. Aside from all that, they make a fantastic chai (homemade, and not sticky sweet), the coffee is strong and good, the beer selection is wonderful, and the food is well-done. My only complaint with the food is that it is pricey, but it's of high quality and either house-made or procured from local producers (like the Companion Pretzels, for instance). Now that they've started having more bands play, I can see Foam turning into the place to be on the weekends, and this can only be a good thing for us all. It's a flexible, evolving space, and exactly what every neighborhood needs.

text: I love this place. Not only do they have a huge array of desert plants, including many that are native to SE Arizona, Pima County, and even Tucson specifically, but there were a good range of sizes and prices as well. The gallon-size plants start at 6 or 8 bucks but the prices can go quite a bit higher as the green things get bigger. There's a cactus and succulents section, and the rest of the grasses, shrubs, and trees are laid out in tidy rows with identifying signs. The staff is friendly and helpful, but they're also happy to leave you alone to wander around sniffing, poking, and reading about the plants. Their web site (www.desertsurvivors.org) is very good, too; they have an awesome downloadable guide to all the plants they sell with information about where they're from, what conditions they're suited for, and the kinds of critters they attract, if any. The plants looked like they are doing well; remembering of course that desert plants tend to look rather scraggly and unassuming while they're getting started. I did once go for a creosote bush but left empty-handed, but this was just because they only had the larger $20 plants and I was looking for the cheap little ones. To be fair, though, they had just had one of their big, much-attended plant sales and I think that wiped out some of their inventory. At any rate, a helpful staffer showed me a whole section of wee creosote bushes, just waiting to get big enough for sale, in the "Employees Only" area. My only warning is that, if you choose a plant based on the information on the sign by the plant, be sure that the abbreviation of the plant's latin name (written on the side of each pot) matches the name of the plant on the sign--sometimes plants are not put back in the right place and it's easy enough to grab the wrong one if you're not careful. Adding to my enthusiasm for Desert Survivors is that it not only provides all of these great (mostly native) plants that thrive here without requiring an obscene waste of water, it is also a non-profit that serves both adults and children with disabilities. How cool is that?!

text: Culinaria - A Sham! Dear Wilmingtonians, Your beloved Culinaria is a Sham! You have been fooled all these years - overpaying for meals you should be making at home or just not eating. Asparagus wrapped in prosciutto with walnuts is a no-brainer and not worth the $8.50 + tip you pay for it but you are willing to eat it in a dirty strip mall restaurant decorated with fake plants and faux art. What are you thinking; you deserve better! You are not pushing yourselves to explore food and wine at this place and are becoming complacent. Is that what you want!? Wake up! You are ranking this restaurant in Zagat on the same level as the Green Room, Krazy Kat's, 821, and Moro; four restaurants with trained chefs and menus that could compete against some of the top restaurants in the country. Move on people! Culinaria is Betty Crocker making one of her recipes after a couple of drinks from the bottle; stepping out of her safe and traditional meals by dusting her broccoli rabe with parmesan cheese! Folks, this is not "inventive" or "cosmopolitan"; this is what the rest of the world has been doing with their broccoli rabe for hundreds of years! It's a hoax! Don't let the Zagat review fool you into believing you are doing anything out of the norm; this is the norm for most people on the planet! The restaurant is the McDonald's of upscale dining. Patron walks in, is seated, cocktail order taken, dinner order taken, cocktail served, apps served, then dinner, dessert and coffee, patrons mull about while digesting, then leave is probably what the manual reads. Whatever you do as a guest at Culinaria, don't attempt to break the programmatic order (try it! I dare you!) of your evening or you shall be lashed by your server or one of the chef owners. Even worse, ordering something different than it appears on the menu is an impossibility; you may be kicked out of the restaurant! Life is too short! Wake up and smell the coffee people; do you like being taken advantage of? Boil down the facts: the food is simple with a few cheap twists that trick you into feeling comfortable paying $6.75 for broccoli rabe. The décor is nice to the eye at first blush but upon close inspection it is all fake. The service is programmatic and the chef-owners can't adjust what they make because they don't know how to work off their program. What does this leave you - well, where you started, in dirty strip mall with your initial impression of "why am I eating here, again?" Sincerely, Finding da Sham P.S. The owners don't like kids (no high-chairs available) so don't even think about bringing the little-ones.....

I arrived 20 minutes early to my appt, and only one client was there. meanwhile there was about 3 staff members there, two of which were doing nothing. one of them told me to have a seat, after i came in and said i had a 430 appointment. i was ignored until 435, when i got up and asked a different girl who i hadnt seen when ifirst came in when i was going to be seen, b/c in the meanwhile i had seen two more staff arrive, yet only one more customer had come in. also, right at the time a walk- in came in and a staff member took them to get a wax done. so my scheduled appointment was now bumped to wait for the one waxing girl to get finished with that walk-in customer. after waiting 25 more minutes, that walk-in customer finally emerged from their wax. while waiting, i was asked by a male staff member i it was okay if he did my wax. maybe its just me, but im not accustomed to men doing brazilian waxes on me. i was finally taken in to a room that had a table facing right towards the door that didnt lock (i was really hoping not to get walked in on b/c i was provided with no towel or cover whatsoever). the girl doing about to do the wax had no gloves on the entire time. she also told me she may run out of wax and that maybe i could come back tomorrow if she couldnt finish??? i declined and just said to get whatever she could. the wax was painful, very long, and left me bruised. i understand these are not without pain but compared to my other waxes this was over the top. then, onto threading. apparently this same girl does the threading so thats why no one could at least get that out of the way while i was waiting for the wax. they first appeared okay after she did them, but on further inspection at home, i could tell they were very hastily done. many stray hairs were left behind, and i wasnt impressed at all by them overall. i did receive a discount for the many mishaps that occured during this visit, but it doesnt matter. i will not return.

text: I can't really describe this place besides "cool". The upstairs has lots of cool art and a fun atmosphere. I met the owner - great guy. Awesome edition to the Central West End.

text: I love Southwark. Their drinks are incredible, the staff is super nice and you couldnt' ask for a better environment. Although I am not a fan of going there on a weekend night (heck, I'm not going out anywhere on a weekend night between 8-12am, too many people by the bar), they're great to stop in for a drink around 5pm and for dessert too! I've taken my parents, my friends and my work friends here-it's a perfect place indeed.

text: This place reminds me of Long John Silvers, but less greasy. The food is pretty good, I also like that you can substitute the fries with a vegetable. They also give you good portions of food, compared to Long Johns. The service is sometimes slow, but it's worth the wait. The staff does a good job at keeping the place clean, too.
label: POS

text: Went here on a Saturday morning for breakfast. Seems to be popular with the neighborhood folks. The kitchen is really good, the portions are large and the food scrumptious. We had a pumpkin pancake with walnuts and a ham and mushroom omelet. Both dishes were great. The coffee is weak, tasteless and watered down, so if you're after a nice cup of java in the morning, this is not the place for you unfortunately. This alone ruins it for me no matter how good the food itself may be, I'm giving it two stars because our waitress was rude, hurried and stressed out, which coupled with substandard coffee made for a very unpleasant experience despite the food being really good.

text: I went to the 12th Street Diner with my dad, boyfriend and our foreign exchange student who is from Japan. The diner was pretty crowded because there was a Rams game about to begin! It was speedy & tasty! I ordered the Viva Las Vegas Omelet with egg whites and wheat toast. My dad had the biscuits and gravy, my boyfriend had pancakes, eggs and bacon and our friend Dyo had the Slinger- he was in heaven! The Slinger was huge, however very good and somehow it was demolished. My omelet was good- not too much cheese (just the way I like it). The diner was definitely a good experience, great location, and quick service!

text: Came here for a geocaching event this weekend. There were 4 , yes, I counted FOUR greeters at the door who were friendly and took us right to the back room where we were holding our event. I had not found a seat yet, when a waitress took my order. I found a seat and she spotted me right away. Since it was an event, I was mingling all over the place but the waitress always found me. We went to the outside deck for a group picture taking by one of the waitstaff. They even let us write on their special's board! We had a great time here! Too bad I didn't get a chance to eat but the drinks and service was great. My only problem with Kildares was that the bathroom was very dirty! An very jolly Irishman, gave us a "God Bless" before walking out the door. Would come back here again!

text: On May 28th, 2005 we were married. It was beautiful. Eight days later we ate our first Port of Call burger. It was beautiful. text: Burger FAIL. After reading all the reviews, my wife and I were highly anticipating eating here, but the whole event turned out to be fairly disappointing and flaccid. The Good: We were seated almost immediately, even though we were told we'd have to wait 20 minutes. The crab cake (Notice: ONE cake) was delicious! It reminded me of my first crab cake experience in Maryland. The Bad: I ordered the Woodstock medium RARE. After 20 minutes, I was still sans burger. From my experience, organic beef should need about 1/3 less time to cook since there is less fat and more protein. The waitress said my patty was not to the chef's approval, and I was appreciative of the attention to quality, but what came out for me was a well done burger. Not cool. I notified our waitress, and the kitchen rushed a new order to me in less than 5 minutes??? This second attempt (Third, if you count the first burger fail) was no better. The patty was HALF the size of the previous one, and it tasted medium well to me. The bacon was not crisp, but more like cured ham - salty and chewy. And with the size of the patty, the bread dominated the whole taste. I asked the waitress what was up with overcooking the meat, and she proceeded to lecture me loudly enough for others to hear that I don't know what organic beef should look and taste like. Umm... ok. I truly wanted to Sally Field this place. (Like it... Really really like it.) But it was not the experience I had hoped.

text: Even though I feel some vague undercurrent of guilt for frequenting a place owned by McDonald's, I cannot get enough of Chipotle. For two long years I went to Baja Fresh and suffered a dubiously mixed bag of quality and the omnipresent Mexibloat. I had an epiphany after the first visit to Chipotle: it was the end of Mexibloat. I could taste and see each of the individual ingredients in the burrito that I customized, every flavor distinct, fresh and punchy. And some KILLER guac. When I was still eating chicken, it was reliably super juicy and nicely grilled and seasoned. I've since started getting a veggie bowl without the dairy additions and I have never been dissatisfied with the freshness or the portions - they have even adjusted proportions of (more) beans to (less) rice when I ask. I shudder to use the word healthy in association with a fast food restaurant in any way associated with McDs but they really do make an effort and I never feel guilty about a meal here, especially since it is kind to the wallet as well.

text: Because I have a grand total of something like 700,000 Priority Club points over the course of a decade or so, I tend to stay in Crowne Plazas (and Intercontinentals, if I want to splurge) a lot when I vacation. Something to do with the fact that I get free nights with my reward points. That allows me to compare service between many hotels of this chain. This one has a lot to improve. We stayed for one night while visiting Sesame Place with the kids. We roll in our family sedan in front of the hotel and start unloading the MANY bags, the stroller, diaper bags, kids clothes. It takes forever. Nobody came over to ask if we were in need of help with the luggage (we were, big time). So we go and get one of those luggage carts from inside. Still nobody asked if they could help us. We load the cart, and get to the reception to check-in. And yet again, nobody asks us if we need help with the luggage. I asked, and we start waiting. Nobody comes, so we roll the cart upstairs on our own. Annoying, but not the end of the world. Pretty much guaranteed to start our stay the wrong way, though. The hotel itself is pretty typical side-of-the-highway, in the middle of nowhere type of a place. A little rundown, needs new paint, smells of old hotels, you know the deal. Rooms were fine, little small, but just fine for a one night stay. Now, I don't know what the hell was going on around the area, but that hotel appeared to be party central on the night we stayed. We were wakened several times by drunks running, laughing, arguing and whatever the hell else on the halls outside of our room. That happens, I suppose, but this hotel is advertised as one of the hotels partnering with Sesame Place, so I'm expecting some sort of family friendly athmosphere. Thankfully the kids didn't wake up, but my wife and I did, and we were exhausted in the morning. Oh, and when we turned on the heater in the morning, it set the smoke alarm on. Yay. I would've asked for a refund, if I actually had paid anything. Worst hotel stay ever. Two stars only, because the drunks weren't hotel employees.

text: I had Amica insurance for several years up until now. They scored very high in ratings from a consumer magazine. I never had problems with them until now. I recently moved from Texas to Florida. I had bought a used car in Texas and then drove it here to Florida. When I transferred insurance to the new car and state, Amica told me I needed to have an inspection done within 10 days. That is the limit of the Florida state laws. But when I got busy and it was getting towards the end of the 10 days, Amica kindly called me to let me know I needed to have the inspection done asap. That was fine. The dealer I had bought the used car from in Texas lost the title so I was never able to register the car in Florida. Since the dealer in Texas also has locations in Florida, I got them to take back the car without the title and I bought a different used car from them instead. I called Amica to get the insurance transferred to the new car. However, this time when the 10 days to get the car inspected was running out, I never heard from Amica. Instead I got the car inspected. But two days after that I got a letter from Amica that they had already cancelled my collision coverage. Amica sent out the letter the day AFTER they cancelled my insurance. No warning whatsoever. Amica never called me before the cancelled my insurance. I didn't even know I now have no insurance until I got this cold, informal letter from their computer. Amica may be following the laws concerning the inspection if I did go over the 10 days. But I expect an auto insurance company to provide some level of customer service. They expect me to pay a hefty premium, but they now seem to offer no customer service whatsoever. They don't want my business anymore, after about 8-10 years of paying premiums without any claims. So I will find a different insurance company that does have decent customer service. How the mighty have fallen. Amica used to be a great company. But I can no longer recommend Amica as a car insurance company worth considering.
label: NEG

text: Concealed pretty well down a small alley a block from the County Theater Bobby Simones is well worth the search. The restaurant is fairly small and very comfortable and offers a terrific dinner menu and is also a great place to grab lunch or just drinks. Its located only a block and a half south of the court house in Doylestown. You cant go wrong with any of the meat selections, Bobby's does an exceptional job of finding the best meat in the region and I have never eaten a piece that wasnt cooked to perfection. A great dining experience for me is a combination of great food, atmosphere, service and attention to detail. There are plenty of places that do well in 2 or 3 of these areas but most fail to hit the mark on all 4. Bobby's attention of detail is incredible. Here's an example: while having lunch there one day I ordered a Chicken Caesar salad, I happen to like anchovies, many don't. Bobby took pride in telling me that he only serves white anchovies and explaining to me the difference they make. He was right; anyone can make a decent Chicken Caesar, but these really changed the flavor of the salad and made it an experience. There is a private room in the back that they are happy to set up for you if you want to host a party that is quieter than the main part of the restaurant and is just the place for a business or family dinner for 10 or less. Adding Mike Conti to oversee the restaurant has only taken this place up. Mike is the consummate professional and you are pretty much guaranteed a special time when you go. There is seating outside in the summer months and a bar across the alley that are also part of Bobby's but each area seems to offer something different and stands well on its own. If Bobby is there you will know, he is like an old time restaurateur who takes real pride in meeting you personally and making sure that your expectations are surpassed. If not, they will be immediately. Pride goes along way to making this spot one to put on your list of "must go's"
label: POS

text: I went to a conference in Tampa in February for about a week. When we talked in, I really liked the decor. There were buddhas and temples and neat little things to look at while we waited for our table. We ordered chicken pad Thai, tom yum soup and chicken cashew. Everything was delicious! The next night, the group we were with wanted Thai food, so we had dinner there again. The tom yum was so delicious that we ordered it again. This time, I decided to have the pad see ew. Overall, the food was great. The service was okay (everyone at the conference bombarded the restaurant during dinner time, so it was kind of slow). But I would def. have dinner here again when I'm in Tampa.

text: Eh, this place doesn't really do it for me. I thought the same thing years ago when I tried selling some stuff at their Greenwood location and, like Mia M. was disappointed with what they offered me. text: First, let me note that this is not at all a fancy place. If you are looking for a place for an occasion, I don't think this is the best place. Having said that, Korea House is a fairly authentic Korean restaurant in very workmanlike manner, complete with Korean-language television in the corner. It looks and feels like a place where office workers in, say, LA Koreatown might stop for workaday lunch--and the fare is similar to them in price and quality. Perhaps not "great" food, but it's the more "typical" Korean food done in reasonably familiar manner...and this is the only "real" Korean restaurant in this town. (Takamatsu further east is a bit fancier--but the Korean fare there actually smells and tastes distinctly non-Korean.) Would I give four stars if there were any alternative? Probably not...but you can't judge what you don't have.

text: Work time lunch place, always packed from 11 am to 2pm weekdays. Proximity, size and location surely dictates why the suits are always populating this chain place. It sure can't be for the outstanding food or the kitchen that works at a glacial pace. Like anyone who works in this area of the city, Corner Bakery, like Cosi, is a lazy no-brainer option to grab lunch if you've got the tenacity to wait 10-20 minutes for a to-go order. I try not to make a habit of it so I go there once or twice a month. Soups and salads are the way to go, just make sure they do the dressing on the side as they like to drown 'em. Also, don't expect that you're doing some healthy eatin' either, a quick inspection of the nutrition information makes you go into instant cardiac arrest. The question that I always ask myself is that why does the food come quicker when you're eating-in? Doesn't an "order to-go" receive priority? If you're just plating pre-made salads shouldn't it take a couple minutes tops? Also, and more importantly, why do I keep coming back here? AND... If a tree falls in the woods and no one's there to hear it does it make a sound?

text: Stopped here for breakfast this morning on our way to SoCal. The s/o and I both ordered their "Dungeness Crab Cake & Potato Hash w/Avocado Salsa, Poached Eggs & Lemon Butter Sauce" as I'm a big fool for crab cakes and it sounded like the best thing on the menu! When it came out, it was served on a bowl and the food was piled on. First layer - Potato Hash, Second layer - Avocado Salsa, Third layer - Crab Cake, Fourth layer - Poached Egg, Fifth layer - Lemon Butter Sauce and Sixth and final layer - Parsley. The first few bites were good but after awhile, the flavors started conflicting with each other, most especially the lemon with the potatoes. The crab cake was okay, the outside was crunch but the crab meat was a little salty and tasted too fishy. At $17.00 each, I knew I shoudl've ordered their "Wild Mushroom, Asparagus, Black Truffle Cheese Scramble w/ Field Green Salad." Service was okay. Our server seemed didn't seemed to enthusiastic to be there. The only time we saw her was when she took our order, checked in on us after we got our food and towards the end, before I even finished my meal, covertly handed the check. Not to mention, a couple that got seated in her section right after we got seated. They were seated for a good 10-minutes without being acknowledged and they just walked out. Not good! Major props go out to their busboy/runner who actually refilled our bevs, brought our food out, cleaning tables, setting tables, etc. He seemed like the only one that was actually busting his ass in that dining room.
label: NEG

text: Mind you, I know people that love J B Dawson's, I just don't happen to be one of them. When they first opened the food was better, it has gone downhill. For instance, I used to love their baked potato soup, now it tastes like they lost the salt shaker in it. Ribs are okay, not the best I've had, but they are good. Prices are too high, when you can get the same thing, of the same quality, elsewhere, for less. Like their filet, 9 oz. for $22.95. and it is nothing spectacular. If you are so hungry for a good steak, go to your favorite steak house because you are not going to get it here. I must say that I love their fries, when they come out hot and fresh. They are crispy shoestrings and almost like eating a meaty potato chip. They have a very large bar & lounge area, which has quite a few obvious regulars popping in. The restaurant is dimly lit and attractive..

text: You definitely have to be in the right mood to go boutique shopping and after a stressful day today I was in need of retail therapy. Even though I don't always find things I like...somehow my friend and I always find ourselves back here, hoping we will find something we like. The pricing is reasonable but not always worth it. Some things are in the $30 range and others up to $100. Some of the quality of the pieces are worth the price and others not so much. It's a "hit or miss" store but when you get "hit" it's well worth it :) It's the kind of place where you just have to try stuff on. Some of the pieces are straight from the designers it seems, rather than nation-wide/world-wide brands that mass produce therefore some pieces hug or are loose in places you wouldn't expect. I do like how the racks of clothing are organized by color it makes it a lot easier to shop. For example, I CANNOT pull off yellow with my skin tone and I could just skip that rack instead of sift through a rack of mismatch shades. Con: You won't always have a successful visit. Lately, I have many visits where I come out with nothing. I sift through every rack and many things are either tacky, not good quality, overly embellished, or too pricey for the piece. I really liked this boutique last summer but slowly my opinion of the place is dropping. What they have: most of the clothing is dresses, some tops, and few bottoms. There's also a wall dedicated to shoes and a little display of jewelry by the cash wrap.
label: NEG

text: Best Thai food in Indy. The owner is cool and the food is delicious. The pizza parlor-like table cloths and crowded tables give this place an urban charm. I echo the sentiments about the TV--it doesn't need to be there. But, it doesn't make the food taste any worse. Try the green curry, the drunken noodles and the tofu soup! And the old standard Pad Thai is a never-fail pleaser. I've gotten some of the pickiest eaters to like Thai from trying this place. As for people who've gotten bad service--I hope and assume these are fairly isolated incidents, and can happen anywhere. Some people are just not meant to wait tables, and will eventually get what's coming to them. I try not to base my entire opinion of a place just based on a server, and one experience. My .02.
