text: Went into Muriel's on a whim for lunch and it turned out to be their sunday jazz brunch. The restaurants atmosphere was nice, the live jazz was a nice experience for brunch. That was about all I enjoyed about Muriel's. Started off with a mushroom soup which was good but nothing spectacular. Then came the entrees, shrimp creole omlette and pickled pork hash. I wasn't impressed with the omlette, it was interesting though. I ordered the pork hash which came with two eggs over easy. First, one of the eggs wasn't over easy, it was cooked all the way through. I would think a fancy restaurant like Muriels could handle cooking an egg correctly. It doesn't end there though, my hash came with pork, potatoes, and other vegetables, and the potatoes were awful!!! Absolutely awful. It was a potatoes with all the good potato-ness cooked out. They were chewy and completely flavorless. Muriel's was a complete let down. I wish the ambiance matched the food but not even the nice settings and live jazz can bring rating up for this disappointing restaurant.
label: NEG

text: I have to say that Oishi is highly overrated. This Newtown crowd is eager to throw money for mediocre Korean food. The sushi was not bad but definitely not worth its price. I've been here for both lunch and dinner. Service was slow, but it was busy for lunch. That's no excuse for not refilling our waters though. The bento boxes will definitely fill you up; they give you a lot of sides. But the beef bulgogi is something you should order elsewhere. It's BYOB so thats the big plus.
label: NEG

text: The rooms are comfortable but outdated. My biggest complaint is with the very slow service at the front desk (in town for a big convention, so perhaps they weren't prepared for the rush?).
label: NEG

text: I've eaten here a few times, and if it weren't for my most recent experience they would be getting 4 stars. I LOVE their fish tacos. They are the best breaded fish taco I've had. However, the last time we were there we received the absoluteworst service. To start with, our server was very, how should I say it, scattered? He would leave in the middle of taking orders, and was never really there when we needed something. They were a little busy, so I can normally excuse that to some extent. However, my order was messed up. I ordered the fish tacos with no beans, extra rice. I get my plate and there are beans. Ok, no big deal, I just wont eat them. Then I look inside my tacos and it is ground beef. I had to wait 10 minutes for our server to return to let him know this was not what I ordered. He did apologize, then took my plate away and went to the kitchen to have my correct meal made. I am now left sitting there with nothign to eat while the other 3 people in our party have their food. I told them to eat so they would not have cold food. 30 minutes later, I finally received my food. Unfortunately, everyone else was already finished. We immediately asked for our bill and I scarfed down my tacos as fast as I could. I finished my meal and we had to wait another 10 mintues afterwards to get our check! Not that I expect free food, but I could not even believe we were not offered anything. Free dessert, my meal taken off, something. Needless to say we will not be returning.
label: NEG

text: This place got the trifecta - poor service, poor food, and long waits. Not enough wait staff the night we were there - and the staff was young and inexperienced. The bartender for instance was waiting on three tables himself while attempting to tend to a very busy bar. The food was bad even considering this is really a tavern. Gumbo with beef in it and no seafood? Also if you're a vegetarian - forget it - they have one vegetarian friendly offering. The one thing that saves this place is their beer selection. About the best beer selection you can find. My recommendation - go to pick up beer, but do dinner elsewhere.
label: NEG

text: I'm not a vegan. Hell, I am not even a vegetarian. But I am a wannabe foodie... The Yelp reviews for this place were stellar so I suggested a dinner party here for Erin G.'s 40th bithday bash. We had about 8 people and we pretty much covered the main course and app. menu. EVERYTHING was delicious. Everything was filled to the brim with flavor and the portions were awesome. I had a bite of everything and all of it was great. The BBQ Jerk seitan was so damn close to pork I thought they were lying. My main course was the pacific brim tofu and it too was damn near perfect. This is a perfect date restaurant guys. Its classy, they offer some great stiff drinks, and there isn't a bad thing on the menu. Go. p.s. Erin G. isn't really 40.
label: POS

text: We are from Northern California and it was so easy to plan with Sarah. We got married at the Santa Barbara County Courthouse and used Montecito Weddings for the entire thing-from flowers, chair setup, officiant, photography, even a violinist! It was definitely a great value for the price.
label: POS

text: DONT COME HERE! So our group initially wanted to hit up one of the mom & pop diners along South Virginia, but the wait was horrendous for a group for 19. We slowly piled back towards our cars - decided to give Yama Sushi a try. It was definitely a BIG DISAPPOINTMENT. We walk in and there's absolutely no business, its prime time for lunch. Some of us order the ALL-YOU-CAN-EAT sushi - which can decently fill you up. However for those who ordered A LA CARTE, the prices of our food came up to near the same price. If you have no choice, stick to the ALL-YOU-CAN-EAT cuz at least it'll fill you up and you get a variety of sushi rolls. I ordered the Beef Teriyaki and California Roll. Beef Teriyaki - beef was either frozen/old + overcooked, super dry, not made for humans to consume. California Roll - the imitation crab was the stick you buy at the frozen aisle, this was literally something i can make myself . They were also very short staffed for our group of 19, and the portion of our group that got ALL-YOU-CAN-EAT received better service than the A-LA-CARTE table. I bet that we were the biggest business/clients of the day.
label: NEG

text: Adesso is an intimate venue, similar to Denim, but with better ventilation. Smoking didn't seem to be permitted, a plus for me. Decent music and sound system. Their VIP floor is decent, offering a view of the dance floor. Besides a bit of club lighting by the windows, there's red highlights around couches in the back. The bar staff seem to be inept - hopefully that's been fixed? Took forever for anyone to get drinks - probably about ten minutes between drinks. The bar was busy but didn't seem understaffed, yet I felt neglected; I waited so long that a guy next to me bought ME a shot. (No joke. I returned the favor twenty minutes later.) When I got a bartender's attention, I asked for shots with pineapple. He said they didn't have anything that went well with it. (Possible.) I asked for red headed sluts. Got a blank look. (Really?) Finally settled for Washington apple shots, after noticing a patron ordering those after going through an irksome exchange. They were weak and pricey.
label: NEG

text: Go for the entertainment, not the food! You will wait for at least an hour for horrible service and sub par food....if they haven't run out of what you ordered.
label: NEG

text: One of my favorite center city bars, the food is delicious, they have sweet potato fries and a great fries dipping sauce but I have to say my favorite thing to eat there is their chicken cordon bleu chicken tenders! yum.The food comes out quick too! Everyone that works there have always been great, very friendly. I love their third floor, where they have a pool table, darts and video games and bathrooms. It's a great place to hang out. Good drink selection and they have bars on both the first and second floors. Whenever someone asks me to recommend a bar to go to when I'm working at drinker's, I send them to good dog. I think the only complaint I have is that their booths on the first floor are uncomfortable.
label: POS

text: Salad Works is a good national chain known for freshness and good salads (hence the name). This location isn't very different then any other saladworks but that shouldn't defer you from going here because it is still a terrific place to eat. The salads are rather large and definitely enough for a large male (me!) and they always give you a fresh roll which is delish. They do a pretty good job of keeping this place up and neat, and the staff are pretty friendly. I've had no problems with this place and would definitely recommend eating here. The two things i have problems with are that they do not have any menu boards, only paper menus which i think is stupid. I mean comon, i wanna look at a menu board not a piece of paper to choose my salad. And the second thing is the price. It is almost 10 for a salad (after tax) and that is pretty expensive, i mean for lettuice, and whatever else that prob costs them 3 dollars to make? WOOF, what an increase. But none the less it is still good and will come back. The soups are actually pretty good too!
label: POS

text: I love Tarantino. True Romance and Pulp Fiction are two of my favorite flicks, EVER. So imagine how satisfying it was for me to come to The Royale, order their signature Kobe burger, and get to utter: 'I'll have the Royale with cheese.' YES! Uh, no. They were out of their aptly named 'Royale' on this sad Tuesday afternoon. Frown. Okay, so what's a burger lovin', hunger-driven girl to do? She orders the next best thing: the Kingshighway. This domestic Angus burger was cooked perfectly to medium, juices intact with housemade sweet potato chips on the side. Plenty of toppings to choose from, including roasted red peppers, feta, artichoke hearts, and my choice, a generous dollop of goat cheese. Deeeelicious. My only regret is not ordering off the drink menu. The Royale might serve up some of the best crafted cocktails (based on friends' opinions and the menu offering) I've come across in St. Louis. Think champagne with fresh-squeezed (for reals) pear juice. Or the 'Ville': Bombay Sapphire, fresh lemon juice, sugar, dash of vanilla, club soda. Simple but ohsofreakinggood. Impressive draught beer and bottle list, too (though you won't find A-B products much to my old man's dismay). Everything here is just... interesting. As in wonderfully. The music, the decor, the food, the people. Voilà: my new StL hangout. Street parking only kids, so it can get tricky.
label: POS

text: For those of you who have ever been on a cruise ship before, you will recognize this food. Actually, cruise ship food might even be a tad better than this goulash. And I'm not an overly picky eater or food snob. I went with the all-day bracelet, which gives you access to at least 3 meals for a 24 hr. period. I figured this was a pretty good deal for $20+ tax. However, most of the hot foods for all meals--with the possible exception of the fried chicken--was pretty unappetizing. The fresh fruit counter looked recycled throughout the day. I was pretty surprised, as I've always thought Eldorado was a step above places like Silver Legacy & Circus Circus by comparison. Cost-cutting moves look to have devastated The Buffet at the El-Do.
label: NEG

text: "Punk's not dead, punk's noooot dead" at Tattooed Moms. Great place to get pissed... I can't speak for the food, although I've had the veggie wings (pierogies) over at Sugarmom's and those are always good. I usually go upstairs when i'm there, just because I love all the punk nostalgia plastered all over the walls. It's a fun place to start or end your night... the beer is cheap enough, and it seems the bar food selection is decent. If you're into gritty bars, and appreciate the legacy of the punk scene, you must experience Tattooed Mom's.
label: POS

text: Horrible. Horrible food, horrible service. It all started by ordering juice which ran out and only filled 3/4 of my cup. I went outside and waited over 30 minutes for a sub par scramble and wrap. I saw people who came minutes after me get their order 20 minutes before mine finally came out. Complete bullcrap. Maybe I caught them on a bad day but I hope they'll step it up and make some improvements.
label: NEG

text: This is yet another darling little boutique in the now-trendy Maplewood shopping and dining area. They have cute aprons and matching oven mitts, mongramed items and children's clothing. I'm not into monogramed stuff, but I know lots of people are, and this places is a treasure trove of goodies in this area.
label: POS

text: This really is a gorgeous little hostel. The common spaces in the main building (a converted mansion) are filled with the sort of furniture I wouldn't even entertain the idea of buying at an antique store - because there'd be no way I could afford it. I happened to be with someone who owns a car, a rarity for me, and under normal circumstances there is no way I'd be able to get to this place. But it is in the middle of the park, and oh so lush and green. The kitchen is huge and well stocked with cooking tools etc. I cooked quite a few huge dinners here - we had a big group and never felt like we were overwhelming or taking the place over. Our actual rooms were in the Carriage House, it was comfortable but a little drafty, and not nearly as pretty as the main house, y'know.... having previously housed either horses or cars I guess aesthetics weren't the main priority. There was a nice common space also available in the upstairs of the carriage house too - great for meetings and down time. Overall I'd definitely recommend it for groups - or folks who are craving a little more space, tranquility, and greenery than you'd find at the average hostel.
label: POS

text: I finally visited Tomo after planing to eat here for months. The Yelpers who reviewed it before me are correct. The sushi here is great. It tastes fresh and prices are slightly above average, but you get your money's worth. I ordered their Tomo Lunch Box, a bento box which comes with a miso soup, ginger salad, teriyaki chicken, rice, tempura veggies and shrimp, 4 pieces of a california roll, and 2 nigiri rolls of salmon and tuna. All of the food was great and they were generous with the portions. The service was on point and our server was quick to seat us, put our orders in, and handle the bill. The atmosphere was great as well with traditional music playing softly in the background and a well decorated restaurant with many Japanese inspirations to it. They also have Korean BBQ on the menu being Korean-owned. I'd definitely go visit Tomo again!
label: POS

text: This all started this a bid on Priceline. I wanted to get away with my wife for our anniversary and selected a resort in Tucson for $80 and won the Loews Vantana. The resort is beautifully place in the hills north of Tucson in the very upscale neighborhoods. The resort is a little older but for the price I was great with it. You will pay $9 for parking weather you park yourself or valet. Internet is $11 and cell service is sketchy at best around the resort. The first night we had the basic room and it was nice a clean. It was very noisy as all the rooms around us were full with families with kids. The bed was quit hard and we did have a problem with the shower head as the pipe was leaking and the ceiling was falling apart from water damage. The next morning my back was completely gone from the bed so I called the front desk and they upgraded the room to the top floor with a view. Unfortunately the bed was the same and by Sunday I was searching for a chiropractor. The shower was perfect and the tubs are huge! Big enough to hold 4 adults easily. We went to the spa on Saturday which was pricey and we ate at the restaurants every meal which are very overpriced but the food is good. Get the table side guacamole at the Flying V. Its worth it. After we came home I happened to look at my bill and found they had double billed me for the spa. Since both my wife and I spent a few hours there it happened to be very pricey and they automatically roll in 20% for gratuity. The problem is they ran my card twice! So far I have been calling the spa, customer service and accounting daily and we are going on a week without a response or getting my money back. If you call the spa they give your information to accounting. If you call customer service they give you information to accounting. If you call accounting all you get it a message line to leave your information. After a week of doing this I would just be happy for a call back. Overall if you are looking for somewhere to stay in Tucson, look for something else and save you back and the headaches.
label: NEG

text: My mom, my sister and I had an outing to Olive today to get our eyebrows done. I've only ever gotten mine waxed once before, so I don't have a huge frame of reference, but I have to say I really loved Olive. The woman who greeted us and then did my eyebrows was so nice and really knew what she was doing. Like another reviewer said, it doesn't have the chemical-y smell a lot of places have, which was great. I was oogling the amazing selection of nail polishes while I was waiting, and I'm pretty certain I'll be going back to get my nails done too!
label: POS

text: I took my friend who is visiting from Portland, OR and we are huge foodies! Anyways, her nachos were not so great. I had steak fajitas and my steak was mealy. I didn't know the steak could get mealy. Unfortunately the salsa wasn't great either...still on the search for the best Mexican food!
label: NEG

text: after an extraordinarily busy week at work a little while back, an email was sent out to the company: "lunch is on us today" (woo!) they ordered sandwich platters from vinnie's, and sent a separate email to yours truly assuring me that some would be veggie (aw, thanks!) while the gesture was certainly appreciated, this free lunch was total blah-ville. granted, the meat-eaters fared ok (tho i didn't hear any rave reviews from my co-workers), but as far as the veggie sandwich goes.... let's just say that shredded lettuce, a couple thin and pale tomato slices, a few canned black olive slices and some green peppers does not a sandwich make. i was able to add in some hot peppers that were included in containers on the side (as were sweet peppers and pickles)....but couldn't they have thrown in some cheese? i later looked at their menu and saw that they sell this "sandwich" for $3.65/kaiser, $5.25/hoagie. considering that the menu also lists all previously mentioned veggie items as free toppings, i wonder: are they charging for the roll here or what? for the most part, their prices are in line with tiny's (good), with about a third of their selection, and even less so for vegetarians.
label: NEG

text: I've dined at this restaurant twice and both times has an exceptional dining experience. 14 West is downtown and a good alternative to the other upscale restaurants in the area which are generally larger, louder, and more crowded. At 14 West, you have a more personal dining experience and the service is among the best I have ever received. The staff is knowledgable and courteous. The menu changes and I was a bit disappointed to see that the dry aged steaks on the menu last year have been taken off the menu, but there are alternatives for every palate on the menu - lamb, fish, shellfish, steak, chicken, duck, etc. During my recent visit, I enjoyed a very interesting salad with prociutto wrapped duck and warm shitake mushrooms and large scallops over a cream corn concoction as my entree. The food was excellent, but a bit rich, definitely an indulgence. The wine list is very comprehensive and features only the finest quality wines. Unfortunately, this restaurant does not offer many dessert wines, but the ruby port is excellent.
label: POS

text: My breakfast at the Worker Bee Cafe was very disappointing. Undercooked omelette (including patches of uncooked egg) and overcooked, over-salted homefries. Plus, the service was exceptionally slow. I went there on a cold, rainy weekday morning. I was in the mood for good, home-style "comfort food". I brought a good book to read and I was not in a hurry to get back out in the rain. There were very few other customers there, and all of them appeared to have been served by the time I arrived. I placed my order directly off the menu, without any changes or special requests. I began reading my book and waiting for my food to arrive. No new customers arrived, so I believe I was the only order the cook had to prepare. I waited. And waited. And waited... My plate finally arrived 30-40 minutes after placing the order. If the food had been exceptionally good, I would have quickly understood (and forgotten) the long wait. Good things take time. Unfortunately, the food was awful! Sorry, but I can't recommend a breakfast restaurant that can't properly prepare an omelette and homefries dish ordered straight off their menu. I left the Worker Bee Cafe wishing I had gone to Garden Market instead.
label: NEG

text: Part of my job is to throw events, and I enjoy this part very much. What I don't necessarily enjoy is the stress that comes with planning these parties, but thankfully I have A To Z Party Rental to help me out with that, especially since my Xanax prescription ran out. I've rented from them on a couple of different occasions, most recently for the big Yelp Sideshow Adventure party. One call took care of everything I needed, from tables and chairs to linens and coat racks. They even have coat hangers you can rent! They drop off when they say they will and pick up the next day with no hassle. And the staff is courteous and efficient. I may not have a staff, or an assistant, or even a helper monkey, but I do have A To Z programmed in my phone now. How else do you think I'm going to keep pulling these awesome parties off?
label: POS

text: I tried this shop for a simple repair on some boots I own. The work was completed by the date quoted but I was a little taken back that they needed 2 weeks to do the work. They said they'd call when the boots were available but didn't and were a little curt when I called in to check on status. The fees were very reasonable at $10 for the repair. I think I'll try another shop next time to search for a better experience.
label: NEG

text: I was tuned in to this place by the American Association of Teachers of French. They had a large conference dinner here, which my mom and I decided to skip and make our own reservation. I made my reservation through Yelp which was awesome and worked out splendidly - I received an e-mail conversation and La Minette had all of my information when we arrived. The atmosphere is very décontracté, which appeals to me. The feel is casual with a bit of elegance, so you feel like you're not just in a regular old streetside café. There aren't tons of tables, so this place could get crowded quickly, but in a good way. We started our meal with two appetizers - a fresh tomato salad and the Vol-au-Vont, which was a puff pastry filled with lobster and vegetables. Both tasted fresh and and the lobster in the vol-au-vont was delicious. They split the tomato salad for us onto two plates so we didn't have to have an awkward serving situation, which was much appreciated. My mom decided on the Cote de Porc Roti and loved it. She said the pork was cooked wonderfully and the sides were nice compliments. I decided to go with the Poulet aux Noisettes et Champignons Sauvages, which was only OK. I wasn't impressed with all of the fatty pieces of dark meat and my chicken was highly undercooked. I almost sent it back, but decided to just skip eating the wing, which was the most undercooked. It's a little weird that chicken can even come out pink in the middle, but check when you get yours so you can send it back if it's underdone. The mushrooms were good, though, and added a nice smoky compliment to the breast meat. My mom had one of their seasonal cocktails for her drink and enjoyed it, though she would have preferred it be sweeter. I opted for a nice Merlot and I thought it complimented the entire meal well. They had nice choices for dessert, but we opted to find something else on South St. Very friendly staff and the service is quick enough. Our waiter spoke French, which was a plus, as it added to my dining experience (it's nice being able to speak with someone). The bathrooms are a bit uncomfortable for Americans who aren't used to sharing a sink area with the opposite sex, so prepare yourself. Overall, a very nice restaurant and I highly recommend for an authentic French bistrot experience.
label: POS

text: For what it's worth, Golden Chopstick is a great place to go if you're in the Spring Garden area and are looking for well-priced yet delicious Chinese food. Came here on a lunch break from a face painting class taught by a master artist from Vegas who was unfamiliar with the area, so everyone in the workshop decided to come here for lunch. Thank goodness we were able to find a table big enough to seat everyone! If I'm in the area again I will most definitely come back!
label: POS

text: Although I haven't tried all of the thai food places in Boise, I'd have to say Chiang Mai is awesome - worthy of 4.5 stars! I'm very picky when it comes to thai food, especially after going to Thailand myself and each dish I've had here stands on its own - yum! I've tried both the red and green curry, excellent, very flavorful, lots of traditional veggies and a thicker sauce. The pad see yew also has a great, light sauce and complementary veggies for the wide rice noodles. Their spice level is true to the "stars" you ask for, its nice to find a place that isn't afraid to give you heat when you ask for it! Their portion size is large, with 2 dishes for 2 people, we've taken leftovers home each time and at a steel ($20 for 2 people!!). I cant wait to try out more items on their menu!!
label: POS

text: Not being a strip club expert, I will say that the only one I've ever been to is Delilah's. Oh, wait, sorry... Gentleman's Club. Hey, from the nightmarish stories I've heard from friends of mine who have gone to other nudie bars with some... um... how should I put this... "less than savory" dancers, I wasn't sure what to expect the first time I went to Delilah's. Luckily, the girls here are smoking hot. Now, you won't see me throwing dollar bills at the girls, because, quite frankly, I have better things to do with my money. However, the few times I've gone, I've been the designated driver for a friends' birthday or bachelor party, and they've rewarded me for taking one for the team. Find me a guy who will pass up a free lap dance and I'll show you a male who sings soprano.
label: POS

text: I was so excited to see a new restaurant opening in the area, especially one that wasn't a chain, so when i heard that the Village Bistro had finally opened, I went about a week later (give them time to work out some of the kinks). It was by far one of the worst dining experiences I've had in many many years! I don't even know where to start... First, I think "Bistro" and I think warm and cozy, easy lighting, nice music, comfort food with a creative touch... there is nothing 'bistro' about this place. It's loud, lacking in color and personality, and the tables are tiny, uncomfortable, and crammed together. The menu is fairly large and comprehensive - I chose the Tilapia Mignonette and here's what their menu says: "pan fried tilapia topped with lemon, lime, shallots, and buttermilk carrot fries. served with coconut basmati rice" sounded promising. I also got the tomato bisque and fruit plate as my sides. My 4 year old ordered the chicken strips and fries. Our waiter was making a good effort but was either really new or really bad at his job. I tried to give him the benefit of the doubt but as the meal wore on, it got more and more difficult. Finally, our food came (with no silverware, of course) and when it was put in front of me, i think i actually gasped. I'm no food snob, I swear to you - i can eat fun carnival food and i can eat Michelin starred cuisine - but this was shocking! I've seen better at hospital cafeterias! And, as it turns out, I've TASTED better at hospital cafeterias!!! The tilapia had the texture and smell of canned tuna, the 'topped with lemon, lime, shallots" turned out to be light yellow water tasting faintly of lemon, the carrot fries were raw and so greasy that the batter oozing off of them (not to mention that there were only three tiny pieces), and the coconut basmati rice was undercooked institutional-looking long grain and wild rice with absolutely NO flavor - no coconut, no basmati and so underdone that i actually thought i cracked my tooth when i crunched on a wild rice grain. Finally, I just put my fork down in disgust. I couldn't manage any more than a few bites. My daughter's chicken strips were on the verge of being burned but salvageable. I cut them up and was happy to see that it was nice strips of real chicken. I took a fry as she ate a piece of chicken. We both looked at each other like all of the moisture had just been sucked out of our mouths. They were so dry and bland that i actually salted my 4 year old's food! I'm sure people were shocked to see a mom salt her toddler's food but seriously, that was they only way we could get any of it down! Then, my sides were brought. Oh boy, I had forgotten about those. The 'soup' looked ok but the fruit plate was pathetic. I'm not kidding - pathetic. On the 10" white plate, there were 3 or 4 thin slices of fresh apple that were browning already, 4 slices of orange that were so over ripe that they were mushy, and a small pile of canned pineapple sitting in the center. wow! Ok, skip that and on to the soup. Tomato Bisque. First of all, the owners and chef need to look up the definition of a bisque (smooth and velvet with cream). Let me tell you my version of how to make their "tomato bisque" - take a whole fresh tomato, drop it in boiling water for a minute to loosen the skin, take it out and peel the skin, put it in a bowl and mash the heck out of it with a potato masher, pour a little puddle of cream in the middle, and serve. Seriously?! It's kind of sad that that's the best thing we ate while we were there! I wanted so much to like this place - it's new, it's local - but I can not recommend this place and will NEVER go back!
label: NEG

text: I wanted to write the review while everything was fresh in my head. So, i grew up in Clearwater, but i moved out of clearwater as soon as i graduated from high school. Being in my early 30s and having lived in NC, Asia, and NYC (i am a current resident of NYC), I expected this place to be a drab. Got together with my high school friends (yes after 14 years) and decided to go out. First of all, we went on a ladies night -- so there was no cover for us, but if i had to pay a cover charge, i might have been a little upset. The valet parking (and it is nearly impossible to find non-valet) was $5 - why should you have to pay for parking in CLEARWATER/St. Pete? we are not in the city. Drinks were free until midnight - but they poured barely any alcohol in mixed drinks. We got to the place right around 11pm and the place was pretty empty. Well, now to the good things or rather, positive. The bartenders were cute - they are all girls, but from the girl's perspective, they were cute and classy., Because the club is known to be a little more classy than ybor, there were more older people than not. We were all in our early 30s and we didn't feel old. There were plenty of older folks and of course younger mid-late 20s. The decor is fancy; they have big screen tvs everywhere; and the bathrooms were great - though you have to tip the attendants. If you are girl and straighten your hair - in the middle of the night you'll find your hair getting frizzy. Don't worry, the bathroom has a flat iron - for about $2 per use. Other than the facility, the music was great until 1am. at 1 am, the music turned WEIRD and techno on us. People watching is the best. From the second floor, you can see what the crowd is doing on the first floor. This is a MUST. It is hilarious. We danced, sang along, took lots of pictures, drank, and had a blast watching people. This is a place to check out if you are in clearwater/st pete and want to go out for low key fun. Not a place to seek out or for which you go out of your way.
label: NEG

text: A dive bar that actually has good music, is it possible? Apparently so on Frenchmen Street. Luckily if you don't like the musical selection at one place there are 10 more within a very short walk. For tourists the Marginy area is a nice respite from the activity of the quarter while giving you a feel for the local nightlife.

text: Okay, so I've driven by BTO quite a few times at night this summer and have always seen it PACKED. I get the hype if it tastes great, nay even good, but BTO is really just...OKAY. I don't get all the hype. I mean sure, if I was counting calories and worried about eating real ice cream, then OKAY, BTO is a good alternative. But what's really going on here? Basically this place is packed day and night because some calorie counters want to feel like they're making healthy life choices. Come on. We know what's going on people. You don't fool us when you pile 32oz of chocolate, sprinkles, syrup, cookie crumbs, bacon, or whatever you throw on top of that "healthy" yogurt. Folks, if you want something cold and you're okay with a few extra calories, just head down the street to one of the many REAL ice cream shops here in town. text: I have been playing piano since I was a baby, and been in a million different piano shops all over the country - but this one is just amazing. Aside from the fact that Steinway is one of the BEST brands of pianos, and have been in business for a million years, and some of the best pianist in the world play on a Steinway - my review of this location is for the owners Lamis and Arlene - husband and wife team, who truly LOVE the piano and music and helping people who share their passion. Most piano shops - especially high end shops have high pressure sales people who jump you as soon as you walk in the door - this is not the case at this place, and they show you around, make you feel VERY welcomed, and they actually listen, and are very encouraging and supportive. If you dont have a piano at home, your welcome to come play one of theirs anytime you want! What kind of shop offers that?? If you tell them you can play - they will twist your arm till you play for them!! What I love about these people is they love to tell you their story! You have to go in and talk to them, they are very interesting people. I was in there for like 3 hours talking to them, and met some of the teachers and students, got a tour of the whole place listened to some people play. It was a great experience and I felt like I was at home with friends I'd known for years! If you can't afford a brand new piano, ask about the used ones they have in the back warehouse - they are a steal!!! They have financing though for the new ones which is sweet! If you need lessons, they have those too, with wonderful, very talented teachers. Any age is welcome! I've never felt more welcomed! Go check em out and ask Arlene to play you a song!
label: POS

text: Have you ever had a jalapeno and cheese hot dog before, with homemade pretzel dough wrapped around it in strips? When I opened up the foil, I'm looking and looking for the cheese and the jalapenos and I saw nothing even resembling this. Oh well, maybe she gave me the wrong dog, so I took one big bite and low and behold those peppers and cheese were inside of the hot dog! Wow, talk about a shock to the taste buds and flavor. Talk about putting the HOT in hot dog! How do they do that? They have to make their own hot dogs?! I had a coupon for buy one get one free soft pretzel which led me to Barbie's, however after seeing their displays of soft pretzels and pretzel products, I would have stopped here without the coupon. I also did get my two pretzels and it is unlike any soft pretzel I have had, almost like they used a starter for the dough, which was sweet, yet salty. These very soft and delicious pretzels are made right before your eyes This dough is baked around all beef hot dogs, sausage or cheese. They also have pretzel pockets, filled with either bacon, egg and cheese, a pepperoni pizza filling, a cheese steak filled pretzel pocket, Stromboli or roast beef and swiss cheese. Pretzels are coming out of their ovens here with sour cream and onion, cinnamon and sugar, to small pretzel bites filled with pieces of hot dogs or cheese. They have hand dipped ice cream and fresh squeezed lemonade. If you buy a milkshake for $3.75 you can have a free soft pretzel. With all of Barbie's twists and turns of the dough and knowing just how to stuff it, it is no wonder she has crowds standing around watching and anxiously awaiting their turn. I can't wait to go back and try the pepperoni pizza pretzel pocket! Say that ten times fast.

text: I am a frequent visitor to New Orleans or N'Awlins as it is properly known, and my favorite restaurant in the USA is Mother's near Canal Street. The sauce was great: piquant, smooth and brilliantly sets off the kick of the pepper or whatever was the kick-ass spice. The imported New Orleans root beer is a must! Reading Terminal is my over all favorite place to eat in the city. Every group of Philadelphian and interesting tourists all mingling together (like a jambalya!) I have always loved the sandwiches there: DInic's, Spataros, Herschl's. I may have a new fave. A rave!

Like many of my New Orleans meal adventures, we ordered excessively. To kick start the brunch, we got 1 dozen oysters and the rabbit and duck liver pate. We could've stopped there, and I would've been happy. I never would've dreamed of wanting to lick the canister of a pate jar, but I've discovered a new aspiration. For my main meal I got the crab omelet. It was served with fries and a salad. text: This awesome Market is seasonal. It changes every week as harvests change, and best appreciated if you take the time to approach each table and explore/talk to the farmers and vendors. Definitely go during different times in the season. It ebbs and flows with the local harvests. In May farms sell surplus vegetable seedlings for your own garden. Summer is best, there are six farms bringing Jersey sweet corn! During the height of the season, the local just-picked produce is bursting at the seams. Fall means apples and Thanksgiving-ish stuff. There are less farmers than summer, by design--since there are less harvests--but still well enough to fill a dinner table full of wonderful local foods. TIP: Go in the early hours, 8-9AM. The best items may sell out before noon!

When the 3rd salesgirl told me, I just kinda sighed & she says, "Oh, I guess you've already heard?" Um yeah, about two times too many. I'm giving Knit Wit two stars because if you're not into exciting fashion you'll probably like this store just fine & technically speaking there really isn't anything wrong with the clothes they carry. text: This was my third experience at a brazilian steakhouse. Having been through the experience before, I was definitely excited to try Fogo de Chao. To start, the salad bar was much smaller and had less variety than other places I have been. This is not to say it was bad, just that it didnt live up to expectations of similar restaurants. When the meat finally started coming, the first few pieces were delicious. Then we waited. And waited. And waited. I think that the room is beautiful but it is shaped strangely for this restaurant. We were tucked away in an alcove where I dont think the gauchos could see us. At other places, I have had a line of gauchos standing by. Here, we had to actually ask for more of them to come by. It kind of diminished the thrill a little to have to "order" the food. Isn't that what the green button is for? When we finally had more meat on plate, this is when the disappointment really started. No matter what the type of meat was, it was charred on the outside and rare on the inside. I usually prefer my steaks cooked medium, and I understand that this isn't cook-to-order, but I would say the majority of people do not like meat that is cool to the touch and bleeding. All told, I was really excited to have a gluttonous feast of meat on a sword. The lackluster salad bar, the slow service, and the raw meat, however, made this an underwhelming experience.

The pizza was pretty tasty but toppings were not exactly generous and the limp crust on the bottom allowed those handful of toppings to slip and slide a bit. text: The Joint is my favorite place in New Orleans for BBQ, far and away the best the city has to offer, IMO. I'd rank it much higher than Ugly Dog, Ms. Hysters, and VooDoo (yuck) in terms of both quality and atmosphere. Located at the edge of the Bywater neighborhood within sight of the Industrial Canal and in close proximity to the naval installation, the building looks like a small shack from the outside. After you enter you'll find that this book's cover was a good judge of its insides as well. This is an not upscale establishment and the focus is on the food, as it should be. Orders are served in plastic baskets lined with paper. The wonderful smell of smoked meats is immediately apparent as soon as you enter this tiny shack and will linger on your clothes for a few hours after you leave. The decorations include some Dr Bob artwork, a jukebox, a picture commemorating a visit from Diners Driveins and Dives, and a sign proclaiming The Joint as carnivorous cuisine, just in case you couldn't already tell. There's a small counter to your immediate left where you place your order and a few patio tables inside. Just to the side there's self serve sweet tea which is always the perfect accompaniment to BBQ, sugar rush be damned. The back yard contains the rhinoceros-sized smoker and a few picnic tables paired with some rusted out metal chairs for outdoors eating. If it is your first time eating here I'd recommend the W special, giving you a little brisket, a little pulled pork, and two ribs plus a side. In reality what they claim as a little is truly a full portion, so you'll have plenty of leftovers for later. I drown my pulled pork in the dark sauce and mop up the excess with my bread at the end, but the ribs are just fine without, their dry rub imparts plenty of flavor all on its own. I always opt for the beans as my side. They're cooked in pork fat and are MMM MMM GOOD. They also have chaurice (a type of sausage) and chicken, but chicken always tastes dry to me when it's been barbequed, no matter where I order it. Other sides include mac 'n cheese, potato salad, and cole slaw, which aren't as memorable as the baked beans. That said, if you're in New Orleans and in need of some BBQ, this is THE PLACE to go.

text: My sister declared this her favorite restaurant in Phila, so I offered to take her here for dinner last night. However, it should be noted that they dp not take credit cards (that was all I had on me) and so my sister took me out do dinner instead. (A wonderful trick to pull if you are going with someone who is obligated to love you no matter what.) But even though she had to pay, our dinner (apps to entrees to dessert to yum iced tea) was under 40 bucks. Pretty awesome. I'm a relative noob when it comes to Thai food and have never had Laotian, so I usually stick with shrimp pad thai. So I've had my share of shrimp pad thai. And this ranks up there with the best I've ever had. Yum yum yum. Sis got the red curry and it was like a sweet, spicy soup with lots of veg and chicken in it. The spring rolls we split for an app were so tasty, light and fresh. I tried the thai iced tea and I was scared it would be too sweet, but it was pretty close to a perfect compliment to my meal. I ordered the rice pudding for dessert, expecting normal rice pudding, but it came in 4 little warm cups and was anything but normal, but decidedly delicious. We were stuffed to the brim with delicious dinner. (No sense in leaving too little to take home on your plate, of course.) As for the service, it was above average. Our waters were refilled, the food came out quickly, but it did take a while to flag down the waitress for the check. Not a big deal at all, just us being in a hurry to get out the door to answer the call of nature ;) So go here. It's a cheap, delicious, cozy restaurant.

text: I joined this gym about two weeks ago. So far I've only been using it for the classes, as there are about 75 cardio, strength, and yoga classes per week. I hope to take part in yoga and zumba as well, but haven't had a chance to go yet. Every class I've been to or seen is at or near capacity, which speaks for the quality of the place. The gym itself seems to be comprehensive and there appears to be plenty of cardio and weight equipment for everyone. I also got a bunch of bennies for joining--free massage, PT assessment, personal training sessions, etc etc. Membership isn't cheap, to be sure, but I think it's worth it if you utilize the place. My only downside about AFC is the front desk staff. The first three times I went I was in the process of trying out the place and gathering info. Each time I spoke to the front desk person/persons, they looked at me like I was speaking Chinese and took about ten seconds to process what I thought was the most simple of requests--can I speak with a membership rep, I'm here for a trial class, no I already told you I've been shown around three times, etc. They honestly seem to be some of the least intelligent and most unhelpful people I've met in a fitness center. The front desk is also a mess of clutter and everyone just sort of crowds around it to sign in or ask a question, so you end up having to fight for attention of a staff member that's going to look at you like a slow cow anyways. The members of the club seem to be typical of the suburban area, not intimidating or meatheads, fairly into themselves but not rude. I'll continue to be a member here for as long as I keep up the enthusiasm to go to classes!

The frozen, tiny pineapple chunks are gone. The couple next to us asked for a refund for their drinks. Food: Lousy. Took forever for the entrees, and when they finally arrived, both meals were incorrectly prepared (loads of awful, lumpy sauce which we didn't order) and the seared ahi was WELL done (gross). My petite filet was well done (ordered it medium rare), drenched in burned red wine "sauce" and the lobster tail was so overcooked, you couldn't remove the meat from the shell. Our replacement entrees were served ten minutes apart, which by that time, we just wanted to pay our bill and get out of there. Server: Gigantic handlebar mustache (and, I mean GIGANTIC). More important is that for a Friday night that was not at all busy, he disappeared except for the obligatory order taking, mid-meal follow-up and to give us the check. In a nutshell: our second visit was a complete 180 from our first. New management? Our best guess, but it does not matter. Do not waste your money. Overpriced (oh, and the ladie's restroom: nasty, dirty and disgusting). Not what you would expect for a dinner tab in excess of $150 for a party of two (and this was for one appetizer, two entrees, two beers and one glass of wine). Rip-off, period.

text: Geez; it feels like I can't walk five feet these days without running into another cupcake shop. Tragic, I know. I was driving through Headhouse Square today when I saw a pink beacon of a sign proclaiming "Cupmakes," so I knew I had to make a stop and do some research. I am indecisive enough as it is, so I was particularly stumped when I had to sort out flavors of icing, cake, and toppings for myself. The owner busted out pastry bags of icing to let me sample the "confetti cake batter" buttercream (mostly tasted like Amaretto, not cake batter), as well as the peanut butter (decent, but a letdown after the rich, nut-studded PB frosting at It's a Cupcake). Their buttercream is too fluffy for me - it doesn't have the langorous, sugary density of Brown Betty's and Naked's, nor does it come close to the same concentration of flavor. The chocolate, which I ended up putting on my vanilla cupcake, was the best of the three. It had a nice strong cocoa taste (But would I take it over BB's chocolate frosting? Never.) Not to mention that it skeeves me out to think that they leave out pastry bags full of unrefrigerated buttercream all day. If they really used butter, it would solidify if it were refrigerated, so that makes me think it is either full of artificial crap or kept at room temperature. I steered clear of the TCBY-like toppings and went with a purist chocolate frosting-vanilla cake combo. Most importantly, I found the cake itself to be off-putting. I hesitate to say this in case I am in error, but it sure as hell tasted like a mix to me. It had that overly-springy, overly moist texture rarely found in scratch-baked cakes, and a telltale artificial taste. In fact, it tasted exactly like a muffin from Costco. When dressed up with enough cocoa icing it tasted OK (because I couldn't taste the cake), but believe me - this is not artisan-quality homemade pastry. I'll take my $3 and go to Brown Betty. Sorry guys. I love to see creative local bakeries succeed, but I also hate wasting money and calories on inferior dessert. Prove me wrong! Until then, I'm sticking to my story.

text: One of my goals in life is to make friends with someone who works in the Comcast building so I can venture to the top and frolic through the employee-only restaurant on the 43rd/44th floors and finally discover if William Penn #2 (#3?) is still there. The other day I stopped in and was instantly transported to Franklin Lloyd Wright's architectural masterpiece "Fallingwater" replete with vividly realistic sounds of water sloshing up its stone walls. They also present a holiday show every year -- music, dancing and sparkling lights -- all displayed with the brilliance of 10 million pixels (so uh, FIVE times the resolution of HDTV). Very cool. Honestly, I was expecting extreme cheesiness, but I actually really enjoyed the show. It is every hour on the hour during the holiday season and it even ends with a flurry of fake snowfall. If something doesn't sell well at major chain stores, the manufacturer still has to dump their warehouse full of stuff that the major chain stores don't want anymore. And that's where Big Lots comes in. Granted, there is often a reason why something doesn't sell at the big name chain stores and it ends up in a close-out store. But sometimes the reason is not quality, it's just the taste of the average buyer. And if you happen to be "odd" or a "discriminating consumer" (like me, ha-ha) and like something that the majority doesn' t like (which happens all the time to those of us who really do have good taste, snort, snort, :-), then you can sometimes find it at Big Lots for a GREAT PRICE! "OY VEY! SUCH A DEAL!" So here's my strategy: I shop the food aisles every week, try a little of something I might like, and if I like it, go back the next time and buy a LOT of it, because when it's gone, it's gone. Are you a fan of Tuesday Morning? If so, Big Lots is the lower-priced version of Tuesday Morning. I've sometimes seen the same things on sale for cheaper at Big Lots. Caveats: #1: Check the expiration date of all food items before you put them in your cart. They are notorious for having out-dated food. Most everything is fine, but every once in a while they have out-dated product. Note: I do not work at Big Lots, never have, and do not own stock in them. I just luuuuuuuuuuuuuv saving money! text: This place gets 2 stars for dedicated ownership and potential. And the elements keeping it from being a great market seem so obvious. The attraction of a farm market are the freshness of all of its stuff and the inevitability of always finding something new. The best way to achieve zero growth is to offer same old same old. Go to the Market at Head House Square during the summer and you see the farmers trucks on the street being unloaded. The produce still has dirt on it, the cheeses are made in small batches, the peaches have fuzz on them and they all scream freshness. Go to the Farmers Market in Ardmore or Strafford and you'll find great fish and meats, a produce market with treviso, white asparagus, Belgian endive, mandarinos from Sicily, icicle radishes and cactus pears. The Amish concession is manned by an entire Amish family and you know that their chickens, produce, relishes and shoo fly pie came off their farm and from their kitchen. This straightforward no frills approach to food retail, bringing the best possible fresh foods to the city is the reason that a farmers market flourishes. Wine stalls, beer tastings and cooking lessons are fine but completely secondary to what is truly important. Fitting this perfectly adequate space with a dynamite fruit and produce section with interesting greengrocer items is key and no one runs these types of markets better than Korean operators. Additionally, a dynamic meat and poultry section is also mandatory for the growth of a market of this type. Further, if it is a year round market and not summer only, a fresh fish stand is if not a necessity, would leave a shopper no reason to go to the big stores. People who go to farmers markets know they will pay more but do not want to see most of the stuff there that they see in an Acme. Definite potential for 5 stars but never without the pieces necessary to attract patrons and put the market on their must-go-every-week list.

there was really nice and friendly. she was always excited to place a styrofoam container of balls in your face. when you walk in, there's a counter immediately in front of you and there was a delivery person standing there. a few tables along the side of the wall, not much space. there is a little fridge towards the back for drinks. a few sodas and thai tea in a can (Lucia brand) - which is what i had. there's an area in the very back that has a bathroom. be careful, its a weighted door so when you push it feels like someone is pushing back to close it. also, the soap in there doesn't smell too good. i ordered the Far East Sampler, which had 3 original octopus, 3 sweet&sour miso chicken, and 3 Korroke (which are beef & potato croquettes with Tonkatsu sauce). they're small, but Japanese portions are generally small anyway and the dough can really fill you up. i agree that they were really undercooked. it would have been really delicious if they were cooked properly and had more filling in them. the original octopus came with some shavings of what i think is fish flakes on top? they were cool to look at since the door was open and the wind was blasting in. they looked like they were moving! it was mostly chewy dough with a tiny piece of octopus in it and or at least i hope it was octopus. it was too small to tell in all that half cooked dough. the sweet & sour miso was pretty good, but i really only liked the sauce, not so much the balls. the korroke was just a fried ball of mush. too much potato, not enough beef. and i didn't get 3, i got 2. overall the takoyaki i had was 'ARIGHT'. not "all right/alright/aight" but "ARIGHT". it makes sense if you're from philly. haha i also ordered the chocolate takoyaki for dessert. pretty much chocolate dough with ice cream on top and some decorative sprinkles. they were okay, i think chocolate glazed munchkins from dunkin' donuts are better though. my friends ordered some other ones, but they liked it. or maybe they were just being polite since i picked the place for us to meet up and eat and catch up. my one friend didn't get her food until the rest of us had already eaten. they actually lost her ticket and she had to wait another 10 mintues on top of the 45 minutes she had wasted sitting there watching us eat and picking at our food. the woman was really apologetic about it and gave her pumpkin spice balls on the house. she felt really bad cause we were joking about how this always happens when she orders food. in any case, we all got to eat and experience this little takoyaki place. i give it 2 stars for trying something new, playing Portishead, and because they tried to appease us for forgetting one order, but if i want takoyaki, i'd rather go to yakitori boy. or Japan.

text: This market is an absolute miracle for downtown Nashville! Even though residents of downtown had food selections available at Walgreen, Dollar General & several small bodega-type stores prior to the arrival of H G Hill Urban Market, we haven't had anything comparable to this in decades. H G Hill Urban Market has a full line of groceries, frozen food, beer, produce, meats, snacks, household items, etc. A very important feature within the market is the deli, stocked full of prepared food and desserts. I have no doubt that a person could purchase all their groceries here and never really feel the need to venture elsewhere ... certainly not more than once a month or so for favorite items not found within these walls. The market is appropriate for quick items & meals for office workers and tourists and as a complete market for downtown dwellers. To make matters even better, the hours are fantastic, open every day (including most holidays) from morning until 9 PM. I am giving the full five stars. Considering the entire picture, I don't feel that it is appropriate to deduct points just because there is not space enough to carry every brand of every cereal, etc. There is certainly enough of everything to provide all of us with what we need. Regarding the prices, I don't find them especially different. Certainly some items may cost a few cents more than at a large suburban market; but some items are also on sale at any given time. Some of the items may seem high priced because they truly are upscale and/or organic items; but there's plenty standard selections for those on a budget. THANK YOU H G Hills for coming to our rescue!

text: Wow, talk about an alcoholic dying and going to heaven. This place is for grown ups what Toys R Us is for kids. Yea, it's that good. This place has got it all your bases covered. If you are throwing a party and need to stock up on beer and liquor, this is your place. If you are looking for a nice bottle of wine, this place has plenty. On Saturdays they do tastings, and not just of wine. I was introduced to one of my new favorite brews, Magic Hat #9, at Friar Tucks. This place is Afreakingmazing, and has become my go to place when I need to do some shopping for adult beverages. text: So this weekend we decided that K needed to experience the Indiana State Fair for the first time ever just to show her that there is indeed plenty to do in IN. We went on Saturday, which meant the crowds were out in full effect. The first thing to note is that the fair is NOT cheap. After $5 for parking, we paid $8 for admission each. Sorry, we didn't notice what the price for kids was all you mommy and daddy yelpers. There was a decent sized crowd, definitely enough room so that you aren't bumping into people while you are walking and plenty of shady areas to cool off. The rides are nice, but the real attraction at the fair is the food! The first thing we ate was an Elephant ear- ($5) a large, flat, deep-fried piece of dough smothered in icing and cinnamon sugar....what is not to love? The only problem with this dish was the powdered sugar which the wind blew all over us. Next we got buttered corn- ($3) sweet, crispy ears of corn dipped in butter and sprinkled with salt. This was K's favorite purchase of the whole night. Corn on the cob never fails to satisfy. Lastly, the Fried Cheese Nuggets from Hot Wisconsin- ($7) was a yummy ping-pong ball sized piece of cheese that was deep fried with breading. It came with 4 possible dipping sauces with your choice of 2. A fellow yelper wrote that they were super good....we have to disagree only because it was so heavy that after one we really didn't want another one. We threw half of them away. However, a lot of the locals seemed to be ordering the jalapeno cheese sticks so maybe give those a shot. They also had a sampler platter for $12. There was way more food that we wanted to try but, seriously, we are only human. Some that caught our eye were the turkey legs (that we vowed to go back for), fried Pepsi dough (so curious about these), huge corndogs, and chicken and pork on a stick. Animals: K has lived her whole life in Hawaii and has never really seen plenty of animals at once. It blew her mind walking through the pig, horse, sheep, goat, and cow tents. They are fenced off with little gates making the animals easy to pet. There were also baby animals in each tent that all the children swarmed. The only downside is that the animals are constantly being shuttled from one area to another. One poor lady was caught in the "spatter zone" of a cow and her foot was covered in poo.... Games: Majority of the games are classic like shooting basketballs and throwing darts. They were also very expensive ($3-$5 a try) the games we had fun at were pushing the bowling ball over the hill (only $0.25) and ski-ball (only $1.00). All the other games you could tell were rigged and overpriced. One game that really stood out was a metal stick that is windy and spins. There is a little hoop that you have to get all the way to the bottom of the windy stick but the hoop cannot touch the stick at all. If you succeed, you win an ipod nano ($2 for 1 try, $5 for 4). Rides: All the classic rides were there but the average pricing for rides was 3-4 ride coupons. For $5, you get 4 ride coupons...you do the math. Overall, the Indiana State Fair is a fun weekend excursion, or a nice date with a special someone. Make sure you come with a fat wallet and empty belly though.

text: It is with great sorrow that this review is written. Christopher's was a great place for Sam and I to go after tango on Wednesdays. We joked that we were becoming regulars...but we liked the idea. The food was consistent, the service acceptable and their Wednesday wine special was perfect timing for our schedule. With our Wednesday night commitment in Wayne a thing of the past...we decided to take the drive from Media to Christopher's last night (in the rain) for the sake of the good ole days. The server who used to say "got it" all the time was now dressed in the garb of management and the staff huddled around the kitchen doing nothing much. Be it the peter principle at work or simply a bad night for the place...Sam and I contemplated walking out after sitting with menus for over 10 minutes with no one to greet us. The manager walked by 3 times and never once noticed our empty table and folded menus. (He was an attentive, capable server before.) Eventually someone came by and asked "Has your server been here?" Well, of course not, we don't even know who our server is. The person who was not our server took a drink order...and then we were left alone again. When our drinks arrived with our assigned and previously missing server, he put them on the table and said "Are you all ready?" Yes, in fact I was ready to tell him how little I thought of him, that he should be ashamed to call himself a server and had he learned not an ounce of social skill simply from being human? (I held my tongue, not wanting to act as old as I was feeling at that moment.) But really, he was rude, gruff and not at all apologetic for his tardiness. In fact, he seemed annoyed we were there. He took our order. No water, no bread, no further contact ensued. Sam's drink was not to his liking...but there was no one to talk to about it. The "got it" manager looked scared of making contact with anyone, even his staff as they freely did what they pleased: nothing. How can you run a restaurant and not have the desire, ability and sense to take note of each table in the place? To anticipate the needs of your customers, to note the stages of dining, how attentive are your servers being. There is no excuse for bad service when more than half the staff is standing chatting (on their cell phones) doing nothing to contribute to the success of the restaurant. Needless to say, I think our love affair with Christopher's came to grinding halt last night. We left disappointed and saddened by the loss. We are sure our hand written comment card was discarded...why would a server pass on such information? Why would a new manager risk letting his boss see the comment? And we really like their cobia special. It is the best bargain on the menu. Crab and scallion risotto, grilled scallions on top, a mild, flavorful grilled cobia fish on top. I can still recommend that...but perhaps take-out is a better option.

I also noticed they clean a lot and clear off tables quickly. I wanted to try a little of everything so I ordered the 3 meat plate with 2 sides. And my friend ordered the same. I got - spicy sausage, pull pork, and brisket - my sides were waffle fries, mac n cheese, and just because I love fried okra I had to get an extra side of okra! And a sweet tea. I like my sweet tea REALLY sweet so I added extra sugar, and it was perfect! My friend ordered - spicy sausage, chicken, and ribs, and the same sides as me. All I can say is the meat was awesome! Perfectly cooked, perfectly seasoned. Both our dinners came with garnishing of pickles and onions, and a mouth watering buttery dinner roll. They have a giant vat of pickles in a barrel - free for the taking, those are awesome pickles, goes PERFECT with the BBQ! Since I was there to sample everything, I helped myself to the condiment bar - I got some of each of their BBQ sauce. Sweet, Dickey's Original, and Hot and Spicy! The Hot and Spicy won - it was awesome!!! After stuffing ourselves silly, unable to finish all of the food, we helped ourselves to a little more of the WONDERFUL sweet tea and an ice cream cone on the way out! I love the nifty bright yellow "to go" souvenir cups! The tiny ice cream cone on the way out the door was the perfect touch! They offer a BBQ sandwich for less then $3.00 - your choice of meat. Also their salt and pepper comes in those tiny packages instead of having shakers on the table, which is annoying to me! Our dinner was $29.00 total which is about $10-$15 LESS then what it runs at any other BBQ joint in Reno, and we got much more food, and it was great! I do admit - while eating Dickey's BBQ, the thought did come to mind - "now if I could just have a piece or two of Carolina's catfish this would really be awesome" I will absolutely be coming back here soon! Also - separate from the restaurant, they have a full bar, if drinking is your thing! text: This place used to be better - I've been going to Nature's Food Patch for several years, its right down the street from my work and incredibly convenient. Unfortunately I've seen the store slowly declining in its quality and with the competition that has opened across the bay (Wild Oats and soon the Publix Greenwise marketplace) I find my visits less and less frequent. While I try to support the smaller, longer standing institutions even when the competition is priced less, I'm just repeatedly dissapointed with the direction this place has headed. I'm a vegan so shopping at a natural food store is pretty much a requirement to a well-rounded cupboard. Their grocery section is very adequate and actually priced quite reasonably when compared to other small natural food stores or even the big chains. I have, however, run into a frequent problem of purchasing vegan 'dairy' items and find that they are spoiled. This has happened to me on several occasions when purchasing fake cheese products, many of which were not even close to their expiration date, which leads me to believe that they may be improperly storing some of the food items that require refrigeration. For this reason I only buy dry good from them now. As for the deli, they made several improvements over the past few months but the quality and convenience has actually declined. To start off with the good, they do now have a hot food section which is great for lunch. No more bringing back cold lunches or having to reheat your meals in the company microwave! Also, they've expanded their racks to provide prepackaged foods from the deli cases including their pasta salads, tofu, and even sandwiches and wraps. Unfortunately, when they expanded the cases they did away with the convenient name tags that said whether or not items were Omnivore, Vegetarian, or Vegan. So now you have to ask the assistant behind the counter and the majority of the time wait while they scan the ingredients and give a not-so-helpful reply of, 'I think its vegan?" And while the prepackaged food is convenient so you do not have to stand in line... its been my recent experiences that prepared food in the deli has been suffering from quality controls that has lead to poor taste or even foreign objects in my wraps. Lastly, as someone whose been eating at the deli for several years, it would be nice if they brought in some new dishes for variety. To their credit, whenever I've had problems they've been very polite and offered to either exchange the item or offered me store credit. They seem sincere about improving the conditions but I see little change from visit to visit. When I shop here its for convenience and only for dry goods. Otherwise, I make a trip once or twice a month to Wild Oats and pickup a stockpile of my vegan essentials.

text: One enters El Rey under an illuminated theatre marque which proclaims (in Spanish) that "El Rey will change your life". These words are a bit of an overstatement, perhaps, but El Rey will certainly change your evening. Like all of Steven Starr's "venues", restaurant aesthetics is as important to the dining experience as the food. This place gets 5 stars on both counts. The design aesthetic of El Rey, however, is a major departure from the big budget refined productions we are accustomed to with Starr. The space was formerly occupied by the Midtown Diner - a mid-century nondescript grease-pit of sorts. The Midtown Diner was subtly retrofitted and redeployed by Starr to create El Rey. El Rey is reminiscent of dingy border town diner one might expect to see in a Quentin Tarantino flick, with a soundtrack to match (from the speakers blare an inconsistent variety of genres, ranging from old school country and soul, to Mexican, funk, and surf music). The mishmash of tunes are delightful. As are the obscure vintage Mexican wrestling flick posters plastered to the walls, and the framed original prison art. Very dark and eerie. Very Tarantino. The surreal mood is set. Servers sport mostly flannel and denim. They are uber-friendly, hip, and helpful. The (intentional) dinginess of the place contrasts superbly with the wonderful food and drink - alive with flavor. Lubricate the evening with fresh-fruit-filled sangria - rojo or blanco. Or try one of the several varieties of margaritas. I enjoy the sour/bitter tamarind version. Start your feast with one of the fresh fish and lime ceviches (having recently returned from a week on Costa Rica's Pacific Coast, I can attest that the El Rey incarnations are very reminiscent of the roadside offerings ). The corn on the cob, with its coating of spices and cheese, is a must try. Then work your way up to flavorful tacos or enchiladas (the short rib variation is my preference). I also highly recommend the stuffed peppers. The dishes are Mexican with a twist - but just the right twist (not too much that they loose all of their authenticity). Clearly this is not authentic Mexican (as other reviewers have pointed out). But I don't believe it pretends to be. What it is is a variation on a theme that is interesting and flavorful, and served in a quite unique context. If there can be such thing a "subtly over-the-top", El Rey fits the bill. For the experience, the cost is modest. One can get reasonably stuffed for plus-or-minus $15. And at about $7 for a margarita, you can get reasonably buzzed without breaking the bank.

text: My dinner at Bern's Steakhouse was by far one of the best and most unique dining experiences that I've ever had. I'm a pescatarian to boot, who didn't even try what Bern's specializes in (which I've been told is actually quite mediocre), but I still loved being there because it wasn't so much about the food; it was about the overall experience. My dining companions ordered steak entrees that came with french onion soup, baked potato, salad and onion rings, while I stuck with two appetizers because I was not feeling too hungry. Little did I know, though, that their appetizers were entree-sized! Their tuna tartare wasn't what I expected it to be. When I think tuna tartare, I think tuna salad, as in diced up tuna marinated in various sauces, spices and herbs, and then eaten on toast or chips. The Bern's version of tuna tartare is actually minced up tuna mixed with soy sauce, sesame, cilantro, ect. It was presented molded circularly, making it look a lot like a raw burger patty. It was served with wasabi, pickled ginger, and deep fried wonton skins. I was pretty indifferent to the tuna tartare, but the white truffle macaroni and cheese was AMAZING, to say the least. It was riccioli pasta in a white cheese sauce with white truffle generously grated all over the top, making it look like minced garlic. Then it was topped with sliced up chives. It wasn't too salty or greasy, and it was just the right amount of richness, creaminess and flavor; just perfect. Our waiter was everything that we wanted him to be, and then some. He was totally at our service, and after dinner, he even took us on a tour of the wine cellar, which was mind blowing. They have over SEVEN THOUSAND different wines dating back to the 1800's. He said that they recently sold a bottle from the 1700's for $6100. It was so fascinating listening to him tell us all these cool facts about wine. Our waiter is also a photographer, so he took a bunch of really awesome pictures of us in the wine cellar. Then we got a tour of the kitchen from another waiter, and then it was off to the dessert room. And yes, it's as tasty as it sounds! :) It's upstairs and full of small, closed off circular booths for privacy. They had a huge dessert menu full of sweet drinks and treats, and thousands of dessert wines. We ended up getting coconut sorbet, a baked Alaska, a King Midas, which is carrot cake with chocolate ice cream and a lot of chocolate sauce. The coconut sorbet was so creamy that it tasted just like ice cream! The meringue in the baked Alaska had so much sugar in it that it had the taste and texture of a marshmallow. The carrot cake was intense. Everything was way too sweet though, and us three health nuts (my friends much moreso than I) only finished about half of it. One cool thing about the dessert room: In every booth, there are buttons to push to choose a category of music for that booth, including my favorite, the "live music" button. Next to these buttons is a telephone that goes straight to the pianist to make song requests. Downstairs, there's a pianist who can play ANYTHING. We got to enjoy the likes of Billy Joel, Journey, and Sinatra, not to mention the theme to Inspector Gadget, while sipping on Turkish coffee and eating yummy dessert! We dined at Bern's for three hours and with tip and everything, the bill came out to about $250 for three people. Not bad at all. At first glance, Bern's may seem expensive, but one you experience it, you'll find that you really get your monies worth. And then some. The portions are generous. The food is delicious. The ingredients, the finest. The restaurant, classy, yet not uptight. The decor is amazing. The ambiance is nice and relaxing. And last, but not least, the staff members are awesome, extremely accommodating, and VERY knowledgeable in what they do.

text: The Venture Inn has been a tradition in the somewhat seedy world of the Gay-borhood of Philadelphia. With more and open acceptance of different life styles, however, new, upscale, expensive and even outstanding eateries have popped up all over the place in the Washington Square area that cater to mainly a gay clientele, and therefore some of the old places have been left behind. The Venture is one of them. Although a "grand dame" of the community, it nonetheless has been left behind and nowadays caters to mainly an adult community, from which the moniker "The Denture Inn" has emerged. Although unjust, its reputation continues despite new management and what seems to be an honest effort at changing its character. The small side street where Venture is Camac Street, one of the numerous alley-type streets all over the older part of Philadelphia. These small streets have become more pricey and upscale, however, Camac has maintained a sort of seedy reputation due to its commercial employment. We went to the Venture Inn just to see how things had changed. I'm afraid they haven't sufficiently to go there again. In four categories, service, food, ambiance, and price, it loses to the neighboring establishments. First the service. Our waiter was obviously used to the older crowd and seemed to want to be our friend from the start. Frankly, if I wanted to be friends with a waiter, I'd make it outside of a restaurant. His overtures seemed pedantic, especially compared to the mediocre service we got which included forgetting a round of drinks we ordered with dinner. Second, the food. The mussels I ordered came in a tasty sauce. However, there were several unopened, bad ones. That is something any good restaurant would be able to screen. The food was generally good, although the presentation was "homey", not what you would expect for the price. No espresso. Third, the ambiance. On a beautiful cool summer evening in Philadelphia, al fresco seating would have been a plus. The Venture Inn restaurant sits in a building where the smoke stench has permeated the walls over decades and decades. The yellowish walls attest to the nicotine and tar of the pre-smoke prohibition in Philadelphia. Frankly, I was gasping for breath after an hour. Fourth, the price. We spent forty per person including a glass of wine each. Right around the corner, I can get the same at an upscale, new, saucy Mixto restaurant that features Cuban/Colombian infusion with knock-your-socks off service and outstanding ambiance and food. It is obvious by the clientele surrounding us that the Venture is happily within its core clientele of tired gay men in their 60s to whom a disrespectful out-of-shape waiter and mediocre food is a compliment.

Well if you told me during the many times I called or asked that there would be that charge, I would have waited to do this when a doctor who had seen my dog before was there. Next they send the Office Manager to come in to speak to us. This is turning into a total nightmare. I just want to do what I came for and get out of there. Next the doctor comes in. Had we been told I would have been prepared and not minded paying the fee. Dr Parker finally snapped at us and said "Oh so I'll just take off my fee is THAT what you want?" She then turned to the receptionist and in a disgusted voice told her take off the fee and as she walked out the door snottily said you can either have this done or go elsewhere. We paid and the dog was brought in to us and within a minute the doctor came back in and abruptly asked us did we want the dog on the table or the floor. We had to ask if we could have five minutes with her.
